# TotalFinance — full reference for LLMs

TotalFinance is a TypeScript financial-computation toolkit. The SDK covers options, strategies, technical analysis, portfolio P&L, valuation, risk, scenarios, and backtesting. The operation registry is a curated serializable subset, not universal SDK coverage. Compute uses caller-supplied data, not live quotes. Package versions below are workspace metadata, not evidence of npm publication.

Generated from package export maps, TypeScript source/checker/JSDoc, public guides, stability files and live operation metadata. No root-only API reports, inferred financial defaults, or publication claims.

## Imports and bundles

Use named imports from `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/<domain>` as the portable browser
default. The main package includes every domain and feature subpath with no runtime dependencies;
only `@insiderfinance/totalfinance-mcp` is a separate optional install. TotalFinance is an unpublished preview: these are supported import
shapes for a built checkout, not evidence of a completed npm installation.

### Start with a domain

With the umbrella installed:

```ts
import { normalCdf } from '@insiderfinance/totalfinance/math';

console.log(normalCdf(0)); // 0.5
```

Supported feature subpaths are another explicit choice:

```ts
import { normalCdf } from '@insiderfinance/totalfinance/math/normal';

console.log(normalCdf(0)); // 0.5
```

Other examples include `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis/rsi` and
`@insiderfinance/totalfinance/options/black-scholes`. Use the package's public export map, never private `dist`
paths. Domain and feature paths are exports of the same main package; they are not separate installs.
Domain named imports need no consumer-specific plugin.

### Namespace convenience has a tradeoff

Direct namespace imports with static member access can tree-shake in both esbuild and Rollup:

```ts
import * as math from '@insiderfinance/totalfinance/math';

console.log(math.normalCdf(0)); // 0.5
```

That is different from the root's namespace re-export:

```ts
import { math } from '@insiderfinance/totalfinance';

console.log(math.normalCdf(0)); // 0.5, but bundler-dependent retention
```

In the tested esbuild configuration, this second form retains the whole math namespace because of
[esbuild issue #1420](https://github.com/evanw/esbuild/issues/1420). Rollup shakes this static use.
The braces in `import { math }` select a namespace object, not a named calculation. Prefer named
domain imports when the same code must stay small across bundlers.

The root namespace API remains supported for convenience and discovery. It also hoists exactly five
option gestures: `blackScholes`, `option`, `market`, `engines`, and `impliedVolatility`. Other option
exports live under `options` or their supported domain/feature entrypoints, not flat on the root.

Runtime-selected access such as `math[name]`, namespace enumeration such as `Object.values(math)`,
and registries that dispatch to many calculations inherently retain the implementations they can
reach. Tree shaking cannot remove functionality your program may select at runtime. This applies
even to a direct namespace import; it is distinct from the esbuild re-export limitation.

### Three different sizes

- **Installation size:** package files and dependencies on disk. The main package includes all domains;
  MCP adds its SDK dependency and depends on the exact main version. Tree shaking does not shrink an install.
- **Final bundle size:** code retained by the production bundler for the imports and calls you use.
  ESM and `sideEffects: false` enable removal of unused code, but access patterns and bundler behavior
  still matter. Installing the umbrella does not require delivering every domain to the browser.
- **Plain Node ESM loading:** Node loads the imported module graph; it performs no automatic dead-code
  elimination. A named import from a broad barrel is not a promise to load only one function. Use a
  supported feature subpath when you want a narrower unbundled module graph.

Type-only imports, such as `import type { BlackScholesKernelInput } from
'@insiderfinance/totalfinance/options/black-scholes'`, are erased from emitted JavaScript and add no runtime code.
Browser-safe compute entrypoints remain separate from Node-only transports and filesystem helpers.

### A facade is more than a formula

`blackScholes` includes input validation, typed errors, and `.explain()` assumptions and diagnostics.
An indicator such as `rsi` also carries its streaming and serialization services. Importing one of
these public objects is not the cost of a bare formula, even when you call just one method.
The expert `blackScholesPrice` export on `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/options/black-scholes` offers a different,
documented contract; choose it for that contract, not to bypass validation.

See the generated [bundle size report](bundle-size.md) for enforced measurements. Whole-entrypoint
budgets and used-function consumer budgets answer different questions: keeping an entire entrypoint
is not the cost of one selected calculation. Compare matching import forms and bundlers, and measure
your own production build; neither set of bundle measurements describes installation size or plain
Node loading.

[Imports and bundles guide](guides/imports-and-bundles.md)

## Journey connect-agent

Use Node at the floor declared by the installed package. In a built checkout (`pnpm build`), launch the stdio server:
```sh
node distribution/mcp/dist/bin.js --profile default
node distribution/mcp/dist/bin.js doctor
```

This checkout declares @insiderfinance/totalfinance-mcp 0.1.2 (pre-1.0; component maturity varies (see stability policy)). After independently confirming availability of that exact release, a client may use command `npx` with args `["-y", "@insiderfinance/totalfinance-mcp@0.1.2", "--profile", "default"]`. Do not assume the workspace version has been published. Stdout in server mode is JSON-RPC only.

Published-package smoke: pending release. This build-time reference does not claim execution against published packages.

### Selection and permissions

Omitted packs select the default compute packs. An explicit packs array is exact, including an empty array. The full profile selects all registered packs but grants no capabilities. Read-only is the server default. Embedded write use requires explicit readOnly: false, the per-operation requiredCapabilities, and the stores the operation requires. The CLI accepts repeatable --capability grants; a write grant enables write visibility but does not create missing stores or trusted authorizations. A sideEffect of none does not imply no permission requirement. Consult doctor, tools/list, and totalfinance://capabilities for effective availability.

Catalog discovery is paged: follow nextCursor until absent for tools, resources and prompts. Treat cursors as opaque and server/catalog-scoped; restart without a cursor if it is rejected. totalfinance://profiles lists task selections; totalfinance://capabilities reports the active filters and grants. Use totalfinance://schema/tool/<name>/input and /output for an enabled tool’s schema, and invoke only prompts actually listed.

Paper trading is local simulation, not a brokerage connection. Authorization, paper submission/cancellation, reconciliation, and portfolio-ledger application are distinct operations. Policy/human authorization, trusted authorization records and idempotency are not bypassed by selecting full. No live brokerage orders or live market-data fetching are supplied by this catalog.

### Handles, results, and errors

Attach an explicit artifact store (--store <directory> in the CLI) to resolve handles. A ResourceHandle is store-scoped, with uri, kind, schema, version, contentHash, createdTimestampMs, expiresTimestampMs and provenance. Only the handleFields declared by an operation accept handle substitution. Inline data and stored data must satisfy the same operation contract. Unknown, wrong-kind, stale or unavailable handles are errors, not invitations to invent data. Read stored reports through listed totalfinance://reports/<hash> resources or totalfinance.artifact.read when enabled.

OperationResult carries operation identity/version, structured output, assumptions, diagnostics, artifacts and completion status. Inspect diagnostics and partial/incomplete status before treating a calculation as complete. QuantError failures are OperationError { code, message, context, operation }; MCP returns isError with the error in text, not success-shaped structuredContent. Schema validation errors may additionally include issues. Unknown protocol tools/resources/prompts are JSON-RPC errors. Never replace non-convergence with a guessed number.

SDK result grammar depends on role: facade calls return plain values and .explain() returns value/assumptions/diagnostics; analysis calls return rich reports; factories return artifacts; expert kernels have their declared numerical contracts. Use units and conventions from the exact field documentation, not generic economic defaults. A missing JSDoc default is shown as not declared; optional never implies zero. Schema defaults below are emitted only when the schema declares them.

### Budgets, seeds, and heavy jobs

Runtime budget metadata (bytes and milliseconds as named; not economic assumptions):
```json
{
  "maxInputBytes": {
    "transportDefault": 65536,
    "maximum": 16777216
  },
  "inlineResultBytes": {
    "default": 262144,
    "maximum": 16777216
  }
}
```

Stochastic metadata may be per-call: evaluate it on parsed inputs (including declared schema defaults). The transport seed policy is published at totalfinance://policy/seed; inspect the resolved seed in results. Deterministic calls do not acquire synthetic seeds.

For job-class work, explicitly attach a local JobRunner and its artifact store to the embedded MCP server. Use the lifecycle tools only when listed by that server: totalfinance.job.submit returns a job id; totalfinance.job.status reports progress; totalfinance.job.result fetches the unchanged completed result later; totalfinance.job.cancel stops unfinished work. Follow the returned status/result resource URIs. Progress may be lifecycle-only, not a measured percentage. Profile selection alone does not attach a runner or grant job access. Job controls are transport lifecycle tools, not additional registry compute operations.

### SDK-only boundaries

The option-price/Greeks wire operations declare Black–Scholes–Merton; do not treat them as generic pricing-engine selectors. The SDK model families (including Heston, SABR, local-volatility and exotic pricing) and custom engines are not universally exposed by MCP. A registered operation may compose a specific model without exposing its whole SDK family. Caller callbacks, custom predicates, custom pricers, and custom policies cannot be serialized into JSON. Use the SDK for those contracts. Operation-specific SDK-only restrictions below are copied from live schema metadata.

[MCP guide](guides/mcp.md) · [Trade lifecycle](guides/trade-lifecycle.md) · [Errors](guides/errors.md)

## Profiles

Profiles select packs, never permissions. Counts below are registry membership, not the effective tools/list after permissions, stores and job attachment.

### Profile default

Packs: `options`, `technical_analysis`, `strategy`, `volatility`, `structure`, `risk`, `performance`, `calendar`, `crypto`, `fixed_income`. Operations: 23.

- options: Price an option (Black–Scholes–Merton); Compute first-order Greeks; Solve implied volatility
- technical_analysis: Calculate a technical indicator; List technical indicators; Describe one technical indicator
- strategy: Analyze an options strategy; List the named-strategy catalog
- volatility: Expected move (1σ); Probability of finishing in-the-money; Probability of touching a level; Fit an implied-vol surface; IV rank / percentile / stats; Event-volatility decomposition (earnings)
- structure: Dealer exposure & levels from an option chain; Classify options flow (sweeps / blocks / spreads)
- risk: Value-at-Risk & Conditional VaR; Portfolio optimization
- performance: Full performance summary
- calendar: Trading sessions & option expirations
- crypto: Perpetual funding → implied carry; Futures basis / cash-and-carry
- fixed_income: Bond price/yield analytics

### Profile options

Packs: `options`, `volatility`. Operations: 9.

## Operation catalog

46 operations from packsForProfile('full'). All schemas below are complete, not abbreviated.

### totalfinance.artifact.compare

Compare two analysis artifacts

Compare a baseline and a candidate artifact of the same type leaf by leaf: value differences with absolute and relative deltas, added and removed paths, whether inputs and producers match, and — when a tolerance is supplied — whether every numeric leaf is within it. The result is compareAnalysisArtifacts(...) verbatim.

Version: 1; pack: artifact; profiles: `backtesting`, `full`, `portfolio`, `scenarios`; defaultEnabled: false; SDKonly: false.

Required capabilities: none. Authorization: none. Side effect: none. Idempotency: not-applicable.

Handle fields: `baseline`, `candidate`. Cost: medium. Cancellation supported: false. Deterministic: true. Stochastic: false.

Annotations: {"readOnlyHint":true,"destructiveHint":false,"idempotentHint":true,"openWorldHint":false}

### totalfinance.artifact.read

Read an analysis artifact

Validate a Gate B analysis artifact (its envelope, its recomputed inputs hash, and its content-hash identity) and return its identity, type, producer, provenance warnings, table names, and a bounded preview of the stored result — the one read door for any artifact over the wire. Migrations are not registered over the wire; a stored older version is refused with the versions named.

Version: 1; pack: artifact; profiles: `backtesting`, `full`, `portfolio`, `scenarios`; defaultEnabled: false; SDKonly: false.

Required capabilities: none. Authorization: none. Side effect: none. Idempotency: not-applicable.

Handle fields: `artifact`. Cost: small. Cancellation supported: false. Deterministic: true. Stochastic: false.

Annotations: {"readOnlyHint":true,"destructiveHint":false,"idempotentHint":true,"openWorldHint":false}

### totalfinance.backtest.cross_sectional_run

Run a cross-sectional backtest

Backtest a point-in-time cross-sectional strategy: a returns dataset with declared features, a universe history with entries and exits, one declarative signal (a versioned factor recipe, a composite score, or a screen), a rebalance schedule, and a portfolio construction (quantile/count/fraction selection on each side; equal, score, inverse-volatility, or risk-budget weights; dollar/sector/beta/factor neutrality; position, weight, turnover, and participation caps — every trim a reported goal). Fills go through the execution policy into the portfolio ledger; the final value reconciles to the ledger NAV. Rebalances, holdings, fills, the ledger, the timeline, attribution, the benchmark block, and the performance summary — crossSectionalBacktest(...) verbatim. Opt-in (backtestPack): payloads and runtime are heavier than the default set; bulk row sets above the row cap travel by handle.

Version: 1; pack: backtest; profiles: `backtesting`, `full`; defaultEnabled: false; SDKonly: false.

Required capabilities: none. Authorization: none. Side effect: none. Idempotency: not-applicable.

Handle fields: `dataset`. Cost: job. Cancellation supported: false. Deterministic: true. Stochastic: false.

Annotations: {"readOnlyHint":true,"destructiveHint":false,"idempotentHint":true,"openWorldHint":false}

SDK-only limitation: 'supplied-weights' takes a caller function and is SDK-only
SDK-only limitation: A declared execution policy over session bars (execution.declared): the label is the caller's claim; a caller fill model, session rules, and quote/order-book observations are SDK-only
SDK-only limitation: The three declarative signal forms; a signal callback is SDK-only

### totalfinance.backtest.environment_episode

Bench a baseline policy over one trading-environment episode

Run one of the six maintained baseline policies through the deterministic trading environment over a catalogue episode (or a named declarative definition) at a seed, and return Agent Bench's report for that episode: operational conformance (look-ahead, replay equality, duplicate orders under the retry drive, external-order attempts, reconciliation; the mask and limit counts) apart from strategy quality (return, volatility, Sharpe, Sortino, drawdown, turnover, cost, exposure, violations) — no single score by design. With artifact: 'embed', the recorded episode travels as an `environment` run artifact that replays to its run hash. Declarative inputs only: a TypeScript policy or a reward goal callback is SDK-only. Opt-in (backtestPack).

Version: 1; pack: backtest; profiles: `backtesting`, `full`; defaultEnabled: false; SDKonly: false.

Required capabilities: none. Authorization: none. Side effect: none. Idempotency: not-applicable.

Handle fields: `episode.definition.marketData`. Cost: job. Cancellation supported: false. Deterministic: true. Stochastic: false.

Annotations: {"readOnlyHint":true,"destructiveHint":false,"idempotentHint":true,"openWorldHint":false}

SDK-only limitation: A built-in kind; 'custom' brings its own adapter and is SDK-only
SDK-only limitation: A declared execution policy over session bars (execution.declared): the label is the caller's claim; a caller fill model, session rules, and quote/order-book observations are SDK-only
SDK-only limitation: A maintained baseline; a TypeScript policy is SDK-only
SDK-only limitation: Run one of the six maintained baseline policies through the deterministic trading environment over a catalogue episode (or a named declarative definition) at a seed, and return Agent Bench's report for that episode: operational conformance (look-ahead, replay equality, duplicate orders under the retry drive, external-order attempts, reconciliation; the mask and limit counts) apart from strategy quality (return, volatility, Sharpe, Sortino, drawdown, turnover, cost, exposure, violations) — no single score by design. With artifact: 'embed', the recorded episode travels as an `environment` run artifact that replays to its run hash. Declarative inputs only: a TypeScript policy or a reward goal callback is SDK-only. Opt-in (backtestPack).
SDK-only limitation: The declared reward composition; a goal callback is SDK-only

### totalfinance.backtest.options_run

Run an options backtest

Backtest a declarative options strategy over chain snapshots: structure selection by delta and DTE, exit and roll triggers, optional delta hedging, declarative commission and slippage, American assignment modelling, and the marking policy (current-quote or entry volatility; what a missing mark does). Several rules may hold several trades at once (book), pre-trade limits reject entries with rows, combo or legged fills, quote freshness, split lineage, dividend evidence, the surface summary, and the portfolio ledger the equity reconciles to. Equity points, trades with per-leg attribution and mark counts, settlements, and the standard performance summary. The result is optionsBacktest(...) verbatim. Opt-in (backtestPack): payloads and runtime are heavier than the default set.

Version: 1; pack: backtest; profiles: `backtesting`, `full`; defaultEnabled: false; SDKonly: false.

Required capabilities: none. Authorization: none. Side effect: none. Idempotency: not-applicable.

Handle fields: none. Cost: job. Cancellation supported: false. Deterministic: true. Stochastic: false.

Annotations: {"readOnlyHint":true,"destructiveHint":false,"idempotentHint":true,"openWorldHint":false}

SDK-only limitation: 'flat' (default) enters only when no position is open; a caller predicate is SDK-only
SDK-only limitation: A `when` predicate is SDK-only
SDK-only limitation: The declarative entry structures; a `build` callback is SDK-only

### totalfinance.backtest.portfolio_run

Run a portfolio backtest

Backtest a multi-asset portfolio through the ledger: instruments with built-in adapters (equity, etf, option, future, fx-forward, crypto-spot, crypto-perpetual, bond), market data by row set, a model or inline targets on a rebalance schedule, an execution policy with settlement lags, external flows, a calendar, and the margin check with forced liquidation. Every fill, flow, lifecycle fact, and liquidation is a portfolio event; the equity is the ledger's net asset value. The result is portfolioBacktest(...) verbatim. Opt-in (backtestPack): payloads and runtime are heavier than the default set; bulk row sets above the row cap travel by handle.

Version: 1; pack: backtest; profiles: `backtesting`, `full`; defaultEnabled: false; SDKonly: false.

Required capabilities: none. Authorization: none. Side effect: none. Idempotency: not-applicable.

Handle fields: `marketData`. Cost: job. Cancellation supported: false. Deterministic: true. Stochastic: false.

Annotations: {"readOnlyHint":true,"destructiveHint":false,"idempotentHint":true,"openWorldHint":false}

SDK-only limitation: A built-in kind; 'custom' brings its own adapter and is SDK-only
SDK-only limitation: A declared execution policy over session bars (execution.declared): the label is the caller's claim; a caller fill model, session rules, and quote/order-book observations are SDK-only
SDK-only limitation: The declarative strategy; an onSession callback is SDK-only

### totalfinance.backtest.vectorized_run

Run a vectorized backtest

Run a single-asset vectorized backtest: signal-following fills at close, optional bps fees. Returns final value, turnover, and the performance summary; every hidden policy the run assumed (fill timing, costs, slippage, settlement, calendar, margin) is echoed in `assumptions`, and the implementation-risk warnings (look-ahead, data alignment) ride `diagnostics`. Deliberately opt-in (backtestPack) — payloads and runtime are heavier than the default tools.

Version: 1; pack: backtest; profiles: `backtesting`, `full`; defaultEnabled: false; SDKonly: false.

Required capabilities: none. Authorization: none. Side effect: none. Idempotency: not-applicable.

Handle fields: none. Cost: small. Cancellation supported: false. Deterministic: true. Stochastic: false.

Annotations: {"readOnlyHint":true,"destructiveHint":false,"idempotentHint":true,"openWorldHint":false}

Solve implied volatility

Solve Black–Scholes–Merton implied volatility from an observed option price using the method suite (auto/brent/newton/halley/householder, with an optional Brent fallback). Supply time as timeToExpiryYears (years) or as expiry + asOf (dates). Non-convergence and no-arbitrage failures are reported in diagnostics (converged: false), never fabricated; the method actually used is echoed in diagnostics.method.

Version: 1; pack: options; profiles: `default`, `full`, `options`, `strategies`; defaultEnabled: true; SDKonly: false.

Required capabilities: none. Authorization: none. Side effect: none. Idempotency: not-applicable.

Handle fields: none. Cost: small. Cancellation supported: false. Deterministic: true. Stochastic: false.

Annotations: {"readOnlyHint":true,"destructiveHint":false,"idempotentHint":true,"openWorldHint":false}

```json
      "description": "Strike price"
```

### totalfinance.performance.analyze

Full performance summary

Summarize a return series or equity curve: total/annualized return, volatility, Sharpe, Sortino, Calmar, max drawdown, omega, hit rate, profit factor, expectancy — plus beta/alpha/tracking error/information ratio/Treynor when a `benchmark` is supplied. Suspicious inputs (prices passed as returns, returns passed as equity) are flagged in diagnostics.warnings, never silently reported.

Version: 1; pack: performance; profiles: `backtesting`, `default`, `full`, `portfolio`; defaultEnabled: true; SDKonly: false.

Required capabilities: none. Authorization: none. Side effect: none. Idempotency: not-applicable.

Handle fields: none. Cost: small. Cancellation supported: false. Deterministic: true. Stochastic: false.

Annotations: {"readOnlyHint":true,"destructiveHint":false,"idempotentHint":true,"openWorldHint":false}

```json
        "type": "number"

    "equity": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "number",

      "type": "array",

        "type": "number"
```

### totalfinance.portfolio.analyze

Analyze a portfolio (snapshot, timeline, monitor)

One report of up to three direct results: the valuation snapshot at `asOf` (always), the dated timeline with P&L since each prior mark and drawdown (when `marks` are supplied), and the policy monitor with its alerts and carried state (when `monitor` is supplied). Each result is the direct function verbatim; nothing is aggregated across them, and one `assumptions` says which parts ran and why the others did not.

Version: 1; pack: portfolio; profiles: `full`, `portfolio`; defaultEnabled: false; SDKonly: false.

Required capabilities: none. Authorization: none. Side effect: none. Idempotency: not-applicable.

### totalfinance.portfolio.explain_pnl

Explain portfolio P&L between two marks

Explain the change in net asset value between two dated valuation marks: external flows, investment return, and the identity components (realized, unrealized, income, transaction costs, financing, foreign exchange) that reconcile to it with a published residual, by currency and by grouping. The result is portfolioPnl(...) verbatim.

Version: 1; pack: portfolio; profiles: `full`, `portfolio`; defaultEnabled: false; SDKonly: false.

Required capabilities: none. Authorization: none. Side effect: none. Idempotency: not-applicable.

Handle fields: `ledger`, `from.market`, `to.market`. Cost: small. Cancellation supported: false. Deterministic: true. Stochastic: false.

Annotations: {"readOnlyHint":true,"destructiveHint":false,"idempotentHint":true,"openWorldHint":false}

### totalfinance.portfolio.rebalance_proposal

Propose a rebalance (a proposal, never an order)

Fold the ledger snapshot to its state, mark it from the market snapshot, and propose the trades that take the portfolio to the policy targets (or only the drifted ones) under the policy limits, lot sizes, minimum notional, transaction-cost estimates, and an optional external flow. The result is proposePortfolioRebalance(...) verbatim: weights before and after, the cash summary, the trades with their estimates, the objective, and every target it could not resolve. Read-only by construction — it returns a proposal and places nothing. Opt-in (portfolioPack).

Version: 1; pack: portfolio; profiles: `full`, `portfolio`; defaultEnabled: false; SDKonly: false.

Required capabilities: `trade:propose`. Authorization: none. Side effect: none. Idempotency: not-applicable.

Handle fields: `ledger`, `market`. Cost: medium. Cancellation supported: false. Deterministic: true. Stochastic: false.

Annotations: {"readOnlyHint":true,"destructiveHint":false,"idempotentHint":true,"openWorldHint":false}

### totalfinance.portfolio.record_events

Apply events to a ledger and store the new ledger

Fold validated portfolio events (fills from trade.submit, deposits, corporate actions) onto a ledger through the ledger's own reducer and put the new ledger into the artifact store as a content-addressed portfolio handle. The write is the put: an unchanged ledger is the same handle; identical replays fold once and applied counts only new events. Changed event bodies are refused. Requires a writable artifact store and the portfolio:write capability. Opt-in (tradePack).

Version: 1; pack: trade; profiles: `full`; defaultEnabled: false; SDKonly: false.

Required capabilities: `portfolio:write`. Authorization: none. Side effect: portfolio-state. Idempotency: required.

Handle fields: `portfolio`. Cost: small. Cancellation supported: false. Deterministic: true. Stochastic: false.

Annotations: {"readOnlyHint":false,"destructiveHint":false,"idempotentHint":true,"openWorldHint":true}

### totalfinance.portfolio.snapshot

Value a portfolio at an instant

Value every cash balance and position of a portfolio at one instant from a Gate B market snapshot: net asset value in the base currency, per-account cash rows (settled and unsettled), per-position marks, cost basis and unrealized P&L. Supply the portfolio as its serialized ledger envelope (re-hydrated through readPortfolioLedgerSnapshot) or as a derived PortfolioState. The result is portfolioSnapshot(...) verbatim.

Version: 1; pack: portfolio; profiles: `full`, `portfolio`; defaultEnabled: false; SDKonly: false.

Required capabilities: none. Authorization: none. Side effect: none. Idempotency: not-applicable.

Handle fields: `portfolio`, `market`. Cost: small. Cancellation supported: false. Deterministic: true. Stochastic: false.

Annotations: {"readOnlyHint":true,"destructiveHint":false,"idempotentHint":true,"openWorldHint":false}

### totalfinance.research.event_study

Run an event study

Measure abnormal returns around dated events under a declared expected-return model (mean-adjusted, market-adjusted, or market model), with explicit session, overlap, and cumulation policies; per-event rows and cumulative abnormal returns, and the average abnormal return by offset with t-statistics. The result is eventStudy(...) verbatim.

Version: 1; pack: research; profiles: `full`, `research`; defaultEnabled: false; SDKonly: false.

Required capabilities: none. Authorization: none. Side effect: none. Idempotency: not-applicable.

Handle fields: none. Cost: medium. Cancellation supported: false. Deterministic: true. Stochastic: false.

Annotations: {"readOnlyHint":true,"destructiveHint":false,"idempotentHint":true,"openWorldHint":false}

SDK-only limitation: The serializable models; a 'custom' expected-return function is SDK-only

### totalfinance.risk.optimize

Portfolio optimization

Solve a portfolio: minVariance, maxSharpe (tangency), meanVariance utility, riskParity (equal risk contribution), hrp (hierarchical risk parity), or kelly. Returns the Computed envelope: value.weights + value.objective, assumptions echo the objective and budget, and diagnostics carry converged/iterations — a non-converged solve adds an optimize.not_converged warning instead of pretending.

Version: 1; pack: risk; profiles: `default`, `full`, `portfolio`; defaultEnabled: true; SDKonly: false.

Required capabilities: none. Authorization: none. Side effect: none. Idempotency: not-applicable.

Handle fields: none. Cost: small. Cancellation supported: false. Deterministic: true. Stochastic: false.

### totalfinance.risk.value_at_risk

Value-at-Risk & Conditional VaR

Estimate Value-at-Risk (VaR) and Conditional VaR / expected shortfall from a return series. Methods: historical (empirical quantile, default), parametric (Gaussian, optional Cornish-Fisher for skew/kurtosis), or monteCarlo. Both are positive loss magnitudes at the given `confidence`; the horizon scales by √-time. The applied confidence/method/horizon ride `assumptions` (with the resolved seed/samples for monteCarlo) and warnings ride `diagnostics`.

Version: 1; pack: risk; profiles: `default`, `full`, `portfolio`; defaultEnabled: true; SDKonly: false.

Required capabilities: none. Authorization: none. Side effect: none. Idempotency: not-applicable.

Handle fields: none. Cost: small. Cancellation supported: false. Deterministic: false. Stochastic: per-call.

Annotations: {"readOnlyHint":true,"destructiveHint":false,"idempotentHint":true,"openWorldHint":false}


Input JSON Schema:
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "returns": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "number"
      },
      "description": "Periodic returns as decimals (e.g. 0.01 = +1%)"
    },
    "confidence": {
      "type": "number",
      "exclusiveMinimum": 0,
      "description": "Confidence level in (0, 1); default 0.95"
    },
    "method": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "historical",
        "parametric",
        "monteCarlo"
      ],
      "description": "Estimation method; default historical"
    },
    "horizonPeriods": {
      "type": "number",
      "exclusiveMinimum": 0,
      "description": "Holding-period horizon in periods; scales by √-time; default 1"
    },
    "cornishFisher": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "Parametric only: Cornish-Fisher adjustment for skew/excess-kurtosis"
    },
    "samples": {
      "type": "integer",
      "maximum": 1000000,
      "exclusiveMinimum": 0,
      "description": "Monte-Carlo only: number of simulated paths; default 10000, capped at 1,000,000 (compute is bounded BEFORE the work starts, not just by the deadline)."
    },
    "seed": {
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Monte-Carlo only: PRNG seed; default 0"
    }
  },
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "required": [
    "returns"
  ]
}
```

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {

    "diagnostics"
  ]
}
```

### totalfinance.scenario.run

Run a scenario set against targets

Revalue every target under every scenario of a Gate B scenario set against a Gate B market snapshot: a scenario-major cell grid with base values, per-cell P&L in local and reporting currency, and per-scenario aggregates. Targets are the serializable kinds — spot assets, Taylor (greeks) positions, and a portfolio bound through Taylor bindings. The result is runScenarios(...) verbatim.

Version: 1; pack: scenario; profiles: `full`, `scenarios`; defaultEnabled: false; SDKonly: false.

Required capabilities: none. Authorization: none. Side effect: none. Idempotency: not-applicable.

SDK-only limitation: Wire targets: kind 'spot' (scenarioTarget.spot), 'taylor' (scenarioTarget.taylor), or 'portfolio' (scenarioTargetsFromPortfolio with Taylor bindings). A custom pricer target is SDK-only.

### totalfinance.strategy.analyze

Analyze an options strategy

Build a multi-leg options position from its legs and return breakevens, net debit/credit, max profit, and max loss. Legs may be given without premiums: pass `premiums: "model"` with a `market` snapshot (spot, volatility, riskFreeRate, asOf, expiry) and every unpriced leg is priced by the BSM engine — so an iron condor’s P&L and probability-of-profit come from strikes alone. Set `probability: true` (with `market`) to also get probability-of-profit, expected value, risk/reward, and probability-of-touch. `premiumSource` reports whether premiums were user- or model-supplied.

Version: 1; pack: strategy; profiles: `default`, `full`, `strategies`; defaultEnabled: true; SDKonly: false.

Required capabilities: none. Authorization: none. Side effect: none. Idempotency: not-applicable.

Handle fields: none. Cost: small. Cancellation supported: false. Deterministic: true. Stochastic: false.

Annotations: {"readOnlyHint":true,"destructiveHint":false,"idempotentHint":true,"openWorldHint":false}

### totalfinance.structure.exposures

Dealer exposure & levels from an option chain

Compute dealer-positioning exposure (net GEX/DEX at spot) and key levels — call/put walls, zero-gamma flip, max pain, pin risk, and 0DTE/weekly/monthly OPEX walls — from an option chain. Each row needs `strike`, `expiry`, `type`, `openInterest`, and either `impliedVolatility` or `price` (IV is implied from price when omitted). Inferred from open interest and a sign convention (echoed in `assumptions.convention`, with its caveats as `model.limitation` warnings in `diagnostics.warnings`) — it does not know true dealer books.

Version: 1; pack: structure; profiles: `default`, `full`; defaultEnabled: true; SDKonly: false.

Required capabilities: none. Authorization: none. Side effect: none. Idempotency: not-applicable.

Handle fields: none. Cost: small. Cancellation supported: false. Deterministic: true. Stochastic: false.

Annotations: {"readOnlyHint":true,"destructiveHint":false,"idempotentHint":true,"openWorldHint":false}

### totalfinance.structure.flow

Classify options flow (sweeps / blocks / spreads)

Classify option prints into aggressor-side flow: sweeps (multi-print bursts, venue-verified when exchange codes are supplied), blocks, and multi-leg spreads. Aggressor side is NBBO-estimated (Lee–Ready style) — the honest caveats ride diagnostics.warnings as `model.limitation` entries (mirrored as `limitations` strings for quick reading); nothing is presented as exchange-confirmed unless it is.

Version: 1; pack: structure; profiles: `default`, `full`; defaultEnabled: true; SDKonly: false.

Required capabilities: none. Authorization: none. Side effect: none. Idempotency: not-applicable.

Handle fields: none. Cost: small. Cancellation supported: false. Deterministic: true. Stochastic: false.

### totalfinance.technical_analysis.calculate

Calculate a technical indicator

Compute any of TotalFinance’s ~300 registered technical indicators over a price series. Close-based (`series`) indicators take `closes`; bar-based indicators take `bars` (OHLCV objects) or parallel column arrays under `series`; pair indicators (e.g. beta, correl) take `x` and `y`. Use `totalfinance.technical_analysis.list` to discover indicator names, input kinds, and parameters. Output is aligned to input length with null during warmup; `assumptions.parameters` echoes the parameters actually used (declared defaults merged with yours), and `diagnostics.warmup` is the first real index.

Version: 1; pack: technical_analysis; profiles: `default`, `full`; defaultEnabled: true; SDKonly: false.

Required capabilities: none. Authorization: none. Side effect: none. Idempotency: not-applicable.

Handle fields: none. Cost: small. Cancellation supported: false. Deterministic: true. Stochastic: false.

### totalfinance.technical_analysis.describe

Describe one technical indicator

Return the full card for a single indicator (alias-aware): category, input kind, parameters, defaults, which parameters are required, its warmup (leading bars before the first real value), and its cross-library aliases. The token-lean way to learn one indicator without listing all ~335. Discover names with `totalfinance.technical_analysis.list`; compute with `totalfinance.technical_analysis.calculate`.

Version: 1; pack: technical_analysis; profiles: `default`, `full`; defaultEnabled: true; SDKonly: false.

Required capabilities: none. Authorization: none. Side effect: none. Idempotency: not-applicable.

Handle fields: none. Cost: small. Cancellation supported: false. Deterministic: true. Stochastic: false.

Annotations: {"readOnlyHint":true,"destructiveHint":false,"idempotentHint":true,"openWorldHint":false}


Input JSON Schema:
```json

  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "name": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Indicator name or a TA-Lib/pandas/TradingView alias (e.g. \"rsi\", \"RSI\", \"STOCH\")"
    }
  },
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "required": [

  ]
```

### totalfinance.technical_analysis.list

List technical indicators

Discover the technical indicators available to `totalfinance.technical_analysis.calculate`. Returns each indicator’s name, category, input kind (series | bars | pair), parameters, defaults, and which parameters are required. Narrow the ~335-indicator catalog with `search` (matches a name or a TA-Lib/pandas/TradingView alias) and/or `category`, and page it with `limit` (default 50) / `offset` (`total` is the full match count). For one indicator’s full card (including its warmup), use `totalfinance.technical_analysis.describe`. Then pass a name to `totalfinance.technical_analysis.calculate`.

Version: 1; pack: technical_analysis; profiles: `default`, `full`; defaultEnabled: true; SDKonly: false.

Required capabilities: none. Authorization: none. Side effect: none. Idempotency: not-applicable.

Handle fields: none. Cost: small. Cancellation supported: false. Deterministic: true. Stochastic: false.

Annotations: {"readOnlyHint":true,"destructiveHint":false,"idempotentHint":true,"openWorldHint":false}


Input JSON Schema:
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "search": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Case-insensitive substring of an indicator name OR a TA-Lib/pandas/TradingView alias"
    },
    "category": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "transform",
        "moving-average",
        "momentum",
        "trend",
        "volatility",
        "volume",
        "cycle",
        "statistic",
        "math",
        "performance",
        "candlestick",
        "price-action"
      ]
    },
    "limit": {
      "type": "integer",
      "exclusiveMinimum": 0,
      "description": "Page size (default 50; `total` is the full match count) — narrow with `search` before paging"
    },
    "offset": {
      "type": "integer",
      "minimum": 0,
      "description": "Page offset (default 0)"
    }
  },
  "additionalProperties": false
}
```

### totalfinance.trade.authorize

Mint an authorization grant for a preflighted plan

Bind human authority to one plan and one preflight report: the plan hash, the portfolio and market hashes preflight judged, the market instant and an age allowance, the paper mode, the account, a variance envelope, an expiry, the approver, and a closed set of idempotency keys. Refuses a denied preflight, an unjudged plan, or a stale expiry. The grant is put into the authorization store under its content hash and returned with its handle. Requires the trade:approve capability. Opt-in (tradePack).

Version: 1; pack: trade; profiles: `full`; defaultEnabled: false; SDKonly: false.

Required capabilities: `trade:approve`. Authorization: human. Side effect: none. Idempotency: not-applicable.

Handle fields: none. Cost: small. Cancellation supported: false. Deterministic: true. Stochastic: false.

Annotations: {"readOnlyHint":true,"destructiveHint":false,"idempotentHint":true,"openWorldHint":false}

### totalfinance.trade.cancel

Cancel an open paper order

Journal cancel-requested then cancelled for an open order in the journal store under `<sourceId>:journal`; a terminal order is not cancelled twice (accepted: false, the state says why). Cancelling a combo leg cancels all remaining legs of that plan-local combo. Both the original journal and authorization stores are required to recover pending submissions before cancellation; no new grant is needed. A fill delivered after the cancellation is Decision 6's late-fill path. Paper only; requires trade:paper. Opt-in (tradePack).

Version: 1; pack: trade; profiles: `full`; defaultEnabled: false; SDKonly: false.

Required capabilities: `trade:paper`. Authorization: policy. Side effect: external-order. Idempotency: optional.

Handle fields: none. Cost: small. Cancellation supported: false. Deterministic: true. Stochastic: false.

Annotations: {"readOnlyHint":false,"destructiveHint":true,"idempotentHint":false,"openWorldHint":true}

### totalfinance.trade.preflight

Preflight a trade plan against the ledger, the market, and the policy

Normalize an intent (or take an execution plan) and judge it: the portfolio before and after through the ledger's own fold of hypothetical fills, every policy check with its verdict, declared-rate cost estimates, the monitor's alerts on the after-state, and one decision — allow only when every check passes, deny on any failure, require-approval when evidence is missing; never an allow from missing information. No effect. Opt-in (tradePack).

Version: 1; pack: trade; profiles: `full`; defaultEnabled: false; SDKonly: false.

Required capabilities: `trade:propose`. Authorization: none. Side effect: none. Idempotency: not-applicable.

Handle fields: `portfolio`, `market`. Cost: small. Cancellation supported: false. Deterministic: true. Stochastic: false.

Annotations: {"readOnlyHint":true,"destructiveHint":false,"idempotentHint":true,"openWorldHint":false}

### totalfinance.trade.reconcile

Reconcile an execution journal to the ledger

Join the journal's order states (from the journal store by `journalId`, or inline events) to the ledger's fills under the execution source in both directions, compare delivered fill quantities per order within an explicit tolerance, list the unresolved orders, and — with an external snapshot — compose reconcilePortfolio verbatim. With planHash, exclude other plans’ journaled orders and fills from both joins; unattributed source fills remain discrepancies. External snapshots are judged over the whole portfolio. reconciled is true only when everything agrees and no order is unresolved. No effect; requires trade:paper. Opt-in (tradePack).

Version: 1; pack: trade; profiles: `full`; defaultEnabled: false; SDKonly: false.

Required capabilities: `trade:paper`. Authorization: none. Side effect: none. Idempotency: not-applicable.

Handle fields: `ledger`. Cost: small. Cancellation supported: false. Deterministic: true. Stochastic: false.

Annotations: {"readOnlyHint":true,"destructiveHint":false,"idempotentHint":true,"openWorldHint":false}

### totalfinance.trade.submit

Submit an authorized plan to the paper broker

Verify the grant against the plan, the portfolio and market hashes, the market instant, the account, and the idempotency key; journal submitted and acknowledged; return the content-addressed receipt — the SAME receipt for a retry with the same key and plan (no second order), trade.idempotency_conflict for the same key with another plan, trade.grant_expired for an expired grant. With `observations`, the open orders meet the market through the engines' own fill path. Top-level fills/events are only this call’s new deltas; the submission receipt is immutable. `recovery: { fills, events }` contains all persisted normalized fills and reproducible ledger envelopes for this receipt’s orders, including this call’s fills. Retry after a lost response and apply recovery.events with portfolio.record_events; identical events fold once. Recovery grows with later fills without replaying the fill engine. The journal continues transactionally from the required journal store under `<sourceId>:journal`; retries must retain that store and source. A grant atomically records its exact prepared submission before journal commit: a retry with the same key into the same store/journal recovers those events and reads the same receipt; any other submission of the grant is trade.grant_consumed. Every journal write recovers earlier pending submissions before allocating new identities. Inline history must match persisted history exactly. Inline grants must exist unchanged in the trusted authorization store. Paper only; requires trade:paper. Opt-in (tradePack).

Version: 1; pack: trade; profiles: `full`; defaultEnabled: false; SDKonly: false.

Required capabilities: `trade:paper`. Authorization: policy. Side effect: external-order. Idempotency: required.

Handle fields: none. Cost: small. Cancellation supported: false. Deterministic: true. Stochastic: false.

Annotations: {"readOnlyHint":false,"destructiveHint":true,"idempotentHint":true,"openWorldHint":true}


Input JSON Schema:
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "plan": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "kind": {
          "const": "totalfinance.execution-plan",

        },
        "schemaVersion": {
          "const": 1,
          "type": "number"
        },
        "accountId": {
          "type": "string",
          "minLength": 1
        },
        "asOf": {
          "type": "number",
          "description": "Epoch milliseconds"
        },
        "baseCurrency": {
          "type": "string",
          "pattern": "^[A-Z]{3}$"
        },
        "portfolioId": {
          "type": "string",
          "minLength": 1
        },
        "orders": {
          "type": "array",
          "items": {
            "$ref": "#/$defs/Orders"
          },
          "minItems": 1,
          "maxItems": 1000
```

### totalfinance.valuation.company

Value a company from its statements

Project the three statements from explicit drivers, take the free cash flows the valuation basis needs, and discount them under the stated conventions (basis, date, currency, the REQUIRED discount rate, compounding, day count, the terminal value method, the enterprise-to-equity bridge). The result is discountedCashFlowFromStatements(...) verbatim — the projection with its balance-sheet reconciliation, the cash flows used, and the valuation — plus discountedCashFlowSensitivityTable(...) over the same flows when a sensitivity request is supplied. Opt-in (valuationPack).

Version: 1; pack: valuation; profiles: `full`, `valuation`; defaultEnabled: false; SDKonly: false.

Required capabilities: none. Authorization: none. Side effect: none. Idempotency: not-applicable.

Handle fields: none. Cost: medium. Cancellation supported: false. Deterministic: true. Stochastic: false.

Annotations: {"readOnlyHint":true,"destructiveHint":false,"idempotentHint":true,"openWorldHint":false}

### totalfinance.volatility.event

Event-volatility decomposition (earnings)

Decompose pre-event implied volatility into base + event variance and the implied one-day event move (the earnings-move read): eventMove = √max(0, atmVolatility²·timeToExpiryYears − baseVolatility²·timeToExpiryYears). Optionally reports the variance risk premium when `realizedVolatility` is supplied.

Version: 1; pack: volatility; profiles: `default`, `full`, `options`, `strategies`; defaultEnabled: true; SDKonly: false.

Required capabilities: none. Authorization: none. Side effect: none. Idempotency: not-applicable.

Handle fields: none. Cost: small. Cancellation supported: false. Deterministic: true. Stochastic: false.

Annotations: {"readOnlyHint":true,"destructiveHint":false,"idempotentHint":true,"openWorldHint":false}


Input JSON Schema:
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "atmVolatility": {
      "type": "number",
      "exclusiveMinimum": 0,
      "description": "Total ATM implied volatility into the event (decimal)"
    },
    "baseVolatility": {
      "type": "number",
      "description": "Baseline (non-event) vol, e.g. post-event or far-month IV (decimal, ≥ 0)"
    },
    "timeToExpiryYears": {
      "type": "number",
      "exclusiveMinimum": 0,
      "description": "Time to expiry in years, e.g. 5/365"
    },
    "realizedVolatility": {
      "type": "number",
      "exclusiveMinimum": 0,
      "description": "ANNUALIZED realized volatility (decimal, e.g. 0.18 — a per-bar σ × √252 on daily bars) — adds the variance risk premium"
    }
  },
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "required": [
    "atmVolatility",
    "baseVolatility",
    "timeToExpiryYears"
  ]
}
```

### totalfinance.volatility.expected_move

Expected move (1σ)

Compute the expected 1-sigma move of the underlying by expiry — the lognormal ±1σ band and the expected absolute move. Provide `impliedVolatility` + `timeToExpiryYears` to imply it from volatility, or `straddlePrice` to imply it from the ATM straddle. Risk-neutral, not a directional forecast.

Version: 1; pack: volatility; profiles: `default`, `full`, `options`, `strategies`; defaultEnabled: true; SDKonly: false.

Required capabilities: none. Authorization: none. Side effect: none. Idempotency: not-applicable.

### totalfinance.volatility.surface

The surface never fabricates: non-convergence and extrapolation are reported in diagnostics/warnings.

Version: 1; pack: volatility; profiles: `default`, `full`, `options`, `strategies`; defaultEnabled: true; SDKonly: false.

Required capabilities: none. Authorization: none. Side effect: none. Idempotency: not-applicable.

Handle fields: none. Cost: small. Cancellation supported: false. Deterministic: true. Stochastic: false.

Annotations: {"readOnlyHint":true,"destructiveHint":false,"idempotentHint":true,"openWorldHint":false}

## Packages and public API

Every import path has its own export identity. Repeated declarations refer to an identical documented declaration. Type-only declarations are not callable JavaScript values. Named member types refer to the corresponding declarations in this catalog. Member lists have no count cap. Namespaces and callable companions expand; requests and returned artifacts expose their fields and method signatures. Named exported contracts use their own declarations rather than recursively duplicating every method-return graph; non-exported data shapes expand until a recursive type reference.

Version: 0.1.2; stability: pre-1.0; component maturity varies (see stability policy).

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance#CreditTriangleHazardInput

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

The credit-triangle approximation of the hazard rate implied by a flat par spread:
`λ ≈ spread / (1 − recovery)`. Exact only in the continuous-premium, flat-curve limit. Returns a
Law-2 envelope: the hazard in `value` plus the recovery assumption and a warnings channel.

```typescript
/**
 * The credit-triangle approximation of the hazard rate implied by a flat par spread:
 * `λ ≈ spread / (1 − recovery)`. Exact only in the continuous-premium, flat-curve limit. Returns a
 * Law-2 envelope: the hazard in `value` plus the recovery assumption and a warnings channel.
 */
export interface CreditTriangleHazardInput {
    spread: number;
    recovery?: number;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- recovery?: number; default: not declared
- spread: number; default: not declared

```typescript
/**
```

```typescript
/** Input for {@link exposure}: the chain, market and convention, plus an optional metric selection. */
export interface ExposureInput<S extends readonly ExposureMetric[] | undefined = undefined> extends ExposureShortcutInput {
    /**
     * The exposures to compute, e.g. `['gex']` or `['gex', 'dex', 'vanna']`. Omit it for the full
     * profile (every metric, exactly as before). A selection — explicit, nonempty, each name once —
     * computes only those metrics and the Black–Scholes outputs they need, and is echoed in
     * `assumptions.metrics`; uncomputed metrics are absent from the result, never zero.

}
```

- config.defaultMultiplier?: number; default: not declared — Contract multiplier when a quote omits one (default 100).
- config.gammaUnit?: GammaUnit; default: not declared — `per1PercentMove` (default, the spec GEX formula) or `perPoint`.
- config.minTimeToExpiry?: number; default: not declared — Skip contracts with time-to-expiry below this many years (default 0).
- config.priceSource?: PriceSource; default: not declared
- market: ExposureMarket; default: not declared

- market.dividendYield?: number; default: not declared — Continuous dividend yield; defaults to 0 when omitted.
- market.riskFreeRate: number; default: not declared
- market.spot?: number; default: not declared — Spot price. Falls back to each quote's `underlyingPrice` when omitted.
- metrics?: S; default: not declared — The exposures to compute, e.g. `['gex']` or `['gex', 'dex', 'vanna']`. Omit it for the full
profile (every metric, exactly as before). A selection — explicit, nonempty, each name once —
computes only those metrics and the Black–Scholes outputs they need, and is echoed in

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance#GarchForecastInput

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Multi-step GARCH(1,1) variance forecast. The `h`-step-ahead conditional variance mean-reverts
geometrically to the long-run variance: `σ²ₜ₊ₕ = LRV + (α+β)^h · (σ²ₜ − LRV)`. Because `0 < α+β < 1`,
the path moves monotonically toward `LRV`; a forecast started exactly at `LRV` stays flat.

```typescript
/**
 * Multi-step GARCH(1,1) variance forecast. The `h`-step-ahead conditional variance mean-reverts
 * geometrically to the long-run variance: `σ²ₜ₊ₕ = LRV + (α+β)^h · (σ²ₜ − LRV)`. Because `0 < α+β < 1`,
 * the path moves monotonically toward `LRV`; a forecast started exactly at `LRV` stays flat.
 */
export interface GarchForecastInput {
    fit: GarchFit;
    lastVariance: number;
    horizonPeriods: number;
    options?: GarchForecastOptions;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- fit: GarchFit; default: not declared
- fit.alpha: number; default: not declared — ARCH coefficient on the lagged squared return (`≥ 0`).
- fit.assumptions: { conventionsVersion: string; mean: 'zero' | 'sample'; observations: number; initialParameters: 'supplied' | 'default'; }; default: not declared — Applied conventions, echoed (Law 2 report grammar).
- fit.assumptions.conventionsVersion: string; default: not declared
- fit.assumptions.initialParameters: 'supplied' | 'default'; default: not declared — Whether the primary start was caller-supplied (`initialParameters`) or the classic (0.05, 0.90).
- fit.assumptions.mean: 'zero' | 'sample'; default: not declared
- fit.assumptions.observations: number; default: not declared
- fit.beta: number; default: not declared — GARCH coefficient on the lagged conditional variance (`≥ 0`).
- fit.converged: boolean; default: not declared — Whether the optimizer converged (never fabricated).
- fit.diagnostics: { warnings: QuantWarning[]; }; default: not declared — Structured warnings; a degenerate / non-converged fit explains itself here.
- fit.diagnostics.warnings: QuantWarning[]; default: not declared
- fit.iterations: number; default: not declared — Optimizer iterations performed.
- fit.logLikelihood: number | null; default: not declared — Maximized Gaussian log-likelihood; `null` when the likelihood is degenerate (disclosed).
- fit.longRunVariance: number; default: not declared — Unconditional variance `ω / (1 − α − β)` the forecast mean-reverts to.
- fit.omega: number; default: not declared — Constant term of the variance recursion (`> 0`).
- fit.persistence: number; default: not declared — `α + β` — the variance half-life driver; `< 1` for a stationary fit.
- horizonPeriods: number; default: not declared
- lastVariance: number; default: not declared
- options?: GarchForecastOptions; default: not declared
- options.periodsPerYear?: number; default: not declared — Periods per year for annualization (default 252 trading days).

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance#HestonPriceRequest

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

One cohesive request for the validated Heston COS pricer or IV bridge.

```typescript
/** One cohesive request for the validated Heston COS pricer or IV bridge. */
export interface HestonPriceRequest {
    type: OptionType;
    input: HestonInput;
    parameters: HestonParameters;
    options?: HestonCosineExpansionOptions;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- input: HestonInput; default: not declared
- input.dividendYield?: number; default: not declared
- input.riskFreeRate: number; default: not declared
- input.spot: number; default: not declared
- input.strike: number; default: not declared
- input.timeToExpiryYears: number; default: not declared — Time to expiry in years.
- options?: HestonCosineExpansionOptions; default: not declared
- options.extendedGreeks?: boolean; default: not declared — Compute the full higher-order (extended) Greek set (implies `greeks`). Volatility Greeks (vega, vanna, …)
are w.r.t. the **vol level** — `√v₀` and `√θ` bumped together — extending the `vega` convention. The
COS price is accurate, so the finite differences are converged (verified stable across term counts).
- options.greeks?: boolean; default: not declared — Compute Greeks by finite differences (default `true`).
- options.terms?: number; default: not declared — Number of cosine terms (default 256, maximum 8,192; COS converges exponentially).
- options.truncation?: number; default: not declared — Truncation width in standard deviations (default 12).
- parameters: HestonParameters; default: not declared
- parameters.kappa: number; default: not declared — Mean-reversion speed κ.
- parameters.rho: number; default: not declared — Spot/variance correlation ρ ∈ [−1, 1].
- parameters.sigma: number; default: not declared — Volatility of variance ξ ("vol of vol").
- parameters.theta: number; default: not declared — Long-run variance θ.
- parameters.v0: number; default: not declared — Initial instantaneous variance v₀ (= σ₀²).
- type: OptionType; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance#KellyInput

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Kelly-optimal weights (`Σ⁻¹μ`, optionally fractional/normalized).

```typescript
/** Kelly-optimal weights (`Σ⁻¹μ`, optionally fractional/normalized). */
export interface KellyInput {
    /** Dense stored-data ArrayLike; values are snapshotted without coercion. */
    mean: ArrayLike<number>;
    covariance: Matrix;
    options?: KellyOptions;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- covariance: Matrix; default: not declared
- mean: ArrayLike<number>; default: not declared — Dense stored-data ArrayLike; values are snapshotted without coercion.
- options?: KellyOptions; default: not declared
- options.bounds?: [number, number][]; default: not declared — Per-asset `[lo, hi]` bounds.
- options.budget?: number; default: not declared — Sum-to budget (`Σw`). Default 1 (fully invested).
- options.fraction?: number; default: not declared — Fraction of full Kelly (e.g. 0.5 for half-Kelly). Must be > 0. Default 1.
- options.groups?: GroupConstraint[]; default: not declared — Sector/group exposure caps (`min ≤ Σ_group w ≤ max`).
- options.longOnly?: boolean; default: not declared — Forbid short positions (`w ≥ 0`). Ignored where `bounds` is given.
- options.maximumIterations?: number; default: not declared — Projected-gradient iteration cap. Default 5000.
- options.normalize?: boolean; default: not declared — Normalize the Kelly weights to the `budget` (fully invested). Default false (leverage implied).
When the raw Kelly weights sum to ≤ 0 (a net-short growth-optimal book), dividing by that total
would flip every position's sign — instead the UNnormalized weights are returned with
`converged: false` and a `risk.kelly_negative_sum` warning (design law #4: disclose, don't flip).
With `constraints`, this flag is a no-op: the constrained solve already pins Σw to the budget.
- options.tolerance?: number; default: not declared — Projected-gradient convergence tolerance on the weight step. Default 1e-11.
- options.transactionCosts?: { perUnitTurnover: number | number[]; previousWeights: number[]; }; default: not declared — Linear transaction cost charged on the trade away from a base portfolio. Subtracted from the
objective as `Σ perUnitTurnover_i·|w_i − previousWeights_i|` (a scalar applies to every asset). Needs `previousWeights`.
- options.transactionCosts.perUnitTurnover: number | number[]; default: not declared
- options.transactionCosts.previousWeights: number[]; default: not declared
- options.turnover?: TurnoverConstraint; default: not declared — Turnover budget against a base portfolio (`Σ|w − previousWeights| ≤ max`).
- options.turnover.max: number; default: not declared — Maximum one-way + reverse (L1) turnover allowed.
- options.turnover.previousWeights: number[]; default: not declared — Current weights to measure turnover against.

Named `riskFreeRatePerPeriod` (renamed from `riskFreeRate` pre-1.0) because every other

silently subtracted a 4%-per-DAY hurdle, turning every excess return negative and dropping
maxSharpe into its min-variance fallback. One spelling per unit: the compiler now catches it.

- options.turnover?: TurnoverConstraint; default: not declared — Turnover budget against a base portfolio (`Σ|w − previousWeights| ≤ max`).

```typescript
export interface ScenarioGridInput {
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- greeks.color?: number; default: not declared — Accepted from a whole `ExtendedGreeks`; not used by the second-order expansion.
- greeks.delta?: number; default: not declared — ∂V/∂S per $1 of spot.
- greeks.deltaRate?: number; default: not declared — ∂²V/∂S∂r per $ per 1% rate — the spot-rate cross (`∂Δ/∂r`). Optional.
- greeks.gamma?: number; default: not declared — ∂²V/∂S² per $1².
- greeks.lambda?: number | null; default: not declared — Accepted from a whole `ExtendedGreeks` (`null` = elasticity undefined); not used by the expansion.
- greeks.phi?: number; default: not declared — φ = ∂V/∂q per 1% dividend yield — the options package's `phi` (dividend rho). Optional.
- greeks.rho?: number; default: not declared — ∂V/∂r per 1% rate (0.01), as the options package reports it.
- greeks.rhoConvexity?: number; default: not declared — ∂²V/∂r² per (1%)² — rho convexity. Optional.
- greeks.speed?: number; default: not declared — Accepted from a whole `ExtendedGreeks`; not used by the second-order expansion.
- greeks.spot?: number; default: not declared — Reference spot, required to resolve percent spot shocks into price moves.
- greeks.theta?: number; default: not declared — ∂V/∂t per CALENDAR DAY (negative for a long option), as the options package reports it.
- greeks.thetaConvexity?: number; default: not declared — ∂²V/∂t² per calendar day² — theta convexity (theta's own bleed). Optional.
- greeks.thetaRate?: number; default: not declared — ∂²V/∂t∂r per calendar day per 1% rate — the time-rate cross (`∂Θ/∂r`). Optional.
- greeks.ultima?: number; default: not declared — Accepted from a whole `ExtendedGreeks`; not used by the second-order expansion.
- greeks.value: number; default: not declared — Current mark value of the position (per unit).
- greeks.vanna?: number; default: not declared — ∂²V/∂S∂σ per 1.00 σ per $ — the options package's `vanna`. Optional — omitted ⇒ its term is 0.
- greeks.vega?: number; default: not declared — ∂V/∂σ per 1 volatility point (0.01), as the options package reports it.
- greeks.vera?: number; default: not declared — ∂²V/∂σ∂r per 1.00 σ per 1.00 rate — the options package's `vera`. Optional.
- greeks.veta?: number; default: not declared — ∂vega/∂T per year of time-to-expiry, vega per 1.00 σ — the options package's `veta`. Optional.
- greeks.vomma?: number; default: not declared — ∂²V/∂σ² per 1.00 σ² — the options package's `vomma`. Optional.
- greeks.zomma?: number; default: not declared — Accepted from a whole `ExtendedGreeks`; not used by the second-order expansion.
- spotShocks: readonly Shock[]; default: not declared
- volatilityShocks: readonly Shock[]; default: not declared

- surface.impliedVolatilityByDelta(callDelta): number; default: not declared
- surface.impliedVolatilityByDelta(expiry): string | number; default: not declared

(forward-moneyness) when `forward` is set — so `impliedVolatilityByMoneyness(1, e)` is the at-the-money(-forward) vol.

For a NUMERIC `expiry` (a maturity in years) the forward is computed AT THAT MATURITY,
`F(t) = spot·e^{(r−q)·t}` — not borrowed from the nearest fitted slice, which anchored a
mid-expiry query to a neighbour's forward and shifted the ATM-forward point off by the carry
between them.

- surface.impliedVolatilityByMoneyness(options)?: { forward?: boolean; }; default: not declared
- surface.impliedVolatilityByMoneyness(options).forward?: boolean; default: not declared
- surface.lookup: (strike: number, expiry: string | number) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SurfaceLookup; default: not declared — Implied vol at `(strike, expiry)` with diagnostics. Strike uses the per-slice smile; expiry
interpolates total variance linearly between the two bracketing slices. `extrapolated` is true
when the query lies outside the fitted strike range or expiry range.
- surface.lookup().return.assumptions: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Assumptions<Record<never, never>>; default: not declared — Every applied convention, echoed back.
- surface.lookup().return.diagnostics: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Diagnostics; default: not declared — How the value was computed, plus any warnings.
- surface.lookup().return.extrapolated: boolean; default: not declared
- surface.lookup().return.provenance?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Provenance; default: not declared — Optional data lineage when the inputs came from a provider.
- surface.lookup().return.value: number; default: not declared — The computed value. Never `NaN` or `±Infinity`: a value the model cannot produce is `null`
beside a diagnostic that says why (Law 7 — a warning never licenses a non-finite number).
- surface.lookup(expiry): string | number; default: not declared
- surface.lookup(strike): number; default: not declared
- surface.model: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SurfaceModel; default: not declared
- surface.points: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SurfacePoint[]; default: not declared
- surface.shock: (shifts: { parallel?: number; skewTilt?: number; }, { sticky }?: { sticky?: 'strike' | 'moneyness'; }) => VolatilitySurface; default: not declared — Return a NEW surface with a shifted vol structure, produced WITHOUT re-fitting: each stored IV
sample gains a `parallel` offset plus a `skewTilt · k` skew rotation (`k = ln(K/forward)`,
log-moneyness), the per-slice deltas are recomputed from the shifted IVs, and only the
interpolators are rebuilt. The shock is echoed in the new surface's `assumptions.shock`.

`sticky`: `'strike'` (default) pins the tilt to each stored strike's own log-moneyness vs the slice
forward; `'moneyness'` lets the same additive shift travel with moneyness. Because the shift is
applied to the stored strike-indexed IV samples, both modes coincide at the stored strikes in this
eager v1 — the distinction only matters once a surface is re-anchored to a new spot/forward, which
this method does not do; the requested mode is recorded in `assumptions.shock.sticky` so a caller
that later re-anchors knows how the tilt was meant to travel.

Parametric models (`svi`/`sabr`/`heston`) have no closed-form shock, so the current smile is SAMPLED
at each slice's stored strikes, those samples are shifted, and the result DEGRADES to
`'interpolated'` with a `volatility.shock_degraded_to_interpolated` `warn` — the parametric fit is not
re-fit. Non-parametric models (`raw`/`interpolated`/`smoothed`) are preserved.
- surface.shock(__1)?: { sticky?: 'strike' | 'moneyness'; }; default: not declared
- surface.shock(__1).sticky?: 'strike' | 'moneyness'; default: not declared
- surface.shock(shifts): { parallel?: number; skewTilt?: number; }; default: not declared
- surface.shock(shifts).parallel?: number; default: not declared
- surface.shock(shifts).skewTilt?: number; default: not declared
- surface.slice: (expiry: string | number) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SurfaceSlice | undefined; default: not declared — The smile at an expiry (exact label or nearest by `t`), or `undefined` if none.
- surface.slice().return.deltas: number[]; default: not declared — Call-delta `e^{−qt}·N(d1)` at each strike (the smile's delta axis, for skew lookups).
- surface.slice().return.essvi?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').ESSVIParameters; default: not declared — The globally-calibrated eSSVI parameters when `model: 'essvi'` (shared across all slices).
- surface.slice().return.expiry: string; default: not declared
- surface.slice().return.forward: number; default: not declared — Forward `S·e^{(r−q)t}`.
- surface.slice().return.heston?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/options').HestonParameters; default: not declared — The globally-calibrated Heston parameters when `model: 'heston'` (shared across all slices).
- surface.slice().return.impliedVolatilities: number[]; default: not declared
- surface.slice().return.sabr?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/options').SabrParameters; default: not declared — Fitted SABR parameters when `model: 'sabr'` (absent if the slice fell back to interpolation).
- surface.slice().return.ssvi?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SSVIParameters; default: not declared — The globally-calibrated SSVI parameters when `model: 'ssvi'` (shared across all slices).
- surface.slice().return.strikes: number[]; default: not declared
- surface.slice().return.svi?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SVIParameters; default: not declared — Fitted raw-SVI parameters when `model: 'svi'` (absent if the slice fell back to interpolation).
- surface.slice().return.timeToExpiryYears: number; default: not declared — Time to expiry in years (ACT/365F).
- surface.slice(expiry): string | number; default: not declared

- surface.ssvi?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SSVIParameters; default: not declared — The global SSVI parameters when `model: 'ssvi'`, else `undefined`.
- surface.ssvi.phi: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SSVIPhi; default: not declared — Curvature function.
- surface.ssvi.phi.eta: number; default: not declared
- surface.ssvi.phi.gamma: number; default: not declared
- surface.ssvi.phi.kind: ('heston') | ('power-law'); default: not declared
- surface.ssvi.phi.lambda: number; default: not declared
- surface.ssvi.rho: number; default: not declared — Global skew `ρ ∈ (−1, 1)`.
- surface.ssvi.thetaTerm: { timeToExpiryYears: number; theta: number; }[]; default: not declared — ATM total-variance knots `(t, θ)`, strictly increasing in both (calendar-arbitrage-free).
- surface.toJSON: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').VolatilitySurfaceSnapshot; default: not declared — Serialize the surface to a plain, JSON-safe {@link VolatilitySurfaceSnapshot} (no closures). Restore it
with {@link VolatilitySurface.fromJSON}; the pair round-trips `iv()` identically on all six models.
- surface.toJSON().return.assumptions: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Assumptions<{ shock?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SurfaceShock; }>; default: not declared
- surface.toJSON().return.config: { riskFreeRate: number; dividendYield: number; sabrBeta: number; sabrVolatilityType: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/options').SabrVolatilityType; smoothingBandwidth?: number; cosineExpansionTerms: number; }; default: not declared — Config knobs needed to rebuild the per-slice interpolators without re-solving from quotes.
- surface.toJSON().return.config.cosineExpansionTerms: number; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance#VolatilitySurfaceInput

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

```typescript
export interface VolatilitySurfaceInput {
    quotes: OptionQuote[];
    market: SurfaceMarket;
    config?: SurfaceConfig;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- config?: SurfaceConfig; default: not declared
- config.cosineExpansionTerms?: number; default: not declared — COS cosine-term count for the `model: 'heston'` calibration & evaluation (default 128).
- config.essviPhi?: 'power-law' | 'heston'; default: not declared — Curvature family for the global `model: 'essvi'` calibration (default `'power-law'`).
- config.essviWeight?: 'vega' | 'uniform'; default: not declared — Least-squares weighting for `model: 'essvi'`: `'uniform'` (default) or `'vega'` (ATM-dominant).
- config.hestonInitialParameters?: Partial<HestonParameters>; default: not declared — Warm start (partial pin) for the global `model: 'heston'` calibration — threads into `calibrateHestonSurface`'s `initialParameters`.
- config.hestonInitialParameters.kappa?: number; default: not declared — Mean-reversion speed κ.
- config.hestonInitialParameters.rho?: number; default: not declared — Spot/variance correlation ρ ∈ [−1, 1].
- config.hestonInitialParameters.sigma?: number; default: not declared — Volatility of variance ξ ("vol of vol").
- config.hestonInitialParameters.theta?: number; default: not declared — Long-run variance θ.
- config.hestonInitialParameters.v0?: number; default: not declared — Initial instantaneous variance v₀ (= σ₀²).
- config.minQuotesPerExpiry?: number; default: not declared — Below this many usable strikes, an expiry slice is flagged sparse (default 3).
- config.model?: SurfaceModel; default: not declared — `interpolated` (PCHIP, default), `raw` (linear), `smoothed` (Gaussian kernel), `svi`/`sabr`
(parametric per expiry), `ssvi` (one global arbitrage-free surface SVI), `essvi` (SSVI with a
per-maturity skew), or `heston` (one global stochastic-vol model fit to the whole surface).
- config.priceSource?: PriceSource; default: not declared — Which quote price to invert when a quote has no `impliedVolatility` (default `mid`).
- config.sabrBeta?: number; default: not declared — SABR backbone exponent β ∈ [0, 1] for `model: 'sabr'` (default 0.5).
- config.sabrVolatilityType?: SabrVolatilityType; default: not declared — SABR Hagan expansion for `model: 'sabr'` (default `'lognormal'`).
- config.smoothingBandwidth?: number; default: not declared — Gaussian-kernel bandwidth (in log-moneyness) for `model: 'smoothed'` (default auto).
- config.ssviPhi?: 'power-law' | 'heston'; default: not declared — Curvature family for the global `model: 'ssvi'` calibration (default `'power-law'`).
- config.ssviWeight?: 'vega' | 'uniform'; default: not declared — Least-squares weighting for `model: 'ssvi'`: `'uniform'` (default) or `'vega'` (ATM-dominant).
- market: SurfaceMarket; default: not declared
- market.asOf: string | number; default: not declared — Snapshot time: epoch ms, `'YYYY-MM-DD'`, or a ZONED ISO datetime — one grammar for "when"
across every package. Each boundary resolves it once via core `resolveAsOf` (zone-less
datetimes are rejected with a teaching error; TotalFinance never reads the machine clock or zone).
- market.dividendYield?: number; default: not declared — Continuous dividend yield; defaults to 0 when omitted.
- market.riskFreeRate: number; default: not declared
- market.spot?: number; default: not declared — Spot price. Falls back to each quote's `underlyingPrice` when omitted.
- quotes: OptionQuote[]; default: not declared

(time value) by more than `threshold·strike`. Only used when `assignment: 'model'`.

- createPortfolioStepper: (request: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/backtest').PortfolioStepperRequest) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/backtest').PortfolioStepper; default: not declared — The engine's seam (Stage 7B.1, Decision 2): the same per-instant loop `portfolioBacktest` runs,
driven from outside. `open(index)` stamps the clock, folds pre-open entitlements and external
flows, and returns a pre-execution context valued at opening or last-completed marks (the mark
source identifies carried prices). `close(index, orders)` executes the caller's orders through
the execution policy, settles close-derived derivative lifecycle, runs the margin check, records the valuation mark and the equity,
and returns the rows the step appended; `finish()` assembles the same result `portfolioBacktest`
returns over the instants closed so far. Calls must alternate `open(0)`, `close(0)`, `open(1)`, …
— an out-of-order call refuses and changes nothing; `finish()` may be called again and returns
the same result. The orders come from the caller, so the
result records `strategy: { kind: 'external', replayable: false }`; a trading environment saves
its own action trace to make an episode replayable.
- createPortfolioStepper().return.close: (index: number, orders: readonly import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/backtest/execution').OrderIntent[]) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/backtest').PortfolioStepFrame; default: not declared — The orders through the execution policy, the margin check, the valuation mark, the equity.
