- meanExcessPlot: (returns: ArrayLike<number>, options?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk').MeanExcessPlotOptions) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk').MeanExcessPlot; default: not declared — The **mean-excess plot** — the standard tool for choosing the EVT peaks-over-threshold cutoff the rest of
the pack takes as an input. The mean-excess `e(u) = E[X − u | X > u]` is linear in `u` (slope `ξ/(1−ξ)`)
above the true tail threshold and non-linear below it, so the threshold is read off as where the curve
straightens. Returns the curve, a heuristic `suggestedThreshold`, the `tailIndexEstimate` from that
region's slope, and the `suggestedTailFraction` to hand to {@link fitGeneralizedParetoTail}. See
`docs/specs/mean-excess-plot.md`.

- meanExcessPlot().return.points: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk').MeanExcessPoint[]; default: not declared
- meanExcessPlot().return.suggestedTailFraction: number; default: not declared — `Nu(suggestedThreshold)/n` — hand to `fitGeneralizedParetoTail({ tailFraction })`.
- meanExcessPlot().return.suggestedThreshold: number; default: not declared — Heuristic tail-onset threshold — the lowest `u` above which `e(·)` is ~linear.
- meanExcessPlot().return.tailIndexEstimate: number; default: not declared — `ξ` from the slope over `[suggestedThreshold, uₘₐₓ]`: `ξ = slope/(1+slope)`.

- nakedPutMargin.explain(callArguments): [input: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk').NakedMarginInput, options?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk').NakedMarginOptions | undefined]; default: not declared
- optionsMargin: (legs: readonly import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk').OptionMarginLeg[], options: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk').OptionsMarginOptions) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk').OptionsMarginResult; default: not declared — Initial margin / buying-power for a single-underlying, single-expiry multi-leg option position
(spec §15.3, product review §6). The expiration payoff is piecewise-linear, so the requirement is:

 - **long only** (all legs bought): the net debit paid (fully-paid, no additional margin);
 - **covered defined risk** (every short leg is offset — verticals, condors, butterflies): the
   max loss;
 - **uncovered short puts** (more short put contracts than long ones): the Reg-T naked-put
   requirement on the uncovered contracts + the max loss of the rest. A short put's loss is
   *bounded* (the underlying stops at 0), but bounded is not the same as covered: charging the
   whole `(strike − premium)` exercise value margins a margin account as if it were
   cash-secured, ~4× the Reg-T requirement one function away (`nakedPutMargin`). Opt into the
   cash-secured basis for a cash/IRA account with `putMarginBasis: 'cash-secured'`;
 - **undefined risk** (a net-short call leaves the upside unbounded): the Reg-T naked requirement
   summed over the short legs — a conservative strategy-based approximation (a portfolio-margin
   engine would net offsets more finely).

Coverage is counted contract-for-contract per option type, pairing the highest strikes first, so
a 1×1 spread is covered and the extra short in a 2×1 ratio is not. `maxLoss` is unaffected by the
margin basis — it stays the position's true worst case at expiration.

Pure and clock-free; premiums, strikes, and the underlier are explicit inputs.
- optionsMargin().return.assumptions: { [k: string]: unknown; conventionsVersion: string; }; default: not declared — Applied conventions, echoed (Law 2 report grammar).
- optionsMargin().return.assumptions.conventionsVersion: string; default: not declared
- optionsMargin().return.buyingPowerReduction: number; default: not declared — Buying-power reduction — what the account must set aside. Equals `initialMargin` for margin
accounts; for a long-only (fully-paid) position it is the net debit paid.
- optionsMargin().return.definedRisk: boolean; default: not declared — True when the position's loss is capped (spreads / condors / butterflies / long options).
- optionsMargin().return.diagnostics: { warnings: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').QuantWarning[]; }; default: not declared — Structured warnings; always present (possibly empty).
- optionsMargin().return.diagnostics.warnings: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').QuantWarning[]; default: not declared
- optionsMargin().return.initialMargin: number; default: not declared — Initial margin / buying-power requirement, in account currency.
- optionsMargin().return.maxLoss: number | null; default: not declared — Worst-case expiration loss magnitude per contract; `null` when the loss is unbounded (e.g. a
naked call — no finite worst case exists; `Infinity` is not JSON-safe, Law 7). `definedRisk:
false` is the primary unbounded discriminant, and a `risk.unbounded_loss` warning explains the
null.
- optionsMargin().return.method: 'reg-t-naked' | 'defined-risk-max-loss' | 'reg-t-naked-put' | 'long-premium'; default: not declared — How the requirement was derived. `'reg-t-naked-put'` is the bounded-but-uncovered case: the
loss IS capped (a put's underlying stops at 0), but the position is short naked puts, so the
requirement is the Reg-T naked-put charge on the uncovered contracts plus the capped max loss
of whatever remains — not the cash-secured exercise value.
- optionsMargin().return.netDebit: number; default: not declared — Net debit paid (> 0) or credit received (< 0), per contract.

- optionsMargin(options).floorRate?: number; default: not declared — Reg-T naked floor rate — the % of underlying (calls) / strike (puts) minimum (default 0.10).
- optionsMargin(options).multiplier?: number; default: not declared — Contract multiplier (default 100).
- optionsMargin(options).putMarginBasis?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk/portfolio').PutMarginBasis; default: not declared — Basis for UNCOVERED short puts. Default `'reg-t-naked'` — a margin account's actual

- probabilityOfBacktestOverfitting: (returns: number[][], options?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk').BacktestOverfittingProbabilityOptions) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk').BacktestOverfittingProbabilityResult; default: not declared — **Probability of backtest overfitting** (Bailey & López de Prado's CSCV). Given a `T × N` matrix of
per-period returns — `T` time observations (rows) × `N` strategy configurations you selected among
(columns) — split the rows into `S` blocks, and over **every** `C(S, S/2)` symmetric partition into an
in-sample and an out-of-sample half: pick the IS-best configuration, then measure its OOS rank. PBO is
the fraction of splits where the IS winner lands **below the OOS median** — the probability that
picking the best backtest buys you a below-average live result. `≈ 0.5` means the selection is worthless
out of sample; `≈ 0` means a genuinely persistent edge. Depends only on `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core`/`math`.
- probabilityOfBacktestOverfitting().return.assumptions: { [k: string]: unknown; conventionsVersion: string; }; default: not declared — Applied conventions, echoed (Law 2 report grammar).
- probabilityOfBacktestOverfitting().return.assumptions.conventionsVersion: string; default: not declared
- probabilityOfBacktestOverfitting().return.backtestOverfittingProbability: number; default: not declared — Probability of backtest overfitting: the fraction of the `C(S, S/2)` symmetric train/test splits on
which the in-sample-best configuration ranks **below the out-of-sample median** (logit `λ < 0`). Near
`0.5` for noise (selection is worthless out of sample), near `0` for a genuinely persistent edge.
- probabilityOfBacktestOverfitting().return.combinations: number; default: not declared — Number of symmetric train/test splits evaluated: `C(S, S/2)`.
- probabilityOfBacktestOverfitting().return.diagnostics: { warnings: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').QuantWarning[]; }; default: not declared — Structured warnings; always present (possibly empty).
- probabilityOfBacktestOverfitting().return.diagnostics.warnings: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').QuantWarning[]; default: not declared
- probabilityOfBacktestOverfitting().return.medianLogit: number; default: not declared — Median logit `λ = ln(r̄/(1−r̄))` across the splits (`r̄` = OOS relative rank of the IS-best); `< 0` ⇒ overfit-leaning.
- probabilityOfBacktestOverfitting().return.observations: number; default: not declared — Observations (rows) used after trimming to a multiple of `S`.
- probabilityOfBacktestOverfitting().return.splits: number; default: not declared — Blocks `S` actually used.
- probabilityOfBacktestOverfitting().return.trials: number; default: not declared — Number of strategy configurations (columns) `N`.
- probabilityOfBacktestOverfitting(options)?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk').BacktestOverfittingProbabilityOptions; default: not declared
- probabilityOfBacktestOverfitting(options).splits?: number; default: not declared — Number of disjoint contiguous row-blocks `S` (even, `4 ≤ S ≤ 16`). Default `16` (Bailey & López de
Prado). The `C(S, S/2)` train/test splits grow fast in `S`; the observation count is trimmed to a
multiple of `S` (the oldest rows dropped).
- probabilityOfBacktestOverfitting(returns): number[][]; default: not declared

- shrunkKelly: (input: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk').ShrunkKellyInput) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk').ShrunkKelly; default: not declared — Estimation-error-shrunk portfolio Kelly. The plug-in weights `Σ̂⁻¹μ̂` overbet because `μ̂`/`Σ̂` are
estimated from a finite sample; this scales them by the growth-optimal factor
`c* = max(0, 1 − (n/T)/θ̂²)` (`θ̂² = μ̂ᵀΣ̂⁻¹μ̂`), returns a zero book when the estimated edge is
indistinguishable from sampling noise (`n/T ≥ θ̂²`), and discloses the biased-vs-corrected Sharpe and
the naive book's (often negative) expected out-of-sample growth. See `docs/specs/shrunk-kelly.md`.
- shrunkKelly().return.appliedScaling: number; default: not declared — The applied scaling `fraction · c*`.
- shrunkKelly().return.assumptions: { conventionsVersion: string; assets: number; sampleSize: number; fraction: number; }; default: not declared
- shrunkKelly().return.assumptions.assets: number; default: not declared
- shrunkKelly().return.assumptions.conventionsVersion: string; default: not declared
- shrunkKelly().return.assumptions.fraction: number; default: not declared
- shrunkKelly().return.assumptions.sampleSize: number; default: not declared

- shrunkKelly().return.diagnostics: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Diagnostics; default: not declared
- shrunkKelly().return.expectedGrowth: number; default: not declared — Expected out-of-sample log-growth at the applied scaling.
- shrunkKelly().return.inSampleSharpeSquared: number; default: not declared — In-sample squared Sharpe `θ̂² = μ̂ᵀΣ̂⁻¹μ̂` (biased high).
- shrunkKelly().return.naiveExpectedGrowth: number; default: not declared — Expected out-of-sample log-growth of the naive (unshrunk) book — often negative.

- shrunkKelly().return.shrinkage: number; default: not declared — Estimation-error shrinkage factor `c* ∈ [0, 1]`.

- valueAtRiskReport().return.assumptions.conventionsVersion: string; default: not declared

- valueAtRiskReport().return.diagnostics.warnings: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').QuantWarning[]; default: not declared

- valueAtRiskReport().return.method: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk').VaRMethod; default: not declared
- valueAtRiskReport().return.samples?: number; default: not declared — Monte-Carlo only: the number of simulated samples actually drawn.
- valueAtRiskReport().return.seed?: number; default: not declared — Monte-Carlo only: the PRNG seed actually used (echoed for reproducibility).

- valueAtRiskReport(options)?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk').VaROptions; default: not declared
- valueAtRiskReport(options).confidence?: number; default: not declared — Confidence level in (0, 1). Default 0.95.
- valueAtRiskReport(options).cornishFisher?: boolean; default: not declared — Parametric only: Cornish-Fisher adjustment for skew/excess-kurtosis. Default false. Applied
only where the expansion is a monotone quantile map; outside that domain the plain Gaussian
quantile is reported with a `risk.cornish_fisher_out_of_domain` warning and
`cornishFisher: false`. Over a multi-period `horizonPeriods` the moments are rescaled to the
horizon under iid aggregation (`skew/√h`, `excessKurtosis/h`), disclosed as
`assumptions.momentScaling: 'iid'`. On a non-parametric method it is ignored with an info
warning, never silently.
- valueAtRiskReport(options).horizonPeriods?: number; default: not declared — Holding-period horizonPeriods in periods; scales by √-time. Default 1.
- valueAtRiskReport(options).method?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk').VaRMethod; default: not declared — Estimation method. Default `'historical'`.
  - `'historical'` — the empirical (hyndman-fan-7) tail quantile of the sample;
  - `'parametric'` — the Gaussian quantile of the fitted (μ, σ), optionally Cornish-Fisher;
  - `'monteCarlo'` — draws from the **fitted NORMAL** and takes its empirical tail. It captures
    no non-normality whatsoever (same two moments as `'parametric'`, plus sampling noise), so
    prefer `'parametric'` unless you specifically want sampling diagnostics; use
    `'historical'` or the EVT tools when the shape of the tail matters.
- valueAtRiskReport(options).samples?: number; default: not declared — Monte-Carlo only: number of simulated paths. Default 10000.
- valueAtRiskReport(options).seed?: number; default: not declared — Monte-Carlo only: PRNG seed for reproducibility. Default 1.
- valueAtRiskReport(returns): ArrayLike<number>; default: not declared
- walkForwardSplits: (observationCount: number, options: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk').WalkForwardOptions) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk').Split[]; default: not declared — Generate walk-forward (rolling or anchored) train/test splits over `n` ordered observations.
- walkForwardSplits(observationCount): number; default: not declared
- walkForwardSplits(options): import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk').WalkForwardOptions; default: not declared
- walkForwardSplits(options).mode?: 'rolling' | 'anchored'; default: not declared — `rolling` (sliding train window) or `anchored` (train always starts at 0). Default `rolling`.
- walkForwardSplits(options).step?: number; default: not declared — Step between successive folds (default `testSize`).
- walkForwardSplits(options).testSize: number; default: not declared — Test window length.
- walkForwardSplits(options).trainSize: number; default: not declared — Training window length (in observations).

- Position().return.value: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketResult; default: not declared — Mark-to-market value, P&L, per-leg and aggregate Greeks via BSM (spec §12.3).
- Position().return.whatIfCube: (options?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeOptions) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeResult; default: not declared — A what-if **cube**: the position marked over the full spot × vol-shock × days-forward grid, plus
the **optimal-exit surface** — for each (spot, vol) outcome, the day along the time axis that
optimizes P&L (`max-pnl` by default, or `min-pnl`). `scenarioTable` extended a dimension: it returns
a navigable cube (axes + row-major cells) with the reductions a trader wants, not a flat row list.

Every cell is a `value()` mark (time-aware, per-leg-IV, shock-through-to-leg-IV), so calendars and
per-leg volatilities behave identically. The optimal-exit surface is a CONDITIONAL what-if ("if the
underlying is here with this vol shock, which day marks best?"), not a path-dependent stopping rule.
See `docs/specs/what-if-cube.md`.

per leg: `leg.expiry` > `expiry` > `market.expiry` (R4).
- Position(config).market?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumMarket; default: not declared — Market for model-priced entry premiums (required when `premiums: 'model'` and any leg omits its
premium) — AND the position's remembered market (R5): `probability()`, `monteCarloProbability()`,
`value()`, `scenarioTable()`, and `chartData()` use it as their default market, with per-call
fields merged over it. Results echo `marketSource: 'construction' | 'call' | 'merged'`.
- Position(config).multiplier?: number; default: not declared — Contract multiplier for option legs (default 100).
- Position(config).premiums?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumSource; default: not declared — Entry-premium source: `'user'` (from the leg inputs, default) or `'model'` (priced from `market`).
- Position(legs): readonly LegInput[]; default: not declared
- SCAN_OBJECTIVES: readonly ['probabilityOfProfit', 'expectedValue', 'returnOnRisk', 'expectedValuePerRisk']; default: not declared — Every ranking objective a scan accepts, as DATA — the single source the type, the runtime guard and
the error message are all derived from.

RV11 — these were three copies: a hand-written union here, a hand-written array in `optimizer.ts`,
and a third hand-written list inside the error string. The string copy drifted and kept teaching
`pop|ev` after both were renamed, because plain prose is invisible to a rename of the quoted
literals. One tuple, and `.join(', ')` for the message, is what makes that impossible rather than
merely fixed.

`'return'` became `'returnOnRisk'` in the same pass: it ranked by `returnOnRisk` and the candidate
output already called that number `returnOnRisk`, so one quantity carried two public names.

- bearCallLadder().return.payoff: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffResult; default: not declared — Expiration payoff metrics plus a chart-ready grid of points (spec §12.2). `prices` is an explicit
grid array or a `{ from, to, steps }` range; omit it to frame the strike-derived default window
(the same one a payoff diagram draws).
- bearCallLadder().return.pnlAtExpiry: (underlyingPrice: number) => number; default: not declared — Expiration P&L at an underlying price.
- bearCallLadder().return.premiumSource: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumSource; default: not declared — How the entry premiums were sourced: `'user'` (supplied) or `'model'` (priced from `market`).
- bearCallLadder().return.premiumVolatilitySource?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumVolatilitySource; default: not declared — When modeled, which volatility priced the entries (`'leg'`, `'position'` or `'mixed'`).
- bearCallLadder().return.probability: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMetrics; default: not declared — Probability & scenario metrics (spec §12.6): probability of profit, expected value, reward/risk,
and the probability of touching each breakeven — under an explicit, echoed lognormal model.
- bearCallLadder().return.scenarioTable: (options?: { market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; volatilityShocks?: number[]; daysForward?: number[]; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ScenarioTableResult; default: not declared — Scenario table (spec §12.6): mark-to-market P&L and Greeks across a grid of underlying prices,
additive vol shocks, and days forward — the standard "what-if" matrix for an options ticket.
- bearCallLadder().return.value: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketResult; default: not declared — Mark-to-market value, P&L, per-leg and aggregate Greeks via BSM (spec §12.3).
- bearCallLadder().return.whatIfCube: (options?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeOptions) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeResult; default: not declared — A what-if **cube**: the position marked over the full spot × vol-shock × days-forward grid, plus
the **optimal-exit surface** — for each (spot, vol) outcome, the day along the time axis that
optimizes P&L (`max-pnl` by default, or `min-pnl`). `scenarioTable` extended a dimension: it returns
a navigable cube (axes + row-major cells) with the reductions a trader wants, not a flat row list.

Every cell is a `value()` mark (time-aware, per-leg-IV, shock-through-to-leg-IV), so calendars and
per-leg volatilities behave identically. The optimal-exit surface is a CONDITIONAL what-if ("if the
underlying is here with this vol shock, which day marks best?"), not a path-dependent stopping rule.
See `docs/specs/what-if-cube.md`.
- bearCallLadder(config)?: PositionConfig | undefined; default: not declared
- bearCallLadder(config).expiry?: string; default: not declared — Position-level default expiry (`YYYY-MM-DD` → 16:00 ET, or a datetime) applied to every leg
that has no `expiry` of its own. Named builders route their input's `expiry` here. Precedence
per leg: `leg.expiry` > `expiry` > `market.expiry` (R4).
- bearCallLadder(config).market?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumMarket; default: not declared — Market for model-priced entry premiums (required when `premiums: 'model'` and any leg omits its
premium) — AND the position's remembered market (R5): `probability()`, `monteCarloProbability()`,
`value()`, `scenarioTable()`, and `chartData()` use it as their default market, with per-call
fields merged over it. Results echo `marketSource: 'construction' | 'call' | 'merged'`.
- bearCallLadder(config).multiplier?: number; default: not declared — Contract multiplier for option legs (default 100).
- bearCallLadder(config).premiums?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumSource; default: not declared — Entry-premium source: `'user'` (from the leg inputs, default) or `'model'` (priced from `market`).
- bearCallLadder(input): import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').LadderInput; default: not declared
- bearCallLadder(input).expiry?: string; default: not declared — Expiry applied to every leg of this structure (`YYYY-MM-DD` → 16:00 ET, or a datetime).
- bearCallLadder(input).lower: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').Role; default: not declared
- bearCallLadder(input).middle: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').Role; default: not declared
- bearCallLadder(input).quantity?: number; default: not declared — Number of structures (default 1). Every leg scales by this.
- bearCallLadder(input).upper: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').Role; default: not declared
- bearCallSpread: (input: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').VerticalInput, config?: PositionConfig) => Position; default: not declared
- bearCallSpread().return.assumptions: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PositionAssumptions; default: not declared — Position-construction assumptions (design law #3): whether the entry premiums were supplied by
the caller (`'user'`) or model-priced from a market (`'model'`), plus the contract multiplier.
- bearCallSpread().return.chartData: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; include?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ChartInclude; market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; }) => Array<{ underlyingPrice: number; expirationPnl?: number; currentPnl?: number; delta?: number; theta?: number; }>; default: not declared — Chart-ready output (spec §12.5). Current P&L / live Greeks need a market: per-call fields
merge over the construction market (R5), so a model-premium position charts with no `market`.
- bearCallSpread().return.constructedAs?: string; default: not declared — PROVENANCE, not identity (dx §4.5): the named builder that constructed this position, absent
for raw `strategy(legs)`. Because positions are immutable this can never go stale — but a
rebuilt-after-tweak position has no name. For "what is this NOW?" use `classifyStrategy`.
- bearCallSpread().return.legs: readonly Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').Leg>[]; default: not declared — The resolved legs — a frozen snapshot (deep-copied at construction, `Object.freeze`d per leg
and as an array). A Position is immutable by design: to tweak a strategy, edit your own leg
list and rebuild with `strategy(editedLegs, config)` — every downstream calculation is generic
over the legs, so the rebuilt position needs no named builder. Mutating this array throws
instead of silently diverging from `assumptions()`/cached results.
- bearCallSpread().return.market?: Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumMarket>; default: not declared — The market this position was built with, if any — a frozen copy (R5), so mutating the caller's
market object later never silently retargets the position. `probability()`, `value()`,
`scenarioTable()`, and `chartData()` default to it; per-call fields merge over it.
- bearCallSpread().return.market.asOf: string | number; default: not declared — Entry time (epoch ms or ISO). Each leg's entry `t = yearFraction(asOf, leg.expiry ?? market.expiry)`.
- bearCallSpread().return.market.dividendYield?: number; default: not declared
- bearCallSpread().return.market.expiry?: string; default: not declared — Default expiry for legs without their own `expiry` (single-expiry structures).
- bearCallSpread().return.market.riskFreeRate: number; default: not declared
- bearCallSpread().return.market.spot: number; default: not declared
- bearCallSpread().return.market.volatility: number; default: not declared — Entry implied volatility (annualized decimal) for unpriced legs that carry no `impliedVolatility`
of their own — a leg's own volatility always wins, exactly as it does when `value()` marks it.
- bearCallSpread().return.metrics: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffMetrics; default: not declared — Net debit/credit, max profit/loss, and breakevens. The expiration payoff is piecewise-linear, so
these are computed ANALYTICALLY from the kink set (every option strike plus every stock entry
price) and the tail slopes — never by sampling a coarse grid, which missed breakevens beyond the
last strike (e.g. a lone long stock, or a deep-ITM option) and ignored stock entry prices.
- bearCallSpread().return.monteCarloProbability: (overrides: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloInput> & { seed: number; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloMetrics; default: not declared — Monte-Carlo probability metrics (spec §12.6): the simulated analogue of {@link probability}, for
cross-validation and path-dependent reads. Terminal lognormal paths give the probability of profit
and expected P&L (with a standard error); the probability of touching each breakeven is estimated
with the Brownian-bridge continuous-monitoring correction. Seeded and deterministic.

- bearPutSpread().return.metrics: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffMetrics; default: not declared — Net debit/credit, max profit/loss, and breakevens. The expiration payoff is piecewise-linear, so
these are computed ANALYTICALLY from the kink set (every option strike plus every stock entry
price) and the tail slopes — never by sampling a coarse grid, which missed breakevens beyond the
last strike (e.g. a lone long stock, or a deep-ITM option) and ignored stock entry prices.
- bearPutSpread().return.monteCarloProbability: (overrides: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloInput> & { seed: number; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloMetrics; default: not declared — Monte-Carlo probability metrics (spec §12.6): the simulated analogue of {@link probability}, for
cross-validation and path-dependent reads. Terminal lognormal paths give the probability of profit
and expected P&L (with a standard error); the probability of touching each breakeven is estimated
with the Brownian-bridge continuous-monitoring correction. Seeded and deterministic.
- bearPutSpread().return.multiplier: number; default: not declared
- bearPutSpread().return.netDebit: () => number; default: not declared — Net cash to enter (positive = debit, negative = credit).
- bearPutSpread().return.payoff: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffResult; default: not declared — Expiration payoff metrics plus a chart-ready grid of points (spec §12.2). `prices` is an explicit
grid array or a `{ from, to, steps }` range; omit it to frame the strike-derived default window
(the same one a payoff diagram draws).
- bearPutSpread().return.pnlAtExpiry: (underlyingPrice: number) => number; default: not declared — Expiration P&L at an underlying price.
- bearPutSpread().return.premiumSource: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumSource; default: not declared — How the entry premiums were sourced: `'user'` (supplied) or `'model'` (priced from `market`).
- bearPutSpread().return.premiumVolatilitySource?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumVolatilitySource; default: not declared — When modeled, which volatility priced the entries (`'leg'`, `'position'` or `'mixed'`).
- bearPutSpread().return.probability: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMetrics; default: not declared — Probability & scenario metrics (spec §12.6): probability of profit, expected value, reward/risk,
and the probability of touching each breakeven — under an explicit, echoed lognormal model.
- bearPutSpread().return.scenarioTable: (options?: { market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; volatilityShocks?: number[]; daysForward?: number[]; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ScenarioTableResult; default: not declared — Scenario table (spec §12.6): mark-to-market P&L and Greeks across a grid of underlying prices,
additive vol shocks, and days forward — the standard "what-if" matrix for an options ticket.
- bearPutSpread().return.value: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketResult; default: not declared — Mark-to-market value, P&L, per-leg and aggregate Greeks via BSM (spec §12.3).
- bearPutSpread().return.whatIfCube: (options?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeOptions) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeResult; default: not declared — A what-if **cube**: the position marked over the full spot × vol-shock × days-forward grid, plus
the **optimal-exit surface** — for each (spot, vol) outcome, the day along the time axis that
optimizes P&L (`max-pnl` by default, or `min-pnl`). `scenarioTable` extended a dimension: it returns
a navigable cube (axes + row-major cells) with the reductions a trader wants, not a flat row list.

Every cell is a `value()` mark (time-aware, per-leg-IV, shock-through-to-leg-IV), so calendars and
per-leg volatilities behave identically. The optimal-exit surface is a CONDITIONAL what-if ("if the
underlying is here with this vol shock, which day marks best?"), not a path-dependent stopping rule.
See `docs/specs/what-if-cube.md`.

that has no `expiry` of its own. Named builders route their input's `expiry` here. Precedence
per leg: `leg.expiry` > `expiry` > `market.expiry` (R4).
- bearPutSpread(config).market?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumMarket; default: not declared — Market for model-priced entry premiums (required when `premiums: 'model'` and any leg omits its
premium) — AND the position's remembered market (R5): `probability()`, `monteCarloProbability()`,
`value()`, `scenarioTable()`, and `chartData()` use it as their default market, with per-call
fields merged over it. Results echo `marketSource: 'construction' | 'call' | 'merged'`.

- bearPutSpread(config).premiums?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumSource; default: not declared — Entry-premium source: `'user'` (from the leg inputs, default) or `'model'` (priced from `market`).

- bullCallSpread().return.monteCarloProbability: (overrides: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloInput> & { seed: number; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloMetrics; default: not declared — Monte-Carlo probability metrics (spec §12.6): the simulated analogue of {@link probability}, for
cross-validation and path-dependent reads. Terminal lognormal paths give the probability of profit
and expected P&L (with a standard error); the probability of touching each breakeven is estimated
with the Brownian-bridge continuous-monitoring correction. Seeded and deterministic.
- bullCallSpread().return.multiplier: number; default: not declared
- bullCallSpread().return.netDebit: () => number; default: not declared — Net cash to enter (positive = debit, negative = credit).
- bullCallSpread().return.payoff: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffResult; default: not declared — Expiration payoff metrics plus a chart-ready grid of points (spec §12.2). `prices` is an explicit
grid array or a `{ from, to, steps }` range; omit it to frame the strike-derived default window
(the same one a payoff diagram draws).
- bullCallSpread().return.pnlAtExpiry: (underlyingPrice: number) => number; default: not declared — Expiration P&L at an underlying price.

- bullCallSpread().return.premiumVolatilitySource?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumVolatilitySource; default: not declared — When modeled, which volatility priced the entries (`'leg'`, `'position'` or `'mixed'`).
- bullCallSpread().return.probability: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMetrics; default: not declared — Probability & scenario metrics (spec §12.6): probability of profit, expected value, reward/risk,
and the probability of touching each breakeven — under an explicit, echoed lognormal model.
- bullCallSpread().return.scenarioTable: (options?: { market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; volatilityShocks?: number[]; daysForward?: number[]; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ScenarioTableResult; default: not declared — Scenario table (spec §12.6): mark-to-market P&L and Greeks across a grid of underlying prices,
additive vol shocks, and days forward — the standard "what-if" matrix for an options ticket.
- bullCallSpread().return.value: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketResult; default: not declared — Mark-to-market value, P&L, per-leg and aggregate Greeks via BSM (spec §12.3).
- bullCallSpread().return.whatIfCube: (options?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeOptions) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeResult; default: not declared — A what-if **cube**: the position marked over the full spot × vol-shock × days-forward grid, plus
the **optimal-exit surface** — for each (spot, vol) outcome, the day along the time axis that
optimizes P&L (`max-pnl` by default, or `min-pnl`). `scenarioTable` extended a dimension: it returns
a navigable cube (axes + row-major cells) with the reductions a trader wants, not a flat row list.

Every cell is a `value()` mark (time-aware, per-leg-IV, shock-through-to-leg-IV), so calendars and
per-leg volatilities behave identically. The optimal-exit surface is a CONDITIONAL what-if ("if the
underlying is here with this vol shock, which day marks best?"), not a path-dependent stopping rule.
See `docs/specs/what-if-cube.md`.

that has no `expiry` of its own. Named builders route their input's `expiry` here. Precedence
per leg: `leg.expiry` > `expiry` > `market.expiry` (R4).

`value()`, `scenarioTable()`, and `chartData()` use it as their default market, with per-call
fields merged over it. Results echo `marketSource: 'construction' | 'call' | 'merged'`.

- calendarCallSpread().return.market.expiry?: string; default: not declared — Default expiry for legs without their own `expiry` (single-expiry structures).
- calendarCallSpread().return.market.riskFreeRate: number; default: not declared
- calendarCallSpread().return.market.spot: number; default: not declared
- calendarCallSpread().return.market.volatility: number; default: not declared — Entry implied volatility (annualized decimal) for unpriced legs that carry no `impliedVolatility`
of their own — a leg's own volatility always wins, exactly as it does when `value()` marks it.
- calendarCallSpread().return.metrics: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffMetrics; default: not declared — Net debit/credit, max profit/loss, and breakevens. The expiration payoff is piecewise-linear, so
these are computed ANALYTICALLY from the kink set (every option strike plus every stock entry
price) and the tail slopes — never by sampling a coarse grid, which missed breakevens beyond the
last strike (e.g. a lone long stock, or a deep-ITM option) and ignored stock entry prices.
- calendarCallSpread().return.monteCarloProbability: (overrides: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloInput> & { seed: number; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloMetrics; default: not declared — Monte-Carlo probability metrics (spec §12.6): the simulated analogue of {@link probability}, for
cross-validation and path-dependent reads. Terminal lognormal paths give the probability of profit
and expected P&L (with a standard error); the probability of touching each breakeven is estimated
with the Brownian-bridge continuous-monitoring correction. Seeded and deterministic.
- calendarCallSpread().return.multiplier: number; default: not declared
- calendarCallSpread().return.netDebit: () => number; default: not declared — Net cash to enter (positive = debit, negative = credit).
- calendarCallSpread().return.payoff: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffResult; default: not declared — Expiration payoff metrics plus a chart-ready grid of points (spec §12.2). `prices` is an explicit
grid array or a `{ from, to, steps }` range; omit it to frame the strike-derived default window
(the same one a payoff diagram draws).
- calendarCallSpread().return.pnlAtExpiry: (underlyingPrice: number) => number; default: not declared — Expiration P&L at an underlying price.
- calendarCallSpread().return.premiumSource: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumSource; default: not declared — How the entry premiums were sourced: `'user'` (supplied) or `'model'` (priced from `market`).
- calendarCallSpread().return.premiumVolatilitySource?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumVolatilitySource; default: not declared — When modeled, which volatility priced the entries (`'leg'`, `'position'` or `'mixed'`).
- calendarCallSpread().return.probability: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMetrics; default: not declared — Probability & scenario metrics (spec §12.6): probability of profit, expected value, reward/risk,
and the probability of touching each breakeven — under an explicit, echoed lognormal model.
- calendarCallSpread().return.scenarioTable: (options?: { market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; volatilityShocks?: number[]; daysForward?: number[]; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ScenarioTableResult; default: not declared — Scenario table (spec §12.6): mark-to-market P&L and Greeks across a grid of underlying prices,
additive vol shocks, and days forward — the standard "what-if" matrix for an options ticket.
- calendarCallSpread().return.value: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketResult; default: not declared — Mark-to-market value, P&L, per-leg and aggregate Greeks via BSM (spec §12.3).
- calendarCallSpread().return.whatIfCube: (options?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeOptions) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeResult; default: not declared — A what-if **cube**: the position marked over the full spot × vol-shock × days-forward grid, plus
the **optimal-exit surface** — for each (spot, vol) outcome, the day along the time axis that
optimizes P&L (`max-pnl` by default, or `min-pnl`). `scenarioTable` extended a dimension: it returns
a navigable cube (axes + row-major cells) with the reductions a trader wants, not a flat row list.

Every cell is a `value()` mark (time-aware, per-leg-IV, shock-through-to-leg-IV), so calendars and
per-leg volatilities behave identically. The optimal-exit surface is a CONDITIONAL what-if ("if the
underlying is here with this vol shock, which day marks best?"), not a path-dependent stopping rule.
See `docs/specs/what-if-cube.md`.
- calendarCallSpread(config)?: PositionConfig | undefined; default: not declared
- calendarCallSpread(config).expiry?: string; default: not declared — Position-level default expiry (`YYYY-MM-DD` → 16:00 ET, or a datetime) applied to every leg
that has no `expiry` of its own. Named builders route their input's `expiry` here. Precedence
per leg: `leg.expiry` > `expiry` > `market.expiry` (R4).
- calendarCallSpread(config).market?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumMarket; default: not declared — Market for model-priced entry premiums (required when `premiums: 'model'` and any leg omits its
premium) — AND the position's remembered market (R5): `probability()`, `monteCarloProbability()`,
`value()`, `scenarioTable()`, and `chartData()` use it as their default market, with per-call
fields merged over it. Results echo `marketSource: 'construction' | 'call' | 'merged'`.
- calendarCallSpread(config).multiplier?: number; default: not declared — Contract multiplier for option legs (default 100).
- calendarCallSpread(config).premiums?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumSource; default: not declared — Entry-premium source: `'user'` (from the leg inputs, default) or `'model'` (priced from `market`).

- callRatioBackspread().return.constructedAs?: string; default: not declared — PROVENANCE, not identity (dx §4.5): the named builder that constructed this position, absent
for raw `strategy(legs)`. Because positions are immutable this can never go stale — but a
rebuilt-after-tweak position has no name. For "what is this NOW?" use `classifyStrategy`.
- callRatioBackspread().return.legs: readonly Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').Leg>[]; default: not declared — The resolved legs — a frozen snapshot (deep-copied at construction, `Object.freeze`d per leg
and as an array). A Position is immutable by design: to tweak a strategy, edit your own leg
list and rebuild with `strategy(editedLegs, config)` — every downstream calculation is generic
over the legs, so the rebuilt position needs no named builder. Mutating this array throws
instead of silently diverging from `assumptions()`/cached results.
- callRatioBackspread().return.market?: Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumMarket>; default: not declared — The market this position was built with, if any — a frozen copy (R5), so mutating the caller's
market object later never silently retargets the position. `probability()`, `value()`,
`scenarioTable()`, and `chartData()` default to it; per-call fields merge over it.
- callRatioBackspread().return.market.asOf: string | number; default: not declared — Entry time (epoch ms or ISO). Each leg's entry `t = yearFraction(asOf, leg.expiry ?? market.expiry)`.
- callRatioBackspread().return.market.dividendYield?: number; default: not declared
- callRatioBackspread().return.market.expiry?: string; default: not declared — Default expiry for legs without their own `expiry` (single-expiry structures).
- callRatioBackspread().return.market.riskFreeRate: number; default: not declared
- callRatioBackspread().return.market.spot: number; default: not declared
- callRatioBackspread().return.market.volatility: number; default: not declared — Entry implied volatility (annualized decimal) for unpriced legs that carry no `impliedVolatility`
of their own — a leg's own volatility always wins, exactly as it does when `value()` marks it.
- callRatioBackspread().return.metrics: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffMetrics; default: not declared — Net debit/credit, max profit/loss, and breakevens. The expiration payoff is piecewise-linear, so
these are computed ANALYTICALLY from the kink set (every option strike plus every stock entry
price) and the tail slopes — never by sampling a coarse grid, which missed breakevens beyond the
last strike (e.g. a lone long stock, or a deep-ITM option) and ignored stock entry prices.
- callRatioBackspread().return.monteCarloProbability: (overrides: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloInput> & { seed: number; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloMetrics; default: not declared — Monte-Carlo probability metrics (spec §12.6): the simulated analogue of {@link probability}, for
cross-validation and path-dependent reads. Terminal lognormal paths give the probability of profit
and expected P&L (with a standard error); the probability of touching each breakeven is estimated
with the Brownian-bridge continuous-monitoring correction. Seeded and deterministic.
- callRatioBackspread().return.multiplier: number; default: not declared
- callRatioBackspread().return.netDebit: () => number; default: not declared — Net cash to enter (positive = debit, negative = credit).
- callRatioBackspread().return.payoff: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffResult; default: not declared — Expiration payoff metrics plus a chart-ready grid of points (spec §12.2). `prices` is an explicit
grid array or a `{ from, to, steps }` range; omit it to frame the strike-derived default window
(the same one a payoff diagram draws).
- callRatioBackspread().return.pnlAtExpiry: (underlyingPrice: number) => number; default: not declared — Expiration P&L at an underlying price.
- callRatioBackspread().return.premiumSource: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumSource; default: not declared — How the entry premiums were sourced: `'user'` (supplied) or `'model'` (priced from `market`).
- callRatioBackspread().return.premiumVolatilitySource?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumVolatilitySource; default: not declared — When modeled, which volatility priced the entries (`'leg'`, `'position'` or `'mixed'`).
- callRatioBackspread().return.probability: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMetrics; default: not declared — Probability & scenario metrics (spec §12.6): probability of profit, expected value, reward/risk,
and the probability of touching each breakeven — under an explicit, echoed lognormal model.
- callRatioBackspread().return.scenarioTable: (options?: { market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; volatilityShocks?: number[]; daysForward?: number[]; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ScenarioTableResult; default: not declared — Scenario table (spec §12.6): mark-to-market P&L and Greeks across a grid of underlying prices,
additive vol shocks, and days forward — the standard "what-if" matrix for an options ticket.
- callRatioBackspread().return.value: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketResult; default: not declared — Mark-to-market value, P&L, per-leg and aggregate Greeks via BSM (spec §12.3).
- callRatioBackspread().return.whatIfCube: (options?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeOptions) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeResult; default: not declared — A what-if **cube**: the position marked over the full spot × vol-shock × days-forward grid, plus
the **optimal-exit surface** — for each (spot, vol) outcome, the day along the time axis that
optimizes P&L (`max-pnl` by default, or `min-pnl`). `scenarioTable` extended a dimension: it returns
a navigable cube (axes + row-major cells) with the reductions a trader wants, not a flat row list.

Every cell is a `value()` mark (time-aware, per-leg-IV, shock-through-to-leg-IV), so calendars and
per-leg volatilities behave identically. The optimal-exit surface is a CONDITIONAL what-if ("if the
underlying is here with this vol shock, which day marks best?"), not a path-dependent stopping rule.
See `docs/specs/what-if-cube.md`.

that has no `expiry` of its own. Named builders route their input's `expiry` here. Precedence
per leg: `leg.expiry` > `expiry` > `market.expiry` (R4).

fields merged over it. Results echo `marketSource: 'construction' | 'call' | 'merged'`.

    matches: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').StrategyMatch[];
    assumptions: {
        conventionsVersion: string;
        matching: 'structural-base-signature';
        tieBreaker: 'wing-gap-symmetry';
    };
    diagnostics: {
        warnings: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').QuantWarning[];
    };
}); default: not declared — Classify a leg list (or a Position) against the named-strategy catalog. `matches` carries every
matching name in manifest order — payoff-identical aliases all match — and is `[]` when the
structure matches nothing (a custom position; every calculation still works, it just has no name).
- classifyStrategy().return.assumptions: { conventionsVersion: string; matching: 'structural-base-signature'; tieBreaker: 'wing-gap-symmetry'; }; default: not declared — Applied conventions, echoed (Law 2 report grammar).
- classifyStrategy().return.assumptions.conventionsVersion: string; default: not declared
- classifyStrategy().return.assumptions.matching: 'structural-base-signature'; default: not declared — Identity is the structural base signature: (kind, sign, strike-rank, ratio, expiry-rank).
- classifyStrategy().return.assumptions.tieBreaker: 'wing-gap-symmetry'; default: not declared — Spacing splits base-signature collisions only (butterflies vs broken wings).
- classifyStrategy().return.diagnostics: { warnings: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').QuantWarning[]; }; default: not declared — Structured warnings; always present (possibly empty).

position (every calculation still works, it just has no name).

- classifyStrategy(input).chartData: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; include?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ChartInclude; market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; }) => Array<{ underlyingPrice: number; expirationPnl?: number; currentPnl?: number; delta?: number; theta?: number; }>; default: not declared — Chart-ready output (spec §12.5). - classifyStrategy(input).legs: readonly Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').Leg>[]; default: not declared — The resolved legs — a frozen snapshot (deep-copied at construction, `Object.freeze`d per leg

- classifyStrategy(input).metrics: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffMetrics; default: not declared — Net debit/credit, max profit/loss, and breakevens. The expiration payoff is piecewise-linear, so
these are computed ANALYTICALLY from the kink set (every option strike plus every stock entry
price) and the tail slopes — never by sampling a coarse grid, which missed breakevens beyond the
last strike (e.g. a lone long stock, or a deep-ITM option) and ignored stock entry prices.
- classifyStrategy(input).monteCarloProbability: (overrides: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloInput> & { seed: number; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloMetrics; default: not declared — Monte-Carlo probability metrics (spec §12.6): the simulated analogue of {@link probability}, for
cross-validation and path-dependent reads. Terminal lognormal paths give the probability of profit
and expected P&L (with a standard error); the probability of touching each breakeven is estimated
with the Brownian-bridge continuous-monitoring correction. Seeded and deterministic.

- classifyStrategy(input).whatIfCube: (options?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeOptions) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeResult; default: not declared — A what-if **cube**: the position marked over the full spot × vol-shock × days-forward grid, plus
the **optimal-exit surface** — for each (spot, vol) outcome, the day along the time axis that
optimizes P&L (`max-pnl` by default, or `min-pnl`). `scenarioTable` extended a dimension: it returns
a navigable cube (axes + row-major cells) with the reductions a trader wants, not a flat row list.

Every cell is a `value()` mark (time-aware, per-leg-IV, shock-through-to-leg-IV), so calendars and
per-leg volatilities behave identically. The optimal-exit surface is a CONDITIONAL what-if ("if the
underlying is here with this vol shock, which day marks best?"), not a path-dependent stopping rule.
See `docs/specs/what-if-cube.md`.

- coveredShortStraddle().return.assumptions: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PositionAssumptions; default: not declared — Position-construction assumptions (design law #3): whether the entry premiums were supplied by
the caller (`'user'`) or model-priced from a market (`'model'`), plus the contract multiplier.
- coveredShortStraddle().return.chartData: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; include?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ChartInclude; market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; }) => Array<{ underlyingPrice: number; expirationPnl?: number; currentPnl?: number; delta?: number; theta?: number; }>; default: not declared — Chart-ready output (spec §12.5). Current P&L / live Greeks need a market: per-call fields
merge over the construction market (R5), so a model-premium position charts with no `market`.
- coveredShortStraddle().return.constructedAs?: string; default: not declared — PROVENANCE, not identity (dx §4.5): the named builder that constructed this position, absent
for raw `strategy(legs)`. Because positions are immutable this can never go stale — but a
rebuilt-after-tweak position has no name. For "what is this NOW?" use `classifyStrategy`.
- coveredShortStraddle().return.legs: readonly Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').Leg>[]; default: not declared — The resolved legs — a frozen snapshot (deep-copied at construction, `Object.freeze`d per leg
and as an array). A Position is immutable by design: to tweak a strategy, edit your own leg
list and rebuild with `strategy(editedLegs, config)` — every downstream calculation is generic
over the legs, so the rebuilt position needs no named builder. Mutating this array throws
instead of silently diverging from `assumptions()`/cached results.
- coveredShortStraddle().return.market?: Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumMarket>; default: not declared — The market this position was built with, if any — a frozen copy (R5), so mutating the caller's
market object later never silently retargets the position. `probability()`, `value()`,
`scenarioTable()`, and `chartData()` default to it; per-call fields merge over it.

- coveredShortStraddle().return.market.dividendYield?: number; default: not declared
- coveredShortStraddle().return.market.expiry?: string; default: not declared — Default expiry for legs without their own `expiry` (single-expiry structures).
- coveredShortStraddle().return.market.riskFreeRate: number; default: not declared
- coveredShortStraddle().return.market.spot: number; default: not declared
- coveredShortStraddle().return.market.volatility: number; default: not declared — Entry implied volatility (annualized decimal) for unpriced legs that carry no `impliedVolatility`
of their own — a leg's own volatility always wins, exactly as it does when `value()` marks it.
- coveredShortStraddle().return.metrics: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffMetrics; default: not declared — Net debit/credit, max profit/loss, and breakevens. The expiration payoff is piecewise-linear, so
these are computed ANALYTICALLY from the kink set (every option strike plus every stock entry
price) and the tail slopes — never by sampling a coarse grid, which missed breakevens beyond the
last strike (e.g. a lone long stock, or a deep-ITM option) and ignored stock entry prices.
- coveredShortStraddle().return.monteCarloProbability: (overrides: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloInput> & { seed: number; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloMetrics; default: not declared — Monte-Carlo probability metrics (spec §12.6): the simulated analogue of {@link probability}, for
cross-validation and path-dependent reads. Terminal lognormal paths give the probability of profit
and expected P&L (with a standard error); the probability of touching each breakeven is estimated
with the Brownian-bridge continuous-monitoring correction. Seeded and deterministic.
- coveredShortStraddle().return.multiplier: number; default: not declared
- coveredShortStraddle().return.netDebit: () => number; default: not declared — Net cash to enter (positive = debit, negative = credit).
- coveredShortStraddle().return.payoff: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffResult; default: not declared — Expiration payoff metrics plus a chart-ready grid of points (spec §12.2). `prices` is an explicit
grid array or a `{ from, to, steps }` range; omit it to frame the strike-derived default window
(the same one a payoff diagram draws).

- coveredShortStraddle().return.premiumVolatilitySource?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumVolatilitySource; default: not declared — When modeled, which volatility priced the entries (`'leg'`, `'position'` or `'mixed'`).
- coveredShortStraddle().return.probability: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMetrics; default: not declared — Probability & scenario metrics (spec §12.6): probability of profit, expected value, reward/risk,
and the probability of touching each breakeven — under an explicit, echoed lognormal model.
- coveredShortStraddle().return.scenarioTable: (options?: { market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; volatilityShocks?: number[]; daysForward?: number[]; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ScenarioTableResult; default: not declared — Scenario table (spec §12.6): mark-to-market P&L and Greeks across a grid of underlying prices,
additive vol shocks, and days forward — the standard "what-if" matrix for an options ticket.
- coveredShortStraddle().return.value: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketResult; default: not declared — Mark-to-market value, P&L, per-leg and aggregate Greeks via BSM (spec §12.3).
- coveredShortStraddle().return.whatIfCube: (options?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeOptions) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeResult; default: not declared — A what-if **cube**: the position marked over the full spot × vol-shock × days-forward grid, plus
the **optimal-exit surface** — for each (spot, vol) outcome, the day along the time axis that
optimizes P&L (`max-pnl` by default, or `min-pnl`). `scenarioTable` extended a dimension: it returns
a navigable cube (axes + row-major cells) with the reductions a trader wants, not a flat row list.

Every cell is a `value()` mark (time-aware, per-leg-IV, shock-through-to-leg-IV), so calendars and
per-leg volatilities behave identically. The optimal-exit surface is a CONDITIONAL what-if ("if the
underlying is here with this vol shock, which day marks best?"), not a path-dependent stopping rule.
See `docs/specs/what-if-cube.md`.

per leg: `leg.expiry` > `expiry` > `market.expiry` (R4).

`volatility` is a silent no-op for legs that fix their own implied volatility.

rebuilt-after-tweak position has no name. For "what is this NOW?" use `classifyStrategy`.
- explainPosition(position).legs: readonly Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').Leg>[]; default: not declared — The resolved legs — a frozen snapshot (deep-copied at construction, `Object.freeze`d per leg
and as an array). A Position is immutable by design: to tweak a strategy, edit your own leg
list and rebuild with `strategy(editedLegs, config)` — every downstream calculation is generic
over the legs, so the rebuilt position needs no named builder. Mutating this array throws
instead of silently diverging from `assumptions()`/cached results.
- explainPosition(position).market?: Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumMarket>; default: not declared — The market this position was built with, if any — a frozen copy (R5), so mutating the caller's
market object later never silently retargets the position. `probability()`, `value()`,
`scenarioTable()`, and `chartData()` default to it; per-call fields merge over it.
- explainPosition(position).market.asOf: string | number; default: not declared — Entry time (epoch ms or ISO). Each leg's entry `t = yearFraction(asOf, leg.expiry ?? market.expiry)`.
- explainPosition(position).market.dividendYield?: number; default: not declared
- explainPosition(position).market.expiry?: string; default: not declared — Default expiry for legs without their own `expiry` (single-expiry structures).
- explainPosition(position).market.riskFreeRate: number; default: not declared
- explainPosition(position).market.spot: number; default: not declared
- explainPosition(position).market.volatility: number; default: not declared — Entry implied volatility (annualized decimal) for unpriced legs that carry no `impliedVolatility`
of their own — a leg's own volatility always wins, exactly as it does when `value()` marks it.
- explainPosition(position).metrics: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffMetrics; default: not declared — Net debit/credit, max profit/loss, and breakevens. The expiration payoff is piecewise-linear, so
these are computed ANALYTICALLY from the kink set (every option strike plus every stock entry
price) and the tail slopes — never by sampling a coarse grid, which missed breakevens beyond the
last strike (e.g. a lone long stock, or a deep-ITM option) and ignored stock entry prices.
- explainPosition(position).monteCarloProbability: (overrides: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloInput> & { seed: number; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloMetrics; default: not declared — Monte-Carlo probability metrics (spec §12.6): the simulated analogue of {@link probability}, for
cross-validation and path-dependent reads. Terminal lognormal paths give the probability of profit
and expected P&L (with a standard error); the probability of touching each breakeven is estimated
with the Brownian-bridge continuous-monitoring correction. Seeded and deterministic.
- explainPosition(position).multiplier: number; default: not declared
- explainPosition(position).netDebit: () => number; default: not declared — Net cash to enter (positive = debit, negative = credit).
- explainPosition(position).payoff: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffResult; default: not declared — Expiration payoff metrics plus a chart-ready grid of points (spec §12.2). `prices` is an explicit
grid array or a `{ from, to, steps }` range; omit it to frame the strike-derived default window
(the same one a payoff diagram draws).
- explainPosition(position).pnlAtExpiry: (underlyingPrice: number) => number; default: not declared — Expiration P&L at an underlying price.
- explainPosition(position).premiumSource: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumSource; default: not declared — How the entry premiums were sourced: `'user'` (supplied) or `'model'` (priced from `market`).
- explainPosition(position).premiumVolatilitySource?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumVolatilitySource; default: not declared — When modeled, which volatility priced the entries (`'leg'`, `'position'` or `'mixed'`).
- explainPosition(position).probability: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMetrics; default: not declared — Probability & scenario metrics (spec §12.6): probability of profit, expected value, reward/risk,
and the probability of touching each breakeven — under an explicit, echoed lognormal model.
- explainPosition(position).scenarioTable: (options?: { market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; volatilityShocks?: number[]; daysForward?: number[]; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ScenarioTableResult; default: not declared — Scenario table (spec §12.6): mark-to-market P&L and Greeks across a grid of underlying prices,
additive vol shocks, and days forward — the standard "what-if" matrix for an options ticket.
- explainPosition(position).value: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketResult; default: not declared — Mark-to-market value, P&L, per-leg and aggregate Greeks via BSM (spec §12.3).
- explainPosition(position).whatIfCube: (options?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeOptions) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeResult; default: not declared — A what-if **cube**: the position marked over the full spot × vol-shock × days-forward grid, plus
the **optimal-exit surface** — for each (spot, vol) outcome, the day along the time axis that
optimizes P&L (`max-pnl` by default, or `min-pnl`). `scenarioTable` extended a dimension: it returns
a navigable cube (axes + row-major cells) with the reductions a trader wants, not a flat row list.

Every cell is a `value()` mark (time-aware, per-leg-IV, shock-through-to-leg-IV), so calendars and
per-leg volatilities behave identically. The optimal-exit surface is a CONDITIONAL what-if ("if the
underlying is here with this vol shock, which day marks best?"), not a path-dependent stopping rule.
See `docs/specs/what-if-cube.md`.

- inverseIronButterfly().return.market.asOf: string | number; default: not declared — Entry time (epoch ms or ISO). Each leg's entry `t = yearFraction(asOf, leg.expiry ?? market.expiry)`.
- inverseIronButterfly().return.market.dividendYield?: number; default: not declared
- inverseIronButterfly().return.market.expiry?: string; default: not declared — Default expiry for legs without their own `expiry` (single-expiry structures).
- inverseIronButterfly().return.market.riskFreeRate: number; default: not declared
- inverseIronButterfly().return.market.spot: number; default: not declared
- inverseIronButterfly().return.market.volatility: number; default: not declared — Entry implied volatility (annualized decimal) for unpriced legs that carry no `impliedVolatility`
of their own — a leg's own volatility always wins, exactly as it does when `value()` marks it.
- inverseIronButterfly().return.metrics: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffMetrics; default: not declared — Net debit/credit, max profit/loss, and breakevens. The expiration payoff is piecewise-linear, so
these are computed ANALYTICALLY from the kink set (every option strike plus every stock entry
price) and the tail slopes — never by sampling a coarse grid, which missed breakevens beyond the
last strike (e.g. a lone long stock, or a deep-ITM option) and ignored stock entry prices.
- inverseIronButterfly().return.monteCarloProbability: (overrides: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloInput> & { seed: number; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloMetrics; default: not declared — Monte-Carlo probability metrics (spec §12.6): the simulated analogue of {@link probability}, for
cross-validation and path-dependent reads. Terminal lognormal paths give the probability of profit
and expected P&L (with a standard error); the probability of touching each breakeven is estimated
with the Brownian-bridge continuous-monitoring correction. Seeded and deterministic.
- inverseIronButterfly().return.multiplier: number; default: not declared
- inverseIronButterfly().return.netDebit: () => number; default: not declared — Net cash to enter (positive = debit, negative = credit).
- inverseIronButterfly().return.payoff: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffResult; default: not declared — Expiration payoff metrics plus a chart-ready grid of points (spec §12.2). `prices` is an explicit
grid array or a `{ from, to, steps }` range; omit it to frame the strike-derived default window
(the same one a payoff diagram draws).

- inverseIronButterfly().return.probability: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMetrics; default: not declared — Probability & scenario metrics (spec §12.6): probability of profit, expected value, reward/risk,
and the probability of touching each breakeven — under an explicit, echoed lognormal model.
- inverseIronButterfly().return.scenarioTable: (options?: { market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; volatilityShocks?: number[]; daysForward?: number[]; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ScenarioTableResult; default: not declared — Scenario table (spec §12.6): mark-to-market P&L and Greeks across a grid of underlying prices,
additive vol shocks, and days forward — the standard "what-if" matrix for an options ticket.
- inverseIronButterfly().return.value: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketResult; default: not declared — Mark-to-market value, P&L, per-leg and aggregate Greeks via BSM (spec §12.3).
- inverseIronButterfly().return.whatIfCube: (options?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeOptions) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeResult; default: not declared — A what-if **cube**: the position marked over the full spot × vol-shock × days-forward grid, plus
the **optimal-exit surface** — for each (spot, vol) outcome, the day along the time axis that
optimizes P&L (`max-pnl` by default, or `min-pnl`). `scenarioTable` extended a dimension: it returns
a navigable cube (axes + row-major cells) with the reductions a trader wants, not a flat row list.

Every cell is a `value()` mark (time-aware, per-leg-IV, shock-through-to-leg-IV), so calendars and
per-leg volatilities behave identically. The optimal-exit surface is a CONDITIONAL what-if ("if the
underlying is here with this vol shock, which day marks best?"), not a path-dependent stopping rule.
See `docs/specs/what-if-cube.md`.
