- strategy.bearPutSpread().return.market.dividendYield?: number; default: not declared
- strategy.bearPutSpread().return.market.expiry?: string; default: not declared — Default expiry for legs without their own `expiry` (single-expiry structures).
- strategy.bearPutSpread().return.market.riskFreeRate: number; default: not declared
- strategy.bearPutSpread().return.market.spot: number; default: not declared
- strategy.bearPutSpread().return.market.volatility: number; default: not declared — Entry implied volatility (annualized decimal) for unpriced legs that carry no `impliedVolatility`
of their own — a leg's own volatility always wins, exactly as it does when `value()` marks it.
- strategy.bearPutSpread().return.metrics: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffMetrics; default: not declared — Net debit/credit, max profit/loss, and breakevens. The expiration payoff is piecewise-linear, so
these are computed ANALYTICALLY from the kink set (every option strike plus every stock entry
price) and the tail slopes — never by sampling a coarse grid, which missed breakevens beyond the
last strike (e.g. a lone long stock, or a deep-ITM option) and ignored stock entry prices.
- strategy.bearPutSpread().return.monteCarloProbability: (overrides: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloInput> & { seed: number; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloMetrics; default: not declared — Monte-Carlo probability metrics (spec §12.6): the simulated analogue of {@link probability}, for
cross-validation and path-dependent reads. Terminal lognormal paths give the probability of profit
and expected P&L (with a standard error); the probability of touching each breakeven is estimated
with the Brownian-bridge continuous-monitoring correction. Seeded and deterministic.
- strategy.bearPutSpread().return.multiplier: number; default: not declared
- strategy.bearPutSpread().return.netDebit: () => number; default: not declared — Net cash to enter (positive = debit, negative = credit).
- strategy.bearPutSpread().return.payoff: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffResult; default: not declared — Expiration payoff metrics plus a chart-ready grid of points (spec §12.2). `prices` is an explicit
grid array or a `{ from, to, steps }` range; omit it to frame the strike-derived default window
(the same one a payoff diagram draws).
- strategy.bearPutSpread().return.pnlAtExpiry: (underlyingPrice: number) => number; default: not declared — Expiration P&L at an underlying price.
- strategy.bearPutSpread().return.premiumSource: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumSource; default: not declared — How the entry premiums were sourced: `'user'` (supplied) or `'model'` (priced from `market`).
- strategy.bearPutSpread().return.premiumVolatilitySource?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumVolatilitySource; default: not declared — When modeled, which volatility priced the entries (`'leg'`, `'position'` or `'mixed'`).
- strategy.bearPutSpread().return.probability: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMetrics; default: not declared — Probability & scenario metrics (spec §12.6): probability of profit, expected value, reward/risk,
and the probability of touching each breakeven — under an explicit, echoed lognormal model.
- strategy.bearPutSpread().return.scenarioTable: (options?: { market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; volatilityShocks?: number[]; daysForward?: number[]; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ScenarioTableResult; default: not declared — Scenario table (spec §12.6): mark-to-market P&L and Greeks across a grid of underlying prices,
additive vol shocks, and days forward — the standard "what-if" matrix for an options ticket.
- strategy.bearPutSpread().return.value: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketResult; default: not declared — Mark-to-market value, P&L, per-leg and aggregate Greeks via BSM (spec §12.3).
- strategy.bearPutSpread().return.whatIfCube: (options?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeOptions) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeResult; default: not declared — A what-if **cube**: the position marked over the full spot × vol-shock × days-forward grid, plus
the **optimal-exit surface** — for each (spot, vol) outcome, the day along the time axis that
optimizes P&L (`max-pnl` by default, or `min-pnl`). `scenarioTable` extended a dimension: it returns
a navigable cube (axes + row-major cells) with the reductions a trader wants, not a flat row list.

Every cell is a `value()` mark (time-aware, per-leg-IV, shock-through-to-leg-IV), so calendars and
per-leg volatilities behave identically. The optimal-exit surface is a CONDITIONAL what-if ("if the
underlying is here with this vol shock, which day marks best?"), not a path-dependent stopping rule.
See `docs/specs/what-if-cube.md`.

- strategy.bullCallSpread().return.legs: readonly Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').Leg>[]; default: not declared — The resolved legs — a frozen snapshot (deep-copied at construction, `Object.freeze`d per leg
and as an array). A Position is immutable by design: to tweak a strategy, edit your own leg
list and rebuild with `strategy(editedLegs, config)` — every downstream calculation is generic
over the legs, so the rebuilt position needs no named builder. Mutating this array throws
instead of silently diverging from `assumptions()`/cached results.
- strategy.bullCallSpread().return.market?: Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumMarket>; default: not declared — The market this position was built with, if any — a frozen copy (R5), so mutating the caller's
market object later never silently retargets the position. `probability()`, `value()`,
`scenarioTable()`, and `chartData()` default to it; per-call fields merge over it.
- strategy.bullCallSpread().return.market.asOf: string | number; default: not declared — Entry time (epoch ms or ISO). Each leg's entry `t = yearFraction(asOf, leg.expiry ?? market.expiry)`.
- strategy.bullCallSpread().return.market.dividendYield?: number; default: not declared
- strategy.bullCallSpread().return.market.expiry?: string; default: not declared — Default expiry for legs without their own `expiry` (single-expiry structures).
- strategy.bullCallSpread().return.market.riskFreeRate: number; default: not declared
- strategy.bullCallSpread().return.market.spot: number; default: not declared
- strategy.bullCallSpread().return.market.volatility: number; default: not declared — Entry implied volatility (annualized decimal) for unpriced legs that carry no `impliedVolatility`
of their own — a leg's own volatility always wins, exactly as it does when `value()` marks it.
- strategy.bullCallSpread().return.metrics: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffMetrics; default: not declared — Net debit/credit, max profit/loss, and breakevens. The expiration payoff is piecewise-linear, so
these are computed ANALYTICALLY from the kink set (every option strike plus every stock entry
price) and the tail slopes — never by sampling a coarse grid, which missed breakevens beyond the
last strike (e.g. a lone long stock, or a deep-ITM option) and ignored stock entry prices.
- strategy.bullCallSpread().return.monteCarloProbability: (overrides: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloInput> & { seed: number; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloMetrics; default: not declared — Monte-Carlo probability metrics (spec §12.6): the simulated analogue of {@link probability}, for
cross-validation and path-dependent reads. Terminal lognormal paths give the probability of profit
and expected P&L (with a standard error); the probability of touching each breakeven is estimated
with the Brownian-bridge continuous-monitoring correction. Seeded and deterministic.
- strategy.bullCallSpread().return.multiplier: number; default: not declared
- strategy.bullCallSpread().return.netDebit: () => number; default: not declared — Net cash to enter (positive = debit, negative = credit).
- strategy.bullCallSpread().return.payoff: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffResult; default: not declared — Expiration payoff metrics plus a chart-ready grid of points (spec §12.2). `prices` is an explicit
grid array or a `{ from, to, steps }` range; omit it to frame the strike-derived default window
(the same one a payoff diagram draws).
- strategy.bullCallSpread().return.pnlAtExpiry: (underlyingPrice: number) => number; default: not declared — Expiration P&L at an underlying price.
- strategy.bullCallSpread().return.premiumSource: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumSource; default: not declared — How the entry premiums were sourced: `'user'` (supplied) or `'model'` (priced from `market`).
- strategy.bullCallSpread().return.premiumVolatilitySource?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumVolatilitySource; default: not declared — When modeled, which volatility priced the entries (`'leg'`, `'position'` or `'mixed'`).
- strategy.bullCallSpread().return.probability: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMetrics; default: not declared — Probability & scenario metrics (spec §12.6): probability of profit, expected value, reward/risk,
and the probability of touching each breakeven — under an explicit, echoed lognormal model.
- strategy.bullCallSpread().return.scenarioTable: (options?: { market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; volatilityShocks?: number[]; daysForward?: number[]; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ScenarioTableResult; default: not declared — Scenario table (spec §12.6): mark-to-market P&L and Greeks across a grid of underlying prices,
additive vol shocks, and days forward — the standard "what-if" matrix for an options ticket.
- strategy.bullCallSpread().return.value: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketResult; default: not declared — Mark-to-market value, P&L, per-leg and aggregate Greeks via BSM (spec §12.3).
- strategy.bullCallSpread().return.whatIfCube: (options?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeOptions) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeResult; default: not declared — A what-if **cube**: the position marked over the full spot × vol-shock × days-forward grid, plus
the **optimal-exit surface** — for each (spot, vol) outcome, the day along the time axis that
optimizes P&L (`max-pnl` by default, or `min-pnl`). `scenarioTable` extended a dimension: it returns
a navigable cube (axes + row-major cells) with the reductions a trader wants, not a flat row list.

Every cell is a `value()` mark (time-aware, per-leg-IV, shock-through-to-leg-IV), so calendars and
per-leg volatilities behave identically. The optimal-exit surface is a CONDITIONAL what-if ("if the
underlying is here with this vol shock, which day marks best?"), not a path-dependent stopping rule.
See `docs/specs/what-if-cube.md`.

that has no `expiry` of its own. Named builders route their input's `expiry` here. Precedence

fields merged over it. Results echo `marketSource: 'construction' | 'call' | 'merged'`.

- strategy.bullPutSpread(input).quantity?: number; default: not declared
- strategy.bullPutSpread(input).short: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').Role; default: not declared — The sold leg: a strike, or `{ strike, premium? }`.
- strategy.calendarCallSpread: (input: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').CalendarInput, config?: PositionConfig) => Position; default: not declared
- strategy.calendarCallSpread().return.assumptions: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PositionAssumptions; default: not declared — Position-construction assumptions (design law #3): whether the entry premiums were supplied by
the caller (`'user'`) or model-priced from a market (`'model'`), plus the contract multiplier.
- strategy.calendarCallSpread().return.chartData: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; include?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ChartInclude; market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; }) => Array<{ underlyingPrice: number; expirationPnl?: number; currentPnl?: number; delta?: number; theta?: number; }>; default: not declared — Chart-ready output (spec §12.5). Current P&L / live Greeks need a market: per-call fields
merge over the construction market (R5), so a model-premium position charts with no `market`.
- strategy.calendarCallSpread().return.constructedAs?: string; default: not declared — PROVENANCE, not identity (dx §4.5): the named builder that constructed this position, absent
for raw `strategy(legs)`. Because positions are immutable this can never go stale — but a
rebuilt-after-tweak position has no name. For "what is this NOW?" use `classifyStrategy`.
- strategy.calendarCallSpread().return.legs: readonly Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').Leg>[]; default: not declared — The resolved legs — a frozen snapshot (deep-copied at construction, `Object.freeze`d per leg
and as an array). A Position is immutable by design: to tweak a strategy, edit your own leg
list and rebuild with `strategy(editedLegs, config)` — every downstream calculation is generic
over the legs, so the rebuilt position needs no named builder. Mutating this array throws
instead of silently diverging from `assumptions()`/cached results.
- strategy.calendarCallSpread().return.market?: Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumMarket>; default: not declared — The market this position was built with, if any — a frozen copy (R5), so mutating the caller's
market object later never silently retargets the position. `probability()`, `value()`,
`scenarioTable()`, and `chartData()` default to it; per-call fields merge over it.
- strategy.calendarCallSpread().return.market.asOf: string | number; default: not declared — Entry time (epoch ms or ISO). Each leg's entry `t = yearFraction(asOf, leg.expiry ?? market.expiry)`.
- strategy.calendarCallSpread().return.market.dividendYield?: number; default: not declared
- strategy.calendarCallSpread().return.market.expiry?: string; default: not declared — Default expiry for legs without their own `expiry` (single-expiry structures).
- strategy.calendarCallSpread().return.market.riskFreeRate: number; default: not declared
- strategy.calendarCallSpread().return.market.spot: number; default: not declared
- strategy.calendarCallSpread().return.market.volatility: number; default: not declared — Entry implied volatility (annualized decimal) for unpriced legs that carry no `impliedVolatility`
of their own — a leg's own volatility always wins, exactly as it does when `value()` marks it.
- strategy.calendarCallSpread().return.metrics: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffMetrics; default: not declared — Net debit/credit, max profit/loss, and breakevens. The expiration payoff is piecewise-linear, so
these are computed ANALYTICALLY from the kink set (every option strike plus every stock entry
price) and the tail slopes — never by sampling a coarse grid, which missed breakevens beyond the
last strike (e.g. a lone long stock, or a deep-ITM option) and ignored stock entry prices.
- strategy.calendarCallSpread().return.monteCarloProbability: (overrides: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloInput> & { seed: number; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloMetrics; default: not declared — Monte-Carlo probability metrics (spec §12.6): the simulated analogue of {@link probability}, for
cross-validation and path-dependent reads. Terminal lognormal paths give the probability of profit
and expected P&L (with a standard error); the probability of touching each breakeven is estimated
with the Brownian-bridge continuous-monitoring correction. Seeded and deterministic.
- strategy.calendarCallSpread().return.multiplier: number; default: not declared
- strategy.calendarCallSpread().return.netDebit: () => number; default: not declared — Net cash to enter (positive = debit, negative = credit).
- strategy.calendarCallSpread().return.payoff: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffResult; default: not declared — Expiration payoff metrics plus a chart-ready grid of points (spec §12.2). `prices` is an explicit
grid array or a `{ from, to, steps }` range; omit it to frame the strike-derived default window
(the same one a payoff diagram draws).
- strategy.calendarCallSpread().return.pnlAtExpiry: (underlyingPrice: number) => number; default: not declared — Expiration P&L at an underlying price.
- strategy.calendarCallSpread().return.premiumSource: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumSource; default: not declared — How the entry premiums were sourced: `'user'` (supplied) or `'model'` (priced from `market`).
- strategy.calendarCallSpread().return.premiumVolatilitySource?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumVolatilitySource; default: not declared — When modeled, which volatility priced the entries (`'leg'`, `'position'` or `'mixed'`).
- strategy.calendarCallSpread().return.probability: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMetrics; default: not declared — Probability & scenario metrics (spec §12.6): probability of profit, expected value, reward/risk,
and the probability of touching each breakeven — under an explicit, echoed lognormal model.
- strategy.calendarCallSpread().return.scenarioTable: (options?: { market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; volatilityShocks?: number[]; daysForward?: number[]; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ScenarioTableResult; default: not declared — Scenario table (spec §12.6): mark-to-market P&L and Greeks across a grid of underlying prices,
additive vol shocks, and days forward — the standard "what-if" matrix for an options ticket.
- strategy.calendarCallSpread().return.value: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketResult; default: not declared — Mark-to-market value, P&L, per-leg and aggregate Greeks via BSM (spec §12.3).
- strategy.calendarCallSpread().return.whatIfCube: (options?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeOptions) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeResult; default: not declared — A what-if **cube**: the position marked over the full spot × vol-shock × days-forward grid, plus
the **optimal-exit surface** — for each (spot, vol) outcome, the day along the time axis that
optimizes P&L (`max-pnl` by default, or `min-pnl`). `scenarioTable` extended a dimension: it returns
a navigable cube (axes + row-major cells) with the reductions a trader wants, not a flat row list.

Every cell is a `value()` mark (time-aware, per-leg-IV, shock-through-to-leg-IV), so calendars and
per-leg volatilities behave identically. The optimal-exit surface is a CONDITIONAL what-if ("if the
underlying is here with this vol shock, which day marks best?"), not a path-dependent stopping rule.
See `docs/specs/what-if-cube.md`.
- strategy.calendarCallSpread(config)?: PositionConfig | undefined; default: not declared
- strategy.calendarCallSpread(config).expiry?: string; default: not declared — Position-level default expiry (`YYYY-MM-DD` → 16:00 ET, or a datetime) applied to every leg
that has no `expiry` of its own. Named builders route their input's `expiry` here. Precedence
per leg: `leg.expiry` > `expiry` > `market.expiry` (R4).
- strategy.calendarCallSpread(config).market?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumMarket; default: not declared — Market for model-priced entry premiums (required when `premiums: 'model'` and any leg omits its
premium) — AND the position's remembered market (R5): `probability()`, `monteCarloProbability()`,
`value()`, `scenarioTable()`, and `chartData()` use it as their default market, with per-call
fields merged over it. Results echo `marketSource: 'construction' | 'call' | 'merged'`.

- strategy.calendarCallSpread(config).premiums?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumSource; default: not declared — Entry-premium source: `'user'` (from the leg inputs, default) or `'model'` (priced from `market`).

Every cell is a `value()` mark (time-aware, per-leg-IV, shock-through-to-leg-IV), so calendars and
per-leg volatilities behave identically. The optimal-exit surface is a CONDITIONAL what-if ("if the
underlying is here with this vol shock, which day marks best?"), not a path-dependent stopping rule.
See `docs/specs/what-if-cube.md`.
- strategy.callBrokenWing(config)?: PositionConfig | undefined; default: not declared
- strategy.callBrokenWing(config).expiry?: string; default: not declared — Position-level default expiry (`YYYY-MM-DD` → 16:00 ET, or a datetime) applied to every leg
that has no `expiry` of its own. Named builders route their input's `expiry` here. Precedence
per leg: `leg.expiry` > `expiry` > `market.expiry` (R4).
- strategy.callBrokenWing(config).market?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumMarket; default: not declared — Market for model-priced entry premiums (required when `premiums: 'model'` and any leg omits its
premium) — AND the position's remembered market (R5): `probability()`, `monteCarloProbability()`,
`value()`, `scenarioTable()`, and `chartData()` use it as their default market, with per-call
fields merged over it. Results echo `marketSource: 'construction' | 'call' | 'merged'`.
- strategy.callBrokenWing(config).multiplier?: number; default: not declared — Contract multiplier for option legs (default 100).
- strategy.callBrokenWing(config).premiums?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumSource; default: not declared — Entry-premium source: `'user'` (from the leg inputs, default) or `'model'` (priced from `market`).
- strategy.callBrokenWing(input): import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').LadderInput; default: not declared
- strategy.callBrokenWing(input).expiry?: string; default: not declared — Expiry applied to every leg of this structure (`YYYY-MM-DD` → 16:00 ET, or a datetime).
- strategy.callBrokenWing(input).lower: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').Role; default: not declared
- strategy.callBrokenWing(input).middle: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').Role; default: not declared
- strategy.callBrokenWing(input).quantity?: number; default: not declared — Number of structures (default 1). Every leg scales by this.
- strategy.callBrokenWing(input).upper: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').Role; default: not declared
- strategy.callRatioBackspread: (input: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').RatioInput, config?: PositionConfig) => Position; default: not declared
- strategy.callRatioBackspread().return.assumptions: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PositionAssumptions; default: not declared — Position-construction assumptions (design law #3): whether the entry premiums were supplied by
the caller (`'user'`) or model-priced from a market (`'model'`), plus the contract multiplier.
- strategy.callRatioBackspread().return.chartData: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; include?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ChartInclude; market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; }) => Array<{ underlyingPrice: number; expirationPnl?: number; currentPnl?: number; delta?: number; theta?: number; }>; default: not declared — Chart-ready output (spec §12.5). Current P&L / live Greeks need a market: per-call fields
merge over the construction market (R5), so a model-premium position charts with no `market`.
- strategy.callRatioBackspread().return.constructedAs?: string; default: not declared — PROVENANCE, not identity (dx §4.5): the named builder that constructed this position, absent
for raw `strategy(legs)`. Because positions are immutable this can never go stale — but a
rebuilt-after-tweak position has no name. For "what is this NOW?" use `classifyStrategy`.
- strategy.callRatioBackspread().return.legs: readonly Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').Leg>[]; default: not declared — The resolved legs — a frozen snapshot (deep-copied at construction, `Object.freeze`d per leg
and as an array). A Position is immutable by design: to tweak a strategy, edit your own leg
list and rebuild with `strategy(editedLegs, config)` — every downstream calculation is generic
over the legs, so the rebuilt position needs no named builder. Mutating this array throws
instead of silently diverging from `assumptions()`/cached results.
- strategy.callRatioBackspread().return.market?: Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumMarket>; default: not declared — The market this position was built with, if any — a frozen copy (R5), so mutating the caller's
market object later never silently retargets the position. `probability()`, `value()`,
`scenarioTable()`, and `chartData()` default to it; per-call fields merge over it.
- strategy.callRatioBackspread().return.market.asOf: string | number; default: not declared — Entry time (epoch ms or ISO). Each leg's entry `t = yearFraction(asOf, leg.expiry ?? market.expiry)`.
- strategy.callRatioBackspread().return.market.dividendYield?: number; default: not declared
- strategy.callRatioBackspread().return.market.expiry?: string; default: not declared — Default expiry for legs without their own `expiry` (single-expiry structures).
- strategy.callRatioBackspread().return.market.riskFreeRate: number; default: not declared
- strategy.callRatioBackspread().return.market.spot: number; default: not declared
- strategy.callRatioBackspread().return.market.volatility: number; default: not declared — Entry implied volatility (annualized decimal) for unpriced legs that carry no `impliedVolatility`
of their own — a leg's own volatility always wins, exactly as it does when `value()` marks it.
- strategy.callRatioBackspread().return.metrics: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffMetrics; default: not declared — Net debit/credit, max profit/loss, and breakevens. The expiration payoff is piecewise-linear, so
these are computed ANALYTICALLY from the kink set (every option strike plus every stock entry
price) and the tail slopes — never by sampling a coarse grid, which missed breakevens beyond the
last strike (e.g. a lone long stock, or a deep-ITM option) and ignored stock entry prices.
- strategy.callRatioBackspread().return.monteCarloProbability: (overrides: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloInput> & { seed: number; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloMetrics; default: not declared — Monte-Carlo probability metrics (spec §12.6): the simulated analogue of {@link probability}, for
cross-validation and path-dependent reads. Terminal lognormal paths give the probability of profit
and expected P&L (with a standard error); the probability of touching each breakeven is estimated
with the Brownian-bridge continuous-monitoring correction. Seeded and deterministic.
- strategy.callRatioBackspread().return.multiplier: number; default: not declared
- strategy.callRatioBackspread().return.netDebit: () => number; default: not declared — Net cash to enter (positive = debit, negative = credit).
- strategy.callRatioBackspread().return.payoff: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffResult; default: not declared — Expiration payoff metrics plus a chart-ready grid of points (spec §12.2). `prices` is an explicit
grid array or a `{ from, to, steps }` range; omit it to frame the strike-derived default window
(the same one a payoff diagram draws).
- strategy.callRatioBackspread().return.pnlAtExpiry: (underlyingPrice: number) => number; default: not declared — Expiration P&L at an underlying price.
- strategy.callRatioBackspread().return.premiumSource: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumSource; default: not declared — How the entry premiums were sourced: `'user'` (supplied) or `'model'` (priced from `market`).
- strategy.callRatioBackspread().return.premiumVolatilitySource?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumVolatilitySource; default: not declared — When modeled, which volatility priced the entries (`'leg'`, `'position'` or `'mixed'`).

- strategy.cashSecuredPut().return.probability: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMetrics; default: not declared — Probability & scenario metrics (spec §12.6): probability of profit, expected value, reward/risk,
and the probability of touching each breakeven — under an explicit, echoed lognormal model.
- strategy.cashSecuredPut().return.scenarioTable: (options?: { market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; volatilityShocks?: number[]; daysForward?: number[]; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ScenarioTableResult; default: not declared — Scenario table (spec §12.6): mark-to-market P&L and Greeks across a grid of underlying prices,
additive vol shocks, and days forward — the standard "what-if" matrix for an options ticket.
- strategy.cashSecuredPut().return.value: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketResult; default: not declared — Mark-to-market value, P&L, per-leg and aggregate Greeks via BSM (spec §12.3).
- strategy.cashSecuredPut().return.whatIfCube: (options?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeOptions) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeResult; default: not declared — A what-if **cube**: the position marked over the full spot × vol-shock × days-forward grid, plus
the **optimal-exit surface** — for each (spot, vol) outcome, the day along the time axis that
optimizes P&L (`max-pnl` by default, or `min-pnl`). `scenarioTable` extended a dimension: it returns
a navigable cube (axes + row-major cells) with the reductions a trader wants, not a flat row list.

Every cell is a `value()` mark (time-aware, per-leg-IV, shock-through-to-leg-IV), so calendars and
per-leg volatilities behave identically. The optimal-exit surface is a CONDITIONAL what-if ("if the
underlying is here with this vol shock, which day marks best?"), not a path-dependent stopping rule.
See `docs/specs/what-if-cube.md`.
- strategy.cashSecuredPut(config)?: PositionConfig | undefined; default: not declared
- strategy.cashSecuredPut(config).expiry?: string; default: not declared — Position-level default expiry (`YYYY-MM-DD` → 16:00 ET, or a datetime) applied to every leg
that has no `expiry` of its own. Named builders route their input's `expiry` here. Precedence
per leg: `leg.expiry` > `expiry` > `market.expiry` (R4).
- strategy.cashSecuredPut(config).market?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumMarket; default: not declared — Market for model-priced entry premiums (required when `premiums: 'model'` and any leg omits its
premium) — AND the position's remembered market (R5): `probability()`, `monteCarloProbability()`,
`value()`, `scenarioTable()`, and `chartData()` use it as their default market, with per-call
fields merged over it. Results echo `marketSource: 'construction' | 'call' | 'merged'`.
- strategy.cashSecuredPut(config).multiplier?: number; default: not declared — Contract multiplier for option legs (default 100).
- strategy.cashSecuredPut(config).premiums?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumSource; default: not declared — Entry-premium source: `'user'` (from the leg inputs, default) or `'model'` (priced from `market`).
- strategy.cashSecuredPut(input): import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').SingleLegInput; default: not declared
- strategy.cashSecuredPut(input).expiry?: string; default: not declared — Expiry applied to every leg of this structure (`YYYY-MM-DD` → 16:00 ET, or a datetime).
- strategy.cashSecuredPut(input).premium?: number; default: not declared
- strategy.cashSecuredPut(input).quantity?: number; default: not declared — Number of structures (default 1). Every leg scales by this.

- strategy.collar: (input: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').CollarInput, config?: PositionConfig) => Position; default: not declared
- strategy.collar().return.assumptions: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PositionAssumptions; default: not declared — Position-construction assumptions (design law #3): whether the entry premiums were supplied by
the caller (`'user'`) or model-priced from a market (`'model'`), plus the contract multiplier.
- strategy.collar().return.chartData: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; include?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ChartInclude; market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; }) => Array<{ underlyingPrice: number; expirationPnl?: number; currentPnl?: number; delta?: number; theta?: number; }>; default: not declared — Chart-ready output (spec §12.5). Current P&L / live Greeks need a market: per-call fields
merge over the construction market (R5), so a model-premium position charts with no `market`.
- strategy.collar().return.constructedAs?: string; default: not declared — PROVENANCE, not identity (dx §4.5): the named builder that constructed this position, absent
for raw `strategy(legs)`. Because positions are immutable this can never go stale — but a
rebuilt-after-tweak position has no name. For "what is this NOW?" use `classifyStrategy`.
- strategy.collar().return.legs: readonly Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').Leg>[]; default: not declared — The resolved legs — a frozen snapshot (deep-copied at construction, `Object.freeze`d per leg
and as an array). A Position is immutable by design: to tweak a strategy, edit your own leg
list and rebuild with `strategy(editedLegs, config)` — every downstream calculation is generic
over the legs, so the rebuilt position needs no named builder. Mutating this array throws
instead of silently diverging from `assumptions()`/cached results.
- strategy.collar().return.market?: Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumMarket>; default: not declared — The market this position was built with, if any — a frozen copy (R5), so mutating the caller's
market object later never silently retargets the position. `probability()`, `value()`,
`scenarioTable()`, and `chartData()` default to it; per-call fields merge over it.
- strategy.collar().return.market.asOf: string | number; default: not declared — Entry time (epoch ms or ISO). Each leg's entry `t = yearFraction(asOf, leg.expiry ?? market.expiry)`.
- strategy.collar().return.market.dividendYield?: number; default: not declared
- strategy.collar().return.market.expiry?: string; default: not declared — Default expiry for legs without their own `expiry` (single-expiry structures).
- strategy.collar().return.market.riskFreeRate: number; default: not declared
- strategy.collar().return.market.spot: number; default: not declared
- strategy.collar().return.market.volatility: number; default: not declared — Entry implied volatility (annualized decimal) for unpriced legs that carry no `impliedVolatility`
of their own — a leg's own volatility always wins, exactly as it does when `value()` marks it.
- strategy.collar().return.metrics: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffMetrics; default: not declared — Net debit/credit, max profit/loss, and breakevens. The expiration payoff is piecewise-linear, so
these are computed ANALYTICALLY from the kink set (every option strike plus every stock entry
price) and the tail slopes — never by sampling a coarse grid, which missed breakevens beyond the
last strike (e.g. a lone long stock, or a deep-ITM option) and ignored stock entry prices.
- strategy.collar().return.monteCarloProbability: (overrides: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloInput> & { seed: number; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloMetrics; default: not declared — Monte-Carlo probability metrics (spec §12.6): the simulated analogue of {@link probability}, for
cross-validation and path-dependent reads. Terminal lognormal paths give the probability of profit
and expected P&L (with a standard error); the probability of touching each breakeven is estimated
with the Brownian-bridge continuous-monitoring correction. Seeded and deterministic.
- strategy.collar().return.multiplier: number; default: not declared
- strategy.collar().return.netDebit: () => number; default: not declared — Net cash to enter (positive = debit, negative = credit).

grid array or a `{ from, to, steps }` range; omit it to frame the strike-derived default window
(the same one a payoff diagram draws).

- strategy.coveredShortStraddle().return.monteCarloProbability: (overrides: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloInput> & { seed: number; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloMetrics; default: not declared — Monte-Carlo probability metrics (spec §12.6): the simulated analogue of {@link probability}, for
cross-validation and path-dependent reads. Terminal lognormal paths give the probability of profit
and expected P&L (with a standard error); the probability of touching each breakeven is estimated
with the Brownian-bridge continuous-monitoring correction. Seeded and deterministic.
- strategy.coveredShortStraddle().return.multiplier: number; default: not declared
- strategy.coveredShortStraddle().return.netDebit: () => number; default: not declared — Net cash to enter (positive = debit, negative = credit).
- strategy.coveredShortStraddle().return.payoff: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffResult; default: not declared — Expiration payoff metrics plus a chart-ready grid of points (spec §12.2). `prices` is an explicit
grid array or a `{ from, to, steps }` range; omit it to frame the strike-derived default window
(the same one a payoff diagram draws).

- strategy.coveredShortStraddle().return.probability: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMetrics; default: not declared — Probability & scenario metrics (spec §12.6): probability of profit, expected value, reward/risk,
and the probability of touching each breakeven — under an explicit, echoed lognormal model.
- strategy.coveredShortStraddle().return.scenarioTable: (options?: { market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; volatilityShocks?: number[]; daysForward?: number[]; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ScenarioTableResult; default: not declared — Scenario table (spec §12.6): mark-to-market P&L and Greeks across a grid of underlying prices,
additive vol shocks, and days forward — the standard "what-if" matrix for an options ticket.
- strategy.coveredShortStraddle().return.value: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketResult; default: not declared — Mark-to-market value, P&L, per-leg and aggregate Greeks via BSM (spec §12.3).
- strategy.coveredShortStraddle().return.whatIfCube: (options?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeOptions) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeResult; default: not declared — A what-if **cube**: the position marked over the full spot × vol-shock × days-forward grid, plus
the **optimal-exit surface** — for each (spot, vol) outcome, the day along the time axis that
optimizes P&L (`max-pnl` by default, or `min-pnl`). `scenarioTable` extended a dimension: it returns
a navigable cube (axes + row-major cells) with the reductions a trader wants, not a flat row list.

Every cell is a `value()` mark (time-aware, per-leg-IV, shock-through-to-leg-IV), so calendars and
per-leg volatilities behave identically. The optimal-exit surface is a CONDITIONAL what-if ("if the
underlying is here with this vol shock, which day marks best?"), not a path-dependent stopping rule.
See `docs/specs/what-if-cube.md`.

that has no `expiry` of its own. Named builders route their input's `expiry` here. Precedence
per leg: `leg.expiry` > `expiry` > `market.expiry` (R4).

fields merged over it. Results echo `marketSource: 'construction' | 'call' | 'merged'`.

and as an array). A Position is immutable by design: to tweak a strategy, edit your own leg
list and rebuild with `strategy(editedLegs, config)` — every downstream calculation is generic
over the legs, so the rebuilt position needs no named builder. Mutating this array throws
instead of silently diverging from `assumptions()`/cached results.

- strategy.diagonalPutSpread().return.market.spot: number; default: not declared

- strategy.diagonalPutSpread().return.metrics: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffMetrics; default: not declared — Net debit/credit, max profit/loss, and breakevens. The expiration payoff is piecewise-linear, so
these are computed ANALYTICALLY from the kink set (every option strike plus every stock entry
price) and the tail slopes — never by sampling a coarse grid, which missed breakevens beyond the
last strike (e.g. a lone long stock, or a deep-ITM option) and ignored stock entry prices.
- strategy.diagonalPutSpread().return.monteCarloProbability: (overrides: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloInput> & { seed: number; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloMetrics; default: not declared — Monte-Carlo probability metrics (spec §12.6): the simulated analogue of {@link probability}, for
cross-validation and path-dependent reads. Terminal lognormal paths give the probability of profit
and expected P&L (with a standard error); the probability of touching each breakeven is estimated
with the Brownian-bridge continuous-monitoring correction. Seeded and deterministic.

- strategy.diagonalPutSpread().return.whatIfCube: (options?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeOptions) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeResult; default: not declared — A what-if **cube**: the position marked over the full spot × vol-shock × days-forward grid, plus
the **optimal-exit surface** — for each (spot, vol) outcome, the day along the time axis that
optimizes P&L (`max-pnl` by default, or `min-pnl`). `scenarioTable` extended a dimension: it returns
a navigable cube (axes + row-major cells) with the reductions a trader wants, not a flat row list.

Every cell is a `value()` mark (time-aware, per-leg-IV, shock-through-to-leg-IV), so calendars and
per-leg volatilities behave identically. The optimal-exit surface is a CONDITIONAL what-if ("if the
underlying is here with this vol shock, which day marks best?"), not a path-dependent stopping rule.
See `docs/specs/what-if-cube.md`.

the caller (`'user'`) or model-priced from a market (`'model'`), plus the contract multiplier.
- strategy.inverseCallBrokenWing().return.chartData: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; include?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ChartInclude; market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; }) => Array<{ underlyingPrice: number; expirationPnl?: number; currentPnl?: number; delta?: number; theta?: number; }>; default: not declared — Chart-ready output (spec §12.5). Current P&L / live Greeks need a market: per-call fields
merge over the construction market (R5), so a model-premium position charts with no `market`.
- strategy.inverseCallBrokenWing().return.constructedAs?: string; default: not declared — PROVENANCE, not identity (dx §4.5): the named builder that constructed this position, absent
for raw `strategy(legs)`. Because positions are immutable this can never go stale — but a
rebuilt-after-tweak position has no name. For "what is this NOW?" use `classifyStrategy`.
- strategy.inverseCallBrokenWing().return.legs: readonly Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').Leg>[]; default: not declared — The resolved legs — a frozen snapshot (deep-copied at construction, `Object.freeze`d per leg
and as an array). A Position is immutable by design: to tweak a strategy, edit your own leg
list and rebuild with `strategy(editedLegs, config)` — every downstream calculation is generic
over the legs, so the rebuilt position needs no named builder. Mutating this array throws
instead of silently diverging from `assumptions()`/cached results.
- strategy.inverseCallBrokenWing().return.market?: Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumMarket>; default: not declared — The market this position was built with, if any — a frozen copy (R5), so mutating the caller's
market object later never silently retargets the position. `probability()`, `value()`,
`scenarioTable()`, and `chartData()` default to it; per-call fields merge over it.
- strategy.inverseCallBrokenWing().return.market.asOf: string | number; default: not declared — Entry time (epoch ms or ISO). Each leg's entry `t = yearFraction(asOf, leg.expiry ?? market.expiry)`.
- strategy.inverseCallBrokenWing().return.market.dividendYield?: number; default: not declared
- strategy.inverseCallBrokenWing().return.market.expiry?: string; default: not declared — Default expiry for legs without their own `expiry` (single-expiry structures).
- strategy.inverseCallBrokenWing().return.market.riskFreeRate: number; default: not declared
- strategy.inverseCallBrokenWing().return.market.spot: number; default: not declared
- strategy.inverseCallBrokenWing().return.market.volatility: number; default: not declared — Entry implied volatility (annualized decimal) for unpriced legs that carry no `impliedVolatility`
of their own — a leg's own volatility always wins, exactly as it does when `value()` marks it.
- strategy.inverseCallBrokenWing().return.metrics: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffMetrics; default: not declared — Net debit/credit, max profit/loss, and breakevens. The expiration payoff is piecewise-linear, so
these are computed ANALYTICALLY from the kink set (every option strike plus every stock entry
price) and the tail slopes — never by sampling a coarse grid, which missed breakevens beyond the
last strike (e.g. a lone long stock, or a deep-ITM option) and ignored stock entry prices.
- strategy.inverseCallBrokenWing().return.monteCarloProbability: (overrides: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloInput> & { seed: number; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloMetrics; default: not declared — Monte-Carlo probability metrics (spec §12.6): the simulated analogue of {@link probability}, for
cross-validation and path-dependent reads. Terminal lognormal paths give the probability of profit
and expected P&L (with a standard error); the probability of touching each breakeven is estimated
with the Brownian-bridge continuous-monitoring correction. Seeded and deterministic.
- strategy.inverseCallBrokenWing().return.multiplier: number; default: not declared
- strategy.inverseCallBrokenWing().return.netDebit: () => number; default: not declared — Net cash to enter (positive = debit, negative = credit).
- strategy.inverseCallBrokenWing().return.payoff: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffResult; default: not declared — Expiration payoff metrics plus a chart-ready grid of points (spec §12.2). `prices` is an explicit
grid array or a `{ from, to, steps }` range; omit it to frame the strike-derived default window
(the same one a payoff diagram draws).
- strategy.inverseCallBrokenWing().return.pnlAtExpiry: (underlyingPrice: number) => number; default: not declared — Expiration P&L at an underlying price.

- strategy.inverseCallBrokenWing().return.premiumVolatilitySource?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumVolatilitySource; default: not declared — When modeled, which volatility priced the entries (`'leg'`, `'position'` or `'mixed'`).
- strategy.inverseCallBrokenWing().return.probability: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMetrics; default: not declared — Probability & scenario metrics (spec §12.6): probability of profit, expected value, reward/risk,

- strategy.inverseCallBrokenWing().return.scenarioTable: (options?: { market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; volatilityShocks?: number[]; daysForward?: number[]; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ScenarioTableResult; default: not declared — Scenario table (spec §12.6): mark-to-market P&L and Greeks across a grid of underlying prices,
additive vol shocks, and days forward — the standard "what-if" matrix for an options ticket.
- strategy.inverseCallBrokenWing().return.value: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketResult; default: not declared — Mark-to-market value, P&L, per-leg and aggregate Greeks via BSM (spec §12.3).
- strategy.inverseCallBrokenWing().return.whatIfCube: (options?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeOptions) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeResult; default: not declared — A what-if **cube**: the position marked over the full spot × vol-shock × days-forward grid, plus
the **optimal-exit surface** — for each (spot, vol) outcome, the day along the time axis that
optimizes P&L (`max-pnl` by default, or `min-pnl`). `scenarioTable` extended a dimension: it returns
a navigable cube (axes + row-major cells) with the reductions a trader wants, not a flat row list.

Every cell is a `value()` mark (time-aware, per-leg-IV, shock-through-to-leg-IV), so calendars and
per-leg volatilities behave identically. The optimal-exit surface is a CONDITIONAL what-if ("if the
underlying is here with this vol shock, which day marks best?"), not a path-dependent stopping rule.
See `docs/specs/what-if-cube.md`.

the **optimal-exit surface** — for each (spot, vol) outcome, the day along the time axis that
optimizes P&L (`max-pnl` by default, or `min-pnl`). `scenarioTable` extended a dimension: it returns
a navigable cube (axes + row-major cells) with the reductions a trader wants, not a flat row list.

Every cell is a `value()` mark (time-aware, per-leg-IV, shock-through-to-leg-IV), so calendars and
per-leg volatilities behave identically. The optimal-exit surface is a CONDITIONAL what-if ("if the
underlying is here with this vol shock, which day marks best?"), not a path-dependent stopping rule.
See `docs/specs/what-if-cube.md`.

- strategy.inverseIronCondor(config).expiry?: string; default: not declared — Position-level default expiry (`YYYY-MM-DD` → 16:00 ET, or a datetime) applied to every leg
that has no `expiry` of its own. Named builders route their input's `expiry` here. Precedence
per leg: `leg.expiry` > `expiry` > `market.expiry` (R4).
- strategy.inverseIronCondor(config).market?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumMarket; default: not declared — Market for model-priced entry premiums (required when `premiums: 'model'` and any leg omits its
premium) — AND the position's remembered market (R5): `probability()`, `monteCarloProbability()`,
`value()`, `scenarioTable()`, and `chartData()` use it as their default market, with per-call
fields merged over it. Results echo `marketSource: 'construction' | 'call' | 'merged'`.
- strategy.inverseIronCondor(config).multiplier?: number; default: not declared — Contract multiplier for option legs (default 100).
- strategy.inverseIronCondor(config).premiums?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumSource; default: not declared — Entry-premium source: `'user'` (from the leg inputs, default) or `'model'` (priced from `market`).

- strategy.inversePutBrokenWing().return.legs: readonly Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').Leg>[]; default: not declared — The resolved legs — a frozen snapshot (deep-copied at construction, `Object.freeze`d per leg
and as an array). A Position is immutable by design: to tweak a strategy, edit your own leg
list and rebuild with `strategy(editedLegs, config)` — every downstream calculation is generic
over the legs, so the rebuilt position needs no named builder. Mutating this array throws
instead of silently diverging from `assumptions()`/cached results.
- strategy.inversePutBrokenWing().return.market?: Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumMarket>; default: not declared — The market this position was built with, if any — a frozen copy (R5), so mutating the caller's

- strategy.inversePutBrokenWing().return.metrics: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffMetrics; default: not declared — Net debit/credit, max profit/loss, and breakevens. The expiration payoff is piecewise-linear, so
these are computed ANALYTICALLY from the kink set (every option strike plus every stock entry
price) and the tail slopes — never by sampling a coarse grid, which missed breakevens beyond the
last strike (e.g. a lone long stock, or a deep-ITM option) and ignored stock entry prices.
- strategy.inversePutBrokenWing().return.monteCarloProbability: (overrides: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloInput> & { seed: number; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloMetrics; default: not declared — Monte-Carlo probability metrics (spec §12.6): the simulated analogue of {@link probability}, for
cross-validation and path-dependent reads. Terminal lognormal paths give the probability of profit
and expected P&L (with a standard error); the probability of touching each breakeven is estimated
with the Brownian-bridge continuous-monitoring correction. Seeded and deterministic.

- strategy.inversePutBrokenWing().return.netDebit: () => number; default: not declared — Net cash to enter (positive = debit, negative = credit).

and expected P&L (with a standard error); the probability of touching each breakeven is estimated
with the Brownian-bridge continuous-monitoring correction. Seeded and deterministic.

- strategy.ironCondor().return.netDebit: () => number; default: not declared — Net cash to enter (positive = debit, negative = credit).
- strategy.ironCondor().return.payoff: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffResult; default: not declared — Expiration payoff metrics plus a chart-ready grid of points (spec §12.2). `prices` is an explicit
grid array or a `{ from, to, steps }` range; omit it to frame the strike-derived default window
(the same one a payoff diagram draws).

- strategy.ironCondor().return.probability: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMetrics; default: not declared — Probability & scenario metrics (spec §12.6): probability of profit, expected value, reward/risk,
and the probability of touching each breakeven — under an explicit, echoed lognormal model.
- strategy.ironCondor().return.scenarioTable: (options?: { market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; volatilityShocks?: number[]; daysForward?: number[]; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ScenarioTableResult; default: not declared — Scenario table (spec §12.6): mark-to-market P&L and Greeks across a grid of underlying prices,
additive vol shocks, and days forward — the standard "what-if" matrix for an options ticket.
- strategy.ironCondor().return.value: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketResult; default: not declared — Mark-to-market value, P&L, per-leg and aggregate Greeks via BSM (spec §12.3).
- strategy.ironCondor().return.whatIfCube: (options?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeOptions) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeResult; default: not declared — A what-if **cube**: the position marked over the full spot × vol-shock × days-forward grid, plus
the **optimal-exit surface** — for each (spot, vol) outcome, the day along the time axis that
optimizes P&L (`max-pnl` by default, or `min-pnl`). `scenarioTable` extended a dimension: it returns
a navigable cube (axes + row-major cells) with the reductions a trader wants, not a flat row list.

Every cell is a `value()` mark (time-aware, per-leg-IV, shock-through-to-leg-IV), so calendars and
per-leg volatilities behave identically. The optimal-exit surface is a CONDITIONAL what-if ("if the
underlying is here with this vol shock, which day marks best?"), not a path-dependent stopping rule.
See `docs/specs/what-if-cube.md`.
- strategy.ironCondor(config)?: PositionConfig | undefined; default: not declared
- strategy.ironCondor(config).expiry?: string; default: not declared — Position-level default expiry (`YYYY-MM-DD` → 16:00 ET, or a datetime) applied to every leg
that has no `expiry` of its own. Named builders route their input's `expiry` here. Precedence
per leg: `leg.expiry` > `expiry` > `market.expiry` (R4).
- strategy.ironCondor(config).market?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumMarket; default: not declared — Market for model-priced entry premiums (required when `premiums: 'model'` and any leg omits its
premium) — AND the position's remembered market (R5): `probability()`, `monteCarloProbability()`,
`value()`, `scenarioTable()`, and `chartData()` use it as their default market, with per-call
fields merged over it. Results echo `marketSource: 'construction' | 'call' | 'merged'`.
- strategy.ironCondor(config).multiplier?: number; default: not declared — Contract multiplier for option legs (default 100).
- strategy.ironCondor(config).premiums?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumSource; default: not declared — Entry-premium source: `'user'` (from the leg inputs, default) or `'model'` (priced from `market`).

- strategy.jadeLizard().return.metrics: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffMetrics; default: not declared — Net debit/credit, max profit/loss, and breakevens. The expiration payoff is piecewise-linear, so

last strike (e.g. a lone long stock, or a deep-ITM option) and ignored stock entry prices.

`scenarioTable()`, and `chartData()` default to it; per-call fields merge over it.
- strategy.longCallButterfly().return.market.asOf: string | number; default: not declared — Entry time (epoch ms or ISO). Each leg's entry `t = yearFraction(asOf, leg.expiry ?? market.expiry)`.
- strategy.longCallButterfly().return.market.dividendYield?: number; default: not declared
- strategy.longCallButterfly().return.market.expiry?: string; default: not declared — Default expiry for legs without their own `expiry` (single-expiry structures).
- strategy.longCallButterfly().return.market.riskFreeRate: number; default: not declared
- strategy.longCallButterfly().return.market.spot: number; default: not declared
- strategy.longCallButterfly().return.market.volatility: number; default: not declared — Entry implied volatility (annualized decimal) for unpriced legs that carry no `impliedVolatility`
of their own — a leg's own volatility always wins, exactly as it does when `value()` marks it.
- strategy.longCallButterfly().return.metrics: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffMetrics; default: not declared — Net debit/credit, max profit/loss, and breakevens. The expiration payoff is piecewise-linear, so
these are computed ANALYTICALLY from the kink set (every option strike plus every stock entry
price) and the tail slopes — never by sampling a coarse grid, which missed breakevens beyond the
last strike (e.g. a lone long stock, or a deep-ITM option) and ignored stock entry prices.
- strategy.longCallButterfly().return.monteCarloProbability: (overrides: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloInput> & { seed: number; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloMetrics; default: not declared — Monte-Carlo probability metrics (spec §12.6): the simulated analogue of {@link probability}, for
cross-validation and path-dependent reads. Terminal lognormal paths give the probability of profit
and expected P&L (with a standard error); the probability of touching each breakeven is estimated
with the Brownian-bridge continuous-monitoring correction. Seeded and deterministic.
- strategy.longCallButterfly().return.multiplier: number; default: not declared
- strategy.longCallButterfly().return.netDebit: () => number; default: not declared — Net cash to enter (positive = debit, negative = credit).
- strategy.longCallButterfly().return.payoff: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffResult; default: not declared — Expiration payoff metrics plus a chart-ready grid of points (spec §12.2). `prices` is an explicit
grid array or a `{ from, to, steps }` range; omit it to frame the strike-derived default window
(the same one a payoff diagram draws).
- strategy.longCallButterfly().return.pnlAtExpiry: (underlyingPrice: number) => number; default: not declared — Expiration P&L at an underlying price.
- strategy.longCallButterfly().return.premiumSource: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumSource; default: not declared — How the entry premiums were sourced: `'user'` (supplied) or `'model'` (priced from `market`).
- strategy.longCallButterfly().return.premiumVolatilitySource?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumVolatilitySource; default: not declared — When modeled, which volatility priced the entries (`'leg'`, `'position'` or `'mixed'`).
- strategy.longCallButterfly().return.probability: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMetrics; default: not declared — Probability & scenario metrics (spec §12.6): probability of profit, expected value, reward/risk,
and the probability of touching each breakeven — under an explicit, echoed lognormal model.
- strategy.longCallButterfly().return.scenarioTable: (options?: { market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; volatilityShocks?: number[]; daysForward?: number[]; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ScenarioTableResult; default: not declared — Scenario table (spec §12.6): mark-to-market P&L and Greeks across a grid of underlying prices,
additive vol shocks, and days forward — the standard "what-if" matrix for an options ticket.
- strategy.longCallButterfly().return.value: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketResult; default: not declared — Mark-to-market value, P&L, per-leg and aggregate Greeks via BSM (spec §12.3).
- strategy.longCallButterfly().return.whatIfCube: (options?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeOptions) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeResult; default: not declared — A what-if **cube**: the position marked over the full spot × vol-shock × days-forward grid, plus
the **optimal-exit surface** — for each (spot, vol) outcome, the day along the time axis that
optimizes P&L (`max-pnl` by default, or `min-pnl`). `scenarioTable` extended a dimension: it returns
a navigable cube (axes + row-major cells) with the reductions a trader wants, not a flat row list.

Every cell is a `value()` mark (time-aware, per-leg-IV, shock-through-to-leg-IV), so calendars and
per-leg volatilities behave identically. The optimal-exit surface is a CONDITIONAL what-if ("if the
underlying is here with this vol shock, which day marks best?"), not a path-dependent stopping rule.
See `docs/specs/what-if-cube.md`.

per leg: `leg.expiry` > `expiry` > `market.expiry` (R4).

premium) — AND the position's remembered market (R5): `probability()`, `monteCarloProbability()`,

fields merged over it. Results echo `marketSource: 'construction' | 'call' | 'merged'`.

- strategy.longPut().return.assumptions: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PositionAssumptions; default: not declared — Position-construction assumptions (design law #3): whether the entry premiums were supplied by
the caller (`'user'`) or model-priced from a market (`'model'`), plus the contract multiplier.
- strategy.longPut().return.chartData: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; include?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ChartInclude; market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; }) => Array<{ underlyingPrice: number; expirationPnl?: number; currentPnl?: number; delta?: number; theta?: number; }>; default: not declared — Chart-ready output (spec §12.5). Current P&L / live Greeks need a market: per-call fields
merge over the construction market (R5), so a model-premium position charts with no `market`.
- strategy.longPut().return.constructedAs?: string; default: not declared — PROVENANCE, not identity (dx §4.5): the named builder that constructed this position, absent
for raw `strategy(legs)`. Because positions are immutable this can never go stale — but a
rebuilt-after-tweak position has no name. For "what is this NOW?" use `classifyStrategy`.
- strategy.longPut().return.legs: readonly Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').Leg>[]; default: not declared — The resolved legs — a frozen snapshot (deep-copied at construction, `Object.freeze`d per leg
and as an array). A Position is immutable by design: to tweak a strategy, edit your own leg
list and rebuild with `strategy(editedLegs, config)` — every downstream calculation is generic
over the legs, so the rebuilt position needs no named builder. Mutating this array throws
instead of silently diverging from `assumptions()`/cached results.
- strategy.longPut().return.market?: Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumMarket>; default: not declared — The market this position was built with, if any — a frozen copy (R5), so mutating the caller's
market object later never silently retargets the position. `probability()`, `value()`,
`scenarioTable()`, and `chartData()` default to it; per-call fields merge over it.
- strategy.longPut().return.market.asOf: string | number; default: not declared — Entry time (epoch ms or ISO). Each leg's entry `t = yearFraction(asOf, leg.expiry ?? market.expiry)`.
- strategy.longPut().return.market.dividendYield?: number; default: not declared
- strategy.longPut().return.market.expiry?: string; default: not declared — Default expiry for legs without their own `expiry` (single-expiry structures).
- strategy.longPut().return.market.riskFreeRate: number; default: not declared
- strategy.longPut().return.market.spot: number; default: not declared
- strategy.longPut().return.market.volatility: number; default: not declared — Entry implied volatility (annualized decimal) for unpriced legs that carry no `impliedVolatility`
of their own — a leg's own volatility always wins, exactly as it does when `value()` marks it.
- strategy.longPut().return.metrics: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffMetrics; default: not declared — Net debit/credit, max profit/loss, and breakevens. The expiration payoff is piecewise-linear, so
these are computed ANALYTICALLY from the kink set (every option strike plus every stock entry
price) and the tail slopes — never by sampling a coarse grid, which missed breakevens beyond the
last strike (e.g. a lone long stock, or a deep-ITM option) and ignored stock entry prices.
- strategy.longPut().return.monteCarloProbability: (overrides: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloInput> & { seed: number; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloMetrics; default: not declared — Monte-Carlo probability metrics (spec §12.6): the simulated analogue of {@link probability}, for
cross-validation and path-dependent reads. Terminal lognormal paths give the probability of profit
and expected P&L (with a standard error); the probability of touching each breakeven is estimated
with the Brownian-bridge continuous-monitoring correction. Seeded and deterministic.
- strategy.longPut().return.multiplier: number; default: not declared
- strategy.longPut().return.netDebit: () => number; default: not declared — Net cash to enter (positive = debit, negative = credit).
- strategy.longPut().return.payoff: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffResult; default: not declared — Expiration payoff metrics plus a chart-ready grid of points (spec §12.2). `prices` is an explicit
grid array or a `{ from, to, steps }` range; omit it to frame the strike-derived default window
(the same one a payoff diagram draws).
- strategy.longPut().return.pnlAtExpiry: (underlyingPrice: number) => number; default: not declared — Expiration P&L at an underlying price.
- strategy.longPut().return.premiumSource: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumSource; default: not declared — How the entry premiums were sourced: `'user'` (supplied) or `'model'` (priced from `market`).
- strategy.longPut().return.premiumVolatilitySource?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumVolatilitySource; default: not declared — When modeled, which volatility priced the entries (`'leg'`, `'position'` or `'mixed'`).
- strategy.longPut().return.probability: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMetrics; default: not declared — Probability & scenario metrics (spec §12.6): probability of profit, expected value, reward/risk,
and the probability of touching each breakeven — under an explicit, echoed lognormal model.
- strategy.longPut().return.scenarioTable: (options?: { market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; volatilityShocks?: number[]; daysForward?: number[]; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ScenarioTableResult; default: not declared — Scenario table (spec §12.6): mark-to-market P&L and Greeks across a grid of underlying prices,
additive vol shocks, and days forward — the standard "what-if" matrix for an options ticket.
- strategy.longPut().return.value: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketResult; default: not declared — Mark-to-market value, P&L, per-leg and aggregate Greeks via BSM (spec §12.3).
- strategy.longPut().return.whatIfCube: (options?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeOptions) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeResult; default: not declared — A what-if **cube**: the position marked over the full spot × vol-shock × days-forward grid, plus
the **optimal-exit surface** — for each (spot, vol) outcome, the day along the time axis that
optimizes P&L (`max-pnl` by default, or `min-pnl`). `scenarioTable` extended a dimension: it returns
a navigable cube (axes + row-major cells) with the reductions a trader wants, not a flat row list.

Every cell is a `value()` mark (time-aware, per-leg-IV, shock-through-to-leg-IV), so calendars and
per-leg volatilities behave identically. The optimal-exit surface is a CONDITIONAL what-if ("if the
underlying is here with this vol shock, which day marks best?"), not a path-dependent stopping rule.
See `docs/specs/what-if-cube.md`.
- strategy.longPut(config)?: PositionConfig | undefined; default: not declared
- strategy.longPut(config).expiry?: string; default: not declared — Position-level default expiry (`YYYY-MM-DD` → 16:00 ET, or a datetime) applied to every leg
that has no `expiry` of its own. Named builders route their input's `expiry` here. Precedence
per leg: `leg.expiry` > `expiry` > `market.expiry` (R4).
- strategy.longPut(config).market?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumMarket; default: not declared — Market for model-priced entry premiums (required when `premiums: 'model'` and any leg omits its
premium) — AND the position's remembered market (R5): `probability()`, `monteCarloProbability()`,
`value()`, `scenarioTable()`, and `chartData()` use it as their default market, with per-call
fields merged over it. Results echo `marketSource: 'construction' | 'call' | 'merged'`.

- strategy.longPutCondor(config).market?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumMarket; default: not declared — Market for model-priced entry premiums (required when `premiums: 'model'` and any leg omits its
premium) — AND the position's remembered market (R5): `probability()`, `monteCarloProbability()`,
`value()`, `scenarioTable()`, and `chartData()` use it as their default market, with per-call
fields merged over it. Results echo `marketSource: 'construction' | 'call' | 'merged'`.
- strategy.longPutCondor(config).multiplier?: number; default: not declared — Contract multiplier for option legs (default 100).
- strategy.longPutCondor(config).premiums?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumSource; default: not declared — Entry-premium source: `'user'` (from the leg inputs, default) or `'model'` (priced from `market`).
- strategy.longPutCondor(input): import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').CondorInput; default: not declared
- strategy.longPutCondor(input).expiry?: string; default: not declared — Expiry applied to every leg of this structure (`YYYY-MM-DD` → 16:00 ET, or a datetime).
- strategy.longPutCondor(input).k1: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').Role; default: not declared
- strategy.longPutCondor(input).k2: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').Role; default: not declared
- strategy.longPutCondor(input).k3: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').Role; default: not declared
- strategy.longPutCondor(input).k4: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').Role; default: not declared
- strategy.longPutCondor(input).quantity?: number; default: not declared — Number of structures (default 1). Every leg scales by this.

- strategy.longSyntheticFuture().return.assumptions: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PositionAssumptions; default: not declared — Position-construction assumptions (design law #3): whether the entry premiums were supplied by
the caller (`'user'`) or model-priced from a market (`'model'`), plus the contract multiplier.
- strategy.longSyntheticFuture().return.chartData: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; include?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ChartInclude; market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; }) => Array<{ underlyingPrice: number; expirationPnl?: number; currentPnl?: number; delta?: number; theta?: number; }>; default: not declared — Chart-ready output (spec §12.5). Current P&L / live Greeks need a market: per-call fields
merge over the construction market (R5), so a model-premium position charts with no `market`.
- strategy.longSyntheticFuture().return.constructedAs?: string; default: not declared — PROVENANCE, not identity (dx §4.5): the named builder that constructed this position, absent
for raw `strategy(legs)`. Because positions are immutable this can never go stale — but a
rebuilt-after-tweak position has no name. For "what is this NOW?" use `classifyStrategy`.
- strategy.longSyntheticFuture().return.legs: readonly Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').Leg>[]; default: not declared — The resolved legs — a frozen snapshot (deep-copied at construction, `Object.freeze`d per leg
and as an array). A Position is immutable by design: to tweak a strategy, edit your own leg
list and rebuild with `strategy(editedLegs, config)` — every downstream calculation is generic
over the legs, so the rebuilt position needs no named builder. Mutating this array throws
instead of silently diverging from `assumptions()`/cached results.
- strategy.longSyntheticFuture().return.market?: Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumMarket>; default: not declared — The market this position was built with, if any — a frozen copy (R5), so mutating the caller's
market object later never silently retargets the position. `probability()`, `value()`,
