- strategy.longSyntheticFuture().return.market.dividendYield?: number; default: not declared
- strategy.longSyntheticFuture().return.market.expiry?: string; default: not declared — Default expiry for legs without their own `expiry` (single-expiry structures).
- strategy.longSyntheticFuture().return.market.riskFreeRate: number; default: not declared
- strategy.longSyntheticFuture().return.market.spot: number; default: not declared
- strategy.longSyntheticFuture().return.market.volatility: number; default: not declared — Entry implied volatility (annualized decimal) for unpriced legs that carry no `impliedVolatility`
of their own — a leg's own volatility always wins, exactly as it does when `value()` marks it.
- strategy.longSyntheticFuture().return.metrics: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffMetrics; default: not declared — Net debit/credit, max profit/loss, and breakevens. The expiration payoff is piecewise-linear, so
these are computed ANALYTICALLY from the kink set (every option strike plus every stock entry
price) and the tail slopes — never by sampling a coarse grid, which missed breakevens beyond the
last strike (e.g. a lone long stock, or a deep-ITM option) and ignored stock entry prices.
- strategy.longSyntheticFuture().return.monteCarloProbability: (overrides: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloInput> & { seed: number; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloMetrics; default: not declared — Monte-Carlo probability metrics (spec §12.6): the simulated analogue of {@link probability}, for
cross-validation and path-dependent reads. Terminal lognormal paths give the probability of profit
and expected P&L (with a standard error); the probability of touching each breakeven is estimated
with the Brownian-bridge continuous-monitoring correction. Seeded and deterministic.
- strategy.longSyntheticFuture().return.multiplier: number; default: not declared
- strategy.longSyntheticFuture().return.netDebit: () => number; default: not declared — Net cash to enter (positive = debit, negative = credit).
- strategy.longSyntheticFuture().return.payoff: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffResult; default: not declared — Expiration payoff metrics plus a chart-ready grid of points (spec §12.2). `prices` is an explicit
grid array or a `{ from, to, steps }` range; omit it to frame the strike-derived default window
(the same one a payoff diagram draws).
- strategy.longSyntheticFuture().return.pnlAtExpiry: (underlyingPrice: number) => number; default: not declared — Expiration P&L at an underlying price.
- strategy.longSyntheticFuture().return.premiumSource: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumSource; default: not declared — How the entry premiums were sourced: `'user'` (supplied) or `'model'` (priced from `market`).
- strategy.longSyntheticFuture().return.premiumVolatilitySource?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumVolatilitySource; default: not declared — When modeled, which volatility priced the entries (`'leg'`, `'position'` or `'mixed'`).
- strategy.longSyntheticFuture().return.probability: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMetrics; default: not declared — Probability & scenario metrics (spec §12.6): probability of profit, expected value, reward/risk,
and the probability of touching each breakeven — under an explicit, echoed lognormal model.
- strategy.longSyntheticFuture().return.scenarioTable: (options?: { market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; volatilityShocks?: number[]; daysForward?: number[]; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ScenarioTableResult; default: not declared — Scenario table (spec §12.6): mark-to-market P&L and Greeks across a grid of underlying prices,
additive vol shocks, and days forward — the standard "what-if" matrix for an options ticket.
- strategy.longSyntheticFuture().return.value: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketResult; default: not declared — Mark-to-market value, P&L, per-leg and aggregate Greeks via BSM (spec §12.3).
- strategy.longSyntheticFuture().return.whatIfCube: (options?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeOptions) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeResult; default: not declared — A what-if **cube**: the position marked over the full spot × vol-shock × days-forward grid, plus
the **optimal-exit surface** — for each (spot, vol) outcome, the day along the time axis that
optimizes P&L (`max-pnl` by default, or `min-pnl`). `scenarioTable` extended a dimension: it returns
a navigable cube (axes + row-major cells) with the reductions a trader wants, not a flat row list.

Every cell is a `value()` mark (time-aware, per-leg-IV, shock-through-to-leg-IV), so calendars and
per-leg volatilities behave identically. The optimal-exit surface is a CONDITIONAL what-if ("if the
underlying is here with this vol shock, which day marks best?"), not a path-dependent stopping rule.
See `docs/specs/what-if-cube.md`.

- strategy.putBrokenWing().return.value: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketResult; default: not declared — Mark-to-market value, P&L, per-leg and aggregate Greeks via BSM (spec §12.3).
- strategy.putBrokenWing().return.whatIfCube: (options?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeOptions) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeResult; default: not declared — A what-if **cube**: the position marked over the full spot × vol-shock × days-forward grid, plus
the **optimal-exit surface** — for each (spot, vol) outcome, the day along the time axis that
optimizes P&L (`max-pnl` by default, or `min-pnl`). `scenarioTable` extended a dimension: it returns
a navigable cube (axes + row-major cells) with the reductions a trader wants, not a flat row list.

Every cell is a `value()` mark (time-aware, per-leg-IV, shock-through-to-leg-IV), so calendars and
per-leg volatilities behave identically. The optimal-exit surface is a CONDITIONAL what-if ("if the
underlying is here with this vol shock, which day marks best?"), not a path-dependent stopping rule.
See `docs/specs/what-if-cube.md`.
- strategy.putBrokenWing(config)?: PositionConfig | undefined; default: not declared
- strategy.putBrokenWing(config).expiry?: string; default: not declared — Position-level default expiry (`YYYY-MM-DD` → 16:00 ET, or a datetime) applied to every leg
that has no `expiry` of its own. Named builders route their input's `expiry` here. Precedence
per leg: `leg.expiry` > `expiry` > `market.expiry` (R4).
- strategy.putBrokenWing(config).market?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumMarket; default: not declared — Market for model-priced entry premiums (required when `premiums: 'model'` and any leg omits its
premium) — AND the position's remembered market (R5): `probability()`, `monteCarloProbability()`,
`value()`, `scenarioTable()`, and `chartData()` use it as their default market, with per-call
fields merged over it. Results echo `marketSource: 'construction' | 'call' | 'merged'`.
- strategy.putBrokenWing(config).multiplier?: number; default: not declared — Contract multiplier for option legs (default 100).
- strategy.putBrokenWing(config).premiums?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumSource; default: not declared — Entry-premium source: `'user'` (from the leg inputs, default) or `'model'` (priced from `market`).

- strategy.putRatioBackspread().return.chartData: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; include?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ChartInclude; market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; }) => Array<{ underlyingPrice: number; expirationPnl?: number; currentPnl?: number; delta?: number; theta?: number; }>; default: not declared — Chart-ready output (spec §12.5). Current P&L / live Greeks need a market: per-call fields
merge over the construction market (R5), so a model-premium position charts with no `market`.
- strategy.putRatioBackspread().return.constructedAs?: string; default: not declared — PROVENANCE, not identity (dx §4.5): the named builder that constructed this position, absent
for raw `strategy(legs)`. Because positions are immutable this can never go stale — but a
rebuilt-after-tweak position has no name. For "what is this NOW?" use `classifyStrategy`.
- strategy.putRatioBackspread().return.legs: readonly Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').Leg>[]; default: not declared — The resolved legs — a frozen snapshot (deep-copied at construction, `Object.freeze`d per leg
and as an array). A Position is immutable by design: to tweak a strategy, edit your own leg
list and rebuild with `strategy(editedLegs, config)` — every downstream calculation is generic
over the legs, so the rebuilt position needs no named builder. Mutating this array throws
instead of silently diverging from `assumptions()`/cached results.
- strategy.putRatioBackspread().return.market?: Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumMarket>; default: not declared — The market this position was built with, if any — a frozen copy (R5), so mutating the caller's
market object later never silently retargets the position. `probability()`, `value()`,
`scenarioTable()`, and `chartData()` default to it; per-call fields merge over it.

- strategy.putRatioBackspread().return.market.dividendYield?: number; default: not declared
- strategy.putRatioBackspread().return.market.expiry?: string; default: not declared — Default expiry for legs without their own `expiry` (single-expiry structures).

- strategy.putRatioBackspread().return.market.spot: number; default: not declared
- strategy.putRatioBackspread().return.market.volatility: number; default: not declared — Entry implied volatility (annualized decimal) for unpriced legs that carry no `impliedVolatility`
of their own — a leg's own volatility always wins, exactly as it does when `value()` marks it.
- strategy.putRatioBackspread().return.metrics: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffMetrics; default: not declared — Net debit/credit, max profit/loss, and breakevens. The expiration payoff is piecewise-linear, so
these are computed ANALYTICALLY from the kink set (every option strike plus every stock entry
price) and the tail slopes — never by sampling a coarse grid, which missed breakevens beyond the
last strike (e.g. a lone long stock, or a deep-ITM option) and ignored stock entry prices.
- strategy.putRatioBackspread().return.monteCarloProbability: (overrides: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloInput> & { seed: number; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloMetrics; default: not declared — Monte-Carlo probability metrics (spec §12.6): the simulated analogue of {@link probability}, for
cross-validation and path-dependent reads. Terminal lognormal paths give the probability of profit
and expected P&L (with a standard error); the probability of touching each breakeven is estimated
with the Brownian-bridge continuous-monitoring correction. Seeded and deterministic.
- strategy.putRatioBackspread().return.multiplier: number; default: not declared
- strategy.putRatioBackspread().return.netDebit: () => number; default: not declared — Net cash to enter (positive = debit, negative = credit).
- strategy.putRatioBackspread().return.payoff: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffResult; default: not declared — Expiration payoff metrics plus a chart-ready grid of points (spec §12.2). `prices` is an explicit
grid array or a `{ from, to, steps }` range; omit it to frame the strike-derived default window
(the same one a payoff diagram draws).

and expected P&L (with a standard error); the probability of touching each breakeven is estimated
with the Brownian-bridge continuous-monitoring correction. Seeded and deterministic.
- strategy.reverseJadeLizard().return.multiplier: number; default: not declared
- strategy.reverseJadeLizard().return.netDebit: () => number; default: not declared — Net cash to enter (positive = debit, negative = credit).
- strategy.reverseJadeLizard().return.payoff: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffResult; default: not declared — Expiration payoff metrics plus a chart-ready grid of points (spec §12.2). `prices` is an explicit
grid array or a `{ from, to, steps }` range; omit it to frame the strike-derived default window
(the same one a payoff diagram draws).
- strategy.reverseJadeLizard().return.pnlAtExpiry: (underlyingPrice: number) => number; default: not declared — Expiration P&L at an underlying price.
- strategy.reverseJadeLizard().return.premiumSource: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumSource; default: not declared — How the entry premiums were sourced: `'user'` (supplied) or `'model'` (priced from `market`).
- strategy.reverseJadeLizard().return.premiumVolatilitySource?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumVolatilitySource; default: not declared — When modeled, which volatility priced the entries (`'leg'`, `'position'` or `'mixed'`).
- strategy.reverseJadeLizard().return.probability: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMetrics; default: not declared — Probability & scenario metrics (spec §12.6): probability of profit, expected value, reward/risk,
and the probability of touching each breakeven — under an explicit, echoed lognormal model.
- strategy.reverseJadeLizard().return.scenarioTable: (options?: { market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; volatilityShocks?: number[]; daysForward?: number[]; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ScenarioTableResult; default: not declared — Scenario table (spec §12.6): mark-to-market P&L and Greeks across a grid of underlying prices,
additive vol shocks, and days forward — the standard "what-if" matrix for an options ticket.
- strategy.reverseJadeLizard().return.value: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketResult; default: not declared — Mark-to-market value, P&L, per-leg and aggregate Greeks via BSM (spec §12.3).
- strategy.reverseJadeLizard().return.whatIfCube: (options?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeOptions) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeResult; default: not declared — A what-if **cube**: the position marked over the full spot × vol-shock × days-forward grid, plus
the **optimal-exit surface** — for each (spot, vol) outcome, the day along the time axis that
optimizes P&L (`max-pnl` by default, or `min-pnl`). `scenarioTable` extended a dimension: it returns
a navigable cube (axes + row-major cells) with the reductions a trader wants, not a flat row list.

Every cell is a `value()` mark (time-aware, per-leg-IV, shock-through-to-leg-IV), so calendars and
per-leg volatilities behave identically. The optimal-exit surface is a CONDITIONAL what-if ("if the
underlying is here with this vol shock, which day marks best?"), not a path-dependent stopping rule.
See `docs/specs/what-if-cube.md`.
- strategy.reverseJadeLizard(config)?: PositionConfig | undefined; default: not declared
- strategy.reverseJadeLizard(config).expiry?: string; default: not declared — Position-level default expiry (`YYYY-MM-DD` → 16:00 ET, or a datetime) applied to every leg
that has no `expiry` of its own. Named builders route their input's `expiry` here. Precedence
per leg: `leg.expiry` > `expiry` > `market.expiry` (R4).
- strategy.reverseJadeLizard(config).market?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumMarket; default: not declared — Market for model-priced entry premiums (required when `premiums: 'model'` and any leg omits its
premium) — AND the position's remembered market (R5): `probability()`, `monteCarloProbability()`,
`value()`, `scenarioTable()`, and `chartData()` use it as their default market, with per-call
fields merged over it. Results echo `marketSource: 'construction' | 'call' | 'merged'`.
- strategy.reverseJadeLizard(config).multiplier?: number; default: not declared — Contract multiplier for option legs (default 100).
- strategy.reverseJadeLizard(config).premiums?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumSource; default: not declared — Entry-premium source: `'user'` (from the leg inputs, default) or `'model'` (priced from `market`).

- strategy.shortCall().return.chartData: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; include?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ChartInclude; market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; }) => Array<{ underlyingPrice: number; expirationPnl?: number; currentPnl?: number; delta?: number; theta?: number; }>; default: not declared — Chart-ready output (spec §12.5). Current P&L / live Greeks need a market: per-call fields
merge over the construction market (R5), so a model-premium position charts with no `market`.

for raw `strategy(legs)`. Because positions are immutable this can never go stale — but a
rebuilt-after-tweak position has no name. For "what is this NOW?" use `classifyStrategy`.
- strategy.shortCall().return.legs: readonly Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').Leg>[]; default: not declared — The resolved legs — a frozen snapshot (deep-copied at construction, `Object.freeze`d per leg
and as an array). A Position is immutable by design: to tweak a strategy, edit your own leg
list and rebuild with `strategy(editedLegs, config)` — every downstream calculation is generic
over the legs, so the rebuilt position needs no named builder. Mutating this array throws
instead of silently diverging from `assumptions()`/cached results.
- strategy.shortCall().return.market?: Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumMarket>; default: not declared — The market this position was built with, if any — a frozen copy (R5), so mutating the caller's

- strategy.shortCall().return.metrics: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffMetrics; default: not declared — Net debit/credit, max profit/loss, and breakevens. The expiration payoff is piecewise-linear, so
these are computed ANALYTICALLY from the kink set (every option strike plus every stock entry

last strike (e.g. a lone long stock, or a deep-ITM option) and ignored stock entry prices.

- strategy.shortCallCondor().return.market.spot: number; default: not declared

- strategy.shortCallCondor().return.metrics: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffMetrics; default: not declared — Net debit/credit, max profit/loss, and breakevens. The expiration payoff is piecewise-linear, so
these are computed ANALYTICALLY from the kink set (every option strike plus every stock entry
price) and the tail slopes — never by sampling a coarse grid, which missed breakevens beyond the
last strike (e.g. a lone long stock, or a deep-ITM option) and ignored stock entry prices.
- strategy.shortCallCondor().return.monteCarloProbability: (overrides: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloInput> & { seed: number; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloMetrics; default: not declared — Monte-Carlo probability metrics (spec §12.6): the simulated analogue of {@link probability}, for
cross-validation and path-dependent reads. Terminal lognormal paths give the probability of profit
and expected P&L (with a standard error); the probability of touching each breakeven is estimated
with the Brownian-bridge continuous-monitoring correction. Seeded and deterministic.

- strategy.shortCallCondor().return.netDebit: () => number; default: not declared — Net cash to enter (positive = debit, negative = credit).

- strategy.shortCallCondor().return.value: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketResult; default: not declared — Mark-to-market value, P&L, per-leg and aggregate Greeks via BSM (spec §12.3).
- strategy.shortCallCondor().return.whatIfCube: (options?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeOptions) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeResult; default: not declared — A what-if **cube**: the position marked over the full spot × vol-shock × days-forward grid, plus
the **optimal-exit surface** — for each (spot, vol) outcome, the day along the time axis that
optimizes P&L (`max-pnl` by default, or `min-pnl`). `scenarioTable` extended a dimension: it returns
a navigable cube (axes + row-major cells) with the reductions a trader wants, not a flat row list.

Every cell is a `value()` mark (time-aware, per-leg-IV, shock-through-to-leg-IV), so calendars and
per-leg volatilities behave identically. The optimal-exit surface is a CONDITIONAL what-if ("if the
underlying is here with this vol shock, which day marks best?"), not a path-dependent stopping rule.
See `docs/specs/what-if-cube.md`.

- strategy.shortPut().return.chartData: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; include?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ChartInclude; market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; }) => Array<{ underlyingPrice: number; expirationPnl?: number; currentPnl?: number; delta?: number; theta?: number; }>; default: not declared — Chart-ready output (spec §12.5). Current P&L / live Greeks need a market: per-call fields
merge over the construction market (R5), so a model-premium position charts with no `market`.
- strategy.shortPut().return.constructedAs?: string; default: not declared — PROVENANCE, not identity (dx §4.5): the named builder that constructed this position, absent
for raw `strategy(legs)`. Because positions are immutable this can never go stale — but a
rebuilt-after-tweak position has no name. For "what is this NOW?" use `classifyStrategy`.
- strategy.shortPut().return.legs: readonly Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').Leg>[]; default: not declared — The resolved legs — a frozen snapshot (deep-copied at construction, `Object.freeze`d per leg
and as an array). A Position is immutable by design: to tweak a strategy, edit your own leg
list and rebuild with `strategy(editedLegs, config)` — every downstream calculation is generic
over the legs, so the rebuilt position needs no named builder. Mutating this array throws
instead of silently diverging from `assumptions()`/cached results.
- strategy.shortPut().return.market?: Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumMarket>; default: not declared — The market this position was built with, if any — a frozen copy (R5), so mutating the caller's
market object later never silently retargets the position. `probability()`, `value()`,
`scenarioTable()`, and `chartData()` default to it; per-call fields merge over it.
- strategy.shortPut().return.market.asOf: string | number; default: not declared — Entry time (epoch ms or ISO). Each leg's entry `t = yearFraction(asOf, leg.expiry ?? market.expiry)`.
- strategy.shortPut().return.market.dividendYield?: number; default: not declared
- strategy.shortPut().return.market.expiry?: string; default: not declared — Default expiry for legs without their own `expiry` (single-expiry structures).
- strategy.shortPut().return.market.riskFreeRate: number; default: not declared
- strategy.shortPut().return.market.spot: number; default: not declared
- strategy.shortPut().return.market.volatility: number; default: not declared — Entry implied volatility (annualized decimal) for unpriced legs that carry no `impliedVolatility`
of their own — a leg's own volatility always wins, exactly as it does when `value()` marks it.
- strategy.shortPut().return.metrics: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffMetrics; default: not declared — Net debit/credit, max profit/loss, and breakevens. The expiration payoff is piecewise-linear, so
these are computed ANALYTICALLY from the kink set (every option strike plus every stock entry
price) and the tail slopes — never by sampling a coarse grid, which missed breakevens beyond the
last strike (e.g. a lone long stock, or a deep-ITM option) and ignored stock entry prices.
- strategy.shortPut().return.monteCarloProbability: (overrides: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloInput> & { seed: number; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloMetrics; default: not declared — Monte-Carlo probability metrics (spec §12.6): the simulated analogue of {@link probability}, for
cross-validation and path-dependent reads. Terminal lognormal paths give the probability of profit
and expected P&L (with a standard error); the probability of touching each breakeven is estimated
with the Brownian-bridge continuous-monitoring correction. Seeded and deterministic.
- strategy.shortPut().return.multiplier: number; default: not declared
- strategy.shortPut().return.netDebit: () => number; default: not declared — Net cash to enter (positive = debit, negative = credit).
- strategy.shortPut().return.payoff: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffResult; default: not declared — Expiration payoff metrics plus a chart-ready grid of points (spec §12.2). `prices` is an explicit
grid array or a `{ from, to, steps }` range; omit it to frame the strike-derived default window
(the same one a payoff diagram draws).
- strategy.shortPut().return.pnlAtExpiry: (underlyingPrice: number) => number; default: not declared — Expiration P&L at an underlying price.
- strategy.shortPut().return.premiumSource: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumSource; default: not declared — How the entry premiums were sourced: `'user'` (supplied) or `'model'` (priced from `market`).
- strategy.shortPut().return.premiumVolatilitySource?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumVolatilitySource; default: not declared — When modeled, which volatility priced the entries (`'leg'`, `'position'` or `'mixed'`).
- strategy.shortPut().return.probability: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMetrics; default: not declared — Probability & scenario metrics (spec §12.6): probability of profit, expected value, reward/risk,
and the probability of touching each breakeven — under an explicit, echoed lognormal model.
- strategy.shortPut().return.scenarioTable: (options?: { market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; volatilityShocks?: number[]; daysForward?: number[]; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ScenarioTableResult; default: not declared — Scenario table (spec §12.6): mark-to-market P&L and Greeks across a grid of underlying prices,
additive vol shocks, and days forward — the standard "what-if" matrix for an options ticket.
- strategy.shortPut().return.value: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketResult; default: not declared — Mark-to-market value, P&L, per-leg and aggregate Greeks via BSM (spec §12.3).
- strategy.shortPut().return.whatIfCube: (options?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeOptions) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeResult; default: not declared — A what-if **cube**: the position marked over the full spot × vol-shock × days-forward grid, plus
the **optimal-exit surface** — for each (spot, vol) outcome, the day along the time axis that
optimizes P&L (`max-pnl` by default, or `min-pnl`). `scenarioTable` extended a dimension: it returns
a navigable cube (axes + row-major cells) with the reductions a trader wants, not a flat row list.

Every cell is a `value()` mark (time-aware, per-leg-IV, shock-through-to-leg-IV), so calendars and
per-leg volatilities behave identically. The optimal-exit surface is a CONDITIONAL what-if ("if the
underlying is here with this vol shock, which day marks best?"), not a path-dependent stopping rule.
See `docs/specs/what-if-cube.md`.
- strategy.shortPut(config)?: PositionConfig | undefined; default: not declared
- strategy.shortPut(config).expiry?: string; default: not declared — Position-level default expiry (`YYYY-MM-DD` → 16:00 ET, or a datetime) applied to every leg
that has no `expiry` of its own. Named builders route their input's `expiry` here. Precedence
per leg: `leg.expiry` > `expiry` > `market.expiry` (R4).
- strategy.shortPut(config).market?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumMarket; default: not declared — Market for model-priced entry premiums (required when `premiums: 'model'` and any leg omits its
premium) — AND the position's remembered market (R5): `probability()`, `monteCarloProbability()`,
`value()`, `scenarioTable()`, and `chartData()` use it as their default market, with per-call
fields merged over it. Results echo `marketSource: 'construction' | 'call' | 'merged'`.
- strategy.shortPut(config).multiplier?: number; default: not declared — Contract multiplier for option legs (default 100).
- strategy.shortPut(config).premiums?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumSource; default: not declared — Entry-premium source: `'user'` (from the leg inputs, default) or `'model'` (priced from `market`).

fields merged over it. Results echo `marketSource: 'construction' | 'call' | 'merged'`.
- strategy.shortPutCondor(config).multiplier?: number; default: not declared — Contract multiplier for option legs (default 100).
- strategy.shortPutCondor(config).premiums?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumSource; default: not declared — Entry-premium source: `'user'` (from the leg inputs, default) or `'model'` (priced from `market`).
- strategy.shortPutCondor(input): import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').CondorInput; default: not declared
- strategy.shortPutCondor(input).expiry?: string; default: not declared — Expiry applied to every leg of this structure (`YYYY-MM-DD` → 16:00 ET, or a datetime).
- strategy.shortPutCondor(input).k1: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').Role; default: not declared
- strategy.shortPutCondor(input).k2: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').Role; default: not declared
- strategy.shortPutCondor(input).k3: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').Role; default: not declared
- strategy.shortPutCondor(input).k4: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').Role; default: not declared
- strategy.shortPutCondor(input).quantity?: number; default: not declared — Number of structures (default 1). Every leg scales by this.
- strategy.shortStraddle: (input: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ShortStraddleInput, config?: PositionConfig) => Position; default: not declared
- strategy.shortStraddle().return.assumptions: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PositionAssumptions; default: not declared — Position-construction assumptions (design law #3): whether the entry premiums were supplied by
the caller (`'user'`) or model-priced from a market (`'model'`), plus the contract multiplier.
- strategy.shortStraddle().return.chartData: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; include?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ChartInclude; market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; }) => Array<{ underlyingPrice: number; expirationPnl?: number; currentPnl?: number; delta?: number; theta?: number; }>; default: not declared — Chart-ready output (spec §12.5). Current P&L / live Greeks need a market: per-call fields
merge over the construction market (R5), so a model-premium position charts with no `market`.
- strategy.shortStraddle().return.constructedAs?: string; default: not declared — PROVENANCE, not identity (dx §4.5): the named builder that constructed this position, absent
for raw `strategy(legs)`. Because positions are immutable this can never go stale — but a
rebuilt-after-tweak position has no name. For "what is this NOW?" use `classifyStrategy`.
- strategy.shortStraddle().return.legs: readonly Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').Leg>[]; default: not declared — The resolved legs — a frozen snapshot (deep-copied at construction, `Object.freeze`d per leg
and as an array). A Position is immutable by design: to tweak a strategy, edit your own leg
list and rebuild with `strategy(editedLegs, config)` — every downstream calculation is generic
over the legs, so the rebuilt position needs no named builder. Mutating this array throws
instead of silently diverging from `assumptions()`/cached results.
- strategy.shortStraddle().return.market?: Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumMarket>; default: not declared — The market this position was built with, if any — a frozen copy (R5), so mutating the caller's
market object later never silently retargets the position. `probability()`, `value()`,
`scenarioTable()`, and `chartData()` default to it; per-call fields merge over it.
- strategy.shortStraddle().return.market.asOf: string | number; default: not declared — Entry time (epoch ms or ISO). Each leg's entry `t = yearFraction(asOf, leg.expiry ?? market.expiry)`.
- strategy.shortStraddle().return.market.dividendYield?: number; default: not declared
- strategy.shortStraddle().return.market.expiry?: string; default: not declared — Default expiry for legs without their own `expiry` (single-expiry structures).
- strategy.shortStraddle().return.market.riskFreeRate: number; default: not declared
- strategy.shortStraddle().return.market.spot: number; default: not declared
- strategy.shortStraddle().return.market.volatility: number; default: not declared — Entry implied volatility (annualized decimal) for unpriced legs that carry no `impliedVolatility`
of their own — a leg's own volatility always wins, exactly as it does when `value()` marks it.
- strategy.shortStraddle().return.metrics: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffMetrics; default: not declared — Net debit/credit, max profit/loss, and breakevens. The expiration payoff is piecewise-linear, so
these are computed ANALYTICALLY from the kink set (every option strike plus every stock entry
price) and the tail slopes — never by sampling a coarse grid, which missed breakevens beyond the
last strike (e.g. a lone long stock, or a deep-ITM option) and ignored stock entry prices.
- strategy.shortStraddle().return.monteCarloProbability: (overrides: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloInput> & { seed: number; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloMetrics; default: not declared — Monte-Carlo probability metrics (spec §12.6): the simulated analogue of {@link probability}, for
cross-validation and path-dependent reads. Terminal lognormal paths give the probability of profit
and expected P&L (with a standard error); the probability of touching each breakeven is estimated
with the Brownian-bridge continuous-monitoring correction. Seeded and deterministic.
- strategy.shortStraddle().return.multiplier: number; default: not declared
- strategy.shortStraddle().return.netDebit: () => number; default: not declared — Net cash to enter (positive = debit, negative = credit).
- strategy.shortStraddle().return.payoff: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffResult; default: not declared — Expiration payoff metrics plus a chart-ready grid of points (spec §12.2). `prices` is an explicit
grid array or a `{ from, to, steps }` range; omit it to frame the strike-derived default window
(the same one a payoff diagram draws).
- strategy.shortStraddle().return.pnlAtExpiry: (underlyingPrice: number) => number; default: not declared — Expiration P&L at an underlying price.
- strategy.shortStraddle().return.premiumSource: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumSource; default: not declared — How the entry premiums were sourced: `'user'` (supplied) or `'model'` (priced from `market`).
- strategy.shortStraddle().return.premiumVolatilitySource?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumVolatilitySource; default: not declared — When modeled, which volatility priced the entries (`'leg'`, `'position'` or `'mixed'`).
- strategy.shortStraddle().return.probability: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMetrics; default: not declared — Probability & scenario metrics (spec §12.6): probability of profit, expected value, reward/risk,
and the probability of touching each breakeven — under an explicit, echoed lognormal model.
- strategy.shortStraddle().return.scenarioTable: (options?: { market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; volatilityShocks?: number[]; daysForward?: number[]; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ScenarioTableResult; default: not declared — Scenario table (spec §12.6): mark-to-market P&L and Greeks across a grid of underlying prices,
additive vol shocks, and days forward — the standard "what-if" matrix for an options ticket.
- strategy.shortStraddle().return.value: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketResult; default: not declared — Mark-to-market value, P&L, per-leg and aggregate Greeks via BSM (spec §12.3).
- strategy.shortStraddle().return.whatIfCube: (options?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeOptions) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeResult; default: not declared — A what-if **cube**: the position marked over the full spot × vol-shock × days-forward grid, plus
the **optimal-exit surface** — for each (spot, vol) outcome, the day along the time axis that
optimizes P&L (`max-pnl` by default, or `min-pnl`). `scenarioTable` extended a dimension: it returns
a navigable cube (axes + row-major cells) with the reductions a trader wants, not a flat row list.

Every cell is a `value()` mark (time-aware, per-leg-IV, shock-through-to-leg-IV), so calendars and
per-leg volatilities behave identically. The optimal-exit surface is a CONDITIONAL what-if ("if the
underlying is here with this vol shock, which day marks best?"), not a path-dependent stopping rule.
See `docs/specs/what-if-cube.md`.

- strategy.shortSyntheticFuture().return.whatIfCube: (options?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeOptions) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeResult; default: not declared — A what-if **cube**: the position marked over the full spot × vol-shock × days-forward grid, plus
the **optimal-exit surface** — for each (spot, vol) outcome, the day along the time axis that
optimizes P&L (`max-pnl` by default, or `min-pnl`). `scenarioTable` extended a dimension: it returns
a navigable cube (axes + row-major cells) with the reductions a trader wants, not a flat row list.

Every cell is a `value()` mark (time-aware, per-leg-IV, shock-through-to-leg-IV), so calendars and
per-leg volatilities behave identically. The optimal-exit surface is a CONDITIONAL what-if ("if the
underlying is here with this vol shock, which day marks best?"), not a path-dependent stopping rule.
See `docs/specs/what-if-cube.md`.
- strategy.shortSyntheticFuture(config)?: PositionConfig | undefined; default: not declared
- strategy.shortSyntheticFuture(config).expiry?: string; default: not declared — Position-level default expiry (`YYYY-MM-DD` → 16:00 ET, or a datetime) applied to every leg
that has no `expiry` of its own. Named builders route their input's `expiry` here. Precedence
per leg: `leg.expiry` > `expiry` > `market.expiry` (R4).
- strategy.shortSyntheticFuture(config).market?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumMarket; default: not declared — Market for model-priced entry premiums (required when `premiums: 'model'` and any leg omits its
premium) — AND the position's remembered market (R5): `probability()`, `monteCarloProbability()`,
`value()`, `scenarioTable()`, and `chartData()` use it as their default market, with per-call
fields merged over it. Results echo `marketSource: 'construction' | 'call' | 'merged'`.
- strategy.shortSyntheticFuture(config).multiplier?: number; default: not declared — Contract multiplier for option legs (default 100).
- strategy.shortSyntheticFuture(config).premiums?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumSource; default: not declared — Entry-premium source: `'user'` (from the leg inputs, default) or `'model'` (priced from `market`).

- strategy.straddle().return.chartData: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; include?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ChartInclude; market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; }) => Array<{ underlyingPrice: number; expirationPnl?: number; currentPnl?: number; delta?: number; theta?: number; }>; default: not declared — Chart-ready output (spec §12.5). Current P&L / live Greeks need a market: per-call fields
merge over the construction market (R5), so a model-premium position charts with no `market`.

for raw `strategy(legs)`. Because positions are immutable this can never go stale — but a
rebuilt-after-tweak position has no name. For "what is this NOW?" use `classifyStrategy`.
- strategy.straddle().return.legs: readonly Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').Leg>[]; default: not declared — The resolved legs — a frozen snapshot (deep-copied at construction, `Object.freeze`d per leg
and as an array). A Position is immutable by design: to tweak a strategy, edit your own leg
list and rebuild with `strategy(editedLegs, config)` — every downstream calculation is generic
over the legs, so the rebuilt position needs no named builder. Mutating this array throws
instead of silently diverging from `assumptions()`/cached results.

- strategy.straddle().return.market.dividendYield?: number; default: not declared

of their own — a leg's own volatility always wins, exactly as it does when `value()` marks it.
- strategy.straddle().return.metrics: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffMetrics; default: not declared — Net debit/credit, max profit/loss, and breakevens. The expiration payoff is piecewise-linear, so
these are computed ANALYTICALLY from the kink set (every option strike plus every stock entry
price) and the tail slopes — never by sampling a coarse grid, which missed breakevens beyond the
last strike (e.g. a lone long stock, or a deep-ITM option) and ignored stock entry prices.
- strategy.straddle().return.monteCarloProbability: (overrides: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloInput> & { seed: number; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloMetrics; default: not declared — Monte-Carlo probability metrics (spec §12.6): the simulated analogue of {@link probability}, for
cross-validation and path-dependent reads. Terminal lognormal paths give the probability of profit
and expected P&L (with a standard error); the probability of touching each breakeven is estimated
with the Brownian-bridge continuous-monitoring correction. Seeded and deterministic.
- strategy.straddle().return.multiplier: number; default: not declared
- strategy.straddle().return.netDebit: () => number; default: not declared — Net cash to enter (positive = debit, negative = credit).
- strategy.straddle().return.payoff: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffResult; default: not declared — Expiration payoff metrics plus a chart-ready grid of points (spec §12.2). `prices` is an explicit
grid array or a `{ from, to, steps }` range; omit it to frame the strike-derived default window
(the same one a payoff diagram draws).

- strategy.strap().return.scenarioTable: (options?: { market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; volatilityShocks?: number[]; daysForward?: number[]; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ScenarioTableResult; default: not declared — Scenario table (spec §12.6): mark-to-market P&L and Greeks across a grid of underlying prices,
additive vol shocks, and days forward — the standard "what-if" matrix for an options ticket.
- strategy.strap().return.value: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketResult; default: not declared — Mark-to-market value, P&L, per-leg and aggregate Greeks via BSM (spec §12.3).
- strategy.strap().return.whatIfCube: (options?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeOptions) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeResult; default: not declared — A what-if **cube**: the position marked over the full spot × vol-shock × days-forward grid, plus
the **optimal-exit surface** — for each (spot, vol) outcome, the day along the time axis that
optimizes P&L (`max-pnl` by default, or `min-pnl`). `scenarioTable` extended a dimension: it returns
a navigable cube (axes + row-major cells) with the reductions a trader wants, not a flat row list.

Every cell is a `value()` mark (time-aware, per-leg-IV, shock-through-to-leg-IV), so calendars and
per-leg volatilities behave identically. The optimal-exit surface is a CONDITIONAL what-if ("if the
underlying is here with this vol shock, which day marks best?"), not a path-dependent stopping rule.
See `docs/specs/what-if-cube.md`.

- strategy.strap(config).expiry?: string; default: not declared — Position-level default expiry (`YYYY-MM-DD` → 16:00 ET, or a datetime) applied to every leg
that has no `expiry` of its own. Named builders route their input's `expiry` here. Precedence
per leg: `leg.expiry` > `expiry` > `market.expiry` (R4).

premium) — AND the position's remembered market (R5): `probability()`, `monteCarloProbability()`,
`value()`, `scenarioTable()`, and `chartData()` use it as their default market, with per-call
fields merged over it. Results echo `marketSource: 'construction' | 'call' | 'merged'`.

- strategy.strip().return.metrics: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffMetrics; default: not declared — Net debit/credit, max profit/loss, and breakevens. The expiration payoff is piecewise-linear, so

cross-validation and path-dependent reads. Terminal lognormal paths give the probability of profit
and expected P&L (with a standard error); the probability of touching each breakeven is estimated

- strategyOf().return.metrics: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffMetrics; default: not declared — Net debit/credit, max profit/loss, and breakevens. The expiration payoff is piecewise-linear, so
these are computed ANALYTICALLY from the kink set (every option strike plus every stock entry
price) and the tail slopes — never by sampling a coarse grid, which missed breakevens beyond the
last strike (e.g. a lone long stock, or a deep-ITM option) and ignored stock entry prices.
- strategyOf().return.monteCarloProbability: (overrides: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloInput> & { seed: number; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloMetrics; default: not declared — Monte-Carlo probability metrics (spec §12.6): the simulated analogue of {@link probability}, for
cross-validation and path-dependent reads. Terminal lognormal paths give the probability of profit
and expected P&L (with a standard error); the probability of touching each breakeven is estimated
with the Brownian-bridge continuous-monitoring correction. Seeded and deterministic.

- strategyOf().return.netDebit: () => number; default: not declared — Net cash to enter (positive = debit, negative = credit).
- strategyOf().return.payoff: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffResult; default: not declared — Expiration payoff metrics plus a chart-ready grid of points (spec §12.2). `prices` is an explicit
grid array or a `{ from, to, steps }` range; omit it to frame the strike-derived default window
(the same one a payoff diagram draws).

- strategyOf().return.premiumVolatilitySource?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumVolatilitySource; default: not declared — When modeled, which volatility priced the entries (`'leg'`, `'position'` or `'mixed'`).

and the probability of touching each breakeven — under an explicit, echoed lognormal model.

- strategyOf().return.whatIfCube: (options?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeOptions) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeResult; default: not declared — A what-if **cube**: the position marked over the full spot × vol-shock × days-forward grid, plus
the **optimal-exit surface** — for each (spot, vol) outcome, the day along the time axis that
optimizes P&L (`max-pnl` by default, or `min-pnl`). `scenarioTable` extended a dimension: it returns
a navigable cube (axes + row-major cells) with the reductions a trader wants, not a flat row list.

per-leg volatilities behave identically. The optimal-exit surface is a CONDITIONAL what-if ("if the
underlying is here with this vol shock, which day marks best?"), not a path-dependent stopping rule.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance#structure

Kind: namespace; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

```typescript
export declare const structure: typeof import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/structure');
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- ExposureProfile: typeof import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/structure').ExposureProfile; default: not declared — A computed exposure profile with levels, by-strike/by-expiry views, and scenario maps. R2
envelope: the sign convention and every resolved knob live in `assumptions`; model limitations
ride `diagnostics.warnings` as `model.limitation` entries — nothing is hoisted top-level.

SELECTIVE (selective Greeks and exposure spec, decision 11). A profile built with
`exposure({ …, metrics })` — or a shortcut such as {@link gammaExposure} — computed ONLY the
selected metrics and the Black–Scholes outputs they need. Its rows and `aggregate` carry exactly
those metrics; an uncomputed metric is ABSENT, never zero. `G` is the set the type guarantees (a
literal selection) and `P` the set that may be present (a dynamic selection); both default to every
metric — the full profile `exposure()` has always returned.
- ExposureProfile().return.aggregate: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/structure').ExposureAggregate<G, P>; default: not declared
- ExposureProfile().return.assumptions: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Assumptions<{ timeDecayDirection: 'perCalendarDayElapsed'; scanVolatilityPolicy: 'stickyStrike'; convention: { name: string; calls: number; puts: number; }; gammaUnit: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/structure').GammaUnit; priceSource: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').PriceSource; minTimeToExpiry: number; defaultMultiplier: number; metrics?: readonly import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/structure').ExposureMetric[]; }>; default: not declared
- ExposureProfile().return.atSpot: (spot: number) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/structure').AtSpotExposure<G, P>; default: not declared — Per-tick fast path: re-evaluate NET dollar-gamma (`gex`) and NET dollar-delta (`dex`) exposure at
a new `spot`, holding each contract's IV, time-to-expiry, and open interest FIXED (sticky-strike,
echoed in `assumptions.scanVolatilityPolicy`) — only spot moves and gamma/delta are re-evaluated. This is
the intraday dashboard path (one cheap greek pass per tick); a full {@link exposure} re-run — which
re-derives IV, the extended greeks, and levels — is the per-refresh path. At the profile's original
spot this reproduces `aggregate.gex`/`aggregate.dex` exactly (same operations, same order).

A selective profile re-evaluates only what it selected: a {@link gammaExposure} profile returns
`{ gex }` and computes gamma alone. A profile that selected neither `gex` nor `dex` refuses.

- ExposureProfile().return.byStrike: <M extends import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/structure').ExposureMetric = G>(metrics?: readonly M[]) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/structure').StrikeRow<M>[]; default: not declared — Chart-ready by-strike profile (one row per strike, totals summed), narrowed to `metrics` —

- ExposureProfile().return.netDrift: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/structure').NetDrift; default: not declared — Net dealer-hedging drift estimate (spec §11.5): the gamma regime (pinning vs trending), the

vol moves. An ESTIMATE from the positioning model — not a price forecast. An empty or
identically-zero book has no gamma structure: `zeroGamma`/`distanceToZeroGamma`/`gammaRegime`/
`bias` are all `null` (never fabricated), and the charm/vanna flows echo the (zero) aggregate.

With no `metrics` the default

outputs its metrics need, in one shared pass (`['gex']` evaluates gamma alone). A scenario is an
explicitly requested analysis, so it may use any metric, whatever this profile selected.

- deltaAdjustedPremium: (trades: readonly import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/structure').DirectionalFlowTrade[]) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/structure').DeltaAdjustedPremium; default: not declared — Delta-adjusted (delta-weighted) premium of a set of directional flow prints (spec §11.6, product
review §4). Weighting premium by |delta| turns raw premium into an approximate directional
exposure: deep-ITM bought calls move the tape far more than lottery-ticket wings of the same
premium. A print leans **bullish** when it is a bought call or a sold put and **bearish** when it
is a bought put or a sold call. Pure; greeks are an explicit input.
- deltaAdjustedPremium().return.bearishPremium: number; default: not declared — Σ |delta|·premium over bearish prints (bought puts / sold calls).
- deltaAdjustedPremium().return.bullishPremium: number; default: not declared — Σ |delta|·premium over prints whose directional lean is bullish (bought calls / sold puts).
- deltaAdjustedPremium().return.netDirectional: number; default: not declared — `bullishPremium − bearishPremium` — net directional delta-adjusted premium (> 0 = net bullish).
- deltaAdjustedPremium().return.totalDeltaAdjusted: number; default: not declared — Σ |delta|·premium regardless of direction — the total delta-weighted premium.
- deltaAdjustedPremium(trades): readonly import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/structure').DirectionalFlowTrade[]; default: not declared

- exposureFromGreeks: <const S extends readonly import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/structure').SuppliedExposureMetric[] | undefined = undefined, const B extends boolean | undefined = undefined>(request: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/structure').SuppliedExposureRequest<S, B>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/structure').SuppliedExposureReport<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/structure').GuaranteedSuppliedExposureMetrics<S>, import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/structure').PossibleSuppliedExposureMetrics<S>, B>; default: not declared — Account for caller-supplied signed Greeks at one spot snapshot. GEX is
`gamma * openInterest * multiplier * gexSign * spot * (spot * 0.01)` for
`per1PercentMove`, or `gamma * openInterest * multiplier * gexSign * spot` for
`perPoint`. DEX is `delta * openInterest * multiplier * dexSign * spot`.
A negative put delta is used unchanged: a negative DEX position sign reverses it ONCE.
Gamma inputs are signed delta-per-spot-point, never dollar gamma or per-contract gamma.

Quotes, contracts, Greeks and market observations are open to harmless decoration; the request,
config and both convention objects are closed. Only consumed fields are validated/copied.
Quote timestamp/source describe the supplied OI snapshot, not a fabricated exchange OI update.
Caller must align currency, deliverable basis, source units and non-overlapping OI observations.
Repeated underlying/type/style/strike/expiry identities are counted and warned, never silently
deduplicated; differing multipliers, sources, timestamps and provider metadata do not hide repeats.
Coverage describes only supplied quote rows, not a full market universe. Empty or entirely
excluded chains produce empty sums, NOT an estimate that market exposure is zero.
Every row is validated, including rows later excluded. Missing OI/Greeks, expired contracts
(`expiresAt <= asOf`), future observations (`timestampMs > asOf`) and stale observations
(`asOf - timestampMs > maximumObservationAgeMs`) are excluded with retained lineage.
Zero OI is a valid included zero contribution. Missing multipliers require an explicit fallback.

Contributions sort by expiry instant, strike, call-before-put, then original input index.
Aggregates sort numerically by strike/expiry instant and include excluded-only buckets as zero.
At most 100,000 dense quote rows and 512 characters per consumed string are accepted; lengths
are refused before traversal. Nonrepresentable contributions or aggregates throw InputError.
No rate/dividend model is invented and fixed supplied Greeks cannot yield scenario repricing,
gamma flips, or model-driven hedging forecasts. Use exposure() for model-based scenarios.

`metrics` selects GEX, DEX or both (omitted: both, exactly as before). `['gex']` reads only supplied
gamma, `gexConvention` and `gammaUnit` — a row's delta may be absent — and `['dex']` only supplied
delta and `dexConvention`. The unselected metric's contribution sign and value, totals, units and
convention echoes are absent from the report (never zero), and `assumptions.metrics` echoes the
selection. A GEX+DEX report requires both supplied Greeks on every row that supplies Greeks, so the
two metrics always cover the same included rows. Modeled Greeks are never substituted. Name the
report as `SuppliedExposureReport` and its input as `SuppliedExposureInput`: `Parameters<typeof
exposureFromGreeks>` and `ReturnType<…>` see the selection's general (dynamic) form.

`breakdowns: false` leaves out `byStrike` and `byExpiry` for a caller that aggregates the
contributions itself: no grouping and no per-group exact totals (two thirds of the summation),
with every other field unchanged and `assumptions.breakdowns` echoing the flag.

- optionFlowDrift: (input: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/structure').OptionFlowDriftInput) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/structure').OptionFlowDriftResult; default: not declared — Aggregate observed raw option trading premium for one explicit session. Example:
`optionFlowDrift({ trades, session: { date: '2026-06-04' }, config: { symbol: 'SPY' } })`.

Each minute/bucket exposes separate `change` and `cumulative` accounting. Buy calls / sell puts
map to bullish premium and volume; sell calls / buy puts map to bearish. Unknowns move neither
drift nor directional volume, but contribute all their premium to worst-case sign bounds.
Classification coverage is a share of premium, NOT a success probability or confidence band.
No delta weighting, dealer-position inference, multi-leg netting, fees, P&L, or income prediction.
All combined premiums must already use one currency; this operation does not convert FX.

Heuristics apply to the SAME window's totals: no prints/zero premium → no-signal; coverage below
the threshold → low-coverage; opposing nonzero volume/premium signs → volume-opposed; call > 0
and put < 0 → bullish-expansion (reverse → bearish-expansion); remaining nonzero net → mixed-flow.
These are descriptive accounting rules, not trading recommendations or measured predictiveness.

Session/cutoff and bucket ends are exclusive. A bucket is a completed END-of-interval observation,
not a value available at its start. Prices carry forward only from observations in this session;
missing prices stay null. Overlay ties prefer underlying trades, then quotes, then option-print
underlyingPrice, with last input winning within a source. Caller timestamps must express when
data was available; embedded underlyingPrice is assumed available at its option print timestamp.
Late vendor corrections/publication delays cannot be reconstructed from these fields alone.

Trades are validated even outside scope, then stably sorted without mutation. Repeated explicit
IDs fail. ID-less prints identical in the consumed trade fields fail (including sequence/venue);
give genuinely distinct identical executions distinct IDs. Vendor metadata stays open. No print
is silently deduplicated; malformed data or unrepresentable arithmetic throws typed InputError.
- optionFlowDrift().return.assumptions: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Assumptions<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/structure').OptionFlowDriftAssumptions>; default: not declared — Every applied convention, echoed back.
- optionFlowDrift().return.diagnostics: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Diagnostics; default: not declared — How the value was computed, plus any warnings.
- optionFlowDrift().return.provenance?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Provenance; default: not declared — Optional data lineage when the inputs came from a provider.
- optionFlowDrift().return.value: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/structure').OptionFlowDriftValue; default: not declared — The computed value. Never `NaN` or `±Infinity`: a value the model cannot produce is `null`
beside a diagnostic that says why (Law 7 — a warning never licenses a non-finite number).

- speedExposure().return.atSpot: (spot: number) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/structure').AtSpotExposure<'speed', 'speed'>; default: not declared — Per-tick fast path: re-evaluate NET dollar-gamma (`gex`) and NET dollar-delta (`dex`) exposure at
a new `spot`, holding each contract's IV, time-to-expiry, and open interest FIXED (sticky-strike,
echoed in `assumptions.scanVolatilityPolicy`) — only spot moves and gamma/delta are re-evaluated. This is
the intraday dashboard path (one cheap greek pass per tick); a full {@link exposure} re-run — which
re-derives IV, the extended greeks, and levels — is the per-refresh path. At the profile's original
spot this reproduces `aggregate.gex`/`aggregate.dex` exactly (same operations, same order).

A selective profile re-evaluates only what it selected: a {@link gammaExposure} profile returns
`{ gex }` and computes gamma alone. A profile that selected neither `gex` nor `dex` refuses.
- speedExposure().return.byExpiry: <M extends import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/structure').ExposureMetric = 'speed'>(metrics?: readonly M[] | undefined) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/structure').ExpiryRow<M>[]; default: not declared — Chart-ready by-expiry profile (one row per expiry), narrowed to `metrics` — by default this
profile's own metrics. A metric this profile did not compute is refused.
- speedExposure().return.byStrike: <M extends import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/structure').ExposureMetric = 'speed'>(metrics?: readonly M[] | undefined) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/structure').StrikeRow<M>[]; default: not declared — Chart-ready by-strike profile (one row per strike, totals summed), narrowed to `metrics` —

`'gex'` is requested each row ALSO carries the call/put split — `callGex`/`putGex`/`callOpenInterest`/`putOpenInterest`
(the {@link GexSplit} columns) — for the canonical dashboard chart (call bars up, put bars down).
`callGex + putGex` equals the row's net `gex` and `callOpenInterest + putOpenInterest` the strike's total OI (WS4.5).

- speedExposure().return.netDrift: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/structure').NetDrift; default: not declared — Net dealer-hedging drift estimate (spec §11.5): the gamma regime (pinning vs trending), the

vol moves. An ESTIMATE from the positioning model — not a price forecast. An empty or
identically-zero book has no gamma structure: `zeroGamma`/`distanceToZeroGamma`/`gammaRegime`/
`bias` are all `null` (never fabricated), and the charm/vanna flows echo the (zero) aggregate.

outputs its metrics need, in one shared pass (`['gex']` evaluates gamma alone). A scenario is an

- unusualness: (value: number, baseline: ArrayLike<number>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/structure').Unusualness; default: not declared — Unusualness of a reading versus a caller-supplied baseline history (spec §11.6, product review §4):

baseline has no defined spread, so the z-score is `null` (never fabricated).

- unusualness().return.mean: number; default: not declared
- unusualness().return.percentile: number; default: not declared — Percentile of `value` within the baseline, in `[0, 100]` (share strictly below).
- unusualness().return.stdev: number; default: not declared — Sample standard deviation of the baseline.
- unusualness().return.zScore: number | null; default: not declared — `(value − mean) / stdev` of the baseline; `null` when the baseline is flat (no defined z).

- vommaExposure().return.byExpiry: <M extends import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/structure').ExposureMetric = 'vomma'>(metrics?: readonly M[] | undefined) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/structure').ExpiryRow<M>[]; default: not declared — Chart-ready by-expiry profile (one row per expiry), narrowed to `metrics` — by default this
profile's own metrics. A metric this profile did not compute is refused.
- vommaExposure().return.byStrike: <M extends import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/structure').ExposureMetric = 'vomma'>(metrics?: readonly M[] | undefined) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/structure').StrikeRow<M>[]; default: not declared — Chart-ready by-strike profile (one row per strike, totals summed), narrowed to `metrics` —
by default this profile's own metrics (every metric for a full profile). When
`'gex'` is requested each row ALSO carries the call/put split — `callGex`/`putGex`/`callOpenInterest`/`putOpenInterest`
(the {@link GexSplit} columns) — for the canonical dashboard chart (call bars up, put bars down).
`callGex + putGex` equals the row's net `gex` and `callOpenInterest + putOpenInterest` the strike's total OI (WS4.5).
A metric this profile did not compute is refused, not reported as zero.
- vommaExposure().return.contracts: readonly Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/structure').ContractExposureRow<'vomma', 'vomma'>>[]; default: not declared — Frozen result rows — a profile is a snapshot; mutate a copy, never the result.
- vommaExposure().return.diagnostics: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Diagnostics; default: not declared
- vommaExposure().return.levels: (options?: { pinRiskBand?: number; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/structure').Levels; default: not declared — Dealer-positioning levels (walls, zero-gamma, max pain, pin risk). On a selective profile this
computes what it reads — per-contract gex, gamma, vanna and charm at the profile's spot, plus a
gamma-only zero-gamma sweep — and returns exactly what a full profile returns.
- vommaExposure().return.netDrift: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/structure').NetDrift; default: not declared — Net dealer-hedging drift estimate (spec §11.5): the gamma regime (pinning vs trending), the
zero-gamma attractor, and the aggregate charm/vanna hedging flows that push spot over time and as
vol moves. An ESTIMATE from the positioning model — not a price forecast. An empty or
identically-zero book has no gamma structure: `zeroGamma`/`distanceToZeroGamma`/`gammaRegime`/
`bias` are all `null` (never fabricated), and the charm/vanna flows echo the (zero) aggregate.
On a selective profile the charm and vanna aggregates are computed here if they were not selected.
- vommaExposure().return.scenarioMap: <M extends import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/structure').ExposureMetric = import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/structure').DefaultScenarioMetric>(options?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/structure').ScenarioMapOptions<M>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/structure').ScenarioMap<M>; default: not declared — Recompute aggregate metrics across a spot × volatilityShock × time grid. With no `metrics` the default
set is `['gex','dex','vanna','charm']` — and the return type narrows to exactly those, so it never
over-claims the metrics not actually computed (WS2.4). Each cell evaluates only the Black–Scholes
outputs its metrics need, in one shared pass (`['gex']` evaluates gamma alone). A scenario is an
explicitly requested analysis, so it may use any metric, whatever this profile selected.

- RuleBuilder: typeof import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis').RuleBuilder; default: not declared — Builds one rule as a chain of conditions. Evaluation is STRICT LEFT-TO-RIGHT with NO operator
precedence: each `.and(c)` / `.or(c)` folds `c` into the accumulated result immediately, so
`when(a).or(b).and(c)` evaluates as `(a || b) && c` — NOT `a || (b && c)`. When you need
grouping, compose a single condition instead (e.g. with `condition()` / `not()`), or order the
chain so left-to-right folding expresses your intent.
- RuleBuilder().return.and: (condition: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis').Condition) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis').RuleBuilder; default: not declared — Fold `c` into the accumulated result with AND (left-to-right, no precedence — class doc).
- RuleBuilder().return.emit: (label: string) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis').SignalBuilder; default: not declared — Finalise the rule with a label and return to the signal builder.
- RuleBuilder().return.or: (condition: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis').Condition) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis').RuleBuilder; default: not declared — Fold `c` into the accumulated result with OR (left-to-right, no precedence — class doc).

- SCHEMA_VERSION: 3; default: not declared — Current snapshot schema version. Bump when a stored snapshot's shape changes incompatibly.

2 — the flat `{ kind, v?, ...state }` shape became the explicit `{ kind, schemaVersion, state }`
envelope.
3 — non-finite numbers inside `state` are ENCODED (see {@link encodeNonFinite}). Before this,
`JSON.stringify` turned every one of them into `null`, so a snapshot could not round-trip through
the very format it exists for.

No legacy parser is retained at either step: pre-1.0 corrections are clean (law N9), and an older
snapshot is rejected by {@link checkSnapshotVersion} with a teaching error rather than misread.

- alignToBars: (input: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis/resample').AlignToBarsInput) => number[]; default: not declared — Project a higher-timeframe series onto a lower-timeframe bar index, strictly causally (spec §13,
WS6.2). `higherSeries[j]` is a value computed on `higherBars[j]`, whose bucket `[ts, ts + iv)` is
usable only once it has CLOSED, i.e. at LTF times `≥ higherBars[j].timestampMs + intervalMs`. The LTF value at bar `i`
is a step-hold of the last HTF bar that has closed by `lowerBars[i].timestampMs`; it is `NaN` before the
first HTF bucket closes. No LTF output ever depends on an unclosed HTF bar — the `request.security`
lookahead is impossible by construction.

`higherBars` must be ascending by `timestampMs`. The interval is `options.intervalMs` if given, else inferred as the
smallest positive gap between consecutive HTF bars (with a single HTF bar and no `intervalMs`, the
bar never becomes usable and every output is `NaN`).
- alignToBars(input): import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis/resample').AlignToBarsInput; default: not declared
- alignToBars(input).higherBars: ArrayLike<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis').TimeBar>; default: not declared
- alignToBars(input).higherSeries: ArrayLike<number>; default: not declared
- alignToBars(input).lowerBars: ArrayLike<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis').TimeBar>; default: not declared
- alignToBars(input).options?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis').AlignOptions; default: not declared

- alma.explain().return.diagnostics.converged?: boolean; default: not declared — Whether an iterative procedure converged. `false` means the value is not trustworthy.
- alma.explain().return.diagnostics.decomposition?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Named intermediate quantities the value decomposes into — a par spread's protection leg and
risky annuity, a forward variance's near/far legs. The H-series explain paths disclose their
arithmetic here so a caller can audit the ratio, not just receive it (3B.3).
- alma.explain().return.diagnostics.engine?: string; default: not declared — Pricing/solver engine name, e.g. `black-scholes-merton`.
- alma.explain().return.diagnostics.finiteDifferenceBumps?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Finite-difference engines: the ACTUAL bump sizes used for FD Greeks (spec P2.3) — adaptive
near the vol/time boundaries, so the caller can see exactly what was differenced.
Keys: `spotStep`, `volatilityStep`, `timeStepYears`, `rateStep`, and — extended Greeks only —
`dividendYieldStep`. Each is the actual step differenced, in the unit of the coordinate it
bumps. (This doc named the retired `hS`/`hSig`/`hT`/`hR`/`hQ` keys for one release after the
emit sites had moved to the semantic names, so a caller following it read `undefined`.)

- alma.explain().return.diagnostics.method?: string; default: not declared — Numerical method, e.g. `closed-form`, `brent`, `finite-difference`.
- alma.explain().return.diagnostics.selection?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing').SelectionReport; default: not declared — The structured engine-selection report (Gate C, `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing`): who was selected,
why, and — for automatic selection — every candidate considered with its verdict. This is the
machine-readable superset of `engine` + `autoReason` (which remain for compatibility);
`selected.name` always agrees with `engine` when both are present.
- alma.explain().return.diagnostics.timingMs?: number; default: not declared — Wall-clock timing in milliseconds, when measured.

- asin.explain().return.diagnostics.autoReason?: string; default: not declared — When a meta-engine (e.g. `engines.auto()`) selected a delegate, this is a one-sentence,
human-readable explanation of WHY that delegate was chosen (`engine` then names the delegate).
Absent when no auto-selection took place.
- asin.explain().return.diagnostics.converged?: boolean; default: not declared — Whether an iterative procedure converged. `false` means the value is not trustworthy.
- asin.explain().return.diagnostics.decomposition?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Named intermediate quantities the value decomposes into — a par spread's protection leg and
risky annuity, a forward variance's near/far legs. The H-series explain paths disclose their
arithmetic here so a caller can audit the ratio, not just receive it (3B.3).
- asin.explain().return.diagnostics.engine?: string; default: not declared — Pricing/solver engine name, e.g. `black-scholes-merton`.
- asin.explain().return.diagnostics.finiteDifferenceBumps?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Finite-difference engines: the ACTUAL bump sizes used for FD Greeks (spec P2.3) — adaptive
near the vol/time boundaries, so the caller can see exactly what was differenced.
Keys: `spotStep`, `volatilityStep`, `timeStepYears`, `rateStep`, and — extended Greeks only —
`dividendYieldStep`. Each is the actual step differenced, in the unit of the coordinate it
bumps. (This doc named the retired `hS`/`hSig`/`hT`/`hR`/`hQ` keys for one release after the
emit sites had moved to the semantic names, so a caller following it read `undefined`.)
- asin.explain().return.diagnostics.iterations?: number; default: not declared — Iteration count for iterative methods.
- asin.explain().return.diagnostics.method?: string; default: not declared — Numerical method, e.g. `closed-form`, `brent`, `finite-difference`.
- asin.explain().return.diagnostics.selection?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing').SelectionReport; default: not declared — The structured engine-selection report (Gate C, `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing`): who was selected,
why, and — for automatic selection — every candidate considered with its verdict. This is the
machine-readable superset of `engine` + `autoReason` (which remain for compatibility);
`selected.name` always agrees with `engine` when both are present.
- asin.explain().return.diagnostics.timingMs?: number; default: not declared — Wall-clock timing in milliseconds, when measured.
- asin.explain().return.diagnostics.warmup?: number; default: not declared — Series facades: number of leading output slots that are warmup sentinels (null/NaN) while the
computation seeds. Equals the input length when the indicator never emitted.
- asin.explain().return.diagnostics.warnings: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').QuantWarning[]; default: not declared — Structured warnings; always present (possibly empty).
- asin.explain().return.provenance?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Provenance; default: not declared — Optional data lineage when the inputs came from a provider.
- asin.explain().return.value: number[]; default: not declared — The computed value. Never `NaN` or `±Infinity`: a value the model cannot produce is `null`
beside a diagnostic that says why (Law 7 — a warning never licenses a non-finite number).
