- bbands.explain().return.diagnostics.autoReason?: string; default: not declared — When a meta-engine (e.g. `engines.auto()`) selected a delegate, this is a one-sentence,
human-readable explanation of WHY that delegate was chosen (`engine` then names the delegate).
Absent when no auto-selection took place.
- bbands.explain().return.diagnostics.converged?: boolean; default: not declared — Whether an iterative procedure converged. `false` means the value is not trustworthy.
- bbands.explain().return.diagnostics.decomposition?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Named intermediate quantities the value decomposes into — a par spread's protection leg and
risky annuity, a forward variance's near/far legs. The H-series explain paths disclose their
arithmetic here so a caller can audit the ratio, not just receive it (3B.3).
- bbands.explain().return.diagnostics.engine?: string; default: not declared — Pricing/solver engine name, e.g. `black-scholes-merton`.
- bbands.explain().return.diagnostics.finiteDifferenceBumps?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Finite-difference engines: the ACTUAL bump sizes used for FD Greeks (spec P2.3) — adaptive
near the vol/time boundaries, so the caller can see exactly what was differenced.
Keys: `spotStep`, `volatilityStep`, `timeStepYears`, `rateStep`, and — extended Greeks only —
`dividendYieldStep`. Each is the actual step differenced, in the unit of the coordinate it
bumps. (This doc named the retired `hS`/`hSig`/`hT`/`hR`/`hQ` keys for one release after the
emit sites had moved to the semantic names, so a caller following it read `undefined`.)

why, and — for automatic selection — every candidate considered with its verdict. This is the
machine-readable superset of `engine` + `autoReason` (which remain for compatibility);

- brar.stream().return.peek: (input: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis').BarInput) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis').BrarPoint | null; default: not declared — The value that WOULD result from `next(input)` applied to the committed state, WITHOUT committing

closed bars. The default cost is O(snapshot) per call (clone-and-apply); indicators may override

intraday strength against the open.
- brar.stream().return.value.willingnessIndex: number; default: not declared — BR, the willingness index: `100 · Σmax(0, high − prevClose) / Σmax(0, prevClose − low)`.
Measures strength against the PRIOR close, which is what distinguishes it from AR.

- candleAverage: (bars: ArrayLike<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis').BarInput>, setting: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis').CandleSetting) => number[]; default: not declared — TA-Lib's `TA_CANDLEAVERAGE` at every bar: `factor · (avg of `range` over the preceding `averagePeriod`
bars) / denom`, where `denom = 2` for the Shadows range type (it sums two shadows) else `1`. With
`averagePeriod = 0` the current bar's own range is used. Bars before the trailing window is full get
`NaN` (the pattern is in its lookback there).

closed bars. The default cost is O(snapshot) per call (clone-and-apply); indicators may override
with an O(1) form later.

- choppinessIndex.explain().return.diagnostics.finiteDifferenceBumps?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Finite-difference engines: the ACTUAL bump sizes used for FD Greeks (spec P2.3) — adaptive
near the vol/time boundaries, so the caller can see exactly what was differenced.

`dividendYieldStep`. Each is the actual step differenced, in the unit of the coordinate it
bumps. (This doc named the retired `hS`/`hSig`/`hT`/`hR`/`hQ` keys for one release after the
emit sites had moved to the semantic names, so a caller following it read `undefined`.)

why, and — for automatic selection — every candidate considered with its verdict. This is the
machine-readable superset of `engine` + `autoReason` (which remain for compatibility);

arithmetic here so a caller can audit the ratio, not just receive it (3B.3).

risky annuity, a forward variance's near/far legs. The H-series explain paths disclose their
arithmetic here so a caller can audit the ratio, not just receive it (3B.3).
- cvd.explain().return.diagnostics.engine?: string; default: not declared — Pricing/solver engine name, e.g. `black-scholes-merton`.
- cvd.explain().return.diagnostics.finiteDifferenceBumps?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Finite-difference engines: the ACTUAL bump sizes used for FD Greeks (spec P2.3) — adaptive
near the vol/time boundaries, so the caller can see exactly what was differenced.
Keys: `spotStep`, `volatilityStep`, `timeStepYears`, `rateStep`, and — extended Greeks only —
`dividendYieldStep`. Each is the actual step differenced, in the unit of the coordinate it
bumps. (This doc named the retired `hS`/`hSig`/`hT`/`hR`/`hQ` keys for one release after the
emit sites had moved to the semantic names, so a caller following it read `undefined`.)
- cvd.explain().return.diagnostics.iterations?: number; default: not declared — Iteration count for iterative methods.
- cvd.explain().return.diagnostics.method?: string; default: not declared — Numerical method, e.g. `closed-form`, `brent`, `finite-difference`.
- cvd.explain().return.diagnostics.selection?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing').SelectionReport; default: not declared — The structured engine-selection report (Gate C, `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing`): who was selected,
why, and — for automatic selection — every candidate considered with its verdict. This is the
machine-readable superset of `engine` + `autoReason` (which remain for compatibility);
`selected.name` always agrees with `engine` when both are present.
- cvd.explain().return.diagnostics.timingMs?: number; default: not declared — Wall-clock timing in milliseconds, when measured.

computation seeds. Equals the input length when the indicator never emitted.

beside a diagnostic that says why (Law 7 — a warning never licenses a non-finite number).

- elderRay.explain().return.diagnostics.finiteDifferenceBumps?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Finite-difference engines: the ACTUAL bump sizes used for FD Greeks (spec P2.3) — adaptive
near the vol/time boundaries, so the caller can see exactly what was differenced.
Keys: `spotStep`, `volatilityStep`, `timeStepYears`, `rateStep`, and — extended Greeks only —
`dividendYieldStep`. Each is the actual step differenced, in the unit of the coordinate it
bumps. (This doc named the retired `hS`/`hSig`/`hT`/`hR`/`hQ` keys for one release after the
emit sites had moved to the semantic names, so a caller following it read `undefined`.)

why, and — for automatic selection — every candidate considered with its verdict. This is the
machine-readable superset of `engine` + `autoReason` (which remain for compatibility);

- equalLows.explain().return.diagnostics.finiteDifferenceBumps?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Finite-difference engines: the ACTUAL bump sizes used for FD Greeks (spec P2.3) — adaptive

then CALL THE INDICATOR, then build the auto-name from the parameters it just accepted.

The first version built the name first — `` `sma_${field}_${parameters.period}` `` — so a caller
who omitted `parameters` got `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'period')`
from the pipeline instead of `sma`'s own teaching `InputError`. Worse for `rsi` and `atr`, whose
direct forms default to 14: the fluent wrapper was STRICTER than the thing it wraps. Calling the
indicator first delegates every parameter question to the validator that owns it.

- forceIndex.explain().return.diagnostics.finiteDifferenceBumps?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Finite-difference engines: the ACTUAL bump sizes used for FD Greeks (spec P2.3) — adaptive

one closed. A gap fills when a later bar trades back to the prior close.

A gap requires the open to leave the prior bar's RANGE — above its high or below its low — which
is the definition {@link gaps} uses and the only one that means anything on a real tape. This
function previously fired on any open that merely differed from the prior close: on a 500-bar
random walk with no true gaps, `gaps()` returned 0 events and this returned 499, one per bar. The
two are now the same event universe, so `sizeFraction` and `minSizeFraction` mean the same thing
in both and a caller can pair them.

`minSizeFraction` filters small gaps as a FRACTION of the prior close (`0.005` = 0.5%), the same
unit `sizeFraction` reports. Default 0 — every detected gap.

`sizeFraction` is measured from the prior CLOSE — the level a fill has to trade back to — and
`minSizeFraction` filters in that same unit (`0.005` = 0.5%). {@link gapFill} detects exactly these
events and adds fill tracking.

- hma.explain().return.diagnostics.autoReason?: string; default: not declared — When a meta-engine (e.g. `engines.auto()`) selected a delegate, this is a one-sentence,
human-readable explanation of WHY that delegate was chosen (`engine` then names the delegate).
Absent when no auto-selection took place.
- hma.explain().return.diagnostics.converged?: boolean; default: not declared — Whether an iterative procedure converged. `false` means the value is not trustworthy.
- hma.explain().return.diagnostics.decomposition?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Named intermediate quantities the value decomposes into — a par spread's protection leg and
risky annuity, a forward variance's near/far legs. The H-series explain paths disclose their
arithmetic here so a caller can audit the ratio, not just receive it (3B.3).
- hma.explain().return.diagnostics.engine?: string; default: not declared — Pricing/solver engine name, e.g. `black-scholes-merton`.
- hma.explain().return.diagnostics.finiteDifferenceBumps?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Finite-difference engines: the ACTUAL bump sizes used for FD Greeks (spec P2.3) — adaptive
near the vol/time boundaries, so the caller can see exactly what was differenced.
Keys: `spotStep`, `volatilityStep`, `timeStepYears`, `rateStep`, and — extended Greeks only —
`dividendYieldStep`. Each is the actual step differenced, in the unit of the coordinate it
bumps. (This doc named the retired `hS`/`hSig`/`hT`/`hR`/`hQ` keys for one release after the
emit sites had moved to the semantic names, so a caller following it read `undefined`.)
- hma.explain().return.diagnostics.iterations?: number; default: not declared — Iteration count for iterative methods.
- hma.explain().return.diagnostics.method?: string; default: not declared — Numerical method, e.g. `closed-form`, `brent`, `finite-difference`.
- hma.explain().return.diagnostics.selection?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing').SelectionReport; default: not declared — The structured engine-selection report (Gate C, `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing`): who was selected,
why, and — for automatic selection — every candidate considered with its verdict. This is the
machine-readable superset of `engine` + `autoReason` (which remain for compatibility);
`selected.name` always agrees with `engine` when both are present.
- hma.explain().return.diagnostics.timingMs?: number; default: not declared — Wall-clock timing in milliseconds, when measured.
- hma.explain().return.diagnostics.warmup?: number; default: not declared — Series facades: number of leading output slots that are warmup sentinels (null/NaN) while the
computation seeds. Equals the input length when the indicator never emitted.
- hma.explain().return.diagnostics.warnings: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').QuantWarning[]; default: not declared — Structured warnings; always present (possibly empty).

- hma.explain().return.value: number[]; default: not declared — The computed value. Never `NaN` or `±Infinity`: a value the model cannot produce is `null`
beside a diagnostic that says why (Law 7 — a warning never licenses a non-finite number).

with an O(1) form later.

- htTrendMode.explain().return.diagnostics.autoReason?: string; default: not declared — When a meta-engine (e.g. `engines.auto()`) selected a delegate, this is a one-sentence,
human-readable explanation of WHY that delegate was chosen (`engine` then names the delegate).
Absent when no auto-selection took place.
- htTrendMode.explain().return.diagnostics.converged?: boolean; default: not declared — Whether an iterative procedure converged. `false` means the value is not trustworthy.
- htTrendMode.explain().return.diagnostics.decomposition?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Named intermediate quantities the value decomposes into — a par spread's protection leg and
risky annuity, a forward variance's near/far legs. The H-series explain paths disclose their
arithmetic here so a caller can audit the ratio, not just receive it (3B.3).
- htTrendMode.explain().return.diagnostics.engine?: string; default: not declared — Pricing/solver engine name, e.g. `black-scholes-merton`.
- htTrendMode.explain().return.diagnostics.finiteDifferenceBumps?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Finite-difference engines: the ACTUAL bump sizes used for FD Greeks (spec P2.3) — adaptive
near the vol/time boundaries, so the caller can see exactly what was differenced.
Keys: `spotStep`, `volatilityStep`, `timeStepYears`, `rateStep`, and — extended Greeks only —
`dividendYieldStep`. Each is the actual step differenced, in the unit of the coordinate it
bumps. (This doc named the retired `hS`/`hSig`/`hT`/`hR`/`hQ` keys for one release after the
emit sites had moved to the semantic names, so a caller following it read `undefined`.)
- htTrendMode.explain().return.diagnostics.iterations?: number; default: not declared — Iteration count for iterative methods.
- htTrendMode.explain().return.diagnostics.method?: string; default: not declared — Numerical method, e.g. `closed-form`, `brent`, `finite-difference`.
- htTrendMode.explain().return.diagnostics.selection?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing').SelectionReport; default: not declared — The structured engine-selection report (Gate C, `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing`): who was selected,
why, and — for automatic selection — every candidate considered with its verdict. This is the
machine-readable superset of `engine` + `autoReason` (which remain for compatibility);
`selected.name` always agrees with `engine` when both are present.
- htTrendMode.explain().return.diagnostics.timingMs?: number; default: not declared — Wall-clock timing in milliseconds, when measured.

computation seeds. Equals the input length when the indicator never emitted.

risky annuity, a forward variance's near/far legs. The H-series explain paths disclose their
arithmetic here so a caller can audit the ratio, not just receive it (3B.3).
- increasing.explain().return.diagnostics.engine?: string; default: not declared — Pricing/solver engine name, e.g. `black-scholes-merton`.
- increasing.explain().return.diagnostics.finiteDifferenceBumps?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Finite-difference engines: the ACTUAL bump sizes used for FD Greeks (spec P2.3) — adaptive
near the vol/time boundaries, so the caller can see exactly what was differenced.
Keys: `spotStep`, `volatilityStep`, `timeStepYears`, `rateStep`, and — extended Greeks only —
`dividendYieldStep`. Each is the actual step differenced, in the unit of the coordinate it
bumps. (This doc named the retired `hS`/`hSig`/`hT`/`hR`/`hQ` keys for one release after the
emit sites had moved to the semantic names, so a caller following it read `undefined`.)

- increasing.explain().return.diagnostics.method?: string; default: not declared — Numerical method, e.g. `closed-form`, `brent`, `finite-difference`.
- increasing.explain().return.diagnostics.selection?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing').SelectionReport; default: not declared — The structured engine-selection report (Gate C, `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing`): who was selected,
why, and — for automatic selection — every candidate considered with its verdict. This is the
machine-readable superset of `engine` + `autoReason` (which remain for compatibility);
`selected.name` always agrees with `engine` when both are present.

- kama.fromJSON().return.peek: (input: number) => number | null; default: not declared — The value that WOULD result from `next(input)` applied to the committed state, WITHOUT committing

closed bars. The default cost is O(snapshot) per call (clone-and-apply); indicators may override
with an O(1) form later.

- kdj.explain().return.diagnostics.autoReason?: string; default: not declared — When a meta-engine (e.g. `engines.auto()`) selected a delegate, this is a one-sentence,
human-readable explanation of WHY that delegate was chosen (`engine` then names the delegate).
Absent when no auto-selection took place.
- kdj.explain().return.diagnostics.converged?: boolean; default: not declared — Whether an iterative procedure converged. `false` means the value is not trustworthy.
- kdj.explain().return.diagnostics.decomposition?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Named intermediate quantities the value decomposes into — a par spread's protection leg and
risky annuity, a forward variance's near/far legs. The H-series explain paths disclose their
arithmetic here so a caller can audit the ratio, not just receive it (3B.3).
- kdj.explain().return.diagnostics.engine?: string; default: not declared — Pricing/solver engine name, e.g. `black-scholes-merton`.
- kdj.explain().return.diagnostics.finiteDifferenceBumps?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Finite-difference engines: the ACTUAL bump sizes used for FD Greeks (spec P2.3) — adaptive
near the vol/time boundaries, so the caller can see exactly what was differenced.
Keys: `spotStep`, `volatilityStep`, `timeStepYears`, `rateStep`, and — extended Greeks only —
`dividendYieldStep`. Each is the actual step differenced, in the unit of the coordinate it
bumps. (This doc named the retired `hS`/`hSig`/`hT`/`hR`/`hQ` keys for one release after the
emit sites had moved to the semantic names, so a caller following it read `undefined`.)
- kdj.explain().return.diagnostics.iterations?: number; default: not declared — Iteration count for iterative methods.
- kdj.explain().return.diagnostics.method?: string; default: not declared — Numerical method, e.g. `closed-form`, `brent`, `finite-difference`.
- kdj.explain().return.diagnostics.selection?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing').SelectionReport; default: not declared — The structured engine-selection report (Gate C, `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing`): who was selected,
why, and — for automatic selection — every candidate considered with its verdict. This is the
machine-readable superset of `engine` + `autoReason` (which remain for compatibility);
`selected.name` always agrees with `engine` when both are present.
- kdj.explain().return.diagnostics.timingMs?: number; default: not declared — Wall-clock timing in milliseconds, when measured.
- kdj.explain().return.diagnostics.warmup?: number; default: not declared — Series facades: number of leading output slots that are warmup sentinels (null/NaN) while the
computation seeds. Equals the input length when the indicator never emitted.

- kst.explain().return.diagnostics.decomposition?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Named intermediate quantities the value decomposes into — a par spread's protection leg and
risky annuity, a forward variance's near/far legs. The H-series explain paths disclose their
arithmetic here so a caller can audit the ratio, not just receive it (3B.3).
- kst.explain().return.diagnostics.engine?: string; default: not declared — Pricing/solver engine name, e.g. `black-scholes-merton`.
- kst.explain().return.diagnostics.finiteDifferenceBumps?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Finite-difference engines: the ACTUAL bump sizes used for FD Greeks (spec P2.3) — adaptive
near the vol/time boundaries, so the caller can see exactly what was differenced.
Keys: `spotStep`, `volatilityStep`, `timeStepYears`, `rateStep`, and — extended Greeks only —
`dividendYieldStep`. Each is the actual step differenced, in the unit of the coordinate it
bumps. (This doc named the retired `hS`/`hSig`/`hT`/`hR`/`hQ` keys for one release after the
emit sites had moved to the semantic names, so a caller following it read `undefined`.)
- kst.explain().return.diagnostics.iterations?: number; default: not declared — Iteration count for iterative methods.
- kst.explain().return.diagnostics.method?: string; default: not declared — Numerical method, e.g. `closed-form`, `brent`, `finite-difference`.

why, and — for automatic selection — every candidate considered with its verdict. This is the
machine-readable superset of `engine` + `autoReason` (which remain for compatibility);
`selected.name` always agrees with `engine` when both are present.

closed bars. The default cost is O(snapshot) per call (clone-and-apply); indicators may override
with an O(1) form later.

- liquiditySweeps.explain().return.diagnostics.autoReason?: string; default: not declared — When a meta-engine (e.g. `engines.auto()`) selected a delegate, this is a one-sentence,
human-readable explanation of WHY that delegate was chosen (`engine` then names the delegate).
Absent when no auto-selection took place.
- liquiditySweeps.explain().return.diagnostics.converged?: boolean; default: not declared — Whether an iterative procedure converged. `false` means the value is not trustworthy.
- liquiditySweeps.explain().return.diagnostics.decomposition?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Named intermediate quantities the value decomposes into — a par spread's protection leg and
risky annuity, a forward variance's near/far legs. The H-series explain paths disclose their
arithmetic here so a caller can audit the ratio, not just receive it (3B.3).
- liquiditySweeps.explain().return.diagnostics.engine?: string; default: not declared — Pricing/solver engine name, e.g. `black-scholes-merton`.
- liquiditySweeps.explain().return.diagnostics.finiteDifferenceBumps?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Finite-difference engines: the ACTUAL bump sizes used for FD Greeks (spec P2.3) — adaptive
near the vol/time boundaries, so the caller can see exactly what was differenced.
Keys: `spotStep`, `volatilityStep`, `timeStepYears`, `rateStep`, and — extended Greeks only —
`dividendYieldStep`. Each is the actual step differenced, in the unit of the coordinate it
bumps. (This doc named the retired `hS`/`hSig`/`hT`/`hR`/`hQ` keys for one release after the
emit sites had moved to the semantic names, so a caller following it read `undefined`.)

- liquiditySweeps.explain().return.diagnostics.method?: string; default: not declared — Numerical method, e.g. `closed-form`, `brent`, `finite-difference`.
- liquiditySweeps.explain().return.diagnostics.selection?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing').SelectionReport; default: not declared — The structured engine-selection report (Gate C, `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing`): who was selected,
why, and — for automatic selection — every candidate considered with its verdict. This is the
machine-readable superset of `engine` + `autoReason` (which remain for compatibility);

computation seeds. Equals the input length when the indicator never emitted.

bumps. (This doc named the retired `hS`/`hSig`/`hT`/`hR`/`hQ` keys for one release after the
emit sites had moved to the semantic names, so a caller following it read `undefined`.)

- marketStructure: (bars: ArrayLike<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis').BarInput>, options?: { strength?: number; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis').MarketStructure; default: not declared — Label the swing sequence (HH/HL/LH/LL) and flag breaks of structure. A higher-high while already
bullish is a continuation (BOS); a higher-high that reverses a bearish run is a change of character
(CHoCH), and symmetrically for lower-lows.

previous swing of that kind, and there is none yet.

arithmetic here so a caller can audit the ratio, not just receive it (3B.3).
- midprice.explain().return.diagnostics.engine?: string; default: not declared — Pricing/solver engine name, e.g. `black-scholes-merton`.
- midprice.explain().return.diagnostics.finiteDifferenceBumps?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Finite-difference engines: the ACTUAL bump sizes used for FD Greeks (spec P2.3) — adaptive
near the vol/time boundaries, so the caller can see exactly what was differenced.
Keys: `spotStep`, `volatilityStep`, `timeStepYears`, `rateStep`, and — extended Greeks only —
`dividendYieldStep`. Each is the actual step differenced, in the unit of the coordinate it
bumps. (This doc named the retired `hS`/`hSig`/`hT`/`hR`/`hQ` keys for one release after the
emit sites had moved to the semantic names, so a caller following it read `undefined`.)

why, and — for automatic selection — every candidate considered with its verdict. This is the
machine-readable superset of `engine` + `autoReason` (which remain for compatibility);

- mult.explain().return.assumptions: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Assumptions<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis').TechnicalAnalysisAssumptionExtras>; default: not declared — Every applied convention, echoed back.
- mult.explain().return.diagnostics: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Diagnostics & { warmup: number; }; default: not declared
- mult.explain().return.diagnostics.autoReason?: string; default: not declared — When a meta-engine (e.g. `engines.auto()`) selected a delegate, this is a one-sentence,
human-readable explanation of WHY that delegate was chosen (`engine` then names the delegate).
Absent when no auto-selection took place.
- mult.explain().return.diagnostics.converged?: boolean; default: not declared — Whether an iterative procedure converged. `false` means the value is not trustworthy.
- mult.explain().return.diagnostics.decomposition?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Named intermediate quantities the value decomposes into — a par spread's protection leg and
risky annuity, a forward variance's near/far legs. The H-series explain paths disclose their
arithmetic here so a caller can audit the ratio, not just receive it (3B.3).
- mult.explain().return.diagnostics.engine?: string; default: not declared — Pricing/solver engine name, e.g. `black-scholes-merton`.
- mult.explain().return.diagnostics.finiteDifferenceBumps?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Finite-difference engines: the ACTUAL bump sizes used for FD Greeks (spec P2.3) — adaptive
near the vol/time boundaries, so the caller can see exactly what was differenced.
Keys: `spotStep`, `volatilityStep`, `timeStepYears`, `rateStep`, and — extended Greeks only —
`dividendYieldStep`. Each is the actual step differenced, in the unit of the coordinate it
bumps. (This doc named the retired `hS`/`hSig`/`hT`/`hR`/`hQ` keys for one release after the
emit sites had moved to the semantic names, so a caller following it read `undefined`.)
- mult.explain().return.diagnostics.iterations?: number; default: not declared — Iteration count for iterative methods.
- mult.explain().return.diagnostics.method?: string; default: not declared — Numerical method, e.g. `closed-form`, `brent`, `finite-difference`.
- mult.explain().return.diagnostics.selection?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing').SelectionReport; default: not declared — The structured engine-selection report (Gate C, `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing`): who was selected,
why, and — for automatic selection — every candidate considered with its verdict. This is the
machine-readable superset of `engine` + `autoReason` (which remain for compatibility);
`selected.name` always agrees with `engine` when both are present.
- mult.explain().return.diagnostics.timingMs?: number; default: not declared — Wall-clock timing in milliseconds, when measured.
- mult.explain().return.diagnostics.warmup?: number; default: not declared — Series facades: number of leading output slots that are warmup sentinels (null/NaN) while the
computation seeds. Equals the input length when the indicator never emitted.
- mult.explain().return.diagnostics.warnings: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').QuantWarning[]; default: not declared — Structured warnings; always present (possibly empty).
- mult.explain().return.provenance?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Provenance; default: not declared — Optional data lineage when the inputs came from a provider.
- mult.explain().return.value: number[]; default: not declared — The computed value. Never `NaN` or `±Infinity`: a value the model cannot produce is `null`
beside a diagnostic that says why (Law 7 — a warning never licenses a non-finite number).

- mult.fromJSON().return.peek: (input: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis').Pair) => number | null; default: not declared — The value that WOULD result from `next(input)` applied to the committed state, WITHOUT committing

to commit. Between commits the committed state is untouched, so a live chart never repaints its
closed bars. The default cost is O(snapshot) per call (clone-and-apply); indicators may override
with an O(1) form later.

arithmetic here so a caller can audit the ratio, not just receive it (3B.3).
- obv.explain().return.diagnostics.engine?: string; default: not declared — Pricing/solver engine name, e.g. `black-scholes-merton`.
- obv.explain().return.diagnostics.finiteDifferenceBumps?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Finite-difference engines: the ACTUAL bump sizes used for FD Greeks (spec P2.3) — adaptive
near the vol/time boundaries, so the caller can see exactly what was differenced.
Keys: `spotStep`, `volatilityStep`, `timeStepYears`, `rateStep`, and — extended Greeks only —
`dividendYieldStep`. Each is the actual step differenced, in the unit of the coordinate it
bumps. (This doc named the retired `hS`/`hSig`/`hT`/`hR`/`hQ` keys for one release after the
emit sites had moved to the semantic names, so a caller following it read `undefined`.)

why, and — for automatic selection — every candidate considered with its verdict. This is the
machine-readable superset of `engine` + `autoReason` (which remain for compatibility);

- pvi.fromJSON().return.peek: (input: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis').BarInput) => number | null; default: not declared — The value that WOULD result from `next(input)` applied to the committed state, WITHOUT committing
it. Call it repeatedly with the forming bar's evolving value; call `next(input)` once at bar close
to commit. Between commits the committed state is untouched, so a live chart never repaints its
closed bars. The default cost is O(snapshot) per call (clone-and-apply); indicators may override
with an O(1) form later.

- pvo.explain().return.diagnostics.autoReason?: string; default: not declared — When a meta-engine (e.g. `engines.auto()`) selected a delegate, this is a one-sentence,
human-readable explanation of WHY that delegate was chosen (`engine` then names the delegate).
Absent when no auto-selection took place.
- pvo.explain().return.diagnostics.converged?: boolean; default: not declared — Whether an iterative procedure converged. `false` means the value is not trustworthy.
- pvo.explain().return.diagnostics.decomposition?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Named intermediate quantities the value decomposes into — a par spread's protection leg and
risky annuity, a forward variance's near/far legs. The H-series explain paths disclose their
arithmetic here so a caller can audit the ratio, not just receive it (3B.3).
- pvo.explain().return.diagnostics.engine?: string; default: not declared — Pricing/solver engine name, e.g. `black-scholes-merton`.
- pvo.explain().return.diagnostics.finiteDifferenceBumps?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Finite-difference engines: the ACTUAL bump sizes used for FD Greeks (spec P2.3) — adaptive
near the vol/time boundaries, so the caller can see exactly what was differenced.
Keys: `spotStep`, `volatilityStep`, `timeStepYears`, `rateStep`, and — extended Greeks only —
`dividendYieldStep`. Each is the actual step differenced, in the unit of the coordinate it
bumps. (This doc named the retired `hS`/`hSig`/`hT`/`hR`/`hQ` keys for one release after the
emit sites had moved to the semantic names, so a caller following it read `undefined`.)
- pvo.explain().return.diagnostics.iterations?: number; default: not declared — Iteration count for iterative methods.
- pvo.explain().return.diagnostics.method?: string; default: not declared — Numerical method, e.g. `closed-form`, `brent`, `finite-difference`.
- pvo.explain().return.diagnostics.selection?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing').SelectionReport; default: not declared — The structured engine-selection report (Gate C, `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing`): who was selected,
why, and — for automatic selection — every candidate considered with its verdict. This is the
machine-readable superset of `engine` + `autoReason` (which remain for compatibility);
`selected.name` always agrees with `engine` when both are present.
- pvo.explain().return.diagnostics.timingMs?: number; default: not declared — Wall-clock timing in milliseconds, when measured.
- pvo.explain().return.diagnostics.warmup?: number; default: not declared — Series facades: number of leading output slots that are warmup sentinels (null/NaN) while the
computation seeds. Equals the input length when the indicator never emitted.
- pvo.explain().return.diagnostics.warnings: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').QuantWarning[]; default: not declared — Structured warnings; always present (possibly empty).
- pvo.explain().return.provenance?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Provenance; default: not declared — Optional data lineage when the inputs came from a provider.
- pvo.explain().return.value: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis').PvoPoint[]; default: not declared — The computed value. Never `NaN` or `±Infinity`: a value the model cannot produce is `null`
beside a diagnostic that says why (Law 7 — a warning never licenses a non-finite number).

- rangeBars: (bars: ArrayLike<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis').BarInput>, parameters: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis').RangeBarParameters) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis').BarInput[]; default: not declared
- rangeBars(bars): ArrayLike<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis').BarInput>; default: not declared
- rangeBars(parameters): import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis').RangeBarParameters; default: not declared
- rangeBars(parameters).flush?: boolean; default: not declared — Emit the trailing partial bar. Default true.

- readSnapshot: <Kind extends string>(snapshot: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis').TechnicalAnalysisSnapshot, expected: Kind | readonly Kind[]) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis').SnapshotState<Kind>; default: not declared — Validate a snapshot envelope and open its state for checked reading.

`expected` is the kind the CALLING restorer produces. Passing it is what turns a restorer from
"rebuilds itself out of whatever numbers are in front of it" into one that knows whose snapshot it
is holding — and it costs the call site four characters.

A LIST is accepted for the handful of restorers that serve a FAMILY: one `MomentStream` class backs
both `standardDeviation` and `variance`, and reads which one it is off the snapshot. Those are the
restorers that genuinely may not pin a single kind — and a list still pins the family, which is the
whole guarantee. A restorer that pins nothing is the defect this parameter exists to remove, so
there is no form of this call that omits it.

Order matters, and each step is the precondition of the next: an envelope that is not an object has
no version; a version this build cannot read makes every field meaningless; a snapshot from another
indicator has the wrong fields entirely, so reporting a missing field would send the reader looking
in the wrong place.
- readSnapshot().return.boolean: (field: string) => boolean; default: not declared — A boolean flag.
- readSnapshot().return.cached: <T>(field: string) => T | null; default: not declared — The LAST EMITTED OUTPUT, cached so a restored stream's `.value` is not blank until the next bar.

Deliberately the loosest accessor, and the only one that tolerates non-finite: `NaN` is a real
output. `acos` outside [-1, 1] is NaN; a `fairValueGaps` point reads `{ top: NaN, bottom: NaN }`
until a gap forms. Rejecting those would refuse to restore a correct stream.

What it still refuses is a value of a kind no indicator ever outputs — a string, a boolean, a
function — which is what a foreign or hand-edited snapshot looks like.

A missing key reads as `null` rather than throwing: the cache is an optimisation, and a snapshot
that predates an indicator caching its value must restore to "no value yet", not fail.
- readSnapshot().return.child: (field: string) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis').TechnicalAnalysisSnapshot; default: not declared — A nested snapshot envelope — a composed indicator's child (`macd` carries three EMAs).

Only the SHAPE is checked here. The child's own `fromJSON` calls `readSnapshot` with the kind it
expects, so a child from the wrong indicator is convicted there, with that indicator's name on
the message rather than the parent's.
- readSnapshot().return.children: (field: string) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis').TechnicalAnalysisSnapshot[]; default: not declared — A fresh array of nested snapshot envelopes.
- readSnapshot().return.has: (field: string) => boolean; default: not declared — Does the state carry this key at all? For a field a newer build may legitimately omit.
- readSnapshot().return.integer: (field: string) => number; default: not declared — A whole number ≥ 0 — a count, an index, a bar offset. A fractional count restores a stream whose
window boundaries never line up again, which shows up as an off-by-a-fraction output rather than
as an error.
- readSnapshot().return.kind: Kind; default: not declared — The indicator kind this state belongs to — the prefix on every message, and, for a FAMILY
restorer, the narrowed member the guard just proved. `readSnapshot(s, MOMENT_KINDS)` hands back
a state whose `kind` is `'standardDeviation' | 'variance'`, so the restorer feeds it straight
into its constructor instead of re-asserting `snapshot.kind as string` — which is the cast the
guard exists to make unnecessary.
- readSnapshot().return.literal: <T extends string | number>(field: string, allowed: readonly T[]) => T; default: not declared — A value drawn from a closed set — a mode, a method, a moving-average family, a trade direction.

Numbers as well as strings: `TradeDirection` is `-1 | 0 | 1`, and reading it as a plain number
would accept `7` as a trade direction.
- readSnapshot().return.literals: <T extends string | number>(field: string, allowed: readonly T[]) => T[]; default: not declared — A fresh array of values drawn from a closed set.
- readSnapshot().return.lookback: (field: string) => number; default: not declared — A lookback: an integer ≥ 1.

This is the asymmetry the reader exists to close. `ta.rsi.stream({ period: -3 })` throws from
`requirePeriod`; `RsiStream.fromJSON` read the same number straight out of state and built a
stream with a negative window, which produces `undefined` buffer reads and silent NaN.
- readSnapshot().return.number: (field: string) => number; default: not declared — A number: sums, running averages, thresholds, multipliers.

Non-finite is permitted HERE and refused at the door. `readSnapshot` has already walked the whole
state: an encoded non-finite has been decoded (the indicator computed it — a zero price series
makes every log-return NaN), and a raw one has been rejected as damage. By the time an accessor
runs, `NaN` can only mean the first.
- readSnapshot().return.numberOrNull: (field: string) => number | null; default: not declared — A number or `null` — a running value that has not been established yet.
- readSnapshot().return.numberRows: (field: string) => number[][]; default: not declared — A fresh array of fresh number arrays — a matrix of windows.
- readSnapshot().return.numbers: (field: string) => number[]; default: not declared — A FRESH array of finite numbers.

Fresh matters: the previous `state['buf'] as number[]` aliased the caller's snapshot, so two
streams restored from one snapshot object shared a buffer and corrupted each other. Restorers
used to spell that defence themselves (`[...(state['buf'] as number[])]`) and could forget to.
- readSnapshot().return.numbersOrNull: (field: string) => number[] | null; default: not declared — A fresh array of finite numbers, or `null`.
- readSnapshot().return.optionalNumber: (field: string) => number | undefined; default: not declared — A number the state may omit entirely (an optional parameter a stream carries).
- readSnapshot().return.optionalNumbers: (field: string) => number[] | undefined; default: not declared — A fresh array of finite numbers the state may omit.
- readSnapshot().return.raw: Record<string, unknown>; default: not declared — The raw state object. For a restorer that must hand a whole sub-object to a helper.
- readSnapshot().return.record: <T>(field: string) => T; default: not declared — A structured record the indicator persists whole — a bar, a candle, an accumulator.

Members are not walked: their shape is the indicator's own business and varies per record type.
The check is that it IS a record, which is what separates a usable snapshot from `"acc"` or `7`.
- readSnapshot().return.recordOrNull: <T>(field: string) => T | null; default: not declared — A structured record, or `null` when the indicator has not established one.
- readSnapshot().return.records: <T>(field: string) => T[]; default: not declared — A fresh array of structured records — persisted bars, candles, levels.
- readSnapshot().return.text: (field: string) => string; default: not declared — A string.
- readSnapshot(expected): Kind | readonly Kind[]; default: not declared

so its absence is information too. Echoed by `.explain().assumptions.conventions` and surfaced by
`describeIndicator`, which is what makes a divergence from TA-Lib or pandas-ta discoverable from
the result instead of only from prose.
- resolveIndicator().return.defaults?: Record<string, unknown>; default: not declared — Declared default per optional parameter (the disclosure law, dx R1): a parameter listed in
`parameters` but absent here is REQUIRED. A value may be a resolver `(resolved) => value` for the
rare default computed from another parameter. Bound at built-in construction/custom registration so
`.explain().assumptions.parameters` echoes every default that engages.

- returns.explain().return.diagnostics: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Diagnostics & { warmup: number; }; default: not declared
- returns.explain().return.diagnostics.autoReason?: string; default: not declared — When a meta-engine (e.g. `engines.auto()`) selected a delegate, this is a one-sentence,
human-readable explanation of WHY that delegate was chosen (`engine` then names the delegate).
Absent when no auto-selection took place.
- returns.explain().return.diagnostics.converged?: boolean; default: not declared — Whether an iterative procedure converged. `false` means the value is not trustworthy.
- returns.explain().return.diagnostics.decomposition?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Named intermediate quantities the value decomposes into — a par spread's protection leg and
risky annuity, a forward variance's near/far legs. The H-series explain paths disclose their
arithmetic here so a caller can audit the ratio, not just receive it (3B.3).
- returns.explain().return.diagnostics.engine?: string; default: not declared — Pricing/solver engine name, e.g. `black-scholes-merton`.
- returns.explain().return.diagnostics.finiteDifferenceBumps?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Finite-difference engines: the ACTUAL bump sizes used for FD Greeks (spec P2.3) — adaptive
near the vol/time boundaries, so the caller can see exactly what was differenced.
Keys: `spotStep`, `volatilityStep`, `timeStepYears`, `rateStep`, and — extended Greeks only —
`dividendYieldStep`. Each is the actual step differenced, in the unit of the coordinate it
bumps. (This doc named the retired `hS`/`hSig`/`hT`/`hR`/`hQ` keys for one release after the
emit sites had moved to the semantic names, so a caller following it read `undefined`.)
- returns.explain().return.diagnostics.iterations?: number; default: not declared — Iteration count for iterative methods.
- returns.explain().return.diagnostics.method?: string; default: not declared — Numerical method, e.g. `closed-form`, `brent`, `finite-difference`.
- returns.explain().return.diagnostics.selection?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing').SelectionReport; default: not declared — The structured engine-selection report (Gate C, `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing`): who was selected,
why, and — for automatic selection — every candidate considered with its verdict. This is the
machine-readable superset of `engine` + `autoReason` (which remain for compatibility);
`selected.name` always agrees with `engine` when both are present.
- returns.explain().return.diagnostics.timingMs?: number; default: not declared — Wall-clock timing in milliseconds, when measured.

computation seeds. Equals the input length when the indicator never emitted.

- returns.fromJSON().return.peek: (input: number) => number | null; default: not declared — The value that WOULD result from `next(input)` applied to the committed state, WITHOUT committing

to commit. Between commits the committed state is untouched, so a live chart never repaints its
closed bars. The default cost is O(snapshot) per call (clone-and-apply); indicators may override
with an O(1) form later.

- rocp.fromJSON().return.next: (input: number) => number | null; default: not declared
- rocp.fromJSON().return.peek: (input: number) => number | null; default: not declared — The value that WOULD result from `next(input)` applied to the committed state, WITHOUT committing
it. Call it repeatedly with the forming bar's evolving value; call `next(input)` once at bar close
to commit. Between commits the committed state is untouched, so a live chart never repaints its
closed bars. The default cost is O(snapshot) per call (clone-and-apply); indicators may override
with an O(1) form later.

risky annuity, a forward variance's near/far legs. The H-series explain paths disclose their
arithmetic here so a caller can audit the ratio, not just receive it (3B.3).
- rocr.explain().return.diagnostics.engine?: string; default: not declared — Pricing/solver engine name, e.g. `black-scholes-merton`.
- rocr.explain().return.diagnostics.finiteDifferenceBumps?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Finite-difference engines: the ACTUAL bump sizes used for FD Greeks (spec P2.3) — adaptive
near the vol/time boundaries, so the caller can see exactly what was differenced.
Keys: `spotStep`, `volatilityStep`, `timeStepYears`, `rateStep`, and — extended Greeks only —
`dividendYieldStep`. Each is the actual step differenced, in the unit of the coordinate it
bumps. (This doc named the retired `hS`/`hSig`/`hT`/`hR`/`hQ` keys for one release after the
emit sites had moved to the semantic names, so a caller following it read `undefined`.)

- rocr.explain().return.diagnostics.method?: string; default: not declared — Numerical method, e.g. `closed-form`, `brent`, `finite-difference`.
- rocr.explain().return.diagnostics.selection?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing').SelectionReport; default: not declared — The structured engine-selection report (Gate C, `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing`): who was selected,
why, and — for automatic selection — every candidate considered with its verdict. This is the
machine-readable superset of `engine` + `autoReason` (which remain for compatibility);
`selected.name` always agrees with `engine` when both are present.

- rollingMedian.explain().return.diagnostics: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Diagnostics & { warmup: number; }; default: not declared
- rollingMedian.explain().return.diagnostics.autoReason?: string; default: not declared — When a meta-engine (e.g. `engines.auto()`) selected a delegate, this is a one-sentence,
human-readable explanation of WHY that delegate was chosen (`engine` then names the delegate).
Absent when no auto-selection took place.
- rollingMedian.explain().return.diagnostics.converged?: boolean; default: not declared — Whether an iterative procedure converged. `false` means the value is not trustworthy.
- rollingMedian.explain().return.diagnostics.decomposition?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Named intermediate quantities the value decomposes into — a par spread's protection leg and
risky annuity, a forward variance's near/far legs. The H-series explain paths disclose their
arithmetic here so a caller can audit the ratio, not just receive it (3B.3).
- rollingMedian.explain().return.diagnostics.engine?: string; default: not declared — Pricing/solver engine name, e.g. `black-scholes-merton`.
- rollingMedian.explain().return.diagnostics.finiteDifferenceBumps?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Finite-difference engines: the ACTUAL bump sizes used for FD Greeks (spec P2.3) — adaptive
near the vol/time boundaries, so the caller can see exactly what was differenced.
Keys: `spotStep`, `volatilityStep`, `timeStepYears`, `rateStep`, and — extended Greeks only —
`dividendYieldStep`. Each is the actual step differenced, in the unit of the coordinate it
bumps. (This doc named the retired `hS`/`hSig`/`hT`/`hR`/`hQ` keys for one release after the
emit sites had moved to the semantic names, so a caller following it read `undefined`.)
- rollingMedian.explain().return.diagnostics.iterations?: number; default: not declared — Iteration count for iterative methods.
- rollingMedian.explain().return.diagnostics.method?: string; default: not declared — Numerical method, e.g. `closed-form`, `brent`, `finite-difference`.
- rollingMedian.explain().return.diagnostics.selection?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing').SelectionReport; default: not declared — The structured engine-selection report (Gate C, `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing`): who was selected,
why, and — for automatic selection — every candidate considered with its verdict. This is the
machine-readable superset of `engine` + `autoReason` (which remain for compatibility);
`selected.name` always agrees with `engine` when both are present.
- rollingMedian.explain().return.diagnostics.timingMs?: number; default: not declared — Wall-clock timing in milliseconds, when measured.
- rollingMedian.explain().return.diagnostics.warmup?: number; default: not declared — Series facades: number of leading output slots that are warmup sentinels (null/NaN) while the
computation seeds. Equals the input length when the indicator never emitted.

beside a diagnostic that says why (Law 7 — a warning never licenses a non-finite number).

- rsi: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis').Indicator<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis').RsiParameters, number, number>; default: not declared — Wilder's RSI (period 14 default, disclosed via `.explain()`).

Flat-series convention: when the average loss over the window is zero (a flat or monotonically
rising series), TotalFinance returns **100** (the RS → ∞ limit; TradingView's convention). TA-Lib
emits 0 there and pandas-ta NaN — see `docs/compatibility/talib-differences.md`.

arithmetic here so a caller can audit the ratio, not just receive it (3B.3).

`dividendYieldStep`. Each is the actual step differenced, in the unit of the coordinate it
bumps. (This doc named the retired `hS`/`hSig`/`hT`/`hR`/`hQ` keys for one release after the
emit sites had moved to the semantic names, so a caller following it read `undefined`.)

- snapshotOf: (kind: string, state: Record<string, unknown>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis').TechnicalAnalysisSnapshot; default: not declared — Stamp indicator state into the public envelope. Every `toJSON` goes through here.

This is also where the state becomes JSON-SAFE: after `snapshotOf`, no number in the tree is
non-finite, so `JSON.stringify` is lossless and any raw `NaN` a reader later encounters can only
have come from damage — which is what lets {@link SnapshotState} refuse it.

`kind` is guarded because the natural wrong call is `snapshotOf(stream)` — reaching for the
serializer as if it took the thing to serialize. That produced an envelope whose `kind` was a live
stream object and whose `state` was `undefined`: it survives `JSON.stringify` (as `{}`) and only
fails much later, at a `fromJSON` that cannot say why.
- snapshotOf().return.kind: string; default: not declared
- snapshotOf().return.schemaVersion: number; default: not declared — Schema version, stamped at the serialization boundary by {@link snapshotOf}.
- snapshotOf().return.state: Record<string, unknown>; default: not declared — Indicator-private stream state. Round-trip it; never read into it.
- snapshotOf(kind): string; default: not declared
- snapshotOf(state): Record<string, unknown>; default: not declared

- squeezePro(parameters).wideKeltnerChannelMultiplier?: number; default: not declared — Keltner multipliers, wide → tight. Default 2.0 / 1.5 / 1.0.

Named for the CHANNEL, not the compression level they detect. As `low`/`mid`/`high` they
inverted against their own values — `lowMultiplier` was the LARGEST number (2.0, the widest
channel, the loosest squeeze) — so the reader had to know which of the two scales the word
referred to. The point's fields are now `lowCompression`/`normalCompression`/
`highCompression`, so both halves of the indicator say which scale they are on.

- squeezePro.stream(parameters).wideKeltnerChannelMultiplier?: number; default: not declared — Keltner multipliers, wide → tight. Default 2.0 / 1.5 / 1.0.

Named for the CHANNEL, not the compression level they detect. As `low`/`mid`/`high` they
inverted against their own values — `lowMultiplier` was the LARGEST number (2.0, the widest
channel, the loosest squeeze) — so the reader had to know which of the two scales the word
referred to. The point's fields are now `lowCompression`/`normalCompression`/
`highCompression`, so both halves of the indicator say which scale they are on.

- sub.explain().return.diagnostics.finiteDifferenceBumps?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Finite-difference engines: the ACTUAL bump sizes used for FD Greeks (spec P2.3) — adaptive
near the vol/time boundaries, so the caller can see exactly what was differenced.

`dividendYieldStep`. Each is the actual step differenced, in the unit of the coordinate it

- tan(parameters)?: {} | undefined; default: not declared

- tan.explain().return.assumptions: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Assumptions<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis').TechnicalAnalysisAssumptionExtras>; default: not declared — Every applied convention, echoed back.
- tan.explain().return.diagnostics: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Diagnostics & { warmup: number; }; default: not declared
- tan.explain().return.diagnostics.autoReason?: string; default: not declared — When a meta-engine (e.g. `engines.auto()`) selected a delegate, this is a one-sentence,
human-readable explanation of WHY that delegate was chosen (`engine` then names the delegate).
Absent when no auto-selection took place.
- tan.explain().return.diagnostics.converged?: boolean; default: not declared — Whether an iterative procedure converged. `false` means the value is not trustworthy.
- tan.explain().return.diagnostics.decomposition?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Named intermediate quantities the value decomposes into — a par spread's protection leg and
risky annuity, a forward variance's near/far legs. The H-series explain paths disclose their
arithmetic here so a caller can audit the ratio, not just receive it (3B.3).
- tan.explain().return.diagnostics.engine?: string; default: not declared — Pricing/solver engine name, e.g. `black-scholes-merton`.
- tan.explain().return.diagnostics.finiteDifferenceBumps?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Finite-difference engines: the ACTUAL bump sizes used for FD Greeks (spec P2.3) — adaptive
near the vol/time boundaries, so the caller can see exactly what was differenced.
Keys: `spotStep`, `volatilityStep`, `timeStepYears`, `rateStep`, and — extended Greeks only —
`dividendYieldStep`. Each is the actual step differenced, in the unit of the coordinate it
bumps. (This doc named the retired `hS`/`hSig`/`hT`/`hR`/`hQ` keys for one release after the
emit sites had moved to the semantic names, so a caller following it read `undefined`.)
- tan.explain().return.diagnostics.iterations?: number; default: not declared — Iteration count for iterative methods.
- tan.explain().return.diagnostics.method?: string; default: not declared — Numerical method, e.g. `closed-form`, `brent`, `finite-difference`.
- tan.explain().return.diagnostics.selection?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing').SelectionReport; default: not declared — The structured engine-selection report (Gate C, `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing`): who was selected,
why, and — for automatic selection — every candidate considered with its verdict. This is the
machine-readable superset of `engine` + `autoReason` (which remain for compatibility);
`selected.name` always agrees with `engine` when both are present.
- tan.explain().return.diagnostics.timingMs?: number; default: not declared — Wall-clock timing in milliseconds, when measured.
- tan.explain().return.diagnostics.warmup?: number; default: not declared — Series facades: number of leading output slots that are warmup sentinels (null/NaN) while the
computation seeds. Equals the input length when the indicator never emitted.
- tan.explain().return.diagnostics.warnings: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').QuantWarning[]; default: not declared — Structured warnings; always present (possibly empty).
- tan.explain().return.provenance?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Provenance; default: not declared — Optional data lineage when the inputs came from a provider.
- tan.explain().return.value: number[]; default: not declared — The computed value. Never `NaN` or `±Infinity`: a value the model cannot produce is `null`
beside a diagnostic that says why (Law 7 — a warning never licenses a non-finite number).

- tan.fromJSON().return.peek: (input: number) => number | null; default: not declared — The value that WOULD result from `next(input)` applied to the committed state, WITHOUT committing
it. Call it repeatedly with the forming bar's evolving value; call `next(input)` once at bar close
to commit. Between commits the committed state is untouched, so a live chart never repaints its
closed bars. The default cost is O(snapshot) per call (clone-and-apply); indicators may override
with an O(1) form later.

- tosStdevAll: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis').Indicator<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis').TosStdevAllParameters, number, import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis').TosStdevAllPoint>; default: not declared — Thinkorswim Standard Deviation All: OLS line plus source-standard-deviation bands.

Omitting `period` uses **all history seen so far** (a causal, stream-friendly expanding window) —
a deliberate TotalFinance choice. This is NOT the single full-series regression overlay that ThinkorSwim
/ pandas-ta's `tos_stdevall` draws (a constant line over the whole chart); pass an explicit `period`
for a fixed rolling window. See docs/compatibility/talib-differences.md.

- tosStdevAll.explain().return.diagnostics.finiteDifferenceBumps?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Finite-difference engines: the ACTUAL bump sizes used for FD Greeks (spec P2.3) — adaptive
near the vol/time boundaries, so the caller can see exactly what was differenced.
Keys: `spotStep`, `volatilityStep`, `timeStepYears`, `rateStep`, and — extended Greeks only —
`dividendYieldStep`. Each is the actual step differenced, in the unit of the coordinate it

why, and — for automatic selection — every candidate considered with its verdict. This is the

`dividendYieldStep`. Each is the actual step differenced, in the unit of the coordinate it
bumps. (This doc named the retired `hS`/`hSig`/`hT`/`hR`/`hQ` keys for one release after the
emit sites had moved to the semantic names, so a caller following it read `undefined`.)

- vfi.explain().return.diagnostics.selection?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing').SelectionReport; default: not declared — The structured engine-selection report (Gate C, `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing`): who was selected,
why, and — for automatic selection — every candidate considered with its verdict. This is the
machine-readable superset of `engine` + `autoReason` (which remain for compatibility);
`selected.name` always agrees with `engine` when both are present.

- vwap.explain().return.diagnostics.engine?: string; default: not declared — Pricing/solver engine name, e.g. `black-scholes-merton`.
- vwap.explain().return.diagnostics.finiteDifferenceBumps?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Finite-difference engines: the ACTUAL bump sizes used for FD Greeks (spec P2.3) — adaptive
near the vol/time boundaries, so the caller can see exactly what was differenced.
Keys: `spotStep`, `volatilityStep`, `timeStepYears`, `rateStep`, and — extended Greeks only —
`dividendYieldStep`. Each is the actual step differenced, in the unit of the coordinate it
bumps. (This doc named the retired `hS`/`hSig`/`hT`/`hR`/`hQ` keys for one release after the
emit sites had moved to the semantic names, so a caller following it read `undefined`.)
- vwap.explain().return.diagnostics.iterations?: number; default: not declared — Iteration count for iterative methods.
- vwap.explain().return.diagnostics.method?: string; default: not declared — Numerical method, e.g. `closed-form`, `brent`, `finite-difference`.
- vwap.explain().return.diagnostics.selection?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing').SelectionReport; default: not declared — The structured engine-selection report (Gate C, `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing`): who was selected,
why, and — for automatic selection — every candidate considered with its verdict. This is the
machine-readable superset of `engine` + `autoReason` (which remain for compatibility);
`selected.name` always agrees with `engine` when both are present.
- vwap.explain().return.diagnostics.timingMs?: number; default: not declared — Wall-clock timing in milliseconds, when measured.
- vwap.explain().return.diagnostics.warmup?: number; default: not declared — Series facades: number of leading output slots that are warmup sentinels (null/NaN) while the
computation seeds. Equals the input length when the indicator never emitted.

beside a diagnostic that says why (Law 7 — a warning never licenses a non-finite number).

bumps. (This doc named the retired `hS`/`hSig`/`hT`/`hR`/`hQ` keys for one release after the
emit sites had moved to the semantic names, so a caller following it read `undefined`.)

why, and — for automatic selection — every candidate considered with its verdict. This is the
machine-readable superset of `engine` + `autoReason` (which remain for compatibility);

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance#valuation

Kind: namespace; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

```typescript
export declare const valuation: typeof import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/valuation');
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- adjustedPresentValue: (input: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/valuation').AdjustedPresentValueInput) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/valuation').AdjustedPresentValueResult; default: not declared — Adjusted present value: the unlevered operating value at the unlevered cost of capital PLUS the

- convertPriceLevel: { (input: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/valuation').ConvertPriceLevelInput): number; explain: (input: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/valuation').ConvertPriceLevelInput) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Computed<number, import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/valuation').PriceLevelConversionAssumptions>; }; default: not declared — Map a source price level to an approximate target level in the supplied target price unit.

Reference mode: `sourcePriceLevel * referenceTargetPrice / referenceSourcePrice`.
Ratio mode: `sourcePriceLevel * targetPricePerSourcePrice` (target units per source unit).
To invert, swap source/target references and unit labels, or supply the reciprocal ratio.
Inputs are closed and validated on both calls; prices/ratios must be finite and positive,
except the requested level may be zero. No cents/tick rounding or instrument inference occurs.
Overflow and positive underflow to zero throw typed `input.out_of_range` errors.

Unit labels are optional descriptive metadata, not financial defaults or conversion factors.
`.explain()` echoes supplied metadata; resultUnit is null when targetPriceUnit is omitted.
It assumes that the proportional
mapping remains valid at the requested level. This approximation is not a live quote,
predicted ETF open, arbitrage/fair-value result, option premium or notional/delta hedge.
The caller supplies comparable references and freshness policy. For named pairs, start with
helpers such as `esToSpyLevel` or `nqToQqqLevel`; they need only three named prices.

- loanPeriodicInterestRate: (input: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/valuation').LoanPeriodicInterestRateInput) => number; default: not declared — The per-period rate that makes `payment` amortize `principal` — a PROVEN bracket on the monotone
payment-in-rate map (geometric expansion until the sign changes, over the full economic domain
`rate > −1`), then bisection, then a residual check that the found rate actually reproduces the
payment. The closed form for one period shows the rate can be astronomically large
(`payment / principal − 1`), so the expansion never stops at an arbitrary cap and returns —
failing to bracket is a refusal with a teaching error, never a number.

One shape is refused BEFORE the solver: a one-period `'beginning'` loan with no balloon pays its
single installment at time zero, so the rate never touches a cash flow — the rate is
unidentifiable when `payment === principal` (every rate satisfies the identity) and no rate
solves it otherwise. See the inline teaching errors for both sub-cases.

- projectFinancialStatements: (input: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/valuation').ProjectStatementsInput) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/valuation').ProjectStatementsResult; default: not declared — A three-statement projection from a typed historical base and explicit per-period drivers.

The articulation, written out (Δ = period change):

    ΔtotalAssets = Δcash + ΔAR + Δinventory + ΔPPE
                 = (CFO + CFI + CFF) + ΔAR + Δinventory + (capex − D&A)
                 = netIncome + ΔAP + netBorrowing − dividends
    ΔtotalLiabilities + Δequity = ΔAP + netBorrowing + netIncome − dividends

— identical, so the balance sheet ties EXACTLY with cash as the named balancer. Other assets and
other liabilities are carried CONSTANT from the base (disclosed), never grown silently.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance#volatility

Kind: namespace; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

```typescript
export declare const volatility: typeof import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility');
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- RISK_NEUTRAL_ESTIMATE: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').QuantWarning; default: not declared — The standard "this is a risk-neutral model estimate, not a real-world forecast" caveat.
- RISK_NEUTRAL_ESTIMATE.code: string; default: not declared
- RISK_NEUTRAL_ESTIMATE.context?: Record<string, unknown>; default: not declared
- RISK_NEUTRAL_ESTIMATE.message: string; default: not declared
- RISK_NEUTRAL_ESTIMATE.severity: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').WarningSeverity; default: not declared
- SURFACE_SCHEMA_VERSION: '1'; default: not declared — Schema version stamped onto every {@link VolatilitySurface#toJSON } snapshot; checked on restore (WS4.4).
- VolatilitySurface: typeof import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').VolatilitySurface; default: not declared — A fitted implied-volatility surface with diagnostics-bearing lookup.
- VolatilitySurface().return.arbitrage: (options?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').ArbitrageCheckOptions) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').ArbitrageReport; default: not declared — Run the static no-arbitrage diagnostics (calendar + butterfly) over this surface.
- VolatilitySurface().return.assumptions: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Assumptions<{ shock?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SurfaceShock; }>; default: not declared
- VolatilitySurface().return.diagnostics: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Diagnostics; default: not declared
- VolatilitySurface().return.essvi?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').ESSVIParameters; default: not declared — The global eSSVI parameters when `model: 'essvi'`, else `undefined`.
- VolatilitySurface().return.expiries: () => string[]; default: not declared — Sorted list of the surface's expiry labels.
- VolatilitySurface().return.heston?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/options').HestonParameters; default: not declared — The global Heston parameters when `model: 'heston'`, else `undefined`.
- VolatilitySurface().return.impliedVolatility: (strike: number, expiry: string | number) => number; default: not declared — Implied vol at `(strike, expiry)`. Throws if the surface is empty (never fabricates).
- VolatilitySurface().return.impliedVolatilityByDelta: (callDelta: number, expiry: string | number) => number; default: not declared — Implied vol on the call-delta axis: interpolate the strike whose call-delta equals `callDelta`
(∈ (0, 1)) from the slice's stored delta ladder, then read the smile there. A 0.25 delta selects
the 25-delta call strike.
- VolatilitySurface().return.impliedVolatilityByMoneyness: (moneyness: number, expiry: string | number, options?: { forward?: boolean; }) => number; default: not declared — Implied vol on the moneyness axis. `moneyness` is `K/S` (spot-moneyness) by default, or `K/F`
(forward-moneyness) when `forward` is set — so `impliedVolatilityByMoneyness(1, e)` is the at-the-money(-forward) vol.

For a NUMERIC `expiry` (a maturity in years) the forward is computed AT THAT MATURITY,
`F(t) = spot·e^{(r−q)·t}` — not borrowed from the nearest fitted slice, which anchored a
mid-expiry query to a neighbour's forward and shifted the ATM-forward point off by the carry
between them.
- VolatilitySurface().return.lookup: (strike: number, expiry: string | number) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SurfaceLookup; default: not declared — Implied vol at `(strike, expiry)` with diagnostics. Strike uses the per-slice smile; expiry
interpolates total variance linearly between the two bracketing slices. `extrapolated` is true
when the query lies outside the fitted strike range or expiry range.
- VolatilitySurface().return.model: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SurfaceModel; default: not declared
- VolatilitySurface().return.points: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SurfacePoint[]; default: not declared
- VolatilitySurface().return.shock: (shifts: { parallel?: number; skewTilt?: number; }, { sticky }?: { sticky?: 'strike' | 'moneyness'; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').VolatilitySurface; default: not declared — Return a NEW surface with a shifted vol structure, produced WITHOUT re-fitting: each stored IV
sample gains a `parallel` offset plus a `skewTilt · k` skew rotation (`k = ln(K/forward)`,
log-moneyness), the per-slice deltas are recomputed from the shifted IVs, and only the
interpolators are rebuilt. The shock is echoed in the new surface's `assumptions.shock`.

`sticky`: `'strike'` (default) pins the tilt to each stored strike's own log-moneyness vs the slice
forward; `'moneyness'` lets the same additive shift travel with moneyness. Because the shift is
applied to the stored strike-indexed IV samples, both modes coincide at the stored strikes in this
eager v1 — the distinction only matters once a surface is re-anchored to a new spot/forward, which
this method does not do; the requested mode is recorded in `assumptions.shock.sticky` so a caller
that later re-anchors knows how the tilt was meant to travel.

Parametric models (`svi`/`sabr`/`heston`) have no closed-form shock, so the current smile is SAMPLED
at each slice's stored strikes, those samples are shifted, and the result DEGRADES to
`'interpolated'` with a `volatility.shock_degraded_to_interpolated` `warn` — the parametric fit is not
re-fit. Non-parametric models (`raw`/`interpolated`/`smoothed`) are preserved.

Rejects a `schemaVersion` mismatch (design law

- VolatilitySurface.fromJSON().return.impliedVolatilityByDelta: (callDelta: number, expiry: string | number) => number; default: not declared — Implied vol on the call-delta axis: interpolate the strike whose call-delta equals `callDelta`
(∈ (0, 1)) from the slice's stored delta ladder, then read the smile there. A 0.25 delta selects
the 25-delta call strike.
- VolatilitySurface.fromJSON().return.impliedVolatilityByMoneyness: (moneyness: number, expiry: string | number, options?: { forward?: boolean; }) => number; default: not declared — Implied vol on the moneyness axis. `moneyness` is `K/S` (spot-moneyness) by default, or `K/F`
(forward-moneyness) when `forward` is set — so `impliedVolatilityByMoneyness(1, e)` is the at-the-money(-forward) vol.

For a NUMERIC `expiry` (a maturity in years) the forward is computed AT THAT MATURITY,
`F(t) = spot·e^{(r−q)·t}` — not borrowed from the nearest fitted slice, which anchored a
mid-expiry query to a neighbour's forward and shifted the ATM-forward point off by the carry
between them.
- VolatilitySurface.fromJSON().return.lookup: (strike: number, expiry: string | number) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SurfaceLookup; default: not declared — Implied vol at `(strike, expiry)` with diagnostics. Strike uses the per-slice smile; expiry
interpolates total variance linearly between the two bracketing slices. `extrapolated` is true
when the query lies outside the fitted strike range or expiry range.
- VolatilitySurface.fromJSON().return.model: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SurfaceModel; default: not declared
- VolatilitySurface.fromJSON().return.points: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SurfacePoint[]; default: not declared
- VolatilitySurface.fromJSON().return.shock: (shifts: { parallel?: number; skewTilt?: number; }, { sticky }?: { sticky?: 'strike' | 'moneyness'; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').VolatilitySurface; default: not declared — Return a NEW surface with a shifted vol structure, produced WITHOUT re-fitting: each stored IV
sample gains a `parallel` offset plus a `skewTilt · k` skew rotation (`k = ln(K/forward)`,
log-moneyness), the per-slice deltas are recomputed from the shifted IVs, and only the
interpolators are rebuilt. The shock is echoed in the new surface's `assumptions.shock`.

`sticky`: `'strike'` (default) pins the tilt to each stored strike's own log-moneyness vs the slice
forward; `'moneyness'` lets the same additive shift travel with moneyness. Because the shift is
applied to the stored strike-indexed IV samples, both modes coincide at the stored strikes in this
eager v1 — the distinction only matters once a surface is re-anchored to a new spot/forward, which
this method does not do; the requested mode is recorded in `assumptions.shock.sticky` so a caller
that later re-anchors knows how the tilt was meant to travel.

Parametric models (`svi`/`sabr`/`heston`) have no closed-form shock, so the current smile is SAMPLED
at each slice's stored strikes, those samples are shifted, and the result DEGRADES to
`'interpolated'` with a `volatility.shock_degraded_to_interpolated` `warn` — the parametric fit is not
re-fit. Non-parametric models (`raw`/`interpolated`/`smoothed`) are preserved.

call's first-touch teaching errors stay byte-identical.

- calendarSkew.explain(surface).impliedVolatilityByDelta: (callDelta: number, expiry: string | number) => number; default: not declared — Implied vol on the call-delta axis: interpolate the strike whose call-delta equals `callDelta`
(∈ (0, 1)) from the slice's stored delta ladder, then read the smile there. A 0.25 delta selects
the 25-delta call strike.
- calendarSkew.explain(surface).impliedVolatilityByMoneyness: (moneyness: number, expiry: string | number, options?: { forward?: boolean; }) => number; default: not declared — Implied vol on the moneyness axis. `moneyness` is `K/S` (spot-moneyness) by default, or `K/F`
(forward-moneyness) when `forward` is set — so `impliedVolatilityByMoneyness(1, e)` is the at-the-money(-forward) vol.

For a NUMERIC `expiry` (a maturity in years) the forward is computed AT THAT MATURITY,
`F(t) = spot·e^{(r−q)·t}` — not borrowed from the nearest fitted slice, which anchored a
mid-expiry query to a neighbour's forward and shifted the ATM-forward point off by the carry
between them.
- calendarSkew.explain(surface).lookup: (strike: number, expiry: string | number) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SurfaceLookup; default: not declared — Implied vol at `(strike, expiry)` with diagnostics. Strike uses the per-slice smile; expiry
interpolates total variance linearly between the two bracketing slices. `extrapolated` is true
when the query lies outside the fitted strike range or expiry range.
