- calendarSkew.explain(surface).points: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SurfacePoint[]; default: not declared
- calendarSkew.explain(surface).shock: (shifts: { parallel?: number; skewTilt?: number; }, { sticky }?: { sticky?: 'strike' | 'moneyness'; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').VolatilitySurface; default: not declared — Return a NEW surface with a shifted vol structure, produced WITHOUT re-fitting: each stored IV
sample gains a `parallel` offset plus a `skewTilt · k` skew rotation (`k = ln(K/forward)`,
log-moneyness), the per-slice deltas are recomputed from the shifted IVs, and only the
interpolators are rebuilt. The shock is echoed in the new surface's `assumptions.shock`.

`sticky`: `'strike'` (default) pins the tilt to each stored strike's own log-moneyness vs the slice
forward; `'moneyness'` lets the same additive shift travel with moneyness. Because the shift is
applied to the stored strike-indexed IV samples, both modes coincide at the stored strikes in this
eager v1 — the distinction only matters once a surface is re-anchored to a new spot/forward, which
this method does not do; the requested mode is recorded in `assumptions.shock.sticky` so a caller
that later re-anchors knows how the tilt was meant to travel.

Parametric models (`svi`/`sabr`/`heston`) have no closed-form shock, so the current smile is SAMPLED
at each slice's stored strikes, those samples are shifted, and the result DEGRADES to
`'interpolated'` with a `volatility.shock_degraded_to_interpolated` `warn` — the parametric fit is not
re-fit. Non-parametric models (`raw`/`interpolated`/`smoothed`) are preserved.
- calendarSkew.explain(surface).slice: (expiry: string | number) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SurfaceSlice | undefined; default: not declared — The smile at an expiry (exact label or nearest by `t`), or `undefined` if none.

- calibrateVannaVolga5: (input: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').VannaVolga5Input) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').VannaVolga5Smile; default: not declared — Build the FX/crypto smile from the full five-quote set — ATM + the 25Δ and 10Δ risk reversal / butterfly —
so it **exactly reprices all five market pillars** (10Δ put, 25Δ put, ATM, 25Δ call, 10Δ call) and pins the
wings to real quotes instead of extrapolating them like the 3-pillar {@link calibrateVannaVolga} /
{@link vannaVolgaApproximation}. The anchors come from {@link smileFromQuotes} at each delta; the smile is a
shape-preserving PCHIP interpolation of total variance `σ²T` in log-moneyness (exact at the pillars, C¹
smooth, no overshoot). Exact repricing of arbitrary quotes can't guarantee no arbitrage, so the implied
Breeden–Litzenberger density is checked across the pillar span and a butterfly arbitrage is a disclosed
warning. See `docs/specs/vanna-volga-5.md`.

- fitGarch: (returns: number[], options?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').GarchFitOptions) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').GarchFit; default: not declared — Fit a GARCH(1,1) model to a returns series by Gaussian MLE.

The conditional variance follows `σ²ₜ = ω + α·r²ₜ₋₁ + β·σ²ₜ₋₁`, seeded with the sample second moment
`E[r²]`. The optimizer works in the unconstrained space `θ = (log ω, logit p, logit f)` where
`p = α+β` and `f = α/(α+β)`, so `ω>0, α≥0, β≥0, α+β<1` hold at every evaluation. A degenerate
(constant / zero-variance) series has no variance process to fit and returns `converged: false`.
- fitGarch().return.alpha: number; default: not declared — ARCH coefficient on the lagged squared return (`≥ 0`).
- fitGarch().return.assumptions: { conventionsVersion: string; initialParameters: 'supplied' | 'default'; mean: 'zero' | 'sample'; observations: number; }; default: not declared — Applied conventions, echoed (Law 2 report grammar).
- fitGarch().return.assumptions.conventionsVersion: string; default: not declared
- fitGarch().return.assumptions.initialParameters: 'supplied' | 'default'; default: not declared — Whether the primary start was caller-supplied (`initialParameters`) or the classic (0.05, 0.90).
- fitGarch().return.assumptions.mean: 'zero' | 'sample'; default: not declared
- fitGarch().return.assumptions.observations: number; default: not declared
- fitGarch().return.beta: number; default: not declared — GARCH coefficient on the lagged conditional variance (`≥ 0`).
- fitGarch().return.converged: boolean; default: not declared — Whether the optimizer converged (never fabricated).
- fitGarch().return.diagnostics: { warnings: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').QuantWarning[]; }; default: not declared — Structured warnings; a degenerate / non-converged fit explains itself here.
- fitGarch().return.diagnostics.warnings: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').QuantWarning[]; default: not declared
- fitGarch().return.iterations: number; default: not declared — Optimizer iterations performed.
- fitGarch().return.logLikelihood: number | null; default: not declared — Maximized Gaussian log-likelihood; `null` when the likelihood is degenerate (disclosed).
- fitGarch().return.longRunVariance: number; default: not declared — Unconditional variance `ω / (1 − α − β)` the forecast mean-reverts to.
- fitGarch().return.omega: number; default: not declared — Constant term of the variance recursion (`> 0`).
- fitGarch().return.persistence: number; default: not declared — `α + β` — the variance half-life driver; `< 1` for a stationary fit.
- fitGarch(options)?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').GarchFitOptions; default: not declared
- fitGarch(options).initialParameters?: { alpha: number; beta: number; }; default: not declared — Warm start for the `(α, β)` search (Stage 4.5): replaces the primary `(0.05, 0.90)` start; `ω`
is derived by variance targeting and is not a start. The seeded restarts still run.
- fitGarch(options).initialParameters.alpha: number; default: not declared
- fitGarch(options).initialParameters.beta: number; default: not declared
- fitGarch(options).mean?: 'zero' | 'sample'; default: not declared — `'zero'` (default) assumes a zero-mean series; `'sample'` de-means by the sample mean first.
- fitGarch(options).seed?: number; default: not declared — Seed for the deterministic multi-start of the optimizer (default `0x61726368`).
- fitGarch(returns): number[]; default: not declared
- fitHarRv: (realizedVariances: number[], options?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').HarRvOptions) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').HarRvFit; default: not declared — Fit a HAR-RV (heterogeneous autoregressive) model to a realized-variance series by OLS.

Regresses `RVₜ` on `[1, RVₜ₋₁, avg(last {@link HarRvOptions.weekly}), avg(last
{@link HarRvOptions.monthly})]`. The 4×4 least-squares system is solved by QR (stable — no
normal-equations conditioning penalty). Requires more than `monthly` observations, with at least
{@link HAR_PREDICTORS} fitted rows so the system is well-posed.
- fitHarRv().return.assumptions: { conventionsVersion: string; method: 'ols-qr'; weekly: number; monthly: number; }; default: not declared — Applied conventions, echoed (Law 2 report grammar).
- fitHarRv().return.assumptions.conventionsVersion: string; default: not declared
- fitHarRv().return.assumptions.method: 'ols-qr'; default: not declared
- fitHarRv().return.assumptions.monthly: number; default: not declared
- fitHarRv().return.assumptions.weekly: number; default: not declared
- fitHarRv().return.coefficients: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').HarRvCoefficients; default: not declared
- fitHarRv().return.diagnostics: { warnings: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').QuantWarning[]; }; default: not declared — Structured warnings; a flat response (undefined R²) explains itself here.
- fitHarRv().return.diagnostics.warnings: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').QuantWarning[]; default: not declared
- fitHarRv().return.observationCount: number; default: not declared — Number of fitted observations.
- fitHarRv().return.rSquared: number | null; default: not declared — In-sample coefficient of determination (`null` for a flat response — disclosed, never NaN).
- fitHarRv().return.residuals: number[]; default: not declared — In-sample residuals `RVₜ − ŘVₜ`, one per fitted observation.
- fitHarRv().return.windows: { weekly: number; monthly: number; }; default: not declared — The daily/weekly/monthly averaging windows used (also drives {@link harRvForecast}).
- fitHarRv().return.windows.monthly: number; default: not declared
- fitHarRv().return.windows.weekly: number; default: not declared
- fitHarRv(options)?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').HarRvOptions; default: not declared
- fitHarRv(options).monthly?: number; default: not declared — Monthly averaging window in observations (default 22).
- fitHarRv(options).weekly?: number; default: not declared — Weekly averaging window in observations (default 5).
- fitHarRv(realizedVariances): number[]; default: not declared
- forwardSkew: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').ForwardSkewFacade; default: not declared — Forward skew: the skew slope of the *forward-starting* smile between two expiries, built from the
added forward variance at fixed forward-log-moneyness. `d(σ_fwd)/d(logMoneyness)` via a central
difference, where `σ_fwd(k) = √((w_far(k) − w_near(k))/(t_far − t_near))`.

Throws the same {@link ArbitrageError} (`volatility.calendar_arbitrage`) as {@link forwardVolatility}
when the forward variance is negative at either sampled `k` — a forward smile that does not exist
is reported, never clamped to zero and differenced into a plausible-looking number.

Facade (H23): the plain call returns the scalar; `.explain()` discloses the applied `step` in
`assumptions` and BOTH total-variance calculations (the `k = +step` and `k = −step` legs) in
`diagnostics.decomposition`. Hand-attached (not `seriesFacade`) so the closed-request teaching
error for a `null` options bag stays byte-identical.
- forwardSkew(from): string | number; default: not declared
- forwardSkew(options)?: { step?: number; } | undefined; default: not declared
- forwardSkew(options).step?: number; default: not declared
- forwardSkew(surface): import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').VolatilitySurface; default: not declared
- forwardSkew(surface).arbitrage: (options?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').ArbitrageCheckOptions) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').ArbitrageReport; default: not declared — Run the static no-arbitrage diagnostics (calendar + butterfly) over this surface.
- forwardSkew(surface).assumptions: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Assumptions<{ shock?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SurfaceShock; }>; default: not declared
- forwardSkew(surface).diagnostics: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Diagnostics; default: not declared
- forwardSkew(surface).essvi?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').ESSVIParameters; default: not declared — The global eSSVI parameters when `model: 'essvi'`, else `undefined`.
- forwardSkew(surface).expiries: () => string[]; default: not declared — Sorted list of the surface's expiry labels.
- forwardSkew(surface).heston?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/options').HestonParameters; default: not declared — The global Heston parameters when `model: 'heston'`, else `undefined`.
- forwardSkew(surface).impliedVolatility: (strike: number, expiry: string | number) => number; default: not declared — Implied vol at `(strike, expiry)`. Throws if the surface is empty (never fabricates).
- forwardSkew(surface).impliedVolatilityByDelta: (callDelta: number, expiry: string | number) => number; default: not declared — Implied vol on the call-delta axis: interpolate the strike whose call-delta equals `callDelta`
(∈ (0, 1)) from the slice's stored delta ladder, then read the smile there. A 0.25 delta selects
the 25-delta call strike.
- forwardSkew(surface).impliedVolatilityByMoneyness: (moneyness: number, expiry: string | number, options?: { forward?: boolean; }) => number; default: not declared — Implied vol on the moneyness axis. `moneyness` is `K/S` (spot-moneyness) by default, or `K/F`
(forward-moneyness) when `forward` is set — so `impliedVolatilityByMoneyness(1, e)` is the at-the-money(-forward) vol.

For a NUMERIC `expiry` (a maturity in years) the forward is computed AT THAT MATURITY,
`F(t) = spot·e^{(r−q)·t}` — not borrowed from the nearest fitted slice, which anchored a
mid-expiry query to a neighbour's forward and shifted the ATM-forward point off by the carry
between them.
- forwardSkew(surface).lookup: (strike: number, expiry: string | number) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SurfaceLookup; default: not declared — Implied vol at `(strike, expiry)` with diagnostics. Strike uses the per-slice smile; expiry
interpolates total variance linearly between the two bracketing slices. `extrapolated` is true
when the query lies outside the fitted strike range or expiry range.
- forwardSkew(surface).model: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SurfaceModel; default: not declared
- forwardSkew(surface).points: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SurfacePoint[]; default: not declared
- forwardSkew(surface).shock: (shifts: { parallel?: number; skewTilt?: number; }, { sticky }?: { sticky?: 'strike' | 'moneyness'; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').VolatilitySurface; default: not declared — Return a NEW surface with a shifted vol structure, produced WITHOUT re-fitting: each stored IV
sample gains a `parallel` offset plus a `skewTilt · k` skew rotation (`k = ln(K/forward)`,
log-moneyness), the per-slice deltas are recomputed from the shifted IVs, and only the
interpolators are rebuilt. The shock is echoed in the new surface's `assumptions.shock`.

`sticky`: `'strike'` (default) pins the tilt to each stored strike's own log-moneyness vs the slice
forward; `'moneyness'` lets the same additive shift travel with moneyness. Because the shift is
applied to the stored strike-indexed IV samples, both modes coincide at the stored strikes in this
eager v1 — the distinction only matters once a surface is re-anchored to a new spot/forward, which
this method does not do; the requested mode is recorded in `assumptions.shock.sticky` so a caller
that later re-anchors knows how the tilt was meant to travel.

Parametric models (`svi`/`sabr`/`heston`) have no closed-form shock, so the current smile is SAMPLED
at each slice's stored strikes, those samples are shifted, and the result DEGRADES to
`'interpolated'` with a `volatility.shock_degraded_to_interpolated` `warn` — the parametric fit is not
re-fit. Non-parametric models (`raw`/`interpolated`/`smoothed`) are preserved.
- forwardSkew(surface).slice: (expiry: string | number) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SurfaceSlice | undefined; default: not declared — The smile at an expiry (exact label or nearest by `t`), or `undefined` if none.

with {@link VolatilitySurface.fromJSON}; the pair round-trips `iv()` identically on all six models.

sample gains a `parallel` offset plus a `skewTilt · k` skew rotation (`k = ln(K/forward)`,

interpolators are rebuilt. The shock is echoed in the new surface's `assumptions.shock`.

`sticky`: `'strike'` (default) pins the tilt to each stored strike's own log-moneyness vs the slice
forward; `'moneyness'` lets the same additive shift travel with moneyness. Because the shift is
applied to the stored strike-indexed IV samples, both modes coincide at the stored strikes in this
eager v1 — the distinction only matters once a surface is re-anchored to a new spot/forward, which
this method does not do; the requested mode is recorded in `assumptions.shock.sticky` so a caller
that later re-anchors knows how the tilt was meant to travel.

Parametric models (`svi`/`sabr`/`heston`) have no closed-form shock, so the current smile is SAMPLED
at each slice's stored strikes, those samples are shifted, and the result DEGRADES to
`'interpolated'` with a `volatility.shock_degraded_to_interpolated` `warn` — the parametric fit is not
re-fit. Non-parametric models (`raw`/`interpolated`/`smoothed`) are preserved.

`F(t) = spot·e^{(r−q)·t}` — not borrowed from the nearest fitted slice, which anchored a
mid-expiry query to a neighbour's forward and shifted the ATM-forward point off by the carry
between them.

- harRvForecast: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').HarRvForecastFacade; default: not declared — One-step-ahead HAR-RV forecast from the latest daily/weekly/monthly aggregates of `history`,
using the same windows the model was fit with. Requires at least `monthly` observations.

A NEGATIVE forecast throws (`volatility.negative_variance_forecast`): the linear model can
extrapolate below zero, and a negative variance is not a variance — it is never clamped, and never
returned as if it were a successful forecast. `.explain()` throws the same typed error — a failed
model output is never softened into an envelope.

Facade (H24): the plain call returns the scalar; `.explain()` discloses the fitted windows in
`assumptions`, and the three predictors plus the per-term regression contributions (which sum to
the raw model output, i.e. the value) in `diagnostics.decomposition`. Hand-attached (not
`seriesFacade`) so the closed-request teaching error for a hand-rolled `fit` stays byte-identical.

- observedSkew: (input: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').ObservedSkewInput) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').ObservedSkewResult; default: not declared — Observe a single expiry. Compose separate calls for a term structure; compare their mean ATM IVs
only when available. IV/RR/BF/spreads are decimals (multiply by 100 for IV-point displays).
Missing IV/delta is omission, not null/NaN/zero. Missing wings and insufficient/expired samples
return null with reasons. Supplied malformed values throw; no alternate quote/date shapes,
delta recomputation, interpolation, forward adjustment or tail extrapolation is performed.
Distance ties and inclusive boundaries allow only 4 × machine epsilon at the arithmetic operand
scale. Ties are measured against the global minimum, then use the disclosed lower-strike order;
an exact observed target always wins and a zero delta tolerance remains strictly exact.

- riskNeutralDistribution: (volatilitySmile: (strike: number) => number, options: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').RiskNeutralOptions) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').RiskNeutralDistribution; default: not declared — Breeden–Litzenberger (1978): the risk-neutral terminal distribution implied by a call-price curve.
Given the smile `volatilitySmile(strike)`, prices calls via BSM and differentiates numerically:
`f(K) = e^{rT}·∂²C/∂K²` and `F(K) = 1 + e^{rT}·∂C/∂K`. Use it for probability cones / expected-range
bands. The smile must be arbitrage-free for the density to stay non-negative.

Where it repairs itself, it SAYS SO on the returned `diagnostics`: a negative (arbitrageable)
density clamped to zero, and the one-sided difference used for strikes within `step` of zero (a
deep-downside probe like `density(0.05)` on a $100 name, which used to price a negative strike and
return `NaN`). `diagnostics.warnings` fills in as the closures are queried — read it after use.
- riskNeutralDistribution().return.cdf: (strike: number) => number; default: not declared — Risk-neutral CDF `P(S_T ≤ K) = 1 + e^{rT}·∂C/∂K`, clamped to [0, 1].
- riskNeutralDistribution().return.density: (strike: number) => number; default: not declared — Risk-neutral PDF at strike `K`: `e^{rT}·∂²C/∂K²` (clamped ≥ 0 — see {@link diagnostics}).
- riskNeutralDistribution().return.diagnostics: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Diagnostics; default: not declared — LIVE disclosure channel for the two places this object silently repairs itself — it accumulates
as the closures are called, so read it AFTER querying (it starts empty):

 • `model.limitation` "negative density clamped" — `∂²C/∂K²` came out negative, which means the
   smile is butterfly-arbitrageable there. The clamp keeps `density()` a density; the warning
   stops a caller integrating a repaired curve and calling it the market's distribution.
 • `model.limitation` "one-sided difference" — a query within `step` of zero, where the centred
   difference would price a NEGATIVE strike (which returned `NaN`).
- riskNeutralDistribution().return.probabilityAbove: (strike: number) => number; default: not declared
- riskNeutralDistribution().return.probabilityBelow: (strike: number) => number; default: not declared
- riskNeutralDistribution().return.probabilityBetween: (lowerStrike: number, upperStrike: number) => number; default: not declared

- surfaceArbitrageReport(surface).impliedVolatilityByDelta: (callDelta: number, expiry: string | number) => number; default: not declared — Implied vol on the call-delta axis: interpolate the strike whose call-delta equals `callDelta`

- surfaceArbitrageReport(surface).impliedVolatilityByMoneyness: (moneyness: number, expiry: string | number, options?: { forward?: boolean; }) => number; default: not declared — Implied vol on the moneyness axis. `moneyness` is `K/S` (spot-moneyness) by default, or `K/F`
(forward-moneyness) when `forward` is set — so `impliedVolatilityByMoneyness(1, e)` is the at-the-money(-forward) vol.

For a NUMERIC `expiry` (a maturity in years) the forward is computed AT THAT MATURITY,
`F(t) = spot·e^{(r−q)·t}` — not borrowed from the nearest fitted slice, which anchored a
mid-expiry query to a neighbour's forward and shifted the ATM-forward point off by the carry
between them.
- surfaceArbitrageReport(surface).lookup: (strike: number, expiry: string | number) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SurfaceLookup; default: not declared — Implied vol at `(strike, expiry)` with diagnostics. Strike uses the per-slice smile; expiry
interpolates total variance linearly between the two bracketing slices. `extrapolated` is true
when the query lies outside the fitted strike range or expiry range.

- surfaceArbitrageReport(surface).points: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SurfacePoint[]; default: not declared
- surfaceArbitrageReport(surface).shock: (shifts: { parallel?: number; skewTilt?: number; }, { sticky }?: { sticky?: 'strike' | 'moneyness'; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').VolatilitySurface; default: not declared — Return a NEW surface with a shifted vol structure, produced WITHOUT re-fitting: each stored IV
sample gains a `parallel` offset plus a `skewTilt · k` skew rotation (`k = ln(K/forward)`,
log-moneyness), the per-slice deltas are recomputed from the shifted IVs, and only the
interpolators are rebuilt. The shock is echoed in the new surface's `assumptions.shock`.

`sticky`: `'strike'` (default) pins the tilt to each stored strike's own log-moneyness vs the slice
forward; `'moneyness'` lets the same additive shift travel with moneyness. Because the shift is
applied to the stored strike-indexed IV samples, both modes coincide at the stored strikes in this
eager v1 — the distinction only matters once a surface is re-anchored to a new spot/forward, which
this method does not do; the requested mode is recorded in `assumptions.shock.sticky` so a caller
that later re-anchors knows how the tilt was meant to travel.

Parametric models (`svi`/`sabr`/`heston`) have no closed-form shock, so the current smile is SAMPLED
at each slice's stored strikes, those samples are shifted, and the result DEGRADES to
`'interpolated'` with a `volatility.shock_degraded_to_interpolated` `warn` — the parametric fit is not
re-fit. Non-parametric models (`raw`/`interpolated`/`smoothed`) are preserved.

- surfacePcaScenarios: (input: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SurfacePcaScenarioInput) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SurfacePcaScenarios; default: not declared — Turn a fitted {@link surfacePCA} into **stress scenarios**: shock a base surface by `±k` standard
deviations along each principal mode (`k·√λ·loadings`, since `√λ` is the mode's 1-sigma move and the
loadings are unit-norm), and optionally by a combined per-mode move. Shocked volatilities are floored (default 0)
so a large downside shock can't go negative.

The shock is applied in the units the PCA was FITTED in (`pca.changeType`): `absolute` adds the
vector to the base vols, `relative` scales them (`base·(1 + shock)`), because a relative PCA's
modes are proportional moves. See `docs/specs/surface-pca-scenarios.md`.

- surfacePcaScenarios().return.assumptions.changeType: 'absolute' | 'relative'; default: not declared
- surfacePcaScenarios().return.assumptions.conventionsVersion: string; default: not declared
- surfacePcaScenarios().return.assumptions.floor: number; default: not declared
- surfacePcaScenarios().return.base: number[]; default: not declared
- surfacePcaScenarios().return.combinedSurface?: number[]; default: not declared — `base + Σ sᵢ·√λᵢ·loadingsᵢ`, floored — present only when `combined` is supplied.
- surfacePcaScenarios().return.diagnostics: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Diagnostics; default: not declared
- surfacePcaScenarios().return.scenarios: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SurfaceScenario[]; default: not declared — One per `(mode, sigma)`, in mode-major order.

- surfacePcaScenarios(input).combined?: number[]; default: not declared — Optional per-mode sigma moves → one combined shocked surface.

(Bachelier) volatilities are unchanged (a common shift cancels in `forward − strike`). See
`docs/specs/swaption-cube-shift.md`.

- varianceSwapRate: (options: { strikes: number[]; otmPrices: number[]; forward: number; riskFreeRate: number; timeToExpiryYears: number; boundaryCallPrice?: number; boundaryPriceAveraged?: boolean; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Computed<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').VarianceSwapResult, { measure: 'risk-neutral'; method: 'ddkz-replication'; }>; default: not declared — Model-free implied volatility via the CBOE VIX replication (Demeterfi–Derman–Kamal–Zou): a strip of
out-of-the-money option mid-prices integrates to the fair variance
`σ² = (2/T)·Σ (ΔKᵢ/Kᵢ²)·e^{rT}·Q(Kᵢ) − (1/T)·(F/K₀ − 1)²`, where `K₀` is the highest strike below the
forward `F`. `otmPrices[i]` is the OTM option (put below `F`, call above) mid at `strikes[i]`.

**At `K₀` the CBOE strip is the AVERAGE of the put and the call**, and the `−(1/T)(F/K₀ − 1)²`
correction subtracted here is derived for exactly that convention. Supply the `K₀` call as
`boundaryCallPrice` and pass the `K₀` PUT in `otmPrices` — the two are averaged for you. With a
put-only `K₀` price and no `boundaryCallPrice` the strip under-states variance by
`ΔK₀·(F − K₀)/(T·K₀²)` (by put–call parity the missing half-difference is `(C−P)/2 = e^{−rT}(F−K₀)/2`),
which on a typical 1-month index chain is ~1.7 vol points — so the disclosure rides the result.
- varianceSwapRate().return.assumptions: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Assumptions<{ measure: 'risk-neutral'; method: 'ddkz-replication'; }>; default: not declared — Every applied convention, echoed back.
- varianceSwapRate().return.diagnostics: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Diagnostics; default: not declared — How the value was computed, plus any warnings.
- varianceSwapRate().return.provenance?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Provenance; default: not declared — Optional data lineage when the inputs came from a provider.
- varianceSwapRate().return.value: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').VarianceSwapResult; default: not declared — The computed value. Never `NaN` or `±Infinity`: a value the model cannot produce is `null`
beside a diagnostic that says why (Law 7 — a warning never licenses a non-finite number).
- varianceSwapRate(options): { strikes: number[]; otmPrices: number[]; forward: number; riskFreeRate: number; timeToExpiryYears: number; boundaryCallPrice?: number; boundaryPriceAveraged?: boolean; }; default: not declared
- varianceSwapRate(options).boundaryCallPrice?: number; default: not declared — The CALL price at `K₀` (the highest strike ≤ `F`), with the `K₀` PUT passed in `otmPrices`.
Supplied ⇒ the `K₀` term becomes the CBOE put/call average; omitted ⇒ `otmPrices` is used as
given and the put-only bias is disclosed in `diagnostics`.
- varianceSwapRate(options).boundaryPriceAveraged?: boolean; default: not declared — Set when `otmPrices` at `K₀` is ALREADY the CBOE put/call average (a chain extractor that
averaged there). Suppresses the put-only bias disclosure without touching the arithmetic. Cannot
be combined with `boundaryCallPrice` — that would average an average.
- varianceSwapRate(options).forward: number; default: not declared
- varianceSwapRate(options).otmPrices: number[]; default: not declared
- varianceSwapRate(options).riskFreeRate: number; default: not declared
- varianceSwapRate(options).strikes: number[]; default: not declared
- varianceSwapRate(options).timeToExpiryYears: number; default: not declared
- volatilityCone: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').VolatilityConeFacade; default: not declared — Realized-volatility cone: for each lookback `window`, the percentile spread of annualized realized
volatility across all rolling windows of the return series, plus the current reading. The classic
"is implied vol rich or cheap vs the underlying's own realized history" view.

Facade (H27): the plain call returns the rows array; `.explain()` discloses the applied
`periodsPerYear`, windows, and annualization convention in `assumptions`, and the observation
count / annualization factor in `diagnostics.decomposition`. Hand-attached (not `seriesFacade`)
so the closed-request teaching errors for the options bag stay byte-identical.
- volatilityCone(options): { windows: number[]; periodsPerYear?: number; }; default: not declared
- volatilityCone(options).periodsPerYear?: number; default: not declared
- volatilityCone(options).windows: number[]; default: not declared
- volatilityCone(returns): ArrayLike<number>; default: not declared
- volatilityCone.explain: (returns: ArrayLike<number>, options: { windows: number[]; periodsPerYear?: number; }) => Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Computed<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').VolatilityConeWindow[]>, 'assumptions'> & { assumptions: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').VolatilityConeAssumptions; }; default: not declared
- volatilityCone.explain().return.assumptions: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').VolatilityConeAssumptions; default: not declared
- volatilityCone.explain().return.diagnostics: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Diagnostics; default: not declared — How the value was computed, plus any warnings.
- volatilityCone.explain().return.provenance?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Provenance; default: not declared — Optional data lineage when the inputs came from a provider.
- volatilityCone.explain().return.value: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').VolatilityConeWindow[]; default: not declared — The computed value. Never `NaN` or `±Infinity`: a value the model cannot produce is `null`
beside a diagnostic that says why (Law 7 — a warning never licenses a non-finite number).
- volatilityCone.explain(options): { windows: number[]; periodsPerYear?: number; }; default: not declared

- volatilitySurface: (input: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility/surface').VolatilitySurfaceInput) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').VolatilitySurface; default: not declared
- volatilitySurface().return.arbitrage: (options?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').ArbitrageCheckOptions) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').ArbitrageReport; default: not declared — Run the static no-arbitrage diagnostics (calendar + butterfly) over this surface.
- volatilitySurface().return.assumptions: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Assumptions<{ shock?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SurfaceShock; }>; default: not declared

- volatilitySurface().return.expiries: () => string[]; default: not declared — Sorted list of the surface's expiry labels.
- volatilitySurface().return.heston?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/options').HestonParameters; default: not declared — The global Heston parameters when `model: 'heston'`, else `undefined`.
- volatilitySurface().return.impliedVolatility: (strike: number, expiry: string | number) => number; default: not declared — Implied vol at `(strike, expiry)`. Throws if the surface is empty (never fabricates).
- volatilitySurface().return.impliedVolatilityByDelta: (callDelta: number, expiry: string | number) => number; default: not declared — Implied vol on the call-delta axis: interpolate the strike whose call-delta equals `callDelta`
(∈ (0, 1)) from the slice's stored delta ladder, then read the smile there. A 0.25 delta selects
the 25-delta call strike.
- volatilitySurface().return.impliedVolatilityByMoneyness: (moneyness: number, expiry: string | number, options?: { forward?: boolean; }) => number; default: not declared — Implied vol on the moneyness axis. `moneyness` is `K/S` (spot-moneyness) by default, or `K/F`
(forward-moneyness) when `forward` is set — so `impliedVolatilityByMoneyness(1, e)` is the at-the-money(-forward) vol.

For a NUMERIC `expiry` (a maturity in years) the forward is computed AT THAT MATURITY,
`F(t) = spot·e^{(r−q)·t}` — not borrowed from the nearest fitted slice, which anchored a
mid-expiry query to a neighbour's forward and shifted the ATM-forward point off by the carry
between them.
- volatilitySurface().return.lookup: (strike: number, expiry: string | number) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SurfaceLookup; default: not declared — Implied vol at `(strike, expiry)` with diagnostics. Strike uses the per-slice smile; expiry
interpolates total variance linearly between the two bracketing slices. `extrapolated` is true
when the query lies outside the fitted strike range or expiry range.
- volatilitySurface().return.model: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SurfaceModel; default: not declared
- volatilitySurface().return.points: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SurfacePoint[]; default: not declared
- volatilitySurface().return.shock: (shifts: { parallel?: number; skewTilt?: number; }, { sticky }?: { sticky?: 'strike' | 'moneyness'; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').VolatilitySurface; default: not declared — Return a NEW surface with a shifted vol structure, produced WITHOUT re-fitting: each stored IV
sample gains a `parallel` offset plus a `skewTilt · k` skew rotation (`k = ln(K/forward)`,
log-moneyness), the per-slice deltas are recomputed from the shifted IVs, and only the
interpolators are rebuilt. The shock is echoed in the new surface's `assumptions.shock`.

`sticky`: `'strike'` (default) pins the tilt to each stored strike's own log-moneyness vs the slice
forward; `'moneyness'` lets the same additive shift travel with moneyness. Because the shift is
applied to the stored strike-indexed IV samples, both modes coincide at the stored strikes in this
eager v1 — the distinction only matters once a surface is re-anchored to a new spot/forward, which
this method does not do; the requested mode is recorded in `assumptions.shock.sticky` so a caller
that later re-anchors knows how the tilt was meant to travel.

Parametric models (`svi`/`sabr`/`heston`) have no closed-form shock, so the current smile is SAMPLED
at each slice's stored strikes, those samples are shifted, and the result DEGRADES to
`'interpolated'` with a `volatility.shock_degraded_to_interpolated` `warn` — the parametric fit is not
re-fit. Non-parametric models (`raw`/`interpolated`/`smoothed`) are preserved.
- volatilitySurface().return.slice: (expiry: string | number) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SurfaceSlice | undefined; default: not declared — The smile at an expiry (exact label or nearest by `t`), or `undefined` if none.
- volatilitySurface().return.slices: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SurfaceSlice[]; default: not declared
- volatilitySurface().return.ssvi?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SSVIParameters; default: not declared — The global SSVI parameters when `model: 'ssvi'`, else `undefined`.
- volatilitySurface().return.toJSON: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').VolatilitySurfaceSnapshot; default: not declared — Serialize the surface to a plain, JSON-safe {@link VolatilitySurfaceSnapshot} (no closures). Restore it
with {@link VolatilitySurface.fromJSON}; the pair round-trips `iv()` identically on all six models.
- volatilitySurface().return.toRows: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SurfaceRow[]; default: not declared — The smile-chart / heatmap feed: one {@link SurfaceRow} per (slice, stored strike), with
`logMoneyness = ln(strike/forward)` and the stored `delta`/`iv`. Per the workspace missing-value
policy (WS2.12), any non-finite chart-facing numeric is emitted as `null` (never `NaN`, never
omitted).
- volatilitySurface(input): import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility/surface').VolatilitySurfaceInput; default: not declared
- volatilitySurface(input).config?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SurfaceConfig; default: not declared
- volatilitySurface(input).market: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SurfaceMarket; default: not declared
- volatilitySurface(input).quotes: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').OptionQuote[]; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/backtest#BacktestAssumptions

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

The modelling assumptions a backtest makes, echoed on every result's `assumptions` slot so they are
never hidden (spec §16.3 / dx §2.5). Each policy is a short, stable, machine-readable label.

```typescript
/**
 * The modelling assumptions a backtest makes, echoed on every result's `assumptions` slot so they are
 * never hidden (spec §16.3 / dx §2.5). Each policy is a short, stable, machine-readable label.
 */
export interface BacktestAssumptions {
    /** Version of the library's default conventions (core `CONVENTIONS_VERSION`). */
    conventionsVersion: string;
    /** Opening capital the run started from. */
    initialCapital: number;
    /** When/at what price orders fill, e.g. `next-open`, `close`, `trigger-price`. */
    fill: string;
    /** Commission model applied, e.g. `bps(1)`, `per-share(0.005)`, `none`. */
    cost: string;
    /** Slippage model applied, e.g. `bps(2)`, `spread`, `none`. */
    slippage: string;
    /** Cash settlement assumption, e.g. `immediate` (T+0). */
    cashSettlement: string;
    /** Corporate-action handling, e.g. `dividends-as-cash`, `splits-adjusted`, `none`. */
    corporateAction: string;
    /** Rebalancing/trading calendar, e.g. `every-bar`, `monthly`, `signal-driven`. */
    calendar: string;
    /** Leverage/margin regime: `unconstrained` (no cap; unfunded fills allowed) or `maxLeverage`. */
    margin: string;
    /** American early exercise/assignment policy: `model` or `none` (WS7.4). Absent where inapplicable. */
    assignment?: string;
    /**
     * How an OCO group resolves a bar that touches BOTH legs. One bar cannot say which trigger came
     * first, and the engine's answer — the take-profit, because a bracket submits it before the
     * stop-loss and orders fill in submission order — is optimistic. It is disclosed here rather than
     * left as an undocumented mechanic (`take-profit-first-on-ambiguous-bar`). Absent for engines with
     * no order book (the vectorized loop).
     */
    oco?: string;
}
```

- calendar: string; default: not declared — Rebalancing/trading calendar, e.g. `every-bar`, `monthly`, `signal-driven`.
- cashSettlement: string; default: not declared — Cash settlement assumption, e.g. `immediate` (T+0).
- conventionsVersion: string; default: not declared — Version of the library's default conventions (core `CONVENTIONS_VERSION`).
- corporateAction: string; default: not declared — Corporate-action handling, e.g. `dividends-as-cash`, `splits-adjusted`, `none`.
- cost: string; default: not declared — Commission model applied, e.g. `bps(1)`, `per-share(0.005)`, `none`.

- margin: string; default: not declared — Leverage/margin regime: `unconstrained` (no cap; unfunded fills allowed) or `maxLeverage`.
- oco?: string; default: not declared — How an OCO group resolves a bar that touches BOTH legs. One bar cannot say which trigger came

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/backtest#BrokerConfig

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

```typescript
export interface BrokerConfig {
    /** Opening cash. */
    cash: number;
    commission?: CostModel;
    slippage?: SlippageModel;
    borrow?: BorrowModel;
    /** Bars per year, for borrow accrual (default 252). */
    periodsPerYear?: number;
    /** Max gross leverage `Σ|positionNotional| / equity` allowed at fill (default `Infinity`). */
    maxLeverage?: number;
    /** Disallow short positions (default `false`). */
    noShort?: boolean;
    /** Cap a single bar's fill to this fraction of bar volume (partial fills); default `Infinity`. */
    maxVolumeParticipation?: number;
    /**
     * American early exercise/assignment policy (WS7.4). `'none'` (default) settles options only at
     * expiry — every European-style golden is byte-identical. `'model'` options in to modeling early
     * assignment of American short options at ex-dividend dates (short calls) and deep-ITM thresholds
     * (short puts), plus manual `exerciseOption`/`context.exercise` for American longs.
     */
    assignment?: 'model' | 'none';
    /**
     * Short-put early-assignment buffer as a FRACTION of strike (default `0.02`): a short put is
     * assigned early when the interest CARRY benefit of exercising now exceeds the remaining extrinsic
     * (time value) by more than `threshold·strike`. Only used when `assignment: 'model'`.
     */
    assignmentThreshold?: number;
    /**
     * Continuously-compounded risk-free rate (decimal, default `0`) used ONLY for the short-put
     * early-assignment carry economics — early put exercise is driven by the interest earned on the
     * strike over the option's remaining life. With rate `0` there is no carry incentive, so a short
     * put is never assigned early on arbitrage-free prices. Only used when `assignment: 'model'`.
     */
    riskFreeRate?: number;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- assignment?: 'none' | 'model'; default: not declared — American early exercise/assignment policy (WS7.4). `'none'` (default) settles options only at
expiry — every European-style golden is byte-identical. `'model'` options in to modeling early
assignment of American short options at ex-dividend dates (short calls) and deep-ITM thresholds
(short puts), plus manual `exerciseOption`/`context.exercise` for American longs.
- assignmentThreshold?: number; default: not declared — Short-put early-assignment buffer as a FRACTION of strike (default `0.02`): a short put is
assigned early when the interest CARRY benefit of exercising now exceeds the remaining extrinsic
(time value) by more than `threshold·strike`. Only used when `assignment: 'model'`.
- borrow?: BorrowModel; default: not declared
- borrow.annualRate: number; default: not declared — Annualized borrow rate (decimal, e.g. `0.005` = 50 bps/yr).
- borrow.label: string; default: not declared
- cash: number; default: not declared — Opening cash.
- commission?: CostModel; default: not declared
- commission.commission: (input: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/backtest/costs').CommissionInput) => number; default: not declared
- commission.commission(input): import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/backtest/costs').CommissionInput; default: not declared
- commission.commission(input).price: number; default: not declared
- commission.commission(input).quantity: number; default: not declared
- commission.label: string; default: not declared
- maxLeverage?: number; default: not declared — Max gross leverage `Σ|positionNotional| / equity` allowed at fill (default `Infinity`).
- maxVolumeParticipation?: number; default: not declared — Cap a single bar's fill to this fraction of bar volume (partial fills); default `Infinity`.
- noShort?: boolean; default: not declared — Disallow short positions (default `false`).
- periodsPerYear?: number; default: not declared — Bars per year, for borrow accrual (default 252).
- riskFreeRate?: number; default: not declared — Continuously-compounded risk-free rate (decimal, default `0`) used ONLY for the short-put
early-assignment carry economics — early put exercise is driven by the interest earned on the

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/backtest#CrossSectionalBacktestGridRequest

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

```typescript
export interface CrossSectionalBacktestGridRequest {
    /** The base request every variation is applied to; validated once, never mutated. */
    request: CrossSectionalBacktestRequest;
    /** The axes; the cartesian product is run with the last axis varying fastest. */
    variations: readonly GridVariation[];
    /** Variations the sweep may run (default 256, at most 4,096). */
    maximumVariations?: number;
    /** The metric that picks the best trial (default `'sharpe'`); ties resolve to the lower index. */
    selectionMetric?: GridSelectionMetric;
    hygiene?: {
        /** CSCV blocks for `probabilityOfBacktestOverfitting` (even, 4–16). Default: 16, or the largest even count the run's periods allow. */
        splits?: number;
        /** `researchProtocol`'s confidence in (0, 1); default 0.95. */
        confidence?: number;
    };
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- hygiene.confidence?: number; default: not declared — `researchProtocol`'s confidence in (0, 1); default 0.95.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/backtest#CrossSectionalBacktestResult

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

```typescript
export interface CrossSectionalBacktestResult {
    rebalances: RebalanceRow[];
    holdings: HoldingRow[];
    points: EquityPoint[];
    returns: number[];
    trades: Trade[];
    fills: NormalizedFill[];
    ledger: PortfolioLedgerSnapshot;
    timeline: PortfolioTimelineResult;
    attribution: CrossSectionalAttribution;
    benchmark: BenchmarkComparison | null;
    performance: PerformanceSummary;
    /** Bootstrap confidence intervals of the performance block when a seed was given. */
    performanceConfidence: {
        iterations: number;
        seed: number;
        meanTotalReturn: number;
        standardDeviation: number;
        confidenceInterval95: [
            number,
            number
        ];
    } | null;
    finalValue: number;
    runId: string;
    assumptions: CrossSectionalAssumptions;
    diagnostics: CrossSectionalDiagnostics;
}
```

```typescript
export interface CrossSectionalDiagnostics extends Diagnostics {
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- autoReason?: string; default: not declared — When a meta-engine (e.g. `engines.auto()`) selected a delegate, this is a one-sentence,
human-readable explanation of WHY that delegate was chosen (`engine` then names the delegate).
Absent when no auto-selection took place.
- cappedGoalCount: number; default: not declared
- converged?: boolean; default: not declared — Whether an iterative procedure converged. `false` means the value is not trustworthy.
- decomposition?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Named intermediate quantities the value decomposes into — a par spread's protection leg and
risky annuity, a forward variance's near/far legs. The H-series explain paths disclose their
arithmetic here so a caller can audit the ratio, not just receive it (3B.3).
- delistingCount: number; default: not declared
- engine?: string; default: not declared — Pricing/solver engine name, e.g. `black-scholes-merton`.
- exitCount: number; default: not declared
- fillCount: number; default: not declared
- finiteDifferenceBumps?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Finite-difference engines: the ACTUAL bump sizes used for FD Greeks (spec P2.3) — adaptive
near the vol/time boundaries, so the caller can see exactly what was differenced.
Keys: `spotStep`, `volatilityStep`, `timeStepYears`, `rateStep`, and — extended Greeks only —
`dividendYieldStep`. Each is the actual step differenced, in the unit of the coordinate it
bumps. (This doc named the retired `hS`/`hSig`/`hT`/`hR`/`hQ` keys for one release after the
emit sites had moved to the semantic names, so a caller following it read `undefined`.)
- iterations?: number; default: not declared — Iteration count for iterative methods.
- method?: string; default: not declared — Numerical method, e.g. `closed-form`, `brent`, `finite-difference`.
- rebalanceCount: number; default: not declared
- reconciliationResidual: number; default: not declared — The ledger's final base-currency NAV minus the reported `finalValue` — always 0 within 1e-9.
- rejectedFillCount: number; default: not declared
- selection?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing').SelectionReport; default: not declared — The structured engine-selection report (Gate C, `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing`): who was selected,
why, and — for automatic selection — every candidate considered with its verdict. This is the
machine-readable superset of `engine` + `autoReason` (which remain for compatibility);
`selected.name` always agrees with `engine` when both are present.
- selection.candidates?: readonly import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing').SelectionCandidate[]; default: not declared — Candidates an automatic selection considered; absent for explicit mode.
- selection.mode: 'explicit' | 'automatic'; default: not declared
- selection.reason: string; default: not declared — Why the selected engine answers this request.
- selection.selected: { name: string; version?: string; }; default: not declared
- selection.selected.name: string; default: not declared
- selection.selected.version?: string; default: not declared
- sessionCount: number; default: not declared
- timingMs?: number; default: not declared — Wall-clock timing in milliseconds, when measured.
- violatedGoalCount: number; default: not declared
- warmup?: number; default: not declared — Series facades: number of leading output slots that are warmup sentinels (null/NaN) while the
computation seeds. Equals the input length when the indicator never emitted.
- warnings: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').QuantWarning[]; default: not declared — Structured warnings; always present (possibly empty).

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/backtest#CrossSectionalWalkForwardRequest

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

The grid's members inline (`request`, `variations`, `maximumVariations`, `selectionMetric`,
`hygiene`) plus the walk-forward plan — one object, the same shape a grid call takes, so the
cross-sectional request sits where every declaration walker and fixture already reads it.

```typescript
/**
 * The grid's members inline (`request`, `variations`, `maximumVariations`, `selectionMetric`,
 * `hygiene`) plus the walk-forward plan — one object, the same shape a grid call takes, so the
 * cross-sectional request sits where every declaration walker and fixture already reads it.
 */
export interface CrossSectionalWalkForwardRequest extends CrossSectionalBacktestGridRequest {
    /** Sessions in each training span (≥ 2). */
    trainSessions: number;
    /** Sessions in each held-out span (≥ 2). */
    testSessions: number;
    /** Sessions the window advances by; default `testSessions` (adjacent, non-overlapping held-out spans). */
    step?: number;
    /** `'rolling'` (default): training spans slide; `'anchored'`: every training span starts at the first session. */
    mode?: 'rolling' | 'anchored';
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- hygiene?: { confidence?: number; splits?: number; }; default: not declared
- hygiene.confidence?: number; default: not declared — `researchProtocol`'s confidence in (0, 1); default 0.95.
- hygiene.splits?: number; default: not declared — CSCV blocks for `probabilityOfBacktestOverfitting` (even, 4–16). Default: 16, or the largest even count the run's periods allow.
- maximumVariations?: number; default: not declared — Variations the sweep may run (default 256, at most 4,096).
- mode?: 'rolling' | 'anchored'; default: not declared — `'rolling'` (default): training spans slide; `'anchored'`: every training span starts at the first session.
- request: CrossSectionalBacktestRequest; default: not declared — The base request every variation is applied to; validated once, never mutated.
- request.baseCurrency?: string; default: not declared — Default `'USD'`.
- request.dataset: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/backtest').CrossSectionalDataset; default: not declared
- request.dataset.averageDailyVolumes?: Readonly<Record<string, number>>; default: not declared — Average daily volume in return-index units, for the participation constraint.
- request.dataset.benchmarkReturns?: readonly import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/research').ReturnObservation[]; default: not declared — A benchmark's per-session simple returns (one `instrumentId`, e.g. an index proxy).
- request.dataset.betas?: Readonly<Record<string, number>>; default: not declared — Per-instrument betas for beta-neutral targets.
- request.dataset.classification?: Readonly<Record<string, import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/portfolio').InstrumentClassification>>; default: not declared — Grouping for the ledger's exposure reports (asset class, strategy, tags).
- request.dataset.fieldDefinitions: readonly import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/research').FieldDefinition[]; default: not declared — Declared fields; nothing is inferred from the data.
- request.dataset.groups?: Readonly<Record<string, string>>; default: not declared — Grouping for sector-neutral targets and the recipe's sector neutralization.
- request.dataset.observations: readonly import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/research').UniverseObservation[]; default: not declared — Features with `availableTimestampMs` — what a decision may see is decided by availability.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/backtest#EnvironmentEpisode

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/backtest#EnvironmentEpisodeResult

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

```typescript
export interface EnvironmentEpisodeResult {
    runId: string;

    definitionHash: string;

    };
}
```

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/backtest#EnvironmentObservation

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Only what was published at or before `asOf` — the no-leak law (Decision 4).

```typescript
/** Only what was published at or before `asOf` — the no-leak law (Decision 4). */
export interface EnvironmentObservation {
    asOf: EpochMs;
    /** The instant's ordinal among the decision instants. */
    index: number;
    /** Steps since `reset`. */
    sequence: number;
    market: Readonly<Record<string, LatestObservations>>;
    instruments: Readonly<Record<string, InstrumentSpecification>>;
    portfolio: EnvironmentPortfolioView;
    limits: EnvironmentLimitsView;
    features: EnvironmentFeatures;
    freshness: Readonly<Record<string, InstrumentFreshness>>;
    actionMask: ActionMask;
    previous: EnvironmentStepOutcome | null;
    provenance: EnvironmentProvenance;
}
```

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/backtest#EquityPoint

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

One point on the equity curve: a timestamp paired unambiguously with the portfolio value at that
instant (WS2.8). `points[0]` stamps the opening capital at the FIRST bar's timestamp; each later
point is the post-bar equity at that bar's timestamp — one series, no `equityCurve`/`timestamps`
off-by-one to reconcile.

```typescript
/**
 * One point on the equity curve: a timestamp paired unambiguously with the portfolio value at that
 * instant (WS2.8). `points[0]` stamps the opening capital at the FIRST bar's timestamp; each later
 * point is the post-bar equity at that bar's timestamp — one series, no `equityCurve`/`timestamps`
 * off-by-one to reconcile.
 */

    equity: number;
```

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/backtest#ImplementationRisk

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

The implementation-risk diagnostics attached to every {@link BacktestResult} (spec §16.3): core
{@link Diagnostics} (look-ahead / leakage checks and data-alignment warnings — empty when clean)
plus the benchmark fixture version the engine was validated against. The echoed run policies live
on the result's `assumptions` slot (dx §2.5) — diagnostics say how trustworthy the run is,
assumptions say what was assumed.

```typescript
/**
 * The implementation-risk diagnostics attached to every {@link BacktestResult} (spec §16.3): core
 * {@link Diagnostics} (look-ahead / leakage checks and data-alignment warnings — empty when clean)
 * plus the benchmark fixture version the engine was validated against. The echoed run policies live
 * on the result's `assumptions` slot (dx §2.5) — diagnostics say how trustworthy the run is,
 * assumptions say what was assumed.
 */
export interface ImplementationRisk extends Diagnostics {
    /** The benchmark fixture version this engine was validated against. */
    benchmarkFixtureVersion: string;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- autoReason?: string; default: not declared — When a meta-engine (e.g. `engines.auto()`) selected a delegate, this is a one-sentence,
human-readable explanation of WHY that delegate was chosen (`engine` then names the delegate).
Absent when no auto-selection took place.
- benchmarkFixtureVersion: string; default: not declared — The benchmark fixture version this engine was validated against.
- converged?: boolean; default: not declared — Whether an iterative procedure converged. `false` means the value is not trustworthy.
- decomposition?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Named intermediate quantities the value decomposes into — a par spread's protection leg and
risky annuity, a forward variance's near/far legs. The H-series explain paths disclose their
arithmetic here so a caller can audit the ratio, not just receive it (3B.3).
- engine?: string; default: not declared — Pricing/solver engine name, e.g. `black-scholes-merton`.
- finiteDifferenceBumps?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Finite-difference engines: the ACTUAL bump sizes used for FD Greeks (spec P2.3) — adaptive
near the vol/time boundaries, so the caller can see exactly what was differenced.
Keys: `spotStep`, `volatilityStep`, `timeStepYears`, `rateStep`, and — extended Greeks only —
`dividendYieldStep`. Each is the actual step differenced, in the unit of the coordinate it
bumps. (This doc named the retired `hS`/`hSig`/`hT`/`hR`/`hQ` keys for one release after the
emit sites had moved to the semantic names, so a caller following it read `undefined`.)
- iterations?: number; default: not declared — Iteration count for iterative methods.
- method?: string; default: not declared — Numerical method, e.g. `closed-form`, `brent`, `finite-difference`.
- selection?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing').SelectionReport; default: not declared — The structured engine-selection report (Gate C, `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing`): who was selected,
why, and — for automatic selection — every candidate considered with its verdict. This is the

```typescript
/** A request to trade, passed to {@link SimulatedBroker.submit}. Provide `quantity` *or* `notional`. */
```

```typescript
export type OrderType = 'market' | 'limit' | 'stop' | 'stop-limit' | 'market-on-open' | 'market-on-close';
```

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/backtest#OutOfSampleHygiene

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

```typescript
export interface OutOfSampleHygiene {
    windowCount: number;
    /** Windows where a variation could be chosen and evaluated. */
    evaluatedWindowCount: number;
    /** Mean selection metric on the training spans, over evaluated windows. */
    meanTrainMetric: number | null;
    /** Mean selection metric on the held-out spans, over evaluated windows. */
    meanTestMetric: number | null;
    /** `meanTrainMetric − meanTestMetric` — how much the in-sample choice flattered the strategy. */
    degradation: number | null;
    /** Fraction of evaluated windows whose held-out metric was below zero. */
    negativeTestFraction: number | null;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- degradation: number | null; default: not declared — `meanTrainMetric − meanTestMetric` — how much the in-sample choice flattered the strategy.
- evaluatedWindowCount: number; default: not declared — Windows where a variation could be chosen and evaluated.
- meanTestMetric: number | null; default: not declared — Mean selection metric on the held-out spans, over evaluated windows.
- meanTrainMetric: number | null; default: not declared — Mean selection metric on the training spans, over evaluated windows.
- negativeTestFraction: number | null; default: not declared — Fraction of evaluated windows whose held-out metric was below zero.
- windowCount: number; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/backtest#OutOfSampleWindowRow

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

One out-of-sample window: the choice made on the training span and how it fared on the test span.

```typescript
/** One out-of-sample window: the choice made on the training span and how it fared on the test span. */
export interface OutOfSampleWindowRow {
    index: number;
    train: SessionSpan[];
    test: SessionSpan;
    /** The grid's best trial on the training span(s), or `null` when no variation carried the metric there. */
    chosen: {
        variationIndex: number;
        parameters: Record<string, unknown>;
        trainMetric: number;
    } | null;
    /** The held-out run of the chosen variation; `null` when nothing could be chosen. */
    testMetric: number | null;
    testMetrics: GridSummaryMetrics | null;
    /** The chosen variation's held-out run id — replayable through `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/backtest/artifacts`. */
    testRunId: string | null;
    /** The training sweep ids, one per contiguous training segment. */
    trainSweepIds: string[];
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- chosen: { variationIndex: number; parameters: Record<string, unknown>; trainMetric: number; } | null; default: not declared — The grid's best trial on the training span(s), or `null` when no variation carried the metric there.
- chosen.parameters: Record<string, unknown>; default: not declared
- chosen.trainMetric: number; default: not declared
- chosen.variationIndex: number; default: not declared
- index: number; default: not declared
- test: SessionSpan; default: not declared
- test.fromSessionDate: string; default: not declared
- test.fromSessionIndex: number; default: not declared — Index of the first session in the span (0 = the dataset's first session inside the base window).
- test.sessionCount: number; default: not declared
- test.toSessionDate: string; default: not declared
- test.toSessionIndex: number; default: not declared
- testMetric: number | null; default: not declared — The held-out run of the chosen variation; `null` when nothing could be chosen.
- testMetrics: GridSummaryMetrics | null; default: not declared
- testMetrics.annualizedReturn: number | null; default: not declared
- testMetrics.annualizedVolatility: number | null; default: not declared
- testMetrics.calmar: number | null; default: not declared
- testMetrics.cappedGoalCount: number; default: not declared
- testMetrics.fillCount: number; default: not declared
- testMetrics.finalValue: number; default: not declared
- testMetrics.hitRate: number | null; default: not declared
- testMetrics.maxDrawdown: number; default: not declared
- testMetrics.meanTurnover: number | null; default: not declared — Mean allocator turnover per rebalance (fraction of NAV).
- testMetrics.periods: number; default: not declared
- testMetrics.rebalanceCount: number; default: not declared
- testMetrics.sharpe: number | null; default: not declared
- testMetrics.sortino: number | null; default: not declared
- testMetrics.totalCosts: number; default: not declared — Costs charged over the run, in base currency.
- testMetrics.totalReturn: number | null; default: not declared
- testMetrics.tradeCount: number; default: not declared
- testMetrics.violatedGoalCount: number; default: not declared
- testMetrics.warningCount: number; default: not declared
- testRunId: string | null; default: not declared — The chosen variation's held-out run id — replayable through `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/backtest/artifacts`.
- train: SessionSpan[]; default: not declared
- trainSweepIds: string[]; default: not declared — The training sweep ids, one per contiguous training segment.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/backtest#PortfolioStepper

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

`portfolioBacktest`'s loop driven from outside (Stage 7B.1, Decision 2).

```typescript
/** `portfolioBacktest`'s loop driven from outside (Stage 7B.1, Decision 2). */
export interface PortfolioStepper {
    readonly runId: string;
    /** The decision instants, ascending — the same instants `portfolioBacktest` would step. */
    readonly instants: readonly EpochMs[];
    /** Lifecycle facts and external flows due at the instant, then the session context. */
    open(index: number): SessionContext;
    /** The orders through the execution policy, the margin check, the valuation mark, the equity. */
    close(index: number, orders: readonly OrderIntent[]): PortfolioStepFrame;
    /** The session context at the last closed instant — the state after its orders, margin, and mark. */
    context(): SessionContext;
    /** The ledger state, the market snapshot, the conversions, and the valued snapshot at the last closed instant. */
    valuation(): PortfolioValuationInputs;
    /** The same result `portfolioBacktest` returns, over the instants closed so far. */
    finish(): PortfolioBacktestResult;
}
```

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/backtest#ReturnStatistics

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

```typescript
export interface ReturnStatistics {
    /**
     * Fraction of non-zero return bars that were positive. `null` when the series has NO non-zero
     * bar — there is no win/loss population to take a fraction of, so the metric is undefined and is
     * disclosed via a `performance.undefined_metric` warning rather than reported as a `0` hit rate
     * (which reads as "every bar lost"). Matches `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/performance`'s `analyze().hitRate`.
     */
    hitRate: number | null;
    /**
     * Σ gains ÷ |Σ losses|. `null` when there are gains but NO losses — the ratio has no finite
     * value, so it is disclosed via a `performance.undefined_metric` warning, never `Infinity`
     * (Law 7). `0` when there are no gains either.
     */
    profitFactor: number | null;
    /**
     * Mean per-bar return. `null` on an EMPTY series (no bars to average), disclosed the same way —
     * matches `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/performance`'s `analyze().expectancy`, which never reports a fabricated `0`.
     */
    expectancy: number | null;
    averageWin: number;
    averageLoss: number;
    bestPeriod: number;
    worstPeriod: number;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- averageLoss: number; default: not declared
- averageWin: number; default: not declared
- bestPeriod: number; default: not declared
- expectancy: number | null; default: not declared — Mean per-bar return. `null` on an EMPTY series (no bars to average), disclosed the same way —
matches `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/performance`'s `analyze().expectancy`, which never reports a fabricated `0`.
- hitRate: number | null; default: not declared — Fraction of non-zero return bars that were positive. `null` when the series has NO non-zero
bar — there is no win/loss population to take a fraction of, so the metric is undefined and is
disclosed via a `performance.undefined_metric` warning rather than reported as a `0` hit rate
(which reads as "every bar lost"). Matches `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/performance`'s `analyze().hitRate`.
- profitFactor: number | null; default: not declared — Σ gains ÷ |Σ losses|. `null` when there are gains but NO losses — the ratio has no finite
value, so it is disclosed via a `performance.undefined_metric` warning, never `Infinity`
(Law 7). `0` when there are no gains either.
- worstPeriod: number; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/backtest#SeriesSignal

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

A warmup-aware signal: `{ value, warmup }` hand-built, or any `technicalAnalysis.*.explain(...)` envelope
(`{ value, diagnostics: { warmup } }`) — `vectorized` accepts both. `warmup` is the number of
leading bars that may be non-finite by design (an indicator's warmup); {@link vectorized } treats
a non-finite value at index `i < warmup` as a flat (position 0) bar instead of an error.

Defined structurally in this package so `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/backtest` need not depend on `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis`.

```typescript
/**
 * A warmup-aware signal: `{ value, warmup }` hand-built, or any `technicalAnalysis.*.explain(...)` envelope
 * (`{ value, diagnostics: { warmup } }`) — `vectorized` accepts both. `warmup` is the number of
 * leading bars that may be non-finite by design (an indicator's warmup); {@link vectorized} treats
 * a non-finite value at index `i < warmup` as a flat (position 0) bar instead of an error.
 *
 * Defined structurally in this package so `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/backtest` need not depend on `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis`.
 */
export interface SeriesSignal {
    /** Per-bar signal values, aligned to the price bars. */
    value: ArrayLike<number>;
    /** Count of leading bars that may be non-finite by design (the indicator's warmup). */
    warmup: number;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- value: ArrayLike<number>; default: not declared — Per-bar signal values, aligned to the price bars.
- warmup: number; default: not declared — Count of leading bars that may be non-finite by design (the indicator's warmup).

- (config).assignment?: 'none' | 'model'; default: not declared — American early exercise/assignment policy (WS7.4). `'none'` (default) settles options only at
expiry — every European-style golden is byte-identical. `'model'` options in to modeling early
assignment of American short options at ex-dividend dates (short calls) and deep-ITM thresholds
(short puts), plus manual `exerciseOption`/`context.exercise` for American longs.
- (config).assignmentThreshold?: number; default: not declared — Short-put early-assignment buffer as a FRACTION of strike (default `0.02`): a short put is
assigned early when the interest CARRY benefit of exercising now exceeds the remaining extrinsic
(time value) by more than `threshold·strike`. Only used when `assignment: 'model'`.
- (config).borrow?: BorrowModel; default: not declared

- (config).commission?: CostModel; default: not declared

- (config).maxVolumeParticipation?: number; default: not declared — Cap a single bar's fill to this fraction of bar volume (partial fills); default `Infinity`.
- (config).noShort?: boolean; default: not declared — Disallow short positions (default `false`).
- (config).periodsPerYear?: number; default: not declared — Bars per year, for borrow accrual (default 252).
- (config).riskFreeRate?: number; default: not declared — Continuously-compounded risk-free rate (decimal, default `0`) used ONLY for the short-put
early-assignment carry economics — early put exercise is driven by the interest earned on the
strike over the option's remaining life. With rate `0` there is no carry incentive, so a short
put is never assigned early on arbitrage-free prices. Only used when `assignment: 'model'`.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/backtest#StrategyContext

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

The strategy's view of the world on the current bar.

```typescript
/** The strategy's view of the world on the current bar. */
export interface StrategyContext {
    /** The bar currently being handled. */
    readonly bar: Bar;
    /**
     * Register a handler that runs on every bar of `symbol`. Throws if `symbol` already has a handler —
     * one handler per symbol, so behaviour never silently depends on registration order (WS2.8).
     */
    onBar(symbol: SymbolId, handler: () => void): void;
    /**
     * Register a portfolio-level handler that fires ONCE per timestamp, after every symbol's bar handler
     * for that timestamp has run — the right hook for cross-sectional logic (ranking, rebalancing) that
     * must not depend on the input bar order (WS2.8).
     */
    onBars(handler: () => void): void;
    /** Bind a streaming indicator to a symbol; returns a handle refreshed before each handler call. */
    indicator<In, Out>(symbol: SymbolId, stream: Indicator<In, Out>, field: BarField | ((bar: Bar) => In)): IndicatorHandle<Out>;
    /** Buy (target long via `percent`, or add via `quantity`/`value`). Returns the order id. */
    buy(symbol: SymbolId, options?: TradeOptions): string;
    /** Sell / short. Returns the order id. */
    sell(symbol: SymbolId, options?: TradeOptions): string;
    /** Flatten the position in `symbol` with a market order. */
    close(symbol: SymbolId): void;
    /** Cancel a working order. */
    cancel(id: string): void;
    /** Current position in `symbol`. */
    position(symbol: SymbolId): Position;
    /** Register an option symbol (underlying/type/strike/expiry) so it's marked and settled at expiry. */
    registerOption(symbol: SymbolId, specification: OptionContractSpecification): void;
    /**
     * Manually exercise `quantity` contracts of a LONG American option early (WS7.4). Requires the
     * broker's `assignment: 'model'` policy; settles at the current underlier mark.
     */
    exercise(symbol: SymbolId, quantity: number): void;
    /** Current cash. */
    readonly cash: number;
    /** Current portfolio equity (cash + marked positions). */
    readonly equity: number;
}
```

- indicator(symbol): string; default: not declared
- onBar: (symbol: SymbolId, handler: () => void) => void; default: not declared — Register a handler that runs on every bar of `symbol`. Throws if `symbol` already has a handler —
one handler per symbol, so behaviour never silently depends on registration order (WS2.8).
- onBar(handler): () => void; default: not declared
- onBar(symbol): string; default: not declared
- onBars: (handler: () => void) => void; default: not declared — Register a portfolio-level handler that fires ONCE per timestamp, after every symbol's bar handler
for that timestamp has run — the right hook for cross-sectional logic (ranking, rebalancing) that
must not depend on the input bar order (WS2.8).
- onBars(handler): () => void; default: not declared
- position: (symbol: SymbolId) => Position; default: not declared — Current position in `symbol`.
- position().return.averagePrice: number; default: not declared — Average entry price of the current position.
- position().return.quantity: number; default: not declared — Signed quantity (negative = short).
- position().return.symbol: string; default: not declared
- position(symbol): string; default: not declared
- registerOption: (symbol: SymbolId, specification: OptionContractSpecification) => void; default: not declared — Register an option symbol (underlying/type/strike/expiry) so it's marked and settled at expiry.
- registerOption(specification): OptionContractSpecification; default: not declared
- registerOption(specification).expiresAt: number; default: not declared — Expiry instant, epoch ms (B6: the same name every resolved contract carries).
- registerOption(specification).multiplier?: number; default: not declared — Contract multiplier (underlier shares per contract). Default 100.
- registerOption(specification).settlement?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/backtest').OptionSettlementStyle; default: not declared — `physical` (deliver/receive the underlier at strike, default) or `cash` (pay/receive intrinsic).
- registerOption(specification).strike: number; default: not declared
- registerOption(specification).style?: 'european' | 'american'; default: not declared — Exercise style (default `american`). Only `american` options are eligible for the EARLY
exercise/assignment model (WS7.4); `european` options settle only at expiry. The early model is
itself opt-in via the broker's `assignment: 'model'` policy, so this field is inert by default.
- registerOption(specification).type: 'call' | 'put'; default: not declared
- registerOption(specification).underlying: string; default: not declared — The underlying symbol the option exercises into.
- registerOption(symbol): string; default: not declared
- sell: (symbol: SymbolId, options?: TradeOptions) => string; default: not declared — Sell / short. Returns the order id.
- sell(options)?: TradeOptions | undefined; default: not declared
- sell(options).limitPrice?: number; default: not declared
- sell(options).percent?: number; default: not declared — Target allocation as a fraction of equity (a *target*, e.g. `1` = 100% long for `buy`).
- sell(options).quantity?: number; default: not declared — Incremental share quantity.
- sell(options).stopLoss?: number; default: not declared
- sell(options).stopPrice?: number; default: not declared
- sell(options).takeProfit?: number; default: not declared
- sell(options).timeInForce?: TimeInForce; default: not declared
- sell(options).type?: OrderType; default: not declared
- sell(options).value?: number; default: not declared — Incremental notional value (shares = value / price).
- sell(symbol): string; default: not declared
