### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/commodities#commodityCarry

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

The annualized TOTAL carry a spot/forward pair implies, by inverting the compounding growth
factor. When all three components (financing, storage, convenience) are supplied, the result
also reports `impliedResidual = annualizedCarryRate − (f + s − c)` and warns when the residual
exceeds 1e-9 — a parity-priced forward has residual zero, and a nonzero residual is the parity
law made visible, never silently absorbed into a component.

```typescript
export declare function commodityCarry(input: CommodityCarryInput): CommodityCarryResult;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (input): CommodityCarryInput; default: not declared
- (input).annualConvenienceYield?: number; default: not declared — Optional supplied component: annual convenience yield, decimal.
- (input).annualFinancingRate?: number; default: not declared — Optional supplied component: annual financing rate, decimal.
- (input).annualStorageCostRate?: number; default: not declared — Optional supplied component: annual proportional storage cost rate, decimal.
- (input).compounding: InterestCompounding; default: not declared — REQUIRED compounding convention used to annualize the implied carry.
- (input).forwardPrice: number; default: not declared — The observed forward (or futures) price for the delivery date, > 0.
- (input).spotPrice: number; default: not declared — Spot price, > 0.
- (input).timeToDeliveryYears: number; default: not declared — Time to delivery in years, > 0 — carry over zero time is undefined, not zero.
- return.annualizedCarryRate: number; default: not declared — The annualized total carry implied by the spot/forward pair: the rate `r` with
`spotPrice × G(r, timeToDeliveryYears) = forwardPrice` (for `'continuous'`,
`ln(forwardPrice / spotPrice) / timeToDeliveryYears`).
- return.assumptions: { carryDefinition: string; compounding: InterestCompounding; }; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.carryDefinition: string; default: not declared — The fixed carry definition prose: the rate whose growth factor maps spot to forward.
- return.assumptions.compounding: InterestCompounding; default: not declared
- return.components?: { annualConvenienceYield?: number; annualFinancingRate?: number; annualStorageCostRate?: number; }; default: not declared — The supplied components, echoed — present when at least one was supplied.
- return.components.annualConvenienceYield?: number; default: not declared
- return.components.annualFinancingRate?: number; default: not declared
- return.components.annualStorageCostRate?: number; default: not declared
- return.diagnostics: { warnings: string[]; }; default: not declared
- return.diagnostics.warnings: string[]; default: not declared
- return.impliedResidual?: number; default: not declared — `annualizedCarryRate − (financing + storage − convenience)` — the cost-of-carry parity law
made visible. Present exactly when all three components were supplied.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/commodities#commodityForwardPrice

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

THEORETICAL cost-of-carry forward price: `spotPrice × G(netCarryRate, timeToDeliveryYears)`
where `netCarryRate = annualFinancingRate + annualStorageCostRate − annualConvenienceYield` and
`G` is the compounding growth factor. For `'continuous'` compounding that is exactly
`spotPrice × e^((f + s − c) × t)`.

A bare-number primitive (like valuation's `freeCashFlowToFirm`): what carry says the forward
SHOULD be, not a quoted futures price and not a contract value.

```typescript
export declare function commodityForwardPrice(input: CommodityForwardPriceInput): number;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (input): CommodityForwardPriceInput; default: not declared
- (input).annualConvenienceYield: number; default: not declared — Annual convenience yield, decimal — the benefit of holding the physical commodity.
- (input).annualFinancingRate: number; default: not declared — Annual financing (interest) rate, decimal.
- (input).annualStorageCostRate: number; default: not declared — Annual storage cost as a PROPORTIONAL rate of the commodity's value, decimal — not a dollar
amount per unit (v1 models storage as a continuous proportional drag, like a negative yield).
- (input).compounding: InterestCompounding; default: not declared — REQUIRED compounding convention — a market instrument never defaults its convention.
- (input).spotPrice: number; default: not declared — Spot price of the commodity, > 0, in the quote currency per unit.
- (input).timeToDeliveryYears: number; default: not declared — Time to delivery in years, ≥ 0 (zero prices the forward at spot exactly).

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/commodities#commodityForwardValue

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

CURRENT VALUE of an existing forward contract:
`±(currentForwardPrice − contractForwardPrice) × quantity × discountFactorToDelivery`, positive
for `'long'` and negated for `'short'`.

The three quantities this module keeps distinct meet here: `contractForwardPrice` is the price
STRUCK on the contract, `currentForwardPrice` is today's forward PRICE (quoted or theoretical),
and the result is the contract's VALUE — zero at inception when struck at the fair forward.

```typescript
export declare function commodityForwardValue(input: CommodityForwardValueInput): CommodityForwardValueResult;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (input): CommodityForwardValueInput; default: not declared
- (input).contractForwardPrice: number; default: not declared — The forward price STRUCK on the existing contract (the delivery price agreed at inception).
- (input).currentForwardPrice: number; default: not declared — The CURRENT forward price for the same delivery date — a market quote or a theoretical price
from {@link commodityForwardPrice}; either way, a forward PRICE, not a contract value.
- (input).discountFactorToDelivery: number; default: not declared — EXPLICIT discount factor from the delivery date back to the valuation instant, > 0 — the
matched-conventions law: the factor carries its own curve, day count, and compounding, so this
function never re-derives one from a rate it would have to guess conventions for.
- (input).perspective: 'long' | 'short'; default: not declared — Which side of the contract is being valued.
- (input).quantity: number; default: not declared — Number of units underlying the contract, > 0.
- return.assumptions: { discountFactorToDelivery: number; perspective: 'long' | 'short'; valuationConvention: string; }; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.discountFactorToDelivery: number; default: not declared — The factor as supplied — its conventions belong to the caller's curve.
- return.assumptions.perspective: 'long' | 'short'; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.valuationConvention: string; default: not declared — The fixed valuation prose: ±(current − contract) × quantity × factor, long positive.
- return.contractValue: number; default: not declared — The CURRENT VALUE of the existing contract to the stated side (quote currency).
- return.diagnostics: { warnings: string[]; }; default: not declared
- return.diagnostics.warnings: string[]; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/commodities#convertCommodityQuantity

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Convert a commodity quantity between units with an EXPLICIT caller-supplied factor:
`convertedQuantity = quantity × conversionFactor`. Economics are preserved exactly when the
caller scales prices by the reciprocal (price-per-unit × quantity is invariant). An identity
conversion (`fromUnit === toUnit`) with a factor ≠ 1 is a contradiction and is refused.

```typescript
export declare function convertCommodityQuantity(input: ConvertCommodityQuantityInput): ConvertCommodityQuantityResult;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (input): ConvertCommodityQuantityInput; default: not declared
- (input).conversionFactor: number; default: not declared — REQUIRED explicit factor: target units per one source unit. The generic engine does not
invent conversion factors (per spec) — 42 gallons per barrel is the CALLER's physical fact.
- (input).fromUnit: string; default: not declared — The unit the quantity is currently in — a label, echoed (e.g. 'barrel').
- (input).quantity: number; default: not declared
- (input).toUnit: string; default: not declared — The target unit — a label, echoed (e.g. 'gallon').
- return.assumptions: { conversionFactor: number; conversionSource: string; fromUnit: string; toUnit: string; }; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.conversionFactor: number; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.conversionSource: string; default: not declared — The fixed source prose: the factor is the caller's physical fact.
- return.assumptions.fromUnit: string; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.toUnit: string; default: not declared
- return.convertedQuantity: number; default: not declared — `quantity × conversionFactor`, in `toUnit`.
- return.diagnostics: { warnings: string[]; }; default: not declared
- return.diagnostics.warnings: string[]; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/commodities#futuresHedgeRatio

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Futures contracts required to hedge an exposure:
`exposureQuantity × betaOrHedgeEffectiveness / futuresContractSize`. The count is NOT rounded —
whether to round up, down, or trade the fraction via a mini contract is an execution decision
that belongs to the caller, and the assumptions say so.

```typescript
export declare function futuresHedgeRatio(input: FuturesHedgeRatioInput): FuturesHedgeRatioResult;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (input): FuturesHedgeRatioInput; default: not declared
- (input).betaOrHedgeEffectiveness?: number; default: not declared — The minimum-variance hedge ratio (a regression beta or hedge effectiveness), default 1 — a
one-to-one hedge, echoed as such in the assumptions.
- (input).exposureQuantity: number; default: not declared — The exposure being hedged, in commodity units (sign carries the direction).
- (input).futuresContractSize: number; default: not declared — Units of the commodity per futures contract, > 0.
- return.assumptions: { betaOrHedgeEffectiveness: number; hedgeRatioBasis: 'one-to-one' | 'caller-supplied beta or hedge effectiveness'; rounding: string; }; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.betaOrHedgeEffectiveness: number; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.hedgeRatioBasis: 'one-to-one' | 'caller-supplied beta or hedge effectiveness'; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.rounding: string; default: not declared — The fixed rounding prose: the count is real-valued; rounding is the caller's decision.
- return.contractsRequired: number; default: not declared — `exposureQuantity × betaOrHedgeEffectiveness / futuresContractSize` — a REAL number, not
rounded: rounding to whole contracts is the caller's execution decision, disclosed in the
assumptions rather than taken silently.
- return.diagnostics: { warnings: string[]; }; default: not declared
- return.diagnostics.warnings: string[]; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/commodities#impliedConvenienceYield

The convenience yield the spot/forward pair implies, given the other carry components — the
inverse of {@link commodityForwardPrice} solved for `annualConvenienceYield`. The remaining
inputs identify it uniquely: `c = f + s − annualizedCarry`.

```typescript
export declare function impliedConvenienceYield(input: ImpliedConvenienceYieldInput): ImpliedConvenienceYieldResult;
```

- (input).forwardPrice: number; default: not declared — The observed forward (or futures) price, > 0.
- (input).spotPrice: number; default: not declared — Spot price, > 0.
- (input).timeToDeliveryYears: number; default: not declared — Time to delivery in years, > 0.
- return.assumptions: { compounding: InterestCompounding; inversion: string; }; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.compounding: InterestCompounding; default: not declared

- return.diagnostics: { warnings: string[]; }; default: not declared
- return.diagnostics.warnings: string[]; default: not declared
- return.impliedAnnualConvenienceYield: number; default: not declared — `annualFinancingRate + annualStorageCostRate − annualizedCarry` — the yield the pair implies.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/commodities#rollReturnDecomposition

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Decompose the return on a long futures position over one holding period ending at a roll.
With `S0/S1` the initial/final spot and `F0/F1` the held contract's initial/final (before-roll)
prices:

- `totalHoldingReturn = F1/F0 − 1` — the observed total;
- `spotMoveReturn = S1/S0 − 1`;
- `carryConvergenceReturn = (F1/S1)/(F0/S0) − 1` — the basis-ratio change;
- and EXACTLY `(1 + total) = (1 + spotMove) × (1 + carryConvergence)`, because
  `(S1/S0) × ((F1/S1)/(F0/S0)) = F1/F0` — the declared multiplicative convention, tested at the
  declared residual 1e-12.

The roll leg is stated separately: rolling is cash-neutral at execution, so the roll yield
`(F1 − N)/N` is the third component of the economics but belongs to the NEXT period's return,
and this function never folds it into the holding total.

```typescript
export declare function rollReturnDecomposition(input: RollReturnDecompositionInput): RollReturnDecompositionResult;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (input): RollReturnDecompositionInput; default: not declared
- (input).finalContractPriceBeforeRoll: number; default: not declared — Price of the held contract at the end of the holding period, BEFORE rolling, > 0.
- (input).finalSpotPrice: number; default: not declared — Spot price at the end of the holding period (the roll instant), > 0.
- (input).initialContractPrice: number; default: not declared — Price of the held contract at the start of the holding period, > 0.
- (input).initialSpotPrice: number; default: not declared — Spot price at the start of the holding period, > 0.
- (input).nextContractPriceAtRoll: number; default: not declared — Price of the next contract at the roll instant, > 0.
- return.assumptions: { declaredResidualBound: 1e-12; reconciliation: string; }; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.declaredResidualBound: 1e-12; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.reconciliation: string; default: not declared — The fixed reconciliation prose: the components compound exactly to the observed total.
- return.carryConvergenceReturn: number; default: not declared — The change in the contract's basis ratio to spot over the period:
`(finalContractPriceBeforeRoll / finalSpotPrice) / (initialContractPrice / initialSpotPrice) − 1`
— the carry/convergence earned as the contract pulls toward spot (positive for a long in
backwardation).
- return.diagnostics: { reconciliationResidual: number; warnings: string[]; }; default: not declared
- return.diagnostics.reconciliationResidual: number; default: not declared — `(1 + totalHoldingReturn) − (1 + spotMoveReturn) × (1 + carryConvergenceReturn)` — floating point only.
- return.diagnostics.warnings: string[]; default: not declared
- return.rollLeg: { convention: string; rollYieldFraction: number; }; default: not declared — The roll leg, stated SEPARATELY: the roll is cash-neutral at execution, so its yield
`(finalContractPriceBeforeRoll − nextContractPriceAtRoll) / nextContractPriceAtRoll` accrues
over the NEXT holding period and is never added into `totalHoldingReturn`.
- return.rollLeg.convention: string; default: not declared — The fixed roll-leg prose: cash-neutral at execution, accrues next period.
- return.rollLeg.rollYieldFraction: number; default: not declared
- return.spotMoveReturn: number; default: not declared — `finalSpotPrice / initialSpotPrice − 1` — the spot move over the period.
- return.totalHoldingReturn: number; default: not declared — The OBSERVED total return on the held contract over the holding period:
`finalContractPriceBeforeRoll / initialContractPrice − 1`.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/commodities#rollYield

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

The roll yield when rolling a LONG position from the expiring contract into the next:
`(expiring − next) / next`. Positive in backwardation — the next contract is bought below the
expiring one and converges upward under a static curve; negative in contango.

When `spotPriceAtRoll` is supplied the result also decomposes both legs against spot; the
components compound exactly back to the roll yield (see {@link RollYieldResult.decomposition}).
When spot is absent the decomposition is absent WITH its reason — it is never inferred from the
contract prices.

```typescript
export declare function rollYield(input: RollYieldInput): RollYieldResult;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (input): RollYieldInput; default: not declared
- (input).expiringContractPrice: number; default: not declared — Price of the contract being rolled OUT of (the expiring one), > 0.
- (input).nextContractPrice: number; default: not declared — Price of the contract being rolled INTO (the next one), > 0.
- (input).spotPriceAtRoll?: number; default: not declared — The spot price at the roll instant, > 0 — supplied only when observed. Without it the
spot-relative decomposition is ABSENT with its reason, never guessed.
- return.assumptions: { decompositionConvention: string; rollDirection: string; signLaw: string; }; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.decompositionConvention: string; default: not declared — The fixed decomposition prose: the spot-relative components compound exactly.
- return.assumptions.rollDirection: string; default: not declared — The fixed direction prose: a long roller out of the expiring contract into the next.
- return.assumptions.signLaw: string; default: not declared — The fixed sign-law prose: positive in backwardation, negative in contango.
- return.decomposition?: { expiringVersusSpotFraction: number; nextVersusSpotFraction: number; }; default: not declared — Spot-relative decomposition, present exactly when `spotPriceAtRoll` was supplied. The two
components COMPOUND (they do not sum): with `e = expiringVersusSpotFraction` and
`n = nextVersusSpotFraction`, `(1 + rollYieldFraction) = (1 + e) / (1 + n)` EXACTLY — an
algebraic identity, since `(E/S) / (N/S) = E/N`.
- return.decomposition.expiringVersusSpotFraction: number; default: not declared — `(expiringContractPrice − spotPriceAtRoll) / spotPriceAtRoll` — the expiring contract's
residual basis to spot (near zero when rolled at expiry; the carry already converged).
- return.decomposition.nextVersusSpotFraction: number; default: not declared — `(nextContractPrice − spotPriceAtRoll) / spotPriceAtRoll` — the curve slope out to the next
contract; NEGATIVE in backwardation, which is exactly where positive roll yield comes from.
- return.decompositionAbsentReason?: string; default: not declared — Present exactly when the decomposition is absent — the reason, never a guessed spot.
- return.diagnostics: { warnings: string[]; }; default: not declared
- return.diagnostics.warnings: string[]; default: not declared
- return.rollYieldFraction: number; default: not declared — `(expiringContractPrice − nextContractPrice) / nextContractPrice` — the yield a long roller
locks in for the next holding period under a static curve. SIGN LAW: positive in
backwardation (next below expiring), negative in contango.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/commodities#seasonalityProfile

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Group caller-supplied dated observations by calendar month and report the requested statistic
per month plus the overall mean. Purely descriptive: it never extrapolates an empty month
(`null` with reason), and it warns when any month rests on fewer than 3 observations — a
"seasonal pattern" read off one or two points is noise wearing a costume.

```typescript
export declare function seasonalityProfile(input: SeasonalityProfileInput): SeasonalityProfileResult;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (input): SeasonalityProfileInput; default: not declared
- (input).observations: readonly SeasonalityObservation[]; default: not declared
- (input).statistic: 'mean' | 'median'; default: not declared — The per-month statistic — explicit, never defaulted.
- return.assumptions: { scope: string; statistic: 'mean' | 'median'; }; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.scope: string; default: not declared — The fixed scope prose: descriptive only — no seasonality is invented.
- return.assumptions.statistic: 'mean' | 'median'; default: not declared
- return.diagnostics: { observationCountByMonth: number[]; warnings: string[]; }; default: not declared
- return.diagnostics.observationCountByMonth: number[]; default: not declared — Observation counts by calendar month, index 0 = January.
- return.diagnostics.warnings: string[]; default: not declared
- return.months: SeasonalityMonthRow[]; default: not declared — Twelve rows, months 1..12 in order — empty months are null WITH reason, never dropped.
- return.overallMean: number; default: not declared — The mean over ALL observations (regardless of the per-month statistic).

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/commodities#termStructureState

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Classify a forward curve's term structure with the reasoning disclosed. Each adjacent pair is a
segment with fractional slope `far / near − 1`; segments beyond `+flatToleranceFraction` rise,
beyond `−flatToleranceFraction` fall, and within the tolerance are flat. ALL rising → `'contango'`;
ALL falling → `'backwardation'`; ALL flat → `'flat'`; any other mix → `'indeterminate'`, with the
mixed segments named in the diagnostics rather than averaged away. The classification is a pure
function of the curve and the tolerance — the same wiggly curve legitimately reads `'flat'` under
a loose tolerance and `'indeterminate'` under a tight one.

```typescript
export declare function termStructureState(input: TermStructureStateInput): TermStructureStateResult;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (input): TermStructureStateInput; default: not declared
- (input).curve: readonly CommodityCurvePoint[]; default: not declared — The forward curve — ≥ 2 points, strictly ascending delivery times.
- (input).flatToleranceFraction: number; default: not declared — REQUIRED explicit tolerance (e.g. `0.001`): a pairwise price change with
`|forwardPrice[i+1] / forwardPrice[i] − 1| ≤ flatToleranceFraction` counts as flat. No
default — how much wiggle is "flat" is a judgment the caller must state.
- return.assumptions: { definition: string; flatToleranceFraction: number; }; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.definition: string; default: not declared — The fixed classification prose: pairwise slopes against the tolerance, mixes disclosed.
- return.assumptions.flatToleranceFraction: number; default: not declared
- return.diagnostics: { fallingSegmentCount: number; flatSegmentCount: number; risingSegmentCount: number; warnings: string[]; }; default: not declared
- return.diagnostics.fallingSegmentCount: number; default: not declared
- return.diagnostics.flatSegmentCount: number; default: not declared
- return.diagnostics.risingSegmentCount: number; default: not declared
- return.diagnostics.warnings: string[]; default: not declared
- return.state: TermStructureState; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/core#Assumptions

Kind: type; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Assumptions echoed on every pro result. Extra model-specific fields are added via the `Extra`
type parameter so each domain can annotate its own conventions without losing the common shape.

```typescript
/**
 * Assumptions echoed on every pro result. Extra model-specific fields are added via the `Extra`
 * type parameter so each domain can annotate its own conventions without losing the common shape.
 */
export type Assumptions<Extra extends Record<string, unknown> = Record<never, never>> = {
    conventionsVersion: string;
    dayCount?: DayCount;
    compounding?: InterestCompounding;
    calendar?: string;
    calendarVersion?: string;
    asOf?: EpochMs;
    timeToExpiryYears?: number;
    /**
     * How the contract's expiry label was resolved to an instant: `'us-equity-close'` when a
     * date-only `YYYY-MM-DD` expiry resolved to the US equity/options close — 16:00 America/New_York,
     * or 13:00 on an early-close day;
     * `'explicit-instant'` when the caller supplied a zoned datetime. Named so the convention is
     * never silent (alignment spec P1.6); instrument builders own the full story in Phase 3.
     */
    expiryConvention?: 'us-equity-close' | 'explicit-instant';
    timeToExpiryConvention?: never;
    dividendModel?: DividendModel;
    units?: GreekUnits;
    model?: string;
    engine?: string;
    /**
     * The randomness seed this result was computed under — REQUIRED echo for a
     * `randomness: 'seeded'` Pricer (Gate C, 2026-08-23): a stochastic result that does not name
     * its seed cannot be replayed from the result alone. Deterministic paths never set it.
     */
    seed?: number;
} & Extra;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- asOf?: number; default: not declared
- calendar?: string; default: not declared
- calendarVersion?: string; default: not declared
- compounding?: InterestCompounding; default: not declared
- compounding.periodsPerYear: number; default: not declared
- compounding.type: 'periodic'; default: not declared
- conventionsVersion: string; default: not declared
- dayCount?: DayCount; default: not declared
- dividendModel?: DividendModel; default: not declared
- engine?: string; default: not declared
- expiryConvention?: 'us-equity-close' | 'explicit-instant'; default: not declared — How the contract's expiry label was resolved to an instant: `'us-equity-close'` when a
date-only `YYYY-MM-DD` expiry resolved to the US equity/options close — 16:00 America/New_York,
or 13:00 on an early-close day;
`'explicit-instant'` when the caller supplied a zoned datetime. Named so the convention is
never silent (alignment spec P1.6); instrument builders own the full story in Phase 3.
- model?: string; default: not declared
- seed?: number; default: not declared — The randomness seed this result was computed under — REQUIRED echo for a
`randomness: 'seeded'` Pricer (Gate C, 2026-08-23): a stochastic result that does not name
its seed cannot be replayed from the result alone. Deterministic paths never set it.
- timeToExpiryConvention?: never; default: not declared
- timeToExpiryYears?: number; default: not declared

```typescript
export interface CalendarConfig {
    name: string;
    version: string;
    timezone: string;
    /** Default `[0, 6]` (Sun & Sat). */
    weekendDays?: Weekday[];
    /**
     * Regular session hours as `HH:MM` in the calendar's `timezone`. `close: '24:00'` is the sentinel
     * for "no close" — a continuous 24-hour session (e.g. `alwaysOpen`/crypto), distinct from `'00:00'`
     * (midnight). Keep it as `'24:00'`; do not normalize to `'00:00'`.
     */
    session: {
        open: string;
        close: string;
        halfDayClose?: string;
    };
    holidayRules?: HolidayRule[];
    halfDayRules?: HolidayRule[];

    closures?: string[];
}
```

- session: { close: string; halfDayClose?: string; open: string; }; default: not declared — Regular session hours as `HH:MM` in the calendar's `timezone`. `close: '24:00'` is the sentinel

```typescript
export interface ClosedRequestTeaching {
    /** The argument's own label in container errors — defaults to `input`. */
    readonly argumentName?: string;
    /**
     * This argument IS the request — field paths stay bare (`volatility`, `issueDate`) even under a
     * domain-specific argument name like `specification`. Secondary arguments (an options bag beside
     * a subject) omit it and get prefixed paths so a two-object call says which object to fix.
     */
    readonly subject?: boolean;
    /**
     * ONE complete, runnable call for this boundary, or a thunk so the string is only built on the
     * failing path. Hand-authored at the call site: the generator knows the keys, never the values.
     */
    readonly exampleCall: string | (() => string);
    /** Per-field unit-trap notes, keyed by BARE field name (`volatility: 'annualized decimal'`). */
    readonly hints?: Readonly<Record<string, string>>;
    /**
     * The argument is an OPEN structural artifact per its manifest policy (Law 12): every consumed
     * field runs its ladder, but unknown keys are PRESERVED decoration, never rejected — a fit
     * result or market snapshot a user hands back may legitimately carry their own annotations.
     * Curated from the manifest's per-argument `inputPolicies`; closed remains the default.
     */
    readonly open?: boolean;
}
```

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/core#Computed

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

```typescript
export interface Computed<T, Extra extends Record<string, unknown> = Record<never, never>> {
    /**
     * The computed value. Never `NaN` or `±Infinity`: a value the model cannot produce is `null`
     * beside a diagnostic that says why (Law 7 — a warning never licenses a non-finite number).
     */
    value: T;
    /** Every applied convention, echoed back. */
    assumptions: Assumptions<Extra>;
    /** How the value was computed, plus any warnings. */
    diagnostics: Diagnostics;
    /** Optional data lineage when the inputs came from a provider. */
    provenance?: Provenance;
}
```

- assumptions.engine?: string; default: not declared
- assumptions.expiryConvention?: 'us-equity-close' | 'explicit-instant'; default: not declared — How the contract's expiry label was resolved to an instant: `'us-equity-close'` when a
date-only `YYYY-MM-DD` expiry resolved to the US equity/options close — 16:00 America/New_York,
or 13:00 on an early-close day;
`'explicit-instant'` when the caller supplied a zoned datetime. Named so the convention is

- assumptions.units?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').GreekUnits; default: not declared
- assumptions.units.rho: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').RhoUnit; default: not declared
- assumptions.units.theta: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').ThetaUnit; default: not declared

- diagnostics: Diagnostics; default: not declared — How the value was computed, plus any warnings.
- diagnostics.autoReason?: string; default: not declared — When a meta-engine (e.g. `engines.auto()`) selected a delegate, this is a one-sentence,
human-readable explanation of WHY that delegate was chosen (`engine` then names the delegate).
Absent when no auto-selection took place.
- diagnostics.converged?: boolean; default: not declared — Whether an iterative procedure converged. `false` means the value is not trustworthy.
- diagnostics.decomposition?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Named intermediate quantities the value decomposes into — a par spread's protection leg and
risky annuity, a forward variance's near/far legs. The H-series explain paths disclose their
arithmetic here so a caller can audit the ratio, not just receive it (3B.3).
- diagnostics.engine?: string; default: not declared — Pricing/solver engine name, e.g. `black-scholes-merton`.
- diagnostics.finiteDifferenceBumps?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Finite-difference engines: the ACTUAL bump sizes used for FD Greeks (spec P2.3) — adaptive
near the vol/time boundaries, so the caller can see exactly what was differenced.
Keys: `spotStep`, `volatilityStep`, `timeStepYears`, `rateStep`, and — extended Greeks only —
`dividendYieldStep`. Each is the actual step differenced, in the unit of the coordinate it
bumps. (This doc named the retired `hS`/`hSig`/`hT`/`hR`/`hQ` keys for one release after the
emit sites had moved to the semantic names, so a caller following it read `undefined`.)
- diagnostics.iterations?: number; default: not declared — Iteration count for iterative methods.
- diagnostics.method?: string; default: not declared — Numerical method, e.g. `closed-form`, `brent`, `finite-difference`.
- diagnostics.selection?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing').SelectionReport; default: not declared — The structured engine-selection report (Gate C, `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing`): who was selected,
why, and — for automatic selection — every candidate considered with its verdict. This is the
machine-readable superset of `engine` + `autoReason` (which remain for compatibility);
`selected.name` always agrees with `engine` when both are present.
- diagnostics.selection.candidates?: readonly import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing').SelectionCandidate[]; default: not declared — Candidates an automatic selection considered; absent for explicit mode.
- diagnostics.selection.mode: 'explicit' | 'automatic'; default: not declared
- diagnostics.selection.reason: string; default: not declared — Why the selected engine answers this request.
- diagnostics.selection.selected: { name: string; version?: string; }; default: not declared
- diagnostics.selection.selected.name: string; default: not declared
- diagnostics.selection.selected.version?: string; default: not declared
- diagnostics.timingMs?: number; default: not declared — Wall-clock timing in milliseconds, when measured.
- diagnostics.warmup?: number; default: not declared — Series facades: number of leading output slots that are warmup sentinels (null/NaN) while the
computation seeds. Equals the input length when the indicator never emitted.
- diagnostics.warnings: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').QuantWarning[]; default: not declared — Structured warnings; always present (possibly empty).
- provenance?: Provenance; default: not declared — Optional data lineage when the inputs came from a provider.
- provenance.asOf?: number; default: not declared
- provenance.dataset?: string; default: not declared

beside a diagnostic that says why (Law 7 — a warning never licenses a non-finite number).

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/core#Diagnostics

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Non-value metadata about how a result was computed.

```typescript
/** Non-value metadata about how a result was computed. */
export interface Diagnostics {
    /** Pricing/solver engine name, e.g. `black-scholes-merton`. */
    engine?: string;
    /** Numerical method, e.g. `closed-form`, `brent`, `finite-difference`. */
    method?: string;
    /** Whether an iterative procedure converged. `false` means the value is not trustworthy. */
    converged?: boolean;
    /** Iteration count for iterative methods. */
    iterations?: number;
    /**
     * When a meta-engine (e.g. `engines.auto()`) selected a delegate, this is a one-sentence,
     * human-readable explanation of WHY that delegate was chosen (`engine` then names the delegate).
     * Absent when no auto-selection took place.
     */
    autoReason?: string;
    /**
     * The structured engine-selection report (Gate C, `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing`): who was selected,
     * why, and — for automatic selection — every candidate considered with its verdict. This is the
     * machine-readable superset of `engine` + `autoReason` (which remain for compatibility);
     * `selected.name` always agrees with `engine` when both are present.
     */
    selection?: SelectionReport;
    /**
     * Named intermediate quantities the value decomposes into — a par spread's protection leg and
     * risky annuity, a forward variance's near/far legs. The H-series explain paths disclose their
     * arithmetic here so a caller can audit the ratio, not just receive it (3B.3).
     */
    decomposition?: Record<string, number>;
    /** Structured warnings; always present (possibly empty). */
    warnings: QuantWarning[];
    /** Wall-clock timing in milliseconds, when measured. */
    timingMs?: number;
    /**
     * Series facades: number of leading output slots that are warmup sentinels (null/NaN) while the
     * computation seeds. Equals the input length when the indicator never emitted.
     */
    warmup?: number;
    /**
     * Finite-difference engines: the ACTUAL bump sizes used for FD Greeks (spec P2.3) — adaptive
     * near the vol/time boundaries, so the caller can see exactly what was differenced.
     * Keys: `spotStep`, `volatilityStep`, `timeStepYears`, `rateStep`, and — extended Greeks only —
     * `dividendYieldStep`. Each is the actual step differenced, in the unit of the coordinate it
     * bumps. (This doc named the retired `hS`/`hSig`/`hT`/`hR`/`hQ` keys for one release after the
     * emit sites had moved to the semantic names, so a caller following it read `undefined`.)
     */
    finiteDifferenceBumps?: Record<string, number>;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- autoReason?: string; default: not declared — When a meta-engine (e.g. `engines.auto()`) selected a delegate, this is a one-sentence,
human-readable explanation of WHY that delegate was chosen (`engine` then names the delegate).
Absent when no auto-selection took place.
- converged?: boolean; default: not declared — Whether an iterative procedure converged. `false` means the value is not trustworthy.
- decomposition?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Named intermediate quantities the value decomposes into — a par spread's protection leg and
risky annuity, a forward variance's near/far legs. The H-series explain paths disclose their
arithmetic here so a caller can audit the ratio, not just receive it (3B.3).
- engine?: string; default: not declared — Pricing/solver engine name, e.g. `black-scholes-merton`.
- finiteDifferenceBumps?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Finite-difference engines: the ACTUAL bump sizes used for FD Greeks (spec P2.3) — adaptive
near the vol/time boundaries, so the caller can see exactly what was differenced.
Keys: `spotStep`, `volatilityStep`, `timeStepYears`, `rateStep`, and — extended Greeks only —
`dividendYieldStep`. Each is the actual step differenced, in the unit of the coordinate it
bumps. (This doc named the retired `hS`/`hSig`/`hT`/`hR`/`hQ` keys for one release after the
emit sites had moved to the semantic names, so a caller following it read `undefined`.)
- iterations?: number; default: not declared — Iteration count for iterative methods.
- method?: string; default: not declared — Numerical method, e.g. `closed-form`, `brent`, `finite-difference`.
- selection?: SelectionReport; default: not declared — The structured engine-selection report (Gate C, `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing`): who was selected,
why, and — for automatic selection — every candidate considered with its verdict. This is the
machine-readable superset of `engine` + `autoReason` (which remain for compatibility);
`selected.name` always agrees with `engine` when both are present.
- selection.candidates?: readonly import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing').SelectionCandidate[]; default: not declared — Candidates an automatic selection considered; absent for explicit mode.
- selection.mode: 'explicit' | 'automatic'; default: not declared
- selection.reason: string; default: not declared — Why the selected engine answers this request.
- selection.selected: { name: string; version?: string; }; default: not declared
- selection.selected.name: string; default: not declared
- selection.selected.version?: string; default: not declared
- timingMs?: number; default: not declared — Wall-clock timing in milliseconds, when measured.
- warmup?: number; default: not declared — Series facades: number of leading output slots that are warmup sentinels (null/NaN) while the
computation seeds. Equals the input length when the indicator never emitted.
- warnings: QuantWarning[]; default: not declared — Structured warnings; always present (possibly empty).

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/core#Facade

Kind: type; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

`ExplainValue` defaults to `Output` and diverges only for solver facades (Law 7 / E3): the plain
call THROWS on failure so its output stays `number`, while the `.explain` envelope reports the
same failure softly as `value: null` + `converged: false`.

```typescript
/**
 * A callable `(input) => Output` with an `.explain(input) => Computed<Output, Extra>` companion. The
 * `Extra` type parameter carries the domain-specific assumptions the envelope discloses (it defaults
 * to none), so `f.explain(input).assumptions.<extraField>` type-checks.
 */
/**
 * `ExplainValue` defaults to `Output` and diverges only for solver facades (Law 7 / E3): the plain
 * call THROWS on failure so its output stays `number`, while the `.explain` envelope reports the
 * same failure softly as `value: null` + `converged: false`.
 */
export type Facade<Input, Output, Extra extends Record<string, unknown> = Record<never, never>, ExplainValue = Output> = ((input: Input) => Output) & {
    explain: (input: Input) => Computed<ExplainValue, Extra>;
};
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (input): Input; default: not declared
- explain: (input: Input) => Computed<ExplainValue, Extra>; default: not declared
- explain().return.assumptions: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Assumptions<Extra>; default: not declared — Every applied convention, echoed back.
- explain().return.diagnostics: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Diagnostics; default: not declared — How the value was computed, plus any warnings.
- explain().return.provenance?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Provenance; default: not declared — Optional data lineage when the inputs came from a provider.
- explain().return.value: ExplainValue; default: not declared — The computed value. Never `NaN` or `±Infinity`: a value the model cannot produce is `null`
beside a diagnostic that says why (Law 7 — a warning never licenses a non-finite number).
- explain(input): Input; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/core#GuaranteedSelection

Kind: type; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

The names a selection of type `S` is CERTAIN to contain — the names a result may promise as
required. Every other name in `S[number]` was only possibly selected, so a result types it as
optional.

A name is guaranteed when every possible value of `S` holds it as a whole element:
- `readonly ['price', 'gamma']` guarantees `'price' | 'gamma'`;
- a union of selections guarantees only what all of them share:
  `readonly ['gamma'] | readonly ['delta']` (a conditional) guarantees nothing, and
  `readonly ['price', 'gamma'] | readonly ['price']` guarantees `'price'`;
- an element that is itself a union guarantees none of its members: `readonly ['gamma' | 'delta']`
  holds one of the two, and the type cannot say which;
- a list without a fixed length (`BlackScholesOutput[]`) guarantees nothing.

`S extends unknown` distributes over the members of `S`, giving one verdict per possible
selection; a name is kept only when no member says `false`.

```typescript
/**
 * The names a selection of type `S` is CERTAIN to contain — the names a result may promise as
 * required. Every other name in `S[number]` was only possibly selected, so a result types it as
 * optional.
 *
 * A name is guaranteed when every possible value of `S` holds it as a whole element:
 * - `readonly ['price', 'gamma']` guarantees `'price' | 'gamma'`;
 * - a union of selections guarantees only what all of them share:
 *   `readonly ['gamma'] | readonly ['delta']` (a conditional) guarantees nothing, and
 *   `readonly ['price', 'gamma'] | readonly ['price']` guarantees `'price'`;
 * - an element that is itself a union guarantees none of its members: `readonly ['gamma' | 'delta']`
 *   holds one of the two, and the type cannot say which;
 * - a list without a fixed length (`BlackScholesOutput[]`) guarantees nothing.
 *
 * `S extends unknown` distributes over the members of `S`, giving one verdict per possible
 * selection; a name is kept only when no member says `false`.
 */
export type GuaranteedSelection<S extends readonly string[]> = {
    [K in S[number]]: false extends (S extends unknown ? number extends S['length'] ? false : K extends {
        [I in keyof S]: [
            S[I]
        ] extends [
            K
        ] ? K : never;
    }[number] ? true : false : never) ? never : K;
}[S[number]];
```

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/core#MarketInputs

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

The canonical market snapshot every pricing/analytics entrypoint takes (spec §5.3 / WS3.2). One
shape, one vocabulary: `spot`, `rate`, optional `dividendYield` (default 0), and the `asOf` the
snapshot is valid for. Package-specific markets EXTEND this and add their own fields (options adds

```typescript

 * snapshot is valid for. Package-specific markets EXTEND this and add their own fields (options adds
 * `forward`/`volatility`/quotes; structure/vol pair it with a separate `config`), so the same word
 * always means the same thing across the workspace.
 */
export interface MarketInputs {
    spot: number;
    riskFreeRate: number;
    /** Continuous dividend yield; defaults to 0 when omitted. */
    dividendYield?: number;
    /**
     * Snapshot time: epoch ms, `'YYYY-MM-DD'`, or a ZONED ISO datetime — one grammar for "when"

     * datetimes are rejected with a teaching error; TotalFinance never reads the machine clock or zone).

    asOf: EpochMs | string;
}
```

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/core#OptionContract

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

```typescript
export interface OptionContract {
    // ── Identity & pricing fields — every engine reads these (P3.4 pricing/metadata split) ──────
    underlying: string;
    type: OptionType;
    /** REQUIRED at build — never defaulted: US equity options are American, many index options European. */
    style: OptionStyle;
    strike: number;
    /** The expiry LABEL as supplied: `YYYY-MM-DD` (a calendar date) or a zoned ISO datetime. */
    expiry: string;
    /**
     * The exact expiration INSTANT the label resolved to (epoch ms), stamped by the builders at
     * construction: a bare date resolves via the named `expiryConvention`; a zoned datetime is the
     * caller's explicit instant. REQUIRED (E2, one expiry law): engines price against this
     * resolution and cross-validate it against the label — an unresolved literal is not a
     * contract; build one with the option builders.
     */
    expiresAt: EpochMs;
    /** HOW `expiry` resolved to `expiresAt` — named, never silent (spec P1.6/P3.4). */
    expiryConvention: 'us-equity-close' | 'explicit-instant';
    // ── Metadata — portfolio accounting, settlement plumbing, display. Vanilla pricing does NOT
    //    read these; an engine never appears to honor a field it ignores (P3.4). ──────────────────
    multiplier?: number;
    settlement?: Settlement;
    /**
     * AM- or PM-settled — settlement/display metadata. It does NOT move `expiresAt`: the expiry
     * instant always comes from the `expiry` label and `expiryConvention`. Express an AM-settled
     * index expiry as a zoned datetime (`'2026-09-18T09:30:00-04:00'`) when its instant matters.
     */
    exerciseTime?: ExerciseTime;
    currency?: string;
    root?: string;
    occSymbol?: string;
    deliverable?: Deliverable;
    adjusted?: boolean;
}
```

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/core#PostconditionError

A LIBRARY defect surfaced loudly (Law 7 runtime postcondition): a successful facade/analysis
result was about to carry an undisclosed NaN/Infinity. This is never a user-input error — if
you see it, please report it with the inputs; the honest alternatives are `null`-with-reason
or a disclosed diagnostic, and the function failed to produce either.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/core#RateCurvePoint

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

One curve pillar: a `'YYYY-MM-DD'` date and the ZERO RATE quoted there, as a decimal, under the
owning curve's own `compounding`/`dayCount`. The field is `zeroRate` — not a generic `rate` —
because that is exactly what TotalFinance consumers evaluate (`curves.fromZeroRates` semantics):
every discount factor is DERIVED from this rate through the curve's compounding transform.

There is deliberately no `discountFactor` member (removed 2026-08-23, second external review):
two answers to "what discounts this pillar?" on one pillar can contradict each other, and the
old advisory field did — sign-consistency let `zeroRate: 0.05` sit beside `discountFactor: 0.2`.
Discount-factor-quoted data has its own constructor (`curves.fromDiscountFactors`), whose
pillars carry no rates. Entries stay open to vendor decoration (Law 12).

```typescript
/**
 * One curve pillar: a `'YYYY-MM-DD'` date and the ZERO RATE quoted there, as a decimal, under the
 * owning curve's own `compounding`/`dayCount`. The field is `zeroRate` — not a generic `rate` —
 * because that is exactly what TotalFinance consumers evaluate (`curves.fromZeroRates` semantics):
 * every discount factor is DERIVED from this rate through the curve's compounding transform.
 *
 * There is deliberately no `discountFactor` member (removed 2026-08-23, second external review):
 * two answers to "what discounts this pillar?" on one pillar can contradict each other, and the
 * old advisory field did — sign-consistency let `zeroRate: 0.05` sit beside `discountFactor: 0.2`.
 * Discount-factor-quoted data has its own constructor (`curves.fromDiscountFactors`), whose
 * pillars carry no rates. Entries stay open to vendor decoration (Law 12).
 */
export interface RateCurvePoint {
    date: string;
    zeroRate: number;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- date: string; default: not declared
- zeroRate: number; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/core#RawFundamentalsRecord

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

The RAW provider-fundamentals record — an explicitly raw/open DATA-EDGE artifact (FC0). A
vendor's untyped field bag survives ONLY here; compute functions never read `fields`. Typed
analysis attaches to `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/fundamentals`' `FundamentalPeriod` declarations, and a data
adapter's job is to map one of these raw records into them with the availability instant
carried honestly. (Relocation-by-rename of the former generic `Fundamentals`, pre-1.0, no
alias.)

```typescript
/**
 * The RAW provider-fundamentals record — an explicitly raw/open DATA-EDGE artifact (FC0). A
 * vendor's untyped field bag survives ONLY here; compute functions never read `fields`. Typed
 * analysis attaches to `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/fundamentals`' `FundamentalPeriod` declarations, and a data
 * adapter's job is to map one of these raw records into them with the availability instant
 * carried honestly. (Relocation-by-rename of the former generic `Fundamentals`, pre-1.0, no
 * alias.)
 */
export interface RawFundamentalsRecord {
    symbol: SymbolId;
    /** Vendor's own period label, verbatim (e.g. `'Q1 2026'`, `'FY25'`). */
    fiscalPeriod?: string;
    /** When the vendor says the record is as-of, when known. */
    asOf?: EpochMs;
    /** The vendor's untyped field bag — data-edge only, never a compute input. */
    fields: Record<string, number | string | null>;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- asOf?: number; default: not declared — When the vendor says the record is as-of, when known.
- fields: Record<string, string | number | null>; default: not declared — The vendor's untyped field bag — data-edge only, never a compute input.

- symbol: string; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/core#RequireFiniteFieldsOptions

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

The shared enforcement path for a request object's NUMERIC fields (spec 3B.1b).

One call answers the three questions a numeric contract actually makes, in the order a caller
makes mistakes: is the field there, is it a number, is that number usable. Each gets its own code
and its own sentence, because "volatility is required" and "volatility must be a finite number,
received NaN" are different bugs with different fixes and a single `input.not_finite` for both
teaches neither.

Why this exists rather than a hand-rolled check per boundary: measurement found 31 public
boundaries where omitting a declared-required field reached the arithmetic and returned `NaN` —
`blackScholesPrice({ spot, strike, timeToExpiryYears, riskFreeRate, dividendYield })` with no
`volatility` priced the option as `NaN` and handed it back as a success. In a pricing library a
silently wrong number is the worst possible failure: it does not look like an error at any layer
that consumes it. The declaration already said the field was required; only the runtime disagreed.

HOT PATHS: this validates ONE object, not one row. It belongs at a public facade, never inside an
iterative solver or a columnar loop whose columns were already checked — those call the unchecked
kernel behind the facade (spec 3B.1b: unchecked numeric routines stay private and reachable only
after validation). A `for` over a handful of declared names costs nothing next to `Math.log`; the
same loop run 100,000 times inside a batch path is a different thing entirely.

```typescript
/**
 * The shared enforcement path for a request object's NUMERIC fields (spec 3B.1b).
 *
 * One call answers the three questions a numeric contract actually makes, in the order a caller
 * makes mistakes: is the field there, is it a number, is that number usable. Each gets its own code
 * and its own sentence, because "volatility is required" and "volatility must be a finite number,
 * received NaN" are different bugs with different fixes and a single `input.not_finite` for both
 * teaches neither.
 *
 * Why this exists rather than a hand-rolled check per boundary: measurement found 31 public
 * boundaries where omitting a declared-required field reached the arithmetic and returned `NaN` —
 * `blackScholesPrice({ spot, strike, timeToExpiryYears, riskFreeRate, dividendYield })` with no
 * `volatility` priced the option as `NaN` and handed it back as a success. In a pricing library a
 * silently wrong number is the worst possible failure: it does not look like an error at any layer
 * that consumes it. The declaration already said the field was required; only the runtime disagreed.
 *
 * HOT PATHS: this validates ONE object, not one row. It belongs at a public facade, never inside an
 * iterative solver or a columnar loop whose columns were already checked — those call the unchecked
 * kernel behind the facade (spec 3B.1b: unchecked numeric routines stay private and reachable only
 * after validation). A `for` over a handful of declared names costs nothing next to `Math.log`; the
 * same loop run 100,000 times inside a batch path is a different thing entirely.
 */
export interface RequireFiniteFieldsOptions {
    /**
     * ONE complete, runnable call for this boundary — `blackScholesPrice({ type: 'call', spot: 100, … })`,
     * not a field fragment like `volatility: 0.2`.
     *
     * `missingFieldError` documents itself as showing "a WORKING example call", and the rest of the
     * library honours that: `walkForward({ data, trainSize: 30, … })`, `sma(closes, { period: 20 })`.
     * A fragment is helpful but not pasteable, and a caller who is already confused about the shape of
     * the request is exactly who cannot assemble one from a field snippet.
     */
    /**
     * A THUNK is accepted so a derived example costs nothing on the success path.
     *
     * Shared validators must build their example from the reported function name, and RV6 first wrote
     * that as `exampleCall: facadeExampleCall(functionName)` — evaluated on EVERY call, including the
     * millions that never fail. That put string construction inside `blackScholes.price`, a documented
     * hot path, to produce a message thrown away unused. The lazy form keeps the example correct and
     * the success path free; it is only invoked when a field is actually missing.
     */
    exampleCall: string | (() => string);
    /**
     * Optional per-field note appended on its own line — the unit trap or range the call shape cannot
     * carry (`annualized decimal, not 20`). Keyed by the BARE field name.
     */
    hints?: Readonly<Record<string, string>>;
    /**
     * Dotted prefix for a NESTED contract, so the error reads `parameters.kappa` rather than `kappa`.
     * The caller is holding an outer request; the bare name does not say which object to fix.
     */
    path?: string;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- exampleCall: string | (() => string); default: not declared — A THUNK is accepted so a derived example costs nothing on the success path.

Shared validators must build their example from the reported function name, and RV6 first wrote
that as `exampleCall: facadeExampleCall(functionName)` — evaluated on EVERY call, including the
millions that never fail. That put string construction inside `blackScholes.price`, a documented

carry (`annualized decimal, not 20`). Keyed by the BARE field name.
- path?: string; default: not declared — Dotted prefix for a NESTED contract, so the error reads `parameters.kappa` rather than `kappa`.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/core#SeriesFacade

Kind: type; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

A multi-argument (series-first) facade: the plain call takes `(data, parameters?, …)`, and `.explain()`
takes the SAME arguments and returns the {@link Computed} envelope. This is the S2 shape (`rsi(closes,
parameters?)`, `sharpe(returns, options?)`) — distinct from {@link Facade}, which is the single-object S1
shape (`blackScholes.call({ … })`).

```typescript
/**
 * A multi-argument (series-first) facade: the plain call takes `(data, parameters?, …)`, and `.explain()`
 * takes the SAME arguments and returns the {@link Computed} envelope. This is the S2 shape (`rsi(closes,
 * parameters?)`, `sharpe(returns, options?)`) — distinct from {@link Facade}, which is the single-object S1
 * shape (`blackScholes.call({ … })`).
 */
export type SeriesFacade<Args extends unknown[], Output, Extra extends Record<string, unknown> = Record<never, never>> = ((...callArguments: Args) => Output) & {
    explain: (...callArguments: Args) => Computed<Output, Extra>;
};
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (callArguments): Args; default: not declared
- explain: (...callArguments: Args) => Computed<Output, Extra>; default: not declared
- explain().return.assumptions: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Assumptions<Extra>; default: not declared — Every applied convention, echoed back.
- explain().return.diagnostics: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Diagnostics; default: not declared — How the value was computed, plus any warnings.
- explain().return.provenance?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Provenance; default: not declared — Optional data lineage when the inputs came from a provider.
- explain().return.value: Output; default: not declared — The computed value. Never `NaN` or `±Infinity`: a value the model cannot produce is `null`
beside a diagnostic that says why (Law 7 — a warning never licenses a non-finite number).
- explain(callArguments): Args; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/core#ValidationFieldSpecification

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

```typescript
export interface ValidationFieldSpecification {
    readonly name: string;
    readonly kind: ValidationFieldKind;
    readonly optional?: boolean;
    /** The declared union admits `null`; anywhere else a `null` is a wrong-typed value, not omission. */
    readonly nullable?: boolean;
    /**
     * A documented IEEE BOUND field: ±Infinity is the spelled "unbounded" (`localCap: Infinity`,
     * `globalFloor: -Infinity`). CURATED per contract in the validation roster, never inferred —
     * the checker sees `number` either way, and which numbers mean "no bound" is financial
     * semantics (C03). `NaN` stays rejected: no bound is ever spelled NaN.
     */
    readonly allowsInfinity?: boolean;
    /**
     * This numeric field is a synchronous resource count and must be a positive safe integer no
     * larger than this operation-level ceiling. Generated only where the declaration-derived resource
     * inventory owns the semantic classification; ordinary numeric magnitudes never receive it.
     */
    readonly safeIntegerMaximum?: number;
    /** The array's elements are resource counts governed by the same positive-safe-integer ladder. */
    readonly safeIntegerElementsMaximum?: number;
    /** The closed literal domain of an `enum` field. */
    readonly literals?: readonly (string | number | boolean)[];
    /**
     * OPEN primitive alternatives beside the literal domain — a MIXED union such as
     * `Frequency = 'annual' | 'semiannual' | … | number`, where a value is valid when it is a listed
     * literal OR any value of an open kind (numeric runs the finite ladder). Projected from the
     * declaration's arms; without it the collapsed kind rejected the named spellings.
     */
    readonly openKinds?: readonly ValidationFieldKind[];
    /** Nested closed object contract. */
    readonly fields?: readonly ValidationFieldSpecification[];
    /** Declared union alternatives. A field has `branches` OR `fields`, never both. */
    readonly branches?: readonly ValidationBranchSpecification[];
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- allowsInfinity?: boolean; default: not declared — A documented IEEE BOUND field: ±Infinity is the spelled "unbounded" (`localCap: Infinity`,
`globalFloor: -Infinity`). CURATED per contract in the validation roster, never inferred —
the checker sees `number` either way, and which numbers mean "no bound" is financial
semantics (C03). `NaN` stays rejected: no bound is ever spelled NaN.
- branches?: readonly ValidationBranchSpecification[]; default: not declared — Declared union alternatives. A field has `branches` OR `fields`, never both.
- fields?: readonly ValidationFieldSpecification[]; default: not declared — Nested closed object contract.
- kind: ValidationFieldKind; default: not declared
- literals?: readonly (string | number | boolean)[]; default: not declared — The closed literal domain of an `enum` field.
- name: string; default: not declared
- nullable?: boolean; default: not declared — The declared union admits `null`; anywhere else a `null` is a wrong-typed value, not omission.
- openKinds?: readonly ValidationFieldKind[]; default: not declared — OPEN primitive alternatives beside the literal domain — a MIXED union such as
`Frequency = 'annual' | 'semiannual' | … | number`, where a value is valid when it is a listed
literal OR any value of an open kind (numeric runs the finite ladder). Projected from the
declaration's arms; without it the collapsed kind rejected the named spellings.
- optional?: boolean; default: not declared
- safeIntegerElementsMaximum?: number; default: not declared — The array's elements are resource counts governed by the same positive-safe-integer ladder.
- safeIntegerMaximum?: number; default: not declared — This numeric field is a synchronous resource count and must be a positive safe integer no
larger than this operation-level ceiling. Generated only where the declaration-derived resource

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/core#WarningCode

Kind: type; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Canonical warning codes. Like error codes, these are stable public API — consumers branch on them.
The set is open; packages may add codes, but documented ones do not change without a major version.

Codes that are BOTH a thrown-error condition and an emitted warning (`implied_volatility.below_intrinsic`,
`implied_volatility.above_max_bound`, `implied_volatility.no_convergence`, `data.crossed_market`, `data.stale_quote`) live only in
{@link ErrorCode} — the single source of truth — and warning sites reference `ErrorCode.*` for the
code string, so no string is duplicated across the two registries (WS2.9).

```typescript
export type WarningCode = (typeof WarningCode)[keyof typeof WarningCode];
```

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/core#assertFiniteResult

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Law 7 runtime postcondition (spec P2.1, tightened in E3): a SUCCESSFUL explained result is
JSON-safe — it NEVER carries a non-finite number (`JSON.stringify` would silently corrupt it to
`null`). **Warnings never license a non-finite value**: an undefined quantity is reported as
`null` and the warning explains the null. The only ratified exceptions are structural sentinels:

  1. `diagnostics.warmup > 0` with an array value — EXACTLY the first `warmup` slots are the
     documented aligned-series "not yet formed" sentinel; every slot past the prefix is checked;
  2. discriminated "none" elements — zone-style points (`direction: 0`, shape-anchored on their
     zone fields) and divergence points (`code: 0`, shape-anchored on `priceSwings`) — whose
     documented NaN-when-none fields are exempt; every OTHER field of such an element is still
     checked, and an element that merely says `direction: 0` without the zone shape (e.g. an
     honest tdSequential point) is walked in full.

Anything else non-finite throws {@link PostconditionError}: a library defect surfaced loudly at
the boundary rather than shipped silently into a serialization. The walk is exhaustive — full
depth (cycle-safe), value + assumptions + diagnostics + provenance — so nothing hides below a cap.

```typescript
export declare function assertFiniteResult(label: string, result: Computed<unknown>): void;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (label): string; default: not declared
- (result): Computed<unknown, Record<never, never>>; default: not declared
- (result).assumptions: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Assumptions<Record<never, never>>; default: not declared — Every applied convention, echoed back.
- (result).diagnostics: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Diagnostics; default: not declared — How the value was computed, plus any warnings.
- (result).provenance?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Provenance; default: not declared — Optional data lineage when the inputs came from a provider.
- (result).value: unknown; default: not declared — The computed value. Never `NaN` or `±Infinity`: a value the model cannot produce is `null`
beside a diagnostic that says why (Law 7 — a warning never licenses a non-finite number).

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/core#assertFiniteValue

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

```typescript
export declare function assertFiniteValue(label: string, value: unknown): void;
```

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/core#ensureFiniteWhenPresent

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

A finite numeric value WHEN PRESENT — the optional-field sibling of {@link requireFiniteFields}.

`undefined` is allowed (optional omission, C06); anything else runs the same ladder a required
field does, so a string in an optional numeric slot reports `input.wrong_type` exactly as it
would in a required one. Calling bare `ensureFinite` there reported `input.not_finite`, which
contradicted the library's own documented matrix — and a test had been written asserting the
contradiction, which is how it survived.

`null` is NOT omission. This guard originally returned early on null, which silently accepted a
value every one of its call sites declares impossible (`lowerVolatilityBound?: number`, a bar's
`open?: number` — none say `| null`). C06 reserves `null` for declarations that explicitly carry
it; a field that wants nullable semantics declares them and takes a different guard. The
`null-when-nonnullable` enforcement mutation exists to keep this class measurable.

```typescript
export declare function ensureFiniteWhenPresent(value: unknown, field: string, functionName: string): void;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (field): string; default: not declared
- (functionName): string; default: not declared
- (value): unknown; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/core#ensureKnownKeys

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Law 12 — facade, analysis, and builder object inputs REJECT unknown keys (a misspelled option
must never be silently ignored: `greek: false` computing Greeks anyway is the bug class this
kills). Cheap by design: one key scan against a Set-able allowlist, no schema machinery, so it
is safe on hot facade paths. Direct kernels use named objects when financial values could be
confused; adapters that own foreign/superset schemas are declared `passthrough` in the manifest
and skip this guard.

```typescript
export declare function ensureKnownKeys(functionName: string, field: string, value: object, allowed: readonly string[]): void;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (allowed): readonly string[]; default: not declared
- (field): string; default: not declared

- (value): object; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/core#requireRateCurveData

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

The ONE full validator for a stored/observed {@link RateCurve} as PLAIN DATA — shared by the
Gate B market-snapshot spine (`observations.curves`) and the Gate C pricing protocol (the
`discountCurve` observation value), so both refuse the same malformed curves with the same
teaching. Core-internal on purpose: it is validation plumbing, not analysis API.

Checks: `currency` a non-empty string; `asOf` finite epoch ms; `dayCount`/`compounding` valid
conventions (a curve states its own — no silent economics); `points` an array of AT LEAST ONE
pillar (an empty curve discounts nothing — a consumer handed zero pillars has no discount
function, so emptiness is refused here rather than downstream) whose entries have a REAL
`'YYYY-MM-DD'` calendar date (parsed with core's date parser, so `'2025-02-30'` is refused),
strictly ascending pillar dates, dates at or after the curve's own `asOf` (a pillar BEFORE the
curve's valuation instant discounts into the past — no consumer has a meaning for it; a pillar
exactly AT `asOf` is the legal t = 0 anchor), and a finite `zeroRate` whose discount factor is
actually computable and representable under the curve's compounding at that pillar's tenor;
`interpolation` a non-empty string when present (the declared type). Entries stay open (Law 12):
vendor decoration is preserved, not enumerated here.

**Pillar authority — `zeroRate` is the ONE datum (2026-08-23, second external review).** The
semantics are the existing fixed-income consumer's: `curves.fromZeroRates(...)` consumes ZERO
RATES quoted under the curve's own `compounding`/`dayCount` and DERIVES every discount factor
through that compounding transform. The former advisory `discountFactor` pillar member is GONE:
a second, potentially contradictory answer must not share a pillar (the old sign-consistency
tolerance accepted `rate: 0.05` beside `discountFactor: 0.2`), and no consumer in the workspace
ever read it — discount-factor-quoted data has its own constructor
(`curves.fromDiscountFactors`), whose pillars carry no rates. What replaced the tolerance is a
REAL economics check through core's own transform (`discountFactor` in `dates.ts` — the one
compounding engine, not a second one): every pillar's derived discount factor must exist and be
a positive finite number, so `zeroRate: -2` under annual compounding (growth factor
`1 + r/m ≤ 0` — no real discount factor exists) and rate/tenor pairs whose factor overflows,
underflows to zero, or goes negative are refused with the arithmetic named.

```typescript
export declare function requireRateCurveData(functionName: string, path: string, value: unknown): RateCurve;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (functionName): string; default: not declared
- (path): string; default: not declared
- (value): unknown; default: not declared
- return.asOf: number; default: not declared
- return.compounding: InterestCompounding; default: not declared
- return.currency: string; default: not declared
- return.dayCount: DayCount; default: not declared
- return.interpolation?: string; default: not declared
- return.points: RateCurvePoint[]; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/core#requireSelection

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Validate an explicit SELECTION list — `outputs: ['price', 'gamma']`, `metrics: ['gex']` — and
return a dense copy in request order.

A selection decides what is computed, so every malformed form teaches instead of being repaired:
not an array (`input.wrong_type`), empty (`input.out_of_range` — an empty request computes
nothing and would read as a successful empty answer), a sparse hole (`input.missing_field`), an
unknown or non-string name (`input.invalid_enum`, with a did-you-mean), and a repeated name
(`input.duplicate_entry`). A duplicate is never silently collapsed: it usually means the caller
meant a different name.

`functionName` and `field` name the caller's boundary in every one of those errors, so they are
checked first: a missing label would otherwise surface as `undefined: undefined must be …`.

```typescript
export declare function requireSelection<T extends string>(functionName: string, field: string, value: unknown, allowed: readonly T[]): T[];
```

- (value): unknown; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/core#resolveAsOf

Resolve a DATE-GRANULAR `asOf` to epoch ms — ledgers, calendars, fundamentals, performance and

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/core#round

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Round half-away-from-zero to `decimals` places, robust to floating-point representation.

Total over the double domain: `decimals` must be an integer in [-323, 323] (10^±323 spans the
whole representable grid — beyond it nothing survives double precision), and the extremes are
exact identities rather than overflow artifacts: an integer input with `decimals >= 0` is
returned unchanged (so `round(1e16, 0)` is 1e16, not 1e16+2, and `round(Number.MAX_VALUE, 2)`
is MAX_VALUE, not Infinity), and when the requested grid is coarser than the value's own ulp the
value is already its rounded self.

```typescript
export declare function round(value: number, decimals?: number): number;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (decimals)?: number; default: not declared
- (value): number; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/core#stableSum

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Sum signed finite addends without losing a representable answer to evaluation order.

The ordinary path uses a non-overlapping floating-point expansion: low-order residuals survive
cancellation (`1e16 + 1 − 1e16 === 1`). If one partial addition itself overflows, the fallback
decodes each double into an exact BigInt superaccumulator and rounds the exact total once. That
fallback is what makes `1e308 + 1e308 + 1 − 1e308 − 1e308` return `1` in every permutation while
still returning Infinity when the mathematical sum of the supplied doubles exceeds
`Number.MAX_VALUE`. Non-finite addends retain ordinary IEEE-754 propagation semantics.

```typescript
export declare function stableSum(addends: readonly number[]): number;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (addends): readonly number[]; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/core#suspiciousReturnsWarning

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

The third classic footgun (dx WS-3 / R6): a PRICE or equity series passed where per-period
RETURNS are expected. Returns are decimals (`0.01` = +1%); a series whose mean magnitude
exceeds 0.5 (50% per period) is almost certainly prices — a monotonic 100→160 price series
fed to `sharpe()` yields an absurd-but-silent 117. Warning only, never an error (a genuine
>50%/period return series is legal — it is just worth flagging). Returns `undefined` when the
series looks like returns.

```typescript
export declare function suspiciousReturnsWarning(returns: ArrayLike<number>): QuantWarning | undefined;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (returns): ArrayLike<number>; default: not declared
- return.code: string; default: not declared
- return.context?: Record<string, unknown>; default: not declared
- return.message: string; default: not declared
- return.severity: WarningSeverity; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/core#usEquityCloseUtcMs

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/core#usEquityMarketDayIndex

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

The US equity/options market's calendar DAY an instant falls on, as a whole-day index (days since
the epoch of the America/New_York calendar date). Differencing two indices gives whole CALENDAR
DAYS between two market dates; equality means "same trading date". This is the ONE day boundary
shared by 0DTE classification, days-to-expiry counts and earnings day counts: expiries resolve to
16:00 ET (20:00/21:00 UTC), so a UTC-day comparison is already "tomorrow" between 20:00 and
23:59 ET. Pure and clock-free.
