Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- bump?: number; default: not declared — Yield bump for the finite-difference effective measures (default 1bp).
- context?: ProjectionContext; default: not declared
- context.forecastCurve?: YieldCurve; default: not declared — Forecast curve for projecting floating-rate coupons.
- context.forecastCurve.addSpread: (spread: YieldCurve) => YieldCurve; default: not declared — Combine with a term-structure spread curve: the continuous zeros ADD at each tenor (equivalently
discount factors multiply, `D(t)·D_spread(t)`). Unions both curves' pillar tenors so the spread's
shape — not just a level — is preserved. Used to discount over `benchmark + spread` (e.g. OIS + a
sector/rating spread) while keeping curve construction out of leaf entrypoints.
- context.forecastCurve.addSpread(spread): YieldCurve; default: not declared
- context.forecastCurve.bumpPillar: (index: number, delta: number) => YieldCurve; default: not declared — Bump a single pillar's continuous zero by `delta` (key-rate risk).
- context.forecastCurve.bumpPillar(delta): number; default: not declared
- context.forecastCurve.bumpPillar(index): number; default: not declared
- context.forecastCurve.dayCount: FixedIncomeDayCount; default: not declared
- context.forecastCurve.discount: (at: string | number) => number; default: not declared — Discount factor to a date or year fraction.
- context.forecastCurve.discount(at): string | number; default: not declared
- context.forecastCurve.extrapolation: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/fixed-income').CurveExtrapolation; default: not declared
- context.forecastCurve.forwardRate: (from: string | number, to: string | number, dayCount?: FixedIncomeDayCount) => number; default: not declared — Simple (money-market) forward rate between two times/dates under `dayCount`.
- context.forecastCurve.forwardRate(dayCount)?: FixedIncomeDayCount | undefined; default: not declared
- context.forecastCurve.forwardRate(from): string | number; default: not declared
- context.forecastCurve.forwardRate(to): string | number; default: not declared
- context.forecastCurve.instantaneousForward: (at: string | number) => number; default: not declared — Instantaneous (continuously-compounded) forward rate at a time/date.
- context.forecastCurve.instantaneousForward(at): string | number; default: not declared
- context.forecastCurve.interpolation: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/fixed-income').CurveInterpolation; default: not declared
- context.forecastCurve.pillars: readonly import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/fixed-income').CurvePillar[]; default: not declared
- context.forecastCurve.referenceDate: string; default: not declared
- context.forecastCurve.shift: (delta: number) => YieldCurve; default: not declared — Parallel shift of every pillar's continuous zero by `delta` (e.g. +0.0001 = +1bp).
- context.forecastCurve.shift(delta): number; default: not declared
- context.forecastCurve.timeTo: (at: string | number) => number; default: not declared — Year fraction from the reference date to a date (or pass a number through unchanged).
- context.forecastCurve.timeTo(at): string | number; default: not declared
- context.forecastCurve.zeroRate: (at: string | number, compounding?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').InterestCompounding) => number; default: not declared — Zero rate to a date or year fraction, in the requested compounding (default continuous).
- context.forecastCurve.zeroRate(at): string | number; default: not declared
- context.forecastCurve.zeroRate(compounding)?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').InterestCompounding | undefined; default: not declared
- context.forecastCurve.zeroRate(compounding).periodsPerYear: number; default: not declared
- context.forecastCurve.zeroRate(compounding).type: 'periodic'; default: not declared
- context.knownFixingRate?: number; default: not declared — The index fixing (decimal, e.g. `0.0532` for 5.32%) that ALREADY SET the coupon currently
accruing on a floating-rate note — the one whose accrual period began before the forecast
curve's reference date.

A settled-mid-period FRN has one coupon that is no longer a projection: it was fixed in the
past, on a date the curve does not reach. Asking the curve for it is a query before its
reference date, which throws. Supply the observed fixing (SOFR/EURIBOR print for that reset)
and it is used verbatim for that one coupon; every later coupon still projects off the curve.
The note's quoted `spread` is added on top, exactly as for a projected coupon.

Only the in-progress coupon is substituted. Coupons that both began AND ended before the
curve's reference date are settled history, not projections — one fixing cannot honestly stand
in for a whole strip of past resets, so those are rejected rather than fabricated.
- context.referenceIndex?: (date: string) => number; default: not declared — Price-index level at a date, for inflation-linked indexation.
- context.referenceIndex(date): string; default: not declared
- settlementDate: string; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/fixed-income#MultiCurve

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

A dual-curve set (spec §14.2): an OIS `discountCurve` and an index `forecastCurve`. Its shape is
exactly the `SwapCurves` every swap analytic (`swapValue`, `swaptionPrice`, `capFloorPrice`,
`cmsConvexityAdjustment`) already consumes, so a bootstrapped set drops straight in.

```typescript
/**
 * A dual-curve set (spec §14.2): an OIS `discountCurve` and an index `forecastCurve`. Its shape is

 * `cmsConvexityAdjustment`) already consumes, so a bootstrapped set drops straight in.
```

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/fixed-income#OasAnalyticsSpecification

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

```typescript
// ───────────────────────── OAS analytics ─────────────────────────
export interface OasAnalyticsSpecification extends Omit<CallableBondSpecification, 'marketPrice'> {
    /** Market dirty price the OAS and Z-spread are solved to. */
    marketPrice: number;
    /** Curve shock for the effective duration/convexity, in decimal. Default 1e-4 (1 bp). */
    durationShock?: number;
    /**
     * Optional term-structure spread curve added to `curve` before the spreads are solved. The effective
     * benchmark becomes `curve` + `spreadCurve` (continuous zeros add ⇔ discount factors multiply), so the
     * reported OAS and Z-spread are measured OVER a NON-FLAT benchmark — e.g. an OIS discount curve plus a
     * sector/rating spread curve — rather than the plain `curve`. Its zero rates ARE the spreads (build one
     * with `curves.fromZeroRates(spreadPillars)`); it must share `curve`'s reference date.
     */
    spreadCurve?: YieldCurve;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- bond.accrued: (settlementDate: string, context?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/fixed-income').ProjectionContext) => number; default: not declared — Accrued interest at `settlementDate` (per the bond's face value).

- bond.accrued(context).knownFixingRate?: number; default: not declared — The index fixing (decimal, e.g. `0.0532` for 5.32%) that ALREADY SET the coupon currently
accruing on a floating-rate note — the one whose accrual period began before the forecast
curve's reference date.

A settled-mid-period FRN has one coupon that is no longer a projection: it was fixed in the
past, on a date the curve does not reach. Asking the curve for it is a query before its
reference date, which throws. Supply the observed fixing (SOFR/EURIBOR print for that reset)
and it is used verbatim for that one coupon; every later coupon still projects off the curve.
The note's quoted `spread` is added on top, exactly as for a projected coupon.

Only the in-progress coupon is substituted. Coupons that both began AND ended before the
curve's reference date are settled history, not projections — one fixing cannot honestly stand
in for a whole strip of past resets, so those are rejected rather than fabricated.

- context.forecastCurve.referenceDate: string; default: not declared
- context.forecastCurve.shift: (delta: number) => YieldCurve; default: not declared — Parallel shift of every pillar's continuous zero by `delta` (e.g. +0.0001 = +1bp).
- context.forecastCurve.shift(delta): number; default: not declared
- context.forecastCurve.timeTo: (at: string | number) => number; default: not declared — Year fraction from the reference date to a date (or pass a number through unchanged).
- context.forecastCurve.timeTo(at): string | number; default: not declared
- context.forecastCurve.zeroRate: (at: string | number, compounding?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').InterestCompounding) => number; default: not declared — Zero rate to a date or year fraction, in the requested compounding (default continuous).
- context.forecastCurve.zeroRate(at): string | number; default: not declared
- context.forecastCurve.zeroRate(compounding)?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').InterestCompounding | undefined; default: not declared
- context.forecastCurve.zeroRate(compounding).periodsPerYear: number; default: not declared
- context.forecastCurve.zeroRate(compounding).type: 'periodic'; default: not declared
- context.knownFixingRate?: number; default: not declared — The index fixing (decimal, e.g. `0.0532` for 5.32%) that ALREADY SET the coupon currently
accruing on a floating-rate note — the one whose accrual period began before the forecast
curve's reference date.

A settled-mid-period FRN has one coupon that is no longer a projection: it was fixed in the
past, on a date the curve does not reach. Asking the curve for it is a query before its
reference date, which throws. Supply the observed fixing (SOFR/EURIBOR print for that reset)
and it is used verbatim for that one coupon; every later coupon still projects off the curve.
The note's quoted `spread` is added on top, exactly as for a projected coupon.

Only the in-progress coupon is substituted. Coupons that both began AND ended before the
curve's reference date are settled history, not projections — one fixing cannot honestly stand
in for a whole strip of past resets, so those are rejected rather than fabricated.
- context.referenceIndex?: (date: string) => number; default: not declared — Price-index level at a date, for inflation-linked indexation.
- context.referenceIndex(date): string; default: not declared
- settlementDate: string; default: not declared
- yield: number; default: not declared — Annualized yield (decimal).

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/fixed-income#ShortRateTree

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

```typescript
export interface ShortRateTree {
    readonly model: TreeModel;
    readonly steps: number;
    readonly timeStepYears: number;
    /** Short rate at tree node `(i, j)` (time step i, level j). */
    shortRate(stepIndex: number, nodeIndex: number): number;
    /** Tree-implied discount bond price `P(0, T)` for a maturity on the time grid (years). */
    discountBond(maturity: number): number;
    /** Reference discount factors the tree was calibrated to, at each grid time. */
    readonly gridTimes: readonly number[];
    /** Map a year fraction to its grid step, validating it lands on the grid. */
    stepOf(years: number): number;
    /** Half-width of reachable levels at step `i` (nodes span `[-reach, +reach]`). */
    reachAt(stepIndex: number): number;
    /**
     * Generic backward induction from `terminalStep` to the root. `terminal(j)` seeds the value at each
     * terminal node; at every earlier node the discounted expected continuation is passed to `atNode`,
     * which returns the node value (inject cashflows, apply call/exercise via min/max). Returns the root
     * value. The engine behind callable bonds and Bermudan swaptions.
     */
    rollback(terminalStep: number, terminal: (j: number) => number, atNode?: (i: number, j: number, continuation: number) => number): number;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- discountBond: (maturity: number) => number; default: not declared — Tree-implied discount bond price `P(0, T)` for a maturity on the time grid (years).
- discountBond(maturity): number; default: not declared
- gridTimes: readonly number[]; default: not declared — Reference discount factors the tree was calibrated to, at each grid time.
- model: TreeModel; default: not declared
- reachAt: (stepIndex: number) => number; default: not declared — Half-width of reachable levels at step `i` (nodes span `[-reach, +reach]`).
- reachAt(stepIndex): number; default: not declared
- rollback: (terminalStep: number, terminal: (j: number) => number, atNode?: (i: number, j: number, continuation: number) => number) => number; default: not declared — Generic backward induction from `terminalStep` to the root. `terminal(j)` seeds the value at each
terminal node; at every earlier node the discounted expected continuation is passed to `atNode`,
which returns the node value (inject cashflows, apply call/exercise via min/max). Returns the root
value. The engine behind callable bonds and Bermudan swaptions.
- rollback(atNode)?: ((i: number, j: number, continuation: number) => number) | undefined; default: not declared
- rollback(terminal): (j: number) => number; default: not declared
- rollback(terminalStep): number; default: not declared
- shortRate: (stepIndex: number, nodeIndex: number) => number; default: not declared — Short rate at tree node `(i, j)` (time step i, level j).
- shortRate(nodeIndex): number; default: not declared
- shortRate(stepIndex): number; default: not declared
- stepOf: (years: number) => number; default: not declared — Map a year fraction to its grid step, validating it lands on the grid.
- stepOf(years): number; default: not declared
- steps: number; default: not declared
- timeStepYears: number; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/fixed-income#SwapInstrument

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

A par swap or OIS: the fixed leg pays `rate` at `fixedFrequency`; single-curve par condition.

```typescript
/** A par swap or OIS: the fixed leg pays `rate` at `fixedFrequency`; single-curve par condition. */
export interface SwapInstrument {
    type: 'swap' | 'ois';
    maturity: string;
    rate: number;
    /** Fixed-leg frequency. Default annual for `ois`, semiannual for `swap`. */
    fixedFrequency?: Frequency;
    /** Fixed-leg accrual day count. Default `30/360`. */
    fixedDayCount?: FixedIncomeDayCount;
    /**
     * Floating-leg frequency. Used by BOTH bootstraps: each now sums the floating leg explicitly, so
     * that a bootstrapped curve reprices its input swaps under `swapValue` (the single-curve
     * bootstrap used to telescope the leg to `1 − DF(T)` and ignore this field, which is exact only
     * while no payment date rolls to a business day). Default `quarterly`.
     */
    floatFrequency?: Frequency;
    /** Floating-leg day count. Default `ACT/360`. */
    floatDayCount?: FixedIncomeDayCount;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- fixedDayCount?: FixedIncomeDayCount; default: not declared — Fixed-leg accrual day count. Default `30/360`.
- fixedFrequency?: Frequency; default: not declared — Fixed-leg frequency. Default annual for `ois`, semiannual for `swap`.
- floatDayCount?: FixedIncomeDayCount; default: not declared — Floating-leg day count. Default `ACT/360`.
- floatFrequency?: Frequency; default: not declared — Floating-leg frequency. Used by BOTH bootstraps: each now sums the floating leg explicitly, so
that a bootstrapped curve reprices its input swaps under `swapValue` (the single-curve
bootstrap used to telescope the leg to `1 − DF(T)` and ignore this field, which is exact only
while no payment date rolls to a business day). Default `quarterly`.
- maturity: string; default: not declared
- rate: number; default: not declared
- type: 'swap' | 'ois'; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/fixed-income#YieldCurve

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

A discount/zero/forward curve. Immutable; shocks return new curves.

```typescript
/** A discount/zero/forward curve. Immutable; shocks return new curves. */
export interface YieldCurve {
    readonly referenceDate: string;
    readonly dayCount: FixedIncomeDayCount;
    readonly interpolation: CurveInterpolation;
    readonly extrapolation: CurveExtrapolation;
    readonly pillars: readonly CurvePillar[];
    /** Year fraction from the reference date to a date (or pass a number through unchanged). */
    timeTo(at: string | number): number;
    /** Discount factor to a date or year fraction. */
    discount(at: string | number): number;
    /** Zero rate to a date or year fraction, in the requested compounding (default continuous). */
    zeroRate(at: string | number, compounding?: InterestCompounding): number;
    /** Simple (money-market) forward rate between two times/dates under `dayCount`. */
    forwardRate(from: string | number, to: string | number, dayCount?: FixedIncomeDayCount): number;
    /** Instantaneous (continuously-compounded) forward rate at a time/date. */
    instantaneousForward(at: string | number): number;
    /** Parallel shift of every pillar's continuous zero by `delta` (e.g. +0.0001 = +1bp). */
    shift(delta: number): YieldCurve;
    /** Bump a single pillar's continuous zero by `delta` (key-rate risk). */
    bumpPillar(index: number, delta: number): YieldCurve;

     * shape — not just a level — is preserved. Used to discount over `benchmark + spread` (e.g. OIS + a
     * sector/rating spread) while keeping curve construction out of leaf entrypoints.
     */
    addSpread(spread: YieldCurve): YieldCurve;
}
```

- context.forecastCurve.discount: (at: string | number) => number; default: not declared — Discount factor to a date or year fraction.
- context.forecastCurve.discount(at): string | number; default: not declared
- context.forecastCurve.extrapolation: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/fixed-income').CurveExtrapolation; default: not declared
- context.forecastCurve.forwardRate: (from: string | number, to: string | number, dayCount?: FixedIncomeDayCount) => number; default: not declared — Simple (money-market) forward rate between two times/dates under `dayCount`.
- context.forecastCurve.forwardRate(dayCount)?: FixedIncomeDayCount | undefined; default: not declared
- context.forecastCurve.forwardRate(from): string | number; default: not declared
- context.forecastCurve.forwardRate(to): string | number; default: not declared
- context.forecastCurve.instantaneousForward: (at: string | number) => number; default: not declared — Instantaneous (continuously-compounded) forward rate at a time/date.
- context.forecastCurve.instantaneousForward(at): string | number; default: not declared
- context.forecastCurve.interpolation: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/fixed-income').CurveInterpolation; default: not declared
- context.forecastCurve.pillars: readonly import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/fixed-income').CurvePillar[]; default: not declared
- context.forecastCurve.referenceDate: string; default: not declared
- context.forecastCurve.shift: (delta: number) => YieldCurve; default: not declared — Parallel shift of every pillar's continuous zero by `delta` (e.g. +0.0001 = +1bp).
- context.forecastCurve.shift(delta): number; default: not declared
- context.forecastCurve.timeTo: (at: string | number) => number; default: not declared — Year fraction from the reference date to a date (or pass a number through unchanged).
- context.forecastCurve.timeTo(at): string | number; default: not declared
- context.forecastCurve.zeroRate: (at: string | number, compounding?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').InterestCompounding) => number; default: not declared — Zero rate to a date or year fraction, in the requested compounding (default continuous).
- context.forecastCurve.zeroRate(at): string | number; default: not declared
- context.forecastCurve.zeroRate(compounding)?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').InterestCompounding | undefined; default: not declared
- context.forecastCurve.zeroRate(compounding).periodsPerYear: number; default: not declared
- context.forecastCurve.zeroRate(compounding).type: 'periodic'; default: not declared
- context.knownFixingRate?: number; default: not declared — The index fixing (decimal, e.g. `0.0532` for 5.32%) that ALREADY SET the coupon currently
accruing on a floating-rate note — the one whose accrual period began before the forecast
curve's reference date.

A settled-mid-period FRN has one coupon that is no longer a projection: it was fixed in the
past, on a date the curve does not reach. Asking the curve for it is a query before its
reference date, which throws. Supply the observed fixing (SOFR/EURIBOR print for that reset)
and it is used verbatim for that one coupon; every later coupon still projects off the curve.
The note's quoted `spread` is added on top, exactly as for a projected coupon.

Only the in-progress coupon is substituted. Coupons that both began AND ended before the
curve's reference date are settled history, not projections — one fixing cannot honestly stand
in for a whole strip of past resets, so those are rejected rather than fabricated.
- context.referenceIndex?: (date: string) => number; default: not declared — Price-index level at a date, for inflation-linked indexation.
- context.referenceIndex(date): string; default: not declared
- price: number; default: not declared — Either a clean price (default) or a dirty price — set `priceType`.
- priceType?: 'clean' | 'dirty'; default: not declared
- settlementDate: string; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/fixed-income#ZeroCouponInflationSwapInput

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Input for {@link zeroCouponInflationSwap}.

```typescript
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// 4. Zero-coupon inflation swap (ZCIS)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
/** Input for {@link zeroCouponInflationSwap}. */
export interface ZeroCouponInflationSwapInput {
    /** Swap maturity in years (`N`). The single ZCIS cashflow is exchanged at maturity. */
    maturityYears: number;
    /**
     * The par/market ZCIS rate `K` (the geometric annual breakeven). Supply **this or**
     * `forwardIndexRatio` — exactly one.
     */
    swapRate?: number;
    /**
     * The forward index ratio `I(T)/I(0)`. Supply **this or** `swapRate` — exactly one. Implies
     * `swapRate = forwardIndexRatio^(1/N) − 1`.
     */
    forwardIndexRatio?: number;
    /** An existing position's contracted fixed rate `K_c` — supply to value the swap (MTM). */
    contractRate?: number;
    /** Discount factor to maturity for the MTM (default `1` → the undiscounted at-maturity value). */
    discountFactor?: number;
    /** Notional (default `1`). */
    notional?: number;
    /** Which leg the holder **pays** (default `'fixed'` = pay fixed, receive inflation). Signs the MTM. */
    payer?: 'fixed' | 'inflation';
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- contractRate?: number; default: not declared — An existing position's contracted fixed rate `K_c` — supply to value the swap (MTM).
- discountFactor?: number; default: not declared — Discount factor to maturity for the MTM (default `1` → the undiscounted at-maturity value).
- forwardIndexRatio?: number; default: not declared — The forward index ratio `I(T)/I(0)`. Supply **this or** `swapRate` — exactly one. Implies
`swapRate = forwardIndexRatio^(1/N) − 1`.
- maturityYears: number; default: not declared — Swap maturity in years (`N`). The single ZCIS cashflow is exchanged at maturity.
- notional?: number; default: not declared — Notional (default `1`).
- payer?: 'fixed' | 'inflation'; default: not declared — Which leg the holder **pays** (default `'fixed'` = pay fixed, receive inflation). Signs the MTM.
- swapRate?: number; default: not declared — The par/market ZCIS rate `K` (the geometric annual breakeven). Supply **this or**
`forwardIndexRatio` — exactly one.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/fixed-income#ZeroCouponInflationSwapResult

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

The economics of a zero-coupon inflation swap.

```typescript
/** The economics of a zero-coupon inflation swap. */
export interface ZeroCouponInflationSwapResult {
    /** Par ZCIS rate (geometric annual breakeven): `forwardIndexRatio^(1/N) − 1`. */
    parRate: number;
    /** Forward index ratio `I(T)/I(0) = (1 + parRate)^N`. */
    forwardIndexRatio: number;
    /**
     * The single fixed-leg payoff per unit notional at maturity: `(1 + parRate)^N − 1`. Equals the
     * expected inflation-leg payoff (they match at par).
     */
    fixedLeg: number;
    /**
     * Mark-to-market PV of a position at `contractRate` (present only when `contractRate` is supplied):
     * `±notional·DF·[(1+parRate)^N − (1+contractRate)^N]`, signed by `payer`. `null` otherwise.
     */
    markToMarket: number | null;
    assumptions: {
        conventionsVersion: string;
        method: 'zero-coupon-inflation-swap';
    };
    diagnostics: Diagnostics;
}
```

- diagnostics.decomposition?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Named intermediate quantities the value decomposes into — a par spread's protection leg and
risky annuity, a forward variance's near/far legs. The H-series explain paths disclose their
arithmetic here so a caller can audit the ratio, not just receive it (3B.3).
- diagnostics.engine?: string; default: not declared — Pricing/solver engine name, e.g. `black-scholes-merton`.
- diagnostics.finiteDifferenceBumps?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Finite-difference engines: the ACTUAL bump sizes used for FD Greeks (spec P2.3) — adaptive

- diagnostics.timingMs?: number; default: not declared — Wall-clock timing in milliseconds, when measured.
- diagnostics.warmup?: number; default: not declared — Series facades: number of leading output slots that are warmup sentinels (null/NaN) while the
computation seeds. Equals the input length when the indicator never emitted.
- diagnostics.warnings: QuantWarning[]; default: not declared — Structured warnings; always present (possibly empty).
- fixedLeg: number; default: not declared — The single fixed-leg payoff per unit notional at maturity: `(1 + parRate)^N − 1`. Equals the

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/fixed-income#bermudanSwaption

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Price a Bermudan swaption on the Hull-White tree. At each exercise date the holder takes
`max(continuation, swapValue)`, where the node-level forward swap value uses the Hull-White analytic
bond reconstruction `P(tᵢ, T; r_node)`. (Hull-White only — the lognormal Black-Karasinski tree has
no analytic node bond.)

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/fixed-income#bondFutureCtdFrontier

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

The cheapest-to-deliver *frontier*: how the CTD identity and the futures risk move under explicit
parallel-yield (and optional futures-price) scenarios. This is a **switching frontier**, not a
valuation of the short's timing/quality delivery option (which stays deferred). It composes
{@link bondFuture} at every node (one source of basis/carry/implied-repo truth), reprices each
deliverable with {@link priceFromYield}, refines held-constant switch brackets by re-evaluating the
*whole* basket (so a narrow third-deliverable window splits into two honest transitions and no
pairwise root off the global frontier is accepted), and reports the delivery-date futures DV01 from
the CTD's futures-implied forward yield — distinct from the spot cash DV01 / CF. See
`docs/specs/wave6-quant-moats.md` §1 and `docs/specs/bond-future-ctd.md`.

```typescript
export declare function bondFutureCtdFrontier(input: BondFutureCtdFrontierInput): BondFutureCtdFrontierResult;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (input): BondFutureCtdFrontierInput; default: not declared
- (input).deliverables: DeliverableBond[]; default: not declared
- (input).deliveryDate: string; default: not declared — Delivery date — when the short delivers into the future (ISO).
- (input).futuresPrice: number; default: not declared — Futures price per 100 face.
- (input).futuresPrices?: readonly number[]; default: not declared — Optional futures-price path, one entry per *explicit* shift (the `(shift, price)` pairs are sorted
together). Omit to hold the input futures quote constant across the scan (a ceteris-paribus basis
question). A discrete path does not define values between nodes, so its switches stay grid-labeled.
- (input).notionalCoupon?: number; default: not declared — The contract's notional coupon (decimal); default `0.06`.
- (input).refineSwitches?: boolean; default: not declared — Refine held-constant-policy switch brackets to a crossing; default `true`. Invalid with `futuresPrices`.
- (input).repoRate: number; default: not declared — ACT/360 financing (repo) rate (decimal) used for carry / net basis.
- (input).settlementDate: string; default: not declared — Settlement date — when the cash bond is bought (ISO).
- (input).switchLocationToleranceBp?: number; default: not declared — Maximum reported switch-location bracket width in shift basis points; default `0.01`.
- (input).yieldShiftsBp?: YieldShiftGrid; default: not declared — Parallel yield shifts (bp) to scan. Default `{ from: -200, to: 200, step: 25 }` (17 nodes incl. 0).
- return.assumptions: { conventionsVersion: string; deliveryDate: string; futuresPriceScenario: 'held-constant' | 'supplied-path'; refineSwitches: boolean; repoRateTieTolerance: 1e-10; settlementDate: string; switchLocationToleranceBp: number | null; yieldShiftsBp: number[]; yieldShock: 'parallel'; }; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.conventionsVersion: string; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.deliveryDate: string; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.futuresPriceScenario: 'held-constant' | 'supplied-path'; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.refineSwitches: boolean; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.repoRateTieTolerance: 1e-10; default: not declared — Internal global-tie test, decimal annualized implied-repo rate; a fixed library assumption.
- return.assumptions.settlementDate: string; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.switchLocationToleranceBp: number | null; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.yieldShiftsBp: number[]; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.yieldShock: 'parallel'; default: not declared
- return.current: { conversionFactor: number; ctdId: string; ctdYield: number; }; default: not declared — The current (unshifted) cheapest-to-deliver.
- return.current.conversionFactor: number; default: not declared
- return.current.ctdId: string; default: not declared
- return.current.ctdYield: number; default: not declared
- return.diagnostics: Diagnostics; default: not declared
- return.risk: { deliveryDateFuturesDv01: number; impliedForwardYield: number; spotFuturesDv01: number; }; default: not declared
- return.risk.deliveryDateFuturesDv01: number; default: not declared — The futures DV01 from the CTD's *forward* DV01 at the delivery date / CF — the delivery risk.
- return.risk.impliedForwardYield: number; default: not declared — The CTD yield the futures price implies at the forward clean price `F·CF`, as of delivery.
- return.risk.spotFuturesDv01: number; default: not declared — The current futures DV01 from the spot cash DV01 / CF (matches {@link bondFutureHedge}).
- return.scenarios: CtdFrontierScenario[]; default: not declared — Every scanned node, ordered by ascending yield shift.
- return.switches: CtdSwitch[]; default: not declared — Every CTD switch across the scan (a third-deliverable window splits into two transitions).

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/fixed-income#bondFutureHedge

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Bond-future DV01 hedge ratio and futures-implied yield. Composes {@link bondFuture} (to find the CTD and
the conversion factors) with the bond yield/DV01 analytics: the futures DV01 is the CTD's DV01 divided by
its conversion factor (Hull), so a `hedgeDv01` of risk is offset by `hedgeDv01 / futuresDv01` contracts —
exactly `CF` to hedge the CTD itself. Also reports the CTD yield implied by the forward clean price
`F·CF`. See `docs/specs/bond-future-hedge.md`.

```typescript
export declare function bondFutureHedge(input: BondFutureHedgeInput): BondFutureHedgeResult;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (input): BondFutureHedgeInput; default: not declared

- (input).deliveryDate: string; default: not declared — Delivery date — when the short delivers into the future (ISO).
- (input).futuresPrice: number; default: not declared — Futures price per 100 face.
- (input).hedgeDv01?: number; default: not declared — DV01 (per 100 face) of the position to hedge; when given, the result reports `hedgeRatio`.
- (input).notionalCoupon?: number; default: not declared — The contract's notional coupon (decimal); default `0.06`.
- (input).repoRate: number; default: not declared — ACT/360 financing (repo) rate (decimal) used for carry / net basis.
- (input).settlementDate: string; default: not declared — Settlement date — when the cash bond is bought (ISO).
- return.assumptions: { conventionsVersion: string; deliveryDate: string; futuresPrice: number; settlementDate: string; }; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.conventionsVersion: string; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.deliveryDate: string; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.futuresPrice: number; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.settlementDate: string; default: not declared
- return.ctdConversionFactor: number; default: not declared
- return.ctdDv01: number; default: not declared — DV01 of the CTD cash bond per 100 face (at its market yield).
- return.ctdId: string; default: not declared
- return.ctdYield: number; default: not declared — Spot yield of the CTD at its market clean price.
- return.deliverables: DeliverableRisk[]; default: not declared — Per-deliverable spot yield + DV01 across the basket (CTD first).
- return.diagnostics: Diagnostics; default: not declared
- return.futuresDv01: number; default: not declared — The futures contract's DV01 per 100 face of notional (`ctdDv01 / CF_ctd`).

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/fixed-income#cir

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Construct a CIR model `dr = a(b − r)dt + σ√r dW` (affine, non-negative rates).

The Feller condition `2ab ≥ σ²` is what keeps the short rate strictly positive. Parameters that
violate it are perfectly ACCEPTABLE — CIR fits to real curves routinely land there, and the
affine bond price stays valid — but the model then puts mass at r = 0, which changes what the
output means. Violation is therefore disclosed (`model.feller_condition_violated`), never thrown
and never silently absorbed.

```typescript
export declare function cir(parameters: CirParameters): CirModel;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (parameters): CirParameters; default: not declared
- (parameters).a: number; default: not declared
- (parameters).b: number; default: not declared
- (parameters).r0: number; default: not declared
- (parameters).sigma: number; default: not declared
- return.diagnostics: { warnings: QuantWarning[]; }; default: not declared — Structured warnings about the calibration (currently: the Feller condition). Always present.
- return.diagnostics.warnings: QuantWarning[]; default: not declared
- return.discountBond: (shortRate: number, tau: number) => number; default: not declared — Affine discount-bond price `P(t,T)` for a short rate `r` at time `t` (τ = T − t in years).
- return.shortRateMoments: (years: number) => ShortRateMoments; default: not declared — Mean/variance of the short rate at horizonYears `T` (years), from `r0`.
- return.zeroRate: (shortRate: number, tau: number) => number; default: not declared — Continuously-compounded zero rate `−ln P / τ`.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/fixed-income#cmsConvexityAdjustment

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

The standard CMS convexity adjustment (Hull): valuing the swap-rate payoff with the bond function
`G(y) = Σ cᵢ·(1 + y/m)^(−i)` of a par bond paying the swap's fixed cash flows gives
`Δ = −½·y₀²·σ²·T·G''(y₀)/G'(y₀)` (positive, since `G' < 0` and `G'' > 0`). Returns a Law-2
envelope: the adjustment in `value` plus the applied conventions and a warnings channel.

```typescript
export declare function cmsConvexityAdjustment(specification: CmsConvexityInput): CmsConvexityResult;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (specification): CmsConvexityInput; default: not declared
- (specification).expiry: number; default: not declared — Time to the CMS observation, in years.
- (specification).forwardSwapRate: number; default: not declared — Plain forward swap rate `y₀` of the underlying swap.
- (specification).paymentsPerYear: number; default: not declared — Fixed-leg payments per year `m` (drives the bond function G(y)).
- (specification).swapTenorYears: number; default: not declared — Underlying swap tenor in whole years.
- (specification).volatility: number; default: not declared — Lognormal volatility of the underlying swap rate.
- return.assumptions: { [k: string]: unknown; conventionsVersion: string; }; default: not declared — Applied conventions, echoed (Law 2 envelope grammar).
- return.assumptions.conventionsVersion: string; default: not declared
- return.diagnostics: { warnings: QuantWarning[]; }; default: not declared — Structured warnings; always present (possibly empty).
- return.diagnostics.warnings: QuantWarning[]; default: not declared
- return.value: number; default: not declared — The additive adjustment Δ (rate units): expected CMS rate minus the plain forward swap rate.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/fixed-income#crossCurrencyBasisCurve

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Build the domestic-collateralized foreign discount curve (spec §14.5): the foreign OIS curve plus the
cross-currency basis, `D_for^dom = foreign.addSpread(basis)`. This is the curve on which to discount
foreign cash flows collateralized in the domestic currency, and it reprices the FX forwards the xccy
basis market quotes: `F(0,t) = spot · D_for^dom(t) / D_dom(t)`.

```typescript
export declare function crossCurrencyBasisCurve(input: CrossCurrencyBasisInput): CrossCurrencyBasisResult;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (input): CrossCurrencyBasisInput; default: not declared
- (input).basis?: YieldCurve; default: not declared — Cross-currency basis term structure added to the foreign curve (its zero rates ARE the basis
spreads). Omit for the pure covered-interest-parity case (no basis): `fxForward` is then
`spot · D_for(t)/D_dom(t)` and the collateralized curve is the foreign curve itself.
- (input).domestic: YieldCurve; default: not declared — Domestic collateral (OIS) discount curve.
- (input).foreign: YieldCurve; default: not declared — Foreign index/OIS discount curve (pre-basis).
- (input).spot: number; default: not declared — FX spot: domestic units per 1 foreign unit.
- return.assumptions: { [k: string]: unknown; conventionsVersion: string; }; default: not declared — Applied conventions, echoed (Law 2 report grammar).
- return.assumptions.conventionsVersion: string; default: not declared
- return.collateralizedCurve: YieldCurve; default: not declared — The domestic-collateralized foreign discount curve (`foreign + basis`). Discount foreign cash flows on THIS.
- return.diagnostics: { warnings: QuantWarning[]; }; default: not declared — Structured warnings; always present (possibly empty).
- return.diagnostics.warnings: QuantWarning[]; default: not declared
- return.fxForward: (at: string | number) => number; default: not declared — Market FX forward at `at`, from the collateralized curve: `spot · D_for^dom(at) / D_dom(at)`.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/fixed-income#forwardSwap

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

The curve-driven forward swap rate and annuity of a (possibly forward-starting) swap — the two curve
inputs a swaption needs, in one call. For a swaption struck at `K` expiring at `startDate`, the price
is `annuity · Black(forwardSwapRate, K, σ, T)` (Bachelier for normal σ). Pair this with a vol from
`@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility`'s swaption cube (`swaptionCubeVolatility`) for a fully curve-consistent swaption price, so
the forward and annuity come from the live (OIS/projection) curves rather than stale market nodes.

```typescript
export declare function forwardSwap(specification: ForwardSwapSpecification, curves: SwapCurves): ForwardSwapResult;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (curves): SwapCurves; default: not declared
- (curves).discountCurve: YieldCurve; default: not declared
- (curves).forecastCurve?: YieldCurve; default: not declared — Projection curve for floating coupons; defaults to the discount curve (single-curve).
- (specification): ForwardSwapSpecification; default: not declared
- (specification).fixedDayCount?: FixedIncomeDayCount; default: not declared — Fixed-leg day count (default `30/360`).
- (specification).fixedFrequency?: Frequency; default: not declared — Fixed-leg frequency (default semiannual).
- (specification).floatDayCount?: FixedIncomeDayCount; default: not declared — Floating-leg day count (default `ACT/360`).
- (specification).floatFrequency?: Frequency; default: not declared — Floating-leg frequency (default quarterly).
- (specification).floatSpread?: number; default: not declared — Spread over the projected index on the floating leg (default 0).
- (specification).maturityDate: string; default: not declared
- (specification).notional?: number; default: not declared
- (specification).startDate: string; default: not declared
- return.annuity: number; default: not declared — Fixed-leg annuity `Σ τ·DF(payDate)` (the level / PV of a unit annuity).
- return.assumptions: { [k: string]: unknown; conventionsVersion: string; }; default: not declared — Applied conventions, echoed (Law 2 report grammar).
- return.assumptions.conventionsVersion: string; default: not declared
- return.diagnostics: { warnings: QuantWarning[]; }; default: not declared — Structured warnings; always present (possibly empty).
- return.diagnostics.warnings: QuantWarning[]; default: not declared
- return.forwardSwapRate: number; default: not declared — Par (forward) swap rate `S = floatLegPv / annuity` — a swaption's natural forward under the annuity measure.
- return.pv01: number; default: not declared — PV of a 1bp fixed-rate change (`notional · annuity · 1e-4`).

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/fixed-income#g2pp

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

G2++ (two-additive-factor Gaussian) short-rate model `r(t) = φ(t) + x(t) + y(t)` with correlated
Ornstein-Uhlenbeck factors, fit to the initial `curve` (Brigo–Mercurio). Two factors give a richer,
de-correlating term structure of volatility than one-factor Hull-White, while keeping analytic
discount bonds and (Gaussian) zero-coupon-bond options. Reduces to Hull-White when `eta = 0`.

```typescript
export declare function g2pp(curve: YieldCurve, parameters: G2ppParameters): G2ppModel;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (curve): YieldCurve; default: not declared
- (curve).addSpread: (spread: YieldCurve) => YieldCurve; default: not declared — Combine with a term-structure spread curve: the continuous zeros ADD at each tenor (equivalently
discount factors multiply, `D(t)·D_spread(t)`). Unions both curves' pillar tenors so the spread's
shape — not just a level — is preserved. Used to discount over `benchmark + spread` (e.g. OIS + a
sector/rating spread) while keeping curve construction out of leaf entrypoints.
- (curve).bumpPillar: (index: number, delta: number) => YieldCurve; default: not declared — Bump a single pillar's continuous zero by `delta` (key-rate risk).
- (curve).dayCount: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/fixed-income').FixedIncomeDayCount; default: not declared
- (curve).discount: (at: string | number) => number; default: not declared — Discount factor to a date or year fraction.
- (curve).extrapolation: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/fixed-income').CurveExtrapolation; default: not declared
- (curve).forwardRate: (from: string | number, to: string | number, dayCount?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/fixed-income').FixedIncomeDayCount) => number; default: not declared — Simple (money-market) forward rate between two times/dates under `dayCount`.
- (curve).instantaneousForward: (at: string | number) => number; default: not declared — Instantaneous (continuously-compounded) forward rate at a time/date.
- (curve).interpolation: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/fixed-income').CurveInterpolation; default: not declared
- (curve).pillars: readonly import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/fixed-income').CurvePillar[]; default: not declared
- (curve).referenceDate: string; default: not declared
- (curve).shift: (delta: number) => YieldCurve; default: not declared — Parallel shift of every pillar's continuous zero by `delta` (e.g. +0.0001 = +1bp).
- (curve).timeTo: (at: string | number) => number; default: not declared — Year fraction from the reference date to a date (or pass a number through unchanged).
- (curve).zeroRate: (at: string | number, compounding?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').InterestCompounding) => number; default: not declared — Zero rate to a date or year fraction, in the requested compounding (default continuous).
- (parameters): G2ppParameters; default: not declared
- (parameters).a: number; default: not declared — Mean reversion of factor x.
- (parameters).b: number; default: not declared — Mean reversion of factor y.
- (parameters).eta: number; default: not declared — Volatility of factor y.
- (parameters).rho: number; default: not declared — Instantaneous correlation of the two factors, in [-1, 1].
- (parameters).sigma: number; default: not declared — Volatility of factor x.
- return.caplet: (input: RateOptionletInput) => number; default: not declared
- return.discountBond: (input: G2ppDiscountBondInput) => number; default: not declared — Reconstructed discount bond `P(t,T)` given factor values `(x, y)` at `t` (default 0 ⇒ the curve).
- return.floorlet: (input: RateOptionletInput) => number; default: not declared
- return.shortRateVariance: (years: number) => number; default: not declared — Variance of the short rate at horizonYears `t`.
- return.zeroCouponBondOption: (input: ZeroCouponBondOptionInput) => number; default: not declared — Analytic zero-coupon-bond option as of t = 0 (Gaussian, like Hull-White but with the G2++ variance).

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/fixed-income#generateSchedule

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Generate a coupon schedule by rolling backward from maturity at the coupon interval — the market
default, which places any irregular ("stub") period at the front. Accrual boundaries are the
regular unadjusted dates (so coupon amounts use the true period length); payment dates are
business-day-adjusted and optionally lagged.

```typescript
export declare function generateSchedule(options: ScheduleOptions): SchedulePeriod[];
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (options): ScheduleOptions; default: not declared
- (options).calendar?: Calendar; default: not declared — Calendar deciding business days (default weekends-only).
- (options).convention?: BusinessDayConvention; default: not declared — Business-day roll applied to payment dates (default `modifiedFollowing`).
- (options).effectiveDate: string; default: not declared — First accrual date (dated/effective date).
- (options).endOfMonth?: boolean; default: not declared — Force month-end rolling; defaults to auto-detect from whether `maturityDate` is a month end.
- (options).frequency: Frequency; default: not declared
- (options).maturityDate: string; default: not declared — Final accrual date (maturity).
- (options).paymentLagDays?: number; default: not declared — Business days between a period's accrual end and its payment (settlement lag). Default 0.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/fixed-income#impliedCrossCurrencyBasis

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Invert market FX forwards to the cross-currency basis (spec §14.5) — the inverse of
{@link crossCurrencyBasisCurve}. From `F(0,t) = spot · D_for^dom(t)/D_dom(t)`, the collateralized foreign
discount factor is `D_for^dom(t) = F(0,t)·D_dom(t)/spot`, and the implied basis is its continuous zero
minus the foreign curve's own zero.

```typescript
export declare function impliedCrossCurrencyBasis(input: ImpliedCrossCurrencyBasisInput): ImpliedCrossCurrencyBasisResult;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (input).foreign: YieldCurve; default: not declared — Foreign index/OIS discount curve (pre-basis).
- (input).forwards: [string, number][]; default: not declared — Observed market FX forwards `[date, forward]` (domestic per foreign).
- (input).spot: number; default: not declared — FX spot: domestic units per 1 foreign unit.
- return.assumptions: { [k: string]: unknown; conventionsVersion: string; }; default: not declared — Applied conventions, echoed (Law 2 report grammar).
- return.assumptions.conventionsVersion: string; default: not declared
- return.basis: { date: string; spread: number; }[]; default: not declared — Implied continuous cross-currency basis spread at each forward date (collateralized zero − foreign zero).
- return.diagnostics: { warnings: QuantWarning[]; }; default: not declared — Structured warnings; always present (possibly empty).
- return.diagnostics.warnings: QuantWarning[]; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/fixed-income#oasAnalytics

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Market-calibrated option-adjusted-spread analytics for a callable/putable bond: the OAS, the Z-spread,
their difference (the embedded-**option cost**), and the **OAS-consistent** effective duration and
convexity (the curve shocked with the spread held fixed). Composes the same short-rate lattice as
{@link callableBond}. See `docs/specs/oas-analytics.md`.

```typescript
export declare function oasAnalytics(specification: OasAnalyticsSpecification): OasAnalyticsResult;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (specification): OasAnalyticsSpecification; default: not declared
- (specification).bond: Bond; default: not declared
- (specification).calls?: BondOption[]; default: not declared — Issuer call schedule (caps the bond's value at each strike).
- (specification).curve: YieldCurve; default: not declared — Calibration/discount curve (its reference date is the valuation date).
- (specification).durationShock?: number; default: not declared — Curve shock for the effective duration/convexity, in decimal. Default 1e-4 (1 bp).
- (specification).marketPrice: number; default: not declared — Market dirty price the OAS and Z-spread are solved to.
- (specification).meanReversion: number; default: not declared — Mean reversion and short-rate volatility for the tree model.
- (specification).model?: TreeModel; default: not declared — Tree model (default `hull-white`).
- (specification).puts?: BondOption[]; default: not declared — Holder put schedule (floors the bond's value at each strike).
- (specification).sigma: number; default: not declared
- (specification).spreadCurve?: YieldCurve; default: not declared — Optional term-structure spread curve added to `curve` before the spreads are solved. The effective
benchmark becomes `curve` + `spreadCurve` (continuous zeros add ⇔ discount factors multiply), so the
reported OAS and Z-spread are measured OVER a NON-FLAT benchmark — e.g. an OIS discount curve plus a
sector/rating spread curve — rather than the plain `curve`. Its zero rates ARE the spreads (build one
with `curves.fromZeroRates(spreadPillars)`); it must share `curve`'s reference date.
- (specification).stepsPerYear?: number; default: not declared — Tree steps per year (default 24, hard outer maximum 1,000,000; total-tree cap may be lower).
- return.assumptions: { conventionsVersion: string; dayCount: 'ACT/365F'; meanReversion: number; model: TreeModel; settlementDate: string; sigma: number; stepsPerYear: number; }; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.conventionsVersion: string; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.dayCount: 'ACT/365F'; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.meanReversion: number; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.model: TreeModel; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.settlementDate: string; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.sigma: number; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.stepsPerYear: number; default: not declared
- return.diagnostics: Diagnostics; default: not declared
- return.effectiveConvexity: number; default: not declared — OAS-consistent effective convexity.
- return.effectiveDuration: number; default: not declared — OAS-consistent effective duration (curve shocked ±`durationShock` at constant OAS).
- return.marketPrice: number; default: not declared
- return.modelPrice: number; default: not declared — The no-spread lattice model price (the gap `marketPrice − modelPrice` is what the OAS explains).
- return.oas: number; default: not declared — Parallel curve shift repricing the callable model to `marketPrice` (decimal; ×1e4 = bps).
- return.optionCost: number; default: not declared — `zSpread − oas` (decimal) — the embedded-option cost. Positive callable / negative putable.
- return.zSpread: number; default: not declared — Zero-volatility spread on the same lattice's straight leg (decimal).

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/fixed-income#shortRateTree

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Build a Hull-White / Black-Karasinski trinomial tree calibrated to `curve` via forward induction
(Hull's two-stage procedure). Stage 1 lays out a symmetric mean-reverting tree for the transformed
state `x`; stage 2 shifts each time slice by `α(t)` so the tree reprices every grid discount factor.
For Black-Karasinski the short rate is `exp(x)`, so `α` is solved numerically per step.

```typescript
export declare function shortRateTree(curve: YieldCurve, options: ShortRateTreeOptions): ShortRateTree;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (curve): YieldCurve; default: not declared
- (curve).addSpread: (spread: YieldCurve) => YieldCurve; default: not declared — Combine with a term-structure spread curve: the continuous zeros ADD at each tenor (equivalently
discount factors multiply, `D(t)·D_spread(t)`). Unions both curves' pillar tenors so the spread's
shape — not just a level — is preserved. Used to discount over `benchmark + spread` (e.g. OIS + a
sector/rating spread) while keeping curve construction out of leaf entrypoints.
- (curve).bumpPillar: (index: number, delta: number) => YieldCurve; default: not declared — Bump a single pillar's continuous zero by `delta` (key-rate risk).
- (curve).dayCount: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/fixed-income').FixedIncomeDayCount; default: not declared
- (curve).discount: (at: string | number) => number; default: not declared — Discount factor to a date or year fraction.
- (curve).extrapolation: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/fixed-income').CurveExtrapolation; default: not declared
- (curve).forwardRate: (from: string | number, to: string | number, dayCount?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/fixed-income').FixedIncomeDayCount) => number; default: not declared — Simple (money-market) forward rate between two times/dates under `dayCount`.
- (curve).instantaneousForward: (at: string | number) => number; default: not declared — Instantaneous (continuously-compounded) forward rate at a time/date.
- (curve).interpolation: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/fixed-income').CurveInterpolation; default: not declared
- (curve).pillars: readonly import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/fixed-income').CurvePillar[]; default: not declared
- (curve).referenceDate: string; default: not declared
- (curve).shift: (delta: number) => YieldCurve; default: not declared — Parallel shift of every pillar's continuous zero by `delta` (e.g. +0.0001 = +1bp).
- (curve).timeTo: (at: string | number) => number; default: not declared — Year fraction from the reference date to a date (or pass a number through unchanged).
- (curve).zeroRate: (at: string | number, compounding?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').InterestCompounding) => number; default: not declared — Zero rate to a date or year fraction, in the requested compounding (default continuous).
- (options): ShortRateTreeOptions; default: not declared
- (options).horizonYears: number; default: not declared — Tree horizonYears in years.
- (options).meanReversion: number; default: not declared
- (options).model: TreeModel; default: not declared — `hull-white` (Gaussian short rate) or `black-karasinski` (lognormal short rate).
- (options).sigma: number; default: not declared
- (options).steps?: number; default: not declared — Number of time steps (default 50).
- return.discountBond: (maturity: number) => number; default: not declared — Tree-implied discount bond price `P(0, T)` for a maturity on the time grid (years).
- return.gridTimes: readonly number[]; default: not declared — Reference discount factors the tree was calibrated to, at each grid time.
- return.model: TreeModel; default: not declared
- return.reachAt: (stepIndex: number) => number; default: not declared — Half-width of reachable levels at step `i` (nodes span `[-reach, +reach]`).
- return.rollback: (terminalStep: number, terminal: (j: number) => number, atNode?: (i: number, j: number, continuation: number) => number) => number; default: not declared — Generic backward induction from `terminalStep` to the root. `terminal(j)` seeds the value at each
terminal node; at every earlier node the discounted expected continuation is passed to `atNode`,
which returns the node value (inject cashflows, apply call/exercise via min/max). Returns the root
value. The engine behind callable bonds and Bermudan swaptions.
- return.shortRate: (stepIndex: number, nodeIndex: number) => number; default: not declared — Short rate at tree node `(i, j)` (time step i, level j).
- return.stepOf: (years: number) => number; default: not declared — Map a year fraction to its grid step, validating it lands on the grid.
- return.steps: number; default: not declared
- return.timeStepYears: number; default: not declared

the simulator (martingale check) — the honesty signal for the whole exposure profile.

human-readable explanation of WHY that delegate was chosen (`engine` then names the delegate).
Absent when no auto-selection took place.
- return.diagnostics.converged?: boolean; default: not declared — Whether an iterative procedure converged. `false` means the value is not trustworthy.
- return.diagnostics.decomposition?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Named intermediate quantities the value decomposes into — a par spread's protection leg and
risky annuity, a forward variance's near/far legs. The H-series explain paths disclose their
arithmetic here so a caller can audit the ratio, not just receive it (3B.3).
- return.diagnostics.engine?: string; default: not declared — Pricing/solver engine name, e.g. `black-scholes-merton`.
- return.diagnostics.finiteDifferenceBumps?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Finite-difference engines: the ACTUAL bump sizes used for FD Greeks (spec P2.3) — adaptive
near the vol/time boundaries, so the caller can see exactly what was differenced.
Keys: `spotStep`, `volatilityStep`, `timeStepYears`, `rateStep`, and — extended Greeks only —
`dividendYieldStep`. Each is the actual step differenced, in the unit of the coordinate it
bumps. (This doc named the retired `hS`/`hSig`/`hT`/`hR`/`hQ` keys for one release after the
emit sites had moved to the semantic names, so a caller following it read `undefined`.)
- return.diagnostics.iterations?: number; default: not declared — Iteration count for iterative methods.
- return.diagnostics.method?: string; default: not declared — Numerical method, e.g. `closed-form`, `brent`, `finite-difference`.
- return.diagnostics.repricingError: number; default: not declared
- return.diagnostics.selection?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing').SelectionReport; default: not declared — The structured engine-selection report (Gate C, `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing`): who was selected,
why, and — for automatic selection — every candidate considered with its verdict. This is the
machine-readable superset of `engine` + `autoReason` (which remain for compatibility);
`selected.name` always agrees with `engine` when both are present.
- return.diagnostics.timingMs?: number; default: not declared — Wall-clock timing in milliseconds, when measured.
- return.diagnostics.warmup?: number; default: not declared — Series facades: number of leading output slots that are warmup sentinels (null/NaN) while the
computation seeds. Equals the input length when the indicator never emitted.
- return.diagnostics.warnings: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').QuantWarning[]; default: not declared — Structured warnings; always present (possibly empty).
- return.dva: number; default: not declared
- return.exposure: ExposurePoint[]; default: not declared — The exposure profile across the measurement dates.
- return.fva: number; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/fixed-income#zeroCouponInflationSwap

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

A **zero-coupon inflation swap** (ZCIS) — the standard inflation-market instrument. At maturity the
inflation leg pays `I(T)/I(0) − 1` and the fixed leg pays `(1+K)^N − 1`; the par rate `K` is set so the
two match, i.e. `(1+K)^N = I(T)/I(0)`, so the par ZCIS rate **is** the geometric breakeven inflation.
Supply the market rate or the forward index ratio (each implies the other); supply a `contractRate` to
mark an existing position: `MTM = ±notional·DF·[(1+parRate)^N − (1+contractRate)^N]`. Deterministic
(forward-measure) — no inflation-vol model. See `docs/specs/inflation.md`.

```typescript
export declare function zeroCouponInflationSwap(input: ZeroCouponInflationSwapInput): ZeroCouponInflationSwapResult;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (input): ZeroCouponInflationSwapInput; default: not declared
- (input).contractRate?: number; default: not declared — An existing position's contracted fixed rate `K_c` — supply to value the swap (MTM).
- (input).discountFactor?: number; default: not declared — Discount factor to maturity for the MTM (default `1` → the undiscounted at-maturity value).
- (input).forwardIndexRatio?: number; default: not declared — The forward index ratio `I(T)/I(0)`. Supply **this or** `swapRate` — exactly one. Implies
`swapRate = forwardIndexRatio^(1/N) − 1`.
- (input).maturityYears: number; default: not declared — Swap maturity in years (`N`). The single ZCIS cashflow is exchanged at maturity.
- (input).notional?: number; default: not declared — Notional (default `1`).
- (input).payer?: 'fixed' | 'inflation'; default: not declared — Which leg the holder **pays** (default `'fixed'` = pay fixed, receive inflation). Signs the MTM.
- (input).swapRate?: number; default: not declared — The par/market ZCIS rate `K` (the geometric annual breakeven). Supply **this or**
`forwardIndexRatio` — exactly one.
- return.assumptions: { conventionsVersion: string; method: 'zero-coupon-inflation-swap'; }; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.conventionsVersion: string; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.method: 'zero-coupon-inflation-swap'; default: not declared
- return.diagnostics: Diagnostics; default: not declared
- return.fixedLeg: number; default: not declared — The single fixed-leg payoff per unit notional at maturity: `(1 + parRate)^N − 1`. Equals the
expected inflation-leg payoff (they match at par).
- return.forwardIndexRatio: number; default: not declared — Forward index ratio `I(T)/I(0) = (1 + parRate)^N`.
- return.markToMarket: number | null; default: not declared — Mark-to-market PV of a position at `contractRate` (present only when `contractRate` is supplied):
`±notional·DF·[(1+parRate)^N − (1+contractRate)^N]`, signed by `payer`. `null` otherwise.
- return.parRate: number; default: not declared — Par ZCIS rate (geometric annual breakeven): `forwardIndexRatio^(1/N) − 1`.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/fixed-income/artifacts#CurveFittedModelReport

Kind: type; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

The typed report every curve verb reads and writes — the artifact's `result`, verbatim.

```typescript
/** The typed report every curve verb reads and writes — the artifact's `result`, verbatim. */
export type CurveFittedModelReport<F extends CurveModelFamily = CurveModelFamily> = Readonly<Record<string, unknown>> & {
    family: F;
    modelVersion: number;
    summary: FittedModelSummary;
    /** The bootstrap's result as its own data (restored exactly by the public constructors). */
    fit: FitOf<F>;
    /** The bootstrap's input, verbatim, with live curves as their data and referenced row sets as handles. */
    calibration: StoredCalibrationOf<F>;
    referencedData: Record<string, TableHandle>;
    assumptions: {
        conventionsVersion: string;
        family: F;
        modelVersion: number;
        calibrator: string;
        evaluator: string | null;
        inputPolicy: 'embedded' | 'referenced';
        /** The curve's currency — a stored curve without a unit is a number without one. */
        currency: string;
        projection: string;
    };
    diagnostics: {
        warnings: QuantWarning[];
        fitWarningCount: number;
        embeddedCalibrationBytes: number;
        referencedRowSets: string[];
    };
};
```

- artifact.conventionsVersion: string; default: not declared — The library conventions revision the artifact was CREATED under — stamped from core's

- artifact.inputs.inputsHash: string; default: not declared — Hash of everything replay needs: `{ snapshotHash, parameters }` — stamped, not caller-set,
and RECOMPUTED from the stored fields on every validation pass (create and read), so a
tampered hash or tampered inputs are refused even when the outer id was re-minted to match.
- artifact.inputs.parameters?: unknown; default: not declared — The small, JSON-safe call parameters, embedded verbatim. Reference big inputs via tables.
- artifact.inputs.snapshotHash?: string; default: not declared — `marketSnapshotContentHash(...)` of the snapshot the analysis read, when one was used.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/fixed-income/artifacts#ZeroRateAtOrigin

Kind: type; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

How a curve answers `zeroRate(referenceDate)` when a pillar sits ON the reference date:
`'quoted'` echoes that pillar's zero (curves built from zero rates, whose t = 0 pillar is a
rate the caller supplied); `'limit'` takes the first segment's t → 0⁺ limit under the curve's
interpolation (bootstrapped and discount-factor curves, whose origin pillar is the `DF = 1`
anchor with a placeholder zero). The two build identical discount functions; the distinction
is stored so a restored curve answers exactly as the live one did.

```typescript
/**
 * How a curve answers `zeroRate(referenceDate)` when a pillar sits ON the reference date:
 * `'quoted'` echoes that pillar's zero (curves built from zero rates, whose t = 0 pillar is a
 * rate the caller supplied); `'limit'` takes the first segment's t → 0⁺ limit under the curve's
 * interpolation (bootstrapped and discount-factor curves, whose origin pillar is the `DF = 1`
 * anchor with a placeholder zero). The two build identical discount functions; the distinction
 * is stored so a restored curve answers exactly as the live one did.
 */
export type ZeroRateAtOrigin = 'quoted' | 'limit';
```

```typescript
export declare function replayFittedModel(input: { artifact: unknown; migrations?: ArtifactMigrationRegistry; referencedData?: Record<string, unknown[]>; libraryVersion?: string; limits?: ComparisonLimits; }): FittedModelReplay;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (input): { artifact: unknown; migrations?: ArtifactMigrationRegistry; referencedData?: Record<string, unknown[]>; libraryVersion?: string; limits?: ComparisonLimits; }; default: not declared
- (input).artifact: unknown; default: not declared — The artifact as held OR as restored from JSON (`fromCanonicalJson`) — validated at runtime, never trusted by declaration.
- (input).libraryVersion?: string; default: not declared
- (input).limits?: ComparisonLimits; default: not declared

- (input).referencedData?: Record<string, unknown[]>; default: not declared
- return.artifactId: string; default: not declared
- return.assumptions: { conventionsVersion: string; family: CurveModelFamily; modelVersion: number; calibrator: string; libraryVersion: { saved: string | null; current: string | null; }; referencedRowSets: string[]; }; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.calibrator: string; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/fixed-income/credit#CdsParSpreadAssumptions

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

The conventions `cdsParSpread.explain` echoes (FI day-count vocabulary — wider than core's
`Assumptions` enum, so the facade construction below carries the same type-level-only cast as
`bondFacade`; the runtime shape is exactly the core envelope).

```typescript
/**
 * The par (breakeven) CDS spread: protection leg / risky annuity. Facade (H02): the plain call
 * returns the scalar; `.explain()` discloses the leg decomposition and every applied convention.
 */
/** The conventions `cdsParSpread.explain` echoes (FI day-count vocabulary — wider than core's
 *  `Assumptions` enum, so the facade construction below carries the same type-level-only cast as
 *  `bondFacade`; the runtime shape is exactly the core envelope). */
export interface CdsParSpreadAssumptions {
    conventionsVersion: string;
    effectiveDate: string;
    maturityDate: string;
    recovery: number;
    notional: number;
    frequency: Frequency;
    dayCount: FixedIncomeDayCount;
    accrualOnDefault: boolean;
    protectionSteps: number;
}
```

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/fixed-income/pricer#BondDiscountCurvePriceResult

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

The complete direct `priceMultiCurve` result plus Gate C's scalar value and adapter disclosures.

```typescript
/**
 * The complete direct `priceMultiCurve` result plus Gate C's scalar value and adapter disclosures.
 */
export interface BondDiscountCurvePriceResult {
    value: number;
    dirtyPrice: number;
    cleanPrice: number;
    accruedInterest: number;
    assumptions: BondDiscountCurvePricerAssumptions;
    diagnostics: Diagnostics;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- accruedInterest: number; default: not declared
- assumptions: BondDiscountCurvePricerAssumptions; default: not declared
- assumptions.asOf?: number; default: not declared
- assumptions.businessDayConvention: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/fixed-income').BusinessDayConvention; default: not declared — Business-day convention baked into the payment schedule.
- assumptions.calendar?: string; default: not declared
- assumptions.calendarVersion?: string; default: not declared
- assumptions.compounding: 'curve' | 'actuarial'; default: not declared — `actuarial` for yield-based results; `curve` when discounted off a {@link YieldCurve}.
- assumptions.conventionsVersion: string; default: not declared
- assumptions.currency: string; default: not declared
- assumptions.curveId: string; default: not declared
- assumptions.curveReferenceDate: string; default: not declared — The stored curve anchor, preserved exactly rather than silently rolled to valuation time.
- assumptions.dayCount: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/fixed-income').FixedIncomeDayCount; default: not declared
- assumptions.dividendModel?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').DividendModel; default: not declared
- assumptions.engine?: string; default: not declared
- assumptions.expiryConvention?: 'us-equity-close' | 'explicit-instant'; default: not declared — How the contract's expiry label was resolved to an instant: `'us-equity-close'` when a
date-only `YYYY-MM-DD` expiry resolved to the US equity/options close — 16:00 America/New_York,
or 13:00 on an early-close day;
`'explicit-instant'` when the caller supplied a zoned datetime. Named so the convention is
never silent (alignment spec P1.6); instrument builders own the full story in Phase 3.
- assumptions.extrapolation: CurveExtrapolation; default: not declared
- assumptions.frequency: number; default: not declared — Coupon payments per year actually used in discounting.
- assumptions.interpolation: CurveInterpolation; default: not declared
- assumptions.model?: string; default: not declared
- assumptions.priceType: 'clean' | 'dirty'; default: not declared — The clean/dirty quote selected as the adapter's numeric `value`.
- assumptions.seed?: number; default: not declared — The randomness seed this result was computed under — REQUIRED echo for a
`randomness: 'seeded'` Pricer (Gate C, 2026-08-23): a stochastic result that does not name
its seed cannot be replayed from the result alone. Deterministic paths never set it.
- assumptions.settlementDate: string; default: not declared — Settlement date the result was computed as of.
- assumptions.settlementDateProjection: 'UTC calendar date containing valuationInstant'; default: not declared
- assumptions.timeToExpiryConvention?: never; default: not declared
- assumptions.timeToExpiryYears?: number; default: not declared
- assumptions.units?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').GreekUnits; default: not declared
- assumptions.units.rho: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').RhoUnit; default: not declared
- assumptions.units.theta: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').ThetaUnit; default: not declared
- assumptions.units.vega: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').VegaUnit; default: not declared
- assumptions.valuationInstant: number; default: not declared — Resolved epoch milliseconds consumed from the valuation-instant observation.
- cleanPrice: number; default: not declared
- diagnostics: Diagnostics; default: not declared
- diagnostics.autoReason?: string; default: not declared — When a meta-engine (e.g. `engines.auto()`) selected a delegate, this is a one-sentence,
human-readable explanation of WHY that delegate was chosen (`engine` then names the delegate).
Absent when no auto-selection took place.
- diagnostics.converged?: boolean; default: not declared — Whether an iterative procedure converged. `false` means the value is not trustworthy.
- diagnostics.decomposition?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Named intermediate quantities the value decomposes into — a par spread's protection leg and
risky annuity, a forward variance's near/far legs. The H-series explain paths disclose their
arithmetic here so a caller can audit the ratio, not just receive it (3B.3).
- diagnostics.engine?: string; default: not declared — Pricing/solver engine name, e.g. `black-scholes-merton`.
- diagnostics.finiteDifferenceBumps?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Finite-difference engines: the ACTUAL bump sizes used for FD Greeks (spec P2.3) — adaptive
near the vol/time boundaries, so the caller can see exactly what was differenced.
Keys: `spotStep`, `volatilityStep`, `timeStepYears`, `rateStep`, and — extended Greeks only —
`dividendYieldStep`. Each is the actual step differenced, in the unit of the coordinate it
bumps. (This doc named the retired `hS`/`hSig`/`hT`/`hR`/`hQ` keys for one release after the
emit sites had moved to the semantic names, so a caller following it read `undefined`.)
- diagnostics.iterations?: number; default: not declared — Iteration count for iterative methods.
- diagnostics.method?: string; default: not declared — Numerical method, e.g. `closed-form`, `brent`, `finite-difference`.
- diagnostics.selection?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing').SelectionReport; default: not declared — The structured engine-selection report (Gate C, `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing`): who was selected,
why, and — for automatic selection — every candidate considered with its verdict. This is the
machine-readable superset of `engine` + `autoReason` (which remain for compatibility);
`selected.name` always agrees with `engine` when both are present.
- diagnostics.selection.candidates?: readonly import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing').SelectionCandidate[]; default: not declared — Candidates an automatic selection considered; absent for explicit mode.
- diagnostics.selection.mode: 'explicit' | 'automatic'; default: not declared
- diagnostics.selection.reason: string; default: not declared — Why the selected engine answers this request.
- diagnostics.selection.selected: { name: string; version?: string; }; default: not declared
- diagnostics.selection.selected.name: string; default: not declared
- diagnostics.selection.selected.version?: string; default: not declared
- diagnostics.timingMs?: number; default: not declared — Wall-clock timing in milliseconds, when measured.
- diagnostics.warmup?: number; default: not declared — Series facades: number of leading output slots that are warmup sentinels (null/NaN) while the
computation seeds. Equals the input length when the indicator never emitted.
- diagnostics.warnings: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').QuantWarning[]; default: not declared — Structured warnings; always present (possibly empty).
- dirtyPrice: number; default: not declared
- value: number; default: not declared
