### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/foreign-exchange#CurrencyPairQuote

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

One foreign-exchange quote. `quotePerBase` is the price of ONE unit of `baseCurrency` expressed
in `quoteCurrency` — EUR/USD 1.08 is `{ baseCurrency: 'EUR', quoteCurrency: 'USD',
quotePerBase: 1.08 }`: one euro costs 1.08 dollars.

```typescript
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The pair contract and its guards
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
/**
 * One foreign-exchange quote. `quotePerBase` is the price of ONE unit of `baseCurrency` expressed
 * in `quoteCurrency` — EUR/USD 1.08 is `{ baseCurrency: 'EUR', quoteCurrency: 'USD',
 * quotePerBase: 1.08 }`: one euro costs 1.08 dollars.
 */
export interface CurrencyPairQuote {
    /** Uppercase three-letter ISO-style code of the currency being priced (ONE unit of this). */
    baseCurrency: string;
    /** Uppercase three-letter ISO-style code of the currency the price is expressed in. */
    quoteCurrency: string;
    /** Units of quote currency per ONE base unit; must be finite and > 0. */
    quotePerBase: number;
}
```

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/foreign-exchange#convertCurrency

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/foreign-exchange#coveredInterestParityForward

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

The no-arbitrage forward: `forward = spot × growthFactor(domestic) / growthFactor(foreign)`. The
DOMESTIC rate is the QUOTE currency's rate and the FOREIGN rate is the BASE currency's rate —
investing the converted amount at the domestic rate must equal investing one base unit at the
foreign rate and converting at this forward (the covered-interest-parity round trip, tested at
1e-12). Under continuous compounding this is exactly `spot × e^((domestic − foreign) × t)`.

```typescript
export declare function coveredInterestParityForward(input: CoveredInterestParityForwardInput): CoveredInterestParityForwardResult;
```

- (input).domesticAnnualRate: number; default: not declared — Annual rate (decimal) of the QUOTE currency — the 'domestic' leg (USD in EUR/USD).
- (input).foreignAnnualRate: number; default: not declared — Annual rate (decimal) of the BASE currency — the 'foreign' leg (EUR in EUR/USD).
- (input).spotRate: CurrencyPairQuote; default: not declared
- (input).timeYears: number; default: not declared
- return.assumptions: { compounding: InterestCompounding; rateRoles: 'domestic = quote currency, foreign = base currency'; timeYears: number; }; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.compounding: InterestCompounding; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.rateRoles: 'domestic = quote currency, foreign = base currency'; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.timeYears: number; default: not declared

- return.forwardRate: CurrencyPairQuote; default: not declared — The parity forward for the SAME pair as the spot quote.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/foreign-exchange#spotForwardHedgedProfitAndLoss

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

P&L of a base-currency position that hedged `hedgedFraction` of its notional at a forward. The
decomposition is exact and disclosed: the unhedged part rides the spot move
`(finalSpot − initialSpot)`, the hedged part locked `(forwardRateAtHedge − initialSpot)` the
moment the hedge was placed, and the total is their notional-weighted sum in the QUOTE currency.
`hedgedFraction: 0` is the pure spot P&L; `hedgedFraction: 1` is fully locked at the forward and
indifferent to the final spot. `forwardRateAtHedge` is REQUIRED whenever `hedgedFraction` > 0.

```typescript
export declare function spotForwardHedgedProfitAndLoss(input: SpotForwardHedgedProfitAndLossInput): SpotForwardHedgedProfitAndLossResult;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (input): SpotForwardHedgedProfitAndLossInput; default: not declared
- (input).finalSpotRate: CurrencyPairQuote; default: not declared — The spot at measurement, SAME pair, SAME direction.
- (input).forwardRateAtHedge?: CurrencyPairQuote; default: not declared — The forward locked when the hedge was placed. REQUIRED whenever `hedgedFraction` > 0.
- (input).hedgedFraction: number; default: not declared — Fraction of the notional hedged at the forward, in [0, 1].
- (input).initialSpotRate: CurrencyPairQuote; default: not declared — The spot when the position was opened.
- (input).notionalBaseAmount: number; default: not declared — Position size in BASE-currency units; positive = long the base currency, negative flips every sign.
- return.assumptions: { decomposition: typeof HEDGED_PROFIT_AND_LOSS_DECOMPOSITION; hedgedFraction: number; notionalDirection: string; }; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.decomposition: 'totalProfitAndLossInQuoteCurrency = (1 − hedgedFraction) × (finalSpotRate.quotePerBase − initialSpotRate.quotePerBase) × notionalBaseAmount + hedgedFraction × (forwardRateAtHedge.quotePerBase − initialSpotRate.quotePerBase) × notionalBaseAmount, every term in the quote currency'; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.hedgedFraction: number; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.notionalDirection: string; default: not declared — The fixed direction prose: positive notional is long the base; negative flips every sign.
- return.diagnostics: ForeignExchangeDiagnostics; default: not declared
- return.hedgedComponent: number; default: not declared — `hedgedFraction × (forwardRateAtHedge − initialSpot) × notional` — the part locked at the forward.
- return.totalProfitAndLossInQuoteCurrency: number; default: not declared
- return.unhedgedComponent: number; default: not declared — `(1 − hedgedFraction) × (finalSpot − initialSpot) × notional` — the part left floating.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/fundamentals#AnalyzeFundamentalsInput

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Input for {@link analyzeFundamentals}.

```typescript
/** Input for {@link analyzeFundamentals}. */
export interface AnalyzeFundamentalsInput {
    /** The reported history (restatements included) — the analysis sees only what `asOf` allows. */
    statements: readonly FinancialStatements[];
    /** The market side for valuation multiples; without it they are reported missing, not guessed. */
    marketSnapshot?: MarketObservation;
    asOf: EpochMs;
    restatementPolicy: RestatementPolicy;
    /** Day metrics need the explicit period-day count; absent → they are reported missing. */
    periodDays?: number;
    /** Bounds market-observation staleness for the multiples when supplied. */
    maximumStalenessMs?: number;
    /** Explicit tax rate for return on invested capital; else the effective rate is derived. */
    taxRate?: number;
    /** The exact debt-service denominator; absent → debtServiceCoverage is reported missing. */
    debtServiceAmount?: number;
    /** Separately supplied non-operating assets for enterprise value. */
    nonOperatingAssets?: number;
    /** Runs the Altman Z-score under this explicit published variant; absent → reported missing. */
    altmanVariant?: AltmanVariant;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- altmanVariant?: AltmanVariant; default: not declared — Runs the Altman Z-score under this explicit published variant; absent → reported missing.
- asOf: number; default: not declared
- debtServiceAmount?: number; default: not declared — The exact debt-service denominator; absent → debtServiceCoverage is reported missing.
- marketSnapshot?: MarketObservation; default: not declared — The market side for valuation multiples; without it they are reported missing, not guessed.
- marketSnapshot.marketCapitalization?: number; default: not declared
- marketSnapshot.observedTimestampMs: number; default: not declared — When the price was observed (epoch ms). Must not precede the fundamentals' availability.
- marketSnapshot.sharePrice: number; default: not declared
- marketSnapshot.sharesOutstanding?: number; default: not declared — Split-adjusted shares consistent with `sharePrice`.
- maximumStalenessMs?: number; default: not declared — Bounds market-observation staleness for the multiples when supplied.
- nonOperatingAssets?: number; default: not declared — Separately supplied non-operating assets for enterprise value.
- periodDays?: number; default: not declared — Day metrics need the explicit period-day count; absent → they are reported missing.
- restatementPolicy: RestatementPolicy; default: not declared
- statements: readonly FinancialStatements[]; default: not declared — The reported history (restatements included) — the analysis sees only what `asOf` allows.
- taxRate?: number; default: not declared — Explicit tax rate for return on invested capital; else the effective rate is derived.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/fundamentals#AnalyzeFundamentalsResult

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Result of {@link analyzeFundamentals}.

```typescript
/** Result of {@link analyzeFundamentals}. */
export interface AnalyzeFundamentalsResult {
    assumptions: {
        asOf: EpochMs;
        restatementPolicy: RestatementPolicy;
        periodUsed: {
            periodEndDate: string;
            periodType: string;
            fiscalYear: number;
        };
        priorPeriodUsed?: {
            periodEndDate: string;
            periodType: string;
            fiscalYear: number;
        };
    };
    diagnostics: {
        /** One warning per metric that could not be formed (mirrors `missing`). */
        warnings: string[];
    };
    asOf: EpochMs;
    restatementPolicy: RestatementPolicy;
    /** How many statement sets were visible at `asOf` after restatement resolution. */
    periodsVisible: number;
    /** The period the single-period metrics used. */
    periodUsed: {
        periodEndDate: string;
        periodType: string;
        fiscalYear: number;
    };
    /** The prior period the average-balance metrics used, when one was visible. */
    priorPeriodUsed?: {
        periodEndDate: string;
        periodType: string;
        fiscalYear: number;
    };
    ratios: Record<string, AnalyzedRatio>;
    scores: {
        piotroski?: PiotroskiResult;
        altman?: AltmanResult;
        beneish?: BeneishResult;
    };
    /** Every metric that could not be formed, with its reason — the honest gaps ledger. */
    missing: Array<{
        metric: string;
        reason: string;
    }>;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- asOf: number; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/fundamentals#BalanceSheet

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

One reported balance sheet (balances at `period.periodEndDate`).

```typescript
/** One reported balance sheet (balances at `period.periodEndDate`). */
export interface BalanceSheet {
    period: FundamentalPeriod;
    cashAndCashEquivalents: number;
    shortTermInvestments?: number;
    accountsReceivable?: number;
    inventory?: number;
    currentAssets?: number;
    /** Net property, plant, and equipment. */
    propertyPlantEquipmentNet?: number;
    totalAssets: number;
    currentLiabilities?: number;
    accountsPayable?: number;
    /** Interest-bearing debt due within one year. */
    shortTermDebt?: number;
    /** Interest-bearing debt due beyond one year. */
    longTermDebt?: number;
    /**
     * Total interest-bearing debt. When absent and both maturities are present, consumers may derive
     * `shortTermDebt + longTermDebt` and say so; "debt" NEVER silently means total liabilities.
     */
    totalDebt?: number;
    totalLiabilities: number;
    preferredEquity?: number;
    minorityInterest?: number;
    totalEquity: number;
    retainedEarnings?: number;
    /** Source-specific extras, preserved verbatim and never consumed by compute functions. */
    metadata?: Record<string, unknown>;
}
```

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/fundamentals#FinancialStatements

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

The three statements of ONE period. The periods must agree on their identity — end date, type,
currency, and monetary scale — because every ratio that crosses statements assumes it; the set's
point-in-time availability is the LATEST of the three (a set is visible only when whole).

```typescript
/**
 * The three statements of ONE period. The periods must agree on their identity — end date, type,
 * currency, and monetary scale — because every ratio that crosses statements assumes it; the set's
 * point-in-time availability is the LATEST of the three (a set is visible only when whole).
 */
export interface FinancialStatements {
    income: IncomeStatement;
    balance: BalanceSheet;
    cashFlow: CashFlowStatement;
}
```

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/fundamentals#FundamentalGrowthResult

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Result of {@link fundamentalGrowth} — the one analysis report grammar.

```typescript
/** Result of {@link fundamentalGrowth} — the one analysis report grammar. */
export interface FundamentalGrowthResult {
    assumptions: {
        /** Elapsed time between period ends is an ACT/365F year fraction (a label, not a literal). */
        elapsedYearsBasis: string;
        observationCount: number;
    };
    diagnostics: {
        /** Every null growth's reason surfaces here too, so a reader scans one place. */
        warnings: string[];
    };
    /**
     * One row per adjacent pair: fractional growth `current / prior - 1`, or `null` with the reason
     * when the prior amount is zero or the pair crosses sign (a growth rate through zero has no
     * meaningful magnitude).
     */
    periodOverPeriod: Array<{
        fromPeriodEndDate: string;
        toPeriodEndDate: string;
        growth: number | null;
        reason?: string;
    }>;
    /**
     * Compound annual growth from the first to the last observation over the ACTUAL elapsed years
     * (ACT/365F between the period ends), or `null` with the reason when the endpoints make the
     * exponent meaningless (non-positive start, sign change, or zero elapsed time).
     */
    compoundAnnualGrowthRate: number | null;
    compoundAnnualGrowthReason?: string;
    elapsedYears: number;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- assumptions: { elapsedYearsBasis: string; observationCount: number; }; default: not declared
- assumptions.elapsedYearsBasis: string; default: not declared — Elapsed time between period ends is an ACT/365F year fraction (a label, not a literal).
- assumptions.observationCount: number; default: not declared
- compoundAnnualGrowthRate: number | null; default: not declared — Compound annual growth from the first to the last observation over the ACTUAL elapsed years
(ACT/365F between the period ends), or `null` with the reason when the endpoints make the
exponent meaningless (non-positive start, sign change, or zero elapsed time).
- compoundAnnualGrowthReason?: string; default: not declared
- diagnostics: { warnings: string[]; }; default: not declared
- diagnostics.warnings: string[]; default: not declared — Every null growth's reason surfaces here too, so a reader scans one place.
- elapsedYears: number; default: not declared
- periodOverPeriod: { fromPeriodEndDate: string; toPeriodEndDate: string; growth: number | null; reason?: string; }[]; default: not declared — One row per adjacent pair: fractional growth `current / prior - 1`, or `null` with the reason
when the prior amount is zero or the pair crosses sign (a growth rate through zero has no
meaningful magnitude).

```typescript
/** One reported fundamental period, point-in-time aware (FC0 — frozen). */
export interface FundamentalPeriod {
```

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/fundamentals#MarketObservation

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

The market side of a valuation multiple — a narrow structural view, not a market-data feed.
`marketCapitalization` may be given directly or derived as `sharePrice × sharesOutstanding`
(the derivation is disclosed).

UNITS: market amounts are ABSOLUTE currency, not the statements' `monetaryScale`. The kernel
converts statement amounts to absolute currency before a multiple divides, and discloses the
conversion — a thousands-scale filing must not shift every multiple by 1,000×.

```typescript
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Market observation (a ratio input this package owns)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
/**
 * The market side of a valuation multiple — a narrow structural view, not a market-data feed.
 * `marketCapitalization` may be given directly or derived as `sharePrice × sharesOutstanding`
 * (the derivation is disclosed).
 *
 * UNITS: market amounts are ABSOLUTE currency, not the statements' `monetaryScale`. The kernel
 * converts statement amounts to absolute currency before a multiple divides, and discloses the
 * conversion — a thousands-scale filing must not shift every multiple by 1,000×.
 */
export interface MarketObservation {
    /** When the price was observed (epoch ms). Must not precede the fundamentals' availability. */
    observedTimestampMs: EpochMs;
    sharePrice: number;
    /** Split-adjusted shares consistent with `sharePrice`. */
    sharesOutstanding?: number;
    marketCapitalization?: number;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- marketCapitalization?: number; default: not declared
- observedTimestampMs: number; default: not declared — When the price was observed (epoch ms). Must not precede the fundamentals' availability.
- sharePrice: number; default: not declared
- sharesOutstanding?: number; default: not declared — Split-adjusted shares consistent with `sharePrice`.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/fundamentals#PerShareFundamentalsResult

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Result of {@link perShareFundamentals}.

```typescript
/** Result of {@link perShareFundamentals}. */
export interface PerShareFundamentalsResult {
    assumptions: {
        splitFactorSincePeriod: number;
        dilutedSharesUsed: number;
        /** Per-share values are ABSOLUTE currency per share (amount × monetaryScale / shares). */
        unitBasis: 'absolute currency per share';
    };
    diagnostics: {
        warnings: string[];
    };
    /** Split-adjusted diluted shares actually used as the denominator. */
    dilutedSharesUsed: number;
    splitFactorSincePeriod: number;
    earningsPerShare: number;
    revenuePerShare: number;
    bookValuePerShare: number;
    /** `operatingCashFlow - capitalExpenditure` per share; `null` when capex is absent. */
    freeCashFlowPerShare: number | null;
    freeCashFlowPerShareReason?: string;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- assumptions: { dilutedSharesUsed: number; splitFactorSincePeriod: number; unitBasis: 'absolute currency per share'; }; default: not declared
- assumptions.dilutedSharesUsed: number; default: not declared
- assumptions.splitFactorSincePeriod: number; default: not declared
- assumptions.unitBasis: 'absolute currency per share'; default: not declared — Per-share values are ABSOLUTE currency per share (amount × monetaryScale / shares).
- bookValuePerShare: number; default: not declared
- diagnostics: { warnings: string[]; }; default: not declared
- diagnostics.warnings: string[]; default: not declared
- dilutedSharesUsed: number; default: not declared — Split-adjusted diluted shares actually used as the denominator.
- earningsPerShare: number; default: not declared
- freeCashFlowPerShare: number | null; default: not declared — `operatingCashFlow - capitalExpenditure` per share; `null` when capex is absent.
- freeCashFlowPerShareReason?: string; default: not declared
- revenuePerShare: number; default: not declared
- splitFactorSincePeriod: number; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/fundamentals#PiotroskiResult

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Result of {@link piotroskiFScore}.

```typescript
/** Result of {@link piotroskiFScore}. */
export interface PiotroskiResult {
    assumptions: {
        /** The published model name (a label, deliberately not a literal type). */
        model: string;
        /** Returns and turnover use BEGINNING total assets, per the paper. */
        returnBasis: 'beginning total assets';
    };
    diagnostics: {
        /** One warning per unevaluable signal. */
        warnings: string[];
    };
    /** Sum of the evaluable signals (each 0 or 1). */
    fScore: number;
    /** How many of the nine signals could be evaluated; 9 when every input line was present. */
    evaluableSignals: number;
    signals: PiotroskiSignal[];
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- assumptions: { model: string; returnBasis: 'beginning total assets'; }; default: not declared
- assumptions.model: string; default: not declared — The published model name (a label, deliberately not a literal type).
- assumptions.returnBasis: 'beginning total assets'; default: not declared — Returns and turnover use BEGINNING total assets, per the paper.
- diagnostics: { warnings: string[]; }; default: not declared
- diagnostics.warnings: string[]; default: not declared — One warning per unevaluable signal.
- evaluableSignals: number; default: not declared — How many of the nine signals could be evaluated; 9 when every input line was present.
- fScore: number; default: not declared — Sum of the evaluable signals (each 0 or 1).
- signals: PiotroskiSignal[]; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/fundamentals#PiotroskiSignal

```typescript
/** One of the nine binary signals. */
```

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/fundamentals#RatioFacade

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

A ratio head: plain value + `.explain`. The DECLARED input is the head's exact shape — the
declaration never licenses a key the runtime refuses (the shared bag stays kernel-internal).

```typescript
/**
 * A ratio head: plain value + `.explain`. The DECLARED input is the head's exact shape — the
 * declaration never licenses a key the runtime refuses (the shared bag stays kernel-internal).
 */
export interface RatioFacade<Input extends RatioInput = RatioInput> {
    (input: Input): number | null;
    explain(input: Input): RatioReport;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (input): Input; default: not declared
- explain: (input: Input) => RatioReport; default: not declared
- explain().return.assumptions: { category: RatioCategory; conventionsVersion: string; formula: string; period: RatioPeriodIdentity; priorPeriod?: RatioPeriodIdentity; ratioName: string; }; default: not declared
- explain().return.assumptions.category: RatioCategory; default: not declared
- explain().return.assumptions.conventionsVersion: string; default: not declared
- explain().return.assumptions.formula: string; default: not declared — The fixed formula, stated as prose (also in the generated reference documentation).
- explain().return.assumptions.period: RatioPeriodIdentity; default: not declared
- explain().return.assumptions.priorPeriod?: RatioPeriodIdentity; default: not declared
- explain().return.assumptions.ratioName: string; default: not declared
- explain().return.diagnostics: { denominator: { label: string; amount: number; } | null; marketStalenessMs?: number; notes: string[]; numerator: { label: string; amount: number; } | null; reason?: string; warnings: string[]; }; default: not declared
- explain().return.diagnostics.denominator: { amount: number; label: string; } | null; default: not declared
- explain().return.diagnostics.denominator.amount: number; default: not declared
- explain().return.diagnostics.denominator.label: string; default: not declared
- explain().return.diagnostics.marketStalenessMs?: number; default: not declared — For market multiples: how far the price sits after the fundamentals became available.
- explain().return.diagnostics.notes: string[]; default: not declared — Every derivation, omission, and convention the computation relied on.

- explain().return.diagnostics.numerator.amount: number; default: not declared
- explain().return.diagnostics.numerator.label: string; default: not declared
- explain().return.diagnostics.reason?: string; default: not declared — Present exactly when `value` is null.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/fundamentals#RatioInput

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Common inputs a ratio head can declare.

```typescript
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The maker
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
/** Common inputs a ratio head can declare. */
export interface RatioInput {
    /** Single-period heads. */
    statements?: FinancialStatements;
    /** Average-denominator heads: the period being measured… */
    current?: FinancialStatements;
    /** …and the immediately prior period (average balances need both endpoints). */
    prior?: FinancialStatements;
    /** Day-count heads: the explicit number of days in the period (never guessed from periodType). */
    periodDays?: number;
    /** Market-multiple heads. */
    marketObservation?: MarketObservation;
    /** Market-multiple heads: reject a price observed more than this after availability. */
    maximumStalenessMs?: number;
    /** ROIC: explicit tax rate; when absent the effective rate is derived and disclosed. */
    taxRate?: number;
    /** debtServiceCoverage: the exact debt-service denominator (interest + scheduled principal). */
    debtServiceAmount?: number;
    /** Enterprise-value heads: separately supplied non-operating assets. */
    nonOperatingAssets?: number;
}
```

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/fundamentals#RatioPeriodIdentity

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

The identity of the period a ratio was computed over.

```typescript
/** The identity of the period a ratio was computed over. */
export interface RatioPeriodIdentity {
    periodEndDate: string;
    periodType: string;
    fiscalYear: number;
    currency: string;
    monetaryScale: number;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- monetaryScale: number; default: not declared
- periodEndDate: string; default: not declared
- periodType: string; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/fundamentals#RatioReport

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

What `.explain()` returns for every ratio head — the ONE `Computed` envelope (dx §7.2).

```typescript
/** What `.explain()` returns for every ratio head — the ONE `Computed` envelope (dx §7.2). */
export interface RatioReport {
    /** A decimal ratio (never a displayed percentage), or `null` with `diagnostics.reason`. */
    value: number | null;
    assumptions: {
        conventionsVersion: string;
        ratioName: string;
        category: RatioCategory;
        /** The fixed formula, stated as prose (also in the generated reference documentation). */
        formula: string;
        period: RatioPeriodIdentity;
        priorPeriod?: RatioPeriodIdentity;
    };
    diagnostics: {
        warnings: string[];
        numerator: {
            label: string;
            amount: number;
        } | null;
        denominator: {
            label: string;
            amount: number;
        } | null;
        /** Every derivation, omission, and convention the computation relied on. */
        notes: string[];
        /** Present exactly when `value` is null. */
        reason?: string;
        /** For market multiples: how far the price sits after the fundamentals became available. */
        marketStalenessMs?: number;
    };
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- assumptions: { category: RatioCategory; conventionsVersion: string; formula: string; period: RatioPeriodIdentity; priorPeriod?: RatioPeriodIdentity; ratioName: string; }; default: not declared
- assumptions.category: RatioCategory; default: not declared
- assumptions.conventionsVersion: string; default: not declared
- assumptions.formula: string; default: not declared — The fixed formula, stated as prose (also in the generated reference documentation).
- assumptions.period: RatioPeriodIdentity; default: not declared
- assumptions.period.currency: string; default: not declared
- assumptions.period.fiscalYear: number; default: not declared
- assumptions.period.monetaryScale: number; default: not declared
- assumptions.period.periodEndDate: string; default: not declared
- assumptions.period.periodType: string; default: not declared
- assumptions.priorPeriod?: RatioPeriodIdentity; default: not declared
- assumptions.priorPeriod.currency: string; default: not declared
- assumptions.priorPeriod.fiscalYear: number; default: not declared
- assumptions.priorPeriod.monetaryScale: number; default: not declared
- assumptions.priorPeriod.periodEndDate: string; default: not declared
- assumptions.priorPeriod.periodType: string; default: not declared
- assumptions.ratioName: string; default: not declared
- diagnostics: { denominator: { label: string; amount: number; } | null; marketStalenessMs?: number; notes: string[]; numerator: { label: string; amount: number; } | null; reason?: string; warnings: string[]; }; default: not declared
- diagnostics.denominator: { amount: number; label: string; } | null; default: not declared
- diagnostics.denominator.amount: number; default: not declared
- diagnostics.denominator.label: string; default: not declared
- diagnostics.marketStalenessMs?: number; default: not declared — For market multiples: how far the price sits after the fundamentals became available.
- diagnostics.notes: string[]; default: not declared — Every derivation, omission, and convention the computation relied on.
- diagnostics.numerator: { amount: number; label: string; } | null; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/fundamentals#altmanZScore

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

The Altman Z-score with the published coefficients and denominator definitions per variant.
`X1` working capital / assets, `X2` retained earnings / assets, `X3` operating income / assets,
`X4` the variant's equity basis / total liabilities, `X5` sales / assets where the variant has
one. The variant is REQUIRED — there is no default bankruptcy model.

```typescript
export declare function altmanZScore(input: AltmanInput): AltmanResult;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (input): AltmanInput; default: not declared
- (input).marketEquity?: number; default: not declared — REQUIRED for `public-manufacturing` (its X4 uses market equity); rejected otherwise.
- (input).statements: FinancialStatements; default: not declared
- (input).variant: AltmanVariant; default: not declared
- return.assumptions: { equityBasis: 'market' | 'book'; model: string; variant: AltmanVariant; }; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.equityBasis: 'market' | 'book'; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.model: string; default: not declared — The published model name (a label, deliberately not a literal type).
- return.assumptions.variant: AltmanVariant; default: not declared
- return.components: AltmanComponent[]; default: not declared
- return.diagnostics: { warnings: string[]; }; default: not declared
- return.diagnostics.warnings: string[]; default: not declared
- return.variant: AltmanVariant; default: not declared
- return.zScore: number; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/fundamentals#analyzeFundamentals

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/fundamentals#beneishMScore

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

The original eight-variable 1999 Beneish equation
`-4.84 + 0.920 DSRI + 0.528 GMI + 0.404 AQI + 0.892 SGI + 0.115 DEPI - 0.172 SGAI + 4.679 TATA
- 0.327 LVGI`, with the component definitions fixed to the paper. Every variable the model needs
must be present in both periods — there is NO five-variable fallback, silent or otherwise.

```typescript
export declare function beneishMScore(input: BeneishInput): BeneishResult;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (input): BeneishInput; default: not declared
- (input).current: FinancialStatements; default: not declared
- (input).prior: FinancialStatements; default: not declared
- return.assumptions: { model: string; }; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.model: string; default: not declared — The published model name (a label, deliberately not a literal type).
- return.components: BeneishComponent[]; default: not declared
- return.diagnostics: { warnings: string[]; }; default: not declared
- return.diagnostics.warnings: string[]; default: not declared — Conventions the inputs forced (e.g. D&A standing in for pure depreciation) — disclosed.
- return.mScore: number; default: not declared
- return.notes: string[]; default: not declared — The same disclosures as `diagnostics.warnings` (kept for direct reading).

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/fundamentals#commonSizeFinancialStatements

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Common-size statements: every reported numeric line divided by its conventional base — income
and cash-flow lines by revenue, balance lines by total assets. Fractions, never display
percentages. A zero base is an error naming itself, not an Infinity.

```typescript

```

```typescript
export declare function fundamentalGrowth(input: FundamentalGrowthInput): FundamentalGrowthResult;
```

- return.elapsedYears: number; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/fundamentals#isPeriodAvailableAt

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Point-in-time eligibility: whether `period` was AVAILABLE to an observer at `asOf` (epoch ms).
`availableTimestampMs`, not `periodEndDate`, controls eligibility — a restatement is a NEW
version with its own availability and provenance, so a backtest never sees it early.

```typescript
export declare function isPeriodAvailableAt(period: FundamentalPeriod, asOf: EpochMs): boolean;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (asOf): number; default: not declared
- (period): FundamentalPeriod; default: not declared
- (period).accession?: string; default: not declared — Source accession identifier, when known.
- (period).availableTimestampMs: number; default: not declared — When the data became AVAILABLE to an observer — the point-in-time eligibility instant. A
backtest or event study must not see this period before this time; `periodEndDate` never
controls eligibility.
- (period).currency: string; default: not declared — ISO 4217 currency of the monetary figures.
- (period).filedTimestampMs?: number; default: not declared — When the filing was made, when known.
- (period).fiscalQuarter?: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4; default: not declared
- (period).fiscalYear: number; default: not declared
- (period).form?: string; default: not declared — Source form (e.g. `10-Q`), when known.
- (period).monetaryScale: 1 | 1000 | 1000000; default: not declared — Monetary figures are reported in units of this scale.
- (period).periodEndDate: string; default: not declared — Strict `YYYY-MM-DD` calendar date the period ends on.
- (period).periodStartDate?: string; default: not declared — Strict `YYYY-MM-DD` calendar date; optional because some sources report only period ends.
- (period).periodType: 'quarter' | 'year' | 'trailing-twelve-months'; default: not declared
- (period).restatementOf?: string; default: not declared — When this record restates an earlier one, the accession (or identifier) it restates.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/fundamentals#perShareFundamentals

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Split-aware per-share normalization: the period's diluted shares are multiplied by the supplied
cumulative split factor so a pre-split period and a post-split observer meet on one basis. The
factor and the shares used are echoed; shares absent or non-positive is an error, never a NaN.


2-for-1 split since the period end). Default `1` — no split; the factor used is echoed.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/fundamentals#piotroskiFScore

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

The standard nine binary signals, per the paper: profitability (return on beginning assets,
operating cash flow, their improvement, accruals), leverage/liquidity/funding (falling
long-term-debt ratio, improving current ratio, no net share issuance), and efficiency
(improving gross margin, improving beginning-assets turnover). Each signal is reported, not
only the total; a signal whose statement line is absent reports `null` with the reason and is
excluded from `fScore` — never guessed to 0 or 1.

```typescript
export declare function piotroskiFScore(input: PiotroskiInput): PiotroskiResult;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (input): PiotroskiInput; default: not declared
- (input).current: FinancialStatements; default: not declared
- (input).prior: FinancialStatements; default: not declared
- (input).priorPrior: FinancialStatements; default: not declared — The period before `prior`. Needed because the paper's return and turnover use BEGINNING
assets, so the prior year's own signal needs the balance sheet one further back.
- return.assumptions: { model: string; returnBasis: 'beginning total assets'; }; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.model: string; default: not declared — The published model name (a label, deliberately not a literal type).
- return.assumptions.returnBasis: 'beginning total assets'; default: not declared — Returns and turnover use BEGINNING total assets, per the paper.
- return.diagnostics: { warnings: string[]; }; default: not declared
- return.diagnostics.warnings: string[]; default: not declared — One warning per unevaluable signal.
- return.evaluableSignals: number; default: not declared — How many of the nine signals could be evaluated; 9 when every input line was present.
- return.fScore: number; default: not declared — Sum of the evaluable signals (each 0 or 1).
- return.signals: PiotroskiSignal[]; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/fundamentals#requireFundamentalPeriod

Validate a {@link FundamentalPeriod} at a public boundary (Law 12 closed request): presence,

```typescript
export declare function requireFundamentalPeriod(functionName: string, period: FundamentalPeriod): asserts period is FundamentalPeriod;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (period).monetaryScale: 1 | 1000 | 1000000; default: not declared — Monetary figures are reported in units of this scale.

- (period).periodStartDate?: string; default: not declared — Strict `YYYY-MM-DD` calendar date; optional because some sources report only period ends.
- (period).periodType: 'quarter' | 'year' | 'trailing-twelve-months'; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/fundamentals#selectFundamentalSnapshot

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

The point-in-time view of a series: availability-gated by `statementsAvailableTimestampMs` (never
by period end), then resolved to ONE version per (periodType, periodEndDate) under the stated
restatement policy — `'latest-available'` takes the newest visible version, `'first-reported'`
takes the original filing and ignores restatements entirely.

```typescript
export declare function selectFundamentalSnapshot(input: SelectFundamentalSnapshotInput): FundamentalSnapshot;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (input): SelectFundamentalSnapshotInput; default: not declared
- (input).asOf: number; default: not declared — The observation instant (epoch ms). Only sets whose availability is at or before it qualify.
- (input).restatementPolicy: RestatementPolicy; default: not declared — How multiple visible versions of one period resolve.
- (input).series: FundamentalSeries; default: not declared
- return.asOf: number; default: not declared
- return.entity?: string; default: not declared
- return.restatementPolicy: RestatementPolicy; default: not declared
- return.statements: readonly FinancialStatements[]; default: not declared — One resolved version per (periodType, periodEndDate), period end ascending.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/fundamentals#statementsAvailableTimestampMs

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

The point-in-time availability of a statement SET: the latest of the three statements'
`availableTimestampMs` — a set is visible only when every statement in it is. The set is
validated IN FULL: a helper that answers an eligibility instant from a malformed set would
smuggle that malformation into every point-in-time decision built on it.

```typescript
export declare function statementsAvailableTimestampMs(statements: FinancialStatements): number;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (statements): FinancialStatements; default: not declared
- (statements).balance: BalanceSheet; default: not declared
- (statements).cashFlow: CashFlowStatement; default: not declared
- (statements).income: IncomeStatement; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/fundamentals#trailingTwelveMonthStatements

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Compose four consecutive fiscal quarters into one trailing-twelve-months set: income and
cash-flow FLOWS sum; BALANCES are the latest quarter's (a balance is a point, not a flow);
`dilutedSharesOutstanding` is the four-quarter arithmetic mean (disclosed convention). The
quarter chain is verified — a gap or an overlap is an error naming the break, never a silent
annualization.

```typescript
export declare function trailingTwelveMonthStatements(input: TrailingTwelveMonthInput): FinancialStatements;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (input): TrailingTwelveMonthInput; default: not declared
- (input).statements: readonly FinancialStatements[]; default: not declared — Exactly four consecutive fiscal quarters, period end ascending.
- return.balance: BalanceSheet; default: not declared
- return.cashFlow: CashFlowStatement; default: not declared
- return.income: IncomeStatement; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/http#LocalHttpServer

Kind: interface; stability: preview (pre-1.0).

```typescript
export interface LocalHttpServer {
    document: OpenApiDocument;
    /** The bound address once started (`null` before `start()` / after `stop()`). */
    address(): {
        host: string;
        port: number;
        url: string;
    } | null;
    /** Bind and listen; resolves with the bound address (port 0 picks a free port). */
    start(): Promise<{
        host: string;
        port: number;
        url: string;
    }>;
    stop(): Promise<void>;
}
```

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/http#LocalHttpServerBudgets

```typescript
export interface LocalHttpServerBudgets {
    /** The wire byte budget (default 65,536; maximum 16,777,216). */

    deadlineMs?: number;

}
```

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/http#LocalHttpServerInput

Kind: interface; stability: preview (pre-1.0).

```typescript
export interface LocalHttpServerInput {
    registry: OperationRegistry;
    /** Handles resolve through this store; a writable store also receives spilled results. */
    artifacts?: ArtifactStoreReader | ArtifactStore;
    /** The server's capability ceiling (default the runtime's defaults). Writes also need the bearer credential. */
    capabilities?: readonly string[];
    /** Server-owned bearer credential, at least 32 cryptographically random characters (e.g. randomBytes(32).toString('hex')). Required for enabled write operations, including trade:approve. Never returned by discovery. Read-only analytics remain public; job submission/cancellation always require this token. */
    authenticationToken?: string;
    /** The trade lifecycle's stores (Decision 10). */
    stores?: {
        authorization?: AuthorizationStore;
        journal?: ExecutionJournalStore;
    };
    /** The job runner (`@insiderfinance/totalfinance/workflows/local`'s or another implementation of the contract). */
    jobs?: JobRunner;
    host?: string;
    port?: number;
    /** Binding anything but loopback needs this flag and your own network/TLS boundary; reads remain unauthenticated. */
    allowNonLoopback?: boolean;
    budgets?: LocalHttpServerBudgets;
    /** The caller's clock (ISO instants for spilled results and job transitions); default `Date`. */
    clock?: () => string;
}
```

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/math#AdaptiveSimpsonOptions

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

```typescript
export interface AdaptiveSimpsonOptions {
    tolerance?: number;
    maxDepth?: number;
    /**
     * Maximum integrand evaluations before stopping with `converged: false`. Default 100,000.
     *
     * `maxDepth` bounds the DEPTH of a binary subdivision, so it bounds the work at 2^depth — the
     * default of 50 therefore permits about 10^15 evaluations, which is a budget in name only. This is
     * the bound that actually holds.
     */
    maxEvaluations?: number;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- maxDepth?: number; default: not declared
- maxEvaluations?: number; default: not declared — Maximum integrand evaluations before stopping with `converged: false`. Default 100,000.

`maxDepth` bounds the DEPTH of a binary subdivision, so it bounds the work at 2^depth — the
default of 50 therefore permits about 10^15 evaluations, which is a budget in name only. This is
the bound that actually holds.
- tolerance?: number; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/math#CovarianceEstimate

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

A well-conditioned covariance estimate plus its conditioning diagnostics.

```typescript
/** A well-conditioned covariance estimate plus its conditioning diagnostics. */
export interface CovarianceEstimate {
    /** The estimated covariance. */
    covariance: Matrix;
    /** The estimator actually used (`'auto'` resolves to one of these). */
    method: 'sample' | 'ledoit-wolf' | 'ridge' | 'ewma';
    /** Number of variables `p`. */
    variables: number;
    /** Number of observations `T`. */
    observations: number;
    /** Smallest eigenvalue of the returned covariance. */
    minEigenvalue: number;
    /** Largest eigenvalue of the returned covariance. */
    maxEigenvalue: number;
    /** `maxEigenvalue / minEigenvalue` (`Infinity` when singular). */
    conditionNumber: number;
    /** Whether the returned covariance is positive-definite (invertible). */
    isPositiveDefinite: boolean;
    /** Number of eigenvalues `> 1e-9 · maxEigenvalue` — the effective rank. */
    effectiveRank: number;
    /** Ledoit–Wolf shrinkage intensity, present when `method` is `'ledoit-wolf'`. */
    shrinkage?: number;
    /** The EWMA decay used — present only for method `'ewma'`. */
    lambda?: number;
    /** Kish effective sample size `1/Σwₜ²` — present only for method `'ewma'`. */
    effectiveObservations?: number;
    assumptions: {
        conventionsVersion: string;
        method: string;
        population: boolean;
        /** Single-index target only: the caller's observed market series vs the equal-weight proxy. */
        marketProxy?: 'observed-series' | 'equal-weight';
    };
    diagnostics: Diagnostics;
}
```

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/math#KalmanFilterResult

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Forward-pass (filter) output. All arrays are length `T`, aligned to the observation sequence.

```typescript
/** Forward-pass (filter) output. All arrays are length `T`, aligned to the observation sequence. */
export interface KalmanFilterResult {
    /** Filtered state means `x̂ₜ|ₜ` (`T × n`). */
    filteredStates: number[][];
    /** Filtered state covariances `Pₜ|ₜ`. */
    filteredCovariances: Matrix[];
    /** One-step predicted state means `x̂ₜ|ₜ₋₁` (`T × n`). */
    predictedStates: number[][];
    /** One-step predicted state covariances `Pₜ|ₜ₋₁`. */
    predictedCovariances: Matrix[];
    /** Innovations `zₜ − H·x̂ₜ|ₜ₋₁` (`null` at missing-observation steps). */
    innovations: (number[] | null)[];
    /** Innovation covariances `Sₜ = H·Pₜ|ₜ₋₁·Hᵀ + R` (`null` at missing steps). */
    innovationCovariances: (Matrix | null)[];
    /** Gaussian log-likelihood `Σₜ log N(zₜ; H·x̂ₜ|ₜ₋₁, Sₜ)`, summed over OBSERVED steps only. */
    logLikelihood: number;
    /** Number of steps that contributed to the likelihood (observed steps). */
    observedCount: number;
    /** State dimension. */
    stateDimension: number;
    /** Observation dimension. */
    observationDimension: number;
}
```

- logLikelihood: number; default: not declared — Gaussian log-likelihood `Σₜ log N(zₜ; H·x̂ₜ|ₜ₋₁, Sₜ)`, summed over OBSERVED steps only.
- observationDimension: number; default: not declared — Observation dimension.
- observedCount: number; default: not declared — Number of steps that contributed to the likelihood (observed steps).
- predictedCovariances: Matrix[]; default: not declared — One-step predicted state covariances `Pₜ|ₜ₋₁`.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/math#LedoitWolfOptions

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Options for {@link ledoitWolfShrinkage}.

```typescript
/** Options for {@link ledoitWolfShrinkage}. */
export interface LedoitWolfOptions {
    /**
     * Shrinkage target: `'identity'` (the scaled identity `μI`, the default and original),
     * `'constant-correlation'` (the Ledoit–Wolf 2004 target — each variable's own variance with the
     * **average** sample correlation on every off-diagonal, which fits correlated asset returns far better), or
     * `'single-index'` (the Ledoit–Wolf 2003 market-model target — a one-factor structure built from each
     * variable's covariance with the equal-weighted market, the best-specified target for stock returns).
     */
    target?: 'identity' | 'constant-correlation' | 'single-index';
    /**
     * Observed market return series (length `T`, chronological) for the `'single-index'` target.
     * When omitted the equal-weight cross-sectional average of `series` is used as the market proxy
     * (Ledoit–Wolf 2003's construction); {@link estimateCovariance} discloses which was used.
     */
    market?: ArrayLike<number>;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- market?: ArrayLike<number>; default: not declared — Observed market return series (length `T`, chronological) for the `'single-index'` target.
When omitted the equal-weight cross-sectional average of `series` is used as the market proxy
(Ledoit–Wolf 2003's construction); {@link estimateCovariance} discloses which was used.
- target?: 'identity' | 'constant-correlation' | 'single-index'; default: not declared — Shrinkage target: `'identity'` (the scaled identity `μI`, the default and original),
`'constant-correlation'` (the Ledoit–Wolf 2004 target — each variable's own variance with the
**average** sample correlation on every off-diagonal, which fits correlated asset returns far better), or
`'single-index'` (the Ledoit–Wolf 2003 market-model target — a one-factor structure built from each
variable's covariance with the equal-weighted market, the best-specified target for stock returns).

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/math#RandomNumberGeneratorState

Kind: type; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Serializable PRNG state — restore an RNG mid-stream with `restoreRandomNumberGenerator`.

A DISCRIMINATED UNION, because `algorithm: string` with `state: number[]` declared something the
runtime does not accept: every string was a legal algorithm and every length a legal state, while
the implementation admits exactly two algorithms and a fixed word count for each. A caller reading
the type could not tell that `{ algorithm: 'mt19937', state: [] }` is unusable, and the harness
could not either — it filed the refusal as a boundary that rejects valid input.

The state word counts are part of the contract, not an implementation note: mulberry32 carries one
32-bit word, xoshiro128** carries four. Tuple types state that, so the length check below is a
restatement of the declaration rather than a rule that lives only in the runtime.

```typescript
/**
 * Serializable PRNG state — restore an RNG mid-stream with `restoreRandomNumberGenerator`.
 *
 * A DISCRIMINATED UNION, because `algorithm: string` with `state: number[]` declared something the
 * runtime does not accept: every string was a legal algorithm and every length a legal state, while
 * the implementation admits exactly two algorithms and a fixed word count for each. A caller reading
 * the type could not tell that `{ algorithm: 'mt19937', state: [] }` is unusable, and the harness
 * could not either — it filed the refusal as a boundary that rejects valid input.
 *
 * The state word counts are part of the contract, not an implementation note: mulberry32 carries one
 * 32-bit word, xoshiro128** carries four. Tuple types state that, so the length check below is a
 * restatement of the declaration rather than a rule that lives only in the runtime.
 */
export type RandomNumberGeneratorState = {
    algorithm: 'mulberry32';
    state: [
        number
    ];
    seed: number;
} | {
    algorithm: 'xoshiro128ss';
    state: [
        number,
        number,
        number,
        number
    ];
    seed: number;
};
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- algorithm: ('mulberry32') | ('xoshiro128ss'); default: not declared
- seed: number; default: not declared
- state: ([number, number, number, number]) | ([number]); default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/math#adaptiveSimpsonSafe

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/math#augmentedDickeyFullerTest

Augmented Dickey–Fuller test for a unit root. Regresses `Δyₜ` on `y_{t−1}`, a constant (and a trend
for `'ct'`), and `lags` lagged differences; the statistic is the t-ratio on `y_{t−1}`. A very negative

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/math#engleGranger

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Engle–Granger two-step cointegration test. Step 1 regresses `y` on `x` (with intercept); step 2 runs
an ADF test on the residuals. Because the residuals are estimated, the decision uses the
residual-based Engle–Granger critical value (≈ −3.34 at 5% for one regressor), not the raw ADF table.

```typescript
export declare function engleGranger(dependent: number[], independent: number[]): EngleGrangerResult;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (dependent): number[]; default: not declared
- (independent): number[]; default: not declared
- return.alpha: number; default: not declared — Intercept of the cointegrating regression.
- return.beta: number; default: not declared — Slope of the cointegrating regression `y = α + β·x + resid`.
- return.cointegrated: boolean; default: not declared — `true` when the residual ADF statistic falls below the 5% Engle–Granger critical value.
- return.residualAugmentedDickeyFuller: TestResult; default: not declared — ADF test on the regression residuals (the cointegration test statistic).

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/math#estimateCovariance

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

The covariance-estimation front door: turn a returns matrix into a well-conditioned (usually
invertible) covariance and report its **conditioning** so a caller knows whether it is safe to invert.
`'sample'` and `'ewma'` are the raw estimators (never altered; flagged + `converged: false` when
singular); `'ledoit-wolf'` and `'ridge'` GUARANTEE an SPD result — degenerate/collinear inputs are
eigenvalue-floored with a `math.covariance_floored` warning rather than returned singular; `'auto'`
(default) uses the sample when it is SPD and well-conditioned, else shrinks (inheriting the SPD
guarantee). `series[k]` is variable
k's observations (p × T), matching {@link covarianceMatrix}. See `docs/specs/estimate-covariance.md`.

```typescript
export declare function estimateCovariance(series: number[][], options?: EstimateCovarianceOptions): CovarianceEstimate;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (options)?: EstimateCovarianceOptions; default: not declared
- (options).conditionThreshold?: number; default: not declared — Condition-number threshold above which `'auto'` shrinks rather than using the sample. Default 1e4.
- (options).halfLife?: number; default: not declared — EWMA half-life in periods (method `'ewma'`); `λ = 2^{−1/halfLife}` when `lambda` is omitted.
- (options).lambda?: number; default: not declared — EWMA decay `0 < λ < 1` (method `'ewma'`). Default 0.94 (RiskMetrics).
- (options).ledoitWolfTarget?: 'identity' | 'constant-correlation' | 'single-index'; default: not declared — Ledoit–Wolf shrinkage target when the method resolves to `'ledoit-wolf'` (explicitly or via `'auto'`).
`'identity'` (default), `'constant-correlation'` (fits correlated returns better), or `'single-index'`
(the market-model target, best-specified for stock returns).
- (options).market?: ArrayLike<number>; default: not declared — Observed market return series for the `'single-index'` target (length `T`). Omitted → the
equal-weight cross-sectional proxy is used and disclosed via `assumptions.marketProxy`.
- (options).method?: CovarianceMethod; default: not declared — Estimator; default `'auto'`.
- (options).population?: boolean; default: not declared — Population (`1/T`) vs sample (`1/(T−1)`) normalization. Default `true` (matches Ledoit–Wolf).
- (options).ridge?: number; default: not declared — Ridge diagonal load as a fraction of the average variance (method `'ridge'`). Default 0.1; > 0.
- (series): number[][]; default: not declared
- return.assumptions: { conventionsVersion: string; marketProxy?: 'observed-series' | 'equal-weight'; method: string; population: boolean; }; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.conventionsVersion: string; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.marketProxy?: 'observed-series' | 'equal-weight'; default: not declared — Single-index target only: the caller's observed market series vs the equal-weight proxy.
- return.assumptions.method: string; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.population: boolean; default: not declared
- return.conditionNumber: number; default: not declared — `maxEigenvalue / minEigenvalue` (`Infinity` when singular).
- return.covariance: Matrix; default: not declared — The estimated covariance.
- return.diagnostics: Diagnostics; default: not declared
- return.effectiveObservations?: number; default: not declared — Kish effective sample size `1/Σwₜ²` — present only for method `'ewma'`.
- return.effectiveRank: number; default: not declared — Number of eigenvalues `> 1e-9 · maxEigenvalue` — the effective rank.
- return.isPositiveDefinite: boolean; default: not declared — Whether the returned covariance is positive-definite (invertible).
- return.lambda?: number; default: not declared — The EWMA decay used — present only for method `'ewma'`.
- return.maxEigenvalue: number; default: not declared — Largest eigenvalue of the returned covariance.
- return.method: 'sample' | 'ledoit-wolf' | 'ridge' | 'ewma'; default: not declared — The estimator actually used (`'auto'` resolves to one of these).
- return.minEigenvalue: number; default: not declared — Smallest eigenvalue of the returned covariance.
- return.observations: number; default: not declared — Number of observations `T`.
- return.shrinkage?: number; default: not declared — Ledoit–Wolf shrinkage intensity, present when `method` is `'ledoit-wolf'`.
- return.variables: number; default: not declared — Number of variables `p`.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/math#gaussLegendreNodes

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Gauss–Legendre nodes and weights on `[-1, 1]` for `n` points, as a FRESH pair of arrays.

The rule is computed once per order and memoized, but the cached arrays are never handed out: a
caller who scaled the returned nodes in place (the obvious way to map them onto `[a, b]`) used to
corrupt the shared cache, and every later integral at that order — anywhere in the process —
silently integrated against the mutated rule. A copy per call costs `2n` doubles; the alternative
is a global that any caller can poison.

```typescript
export declare function gaussLegendreNodes(nodeCount: number): Quadrature;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (nodeCount): number; default: not declared
- return.nodes: number[]; default: not declared
- return.weights: number[]; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/math#hurstExponent

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Hurst exponent via rescaled-range (R/S) analysis. For a geometric progression of window sizes the
mean rescaled range `⟨R/S⟩ₙ` scales as `nᴴ`; `H` is the slope of `log⟨R/S⟩` on `log n`. R/S is
computed on the input series AS GIVEN, so the usual reading — `H ≈ 0.5` random walk, `H > 0.5`
persistence/trending, `H < 0.5` mean reversion — assumes an INCREMENT (returns) series. Passing an
integrated level series (e.g. a price path) instead yields `H ≈ 1`.

BIAS CAVEAT — read this before calling 0.55 "persistence". This is PLAIN R/S with no Anis–Lloyd
(1976) small-sample correction, and plain R/S is biased UPWARD at every finite sample size: for
independent data `E[R/S]ₙ` is not `n^0.5`, so the slope is not 0.5 either. Measured on this
implementation over 20 seeds of iid normal input (mean, and the spread across seeds):

  - `n = 512` → `H ≈ 0.565` (0.52 … 0.65)
  - `n = 4096` → `H ≈ 0.538` (0.48 … 0.59)
  - `n = 32768` → `H ≈ 0.534` (0.51 … 0.56)

The bias shrinks with `n` but is still ~0.03 at 32k points, and the seed-to-seed spread is wider
than the bias itself. So a lone `H = 0.55` on 4k observations is evidence of NOTHING. Compare
against a shuffled (or synthetic iid) version of your own series at the SAME length rather than
against the textbook 0.5, or use a corrected estimator. The ORDERING (anti-persistent < iid <
persistent, as the test suite asserts) is reliable; the absolute level is not.

```typescript
export declare function hurstExponent(series: number[]): number;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (series): number[]; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/math#jacobiEigen

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Symmetric eigendecomposition via cyclic Jacobi rotations. The tolerance is RELATIVE to the input's
off-diagonal Frobenius norm, so a matrix scaled by any constant converges identically (an absolute
tolerance would spin to `maximumIterations` on a large-scaled covariance matrix). Throws `ConvergenceError`
(`linalg.no_convergence`) if the sweeps do not reach the tolerance within `maximumIterations`.

The input must be SQUARE and finite. It used to be neither checked nor needed: every loop is
indexed by `input.length`, so a `2×3` matrix quietly returned the eigenvalues of its leading `2×2`
block — the right shape, the wrong matrix, and no way for the caller to tell. (Non-symmetric square
input is still accepted and still reports non-convergence through `ConvergenceError` when the
rotations cannot diagonalize it; use {@link eigenvalues} for the general case.)

```typescript
export declare function jacobiEigen(input: Matrix, options?: { maximumIterations?: number; tolerance?: number; }): EigenResult;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (input): Matrix; default: not declared
- (options)?: { maximumIterations?: number; tolerance?: number; }; default: not declared
- (options).maximumIterations?: number; default: not declared
- (options).tolerance?: number; default: not declared
- return.values: number[]; default: not declared — Eigenvalues (not sorted).
- return.vectors: Matrix; default: not declared — Eigenvectors as columns of the matrix.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/math#kalmanSmooth

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Rauch–Tung–Striebel fixed-interval smoother. Runs the forward filter, then a backward pass giving
`xₜ|T` / `Pₜ|T` — the state estimates conditioned on the WHOLE sample, always at least as sharp as
the filtered estimates. The backward gain is `Cₜ = Pₜ|ₜ·Fᵀ·(Pₜ₊₁|ₜ)⁻¹`, solved through the Cholesky
factor of the predicted covariance — or, when that covariance is singular because the model has a
deterministic component, through its pseudoinverse (see {@link rtsGain}).

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/math#ljungBox

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Ljung–Box portmanteau test for autocorrelation up to `lags`:
`Q = N(N+2) Σ_{k=1}^{h} ρ̂ₖ² / (N−k)`, distributed `χ²(h)` under the white-noise null. The p-value is
the exact chi-square survival function.

On ARMA RESIDUALS the white-noise null is the wrong reference: fitting `p + q` parameters to the
same data absorbs autocorrelation the statistic then fails to see, so `χ²(h)` is too conservative
and the test under-rejects. Pass `fittedParameterCount` to use the standard corrected reference
`χ²(h − p − q)` (Box–Jenkins); the returned `method` discloses the degrees of freedom actually
used. The statistic itself is unchanged — only the reference distribution moves.

```typescript
export declare function ljungBox(series: number[], lags: number, options?: LjungBoxOptions): TestResult;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (lags): number; default: not declared
- (options)?: LjungBoxOptions; default: not declared
- (options).fittedParameterCount?: number; default: not declared — Number of parameters ESTIMATED from the same series before the test (e.g. `p + q` for the
residuals of an ARMA(p, q) fit). The reference distribution loses one degree of freedom per
fitted parameter: `Q ~ χ²(lags − fittedParameterCount)`. Default 0 — the raw white-noise null,
which is the right reference only for a series that was NOT fitted.
- (series): number[]; default: not declared
- return.criticalValues?: { '1%': number; '10%': number; '5%': number; }; default: not declared — Asymptotic critical values at the 1% / 5% / 10% levels, when the test tabulates them.
- return.criticalValues.1%: number; default: not declared
- return.criticalValues.10%: number; default: not declared
- return.criticalValues.5%: number; default: not declared
- return.method: string; default: not declared — Human-readable identifier of the test and its configuration.
- return.pValue?: number; default: not declared — Approximate (or, for Ljung–Box, exact) p-value, when defined.
- return.statistic: number; default: not declared — The test statistic.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/math#mulberry32

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Mulberry32 — a small, fast, well-distributed seedable PRNG.

The state is seeded with `seed >>> 0` (the algorithm is 32-bit), but the ECHOED `seed` is the
caller's literal argument: a run seeded with `-1` is reproduced by passing `-1`, and reporting
`4294967295` back would send a reader looking for a seed they never used.

```typescript
export declare function mulberry32(seed: number): RandomNumberGenerator;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (seed): number; default: not declared
- return.getState: () => RandomNumberGeneratorState; default: not declared — Snapshot the current internal state for exact restoration.
- return.next: () => number; default: not declared — Uniform sample in [0, 1).
- return.seed: number; default: not declared — The seed this generator was created with (echoed for reproducibility).

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/math#nearestCorrelation

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

A valid correlation matrix near `matrix`: ONE eigenvalue-clipping pass to PSD ({@link nearestPsd}),
then a rescale to a unit diagonal.

Not the Frobenius-NEAREST correlation matrix. That is Higham's (2002) alternating-projections
problem, iterated to convergence between the PSD cone and the unit-diagonal set; the rescale here
is a single projection that can push the result slightly off the PSD cone again (the output is PSD
to within the rescale, not by construction). It is the standard cheap repair — good enough to make
a noisy correlation estimate usable for Cholesky/simulation — and it is deterministic and O(n³),
but a caller who needs the true minimizer needs Higham's iteration, not this.

```typescript
export declare function nearestCorrelation(matrix: Matrix): Matrix;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (matrix): Matrix; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/math#nearestPsd

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/math#qrSolve

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Least-squares solve of `A·x ≈ b` (`m ≥ n`) via QR back-substitution.

Rejects a rank-deficient (numerically singular) system rather than silently returning zeroed or
blown-up coefficients: if the smallest `|Rᵢᵢ|` pivot falls below `rcond × max|Rᵢᵢ|`, the columns
of `A` are collinear and the least-squares solution is not well defined (design law #4 — no silent
garbage). Raise `rcond` to reject more aggressively; lower it to admit borderline-conditioned fits.

```typescript
export declare function qrSolve(matrix: Matrix, b: number[], options?: { rcond?: number; }): number[];
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (b): number[]; default: not declared
- (matrix): Matrix; default: not declared
- (options)?: { rcond?: number; }; default: not declared
- (options).rcond?: number; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/math#ridder

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Ridder's method: exponential interpolation on a sign-changing bracket. Often beats bisection.

```typescript
export declare function ridder(objective: ScalarFunction, a0: number, b0: number, options?: SolverOptions): SolverResult;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (b0): number; default: not declared
- (objective): ScalarFunction; default: not declared
- (options)?: SolverOptions; default: not declared
- (options).maximumIterations?: number; default: not declared — Maximum iterations before reporting non-convergence.
- (options).residualTolerance?: number; default: not declared — Absolute tolerance on |f|. When `f` falls below this, the solve converges early.
- (options).stepTolerance?: number; default: not declared — Absolute tolerance on the x-step / bracket width.
- (options).tolerance?: number; default: not declared — Tolerance on the bracket width / x-step (alias for `stepTolerance`).
- return.bracket?: [number, number]; default: not declared — Final bracket `[lo, hi]` for bracketing methods, when one was established.
- return.converged: boolean; default: not declared — Whether the method actually converged to the requested tolerance.
- return.iterations: number; default: not declared — Iterations performed.
- return.method: string; default: not declared — The method that produced this result (e.g. `brent`, `newton`).
- return.reason?: SolverFailureReason; default: not declared — Machine-readable failure reason when `converged` is `false`.
- return.residual?: number; default: not declared — Residual |f(value)| at the returned estimate, when finite.
- return.value: number; default: not declared — Best estimate of the root. May be `NaN` when bracketing failed.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/math#studentT

Kind: value; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Student's t-distribution with `df` degrees of freedom (`df > 0`, need not be an integer).

```typescript
export declare const studentT: { readonly cdf: (x: number, degreesOfFreedom: number) => number; readonly inverseCdf: (probability: number, degreesOfFreedom: number) => number; readonly pdf: (x: number, degreesOfFreedom: number) => number; readonly survivalFunction: (x: number, degreesOfFreedom: number) => number; };
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- cdf: (x: number, degreesOfFreedom: number) => number; default: not declared — Cumulative distribution `F(x; ν)`. Uses `F(x) = 1 − ½·I_{ν/(ν+x²)}(ν/2, ½)` for `x > 0` and the
mirror image for `x < 0`; `F(0) = ½` exactly by symmetry.
- cdf(degreesOfFreedom): number; default: not declared
- cdf(x): number; default: not declared
- inverseCdf: (probability: number, degreesOfFreedom: number) => number; default: not declared — Quantile (inverse CDF). Returns `±Infinity` at the boundaries `p = 0` / `p = 1`.
- inverseCdf(degreesOfFreedom): number; default: not declared
- inverseCdf(probability): number; default: not declared
- pdf: (x: number, degreesOfFreedom: number) => number; default: not declared — Probability density `f(x; ν)`.
- pdf(degreesOfFreedom): number; default: not declared
- pdf(x): number; default: not declared
- survivalFunction: (x: number, degreesOfFreedom: number) => number; default: not declared — Survival function `1 − F(x; ν)` (equivalently `F(−x; ν)` by symmetry).
- survivalFunction(degreesOfFreedom): number; default: not declared
- survivalFunction(x): number; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/math/statistics#TrimmedMeanOptions

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

```typescript
export interface TrimmedMeanOptions extends StatisticsOptions {
    /**
     * Fraction dropped from EACH tail before averaging (default 0.1), in [0, 0.5]. At 0.5 nothing
     * but the middle remains and the result is the median; the same fallback applies whenever the
     * two trims would consume the whole sample.
     */
    fraction?: number;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- fraction?: number; default: not declared — Fraction dropped from EACH tail before averaging (default 0.1), in [0, 0.5]. At 0.5 nothing
but the middle remains and the result is the median; the same fallback applies whenever the
two trims would consume the whole sample.
- nanPolicy?: NanPolicy; default: not declared

```typescript
    contract: OptionContract;

}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- contract: OptionContract; default: not declared
- contract.adjusted?: boolean; default: not declared
- contract.currency?: string; default: not declared
- contract.deliverable?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Deliverable; default: not declared
- contract.deliverable.cash?: number; default: not declared
- contract.deliverable.notes?: string; default: not declared
- contract.deliverable.shares?: { symbol: string; quantity: number; }[]; default: not declared
- contract.exerciseTime?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').ExerciseTime; default: not declared — AM- or PM-settled — settlement/display metadata. It does NOT move `expiresAt`: the expiry

- contract.occSymbol?: string; default: not declared

- contract.strike: number; default: not declared
- contract.style: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').OptionStyle; default: not declared — REQUIRED at build — never defaulted: US equity options are American, many index options European.

- contract.underlying: string; default: not declared
- market: OptionMarket; default: not declared
- market.asOf: string | number; default: not declared — Snapshot time: epoch ms, `'YYYY-MM-DD'`, or a ZONED ISO datetime — one grammar for "when"
across every package. Each boundary resolves it once via core `resolveAsOf` (zone-less
