### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/options#AmericanExerciseResult

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

The American exercise analysis.

```typescript
/** The American exercise analysis. */
export interface AmericanExerciseResult {
    /**
     * Which leg was analysed — `'call'` or `'put'`.
     *
     * Named `optionType` because that is what it holds: in TotalFinance `style` is the EXERCISE style
     * (`'european' | 'american'`) everywhere else, and every one of these results is American by
     * construction, so a field called `style` reading `'put'` was a straight collision of two
     * vocabularies (pre-1.0 clean break, defect-fix wave, review-1).
     */
    optionType: 'call' | 'put';
    spot: number;
    /** American value (Barone–Adesi–Whaley). */
    american: number;
    /** European value (BSM) — the value stripped of the early-exercise right. */
    european: number;
    /** `american − european ≥ 0` — the dollars the early-exercise right adds. */
    earlyExercisePremium: number;
    /** `premium / american`. */
    premiumFractionOfValue: number;
    intrinsic: number;
    /** `american − intrinsic ≥ 0`. */
    timeValue: number;
    /** `false` for a non-dividend call (early exercise never optimal). */
    earlyExerciseCanBeOptimal: boolean;
    /** `S*(τ)` at the current maturity; `null` when early exercise is never optimal. */
    criticalSpot: number | null;
    /** The American value has collapsed to intrinsic — no time value left to give up. */
    shouldExerciseNow: boolean;
    /** Signed fraction of spot to the boundary (put: `(S−S*)/S`, call: `(S*−S)/S`); `null` if no boundary. */
    spotToBoundary: number | null;
    /** The `S*(τ)` curve over the remaining life (empty when never optimal). */
    boundary: BoundaryPoint[];
    /** Prose an agent relays. */
    rationale: string;
    assumptions: {
        conventionsVersion: string;
        valueEngine: 'barone-adesi-whaley';
        dividendModel: DividendModel;
        timeToExpiryYears: number;
    };
    diagnostics: Diagnostics;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- american: number; default: not declared — American value (Barone–Adesi–Whaley).
- assumptions: { conventionsVersion: string; dividendModel: DividendModel; timeToExpiryYears: number; valueEngine: 'barone-adesi-whaley'; }; default: not declared
- assumptions.conventionsVersion: string; default: not declared
- assumptions.dividendModel: DividendModel; default: not declared
- assumptions.timeToExpiryYears: number; default: not declared
- assumptions.valueEngine: 'barone-adesi-whaley'; default: not declared
- boundary: BoundaryPoint[]; default: not declared — The `S*(τ)` curve over the remaining life (empty when never optimal).
- criticalSpot: number | null; default: not declared — `S*(τ)` at the current maturity; `null` when early exercise is never optimal.
- diagnostics: Diagnostics; default: not declared
- diagnostics.autoReason?: string; default: not declared — When a meta-engine (e.g. `engines.auto()`) selected a delegate, this is a one-sentence,
human-readable explanation of WHY that delegate was chosen (`engine` then names the delegate).
Absent when no auto-selection took place.
- diagnostics.converged?: boolean; default: not declared — Whether an iterative procedure converged. `false` means the value is not trustworthy.
- diagnostics.decomposition?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Named intermediate quantities the value decomposes into — a par spread's protection leg and
risky annuity, a forward variance's near/far legs. The H-series explain paths disclose their
arithmetic here so a caller can audit the ratio, not just receive it (3B.3).
- diagnostics.engine?: string; default: not declared — Pricing/solver engine name, e.g. `black-scholes-merton`.
- diagnostics.finiteDifferenceBumps?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Finite-difference engines: the ACTUAL bump sizes used for FD Greeks (spec P2.3) — adaptive
near the vol/time boundaries, so the caller can see exactly what was differenced.
Keys: `spotStep`, `volatilityStep`, `timeStepYears`, `rateStep`, and — extended Greeks only —
`dividendYieldStep`. Each is the actual step differenced, in the unit of the coordinate it
bumps. (This doc named the retired `hS`/`hSig`/`hT`/`hR`/`hQ` keys for one release after the
emit sites had moved to the semantic names, so a caller following it read `undefined`.)
- diagnostics.iterations?: number; default: not declared — Iteration count for iterative methods.
- diagnostics.method?: string; default: not declared — Numerical method, e.g. `closed-form`, `brent`, `finite-difference`.
- diagnostics.selection?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing').SelectionReport; default: not declared — The structured engine-selection report (Gate C, `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing`): who was selected,
why, and — for automatic selection — every candidate considered with its verdict. This is the
machine-readable superset of `engine` + `autoReason` (which remain for compatibility);
`selected.name` always agrees with `engine` when both are present.
- diagnostics.selection.candidates?: readonly import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing').SelectionCandidate[]; default: not declared — Candidates an automatic selection considered; absent for explicit mode.
- diagnostics.selection.mode: 'explicit' | 'automatic'; default: not declared
- diagnostics.selection.reason: string; default: not declared — Why the selected engine answers this request.
- diagnostics.selection.selected: { name: string; version?: string; }; default: not declared
- diagnostics.selection.selected.name: string; default: not declared
- diagnostics.selection.selected.version?: string; default: not declared
- diagnostics.timingMs?: number; default: not declared — Wall-clock timing in milliseconds, when measured.
- diagnostics.warmup?: number; default: not declared — Series facades: number of leading output slots that are warmup sentinels (null/NaN) while the
computation seeds. Equals the input length when the indicator never emitted.
- diagnostics.warnings: QuantWarning[]; default: not declared — Structured warnings; always present (possibly empty).
- earlyExerciseCanBeOptimal: boolean; default: not declared — `false` for a non-dividend call (early exercise never optimal).
- earlyExercisePremium: number; default: not declared — `american − european ≥ 0` — the dollars the early-exercise right adds.
- european: number; default: not declared — European value (BSM) — the value stripped of the early-exercise right.
- intrinsic: number; default: not declared
- optionType: 'call' | 'put'; default: not declared — Which leg was analysed — `'call'` or `'put'`.

Named `optionType` because that is what it holds: in TotalFinance `style` is the EXERCISE style
(`'european' | 'american'`) everywhere else, and every one of these results is American by
construction, so a field called `style` reading `'put'` was a straight collision of two
vocabularies (pre-1.0 clean break, defect-fix wave, review-1).
- premiumFractionOfValue: number; default: not declared — `premium / american`.
- rationale: string; default: not declared — Prose an agent relays.
- shouldExerciseNow: boolean; default: not declared — The American value has collapsed to intrinsic — no time value left to give up.
- spot: number; default: not declared
- spotToBoundary: number | null; default: not declared — Signed fraction of spot to the boundary (put: `(S−S*)/S`, call: `(S*−S)/S`); `null` if no boundary.
- timeValue: number; default: not declared — `american − intrinsic ≥ 0`.

- engine.price().return.greeks.ultima: number; default: not declared — `∂vomma/∂σ = ∂³V/∂σ³` (raw).
- engine.price().return.greeks.vanna: number; default: not declared
- engine.price().return.greeks.vega: number; default: not declared
- engine.price().return.greeks.vera: number; default: not declared — `∂rho/∂σ = ∂²V/∂r∂σ` (raw, per 1.00 σ; rho here is per 1.00 rate).
- engine.price().return.greeks.veta: number; default: not declared — `∂vega/∂T` (raw, per year of time-to-expiry; vega here is per 1.00 σ) — the ∂/∂T sibling of vega.
- engine.price().return.greeks.vomma: number; default: not declared
- engine.price().return.greeks.zomma: number; default: not declared — `∂Γ/∂σ = ∂³V/∂S²∂σ` (raw, per 1.00 σ).
- engine.price().return.provenance?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Provenance; default: not declared — Optional data lineage when the inputs came from a provider.
- engine.price().return.value: number; default: not declared — The computed value. Never `NaN` or `±Infinity`: a value the model cannot produce is `null`
beside a diagnostic that says why (Law 7 — a warning never licenses a non-finite number).

- engine.supports(contract).exerciseTime?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').ExerciseTime; default: not declared — AM- or PM-settled — settlement/display metadata. It does NOT move `expiresAt`: the expiry
instant always comes from the `expiry` label and `expiryConvention`. Express an AM-settled
index expiry as a zoned datetime (`'2026-09-18T09:30:00-04:00'`) when its instant matters.
- engine.supports(contract).expiresAt: number; default: not declared — The exact expiration INSTANT the label resolved to (epoch ms), stamped by the builders at
construction: a bare date resolves via the named `expiryConvention`; a zoned datetime is the
caller's explicit instant. REQUIRED (E2, one expiry law): engines price against this
resolution and cross-validate it against the label — an unresolved literal is not a
contract; build one with the option builders.
- engine.supports(contract).expiry: string; default: not declared — The expiry LABEL as supplied: `YYYY-MM-DD` (a calendar date) or a zoned ISO datetime.
- engine.supports(contract).expiryConvention: 'us-equity-close' | 'explicit-instant'; default: not declared — HOW `expiry` resolved to `expiresAt` — named, never silent (spec P1.6/P3.4).

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/options#BlackScholesEvaluateManyResult

Kind: type; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

One `Float64Array` (one value per row) for each selected output. The outputs the selection is
certain to contain are required columns; any other output it might contain is optional
({@link GuaranteedSelection}): a literal selection gives exactly its columns, while a dynamic
selection, a conditional between selections or a union-valued element gives optional ones.

```typescript
/**
 * One `Float64Array` (one value per row) for each selected output. The outputs the selection is
 * certain to contain are required columns; any other output it might contain is optional
 * ({@link GuaranteedSelection}): a literal selection gives exactly its columns, while a dynamic
 * selection, a conditional between selections or a union-valued element gives optional ones.
 */
export type BlackScholesEvaluateManyResult<O extends BlackScholesOutputSelection> = {
    [K in GuaranteedSelection<O>]: Float64Array;
} & {
    [K in Exclude<O[number], GuaranteedSelection<O>>]?: Float64Array;
};
```

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/options#BlackScholesEvaluation

Kind: type; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

The result of a selected evaluation. The outputs the selection is certain to contain are required
numbers; any other output it might contain is optional ({@link GuaranteedSelection}). So a
literal `['price', 'gamma']` gives exactly those two required, while a dynamic selection
(`BlackScholesOutput[]`), a conditional (`c ? ['gamma'] : ['delta']`) or a union-valued element
gives optional properties: the type never claims a value exists that was not requested.

```typescript
/**
 * The result of a selected evaluation. The outputs the selection is certain to contain are required
 * numbers; any other output it might contain is optional ({@link GuaranteedSelection}). So a
 * literal `['price', 'gamma']` gives exactly those two required, while a dynamic selection
 * (`BlackScholesOutput[]`), a conditional (`c ? ['gamma'] : ['delta']`) or a union-valued element
 * gives optional properties: the type never claims a value exists that was not requested.
 */
export type BlackScholesEvaluation<O extends BlackScholesOutputSelection> = {
    [K in GuaranteedSelection<O>]: number;
} & {
    [K in Exclude<O[number], GuaranteedSelection<O>>]?: number;
};
```

whose contract documents vendor decoration (Law 12: entries stay open). `toJSONSchema()` then
emits the complete `properties`/`required` map with `additionalProperties: true`, so MCP
tools, agents, and generated forms see the real field shape instead of a shapeless object.

Distinct from parse-time `mode: 'passthrough'` on purpose: openness declared here is a
property of the PAYLOAD's contract (every caller, every mode, and the emitted JSON Schema all
agree), while `passthrough` is one caller's per-parse leniency toward a schema that itself
remains closed. Like every refiner, returns a NEW schema; the receiver stays closed.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/options#BlackScholesInput

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Flat facade input for a single Black–Scholes–Merton computation.

```typescript
/** Flat facade input for a single Black–Scholes–Merton computation. */
export interface BlackScholesInput {
    /** Spot price of the underlying. */
    spot: number;
    /** Strike price. */
    strike: number;
    /** Time to expiry in years. */
    timeToExpiryYears: number;
    /** Continuously-compounded risk-free rate (decimal, e.g. `0.045`). */
    riskFreeRate: number;
    /** Volatility (decimal, e.g. `0.22`). */
    volatility: number;
    /** Continuous dividend yield (decimal, default `0`). */
    dividendYield?: number;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- dividendYield?: number; default: not declared — Continuous dividend yield (decimal, default `0`).
- riskFreeRate: number; default: not declared — Continuously-compounded risk-free rate (decimal, e.g. `0.045`).
- spot: number; default: not declared — Spot price of the underlying.
- strike: number; default: not declared — Strike price.
- timeToExpiryYears: number; default: not declared — Time to expiry in years.
- volatility: number; default: not declared — Volatility (decimal, e.g. `0.22`).

Distinct from parse-time `mode: 'passthrough'` on purpose: openness declared here is a
property of the PAYLOAD's contract (every caller, every mode, and the emitted JSON Schema all
agree), while `passthrough` is one caller's per-parse leniency toward a schema that itself
remains closed. Like every refiner, returns a NEW schema; the receiver stays closed.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/options#BlackScholesOutputBuffers

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Caller-owned output storage for {@link blackScholesEvaluateManyInto}: the property names ARE the
selection. Each buffer is a `Float64Array` with at least one element per row; only elements
`[0, rows)` are written.

```typescript
/**
 * Caller-owned output storage for {@link blackScholesEvaluateManyInto}: the property names ARE the
 * selection. Each buffer is a `Float64Array` with at least one element per row; only elements
 * `[0, rows)` are written.
 */
export interface BlackScholesOutputBuffers {
    /** Option value. */
    price?: Float64Array;
    /** ∂V/∂S. */
    delta?: Float64Array;
    /** ∂²V/∂S². */
    gamma?: Float64Array;
    /** Value change per calendar day elapsed. */
    theta?: Float64Array;
    /** Value change per 1% (0.01) volatility move. */
    vega?: Float64Array;
    /** Value change per 1% (0.01) rate move. */
    rho?: Float64Array;
    /** ∂Δ/∂σ, per 1.00 σ. */
    vanna?: Float64Array;
    /** ∂Δ/∂T, per added year of time-to-expiry. */
    charm?: Float64Array;
    /** ∂²V/∂σ², per 1.00 σ². */
    vomma?: Float64Array;
    /** ∂Γ/∂S. */
    speed?: Float64Array;
    /** ∂Γ/∂T, per added year of time-to-expiry. */
    color?: Float64Array;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- charm?: Float64Array<ArrayBufferLike>; default: not declared — ∂Δ/∂T, per added year of time-to-expiry.
- color?: Float64Array<ArrayBufferLike>; default: not declared — ∂Γ/∂T, per added year of time-to-expiry.
- delta?: Float64Array<ArrayBufferLike>; default: not declared — ∂V/∂S.
- gamma?: Float64Array<ArrayBufferLike>; default: not declared — ∂²V/∂S².
- price?: Float64Array<ArrayBufferLike>; default: not declared — Option value.
- rho?: Float64Array<ArrayBufferLike>; default: not declared — Value change per 1% (0.01) rate move.
- speed?: Float64Array<ArrayBufferLike>; default: not declared — ∂Γ/∂S.
- theta?: Float64Array<ArrayBufferLike>; default: not declared — Value change per calendar day elapsed.
- vanna?: Float64Array<ArrayBufferLike>; default: not declared — ∂Δ/∂σ, per 1.00 σ.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/options#BoxSpreadDiagnostics

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Diagnostics for {@link boxSpreadRate}.

```typescript
/** Diagnostics for {@link boxSpreadRate}. */
export interface BoxSpreadDiagnostics extends Diagnostics {
    /** Net debit of the box `(C(k1) − C(k2)) + (P(k2) − P(k1))`. */
    debit: number;
    /** Strike width `k2 − k1`, the guaranteed expiry payoff. */
    width: number;
    /** `debit / width = e^(−rT)`, the implied discount factor. */
    discountFactor: number;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- autoReason?: string; default: not declared — When a meta-engine (e.g. `engines.auto()`) selected a delegate, this is a one-sentence,
human-readable explanation of WHY that delegate was chosen (`engine` then names the delegate).
Absent when no auto-selection took place.
- converged?: boolean; default: not declared — Whether an iterative procedure converged. `false` means the value is not trustworthy.
- debit: number; default: not declared — Net debit of the box `(C(k1) − C(k2)) + (P(k2) − P(k1))`.
- decomposition?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Named intermediate quantities the value decomposes into — a par spread's protection leg and
risky annuity, a forward variance's near/far legs. The H-series explain paths disclose their
arithmetic here so a caller can audit the ratio, not just receive it (3B.3).
- discountFactor: number; default: not declared — `debit / width = e^(−rT)`, the implied discount factor.
- engine?: string; default: not declared — Pricing/solver engine name, e.g. `black-scholes-merton`.
- finiteDifferenceBumps?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Finite-difference engines: the ACTUAL bump sizes used for FD Greeks (spec P2.3) — adaptive
near the vol/time boundaries, so the caller can see exactly what was differenced.
Keys: `spotStep`, `volatilityStep`, `timeStepYears`, `rateStep`, and — extended Greeks only —
`dividendYieldStep`. Each is the actual step differenced, in the unit of the coordinate it
bumps. (This doc named the retired `hS`/`hSig`/`hT`/`hR`/`hQ` keys for one release after the
emit sites had moved to the semantic names, so a caller following it read `undefined`.)
- iterations?: number; default: not declared — Iteration count for iterative methods.
- method?: string; default: not declared — Numerical method, e.g. `closed-form`, `brent`, `finite-difference`.
- selection?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing').SelectionReport; default: not declared — The structured engine-selection report (Gate C, `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing`): who was selected,
why, and — for automatic selection — every candidate considered with its verdict. This is the
machine-readable superset of `engine` + `autoReason` (which remain for compatibility);
`selected.name` always agrees with `engine` when both are present.
- selection.candidates?: readonly import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing').SelectionCandidate[]; default: not declared — Candidates an automatic selection considered; absent for explicit mode.
- selection.mode: 'explicit' | 'automatic'; default: not declared
- selection.reason: string; default: not declared — Why the selected engine answers this request.
- selection.selected: { name: string; version?: string; }; default: not declared
- selection.selected.name: string; default: not declared
- selection.selected.version?: string; default: not declared
- timingMs?: number; default: not declared — Wall-clock timing in milliseconds, when measured.
- warmup?: number; default: not declared — Series facades: number of leading output slots that are warmup sentinels (null/NaN) while the
computation seeds. Equals the input length when the indicator never emitted.
- warnings: QuantWarning[]; default: not declared — Structured warnings; always present (possibly empty).
- width: number; default: not declared — Strike width `k2 − k1`, the guaranteed expiry payoff.

```typescript
export interface ChainGreeksAssumptionsExtra extends Record<string, unknown> {
```

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/options#DiscreteDividend

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

A discrete cash dividend with an ex-date (ISO) and per-share amount.

```typescript
/** A discrete cash dividend with an ex-date (ISO) and per-share amount. */
export interface DiscreteDividend {
    /**
     * Ex-date, `YYYY-MM-DD` or a zoned ISO datetime.
     *
     * A DATE-ONLY label resolves to the US equity market OPEN, **09:30 America/New_York** — the
     * instant the share starts trading without the dividend. This is deliberately NOT the 16:00 ET
     * convention a date-only option EXPIRY uses: they are different events. The practical consequence
     * is that an `asOf` from 09:30 ET on the ex-date onward treats the dividend as PAID (it is already
     * out of the spot) and stops discounting it into the escrowed spot, while `asOf` earlier that
     * morning, or any time the day before, still accrues it.
     *
     * Pass a zoned datetime (e.g. `'2026-06-01T09:30:00-04:00'`) to name the instant yourself.
     */
    exDate: string;
    /** Cash amount per share (must be finite and non-negative). */
    amount: number;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- amount: number; default: not declared — Cash amount per share (must be finite and non-negative).
- exDate: string; default: not declared — Ex-date, `YYYY-MM-DD` or a zoned ISO datetime.

A DATE-ONLY label resolves to the US equity market OPEN, **09:30 America/New_York** — the
instant the share starts trading without the dividend. This is deliberately NOT the 16:00 ET
convention a date-only option EXPIRY uses: they are different events. The practical consequence
is that an `asOf` from 09:30 ET on the ex-date onward treats the dividend as PAID (it is already
out of the spot) and stops discounting it into the escrowed spot, while `asOf` earlier that
morning, or any time the day before, still accrues it.

Pass a zoned datetime (e.g. `'2026-06-01T09:30:00-04:00'`) to name the instant yourself.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/options#DividendTermStructurePoint

```typescript
    carry: number;
```

- dividendPresentValue: number; default: not declared — PV of the discrete dividends accruing strictly before this expiry.
- forward: number; default: not declared — Dividend-adjusted (escrowed) forward `F(T) = (S − PV)·e^{(r−q)T}`.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/options#EquityLattice

```typescript
export interface EquityLattice {
```

why, and — for automatic selection — every candidate considered with its verdict. This is the
machine-readable superset of `engine` + `autoReason` (which remain for compatibility);
`selected.name` always agrees with `engine` when both are present.

- diagnostics.selection.mode: 'explicit' | 'automatic'; default: not declared

- diagnostics.selection.selected: { name: string; version?: string; }; default: not declared

computation seeds. Equals the input length when the indicator never emitted.
- diagnostics.warnings: QuantWarning[]; default: not declared — Structured warnings; always present (possibly empty).
- monteCarlo: MonteCarloStatistics; default: not declared
- monteCarlo.confidenceInterval: [number, number] | null; default: not declared — Confidence interval at the requested level (default 95%); `null` whenever `standardError` is.
- monteCarlo.method: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/options').MonteCarloMethod; default: not declared — The sampling method actually used (may differ from the request if QMC fell back to pseudo).
- monteCarlo.paths: number; default: not declared — Number of paths actually evaluated (antithetic pairs count as one path).
- monteCarlo.seed: number; default: not declared — The seed, echoed for reproducibility.
- monteCarlo.standardError: number | null; default: not declared — Standard error of the mean estimate — `null` for the QUASI-random methods (`sobol`, `halton`).

The sample-variance formula `√(s²/n)` assumes independent draws. A low-discrepancy sequence is
deterministic and negatively correlated by construction, so that formula does not estimate its
error: at 16k Sobol points on a European call it overstated the true deviation by ~75×, and a
confidence interval built from it was neither a confidence nor an interval. QMC error is
estimated by RANDOMIZING the sequence (scrambling/shifting) and taking the variance ACROSS
independent randomizations — which this estimator does not do, so it reports `null` and says so.
- monteCarlo.varianceReduction: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/options').VarianceReduction; default: not declared — Which variance-reduction techniques were applied.
- monteCarlo.varianceReduction.antithetic: boolean; default: not declared
- monteCarlo.varianceReduction.brownianBridge: boolean; default: not declared
- monteCarlo.varianceReduction.controlVariate: boolean; default: not declared
- provenance?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Provenance; default: not declared — Optional data lineage when the inputs came from a provider.
- provenance.asOf?: number; default: not declared
- provenance.dataset?: string; default: not declared
- provenance.provider?: string; default: not declared
- provenance.receivedAt?: number; default: not declared
- provenance.requestId?: string; default: not declared
- provenance.sourceVersion?: string; default: not declared
- provenance.warnings?: QuantWarning[]; default: not declared
- value: number; default: not declared — The computed value. Never `NaN` or `±Infinity`: a value the model cannot produce is `null`
beside a diagnostic that says why (Law 7 — a warning never licenses a non-finite number).

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/options#HestonCosineExpansionOptions

```typescript
/** Options for the COS analytic pricer. */
export interface HestonCosineExpansionOptions {
    /** Number of cosine terms (default 256, maximum 8,192; COS converges exponentially). */
    terms?: number;

     */
```

- terms?: number; default: not declared — Number of cosine terms (default 256, maximum 8,192; COS converges exponentially).

- greeks.vega: number; default: not declared
- greeks.vera: number; default: not declared — `∂rho/∂σ = ∂²V/∂r∂σ` (raw, per 1.00 σ; rho here is per 1.00 rate).
- greeks.veta: number; default: not declared — `∂vega/∂T` (raw, per year of time-to-expiry; vega here is per 1.00 σ) — the ∂/∂T sibling of vega.
- greeks.vomma: number; default: not declared
- greeks.zomma: number; default: not declared — `∂Γ/∂σ = ∂³V/∂S²∂σ` (raw, per 1.00 σ).

- monteCarlo.confidenceInterval: [number, number] | null; default: not declared — Confidence interval at the requested level (default 95%); `null` whenever `standardError` is.
- monteCarlo.method: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/options').MonteCarloMethod; default: not declared — The sampling method actually used (may differ from the request if QMC fell back to pseudo).
- monteCarlo.paths: number; default: not declared — Number of paths actually evaluated (antithetic pairs count as one path).
- monteCarlo.seed: number; default: not declared — The seed, echoed for reproducibility.
- monteCarlo.standardError: number | null; default: not declared — Standard error of the mean estimate — `null` for the QUASI-random methods (`sobol`, `halton`).

The sample-variance formula `√(s²/n)` assumes independent draws. A low-discrepancy sequence is
deterministic and negatively correlated by construction, so that formula does not estimate its
error: at 16k Sobol points on a European call it overstated the true deviation by ~75×, and a
confidence interval built from it was neither a confidence nor an interval. QMC error is
estimated by RANDOMIZING the sequence (scrambling/shifting) and taking the variance ACROSS
independent randomizations — which this estimator does not do, so it reports `null` and says so.
- monteCarlo.varianceReduction: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/options').VarianceReduction; default: not declared — Which variance-reduction techniques were applied.
- monteCarlo.varianceReduction.antithetic: boolean; default: not declared
- monteCarlo.varianceReduction.brownianBridge: boolean; default: not declared
- monteCarlo.varianceReduction.controlVariate: boolean; default: not declared

- provenance.asOf?: number; default: not declared
- provenance.dataset?: string; default: not declared
- provenance.provider?: string; default: not declared
- provenance.receivedAt?: number; default: not declared
- provenance.requestId?: string; default: not declared
- provenance.sourceVersion?: string; default: not declared
- provenance.warnings?: QuantWarning[]; default: not declared
- value: number; default: not declared — The computed value. Never `NaN` or `±Infinity`: a value the model cannot produce is `null`
beside a diagnostic that says why (Law 7 — a warning never licenses a non-finite number).

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/options#ImpliedVolatilityOptionInput

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Input for {@link impliedVolatilityOption} — one object: `{ contract, market, ...solver options }`.

```typescript
/**
 * Solve implied volatility from `market.price`, returning a rich envelope with diagnostics. Routes on
 * contract style and on whether an engine is named (WS4.2): a European contract with no engine
 * inverts closed-form Black–Scholes–Merton (`method` chooses `auto`/`brent`/`newton`/`halley`/
 * `householder`, `fallback` and `failFast` shape it); an American contract, or any contract with an
 * `engine`, inverts that engine (default Bjerksund–Stensland 2002 for American) over a safeguarded
 * Brent bracket, where the closed-form knobs do not apply and are refused. The engine and
 * actually-used method are reported in `diagnostics`.
 */
/** Input for {@link impliedVolatilityOption} — one object: `{ contract, market, ...solver options }`. */
export interface ImpliedVolatilityOptionInput extends ImpliedVolatilityOptions {
    contract: OptionContract;
    market: OptionMarket;
    /**
     * Engine to invert numerically. An American contract always inverts an engine (default
     * `engines.bjerksundStensland2002()`); a European contract inverts closed-form
     * Black–Scholes–Merton unless an engine is named here, in which case THAT engine is inverted —
     * e.g. a lattice for discrete dividends, or a custom model. `method`/`fallback`/`failFast` belong
     * to the closed-form route and are refused alongside an engine.
     */
    engine?: OptionPricingEngine;
}
```

index expiry as a zoned datetime (`'2026-09-18T09:30:00-04:00'`) when its instant matters.
- engine.supports(contract).expiresAt: number; default: not declared — The exact expiration INSTANT the label resolved to (epoch ms), stamped by the builders at
construction: a bare date resolves via the named `expiryConvention`; a zoned datetime is the
caller's explicit instant. REQUIRED (E2, one expiry law): engines price against this
resolution and cross-validate it against the label — an unresolved literal is not a
contract; build one with the option builders.
- engine.supports(contract).expiry: string; default: not declared — The expiry LABEL as supplied: `YYYY-MM-DD` (a calendar date) or a zoned ISO datetime.
- engine.supports(contract).expiryConvention: 'us-equity-close' | 'explicit-instant'; default: not declared — HOW `expiry` resolved to `expiresAt` — named, never silent (spec P1.6/P3.4).
- engine.supports(contract).multiplier?: number; default: not declared
- engine.supports(contract).occSymbol?: string; default: not declared
- engine.supports(contract).root?: string; default: not declared
- engine.supports(contract).settlement?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Settlement; default: not declared
- engine.supports(contract).strike: number; default: not declared
- engine.supports(contract).style: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').OptionStyle; default: not declared — REQUIRED at build — never defaulted: US equity options are American, many index options European.
- engine.supports(contract).type: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').OptionType; default: not declared
- engine.supports(contract).underlying: string; default: not declared
- engine.version: string; default: not declared
- failFast?: boolean; default: not declared — In batch mode, throw on the first bad row instead of recording it (default `false`).
- fallback?: boolean; default: not declared — Fall back to Brent when a derivative method fails (default `true`).
- market: OptionMarket; default: not declared
- market.asOf: string | number; default: not declared — Snapshot time: epoch ms, `'YYYY-MM-DD'`, or a ZONED ISO datetime — one grammar for "when"
across every package. Each boundary resolves it once via core `resolveAsOf` (zone-less
datetimes are rejected with a teaching error; TotalFinance never reads the machine clock or zone).
- market.dividendYield?: number; default: not declared — Continuous dividend yield; defaults to 0 when omitted.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/options#ImpliedVolatilityReason

Kind: type; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

```typescript
export type ImpliedVolatilityReason = 'below_intrinsic' | 'above_max_bound'
/**
 * The target premium is smaller than the model price at the lowest σ the solver represents, so no
 * volatility in the bracket reproduces it (the σ→0 floor sits ABOVE the target). Distinct from
 * `below_intrinsic` (a no-arbitrage violation) and from `no_bracket` (a bracketing failure with a
 * root that exists): here the inverse simply has no solution at this price scale.
 */
 | 'price_below_resolvable' | 'no_bracket' | 'max_iterations';
```

```typescript
/** An inverse option's risk in both denominations. */
export interface InverseGreeks {
    /**
     * Coin-denominated greeks — derivatives of the coin premium `V_usd/S`. delta/gamma are raw (per $1
     * move in spot), vega/1%, theta/day, rho/1%. The delta carries the `−V_coin/S` correction (the
     * embedded short-coin from paying premium in the coin), so it is NOT the Black–Scholes delta.
     */

    /** USD-linear greeks — equal to the vanilla BSM greeks, since the inverse option's USD payoff is a vanilla's. */
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- antithetic?: boolean; default: not declared — Antithetic variates (pseudo only; ignored for QMC). Default `true`.
- brownianBridge?: boolean; default: not declared — Brownian-bridge path ordering (QMC only; concentrates variance in the leading dimensions).

- method?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/options').MonteCarloMethod; default: not declared — Sampling method (default `'pseudo'`).

- seed: number; default: not declared — Seed — required and echoed for reproducibility.
- steps?: number; default: not declared — Time steps per path (default 100).

- diagnostics.converged?: boolean; default: not declared — Whether an iterative procedure converged. `false` means the value is not trustworthy.

risky annuity, a forward variance's near/far legs. The H-series explain paths disclose their
arithmetic here so a caller can audit the ratio, not just receive it (3B.3).
- diagnostics.engine?: string; default: not declared — Pricing/solver engine name, e.g. `black-scholes-merton`.
- diagnostics.finiteDifferenceBumps?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Finite-difference engines: the ACTUAL bump sizes used for FD Greeks (spec P2.3) — adaptive
near the vol/time boundaries, so the caller can see exactly what was differenced.
Keys: `spotStep`, `volatilityStep`, `timeStepYears`, `rateStep`, and — extended Greeks only —
`dividendYieldStep`. Each is the actual step differenced, in the unit of the coordinate it
bumps. (This doc named the retired `hS`/`hSig`/`hT`/`hR`/`hQ` keys for one release after the
emit sites had moved to the semantic names, so a caller following it read `undefined`.)
- diagnostics.iterations?: number; default: not declared — Iteration count for iterative methods.
- diagnostics.method?: string; default: not declared — Numerical method, e.g. `closed-form`, `brent`, `finite-difference`.
- diagnostics.selection?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing').SelectionReport; default: not declared — The structured engine-selection report (Gate C, `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing`): who was selected,
why, and — for automatic selection — every candidate considered with its verdict. This is the
machine-readable superset of `engine` + `autoReason` (which remain for compatibility);
`selected.name` always agrees with `engine` when both are present.
- diagnostics.selection.candidates?: readonly import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing').SelectionCandidate[]; default: not declared — Candidates an automatic selection considered; absent for explicit mode.
- diagnostics.selection.mode: 'explicit' | 'automatic'; default: not declared
- diagnostics.selection.reason: string; default: not declared — Why the selected engine answers this request.
- diagnostics.selection.selected: { name: string; version?: string; }; default: not declared
- diagnostics.selection.selected.name: string; default: not declared
- diagnostics.selection.selected.version?: string; default: not declared
- diagnostics.timingMs?: number; default: not declared — Wall-clock timing in milliseconds, when measured.
- diagnostics.warmup?: number; default: not declared — Series facades: number of leading output slots that are warmup sentinels (null/NaN) while the
computation seeds. Equals the input length when the indicator never emitted.
- diagnostics.warnings: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').QuantWarning[]; default: not declared — Structured warnings; always present (possibly empty).
- greeks?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/options').Greeks | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/options').ExtendedGreeks; default: not declared
- greeks.charm: number; default: not declared
- greeks.color: number; default: not declared
- greeks.delta: number; default: not declared
- greeks.gamma: number; default: not declared
- greeks.lambda: number | null; default: not declared — Elasticity / effective leverage `Λ = Δ·S / V` (dimensionless). `null` when the price
underflows to zero (deep-OTM): elasticity is undefined at V = 0 and is disclosed as null with
a `greeks.lambda_undefined` warning on explained paths — never NaN/Infinity (Law 7).
- greeks.phi: number; default: not declared — Dividend rho (epsilon) `ε = ∂V/∂q`, per 1% dividend yield (scaled like `rho`).
- greeks.rho: number; default: not declared
- greeks.speed: number; default: not declared
- greeks.theta: number; default: not declared
- greeks.ultima: number; default: not declared — `∂vomma/∂σ = ∂³V/∂σ³` (raw).
- greeks.vanna: number; default: not declared
- greeks.vega: number; default: not declared
- greeks.vera: number; default: not declared — `∂rho/∂σ = ∂²V/∂r∂σ` (raw, per 1.00 σ; rho here is per 1.00 rate).
- greeks.veta: number; default: not declared — `∂vega/∂T` (raw, per year of time-to-expiry; vega here is per 1.00 σ) — the ∂/∂T sibling of vega.
- greeks.vomma: number; default: not declared
- greeks.zomma: number; default: not declared — `∂Γ/∂σ = ∂³V/∂S²∂σ` (raw, per 1.00 σ).
- monteCarlo: MonteCarloStatistics; default: not declared
- monteCarlo.confidenceInterval: [number, number] | null; default: not declared — Confidence interval at the requested level (default 95%); `null` whenever `standardError` is.
- monteCarlo.method: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/options').MonteCarloMethod; default: not declared — The sampling method actually used (may differ from the request if QMC fell back to pseudo).
- monteCarlo.paths: number; default: not declared — Number of paths actually evaluated (antithetic pairs count as one path).
- monteCarlo.seed: number; default: not declared — The seed, echoed for reproducibility.
- monteCarlo.standardError: number | null; default: not declared — Standard error of the mean estimate — `null` for the QUASI-random methods (`sobol`, `halton`).

The sample-variance formula `√(s²/n)` assumes independent draws. A low-discrepancy sequence is
deterministic and negatively correlated by construction, so that formula does not estimate its
error: at 16k Sobol points on a European call it overstated the true deviation by ~75×, and a
confidence interval built from it was neither a confidence nor an interval. QMC error is
estimated by RANDOMIZING the sequence (scrambling/shifting) and taking the variance ACROSS
independent randomizations — which this estimator does not do, so it reports `null` and says so.
- monteCarlo.varianceReduction: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/options').VarianceReduction; default: not declared — Which variance-reduction techniques were applied.
- monteCarlo.varianceReduction.antithetic: boolean; default: not declared
- monteCarlo.varianceReduction.brownianBridge: boolean; default: not declared
- monteCarlo.varianceReduction.controlVariate: boolean; default: not declared
- provenance?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Provenance; default: not declared — Optional data lineage when the inputs came from a provider.
- provenance.asOf?: number; default: not declared
- provenance.dataset?: string; default: not declared
- provenance.provider?: string; default: not declared
- provenance.receivedAt?: number; default: not declared
- provenance.requestId?: string; default: not declared
- provenance.sourceVersion?: string; default: not declared
- provenance.warnings?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').QuantWarning[]; default: not declared
- value: number; default: not declared — The computed value. Never `NaN` or `±Infinity`: a value the model cannot produce is `null`
beside a diagnostic that says why (Law 7 — a warning never licenses a non-finite number).

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/options#MonteCarloPriceOptions

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Options for {@link monteCarloPrice}. Extends the shared MC sampling options.

```typescript
/** Options for {@link monteCarloPrice}. Extends the shared MC sampling options. */
export interface MonteCarloPriceOptions extends MonteCarloSamplingOptions {
    /** Compute Greeks by common-random-number finite differences (default `true`). */
    greeks?: boolean;
    /**
     * Compute the full higher-order (extended) Greek set by CRN finite differences (implies `greeks`).
     * Third-order Greeks (speed/color/ultima) carry more Monte-Carlo error than the first/second order —
     * raise `paths` when you need them tight.
     */
    extendedGreeks?: boolean;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- antithetic?: boolean; default: not declared — Antithetic variates (pseudo only; ignored for QMC). Default `true`.
- brownianBridge?: boolean; default: not declared — Brownian-bridge path ordering (QMC only; concentrates variance in the leading dimensions).
- confidence?: number; default: not declared — Confidence level for the interval (default 0.95).
- extendedGreeks?: boolean; default: not declared — Compute the full higher-order (extended) Greek set by CRN finite differences (implies `greeks`).
Third-order Greeks (speed/color/ultima) carry more Monte-Carlo error than the first/second order —
raise `paths` when you need them tight.
- greeks?: boolean; default: not declared — Compute Greeks by common-random-number finite differences (default `true`).
- method?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/options').MonteCarloMethod; default: not declared — Sampling method (default `'pseudo'`).
- paths?: number; default: not declared — Number of paths (antithetic pairs when `antithetic`). Default 50_000.
- randomNumberGenerator?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/options').MonteCarloRandomNumberGenerator; default: not declared — PRNG for `method: 'pseudo'` (default `'mulberry32'`).
- seed: number; default: not declared — Seed — required and echoed for reproducibility.

- monteCarlo.confidenceInterval: [number, number] | null; default: not declared — Confidence interval at the requested level (default 95%); `null` whenever `standardError` is.
- monteCarlo.method: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/options').MonteCarloMethod; default: not declared — The sampling method actually used (may differ from the request if QMC fell back to pseudo).
- monteCarlo.paths: number; default: not declared — Number of paths actually evaluated (antithetic pairs count as one path).
- monteCarlo.seed: number; default: not declared — The seed, echoed for reproducibility.
- monteCarlo.standardError: number | null; default: not declared — Standard error of the mean estimate — `null` for the QUASI-random methods (`sobol`, `halton`).

The sample-variance formula `√(s²/n)` assumes independent draws. A low-discrepancy sequence is
deterministic and negatively correlated by construction, so that formula does not estimate its
error: at 16k Sobol points on a European call it overstated the true deviation by ~75×, and a
confidence interval built from it was neither a confidence nor an interval. QMC error is
estimated by RANDOMIZING the sequence (scrambling/shifting) and taking the variance ACROSS
independent randomizations — which this estimator does not do, so it reports `null` and says so.
- monteCarlo.varianceReduction: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/options').VarianceReduction; default: not declared — Which variance-reduction techniques were applied.
- monteCarlo.varianceReduction.antithetic: boolean; default: not declared
- monteCarlo.varianceReduction.brownianBridge: boolean; default: not declared
- monteCarlo.varianceReduction.controlVariate: boolean; default: not declared
- provenance?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Provenance; default: not declared — Optional data lineage when the inputs came from a provider.
- provenance.asOf?: number; default: not declared
- provenance.dataset?: string; default: not declared
- provenance.provider?: string; default: not declared
- provenance.receivedAt?: number; default: not declared
- provenance.requestId?: string; default: not declared
- provenance.sourceVersion?: string; default: not declared
- provenance.warnings?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').QuantWarning[]; default: not declared
- value: number; default: not declared — The computed value. Never `NaN` or `±Infinity`: a value the model cannot produce is `null`
beside a diagnostic that says why (Law 7 — a warning never licenses a non-finite number).

```typescript
export interface OptionChainHealthConfig {
    /**
     * Omit for quote-only health. `'black-scholes-merton'` names the dynamics: European rows invert

    maximumQuoteAgeMs: number;

    maximumRelativeSpread: number;

    minimumExpiries?: number;
    /** Default 1; positive safe integer ≤10,000; per expiration instant AND exercise style. */
    minimumStrikesPerExpiry?: number;
    /** Optional smaller row budget; default and hard ceiling 10,000. No silent truncation. */
    maximumQuotes?: number;
    /** Model rows only. Closed optional σ bracket; defaults 1e-7 and 5, hard bounds, never expanded. */
```

- minimumStrikesPerExpiry?: number; default: not declared — Default 1; positive safe integer ≤10,000; per expiration instant AND exercise style.

```typescript
export interface OptionChainHealthModelResult {
    /** Compatibility with the specified model, NOT a verdict that a market observation is bad. */
    status: OptionChainHealthModelStatus;
    /**
     * The engine this row's bounds and inverse come from under the requested dynamics — closed-form
     * BSM for a European contract, Bjerksund–Stensland 2002 for an American one. Null when no model
     * assessment was requested.
     */
    engine: 'black-scholes-merton' | 'bjerksund-stensland-2002' | null;
    /**
     * The style's no-arbitrage price band per underlying share, or null when not evaluable: the
     * discounted band for a European row, the undiscounted intrinsic-to-spot/strike band for an
     * American row.
     */
    bounds: {
        lower: number;
        upper: number;
    } | null;
    /** Every applicable unsupported assumption, not just the first one encountered. */
    unsupportedReasons: ('discrete_dividends' | 'adjusted_deliverable')[];
    impliedVolatility: number | null;
    solver: {
        status: 'converged' | 'not-run' | 'unavailable' | 'failed';
        /** null when no model assessment was requested. */
        method: 'brent' | null;
        converged: boolean;
        iterations: number;
        /** Null only on success. Failed inverses never receive a guessed or supplied IV. */
        reason: string | null;
        /** Absolute repricing residual per share; null if no finite solve was accepted. */
        priceResidual: number | null;
    };
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- bounds: { lower: number; upper: number; } | null; default: not declared — The style's no-arbitrage price band per underlying share, or null when not evaluable: the
discounted band for a European row, the undiscounted intrinsic-to-spot/strike band for an
American row.
- bounds.lower: number; default: not declared
- bounds.upper: number; default: not declared
- engine: 'black-scholes-merton' | 'bjerksund-stensland-2002' | null; default: not declared — The engine this row's bounds and inverse come from under the requested dynamics — closed-form
BSM for a European contract, Bjerksund–Stensland 2002 for an American one. Null when no model
assessment was requested.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/options#OptionMarket

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Market inputs for the pro pricing API (spec §9.1). Extends the workspace-canonical
{@link MarketInputs} (spot/rate/dividendYield/asOf) and adds the option-specific fields. `spot` is
required (every pro engine resolves off it — forward-only pricing uses the flat `black76`/
`bachelier` facades). `rate`/`volatility` are scalars in this milestone; a `VolatilityLookup` variant for
`volatility` arrives with the surface integration.

```typescript
/**
 * Market inputs for the pro pricing API (spec §9.1). Extends the workspace-canonical
 * {@link MarketInputs} (spot/rate/dividendYield/asOf) and adds the option-specific fields. `spot` is
 * required (every pro engine resolves off it — forward-only pricing uses the flat `black76`/
 * `bachelier` facades). `rate`/`volatility` are scalars in this milestone; a `VolatilityLookup` variant for
 * `volatility` arrives with the surface integration.
 */
export interface OptionMarket extends MarketInputs {
    forward?: number;
    /** Discrete cash dividends (American engines use the escrowed-dividend approximation). */
    dividends?: DiscreteDividend[];
    volatility?: number;
    /** The observed premium an inversion reproduces (`option.impliedVolatility`). */
    price?: number;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- asOf: string | number; default: not declared — Snapshot time: epoch ms, `'YYYY-MM-DD'`, or a ZONED ISO datetime — one grammar for "when"
across every package. Each boundary resolves it once via core `resolveAsOf` (zone-less
datetimes are rejected with a teaching error; TotalFinance never reads the machine clock or zone).
- dividendYield?: number; default: not declared — Continuous dividend yield; defaults to 0 when omitted.
- dividends?: DiscreteDividend[]; default: not declared — Discrete cash dividends (American engines use the escrowed-dividend approximation).
- forward?: number; default: not declared
- price?: number; default: not declared — The observed premium an inversion reproduces (`option.impliedVolatility`).
- riskFreeRate: number; default: not declared
- spot: number; default: not declared
- volatility?: number; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/options#OptionPricingEngine

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

```typescript
export interface OptionPricingEngine {
    readonly name: string;
    readonly version: string;
    /** Machine-readable capabilities, behaviorally verified by the engine contract suite (Law 8). */
    readonly capabilities: EngineCapabilities;
    /** Whether this engine can price the given contract. */
    supports(contract: OptionContract): boolean;
    price(input: OptionEnginePriceInput): PriceResult;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- capabilities: EngineCapabilities; default: not declared — Machine-readable capabilities, behaviorally verified by the engine contract suite (Law 8).
- capabilities.deterministic: boolean; default: not declared — Same inputs → identical outputs. `false` marks stochastic engines (Monte-Carlo): a FIXED SEED
makes them reproducible, which is what the contract suite verifies for them.
- capabilities.dividends: readonly ('continuous' | 'none' | 'discrete')[]; default: not declared — Dividend models the engine honors.
- capabilities.extendedGreeks: boolean; default: not declared — Whether the extended (higher-order) Greek set is available on request.
- capabilities.greeks: 'none' | 'analytic' | 'finite-difference' | 'delegated'; default: not declared — How first-order Greeks are produced when requested: closed-form (`analytic`), bump-and-reprice
(`finite-difference`), by the selected delegate (`delegated`, meta-engines), or not at all
(`none` — requests are disclosed as unhonored, never silently dropped).
- capabilities.styles: readonly OptionStyle[]; default: not declared — Exercise styles this engine prices (must agree with `supports()`).
- name: string; default: not declared
- price: (input: OptionEnginePriceInput) => PriceResult; default: not declared
- price().return.assumptions: Assumptions<Record<never, never>>; default: not declared — Every applied convention, echoed back.
- price().return.diagnostics: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Diagnostics; default: not declared — How the value was computed, plus any warnings.
- price().return.greeks?: Greeks | ExtendedGreeks; default: not declared
- price().return.greeks.charm: number; default: not declared
- price().return.greeks.color: number; default: not declared
- price().return.greeks.delta: number; default: not declared
- price().return.greeks.gamma: number; default: not declared
- price().return.greeks.lambda: number | null; default: not declared — Elasticity / effective leverage `Λ = Δ·S / V` (dimensionless). `null` when the price
underflows to zero (deep-OTM): elasticity is undefined at V = 0 and is disclosed as null with
a `greeks.lambda_undefined` warning on explained paths — never NaN/Infinity (Law 7).
- price().return.greeks.phi: number; default: not declared — Dividend rho (epsilon) `ε = ∂V/∂q`, per 1% dividend yield (scaled like `rho`).
- price().return.greeks.rho: number; default: not declared
- price().return.greeks.speed: number; default: not declared
- price().return.greeks.theta: number; default: not declared
- price().return.greeks.ultima: number; default: not declared — `∂vomma/∂σ = ∂³V/∂σ³` (raw).
- price().return.greeks.vanna: number; default: not declared
- price().return.greeks.vega: number; default: not declared
- price().return.greeks.vera: number; default: not declared — `∂rho/∂σ = ∂²V/∂r∂σ` (raw, per 1.00 σ; rho here is per 1.00 rate).
- price().return.greeks.veta: number; default: not declared — `∂vega/∂T` (raw, per year of time-to-expiry; vega here is per 1.00 σ) — the ∂/∂T sibling of vega.
- price().return.greeks.vomma: number; default: not declared
- price().return.greeks.zomma: number; default: not declared — `∂Γ/∂σ = ∂³V/∂S²∂σ` (raw, per 1.00 σ).
- price().return.provenance?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Provenance; default: not declared — Optional data lineage when the inputs came from a provider.
- price().return.value: number; default: not declared — The computed value. Never `NaN` or `±Infinity`: a value the model cannot produce is `null`
beside a diagnostic that says why (Law 7 — a warning never licenses a non-finite number).
- price(input): OptionEnginePriceInput; default: not declared
- price(input).contract: OptionContract; default: not declared
- price(input).market: OptionMarket; default: not declared
- price(input).options?: PriceOptions; default: not declared
- supports: (contract: OptionContract) => boolean; default: not declared — Whether this engine can price the given contract.
- supports(contract): OptionContract; default: not declared
- supports(contract).adjusted?: boolean; default: not declared
- supports(contract).currency?: string; default: not declared
- supports(contract).deliverable?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Deliverable; default: not declared
- supports(contract).exerciseTime?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').ExerciseTime; default: not declared — AM- or PM-settled — settlement/display metadata. It does NOT move `expiresAt`: the expiry
instant always comes from the `expiry` label and `expiryConvention`. Express an AM-settled
index expiry as a zoned datetime (`'2026-09-18T09:30:00-04:00'`) when its instant matters.
- supports(contract).expiresAt: number; default: not declared — The exact expiration INSTANT the label resolved to (epoch ms), stamped by the builders at
construction: a bare date resolves via the named `expiryConvention`; a zoned datetime is the
caller's explicit instant. REQUIRED (E2, one expiry law): engines price against this
resolution and cross-validate it against the label — an unresolved literal is not a
contract; build one with the option builders.
- supports(contract).expiry: string; default: not declared — The expiry LABEL as supplied: `YYYY-MM-DD` (a calendar date) or a zoned ISO datetime.
- supports(contract).expiryConvention: 'us-equity-close' | 'explicit-instant'; default: not declared — HOW `expiry` resolved to `expiresAt` — named, never silent (spec P1.6/P3.4).
- supports(contract).multiplier?: number; default: not declared
- supports(contract).occSymbol?: string; default: not declared
- supports(contract).root?: string; default: not declared
- supports(contract).settlement?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Settlement; default: not declared
- supports(contract).strike: number; default: not declared
- supports(contract).style: OptionStyle; default: not declared — REQUIRED at build — never defaulted: US equity options are American, many index options European.
- supports(contract).type: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').OptionType; default: not declared
- supports(contract).underlying: string; default: not declared
- version: string; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/options#ParityCode

Kind: value; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Stable `parity.*` error/warning codes (public API; the set is open).

```typescript
export declare const ParityCode: { readonly DegenerateBox: 'parity.degenerate_box'; readonly InsufficientStrikes: 'parity.insufficient_strikes'; readonly NonPositiveDiscount: 'parity.nonpositive_discount'; readonly NonPositiveForward: 'parity.nonpositive_forward'; readonly RateMismatch: 'parity.rate_mismatch'; readonly StrikeUnavailable: 'parity.strike_unavailable'; };
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- DegenerateBox: 'parity.degenerate_box'; default: not declared — The box debit is non-positive, so no real financing rate exists.
- InsufficientStrikes: 'parity.insufficient_strikes'; default: not declared — Fewer than two usable strikes with both a call and a put — a line cannot be fit.
- NonPositiveDiscount: 'parity.nonpositive_discount'; default: not declared — The regression slope is non-negative, so no positive discount factor exists.
- NonPositiveForward: 'parity.nonpositive_forward'; default: not declared — The implied forward came out non-positive / non-finite.
- RateMismatch: 'parity.rate_mismatch'; default: not declared — The regression-implied rate disagrees materially with the supplied rate.
- StrikeUnavailable: 'parity.strike_unavailable'; default: not declared — A specifically requested strike/leg quote is missing (box spread).

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/options#ParityDiagnostics

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Diagnostics for the regression-based parity functions. Extends the shared {@link Diagnostics}.

```typescript
/** Diagnostics for the regression-based parity functions. Extends the shared {@link Diagnostics}. */
export interface ParityDiagnostics extends Diagnostics {
    /** Number of strikes used in the final fit (after trimming). */
    strikesUsed: number;
    /** Number of strikes trimmed as MAD outliers. */
    trimmedCount: number;
    /** The strikes that were trimmed, ascending. */
    trimmedStrikes: number[];
    /** Per-strike parity residuals for every usable strike (trimmed ones flagged). */
    perStrike: ParityStrikeResidual[];
    /** Median absolute deviation of the initial-fit residuals used for trimming. */
    medianAbsoluteDeviationResidual: number;
    /** Coefficient of determination of the final regression. */
    rSquared: number;
    /** Implied discount factor `DF = −slope = e^(−rT)`. */
    impliedDiscountFactor: number;
    /** Implied continuously-compounded financing rate `r* = −ln(DF)/T`. */
    impliedRate: number;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- autoReason?: string; default: not declared — When a meta-engine (e.g. `engines.auto()`) selected a delegate, this is a one-sentence,
human-readable explanation of WHY that delegate was chosen (`engine` then names the delegate).
Absent when no auto-selection took place.
- converged?: boolean; default: not declared — Whether an iterative procedure converged. `false` means the value is not trustworthy.
- decomposition?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Named intermediate quantities the value decomposes into — a par spread's protection leg and
risky annuity, a forward variance's near/far legs. The H-series explain paths disclose their
arithmetic here so a caller can audit the ratio, not just receive it (3B.3).
- engine?: string; default: not declared — Pricing/solver engine name, e.g. `black-scholes-merton`.
- finiteDifferenceBumps?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Finite-difference engines: the ACTUAL bump sizes used for FD Greeks (spec P2.3) — adaptive
near the vol/time boundaries, so the caller can see exactly what was differenced.
Keys: `spotStep`, `volatilityStep`, `timeStepYears`, `rateStep`, and — extended Greeks only —
`dividendYieldStep`. Each is the actual step differenced, in the unit of the coordinate it
bumps. (This doc named the retired `hS`/`hSig`/`hT`/`hR`/`hQ` keys for one release after the
emit sites had moved to the semantic names, so a caller following it read `undefined`.)
- impliedDiscountFactor: number; default: not declared — Implied discount factor `DF = −slope = e^(−rT)`.
- impliedRate: number; default: not declared — Implied continuously-compounded financing rate `r* = −ln(DF)/T`.
- iterations?: number; default: not declared — Iteration count for iterative methods.
- medianAbsoluteDeviationResidual: number; default: not declared — Median absolute deviation of the initial-fit residuals used for trimming.
- method?: string; default: not declared — Numerical method, e.g. `closed-form`, `brent`, `finite-difference`.
- perStrike: ParityStrikeResidual[]; default: not declared — Per-strike parity residuals for every usable strike (trimmed ones flagged).
- rSquared: number; default: not declared — Coefficient of determination of the final regression.
- selection?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing').SelectionReport; default: not declared — The structured engine-selection report (Gate C, `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing`): who was selected,
why, and — for automatic selection — every candidate considered with its verdict. This is the
machine-readable superset of `engine` + `autoReason` (which remain for compatibility);
`selected.name` always agrees with `engine` when both are present.
- selection.candidates?: readonly import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing').SelectionCandidate[]; default: not declared — Candidates an automatic selection considered; absent for explicit mode.
- selection.mode: 'explicit' | 'automatic'; default: not declared
- selection.reason: string; default: not declared — Why the selected engine answers this request.
- selection.selected: { name: string; version?: string; }; default: not declared
- selection.selected.name: string; default: not declared
- selection.selected.version?: string; default: not declared
- strikesUsed: number; default: not declared — Number of strikes used in the final fit (after trimming).
- timingMs?: number; default: not declared — Wall-clock timing in milliseconds, when measured.
- trimmedCount: number; default: not declared — Number of strikes trimmed as MAD outliers.
- trimmedStrikes: number[]; default: not declared — The strikes that were trimmed, ascending.
- warmup?: number; default: not declared — Series facades: number of leading output slots that are warmup sentinels (null/NaN) while the
computation seeds. Equals the input length when the indicator never emitted.
- warnings: QuantWarning[]; default: not declared — Structured warnings; always present (possibly empty).

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/options#PriceResult

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Result of a pro `option.price(...)` call: a value envelope plus Greeks. `greeks` is OPTIONAL — absent
means "not computed" (e.g. a Monte-Carlo engine priced without the extra Greek budget). Absent is never
the same as a genuine zero: engines never fabricate `{delta:0, …}`. It is the **first-order** `Greeks`
by default, or the full {@link ExtendedGreeks} when the call passes `{ extendedGreeks: true }`.

```typescript
/**
 * Result of a pro `option.price(...)` call: a value envelope plus Greeks. `greeks` is OPTIONAL — absent
 * means "not computed" (e.g. a Monte-Carlo engine priced without the extra Greek budget). Absent is never
 * the same as a genuine zero: engines never fabricate `{delta:0, …}`. It is the **first-order** `Greeks`
 * by default, or the full {@link ExtendedGreeks} when the call passes `{ extendedGreeks: true }`.
 */
export interface PriceResult extends Computed<number> {
    greeks?: Greeks | ExtendedGreeks;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- assumptions: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Assumptions<Record<never, never>>; default: not declared — Every applied convention, echoed back.
- assumptions.asOf?: number; default: not declared
- assumptions.calendar?: string; default: not declared
- assumptions.calendarVersion?: string; default: not declared
- assumptions.compounding?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').InterestCompounding; default: not declared
- assumptions.compounding.periodsPerYear: number; default: not declared
- assumptions.compounding.type: 'periodic'; default: not declared
- assumptions.conventionsVersion: string; default: not declared
- assumptions.dayCount?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').DayCount; default: not declared
- assumptions.dividendModel?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').DividendModel; default: not declared
- assumptions.engine?: string; default: not declared
- assumptions.expiryConvention?: 'us-equity-close' | 'explicit-instant'; default: not declared — How the contract's expiry label was resolved to an instant: `'us-equity-close'` when a
date-only `YYYY-MM-DD` expiry resolved to the US equity/options close — 16:00 America/New_York,
or 13:00 on an early-close day;
`'explicit-instant'` when the caller supplied a zoned datetime. Named so the convention is
never silent (alignment spec P1.6); instrument builders own the full story in Phase 3.
- assumptions.model?: string; default: not declared
- assumptions.seed?: number; default: not declared — The randomness seed this result was computed under — REQUIRED echo for a
`randomness: 'seeded'` Pricer (Gate C, 2026-08-23): a stochastic result that does not name
its seed cannot be replayed from the result alone. Deterministic paths never set it.
- assumptions.timeToExpiryConvention?: never; default: not declared
- assumptions.timeToExpiryYears?: number; default: not declared
- assumptions.units?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').GreekUnits; default: not declared
- assumptions.units.rho: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').RhoUnit; default: not declared

The sample-variance formula `√(s²/n)` assumes independent draws. A low-discrepancy sequence is
deterministic and negatively correlated by construction, so that formula does not estimate its
error: at 16k Sobol points on a European call it overstated the true deviation by ~75×, and a
confidence interval built from it was neither a confidence nor an interval. QMC error is
estimated by RANDOMIZING the sequence (scrambling/shifting) and taking the variance ACROSS
independent randomizations — which this estimator does not do, so it reports `null` and says so.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/options#SabrOptions

```typescript
export interface SabrOptions {
    /** Hagan expansion (default `'lognormal'`). */
    volatilityType?: SabrVolatilityType;
    /** Compute Greeks by finite differences (default `true`). */
    greeks?: boolean;
    /**
     * Compute the full higher-order (extended) Greek set (implies `greeks`). Volatility Greeks (vega, vanna, …)
     * are w.r.t. the SABR level `α` — extending the `vega` convention; `phi = 0` (forward model). Hagan's
     * vol is smooth, so the finite differences are stable.
     */
    extendedGreeks?: boolean;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- extendedGreeks?: boolean; default: not declared — Compute the full higher-order (extended) Greek set (implies `greeks`). Volatility Greeks (vega, vanna, …)
are w.r.t. the SABR level `α` — extending the `vega` convention; `phi = 0` (forward model). Hagan's
vol is smooth, so the finite differences are stable.
- greeks?: boolean; default: not declared — Compute Greeks by finite differences (default `true`).
- volatilityType?: SabrVolatilityType; default: not declared — Hagan expansion (default `'lognormal'`).

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/options#americanExercise

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Decompose an American option into its European value plus early-exercise premium, recover the exercise
boundary `S*(τ)`, and say whether to exercise now. See `docs/specs/american-exercise.md`.

```typescript
export declare function americanExercise(input: AmericanExerciseInput): AmericanExerciseResult;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (input): AmericanExerciseInput; default: not declared
- (input).contract: OptionContract; default: not declared
- (input).market: OptionMarket; default: not declared
- (input).options?: AmericanExerciseOptions; default: not declared
- return.american: number; default: not declared — American value (Barone–Adesi–Whaley).
- return.assumptions: { conventionsVersion: string; dividendModel: DividendModel; timeToExpiryYears: number; valueEngine: 'barone-adesi-whaley'; }; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.conventionsVersion: string; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.dividendModel: DividendModel; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.timeToExpiryYears: number; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.valueEngine: 'barone-adesi-whaley'; default: not declared
- return.boundary: BoundaryPoint[]; default: not declared — The `S*(τ)` curve over the remaining life (empty when never optimal).
- return.criticalSpot: number | null; default: not declared — `S*(τ)` at the current maturity; `null` when early exercise is never optimal.
- return.diagnostics: Diagnostics; default: not declared
- return.earlyExerciseCanBeOptimal: boolean; default: not declared — `false` for a non-dividend call (early exercise never optimal).
- return.earlyExercisePremium: number; default: not declared — `american − european ≥ 0` — the dollars the early-exercise right adds.
- return.european: number; default: not declared — European value (BSM) — the value stripped of the early-exercise right.
- return.intrinsic: number; default: not declared
- return.optionType: 'call' | 'put'; default: not declared — Which leg was analysed — `'call'` or `'put'`.

Named `optionType` because that is what it holds: in TotalFinance `style` is the EXERCISE style
(`'european' | 'american'`) everywhere else, and every one of these results is American by
construction, so a field called `style` reading `'put'` was a straight collision of two
vocabularies (pre-1.0 clean break, defect-fix wave, review-1).
- return.premiumFractionOfValue: number; default: not declared — `premium / american`.
- return.rationale: string; default: not declared — Prose an agent relays.
- return.shouldExerciseNow: boolean; default: not declared — The American value has collapsed to intrinsic — no time value left to give up.
- return.spot: number; default: not declared
- return.spotToBoundary: number | null; default: not declared — Signed fraction of spot to the boundary (put: `(S−S*)/S`, call: `(S*−S)/S`); `null` if no boundary.
- return.timeValue: number; default: not declared — `american − intrinsic ≥ 0`.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/options#americanImpliedVolatility

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Solve the implied volatility of an American contract from `market.price` by inverting an American
pricing engine over σ with a safeguarded Brent bracket (`[1e-4, 5]`, expanded once to `[1e-6, 10]`).
No-arbitrage bounds use the American intrinsic (`max(S−K,0)` calls, `max(K−S,0)` puts, no
discounting): a price below intrinsic, above the upper bound, or at intrinsic (no time value to
imply a vol) fails honestly instead of returning a fabricated number. A European contract is
refused — its door is `option.impliedVolatility`, closed-form by default or engine-inverted when
an engine is named.

```typescript
export declare function americanImpliedVolatility(input: AmericanImpliedVolatilityInput): ImpliedVolatilitySolveResult;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (input): AmericanImpliedVolatilityInput; default: not declared
- (input).contract: OptionContract; default: not declared
- (input).market: OptionMarket; default: not declared
- (input).options?: AmericanImpliedVolatilityOptions; default: not declared
- return.assumptions: Assumptions<Record<never, never>>; default: not declared — Every applied convention, echoed back.
- return.diagnostics: (import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Diagnostics) | (import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/options').ImpliedVolatilityDiagnostics); default: not declared — How the value was computed, plus any warnings.
- return.provenance?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Provenance; default: not declared — Optional data lineage when the inputs came from a provider.
- return.value: number | null; default: not declared — The computed value. Never `NaN` or `±Infinity`: a value the model cannot produce is `null`
beside a diagnostic that says why (Law 7 — a warning never licenses a non-finite number).

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/options#boxSpreadRate

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Implied financing rate from the box spread between strikes `k1 < k2`.

A box (bull call spread `+` bear put spread) locks in `(k2 − k1)` at expiry for a net debit
`box = (C(k1) − C(k2)) + (P(k2) − P(k1))`, so `box = (k2 − k1)·e^(−rT)` and
`rate = −ln(box / (k2 − k1)) / T`. Throws `parity.strike_unavailable` when a needed leg is missing.

```typescript
export declare function boxSpreadRate(input: BoxSpreadRateInput): BoxSpreadResult;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (input): BoxSpreadRateInput; default: not declared
- (input).expiry: string; default: not declared
- (input).lowerStrike: number; default: not declared
- (input).options: BoxSpreadOptions; default: not declared
- (input).quotes: readonly OptionQuote[]; default: not declared
- (input).upperStrike: number; default: not declared
- return.assumptions: BoxSpreadAssumptions; default: not declared
- return.diagnostics: BoxSpreadDiagnostics; default: not declared
- return.value: number; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/options#compareEngines

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Price one contract across many engines and report each engine's value, Greeks, convergence,
timing, and deviation from a high-resolution reference (spec §9.7). Rows are sorted most-accurate
first. This is the tool for choosing an engine and for validating new ones against the lattice
convergence benchmark — no silent "best" pick, every number is shown with its diagnostics.

Supply a custom panel as `options.engines`; all request fields live in one object so adding a
benchmark or clock never creates a second calling form.

```typescript
export declare function compareEngines(input: CompareEnginesInput): EngineComparison;
```

- (input).options.now?: () => number; default: not declared — Optional monotonic clock (e.g. `() => performance.now()`). When supplied, each engine's
wall-clock pricing time is measured into `timingMs`. Omitted by default so the function stays

- (input).options.reference?: OptionPricingEngine; default: not declared — Convergence benchmark. Defaults to a 1001-step Leisen–Reimer lattice.

- return.reference: { engine: string; value: number; }; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/options#defineOptionPricingEngine

Define a custom pricing engine (spec §22.1). TotalFinance treats it like any built-in engine: pass it
to `option.price({ contract: contract, market: market, engine: engine })`.

```typescript
export declare function defineOptionPricingEngine(engine: OptionPricingEngine): OptionPricingEngine;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):
