- extendedGreeks: (input: DigitalInput & { type: OptionType; kind: DigitalKind; }) => Computed<ExtendedGreeks>; default: not declared — The full higher-order (extended) Greek set for the European binary — completing {@link digital.greeks}
with vanna, charm, vomma, speed, color, phi, zomma, veta, vera, ultima, and lambda. The binary price is
a smooth function of `(S, σ, r, q, T)` for `T > 0`, so the higher-order Greeks are taken by central
finite differences of the exact `digital.price` closed form (the shared `finiteDifferenceExtendedGreeks`

binary's Greeks spike (pin risk) — they stay finite for `T > 0`, but very close to expiry-at-the-pin the
higher-order finite differences lose precision; widen `t` or read the sign/scale rather than the digit.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/options#european

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

European-exercise contract with the convention in the name (index-style options).

A DATE-ONLY expiry must say which instant it means: pass a zoned datetime, or add
`convention: 'us-equity-close'` to opt into the 16:00 ET close explicitly. The silent
US-equity default belongs to `usEquityCall`/`usEquityPut`, whose NAMES carry it — European
index products settle at different instants (AM auctions, European closes), so guessing here
would be silent economics (Law 6).

```typescript
export declare function european(input: InstrumentBuilderInput & { type: OptionType; convention?: 'us-equity-close'; }): OptionContract;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (input): InstrumentBuilderInput & { convention?: 'us-equity-close'; type: OptionType; }; default: not declared
- (input).convention?: 'us-equity-close'; default: not declared — REQUIRED for a date-only `expiry` (D2, one expiry law): a bare date does not name its
INSTANT, and the generic builders never guess one — `'us-equity-close'` options into the
16:00 ET session close explicitly. The `usEquityCall`/`usEquityPut` names carry it for you.
- (input).currency?: string; default: not declared
- (input).expiry: string; default: not declared — Expiry label: `YYYY-MM-DD` (requires `convention`) or a zoned ISO datetime.
- (input).multiplier?: number; default: not declared
- (input).root?: string; default: not declared
- (input).strike: number; default: not declared
- (input).type: OptionType; default: not declared
- (input).underlying: string; default: not declared
- return.adjusted?: boolean; default: not declared
- return.currency?: string; default: not declared
- return.deliverable?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Deliverable; default: not declared
- return.exerciseTime?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').ExerciseTime; default: not declared — AM- or PM-settled — settlement/display metadata. It does NOT move `expiresAt`: the expiry
instant always comes from the `expiry` label and `expiryConvention`. Express an AM-settled
index expiry as a zoned datetime (`'2026-09-18T09:30:00-04:00'`) when its instant matters.
- return.expiresAt: number; default: not declared — The exact expiration INSTANT the label resolved to (epoch ms), stamped by the builders at
construction: a bare date resolves via the named `expiryConvention`; a zoned datetime is the
caller's explicit instant. REQUIRED (E2, one expiry law): engines price against this
resolution and cross-validate it against the label — an unresolved literal is not a
contract; build one with the option builders.
- return.expiry: string; default: not declared — The expiry LABEL as supplied: `YYYY-MM-DD` (a calendar date) or a zoned ISO datetime.
- return.expiryConvention: 'us-equity-close' | 'explicit-instant'; default: not declared — HOW `expiry` resolved to `expiresAt` — named, never silent (spec P1.6/P3.4).
- return.multiplier?: number; default: not declared
- return.occSymbol?: string; default: not declared

- return.settlement?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Settlement; default: not declared
- return.strike: number; default: not declared
- return.style: OptionStyle; default: not declared — REQUIRED at build — never defaulted: US equity options are American, many index options European.
- return.type: OptionType; default: not declared
- return.underlying: string; default: not declared

The sample-variance formula `√(s²/n)` assumes independent draws. A low-discrepancy sequence is
deterministic and negatively correlated by construction, so that formula does not estimate its
error: at 16k Sobol points on a European call it overstated the true deviation by ~75×, and a
confidence interval built from it was neither a confidence nor an interval. QMC error is
estimated by RANDOMIZING the sequence (scrambling/shifting) and taking the variance ACROSS
independent randomizations — which this estimator does not do, so it reports `null` and says so.
- monteCarloEstimate().return.value: number; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/options#impliedForward

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Implied forward `F` from put-call parity across one expiry's chain.

Regresses `C(K) − P(K)` on `K`; from `slope = −e^(−rT)` and `intercept = e^(−rT)·F`,
`F = −intercept / slope`. The supplied `rate` is echoed and compared against the
regression-implied financing rate (reported in `diagnostics.impliedRate`); it does not bias `F`.

```typescript
export declare function impliedForward(input: ImpliedForwardInput): ParityResult;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (input): ImpliedForwardInput; default: not declared

- (input).quotes: readonly OptionQuote[]; default: not declared
- return.assumptions: ParityAssumptions; default: not declared
- return.diagnostics: ParityDiagnostics; default: not declared
- return.value: number; default: not declared

the coin premium `V_usd/S`: delta and gamma carry the numeraire corrections (`Δ_coin = Δ_usd/S −
V_usd/S²`, `Γ_coin = Γ_usd/S − 2Δ_usd/S² + 2V_usd/S³`), while vega/theta/rho scale by `1/S`. The `usd`
greeks equal the vanilla BSM greeks. The `−V_coin/S` delta term is the embedded short-coin from the
coin-denominated premium — an inverse option is NOT hedged at its Black–Scholes delta.
- greeks().return.assumptions: Assumptions<Record<never, never>>; default: not declared — Every applied convention, echoed back.
- greeks().return.diagnostics: Diagnostics; default: not declared — How the value was computed, plus any warnings.
- greeks().return.provenance?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Provenance; default: not declared — Optional data lineage when the inputs came from a provider.
- greeks().return.value: InverseGreeks; default: not declared — The computed value. Never `NaN` or `±Infinity`: a value the model cannot produce is `null`
beside a diagnostic that says why (Law 7 — a warning never licenses a non-finite number).
- greeks(input): InverseOptionInput & { type: OptionType; }; default: not declared
- greeks(input).coinYield?: number; default: not declared — Coin (base-currency) yield — lending/staking. Default 0. Enters the forward as the dividend yield.
- greeks(input).riskFreeRate: number; default: not declared — USD (quote-currency) risk-free rate.
- greeks(input).spot: number; default: not declared — Underlying spot, quote per coin (e.g. BTC/USD).
- greeks(input).strike: number; default: not declared — Strike, in the QUOTE currency (USD).
- greeks(input).timeToExpiryYears: number; default: not declared
- greeks(input).type: OptionType; default: not declared
- greeks(input).volatility: number; default: not declared — Volatility.
- monteCarloPrice: (input: InverseOptionInput & { type: OptionType; }, options: InverseOptionMonteCarloOptions) => ExoticMonteCarloResult; default: not declared — One-factor **coin-numeraire** Monte-Carlo: under the coin money-market numeraire the spot drifts at the
self-quanto rate `r − q + σ²`, and the coin premium is `E[e^{−qT}·(±(S_T−K))⁺/S_T]`. Converges to the
closed-form coin premium, corroborating the `V_usd/S` identity from the other measure.
- monteCarloPrice().return.assumptions: Assumptions<Record<never, never>>; default: not declared — Every applied convention, echoed back.
- monteCarloPrice().return.diagnostics: Diagnostics; default: not declared — How the value was computed, plus any warnings.
- monteCarloPrice().return.monteCarlo: MonteCarloStatistics; default: not declared
- monteCarloPrice().return.provenance?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Provenance; default: not declared — Optional data lineage when the inputs came from a provider.
- monteCarloPrice().return.value: number; default: not declared — The computed value. Never `NaN` or `±Infinity`: a value the model cannot produce is `null`
beside a diagnostic that says why (Law 7 — a warning never licenses a non-finite number).
- monteCarloPrice(input): InverseOptionInput & { type: OptionType; }; default: not declared
- monteCarloPrice(input).coinYield?: number; default: not declared — Coin (base-currency) yield — lending/staking. Default 0. Enters the forward as the dividend yield.

The sample-variance formula `√(s²/n)` assumes independent draws. A low-discrepancy sequence is
deterministic and negatively correlated by construction, so that formula does not estimate its
error: at 16k Sobol points on a European call it overstated the true deviation by ~75×, and a
confidence interval built from it was neither a confidence nor an interval. QMC error is
estimated by RANDOMIZING the sequence (scrambling/shifting) and taking the variance ACROSS
independent randomizations — which this estimator does not do, so it reports `null` and says so.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/options#optionChainHealth

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Consolidated chain-health report. Structural malformations throw indexed InputError; absent
prices/timestamps, empty chains and unavailable inverses are valid reports, never fake IVs.

Omit config.model for quote health and coverage only: market needs just underlying and asOf,
with no invented spot/rate/yield. Each model.status is 'not-requested', bounds/IV are null and
the solver is not run. Select config.model: 'black-scholes-merton' to additionally assess
compatibility under BSM dynamics, supplying market.spot and riskFreeRate (dividendYield follows
the package rule: omitted is 0, echoed and disclosed). Each row is assessed under its OWN
exercise style — a European row against the discounted closed-form band and inverse, an American
row against the undiscounted intrinsic band and the Bjerksund–Stensland 2002 engine — never as
the other style. This is quote health plus SELECTED model compatibility, NOT certification of all
option pricing. Nonempty canonical DiscreteDividend schedules and adjusted deliverables report
unsupported; no escrowed-dividend approximation is performed here.

No clock, rate, exercise, or quote-source inference. Prices are per underlying share;
multiplier and unconsumed provider fields are ignored. Stale/future/wide quotes are retained and
may be inverted with their warnings attached; crossed markets are not inverted. BSM compatibility
is NOT proof of quote validity, nor is incompatibility proof of a bad market observation. This
report checks individual model bounds, not cross-strike/calendar static arbitrage.

Controls are closed. Quote/contract/dividend observations are open and never mutated. Coverage
counts all observations (including expired/unavailable), not an automatically filtered universe.
Expected contracts use pricing identity; different venue/multiplier metadata does not create a
second slot. A missing call/put side is only an observed-grid gap unless explicitly expected.

Work: ≤10,000 quotes, ≤10,000 expected contracts, ≤1,000 dividends, bounded strings and at most
100 Brent iterations per quote. All lengths are checked before row traversal or result allocation.
Rows preserve input order; coverage and missing-contract identities are sorted deterministically.

```typescript
export declare function optionChainHealth(input: OptionChainHealthInput): OptionChainHealthReport;
```

Example (source JSDoc):
```ts
import { option, optionChainHealth } from '@insiderfinance/totalfinance/options';

const contract = option.call({
  underlying: 'X', style: 'european', strike: 100,
  expiry: '2027-01-01T00:00:00Z',
});
const report = optionChainHealth({
  quotes: [{ contract, timestampMs: 1767225600000, bid: 7.9, ask: 8.1 }],
  market: { underlying: 'X', spot: 100, asOf: '2026-01-01T00:00:00Z', riskFreeRate: 0, dividendYield: 0 },
  config: {
    model: 'black-scholes-merton', priceSource: 'mid', maximumQuoteAgeMs: 60_000,
    maximumRelativeSpread: 0.1,
  },
});
if (!report.rows[0]?.model.solver.converged) throw new Error('IV unavailable');
// One-year ATM price 8 => annualized IV about 0.20086744, NOT an assumed 20%.
if (Math.abs(report.rows[0].model.impliedVolatility! - 0.20086744) > 1e-7) throw new Error('Unexpected IV');
if (report.coverage.expiries[0]?.missingPutStrikes[0] !== 100) throw new Error('Expected unobserved put side');

const quotesOnly = optionChainHealth({
  quotes: [{ contract, timestampMs: 1767225600000, bid: 9, ask: 7 }],
  market: { underlying: 'X', asOf: '2026-01-01T00:00:00Z' },
  config: { priceSource: 'mid', maximumQuoteAgeMs: 60_000, maximumRelativeSpread: 0.1 },
});
if (quotesOnly.summary.issueCounts.crossed !== 1) throw new Error('Expected crossed quote');
if (quotesOnly.rows[0]?.model.status !== 'not-requested') throw new Error('No model requested');
```

The SABR model namespace — the grouped, discoverable surface over the flat `sabr*` functions.
`sabr.volatility` / `sabr.price` / `sabr.monteCarloPrice` / `sabr.monteCarloEstimate` are the same functions; prefer the
namespace over the deprecated flat exports.

```typescript
export declare const sabr: { readonly monteCarloEstimate: (input: SabrMonteCarloEstimateInput) => MonteCarloEstimate; readonly monteCarloPrice: (request: SabrPriceMonteCarloRequest) => SabrMonteCarloResult; readonly price: (request: SabrPriceRequest) => PriceResult; readonly volatility: (request: SabrVolatilityRequest) => number; };
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- monteCarloEstimate: (input: SabrMonteCarloEstimateInput) => MonteCarloEstimate; default: not declared
- monteCarloEstimate().return.confidenceInterval: [number, number] | null; default: not declared — Confidence interval at the requested level (default 95%); `null` whenever `standardError` is.
- monteCarloEstimate().return.converged: boolean; default: not declared — Whether the estimate is trustworthy (finite value and standard error).
- monteCarloEstimate().return.method: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/options').MonteCarloMethod; default: not declared — The sampling method actually used (may differ from the request if QMC fell back to pseudo).
- monteCarloEstimate().return.paths: number; default: not declared — Number of paths actually evaluated (antithetic pairs count as one path).
- monteCarloEstimate().return.seed: number; default: not declared — The seed, echoed for reproducibility.
- monteCarloEstimate().return.standardError: number | null; default: not declared — Standard error of the mean estimate — `null` for the QUASI-random methods (`sobol`, `halton`).

The sample-variance formula `√(s²/n)` assumes independent draws. A low-discrepancy sequence is
deterministic and negatively correlated by construction, so that formula does not estimate its
error: at 16k Sobol points on a European call it overstated the true deviation by ~75×, and a
confidence interval built from it was neither a confidence nor an interval. QMC error is
estimated by RANDOMIZING the sequence (scrambling/shifting) and taking the variance ACROSS
independent randomizations — which this estimator does not do, so it reports `null` and says so.
- monteCarloEstimate().return.value: number; default: not declared

whose contract documents vendor decoration (Law 12: entries stay open). `toJSONSchema()` then
emits the complete `properties`/`required` map with `additionalProperties: true`, so MCP
tools, agents, and generated forms see the real field shape instead of a shapeless object.

Distinct from parse-time `mode: 'passthrough'` on purpose: openness declared here is a
property of the PAYLOAD's contract (every caller, every mode, and the emitted JSON Schema all
agree), while `passthrough` is one caller's per-parse leniency toward a schema that itself
remains closed. Like every refiner, returns a NEW schema; the receiver stays closed.

property of the PAYLOAD's contract (every caller, every mode, and the emitted JSON Schema all
agree), while `passthrough` is one caller's per-parse leniency toward a schema that itself
remains closed. Like every refiner, returns a NEW schema; the receiver stays closed.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/options#selectQuotePrice

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Resolve a single price from an option quote per the requested source. Returns `undefined` when
the requested fields are absent. `mid` falls back to (bid+ask)/2 when an explicit mid is missing.
Quote records are structural artifacts, so venue/provenance fields and declared subtypes may
decorate them; only the fields consumed by the selected source are interpreted here.

Kind: value; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

```typescript
export declare const touch: { readonly greeks: (input: TouchInput & { kind: TouchKind; }) => Computed<Greeks>; readonly monteCarloPrice: (input: TouchInput & { kind: TouchKind; }, options: TouchMonteCarloOptions) => ExoticMonteCarloResult; readonly price: (input: TouchInput & { kind: TouchKind; }) => ExoticResult; };
```

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/options#usEquityOption

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

US listed equity option from DATA (B7): either an OCC symbol, or `type` plus the fields
`usEquityCall`/`usEquityPut` take. The two named builders remain the sugar; this is the door a
chain row, a fill, or a broker symbol goes through without branching on `type` first. A field
given beside `occSymbol` must agree with the symbol — a contradiction is refused, never resolved
by preference.

```typescript
export declare function usEquityOption(input: UsEquityOptionInput): OptionContract;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (input): UsEquityOptionInput; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/options#validateOptionPricingEngine

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Behaviorally verify a custom pricing engine against CALLER-SUPPLIED fixtures. Registration via
{@link defineOptionPricingEngine} is deliberately side-effect-free; this explicit companion is
the place for potentially expensive pricing calls and therefore works for spot, forward,
stateful, remote, and domain-specific engines without TotalFinance guessing their inputs.

At least one probe is required for every claimed exercise style. Each probe verifies
`supports()`, a finite non-negative price, Greek capability claims, extended-Greek claims, and
repeat-call value equality when `deterministic` is true. The validated immutable engine is
returned for convenient inline use.

```typescript
export declare function validateOptionPricingEngine(engine: OptionPricingEngine, probes: readonly OptionPricingEngineProbe[]): OptionPricingEngine;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (engine): OptionPricingEngine; default: not declared
- (engine).capabilities: EngineCapabilities; default: not declared — Machine-readable capabilities, behaviorally verified by the engine contract suite (Law 8).
- (engine).capabilities.deterministic: boolean; default: not declared — Same inputs → identical outputs. `false` marks stochastic engines (Monte-Carlo): a FIXED SEED
makes them reproducible, which is what the contract suite verifies for them.
- (engine).capabilities.dividends: readonly ('continuous' | 'none' | 'discrete')[]; default: not declared — Dividend models the engine honors.
- (engine).capabilities.extendedGreeks: boolean; default: not declared — Whether the extended (higher-order) Greek set is available on request.
- (engine).capabilities.greeks: 'none' | 'analytic' | 'finite-difference' | 'delegated'; default: not declared — How first-order Greeks are produced when requested: closed-form (`analytic`), bump-and-reprice
(`finite-difference`), by the selected delegate (`delegated`, meta-engines), or not at all
(`none` — requests are disclosed as unhonored, never silently dropped).
- (engine).capabilities.styles: readonly OptionStyle[]; default: not declared — Exercise styles this engine prices (must agree with `supports()`).
- (engine).name: string; default: not declared
- (engine).price: (input: OptionEnginePriceInput) => PriceResult; default: not declared
- (engine).supports: (contract: OptionContract) => boolean; default: not declared — Whether this engine can price the given contract.
- (engine).version: string; default: not declared
- (probes): readonly OptionPricingEngineProbe[]; default: not declared
- return.capabilities: EngineCapabilities; default: not declared — Machine-readable capabilities, behaviorally verified by the engine contract suite (Law 8).
- return.capabilities.deterministic: boolean; default: not declared — Same inputs → identical outputs. `false` marks stochastic engines (Monte-Carlo): a FIXED SEED
makes them reproducible, which is what the contract suite verifies for them.
- return.capabilities.dividends: readonly ('continuous' | 'none' | 'discrete')[]; default: not declared — Dividend models the engine honors.
- return.capabilities.extendedGreeks: boolean; default: not declared — Whether the extended (higher-order) Greek set is available on request.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/options#vanillaIntrinsic

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Gross vanilla intrinsic value per unit: `max(underlyingPrice − strike, 0)` for a call,
`max(strike − underlyingPrice, 0)` for a put.

A plain number out, and nothing else in: no premium (this is not P&L), no quantity or multiplier
(per unit), no volatility or time (intrinsic is model-free). `underlyingPrice` and `strike` must be
finite and `>= 0` — zero is legal on either leg (a worthless underlying or a zero strike still has
a well-defined intrinsic value).

```typescript
export declare function vanillaIntrinsic(input: VanillaIntrinsicInput): number;
```

Example (source JSDoc):
```ts
import { vanillaIntrinsic } from '@insiderfinance/totalfinance/options/payoff';

vanillaIntrinsic({ type: 'call', underlyingPrice: 112, strike: 100 }); // 12
vanillaIntrinsic({ type: 'put', underlyingPrice: 88, strike: 100 }); // 12
vanillaIntrinsic({ type: 'put', underlyingPrice: 112, strike: 100 }); // 0
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (input): VanillaIntrinsicInput; default: not declared
- (input).strike: number; default: not declared — The option's strike price per unit.
- (input).type: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').OptionType; default: not declared — Which leg — `'call'` or `'put'`.
- (input).underlyingPrice: number; default: not declared — The underlying's price per unit, in the same currency unit as `strike`.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/options#volatilitySwap

Kind: value; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

```typescript
export declare const volatilitySwap: { readonly approximateFairVolatility: (input: { fairVariance: number; varianceOfVariance?: number; }) => number; };
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- approximateFairVolatility: (input: { fairVariance: number; varianceOfVariance?: number; }) => number; default: not declared — Brockhaus–Long convexity-adjusted fair vol:
`K_vol ≈ √K_var·(1 − Var[realized variance]/(8·K_var²))`. With no variance-of-variance it reduces
to `√K_var`; the adjustment captures the (downward) Jensen gap between √E[var] and E[√var].

- approximateFairVolatility(input).varianceOfVariance?: number; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/options/bachelier#bachelierExtendedGreeks

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Bachelier (normal-model) higher-order Greeks (w.r.t. the forward `F` and the NORMAL vol `σ_N`). These
are the arithmetic-BM analogues of {@link blackScholesExtendedGreeks } — different formulas, since the density is
`φ((F−K)/σ_N√T)`, and `vega`/`vanna`/… are per 1.00 of normal vol (price units). `phi` (dividend rho)
is 0 (a forward model has no dividend yield); `lambda = Δ·F/V`. All validated against finite
differences of the first-order Greeks / the price.

```typescript
export declare function bachelierExtendedGreeks(input: BachelierTypedInput): ExtendedGreeks;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (input): BachelierTypedInput; default: not declared
- (input).forward: number; default: not declared
- (input).normalVolatility: number; default: not declared — NORMAL (absolute) volatility in PRICE UNITS — deliberately NOT named `vol` (Law 4): the
lognormal decimal and the price-unit normal vol must never share a field name. `vega` is
reported per 1.00 of normal vol (`units.vega: perPoint`).
- (input).riskFreeRate: number; default: not declared
- (input).strike: number; default: not declared
- (input).timeToExpiryYears: number; default: not declared
- (input).type: OptionType; default: not declared
- return.charm: number; default: not declared
- return.color: number; default: not declared
- return.delta: number; default: not declared
- return.gamma: number; default: not declared
- return.lambda: number | null; default: not declared — Elasticity / effective leverage `Λ = Δ·S / V` (dimensionless). `null` when the price
underflows to zero (deep-OTM): elasticity is undefined at V = 0 and is disclosed as null with
a `greeks.lambda_undefined` warning on explained paths — never NaN/Infinity (Law 7).
- return.phi: number; default: not declared — Dividend rho (epsilon) `ε = ∂V/∂q`, per 1% dividend yield (scaled like `rho`).
- return.rho: number; default: not declared
- return.speed: number; default: not declared
- return.theta: number; default: not declared
- return.ultima: number; default: not declared — `∂vomma/∂σ = ∂³V/∂σ³` (raw).
- return.vanna: number; default: not declared
- return.vega: number; default: not declared
- return.vera: number; default: not declared — `∂rho/∂σ = ∂²V/∂r∂σ` (raw, per 1.00 σ; rho here is per 1.00 rate).
- return.veta: number; default: not declared — `∂vega/∂T` (raw, per year of time-to-expiry; vega here is per 1.00 σ) — the ∂/∂T sibling of vega.
- return.vomma: number; default: not declared
- return.zomma: number; default: not declared — `∂Γ/∂σ = ∂³V/∂S²∂σ` (raw, per 1.00 σ).

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/options/bachelier#bachelierImpliedVolatility

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Solve Bachelier (normal) implied volatility. Reports failure honestly. Endpoint acceptance uses
the same RELATIVE tolerance as the BSM kernel (see {@link impliedVolatilityPriceTolerance}), so a
target below the σ_N→0 price floor fails as `price_below_resolvable` instead of being "matched" by
the bracket's low endpoint. The normal model has no upper price bound (the call price grows
without limit in σ_N), so there is no above-max case here.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/options/batch#blackScholesEvaluateMany

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Black–Scholes–Merton outputs for every row of a columnar batch, computing ONLY the selected
outputs and their dependencies — `{ outputs: ['gamma'] }` evaluates no cumulative normal.

Validates the columns (closed keys, exact row counts), every row's values (positive finite spot,
strike, time and volatility; finite rate, dividend yield and type) and the selection, then
allocates one `Float64Array` per selected output. Values are bit-identical to the scalar
`blackScholes` functions on the same row. Units: theta per calendar day, vega and rho per 1%,
higher-order Greeks in the raw units of `blackScholes.extendedGreeks`.

```typescript
export declare function blackScholesEvaluateMany<const O extends BlackScholesOutputSelection>(columns: OptionBatchColumns, options: BlackScholesEvaluateManyOptions<O>): BlackScholesEvaluateManyResult<O>;
```

Example (source JSDoc):
const { gamma } = blackScholesEvaluateMany(columns, { outputs: ['gamma'] });

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (columns): OptionBatchColumns; default: not declared
- (columns).dividendYield?: Float64Array<ArrayBufferLike>; default: not declared — Optional per-row continuous dividend yield (defaults to 0).
- (columns).riskFreeRate: Float64Array<ArrayBufferLike>; default: not declared
- (columns).spot: Float64Array<ArrayBufferLike>; default: not declared
- (columns).strike: Float64Array<ArrayBufferLike>; default: not declared
- (columns).timeToExpiryYears: Float64Array<ArrayBufferLike>; default: not declared — Time to expiry in years.
- (columns).type: Int8Array<ArrayBufferLike>; default: not declared
- (columns).volatility: Float64Array<ArrayBufferLike>; default: not declared
- (options): BlackScholesEvaluateManyOptions<O>; default: not declared
- (options).outputs: O; default: not declared — The outputs to compute, e.g. `['gamma']` or `['price', 'delta']`. Required, nonempty, dense and
duplicate-free; only these are computed and returned.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/options/batch#blackScholesEvaluateManyInto

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Write the selected Black–Scholes–Merton outputs for every row into caller-owned buffers — the
zero-allocation form of {@link blackScholesEvaluateMany} for hot loops that reuse storage. The
property names of `outputs` are the selection: `{ gamma: buffer }` computes gamma only.

Reusable storage is not unchecked input. Before anything is written this validates the columns
and every row's values exactly as {@link blackScholesEvaluateMany} does, and every buffer: a
`Float64Array` (not a plain array or another typed array) with at least one element per row. No
buffer may overlap an input column or another output buffer in memory — not even an exact alias —
because a write would then change values that are still to be read or returned. A rejected call
writes nothing; a successful one writes elements `[0, rows)` of each buffer and leaves the rest
untouched. An `undefined` entry is treated as omitted.

```typescript
export declare function blackScholesEvaluateManyInto(columns: OptionBatchColumns, outputs: BlackScholesOutputBuffers): void;
```

Example (source JSDoc):
const gamma = new Float64Array(capacity);
blackScholesEvaluateManyInto(columns, { gamma });

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (columns): OptionBatchColumns; default: not declared
- (columns).dividendYield?: Float64Array<ArrayBufferLike>; default: not declared — Optional per-row continuous dividend yield (defaults to 0).
- (columns).riskFreeRate: Float64Array<ArrayBufferLike>; default: not declared
- (columns).spot: Float64Array<ArrayBufferLike>; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/options/black-scholes#blackScholesExtendedGreeks

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Higher-order Greeks under BSM (spec §9.4), analytic and exact. First-order fields (`delta`…`rho`)
carry the same default units as {@link blackScholesGreeks}; the second/third-order fields are in raw units:
  - `vanna` = ∂Δ/∂σ = ∂²V/∂S∂σ  (per 1.00 σ, per $),
  - `vomma` = ∂(vega)/∂σ = ∂²V/∂σ²  (per 1.00 σ²; vega here is per 1.00 σ),
  - `charm` = ∂Δ/∂T  (delta drift per added year of time-to-expiry),
  - `speed` = ∂Γ/∂S = ∂³V/∂S³,
  - `color` = ∂Γ/∂T  (gamma drift per added year of time-to-expiry),
  - `phi`   = ε = ∂V/∂q  (dividend rho, per 1% dividend yield — scaled like rho),
  - `zomma` = ∂Γ/∂σ = ∂³V/∂S²∂σ,
  - `veta`  = ∂vega/∂T  (per year of time-to-expiry; the ∂/∂T sibling of vega),
  - `vera`  = ∂rho/∂σ = ∂²V/∂r∂σ,
  - `ultima`= ∂vomma/∂σ = ∂³V/∂σ³,
  - `lambda`= Δ·S/V  (elasticity / effective leverage, dimensionless).
All are validated against finite differences of the first-order Greeks / the price.

```typescript
export declare function blackScholesExtendedGreeks(input: BlackScholesKernelInput): ExtendedGreeks;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (input): BlackScholesKernelInput; default: not declared
- (input).dividendYield: number; default: not declared
- (input).riskFreeRate: number; default: not declared
- (input).spot: number; default: not declared
- (input).strike: number; default: not declared
- (input).timeToExpiryYears: number; default: not declared
- (input).type: OptionType; default: not declared
- (input).volatility: number; default: not declared
- return.charm: number; default: not declared
- return.color: number; default: not declared
- return.delta: number; default: not declared
- return.gamma: number; default: not declared
- return.lambda: number | null; default: not declared — Elasticity / effective leverage `Λ = Δ·S / V` (dimensionless). `null` when the price
underflows to zero (deep-OTM): elasticity is undefined at V = 0 and is disclosed as null with
a `greeks.lambda_undefined` warning on explained paths — never NaN/Infinity (Law 7).
- return.phi: number; default: not declared — Dividend rho (epsilon) `ε = ∂V/∂q`, per 1% dividend yield (scaled like `rho`).
- return.rho: number; default: not declared
- return.speed: number; default: not declared
- return.theta: number; default: not declared
- return.ultima: number; default: not declared — `∂vomma/∂σ = ∂³V/∂σ³` (raw).
- return.vanna: number; default: not declared
- return.vega: number; default: not declared
- return.vera: number; default: not declared — `∂rho/∂σ = ∂²V/∂r∂σ` (raw, per 1.00 σ; rho here is per 1.00 rate).
- return.veta: number; default: not declared — `∂vega/∂T` (raw, per year of time-to-expiry; vega here is per 1.00 σ) — the ∂/∂T sibling of vega.
- return.vomma: number; default: not declared
- return.zomma: number; default: not declared — `∂Γ/∂σ = ∂³V/∂S²∂σ` (raw, per 1.00 σ).

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/options/black-scholes#blackScholesImpliedVolatility

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Solve implied volatility from a price using Brent with no-arbitrage bound checks.

Returns `converged: false` with a machine-readable `reason` on failure — never a fabricated value
(design law #4). Three ways there is no answer, reported apart: the price violates the intrinsic
floor (`below_intrinsic`), it sits at or above the upper no-arbitrage bound, which is a SUPREMUM
attained only as σ→∞ (`above_max_bound`), or it is below the model price at the lowest σ in the
bracket (`price_below_resolvable`).

```typescript
export declare function blackScholesImpliedVolatility(input: BlackScholesImpliedVolatilityKernelInput): BlackScholesImpliedVolatilityResult;
```

- (input).riskFreeRate: number; default: not declared
- (input).spot: number; default: not declared
- (input).strike: number; default: not declared
- (input).timeToExpiryYears: number; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/options/black-scholes#blackScholesPrice

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Black–Scholes–Merton price for a European call/put with continuous dividend yield `q`.

This is the seed defect Phase 3B was opened on. It validated the object and the `type` enum, then
destructured six numeric fields and checked none of them: omitting `volatility` made `sigma`
`undefined`, `d1` `NaN`, and the returned PRICE `NaN` — handed back as a success, through a
declaration that said the field was required. A pricing function that answers `NaN` is worse than
one that throws, because every layer above it treats the answer as a number.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/options/black76#black76ExtendedGreeks

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Black-76 higher-order Greeks (w.r.t. the forward `F`). The forward-price derivatives (vanna, charm,
vomma, speed, color, zomma, veta, ultima) coincide with BSM's at `S = F`, `q = r` — Black-76 has the
same `d1`/`d2` and discount as that BSM instance — so they are borrowed from {@link blackScholesExtendedGreeks};
the forward-model-specific ones are computed directly:
  - `vera` = ∂rho/∂σ = ∂(−T·price)/∂σ = −T·vega,
  - `phi`  = 0 (the forward model has no dividend yield; carry is embedded in `F`),
  - `lambda` = Δ·F/V.
First-order fields (theta/rho) come from {@link black76Greeks}, which are the Black-76 conventions.

```typescript
export declare function black76ExtendedGreeks(input: Black76TypedInput): ExtendedGreeks;
```

- (input): Black76TypedInput; default: not declared
- (input).forward: number; default: not declared
- (input).riskFreeRate: number; default: not declared
- (input).strike: number; default: not declared
- (input).timeToExpiryYears: number; default: not declared
- (input).type: OptionType; default: not declared
- (input).volatility: number; default: not declared
- return.charm: number; default: not declared
- return.color: number; default: not declared
- return.delta: number; default: not declared
- return.gamma: number; default: not declared
- return.lambda: number | null; default: not declared — Elasticity / effective leverage `Λ = Δ·S / V` (dimensionless). `null` when the price
underflows to zero (deep-OTM): elasticity is undefined at V = 0 and is disclosed as null with
a `greeks.lambda_undefined` warning on explained paths — never NaN/Infinity (Law 7).
- return.phi: number; default: not declared — Dividend rho (epsilon) `ε = ∂V/∂q`, per 1% dividend yield (scaled like `rho`).
- return.rho: number; default: not declared
- return.speed: number; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/options/heston#hestonMonteCarloEstimate

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Low-level kernel: Heston QE Monte-Carlo estimate of the discounted European payoff.

Expert kernel form (model-subpath surface) — the curated root surface is {@link heston.monteCarloEstimate}.

```typescript
export declare function hestonMonteCarloEstimate(input: HestonMonteCarloEstimateInput): MonteCarloEstimate;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (input): HestonMonteCarloEstimateInput; default: not declared
- (input).dividendYield: number; default: not declared
- (input).options: HestonMonteCarloOptions; default: not declared
- (input).parameters: HestonParameters; default: not declared
- (input).riskFreeRate: number; default: not declared
- (input).spot: number; default: not declared
- (input).strike: number; default: not declared
- (input).timeToExpiryYears: number; default: not declared
- (input).type: OptionType; default: not declared
- return.confidenceInterval: [number, number] | null; default: not declared — Confidence interval at the requested level (default 95%); `null` whenever `standardError` is.
- return.converged: boolean; default: not declared — Whether the estimate is trustworthy (finite value and standard error).
- return.method: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/options').MonteCarloMethod; default: not declared — The sampling method actually used (may differ from the request if QMC fell back to pseudo).
- return.paths: number; default: not declared — Number of paths actually evaluated (antithetic pairs count as one path).
- return.seed: number; default: not declared — The seed, echoed for reproducibility.
- return.standardError: number | null; default: not declared — Standard error of the mean estimate — `null` for the QUASI-random methods (`sobol`, `halton`).

The sample-variance formula `√(s²/n)` assumes independent draws. A low-discrepancy sequence is
deterministic and negatively correlated by construction, so that formula does not estimate its
error: at 16k Sobol points on a European call it overstated the true deviation by ~75×, and a
confidence interval built from it was neither a confidence nor an interval. QMC error is
estimated by RANDOMIZING the sequence (scrambling/shifting) and taking the variance ACROSS
independent randomizations — which this estimator does not do, so it reports `null` and says so.
- return.value: number; default: not declared
- return.varianceReduction: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/options').VarianceReduction; default: not declared — Which variance-reduction techniques were applied.
- return.warnings: QuantWarning[]; default: not declared — Structured warnings (e.g. a QMC dimension fallback).

- return.greeks.charm: number; default: not declared

- return.greeks.vanna: number; default: not declared
- return.greeks.vega: number; default: not declared
- return.greeks.vera: number; default: not declared — `∂rho/∂σ = ∂²V/∂r∂σ` (raw, per 1.00 σ; rho here is per 1.00 rate).
- return.greeks.veta: number; default: not declared — `∂vega/∂T` (raw, per year of time-to-expiry; vega here is per 1.00 σ) — the ∂/∂T sibling of vega.
- return.greeks.vomma: number; default: not declared
- return.greeks.zomma: number; default: not declared — `∂Γ/∂σ = ∂³V/∂S²∂σ` (raw, per 1.00 σ).
- return.monteCarlo: MonteCarloStatistics; default: not declared
- return.provenance?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Provenance; default: not declared — Optional data lineage when the inputs came from a provider.
- return.value: number; default: not declared — The computed value. Never `NaN` or `±Infinity`: a value the model cannot produce is `null`
beside a diagnostic that says why (Law 7 — a warning never licenses a non-finite number).

- return.greeks.phi: number; default: not declared — Dividend rho (epsilon) `ε = ∂V/∂q`, per 1% dividend yield (scaled like `rho`).
- return.greeks.rho: number; default: not declared
- return.greeks.speed: number; default: not declared
- return.greeks.theta: number; default: not declared
- return.greeks.ultima: number; default: not declared — `∂vomma/∂σ = ∂³V/∂σ³` (raw).
- return.greeks.vanna: number; default: not declared
- return.greeks.vega: number; default: not declared
- return.greeks.vera: number; default: not declared — `∂rho/∂σ = ∂²V/∂r∂σ` (raw, per 1.00 σ; rho here is per 1.00 rate).
- return.greeks.veta: number; default: not declared — `∂vega/∂T` (raw, per year of time-to-expiry; vega here is per 1.00 σ) — the ∂/∂T sibling of vega.
- return.greeks.vomma: number; default: not declared
- return.greeks.zomma: number; default: not declared — `∂Γ/∂σ = ∂³V/∂S²∂σ` (raw, per 1.00 σ).
- return.provenance?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Provenance; default: not declared — Optional data lineage when the inputs came from a provider.
- return.value: number; default: not declared — The computed value. Never `NaN` or `±Infinity`: a value the model cannot produce is `null`
beside a diagnostic that says why (Law 7 — a warning never licenses a non-finite number).

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/options/local-volatility#dupireLocalVolatility

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Build the Dupire local-volatility function σ_loc(level, t) from an implied-vol surface. The returned
function is pure and can be evaluated anywhere on the (level, t) plane; out-of-range or locally
arbitrageable points are floored at `floorVolatility` rather than returning NaN.

Expert kernel form (model-subpath surface) — the curated root surface is {@link localVolatility.fromImplied}.

```typescript
export declare function dupireLocalVolatility(input: DupireLocalVolatilityInput): LocalVolatilityFunction;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/options/local-volatility#localVolatilityGrid

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Precompute a local-volatility function onto a (level × time) grid and return a fast bilinear-interpolating
`LocalVolatilityFunction`. The exact `dupireLocalVolatility` does ~4 surface evaluations per call — far too slow to run
inside a Monte-Carlo step loop — so cache it once on a grid and interpolate. Off-grid queries clamp
to the nearest edge (a documented, no-NaN extrapolation).

Expert kernel form (model-subpath surface) — the curated root surface is {@link localVolatility.grid}.

```typescript
export declare function localVolatilityGrid(localVolatility: LocalVolatilityFunction, specification: LocalVolatilityGridSpecification): LocalVolatilityFunction;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (localVolatility): LocalVolatilityFunction; default: not declared
- (specification): LocalVolatilityGridSpecification; default: not declared
- (specification).levels: number[]; default: not declared — Underlying levels, ascending (e.g. 0.4·S₀ … 2.5·S₀).
- (specification).times: number[]; default: not declared — Times in years, ascending (e.g. up to the longest expiry priced).

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/options/local-volatility#localVolatilityMonteCarloEstimate

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Low-level kernel: local-volatility Monte-Carlo estimate of the discounted European payoff.

Expert kernel form (model-subpath surface) — the curated root surface is {@link localVolatility.monteCarloEstimate }.

```typescript
export declare function localVolatilityMonteCarloEstimate(input: LocalVolatilityMonteCarloEstimateInput): MonteCarloEstimate;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (input): LocalVolatilityMonteCarloEstimateInput; default: not declared
- (input).dividendYield: number; default: not declared
- (input).localVolatility: LocalVolatilityFunction; default: not declared
- (input).options: LocalVolatilityMonteCarloOptions; default: not declared
- (input).riskFreeRate: number; default: not declared
- (input).spot: number; default: not declared
- (input).strike: number; default: not declared
- (input).timeToExpiryYears: number; default: not declared
- (input).type: OptionType; default: not declared
- return.confidenceInterval: [number, number] | null; default: not declared — Confidence interval at the requested level (default 95%); `null` whenever `standardError` is.
- return.converged: boolean; default: not declared — Whether the estimate is trustworthy (finite value and standard error).
- return.method: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/options').MonteCarloMethod; default: not declared — The sampling method actually used (may differ from the request if QMC fell back to pseudo).
- return.paths: number; default: not declared — Number of paths actually evaluated (antithetic pairs count as one path).
- return.seed: number; default: not declared — The seed, echoed for reproducibility.
- return.standardError: number | null; default: not declared — Standard error of the mean estimate — `null` for the QUASI-random methods (`sobol`, `halton`).

The sample-variance formula `√(s²/n)` assumes independent draws. A low-discrepancy sequence is
deterministic and negatively correlated by construction, so that formula does not estimate its
error: at 16k Sobol points on a European call it overstated the true deviation by ~75×, and a
confidence interval built from it was neither a confidence nor an interval. QMC error is
estimated by RANDOMIZING the sequence (scrambling/shifting) and taking the variance ACROSS
independent randomizations — which this estimator does not do, so it reports `null` and says so.
- return.value: number; default: not declared
- return.varianceReduction: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/options').VarianceReduction; default: not declared — Which variance-reduction techniques were applied.
- return.warnings: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').QuantWarning[]; default: not declared — Structured warnings (e.g. a QMC dimension fallback).

Price a European contract by Monte-Carlo simulation, returning value, Greeks, assumptions, and the
MC error statistics (`result.mc`). Validates the market the same way the analytic engines do, and
applies the escrowed-spot model for discrete dividends.

```typescript
/**
 * Price a European contract by Monte-Carlo simulation, returning value, Greeks, assumptions, and the

 * applies the escrowed-spot model for discrete dividends.
 */
export interface MonteCarloPriceInput {

    market: OptionMarket;
    options: MonteCarloPriceOptions;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- contract.expiresAt: number; default: not declared — The exact expiration INSTANT the label resolved to (epoch ms), stamped by the builders at

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/options/monte-carlo#monteCarloEuropean

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Low-level kernel: estimate the discounted European payoff on GBM. Inputs are assumed validated
(S, K, T, σ all > 0). Uses the discounted terminal price as a control variate.

The raw kernel remains direct and assumption-light, but its financially interchangeable values
are named so a transposed rate, yield, time, or volatility cannot typecheck unnoticed.

```typescript
export declare function monteCarloEuropean(input: MonteCarloEuropeanInput): MonteCarloEstimate;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (input): MonteCarloEuropeanInput; default: not declared
- (input).dividendYield: number; default: not declared
- (input).options: MonteCarloPriceOptions; default: not declared
- (input).riskFreeRate: number; default: not declared
- (input).spot: number; default: not declared
- (input).strike: number; default: not declared
- (input).timeToExpiryYears: number; default: not declared
- (input).type: OptionType; default: not declared
- (input).volatility: number; default: not declared
- return.confidenceInterval: [number, number] | null; default: not declared — Confidence interval at the requested level (default 95%); `null` whenever `standardError` is.
- return.converged: boolean; default: not declared — Whether the estimate is trustworthy (finite value and standard error).
- return.method: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/options').MonteCarloMethod; default: not declared — The sampling method actually used (may differ from the request if QMC fell back to pseudo).
- return.paths: number; default: not declared — Number of paths actually evaluated (antithetic pairs count as one path).
- return.seed: number; default: not declared — The seed, echoed for reproducibility.
- return.standardError: number | null; default: not declared — Standard error of the mean estimate — `null` for the QUASI-random methods (`sobol`, `halton`).

The sample-variance formula `√(s²/n)` assumes independent draws. A low-discrepancy sequence is
deterministic and negatively correlated by construction, so that formula does not estimate its
error: at 16k Sobol points on a European call it overstated the true deviation by ~75×, and a
confidence interval built from it was neither a confidence nor an interval. QMC error is
estimated by RANDOMIZING the sequence (scrambling/shifting) and taking the variance ACROSS
independent randomizations — which this estimator does not do, so it reports `null` and says so.
- return.value: number; default: not declared
- return.varianceReduction: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/options').VarianceReduction; default: not declared — Which variance-reduction techniques were applied.
- return.warnings: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').QuantWarning[]; default: not declared — Structured warnings (e.g. a QMC dimension fallback).

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/options/sabr#sabrMonteCarloEstimate

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Low-level kernel: SABR Euler Monte-Carlo estimate of the discounted European payoff.

Expert kernel form (model-subpath surface) — the curated root surface is {@link sabr.monteCarloEstimate}.

```typescript
export declare function sabrMonteCarloEstimate(input: SabrMonteCarloEstimateInput): MonteCarloEstimate;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (input): SabrMonteCarloEstimateInput; default: not declared
- (input).forward: number; default: not declared
- (input).options: SabrMonteCarloOptions; default: not declared
- (input).parameters: SabrParameters; default: not declared
- (input).riskFreeRate: number; default: not declared
- (input).strike: number; default: not declared
- (input).timeToExpiryYears: number; default: not declared
- (input).type: OptionType; default: not declared
- return.confidenceInterval: [number, number] | null; default: not declared — Confidence interval at the requested level (default 95%); `null` whenever `standardError` is.
- return.converged: boolean; default: not declared — Whether the estimate is trustworthy (finite value and standard error).
- return.method: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/options').MonteCarloMethod; default: not declared — The sampling method actually used (may differ from the request if QMC fell back to pseudo).
- return.paths: number; default: not declared — Number of paths actually evaluated (antithetic pairs count as one path).
- return.seed: number; default: not declared — The seed, echoed for reproducibility.
- return.standardError: number | null; default: not declared — Standard error of the mean estimate — `null` for the QUASI-random methods (`sobol`, `halton`).

The sample-variance formula `√(s²/n)` assumes independent draws. A low-discrepancy sequence is
deterministic and negatively correlated by construction, so that formula does not estimate its
error: at 16k Sobol points on a European call it overstated the true deviation by ~75×, and a
confidence interval built from it was neither a confidence nor an interval. QMC error is
estimated by RANDOMIZING the sequence (scrambling/shifting) and taking the variance ACROSS
independent randomizations — which this estimator does not do, so it reports `null` and says so.
- return.value: number; default: not declared
- return.varianceReduction: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/options').VarianceReduction; default: not declared — Which variance-reduction techniques were applied.
- return.warnings: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').QuantWarning[]; default: not declared — Structured warnings (e.g. a QMC dimension fallback).

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/options/sabr#sabrPrice

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Price a European option under SABR by evaluating Hagan's implied vol and pricing with Black-76
(lognormal) or Bachelier (normal). Greeks are finite differences: `delta`/`gamma` w.r.t. the
forward, `theta` per day, `vega` per 1% change in α, `rho` per 1% change in the rate — all echoed in
`assumptions.units`.

A point outside Hagan's expansion domain (see {@link requireExpansionInDomain}) REFUSES with a
typed `input.out_of_range` error carrying the ν²T·ρ diagnosis — never a negative volatility, never
a negative "price" reported as converged. Through `engines.sabr()` that surfaces as a failed
`compareEngines` row; the value type stays `number` so no caller has to defend against a null.

Expert kernel form (model-subpath surface) — the curated root surface is {@link sabr.price}.

```typescript
export declare function sabrPrice(request: SabrPriceRequest): PriceResult;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (request): SabrPriceRequest; default: not declared
- (request).input: SabrInput; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/options/sabr#sabrVolatility

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Hagan implied volatility (lognormal/Black by default, or normal/Bachelier). Returns the volatility
to feed into Black-76 (lognormal) or Bachelier (normal) at the same forward, strike, and maturity.

Subject-first like its namespace sibling `sabr.price(type, input, parameters, options)`: the smile POINT
(`input`) comes before the model PARAMETERS (`parameters`).

Expert kernel form (model-subpath surface) — the curated root surface is {@link sabr.volatility}.

```typescript
export declare function sabrVolatility(request: SabrVolatilityRequest): number;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (request): SabrVolatilityRequest; default: not declared
- (request).input: SabrVolatilityInput; default: not declared
- (request).options?: SabrVolatilityOptions; default: not declared
- (request).parameters: SabrParameters; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/options/schema#blackScholesShape

Kind: value; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

The Black–Scholes–Merton input field descriptors — the ONE source of truth for every option
payload schema (facade, typed, implied-vol) and for consumers (MCP tools) that compose date-aware
variants. Reusing these fields is why every option schema carries the same field descriptions
instead of drifting apart.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/performance#DrawdownResult

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

```typescript
export interface DrawdownResult {
    /** Maximum drawdown as a positive fraction (0.2 = a 20% peak-to-trough decline). */
    maxDrawdown: number;
    /** Index of the peak preceding the worst drawdown. */
    peakIndex: number;
    /** Index of the trough of the worst drawdown. */
    troughIndex: number;
    /** Longest underwater stretch, in periods. */
    longestDurationPeriods: number;
    /**
     * Index at which equity first regained the pre-drawdown peak after the worst trough (WS3.3c).
     * Absent when the curve never recovered by the end of the series (still underwater).
     */
    recoveryIndex?: number;
}
```

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/performance#TimeWeightedReturnResult

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Result of {@link timeWeightedReturn}.

```typescript
/** Result of {@link timeWeightedReturn}. */
export interface TimeWeightedReturnResult {
    /** Geometric link of the measured subperiod returns; `null` when every subperiod is a gap. */
    timeWeightedReturn: number | null;
    /** Present exactly when `timeWeightedReturn` is `null`. */
    reason?: string;
    /**
     * Present only when `annualization` declared a basis AND the linked return exists, is
     * annualizable (its growth factor is positive), AND NO subperiod is a gap:
     * `(1 + timeWeightedReturn)^(1 / elapsedYears) − 1` over the ACT/365F year fraction between the
     * first and last valuation dates. When any subperiod is a gap the linked return does not cover
     * the whole window, so no annualized rate is stated (withheld with a warning).
     */
    annualizedReturn?: number;
    subperiods: TimeWeightedSubperiod[];
    assumptions: {
        flowTiming: 'at-flow-timestamp';
        flowConvention: string;
        annualization: AnnualizationPolicy;
        linking: 'geometric';
    };
    diagnostics: {
        warnings: string[];
        gaps: PerformanceGap[];
        flowCount: number;
        subperiodCount: number;
    };
}
```

first and last valuation dates. When any subperiod is a gap the linked return does not cover

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/performance#TimeWeightedSubperiod

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

One measured subperiod between consecutive valuation dates.

```typescript
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Time-weighted subperiod core (shared by timeWeightedReturn and portfolioReturnIndex)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
/** One measured subperiod between consecutive valuation dates. */
export interface TimeWeightedSubperiod {
    startDate: string;
    endDate: string;
    startNetAssetValue: number;

     * Net external flows attributed to this subperiod (dated on its start valuation date). Under the

     * the subperiod and is invested for its whole length — it joins the return base.

}
```

the subperiod and is invested for its whole length — it joins the return base.

```typescript
export interface WinLossStatistics {
```

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/performance#benchmarkRelativeTimeline

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Benchmark-relative timeline: aligns a portfolio total-return index with benchmark period
returns BY DATE and reports cumulative relative performance rows. A row exists only where BOTH
a portfolio index value and a benchmark return dated exactly that day exist; missing dates on
either side become `diagnostics.gaps` — never interpolated. Benchmark observations on
non-portfolio dates are real growth: they still compound into the benchmark cumulative at the
next aligned row (compounding observed returns is not interpolation), and their absence of a
row is recorded as a gap.

```typescript
export declare function benchmarkRelativeTimeline(input: BenchmarkRelativeTimelineInput): BenchmarkRelativeTimelineResult;
```

- (input).portfolioIndex: readonly ReturnIndexPoint[]; default: not declared
- return.assumptions: { anchorDate: string; benchmarkBasis: 'total-return' | 'price-return'; benchmarkReturnConvention: string; relativeMethod: string; }; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/performance#contributionByGroup

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/performance#modifiedDietzReturn

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Classic Modified Dietz single-period return:
`(netAssetValue₁ − netAssetValue₀ − F) / (netAssetValue₀ + Σ weightᵢ·flowᵢ)` where `F` is the
net external flow and each `weightᵢ = (daysInPeriod − daysSinceStartᵢ) / daysInPeriod` under ACT day
counts. The weights actually used are exposed in `flowWeights`. When the average-capital
denominator is not positive the result is `null` with a reason — never a fabricated rate.

```typescript
export declare function modifiedDietzReturn(input: ModifiedDietzReturnInput): ModifiedDietzReturnResult;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (input): ModifiedDietzReturnInput; default: not declared
- (input).externalCashFlows: readonly ExternalCashFlow[]; default: not declared
- (input).valuations: readonly PortfolioValuation[]; default: not declared — EXACTLY the two period endpoints: the start and end valuations.
- return.assumptions: { dayCount: 'ACT (actual calendar days)'; weightFormula: string; }; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.dayCount: 'ACT (actual calendar days)'; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.weightFormula: string; default: not declared
- return.diagnostics: { daysInPeriod: number; flowCount: number; warnings: string[]; }; default: not declared
- return.diagnostics.daysInPeriod: number; default: not declared
- return.diagnostics.flowCount: number; default: not declared
- return.diagnostics.warnings: string[]; default: not declared
- return.flowWeights: ModifiedDietzFlowWeight[]; default: not declared — The exact weight applied to each flow — exposed, never hidden.
- return.modifiedDietzReturn: number | null; default: not declared — `null` (with `reason`) when the average-capital denominator is not positive.
- return.reason?: string; default: not declared — Present exactly when `modifiedDietzReturn` is `null`.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/performance#moneyWeightedReturn

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Money-weighted return: the dated internal rate of return of the INVESTOR's cash-flow schedule,
composed from `datedInternalRateOfReturn` in `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/valuation` (annual compounding,
ACT/365F — echoed in `solverReport.assumptions`).

Sign convention (echoed in `assumptions.signConvention`): flows are stated from the INVESTOR's
perspective — the beginning net asset value is money the investor has committed (an outflow,
`−netAssetValue₀`), a deposit is the investor paying in (an outflow, `−amount`), a withdrawal is
the investor taking money out (an inflow, `+amount`), and the ending net asset value is what the
investor could take out (an inflow, `+netAssetValueₙ`). The solver's `.explain()` report is
preserved whole in `solverReport` so every admissible root and convergence detail rides along.

```typescript
export declare function moneyWeightedReturn(input: MoneyWeightedReturnInput): MoneyWeightedReturnResult;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (input): MoneyWeightedReturnInput; default: not declared
- (input).externalCashFlows: readonly ExternalCashFlow[]; default: not declared
- (input).valuations: readonly PortfolioValuation[]; default: not declared — First and last valuations REQUIRED — they anchor the schedule. Interior marks do not enter.
- return.assumptions: { asOf: string; signConvention: string; }; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.asOf: string; default: not declared — The first valuation date — the solver's valuation instant.
- return.assumptions.signConvention: string; default: not declared
- return.diagnostics: { scheduleRowCount: number; warnings: string[]; }; default: not declared
- return.diagnostics.scheduleRowCount: number; default: not declared
- return.diagnostics.warnings: string[]; default: not declared
- return.moneyWeightedReturn: number | null; default: not declared — The dated internal rate of return of the investor schedule; `null` on no root or ambiguity.
- return.reason?: string; default: not declared — Present exactly when `moneyWeightedReturn` is `null` — why the solver withheld a value.
- return.solverReport: InternalRateOfReturnReport; default: not declared — The FC1 solver's full `.explain()` report: roots, convergence, and warnings ride along.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/performance#timeWeightedReturn

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Time-weighted return: simple returns between consecutive valuation dates, linked geometrically.

Flow convention (also echoed in `assumptions.flowConvention`): a valuation dated D marks the
portfolio BEFORE any external flow dated D lands, so a flow dated on a valuation date is
attributed to the START of the subperiod beginning at D and is invested for its whole length.
Each subperiod uses
`simpleReturn = endNetAssetValue / (startNetAssetValue + netExternalFlows) − 1` — the flow
principal joins the start-of-subperiod base (denominator), so external deposits and
withdrawals are never profit or loss. A flow dated between valuations has no mark
to be valued at, so its surrounding subperiod becomes a GAP: excluded from linking, recorded in
`diagnostics.gaps`, never forward-filled. `annualizedReturn` appears only under the explicit
`{ basis: 'ACT/365F' }` policy, and only when NO subperiod is a gap — a linked return that
covers part of the window is never annualized over the whole window.

```typescript
export declare function timeWeightedReturn(input: TimeWeightedReturnInput): TimeWeightedReturnResult;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (input): TimeWeightedReturnInput; default: not declared
- (input).annualization: AnnualizationPolicy; default: not declared — REQUIRED and explicit: `'none'` or `{ basis: 'ACT/365F' }` — never inferred from timestamps.
- (input).externalCashFlows: readonly ExternalCashFlow[]; default: not declared
- (input).flowTiming: 'at-flow-timestamp'; default: not declared — The only v1 policy: a flow is valued at the net asset value dated the SAME date; a flow date
with no valuation makes its surrounding subperiod a gap — never a forward fill.
- (input).valuations: readonly PortfolioValuation[]; default: not declared
- return.annualizedReturn?: number; default: not declared — Present only when `annualization` declared a basis AND the linked return exists, is
annualizable (its growth factor is positive), AND NO subperiod is a gap:
`(1 + timeWeightedReturn)^(1 / elapsedYears) − 1` over the ACT/365F year fraction between the
first and last valuation dates. When any subperiod is a gap the linked return does not cover
the whole window, so no annualized rate is stated (withheld with a warning).
- return.assumptions: { annualization: AnnualizationPolicy; flowConvention: string; flowTiming: 'at-flow-timestamp'; linking: 'geometric'; }; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.annualization: AnnualizationPolicy; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.flowConvention: string; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.flowTiming: 'at-flow-timestamp'; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.linking: 'geometric'; default: not declared
- return.diagnostics: { flowCount: number; gaps: PerformanceGap[]; subperiodCount: number; warnings: string[]; }; default: not declared
- return.diagnostics.flowCount: number; default: not declared
- return.diagnostics.gaps: PerformanceGap[]; default: not declared
- return.diagnostics.subperiodCount: number; default: not declared
- return.diagnostics.warnings: string[]; default: not declared
- return.reason?: string; default: not declared — Present exactly when `timeWeightedReturn` is `null`.
- return.subperiods: TimeWeightedSubperiod[]; default: not declared
- return.timeWeightedReturn: number | null; default: not declared — Geometric link of the measured subperiod returns; `null` when every subperiod is a gap.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/performance/sharpe#degenerateAwareDiagnostics

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Degenerate-NaN honesty (design law #4: a NaN result must ride with an explicit diagnostic, never
alone). Wraps {@link returnsDiagnostics} and — when the computed `value` is NaN — appends a
`WarningCode.DegenerateInput` warning saying WHY the metric is undefined for this input. Used by
the `.explain()` paths only; plain calls stay silent-and-correct (they still return the NaN).
Pass no `series` for non-returns inputs (e.g. weight rows) where the prices-as-returns
plausibility scan must not apply.

```typescript
export declare function degenerateAwareDiagnostics(value: number, functionName: string, reason: string, ...series: ArrayLike<number>[]): Diagnostics;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (functionName): string; default: not declared
- (reason): string; default: not declared
- (series): ArrayLike<number>[]; default: not declared
- (value): number; default: not declared
- return.autoReason?: string; default: not declared — When a meta-engine (e.g. `engines.auto()`) selected a delegate, this is a one-sentence,
human-readable explanation of WHY that delegate was chosen (`engine` then names the delegate).
Absent when no auto-selection took place.
- return.converged?: boolean; default: not declared — Whether an iterative procedure converged. `false` means the value is not trustworthy.
- return.decomposition?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Named intermediate quantities the value decomposes into — a par spread's protection leg and
risky annuity, a forward variance's near/far legs. The H-series explain paths disclose their
arithmetic here so a caller can audit the ratio, not just receive it (3B.3).
- return.engine?: string; default: not declared — Pricing/solver engine name, e.g. `black-scholes-merton`.
- return.finiteDifferenceBumps?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Finite-difference engines: the ACTUAL bump sizes used for FD Greeks (spec P2.3) — adaptive
near the vol/time boundaries, so the caller can see exactly what was differenced.
Keys: `spotStep`, `volatilityStep`, `timeStepYears`, `rateStep`, and — extended Greeks only —
`dividendYieldStep`. Each is the actual step differenced, in the unit of the coordinate it
bumps. (This doc named the retired `hS`/`hSig`/`hT`/`hR`/`hQ` keys for one release after the
emit sites had moved to the semantic names, so a caller following it read `undefined`.)
- return.iterations?: number; default: not declared — Iteration count for iterative methods.
- return.method?: string; default: not declared — Numerical method, e.g. `closed-form`, `brent`, `finite-difference`.
- return.selection?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing').SelectionReport; default: not declared — The structured engine-selection report (Gate C, `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing`): who was selected,
why, and — for automatic selection — every candidate considered with its verdict. This is the
machine-readable superset of `engine` + `autoReason` (which remain for compatibility);
`selected.name` always agrees with `engine` when both are present.
- return.timingMs?: number; default: not declared — Wall-clock timing in milliseconds, when measured.
- return.warmup?: number; default: not declared — Series facades: number of leading output slots that are warmup sentinels (null/NaN) while the
computation seeds. Equals the input length when the indicator never emitted.
- return.warnings: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').QuantWarning[]; default: not declared — Structured warnings; always present (possibly empty).

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/performance/sharpe#requireSeries

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Boundary guard for every series-consuming performance facade (dx §1.2 applied here): the input
must be a real array (or typed array) of numbers — a string, `undefined`, or a plain object
throws a typed teaching error instead of a raw `TypeError` from `series.length` downstream.
The container being an array is not enough: EVERY element is validated (E4) — a single NaN,
`undefined`, or string mid-series poisons a mean/stddev into a silently-wrong number, and a
`sharpe([0.01, NaN, 0.02])` masquerading as a real ratio is exactly the corruption Law 7 kills
at the boundary. A `Float64Array` of finite values always passes; empty arrays keep their
documented null-with-reason behavior downstream.

```typescript
export declare function requireSeries(series: ArrayLike<number>, functionName: string, field?: string): void;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (field)?: string; default: not declared
- (functionName): string; default: not declared
- (series): ArrayLike<number>; default: not declared

risky annuity, a forward variance's near/far legs. The H-series explain paths disclose their

Keys: `spotStep`, `volatilityStep`, `timeStepYears`, `rateStep`, and — extended Greeks only —
`dividendYieldStep`. Each is the actual step differenced, in the unit of the coordinate it
bumps. (This doc named the retired `hS`/`hSig`/`hT`/`hR`/`hQ` keys for one release after the
emit sites had moved to the semantic names, so a caller following it read `undefined`.)
- return.iterations?: number; default: not declared — Iteration count for iterative methods.
- return.method?: string; default: not declared — Numerical method, e.g. `closed-form`, `brent`, `finite-difference`.
- return.selection?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing').SelectionReport; default: not declared — The structured engine-selection report (Gate C, `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing`): who was selected,
why, and — for automatic selection — every candidate considered with its verdict. This is the
machine-readable superset of `engine` + `autoReason` (which remain for compatibility);
`selected.name` always agrees with `engine` when both are present.
- return.timingMs?: number; default: not declared — Wall-clock timing in milliseconds, when measured.
- return.warmup?: number; default: not declared — Series facades: number of leading output slots that are warmup sentinels (null/NaN) while the
computation seeds. Equals the input length when the indicator never emitted.
- return.warnings: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').QuantWarning[]; default: not declared — Structured warnings; always present (possibly empty).
