### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/research#winsorizeFactor

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Winsorize a factor vector under an EXPLICIT method. The percentile form uses the CLASSIC Winsor
convention — order-statistic replacement: the `floor(n × lowerPercentile)` smallest values are
replaced by the next order statistic (and symmetrically at the top). Chosen over interpolating
quantiles deliberately: order-statistic replacement is EXACTLY idempotent (re-winsorizing a
winsorized vector is the identity — the metamorphic law in the evidence plan), while an
interpolated cutoff moves every time it is recomputed over its own output. Nulls pass through
untouched; the realized clip bounds are echoed.

```typescript
export declare function winsorizeFactor(input: WinsorizeFactorInput): WinsorizeFactorResult;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (input): WinsorizeFactorInput; default: not declared
- (input).entries: readonly FactorEntry[]; default: not declared
- (input).method: WinsorizationMethod; default: not declared
- (input).minimumCoverageFraction?: number; default: not declared
- return.assumptions: { lowerBound: number; method: WinsorizationMethod; minimumCoverageFraction: number; upperBound: number; }; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.lowerBound: number; default: not declared — The realized clip bounds, so the transform is reproducible without the input.
- return.assumptions.method: WinsorizationMethod; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.minimumCoverageFraction: number; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.upperBound: number; default: not declared
- return.diagnostics: { clippedLowerCount: number; clippedUpperCount: number; coverage: FactorCoverage; warnings: string[]; }; default: not declared
- return.diagnostics.clippedLowerCount: number; default: not declared
- return.diagnostics.clippedUpperCount: number; default: not declared
- return.diagnostics.coverage: FactorCoverage; default: not declared
- return.diagnostics.warnings: string[]; default: not declared
- return.entries: FactorEntry[]; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/research/artifacts#Referenced

Kind: type; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

The stored form of an input: every bulk array may be a `TableHandle` instead of its rows, and a
caller function is never stored (the run is recorded non-replayable and the field omitted).

```typescript
/**
 * The stored form of an input: every bulk array may be a `TableHandle` instead of its rows, and a
 * caller function is never stored (the run is recorded non-replayable and the field omitted).
 */
export type Referenced<T> = T extends (...args: never[]) => unknown ? never : T extends readonly (infer Element)[] ? readonly Referenced<Element>[] | TableHandle : T extends object ? {
    [P in keyof T]: Referenced<T[P]>;
} : T;
```

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/research/artifacts#ResearchRunReport

Kind: type; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

The typed report every verb reads and writes — the artifact's `result`, verbatim.

```typescript
/** The typed report every verb reads and writes — the artifact's `result`, verbatim. */
export type ResearchRunReport<Kind extends ResearchRunKind = ResearchRunKind> = Readonly<Record<string, unknown>> & {
    kind: Kind;
    runVersion: number;
    /** The direct operation's result, verbatim. */
    run: RunOf<Kind>;
    /** The operation's input with bulk rows either embedded or replaced by verified table references. */
    inputs: Referenced<InputOf<Kind>>;
    /** Table references for every bulk row set that was not embedded (Gate B TableHandle). */
    referencedData: Record<string, TableHandle>;
    /** Statistical-hygiene results the caller attached, verbatim — computed by @insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk, never here. */
    hygiene: ResearchHygieneBlock | null;
    /** The versioned recipe the caller says produced the factor, when one did. */
    recipe: FactorRecipe | null;
    assumptions: {
        conventionsVersion: string;
        kind: Kind;
        runVersion: number;
        operation: string;
        /** `false` exactly when a non-serializable callback participated. */
        replayable: boolean;
        /** The callback field that made the run non-replayable, when one did. */
        nonReplayableField: string | null;
        inputPolicy: 'embedded' | 'referenced';
        embeddedRowLimit: number;
        projection: string;
    };
    diagnostics: {
        warnings: QuantWarning[];
        embeddedRows: number;
        referencedRows: number;
        runWarningCount: number;
    };
};
```

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/research/artifacts#compareResearchRuns

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Compare two research runs of one kind: identity (universe, as-of, filter / rank field /
components), membership, rank moves, score deltas, exclusion-reason deltas, coefficient deltas,
abnormal-return deltas per session offset, per-quantile and per-horizon deltas, the hygiene
verdict change, and the structural diff of the two verbatim runs (Decision 6). Baseline and
candidate are named, never "a" and "b"; nothing is a single similarity score.

```typescript
export declare function compareResearchRuns<Kind extends ResearchRunKind>(input: { baseline: ResearchRunReport<Kind> | AnalysisArtifact; candidate: ResearchRunReport<Kind> | AnalysisArtifact; limits?: ComparisonLimits & { listedIds?: number; }; }): ResearchRunComparison<Kind>;
```

`CONVENTIONS_VERSION` (the market snapshot's law, one law), never an echo of the result and

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk#AggregateGreeksResult

Kind: type; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

{@link aggregateGreeks}'s envelope: `value` carries the book-level totals; `assumptions` echo the
position count and the missing-greeks-count-as-0 convention.

```typescript
/**
 * {@link aggregateGreeks}'s envelope: `value` carries the book-level totals; `assumptions` echo the
 * position count and the missing-greeks-count-as-0 convention.
 */
export type AggregateGreeksResult = Computed<PortfolioGreeks, {
    positions: number;
    missingGreeks: 'counted-as-zero';
    /** Each position's `multiplier` (default 1) scales its value and Greeks with its `quantity`. */
    contractMultiplier: 'applied';
    /** The unit system of the totals: the options package's (theta per day, vega/rho per 1%). */
    greekUnits: {
        theta: 'perDay';
        vega: 'per1Percent';
        rho: 'per1Percent';
    };
}>;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- assumptions: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Assumptions<{ positions: number; missingGreeks: 'counted-as-zero'; contractMultiplier: 'applied'; greekUnits: { theta: 'perDay'; vega: 'per1Percent'; rho: 'per1Percent'; }; }>; default: not declared — Every applied convention, echoed back.
- assumptions.asOf?: number; default: not declared
- assumptions.calendar?: string; default: not declared
- assumptions.calendarVersion?: string; default: not declared
- assumptions.compounding?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').InterestCompounding; default: not declared
- assumptions.compounding.periodsPerYear: number; default: not declared
- assumptions.compounding.type: 'periodic'; default: not declared
- assumptions.contractMultiplier: 'applied'; default: not declared — Each position's `multiplier` (default 1) scales its value and Greeks with its `quantity`.
- assumptions.conventionsVersion: string; default: not declared
- assumptions.dayCount?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').DayCount; default: not declared
- assumptions.dividendModel?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').DividendModel; default: not declared
- assumptions.engine?: string; default: not declared
- assumptions.expiryConvention?: 'us-equity-close' | 'explicit-instant'; default: not declared — How the contract's expiry label was resolved to an instant: `'us-equity-close'` when a
date-only `YYYY-MM-DD` expiry resolved to the US equity/options close — 16:00 America/New_York,
or 13:00 on an early-close day;
`'explicit-instant'` when the caller supplied a zoned datetime. Named so the convention is
never silent (alignment spec P1.6); instrument builders own the full story in Phase 3.
- assumptions.greekUnits: { theta: 'perDay'; vega: 'per1Percent'; rho: 'per1Percent'; }; default: not declared — The unit system of the totals: the options package's (theta per day, vega/rho per 1%).
- assumptions.greekUnits.rho: 'per1Percent'; default: not declared
- assumptions.greekUnits.theta: 'perDay'; default: not declared
- assumptions.greekUnits.vega: 'per1Percent'; default: not declared
- assumptions.missingGreeks: 'counted-as-zero'; default: not declared
- assumptions.model?: string; default: not declared
- assumptions.positions: number; default: not declared
- assumptions.seed?: number; default: not declared — The randomness seed this result was computed under — REQUIRED echo for a
`randomness: 'seeded'` Pricer (Gate C, 2026-08-23): a stochastic result that does not name
its seed cannot be replayed from the result alone. Deterministic paths never set it.
- assumptions.timeToExpiryConvention?: never; default: not declared
- assumptions.timeToExpiryYears?: number; default: not declared
- assumptions.units?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').GreekUnits; default: not declared

- assumptions.units.theta: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').ThetaUnit; default: not declared
- assumptions.units.vega: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').VegaUnit; default: not declared
- diagnostics: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Diagnostics; default: not declared — How the value was computed, plus any warnings.
- diagnostics.autoReason?: string; default: not declared — When a meta-engine (e.g. `engines.auto()`) selected a delegate, this is a one-sentence,
human-readable explanation of WHY that delegate was chosen (`engine` then names the delegate).
Absent when no auto-selection took place.
- diagnostics.converged?: boolean; default: not declared — Whether an iterative procedure converged. `false` means the value is not trustworthy.
- diagnostics.decomposition?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Named intermediate quantities the value decomposes into — a par spread's protection leg and
risky annuity, a forward variance's near/far legs. The H-series explain paths disclose their
arithmetic here so a caller can audit the ratio, not just receive it (3B.3).
- diagnostics.engine?: string; default: not declared — Pricing/solver engine name, e.g. `black-scholes-merton`.
- diagnostics.finiteDifferenceBumps?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Finite-difference engines: the ACTUAL bump sizes used for FD Greeks (spec P2.3) — adaptive
near the vol/time boundaries, so the caller can see exactly what was differenced.

`dividendYieldStep`. Each is the actual step differenced, in the unit of the coordinate it
bumps. (This doc named the retired `hS`/`hSig`/`hT`/`hR`/`hQ` keys for one release after the
emit sites had moved to the semantic names, so a caller following it read `undefined`.)
- diagnostics.iterations?: number; default: not declared — Iteration count for iterative methods.
- diagnostics.method?: string; default: not declared — Numerical method, e.g. `closed-form`, `brent`, `finite-difference`.

`selected.name` always agrees with `engine` when both are present.
- diagnostics.selection.candidates?: readonly import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing').SelectionCandidate[]; default: not declared — Candidates an automatic selection considered; absent for explicit mode.
- diagnostics.selection.mode: 'explicit' | 'automatic'; default: not declared
- diagnostics.selection.reason: string; default: not declared — Why the selected engine answers this request.

- diagnostics.selection.selected.name: string; default: not declared
- diagnostics.selection.selected.version?: string; default: not declared
- diagnostics.timingMs?: number; default: not declared — Wall-clock timing in milliseconds, when measured.
- diagnostics.warmup?: number; default: not declared — Series facades: number of leading output slots that are warmup sentinels (null/NaN) while the

- diagnostics.warnings: QuantWarning[]; default: not declared — Structured warnings; always present (possibly empty).
- provenance?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Provenance; default: not declared — Optional data lineage when the inputs came from a provider.
- provenance.asOf?: number; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk#BacktestOverfittingProbabilityOptions

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Options for {@link probabilityOfBacktestOverfitting}.

```typescript
// ───────────────────────── PBO (combinatorially-symmetric cross-validation) ─────────────────────────
/** Options for {@link probabilityOfBacktestOverfitting}. */
export interface BacktestOverfittingProbabilityOptions {
    /**
     * Number of disjoint contiguous row-blocks `S` (even, `4 ≤ S ≤ 16`). Default `16` (Bailey & López de
     * Prado). The `C(S, S/2)` train/test splits grow fast in `S`; the observation count is trimmed to a
     * multiple of `S` (the oldest rows dropped).
     */
    splits?: number;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- splits?: number; default: not declared — Number of disjoint contiguous row-blocks `S` (even, `4 ≤ S ≤ 16`). Default `16` (Bailey & López de
Prado). The `C(S, S/2)` train/test splits grow fast in `S`; the observation count is trimmed to a
multiple of `S` (the oldest rows dropped).

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk#BacktestOverfittingProbabilityResult

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

The result of a CSCV probability-of-backtest-overfitting analysis.

```typescript
/** The result of a CSCV probability-of-backtest-overfitting analysis. */
export interface BacktestOverfittingProbabilityResult {
    /**
     * Probability of backtest overfitting: the fraction of the `C(S, S/2)` symmetric train/test splits on
     * which the in-sample-best configuration ranks **below the out-of-sample median** (logit `λ < 0`). Near
     * `0.5` for noise (selection is worthless out of sample), near `0` for a genuinely persistent edge.
     */
    backtestOverfittingProbability: number;
    /** Number of symmetric train/test splits evaluated: `C(S, S/2)`. */
    combinations: number;
    /** Blocks `S` actually used. */
    splits: number;
    /** Observations (rows) used after trimming to a multiple of `S`. */
    observations: number;
    /** Number of strategy configurations (columns) `N`. */
    trials: number;
    /** Median logit `λ = ln(r̄/(1−r̄))` across the splits (`r̄` = OOS relative rank of the IS-best); `< 0` ⇒ overfit-leaning. */
    medianLogit: number;
    /** Applied conventions, echoed (Law 2 report grammar). */
    assumptions: {
        conventionsVersion: string;
        [k: string]: unknown;
    };
    /** Structured warnings; always present (possibly empty). */
    diagnostics: {
        warnings: QuantWarning[];
    };
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- assumptions: { [k: string]: unknown; conventionsVersion: string; }; default: not declared — Applied conventions, echoed (Law 2 report grammar).
- assumptions.conventionsVersion: string; default: not declared
- backtestOverfittingProbability: number; default: not declared — Probability of backtest overfitting: the fraction of the `C(S, S/2)` symmetric train/test splits on
which the in-sample-best configuration ranks **below the out-of-sample median** (logit `λ < 0`). Near
`0.5` for noise (selection is worthless out of sample), near `0` for a genuinely persistent edge.
- combinations: number; default: not declared — Number of symmetric train/test splits evaluated: `C(S, S/2)`.
- diagnostics: { warnings: QuantWarning[]; }; default: not declared — Structured warnings; always present (possibly empty).
- diagnostics.warnings: QuantWarning[]; default: not declared
- medianLogit: number; default: not declared — Median logit `λ = ln(r̄/(1−r̄))` across the splits (`r̄` = OOS relative rank of the IS-best); `< 0` ⇒ overfit-leaning.
- observations: number; default: not declared — Observations (rows) used after trimming to a multiple of `S`.
- splits: number; default: not declared — Blocks `S` actually used.
- trials: number; default: not declared — Number of strategy configurations (columns) `N`.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk#BlackLittermanOptions

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

```typescript
export interface BlackLittermanOptions {
    /** Asset return covariance Σ (n×n). */
    covariance: Matrix;
    /** Prior (equilibrium) expected returns π. Provide this, or `marketWeights` to imply it. */
    priorMean?: ArrayLike<number>;
    /** Market-cap weights to reverse-engineer the prior `π = δ·Σ·w_mkt`. */
    marketWeights?: ArrayLike<number>;
    /** Risk-aversion δ for the implied prior and the posterior mean-variance weights. Default 2.5. */
    riskAversion?: number;
    /** Investor views (at least one). */
    views: BlackLittermanView[];
    /** Scalar τ scaling the prior uncertainty of the mean (default 0.05). */
    tau?: number;
    /** Constraints applied to the posterior mean-variance weights. */
    constraints?: OptimizeConstraints;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- constraints?: OptimizeConstraints; default: not declared — Constraints applied to the posterior mean-variance weights.
- constraints.bounds?: [number, number][]; default: not declared — Per-asset `[lo, hi]` bounds.
- constraints.budget?: number; default: not declared — Sum-to budget (`Σw`). Default 1 (fully invested).
- constraints.groups?: GroupConstraint[]; default: not declared — Sector/group exposure caps (`min ≤ Σ_group w ≤ max`).
- constraints.longOnly?: boolean; default: not declared — Forbid short positions (`w ≥ 0`). Ignored where `bounds` is given.
- constraints.maximumIterations?: number; default: not declared — Projected-gradient iteration cap. Default 5000.
- constraints.tolerance?: number; default: not declared — Projected-gradient convergence tolerance on the weight step. Default 1e-11.
- constraints.transactionCosts?: { perUnitTurnover: number | number[]; previousWeights: number[]; }; default: not declared — Linear transaction cost charged on the trade away from a base portfolio. Subtracted from the
objective as `Σ perUnitTurnover_i·|w_i − previousWeights_i|` (a scalar applies to every asset). Needs `previousWeights`.
- constraints.transactionCosts.perUnitTurnover: number | number[]; default: not declared
- constraints.transactionCosts.previousWeights: number[]; default: not declared
- constraints.turnover?: TurnoverConstraint; default: not declared — Turnover budget against a base portfolio (`Σ|w − previousWeights| ≤ max`).
- constraints.turnover.max: number; default: not declared — Maximum one-way + reverse (L1) turnover allowed.
- constraints.turnover.previousWeights: number[]; default: not declared — Current weights to measure turnover against.
- covariance: Matrix; default: not declared — Asset return covariance Σ (n×n).
- marketWeights?: ArrayLike<number>; default: not declared — Market-cap weights to reverse-engineer the prior `π = δ·Σ·w_mkt`.
- priorMean?: ArrayLike<number>; default: not declared — Prior (equilibrium) expected returns π. Provide this, or `marketWeights` to imply it.
- riskAversion?: number; default: not declared — Risk-aversion δ for the implied prior and the posterior mean-variance weights. Default 2.5.
- tau?: number; default: not declared — Scalar τ scaling the prior uncertainty of the mean (default 0.05).
- views: BlackLittermanView[]; default: not declared — Investor views (at least one).

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk#BlackLittermanResult

Kind: type; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

The Black-Litterman result (dx §2.4): the core `Computed` envelope, like the other optimizers.
`value` carries the prior/posterior returns and the posterior-optimal weights; `assumptions` echo
the (possibly defaulted) `tau` and `riskAversion` plus the number of views blended; `diagnostics`
carry the posterior mean-variance solver's `converged`/`iterations` and all warnings.

```typescript
/**
 * The Black-Litterman result (dx §2.4): the core `Computed` envelope, like the other optimizers.
 * `value` carries the prior/posterior returns and the posterior-optimal weights; `assumptions` echo
 * the (possibly defaulted) `tau` and `riskAversion` plus the number of views blended; `diagnostics`
 * carry the posterior mean-variance solver's `converged`/`iterations` and all warnings.
 */
export type BlackLittermanResult = Computed<{
    /** The supplied or market-implied equilibrium prior π. */
    priorMean: number[];
    /** Posterior (views-blended) expected returns. */
    posteriorMean: number[];
    /** Posterior return covariance `Σ + M`, where `M` is the posterior covariance of the mean. */
    posteriorCovariance: number[][];
    /** Mean-variance-optimal weights under the posterior. */
    weights: number[];
}, {
    tau: number;
    riskAversion: number;
    views: number;
}>;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- assumptions: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Assumptions<{ tau: number; riskAversion: number; views: number; }>; default: not declared — Every applied convention, echoed back.
- assumptions.asOf?: number; default: not declared
- assumptions.calendar?: string; default: not declared
- assumptions.calendarVersion?: string; default: not declared
- assumptions.compounding?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').InterestCompounding; default: not declared
- assumptions.compounding.periodsPerYear: number; default: not declared
- assumptions.compounding.type: 'periodic'; default: not declared
- assumptions.conventionsVersion: string; default: not declared
- assumptions.dayCount?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').DayCount; default: not declared
- assumptions.dividendModel?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').DividendModel; default: not declared
- assumptions.engine?: string; default: not declared
- assumptions.expiryConvention?: 'us-equity-close' | 'explicit-instant'; default: not declared — How the contract's expiry label was resolved to an instant: `'us-equity-close'` when a
date-only `YYYY-MM-DD` expiry resolved to the US equity/options close — 16:00 America/New_York,
or 13:00 on an early-close day;
`'explicit-instant'` when the caller supplied a zoned datetime. Named so the convention is
never silent (alignment spec P1.6); instrument builders own the full story in Phase 3.
- assumptions.model?: string; default: not declared
- assumptions.riskAversion: number; default: not declared

human-readable explanation of WHY that delegate was chosen (`engine` then names the delegate).

- diagnostics.converged?: boolean; default: not declared — Whether an iterative procedure converged. `false` means the value is not trustworthy.
- diagnostics.decomposition?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Named intermediate quantities the value decomposes into — a par spread's protection leg and
risky annuity, a forward variance's near/far legs. The H-series explain paths disclose their
arithmetic here so a caller can audit the ratio, not just receive it (3B.3).
- diagnostics.engine?: string; default: not declared — Pricing/solver engine name, e.g. `black-scholes-merton`.
- diagnostics.finiteDifferenceBumps?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Finite-difference engines: the ACTUAL bump sizes used for FD Greeks (spec P2.3) — adaptive

- diagnostics.iterations?: number; default: not declared — Iteration count for iterative methods.

- diagnostics.selection?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing').SelectionReport; default: not declared — The structured engine-selection report (Gate C, `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing`): who was selected,

- diagnostics.timingMs?: number; default: not declared — Wall-clock timing in milliseconds, when measured.

computation seeds. Equals the input length when the indicator never emitted.
- diagnostics.warnings: QuantWarning[]; default: not declared — Structured warnings; always present (possibly empty).

- provenance.warnings?: QuantWarning[]; default: not declared
- value: { posteriorCovariance: number[][]; posteriorMean: number[]; priorMean: number[]; weights: number[]; }; default: not declared — The computed value. Never `NaN` or `±Infinity`: a value the model cannot produce is `null`
beside a diagnostic that says why (Law 7 — a warning never licenses a non-finite number).
- value.posteriorCovariance: number[][]; default: not declared — Posterior return covariance `Σ + M`, where `M` is the posterior covariance of the mean.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk#CVaROptimizeOptions

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

```typescript
// ───────────────────────── CVaR optimization (Rockafellar–Uryasev) ─────────────────────────
export interface CVaROptimizeOptions extends OptimizeConstraints {
    /** Tail confidence α: optimize the mean of the worst `(1 − α)` fraction of losses. Default 0.95. */
    alpha?: number;
    /** Optional minimum mean return `μᵀw ≥ minReturn` (μ = per-asset scenario means). */
    minReturn?: number;
    /** Projected-subgradient iteration cap. Default 4000. */
    maximumIterations?: number;
    /**
     * Initial subgradient step size (decays as `step/√t`). Defaults to `1/‖g₀‖` — the step that moves
     * the FIRST iterate a distance of about 1 in weight space, which is the scale weights live on.
     * A fixed default (this used to be `1`) is unit-dependent: on decimal daily returns ‖g‖ ≈ 0.01,
     * so every step moved ~1e-2·(1/√t) and the run plateaued a long way from the optimum while
     * reporting `converged: true`. Pass an explicit `step` only to override that scaling.
     */
    step?: number;
    /**
     * Relative-improvement tolerance for convergence: the run is `converged` only once the best CVaR
     * improves by less than this over the final 25 iterations. Default `1e-6`.
     */
    tolerance?: number;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- alpha?: number; default: not declared — Tail confidence α: optimize the mean of the worst `(1 − α)` fraction of losses. Default 0.95.
- bounds?: [number, number][]; default: not declared — Per-asset `[lo, hi]` bounds.
- budget?: number; default: not declared — Sum-to budget (`Σw`). Default 1 (fully invested).
- groups?: GroupConstraint[]; default: not declared — Sector/group exposure caps (`min ≤ Σ_group w ≤ max`).
- longOnly?: boolean; default: not declared — Forbid short positions (`w ≥ 0`). Ignored where `bounds` is given.
- maximumIterations?: number; default: not declared — Projected-subgradient iteration cap. Default 4000.
- minReturn?: number; default: not declared — Optional minimum mean return `μᵀw ≥ minReturn` (μ = per-asset scenario means).
- step?: number; default: not declared — Initial subgradient step size (decays as `step/√t`). Defaults to `1/‖g₀‖` — the step that moves
the FIRST iterate a distance of about 1 in weight space, which is the scale weights live on.
A fixed default (this used to be `1`) is unit-dependent: on decimal daily returns ‖g‖ ≈ 0.01,
so every step moved ~1e-2·(1/√t) and the run plateaued a long way from the optimum while
reporting `converged: true`. Pass an explicit `step` only to override that scaling.
- tolerance?: number; default: not declared — Relative-improvement tolerance for convergence: the run is `converged` only once the best CVaR
improves by less than this over the final 25 iterations. Default `1e-6`.
- transactionCosts?: { perUnitTurnover: number | number[]; previousWeights: number[]; }; default: not declared — Linear transaction cost charged on the trade away from a base portfolio. Subtracted from the
objective as `Σ perUnitTurnover_i·|w_i − previousWeights_i|` (a scalar applies to every asset). Needs `previousWeights`.
- transactionCosts.perUnitTurnover: number | number[]; default: not declared
- transactionCosts.previousWeights: number[]; default: not declared
- turnover?: TurnoverConstraint; default: not declared — Turnover budget against a base portfolio (`Σ|w − previousWeights| ≤ max`).
- turnover.max: number; default: not declared — Maximum one-way + reverse (L1) turnover allowed.
- turnover.previousWeights: number[]; default: not declared — Current weights to measure turnover against.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk#CovarianceOptions

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk#CovarianceResult

```typescript
export interface CovarianceResult {
    value: CovarianceValue;
```

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk#EfficientFrontierGrid

Kind: type; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

How the frontier is sampled — an explicit choice, never defaulted.

```typescript
/** How the frontier is sampled — an explicit choice, never defaulted. */
export type EfficientFrontierGrid =
/** One point per risk aversion λ in `max μᵀw − (λ/2)·wᵀΣw` (each > 0). */
{
    kind: 'risk-aversion';
    values: number[];
}
/** One point per target expected return, in the units of `mean`. */
 | {
    kind: 'target-return';
    values: number[];
}
/**
 * `count` (≥ 2, ≤ 10,000) targets evenly spaced from the minimum-variance return to the maximum
 * achievable return under the constraints. When that maximum is unbounded or cannot be proved
 * from the supported constraint grammar, the points fall back to a logarithmic λ grid and the
 * result says which case occurred.
 */
 | {
    kind: 'points';
    count: number;
};
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- count: number; default: not declared
- kind: ('points') | ('risk-aversion') | ('target-return'); default: not declared
- values: number[]; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk#ExplainPnlInput

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Decompose a realized P&L into greek terms + residual, given the position's Greeks (in the options
package's units — theta per day, vega per vol point, rho per 1%; see `PositionGreeks`), the
realized move, and the actual P&L. The general primitive — works for any instrument whose greeks
you can supply.

```typescript
/**
 * Decompose a realized P&L into greek terms + residual, given the position's Greeks (in the options
 * package's units — theta per day, vega per vol point, rho per 1%; see `PositionGreeks`), the
 * realized move, and the actual P&L. The general primitive — works for any instrument whose greeks
 * you can supply.
 */
export interface ExplainPnlInput {
    greeks: PositionGreeks;
    move: PnlMove;
    actualPnl: number;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- actualPnl: number; default: not declared
- greeks: PositionGreeks; default: not declared
- greeks.charm?: number; default: not declared — ∂Δ/∂T per year of time-to-expiry — the options package's `charm` (delta drift as expiry recedes). Optional.
- greeks.color?: number; default: not declared — Accepted from a whole `ExtendedGreeks`; not used by the second-order expansion.
- greeks.delta?: number; default: not declared — ∂V/∂S per $1 of spot.
- greeks.deltaRate?: number; default: not declared — ∂²V/∂S∂r per $ per 1% rate — the spot-rate cross (`∂Δ/∂r`). Optional.
- greeks.gamma?: number; default: not declared — ∂²V/∂S² per $1².
- greeks.lambda?: number | null; default: not declared — Accepted from a whole `ExtendedGreeks` (`null` = elasticity undefined); not used by the expansion.
- greeks.phi?: number; default: not declared — φ = ∂V/∂q per 1% dividend yield — the options package's `phi` (dividend rho). Optional.
- greeks.rho?: number; default: not declared — ∂V/∂r per 1% rate (0.01), as the options package reports it.
- greeks.rhoConvexity?: number; default: not declared — ∂²V/∂r² per (1%)² — rho convexity. Optional.
- greeks.speed?: number; default: not declared — Accepted from a whole `ExtendedGreeks`; not used by the second-order expansion.
- greeks.spot?: number; default: not declared — Reference spot, required to resolve percent spot shocks into price moves.
- greeks.theta?: number; default: not declared — ∂V/∂t per CALENDAR DAY (negative for a long option), as the options package reports it.
- greeks.thetaConvexity?: number; default: not declared — ∂²V/∂t² per calendar day² — theta convexity (theta's own bleed). Optional.
- greeks.thetaRate?: number; default: not declared — ∂²V/∂t∂r per calendar day per 1% rate — the time-rate cross (`∂Θ/∂r`). Optional.
- greeks.ultima?: number; default: not declared — Accepted from a whole `ExtendedGreeks`; not used by the second-order expansion.
- greeks.value: number; default: not declared — Current mark value of the position (per unit).
- greeks.vanna?: number; default: not declared — ∂²V/∂S∂σ per 1.00 σ per $ — the options package's `vanna`. Optional — omitted ⇒ its term is 0.
- greeks.vega?: number; default: not declared — ∂V/∂σ per 1 volatility point (0.01), as the options package reports it.
- greeks.vera?: number; default: not declared — ∂²V/∂σ∂r per 1.00 σ per 1.00 rate — the options package's `vera`. Optional.
- greeks.veta?: number; default: not declared — ∂vega/∂T per year of time-to-expiry, vega per 1.00 σ — the options package's `veta`. Optional.
- greeks.vomma?: number; default: not declared — ∂²V/∂σ² per 1.00 σ² — the options package's `vomma`. Optional.
- greeks.zomma?: number; default: not declared — Accepted from a whole `ExtendedGreeks`; not used by the second-order expansion.
- move: PnlMove; default: not declared
- move.dDividendYield?: number; default: not declared — Absolute dividend-yield change (decimal; `+0.005` = +50 bp) — drives the `ε·dq` carry term.
- move.dRate?: number; default: not declared — Absolute rate change (decimal; `+0.005` = +50 bp).
- move.dSpot?: number; default: not declared — Absolute spot change ($).
- move.dTimeYears?: number; default: not declared — Time elapsed, in YEARS. The unit is in the name; the Greeks are per DAY (the options package's
units) and the engine converts, so a caller never scales either side by 365.
- move.dVolatility?: number; default: not declared — Absolute vol change (decimal; `+0.02` = +2 vol points).

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk#ExplainPositionPnlInput

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Decompose a strategy {@link StrategyPosition}'s realized P&L between two market states, aggregate and
per leg. Marks the position at each state with `Position.value()` (respecting per-leg IV and expiry),
attributes each leg via t0's greeks, and reports the residual. The aggregate is the term-wise sum
of the per-leg attributions — exactly consistent with the breakdown, and correct when different
legs respond to different volatilities (below).

**Volatility attribution is honest per leg.** A leg built with its own fixed IV holds that IV in
`Position.value()`, so a change in the position-level `volatility` does not move it — its actual vol P&L is
0, and its vega is therefore attributed against a **zero** vol move, not the position-level one. So
a fixed-IV leg reports vega ≈ 0 (matching reality) rather than a phantom vega offset by the
residual. A leg pricing off the position `volatility` (no per-leg IV) is attributed with the full
`to.volatility − from.volatility` move. To attribute a per-leg IV change, mark that leg's own IV, or use
{@link explainPnl} directly with your greeks + the vol move you observed.

```typescript
/**
 * Decompose a strategy {@link StrategyPosition}'s realized P&L between two market states, aggregate and
 * per leg. Marks the position at each state with `Position.value()` (respecting per-leg IV and expiry),
 * attributes each leg via t0's greeks, and reports the residual. The aggregate is the term-wise sum
 * of the per-leg attributions — exactly consistent with the breakdown, and correct when different
 * legs respond to different volatilities (below).
 *
 * **Volatility attribution is honest per leg.** A leg built with its own fixed IV holds that IV in
 * `Position.value()`, so a change in the position-level `volatility` does not move it — its actual vol P&L is
 * 0, and its vega is therefore attributed against a **zero** vol move, not the position-level one. So
 * a fixed-IV leg reports vega ≈ 0 (matching reality) rather than a phantom vega offset by the
 * residual. A leg pricing off the position `volatility` (no per-leg IV) is attributed with the full
 * `to.volatility − from.volatility` move. To attribute a per-leg IV change, mark that leg's own IV, or use
 * {@link explainPnl} directly with your greeks + the vol move you observed.
 */
export interface ExplainPositionPnlInput {
    position: StrategyPosition;
    from: PnlMarket;
    to: PnlMarket;
}
```

- from.legVolatilities?: readonly (number | undefined)[]; default: not declared — Per-leg volatilities at this market state (Preview P1), aligned to `position.legs`: a number
marks leg `i` at that volatility (through `Position.value`'s `legVolatilities`) and its vol move
is attributed at the LEG level (`to − from`, each side resolving to the override, else the leg's
fixed `impliedVolatility`, else the position-level `volatility`). `undefined` leaves that leg on
its own precedence. This is how a leg re-marked from a current quote reports a live vega.
- from.riskFreeRate: number; default: not declared
- from.spot: number; default: not declared

- position.metrics().return.bounded.loss: boolean; default: not declared
- position.metrics().return.bounded.profit: boolean; default: not declared
- position.metrics().return.maxLoss: number | null; default: not declared
- position.value: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk').StrategyMarkToMarketMarket>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk').StrategyMarkToMarketResult; default: not declared

- position.value(overrides)?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk').StrategyMarkToMarketMarket> | undefined; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk#HistoricalMeanExpectedReturnsInput

```typescript
export interface HistoricalMeanExpectedReturnsInput extends SampleExpectedReturnsFields {
    method: 'historical-mean';
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- asOf?: string | number; default: not declared — Point-in-time cut: every row whose timestamp is AFTER this instant is excluded from the

an ISO date / zoned datetime), non-decreasing. Required for `asOf` to screen anything.
- periodsPerYear?: number; default: not declared — Annualize by this factor (e.g. `252` for daily, `12` for monthly data): the reported means
become `periodMean × periodsPerYear`. OMITTED means per-period means with `annualized: false`
— annualization is never silent.
- returns: number[][]; default: not declared — Observations-major returns — the same orientation as `CovarianceInput`: `returns[t][k]` is
asset `k`'s simple return in period `t` (one row per period, one column per asset).

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk#KellyOptions

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

```typescript
// ───────────────────────── Kelly ─────────────────────────
export interface KellyOptions extends OptimizeConstraints {
    /** Fraction of full Kelly (e.g. 0.5 for half-Kelly). Must be > 0. Default 1. */
    fraction?: number;
    /**
     * Normalize the Kelly weights to the `budget` (fully invested). Default false (leverage implied).
     * When the raw Kelly weights sum to ≤ 0 (a net-short growth-optimal book), dividing by that total
     * would flip every position's sign — instead the UNnormalized weights are returned with
     * `converged: false` and a `risk.kelly_negative_sum` warning (design law #4: disclose, don't flip).
     * With `constraints`, this flag is a no-op: the constrained solve already pins Σw to the budget.
     */
    normalize?: boolean;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- bounds?: [number, number][]; default: not declared — Per-asset `[lo, hi]` bounds.
- budget?: number; default: not declared — Sum-to budget (`Σw`). Default 1 (fully invested).
- fraction?: number; default: not declared — Fraction of full Kelly (e.g. 0.5 for half-Kelly). Must be > 0. Default 1.
- groups?: GroupConstraint[]; default: not declared — Sector/group exposure caps (`min ≤ Σ_group w ≤ max`).
- longOnly?: boolean; default: not declared — Forbid short positions (`w ≥ 0`). Ignored where `bounds` is given.
- maximumIterations?: number; default: not declared — Projected-gradient iteration cap. Default 5000.
- normalize?: boolean; default: not declared — Normalize the Kelly weights to the `budget` (fully invested). Default false (leverage implied).
When the raw Kelly weights sum to ≤ 0 (a net-short growth-optimal book), dividing by that total
would flip every position's sign — instead the UNnormalized weights are returned with
`converged: false` and a `risk.kelly_negative_sum` warning (design law #4: disclose, don't flip).
With `constraints`, this flag is a no-op: the constrained solve already pins Σw to the budget.
- tolerance?: number; default: not declared — Projected-gradient convergence tolerance on the weight step. Default 1e-11.
- transactionCosts?: { perUnitTurnover: number | number[]; previousWeights: number[]; }; default: not declared — Linear transaction cost charged on the trade away from a base portfolio. Subtracted from the
objective as `Σ perUnitTurnover_i·|w_i − previousWeights_i|` (a scalar applies to every asset). Needs `previousWeights`.
- transactionCosts.perUnitTurnover: number | number[]; default: not declared
- transactionCosts.previousWeights: number[]; default: not declared
- turnover?: TurnoverConstraint; default: not declared — Turnover budget against a base portfolio (`Σ|w − previousWeights| ≤ max`).
- turnover.max: number; default: not declared — Maximum one-way + reverse (L1) turnover allowed.
- turnover.previousWeights: number[]; default: not declared — Current weights to measure turnover against.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk#KellySizing

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

The sizing verdict.

```typescript
/** The sizing verdict. */
export interface KellySizing {
    /**
     * `f*` — the growth-optimal fraction of bankroll. `null` when the edge has **no downside**, so
     * log-growth increases without bound and there is no finite unconstrained optimum (finite-success
     * law — never `Infinity`; a `risk.kelly_unbounded` diagnostic explains it).
     */
    fullKelly: number | null;
    /**
     * The recommended fraction after the fractional/drawdown/max caps (≥ 0). `null` only for a
     * no-downside edge with **no** explicit cap — a finite recommendation then requires a `maxFraction`.
     */
    recommendedFraction: number | null;
    /** `κ = recommendedFraction / fullKelly` — the applied Kelly multiple (0 when there's no edge);
     *  `null` when `fullKelly` is null (undefined against a non-existent optimum). */
    appliedFraction: number | null;
    /** Expected per-period log-growth at the recommended fraction; `null` when there is none. */
    growthRate: number | null;
    /** Expected per-period log-growth at full Kelly (the maximum); `null` for a no-downside edge. */
    growthRateFull: number | null;
    /** `ln 2 / growthRate` — periods to double at the recommended fraction (`Infinity` when growth ≤ 0,
     *  `null` when there is no finite recommendation). */
    periodsToDouble: number | null;
    /** `P(wealth ever falls to toFraction of the starting bankroll)` at the recommended fraction (continuous model). */
    drawdownRisk: {
        toFraction: number;
        probability: number;
    };
    /** Which cap set the recommended fraction (`no-downside` = unbounded edge with no cap supplied). */
    bindingConstraint: 'fraction' | 'drawdown-limit' | 'max-fraction' | 'no-edge' | 'no-downside';
    /** Returns path only: the Gaussian `μ/σ²` estimate, for comparison with the exact empirical `f*`. */
    gaussianKelly?: number;
    /** Present when `horizonPeriods` is given: the median wealth projection over the horizonPeriods. */
    horizonGrowth?: {
        horizonPeriods: number;
        logGrowth: number;
        growthMultiple: number;
    };
    /** Prose an agent relays. */
    rationale: string;
    assumptions: {
        conventionsVersion: string;
        fraction: number;
        drawdownModel: 'continuous-gbm';
        edgeType: 'binary' | 'outcomes' | 'gaussian' | 'returns';
    };
    diagnostics: Diagnostics;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- appliedFraction: number | null; default: not declared — `κ = recommendedFraction / fullKelly` — the applied Kelly multiple (0 when there's no edge);

- assumptions.edgeType: 'returns' | 'gaussian' | 'binary' | 'outcomes'; default: not declared

- bindingConstraint: 'fraction' | 'drawdown-limit' | 'max-fraction' | 'no-edge' | 'no-downside'; default: not declared — Which cap set the recommended fraction (`no-downside` = unbounded edge with no cap supplied).
- diagnostics: Diagnostics; default: not declared
- diagnostics.autoReason?: string; default: not declared — When a meta-engine (e.g. `engines.auto()`) selected a delegate, this is a one-sentence,
human-readable explanation of WHY that delegate was chosen (`engine` then names the delegate).
Absent when no auto-selection took place.
- diagnostics.converged?: boolean; default: not declared — Whether an iterative procedure converged. `false` means the value is not trustworthy.
- diagnostics.decomposition?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Named intermediate quantities the value decomposes into — a par spread's protection leg and
risky annuity, a forward variance's near/far legs. The H-series explain paths disclose their

- diagnostics.timingMs?: number; default: not declared — Wall-clock timing in milliseconds, when measured.

- drawdownRisk: { probability: number; toFraction: number; }; default: not declared — `P(wealth ever falls to toFraction of the starting bankroll)` at the recommended fraction (continuous model).

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk#MaxSharpeOptions

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

```typescript
// ───────────────────────── maximum Sharpe (tangency) ─────────────────────────
export interface MaxSharpeOptions extends OptimizeConstraints {
    /**
     * Risk-free rate **in the same per-period units as `mean` and `covariance`** — a daily-return
     * problem takes a daily rate (0.04/252), not 0.04. Default 0.
     *
     * Named `riskFreeRatePerPeriod` (renamed from `riskFreeRate` pre-1.0) because every other
     * `riskFreeRate` in the library — `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/performance`'s sharpe/sortino/alpha, the backtest
     * report — is an ANNUAL rate that the callee de-annualizes. Passing 0.04 here on daily inputs
     * silently subtracted a 4%-per-DAY hurdle, turning every excess return negative and dropping
     * maxSharpe into its min-variance fallback. One spelling per unit: the compiler now catches it.
     */
    riskFreeRatePerPeriod?: number;
}
```

- groups?: GroupConstraint[]; default: not declared — Sector/group exposure caps (`min ≤ Σ_group w ≤ max`).
- longOnly?: boolean; default: not declared — Forbid short positions (`w ≥ 0`). Ignored where `bounds` is given.
- maximumIterations?: number; default: not declared — Projected-gradient iteration cap. Default 5000.
- riskFreeRatePerPeriod?: number; default: not declared — Risk-free rate **in the same per-period units as `mean` and `covariance`** — a daily-return
problem takes a daily rate (0.04/252), not 0.04. Default 0.

Named `riskFreeRatePerPeriod` (renamed from `riskFreeRate` pre-1.0) because every other
`riskFreeRate` in the library — `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/performance`'s sharpe/sortino/alpha, the backtest

silently subtracted a 4%-per-DAY hurdle, turning every excess return negative and dropping
maxSharpe into its min-variance fallback. One spelling per unit: the compiler now catches it.

only). `false` when it was requested but its expansion was out of domain — the plain Gaussian
quantile was reported instead and a `risk.cornish_fisher_out_of_domain` warning says so.

- diagnostics.warnings: QuantWarning[]; default: not declared
- horizonPeriods: number; default: not declared
- method: VaRMethod; default: not declared
- samples: number; default: not declared — The number of simulated samples actually drawn (always echoed).
- seed: number; default: not declared — The PRNG seed actually used (always echoed for reproducibility).
- valueAtRisk: number; default: not declared — Positive loss magnitude at `confidence`.

```typescript
export interface OptimizeConstraints {
    /** Forbid short positions (`w ≥ 0`). Ignored where `bounds` is given. */
    longOnly?: boolean;

    bounds?: [
        number,
        number
    ][];

    /** Sector/group exposure caps (`min ≤ Σ_group w ≤ max`). */
    groups?: GroupConstraint[];

    turnover?: TurnoverConstraint;
    /**
     * Linear transaction cost charged on the trade away from a base portfolio. Subtracted from the
     * objective as `Σ perUnitTurnover_i·|w_i − previousWeights_i|` (a scalar applies to every asset). Needs `previousWeights`.
     */
    transactionCosts?: {
        perUnitTurnover: number | number[];
        previousWeights: number[];
    };
    /** Projected-gradient iteration cap. Default 5000. */
    maximumIterations?: number;
    /** Projected-gradient convergence tolerance on the weight step. Default 1e-11. */
    tolerance?: number;
}
```

- groups?: GroupConstraint[]; default: not declared — Sector/group exposure caps (`min ≤ Σ_group w ≤ max`).
- longOnly?: boolean; default: not declared — Forbid short positions (`w ≥ 0`). Ignored where `bounds` is given.
- maximumIterations?: number; default: not declared — Projected-gradient iteration cap. Default 5000.
- tolerance?: number; default: not declared — Projected-gradient convergence tolerance on the weight step. Default 1e-11.

objective as `Σ perUnitTurnover_i·|w_i − previousWeights_i|` (a scalar applies to every asset). Needs `previousWeights`.
- transactionCosts.perUnitTurnover: number | number[]; default: not declared
- transactionCosts.previousWeights: number[]; default: not declared
- turnover?: TurnoverConstraint; default: not declared — Turnover budget against a base portfolio (`Σ|w − previousWeights| ≤ max`).

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk#OptionsMarginResult

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

```typescript
export interface OptionsMarginResult {
    /** Applied conventions, echoed (Law 2 report grammar). */
    assumptions: {
        conventionsVersion: string;
        [k: string]: unknown;
    };
    /** Structured warnings; always present (possibly empty). */
    diagnostics: {
        warnings: QuantWarning[];
    };
    /** Initial margin / buying-power requirement, in account currency. */
    initialMargin: number;
    /**
     * Buying-power reduction — what the account must set aside. Equals `initialMargin` for margin
     * accounts; for a long-only (fully-paid) position it is the net debit paid.
     */
    buyingPowerReduction: number;
    /**
     * Worst-case expiration loss magnitude per contract; `null` when the loss is unbounded (e.g. a
     * naked call — no finite worst case exists; `Infinity` is not JSON-safe, Law 7). `definedRisk:
     * false` is the primary unbounded discriminant, and a `risk.unbounded_loss` warning explains the
     * null.
     */
    maxLoss: number | null;
    /** Net debit paid (> 0) or credit received (< 0), per contract. */
    netDebit: number;
    /** True when the position's loss is capped (spreads / condors / butterflies / long options). */
    definedRisk: boolean;
    /**
     * How the requirement was derived. `'reg-t-naked-put'` is the bounded-but-uncovered case: the
     * loss IS capped (a put's underlying stops at 0), but the position is short naked puts, so the
     * requirement is the Reg-T naked-put charge on the uncovered contracts plus the capped max loss
     * of whatever remains — not the cash-secured exercise value.
     */
    method: 'defined-risk-max-loss' | 'reg-t-naked' | 'reg-t-naked-put' | 'long-premium';
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- assumptions: { [k: string]: unknown; conventionsVersion: string; }; default: not declared — Applied conventions, echoed (Law 2 report grammar).
- assumptions.conventionsVersion: string; default: not declared
- buyingPowerReduction: number; default: not declared — Buying-power reduction — what the account must set aside. Equals `initialMargin` for margin
accounts; for a long-only (fully-paid) position it is the net debit paid.
- definedRisk: boolean; default: not declared — True when the position's loss is capped (spreads / condors / butterflies / long options).
- diagnostics: { warnings: QuantWarning[]; }; default: not declared — Structured warnings; always present (possibly empty).
- diagnostics.warnings: QuantWarning[]; default: not declared
- initialMargin: number; default: not declared — Initial margin / buying-power requirement, in account currency.
- maxLoss: number | null; default: not declared — Worst-case expiration loss magnitude per contract; `null` when the loss is unbounded (e.g. a
naked call — no finite worst case exists; `Infinity` is not JSON-safe, Law 7). `definedRisk:
false` is the primary unbounded discriminant, and a `risk.unbounded_loss` warning explains the
null.
- method: 'reg-t-naked' | 'defined-risk-max-loss' | 'reg-t-naked-put' | 'long-premium'; default: not declared — How the requirement was derived. `'reg-t-naked-put'` is the bounded-but-uncovered case: the
loss IS capped (a put's underlying stops at 0), but the position is short naked puts, so the
requirement is the Reg-T naked-put charge on the uncovered contracts plus the capped max loss
of whatever remains — not the cash-secured exercise value.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk#PnlExplain

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

A realized P&L attribution: greek terms + the unexplained residual, summing exactly to `total`.

```typescript
/** A realized P&L attribution: greek terms + the unexplained residual, summing exactly to `total`. */
export interface PnlExplain {
    /** Applied conventions, echoed (Law 2 report grammar). */
    assumptions: {
        conventionsVersion: string;
        [k: string]: unknown;
    };
    /** Structured warnings (e.g. a dominant residual); always present (possibly empty). */
    diagnostics: {
        warnings: QuantWarning[];
    };

    total: number;
    /** Delta term: `Δ·dS`. */
    delta: number;
    /** Gamma term: `½Γ·dS²`. */
    gamma: number;
    /** Vega term: `Vega·dσ`. */
    vega: number;
    /** Theta term: `Θ·dt`. */
    theta: number;
    /** Rho term: `Rho·dr`. */
    rho: number;
    /** Second-order spot–vol cross term: `vanna·dS·dσ` (0 unless the greeks carry `vanna`). */
    vanna: number;
    /** Second-order vol-convexity term: `½·vomma·dσ²` (0 unless the greeks carry `vomma`). */
    vomma: number;
    /** Second-order spot–time cross term: `charm·dS·dt` (0 unless the greeks carry `charm`). */
    charm: number;
    /** Second-order vol–time cross term: `veta·dσ·dt` (0 unless the greeks carry `veta`). */
    veta: number;
    /** Second-order vol–rate cross term: `vera·dσ·dr` (0 unless the greeks carry `vera`). */
    vera: number;
    /** Second-order spot–rate cross term: `deltaRate·dS·dr` (0 unless the greeks carry `deltaRate`). */
    deltaRate: number;
    /** Second-order time–rate cross term: `thetaRate·dt·dr` (0 unless the greeks carry `thetaRate`). */
    thetaRate: number;
    /** Second-order rate-convexity term: `½·rhoConvexity·dr²` (0 unless the greeks carry `rhoConvexity`). */
    rhoConvexity: number;
    /** Second-order time-convexity term: `½·thetaConvexity·dt²` (0 unless the greeks carry `thetaConvexity`). */
    thetaConvexity: number;
    /** First-order dividend-carry term: `φ·dq` (0 unless the greeks carry `phi`). */
    phi: number;
    /**
     * `total − Σ(terms)` — the full 2nd-order Taylor in (spot, vol, time, rate) plus the dividend carry
     * is now attributed, so the residual is only 3rd-order-and-higher (speed/ultima/…), any 2nd-order
     * greek the caller did not supply, and model/data. Grows as the greek expansion breaks.
     */
    unexplained: number;
}
```

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk#PortfolioVaRInput

Kind: type; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

The one request for a portfolio's VaR: `method` names the model — `'parametric'` (a Gaussian on
the covariance), `'monteCarlo'` (correlated normal draws on the covariance, seeded), or
`'historical'` (the empirical tail of the weighted return history). No method is defaulted.

```typescript
/**
 * The one request for a portfolio's VaR: `method` names the model — `'parametric'` (a Gaussian on
 * the covariance), `'monteCarlo'` (correlated normal draws on the covariance, seeded), or
 * `'historical'` (the empirical tail of the weighted return history). No method is defaulted.
 */
export type PortfolioVaRInput = (ParametricPortfolioVaRInput & {
    method: 'parametric';
}) | (MonteCarloPortfolioVaRInput & {
    method: 'monteCarlo';
}) | HistoricalPortfolioVaRInput;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- method: 'historical'; default: not declared
- options?: HistoricalPortfolioVaROptions; default: not declared
- options.confidence?: number; default: not declared
- options.horizonPeriods?: number; default: not declared
- returns: ArrayLike<ArrayLike<number>>; default: not declared
- weights: ArrayLike<number>; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk#Position

```typescript
export interface Position<T = unknown> {
    id?: string;

     * Contract multiplier applied to per-unit value and Greeks (100 for a listed US equity option

}
```

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk#PositionGreeks

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

A position's Greeks in TotalFinance's ONE unit system — the units `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/options` and
`@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy` report (`DEFAULT_GREEK_UNITS`), so a `blackScholesGreeks(...)` /
`Position.value().greeks` object spreads straight in: `{ value, spot, ...greeks }`.

Per unit of the position (per share of one contract when `Position.multiplier` scales it):
  - `delta` per $1 of spot, `gamma` per $1²;
  - `theta` per CALENDAR DAY; `vega` per 1 volatility POINT (0.01); `rho` per 1% rate (0.01);
    `phi` per 1% dividend yield;
  - the second-order Greeks in the options package's own units: `vanna` ∂Δ/∂σ and `vomma` ∂²V/∂σ²
    per 1.00 σ, `charm` = ∂Δ/∂T and `veta` = ∂vega/∂T per YEAR of time-to-expiry (vega per 1.00 σ),
    `vera` per 1.00 σ per 1.00 rate;
  - the rate cross terms the options package does not emit follow the first-order conventions:
    `deltaRate` per 1% rate, `thetaRate` per day per 1% rate, `rhoConvexity` per (1%)²,
    `thetaConvexity` per day².
The Taylor engine converts to the raw per-year / per-1.00 form internally, in one place. Third-order
Greeks (`speed`, `color`, `zomma`, `ultima`) and `lambda` are accepted so a whole `ExtendedGreeks`
can be passed, and are not used by the second-order expansion.

```typescript
/**
 * A position's Greeks in TotalFinance's ONE unit system — the units `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/options` and
 * `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy` report (`DEFAULT_GREEK_UNITS`), so a `blackScholesGreeks(...)` /
 * `Position.value().greeks` object spreads straight in: `{ value, spot, ...greeks }`.
 *
 * Per unit of the position (per share of one contract when `Position.multiplier` scales it):
 *   - `delta` per $1 of spot, `gamma` per $1²;
 *   - `theta` per CALENDAR DAY; `vega` per 1 volatility POINT (0.01); `rho` per 1% rate (0.01);
 *     `phi` per 1% dividend yield;
 *   - the second-order Greeks in the options package's own units: `vanna` ∂Δ/∂σ and `vomma` ∂²V/∂σ²
 *     per 1.00 σ, `charm` = ∂Δ/∂T and `veta` = ∂vega/∂T per YEAR of time-to-expiry (vega per 1.00 σ),
 *     `vera` per 1.00 σ per 1.00 rate;
 *   - the rate cross terms the options package does not emit follow the first-order conventions:
 *     `deltaRate` per 1% rate, `thetaRate` per day per 1% rate, `rhoConvexity` per (1%)²,
 *     `thetaConvexity` per day².
 * The Taylor engine converts to the raw per-year / per-1.00 form internally, in one place. Third-order
 * Greeks (`speed`, `color`, `zomma`, `ultima`) and `lambda` are accepted so a whole `ExtendedGreeks`
 * can be passed, and are not used by the second-order expansion.
 */
export interface PositionGreeks {
    /** Current mark value of the position (per unit). */
    value: number;
    /** Reference spot, required to resolve percent spot shocks into price moves. */
    spot?: number;
    /** ∂V/∂S per $1 of spot. */
    delta?: number;
    /** ∂²V/∂S² per $1². */
    gamma?: number;
    /** ∂V/∂σ per 1 volatility point (0.01), as the options package reports it. */
    vega?: number;
    /** ∂V/∂t per CALENDAR DAY (negative for a long option), as the options package reports it. */
    theta?: number;
    /** ∂V/∂r per 1% rate (0.01), as the options package reports it. */
    rho?: number;
    /** ∂²V/∂S∂σ per 1.00 σ per $ — the options package's `vanna`. Optional — omitted ⇒ its term is 0. */
    vanna?: number;
    /** ∂²V/∂σ² per 1.00 σ² — the options package's `vomma`. Optional. */
    vomma?: number;
    /** ∂Δ/∂T per year of time-to-expiry — the options package's `charm` (delta drift as expiry recedes). Optional. */
    charm?: number;
    /** ∂vega/∂T per year of time-to-expiry, vega per 1.00 σ — the options package's `veta`. Optional. */
    veta?: number;
    /** ∂²V/∂σ∂r per 1.00 σ per 1.00 rate — the options package's `vera`. Optional. */
    vera?: number;
    /** ∂²V/∂S∂r per $ per 1% rate — the spot-rate cross (`∂Δ/∂r`). Optional. */
    deltaRate?: number;
    /** ∂²V/∂t∂r per calendar day per 1% rate — the time-rate cross (`∂Θ/∂r`). Optional. */
    thetaRate?: number;
    /** ∂²V/∂r² per (1%)² — rho convexity. Optional. */
    rhoConvexity?: number;
    /** ∂²V/∂t² per calendar day² — theta convexity (theta's own bleed). Optional. */
    thetaConvexity?: number;
    /** φ = ∂V/∂q per 1% dividend yield — the options package's `phi` (dividend rho). Optional. */
    phi?: number;
    /** Accepted from a whole `ExtendedGreeks`; not used by the second-order expansion. */
    speed?: number;
    /** Accepted from a whole `ExtendedGreeks`; not used by the second-order expansion. */
    color?: number;
    /** Accepted from a whole `ExtendedGreeks`; not used by the second-order expansion. */
    zomma?: number;
    /** Accepted from a whole `ExtendedGreeks`; not used by the second-order expansion. */
    ultima?: number;
    /** Accepted from a whole `ExtendedGreeks` (`null` = elasticity undefined); not used by the expansion. */
    lambda?: number | null;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- charm?: number; default: not declared — ∂Δ/∂T per year of time-to-expiry — the options package's `charm` (delta drift as expiry recedes). Optional.
- color?: number; default: not declared — Accepted from a whole `ExtendedGreeks`; not used by the second-order expansion.
- delta?: number; default: not declared — ∂V/∂S per $1 of spot.
- deltaRate?: number; default: not declared — ∂²V/∂S∂r per $ per 1% rate — the spot-rate cross (`∂Δ/∂r`). Optional.
- gamma?: number; default: not declared — ∂²V/∂S² per $1².
- lambda?: number | null; default: not declared — Accepted from a whole `ExtendedGreeks` (`null` = elasticity undefined); not used by the expansion.
- phi?: number; default: not declared — φ = ∂V/∂q per 1% dividend yield — the options package's `phi` (dividend rho). Optional.
- rho?: number; default: not declared — ∂V/∂r per 1% rate (0.01), as the options package reports it.
- rhoConvexity?: number; default: not declared — ∂²V/∂r² per (1%)² — rho convexity. Optional.
- speed?: number; default: not declared — Accepted from a whole `ExtendedGreeks`; not used by the second-order expansion.
- spot?: number; default: not declared — Reference spot, required to resolve percent spot shocks into price moves.
- theta?: number; default: not declared — ∂V/∂t per CALENDAR DAY (negative for a long option), as the options package reports it.
- thetaConvexity?: number; default: not declared — ∂²V/∂t² per calendar day² — theta convexity (theta's own bleed). Optional.
- thetaRate?: number; default: not declared — ∂²V/∂t∂r per calendar day per 1% rate — the time-rate cross (`∂Θ/∂r`). Optional.
- ultima?: number; default: not declared — Accepted from a whole `ExtendedGreeks`; not used by the second-order expansion.
- value: number; default: not declared — Current mark value of the position (per unit).
- vanna?: number; default: not declared — ∂²V/∂S∂σ per 1.00 σ per $ — the options package's `vanna`. Optional — omitted ⇒ its term is 0.
- vega?: number; default: not declared — ∂V/∂σ per 1 volatility point (0.01), as the options package reports it.
- vera?: number; default: not declared — ∂²V/∂σ∂r per 1.00 σ per 1.00 rate — the options package's `vera`. Optional.
- veta?: number; default: not declared — ∂vega/∂T per year of time-to-expiry, vega per 1.00 σ — the options package's `veta`. Optional.
- vomma?: number; default: not declared — ∂²V/∂σ² per 1.00 σ² — the options package's `vomma`. Optional.
- zomma?: number; default: not declared — Accepted from a whole `ExtendedGreeks`; not used by the second-order expansion.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk#ShrunkKelly

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

The estimation-error-shrunk Kelly book.

```typescript
/** The estimation-error-shrunk Kelly book. */
export interface ShrunkKelly {
    /** Estimation-error shrinkage factor `c* ∈ [0, 1]`. */
    shrinkage: number;
    /** The applied scaling `fraction · c*`. */
    appliedScaling: number;
    /** Shrunk Kelly weights `fraction · c* · Σ̂⁻¹μ̂`. */
    weights: number[];
    /** Naive plug-in Kelly weights `Σ̂⁻¹μ̂` (before any shrinkage). */
    naiveWeights: number[];
    /** In-sample squared Sharpe `θ̂² = μ̂ᵀΣ̂⁻¹μ̂` (biased high). */
    inSampleSharpeSquared: number;
    /** Bias-corrected out-of-sample squared Sharpe `θ̂² − n/T` (may be ≤ 0). */
    correctedSharpeSquared: number;
    /** Expected out-of-sample log-growth at the applied scaling. */
    expectedGrowth: number;
    /** Expected out-of-sample log-growth of the naive (unshrunk) book — often negative. */
    naiveExpectedGrowth: number;
    assumptions: {
        conventionsVersion: string;
        assets: number;
        sampleSize: number;
        fraction: number;
    };
    diagnostics: Diagnostics;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- appliedScaling: number; default: not declared — The applied scaling `fraction · c*`.
- assumptions: { assets: number; conventionsVersion: string; fraction: number; sampleSize: number; }; default: not declared
- assumptions.assets: number; default: not declared
- assumptions.conventionsVersion: string; default: not declared
- assumptions.fraction: number; default: not declared
- assumptions.sampleSize: number; default: not declared
- correctedSharpeSquared: number; default: not declared — Bias-corrected out-of-sample squared Sharpe `θ̂² − n/T` (may be ≤ 0).
- diagnostics: Diagnostics; default: not declared
- diagnostics.autoReason?: string; default: not declared — When a meta-engine (e.g. `engines.auto()`) selected a delegate, this is a one-sentence,
human-readable explanation of WHY that delegate was chosen (`engine` then names the delegate).
Absent when no auto-selection took place.
- diagnostics.converged?: boolean; default: not declared — Whether an iterative procedure converged. `false` means the value is not trustworthy.
- diagnostics.decomposition?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Named intermediate quantities the value decomposes into — a par spread's protection leg and
risky annuity, a forward variance's near/far legs. The H-series explain paths disclose their
arithmetic here so a caller can audit the ratio, not just receive it (3B.3).
- diagnostics.engine?: string; default: not declared — Pricing/solver engine name, e.g. `black-scholes-merton`.
- diagnostics.finiteDifferenceBumps?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Finite-difference engines: the ACTUAL bump sizes used for FD Greeks (spec P2.3) — adaptive
near the vol/time boundaries, so the caller can see exactly what was differenced.
Keys: `spotStep`, `volatilityStep`, `timeStepYears`, `rateStep`, and — extended Greeks only —
`dividendYieldStep`. Each is the actual step differenced, in the unit of the coordinate it
bumps. (This doc named the retired `hS`/`hSig`/`hT`/`hR`/`hQ` keys for one release after the
emit sites had moved to the semantic names, so a caller following it read `undefined`.)
- diagnostics.iterations?: number; default: not declared — Iteration count for iterative methods.
- diagnostics.method?: string; default: not declared — Numerical method, e.g. `closed-form`, `brent`, `finite-difference`.
- diagnostics.selection?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing').SelectionReport; default: not declared — The structured engine-selection report (Gate C, `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing`): who was selected,
why, and — for automatic selection — every candidate considered with its verdict. This is the
machine-readable superset of `engine` + `autoReason` (which remain for compatibility);
`selected.name` always agrees with `engine` when both are present.
- diagnostics.selection.candidates?: readonly import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing').SelectionCandidate[]; default: not declared — Candidates an automatic selection considered; absent for explicit mode.
- diagnostics.selection.mode: 'explicit' | 'automatic'; default: not declared
- diagnostics.selection.reason: string; default: not declared — Why the selected engine answers this request.
- diagnostics.selection.selected: { name: string; version?: string; }; default: not declared
- diagnostics.selection.selected.name: string; default: not declared
- diagnostics.selection.selected.version?: string; default: not declared
- diagnostics.timingMs?: number; default: not declared — Wall-clock timing in milliseconds, when measured.
- diagnostics.warmup?: number; default: not declared — Series facades: number of leading output slots that are warmup sentinels (null/NaN) while the
computation seeds. Equals the input length when the indicator never emitted.
- diagnostics.warnings: QuantWarning[]; default: not declared — Structured warnings; always present (possibly empty).
- expectedGrowth: number; default: not declared — Expected out-of-sample log-growth at the applied scaling.
- inSampleSharpeSquared: number; default: not declared — In-sample squared Sharpe `θ̂² = μ̂ᵀΣ̂⁻¹μ̂` (biased high).
- naiveExpectedGrowth: number; default: not declared — Expected out-of-sample log-growth of the naive (unshrunk) book — often negative.
- naiveWeights: number[]; default: not declared — Naive plug-in Kelly weights `Σ̂⁻¹μ̂` (before any shrinkage).
- shrinkage: number; default: not declared — Estimation-error shrinkage factor `c* ∈ [0, 1]`.
- weights: number[]; default: not declared — Shrunk Kelly weights `fraction · c* · Σ̂⁻¹μ̂`.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk#ShrunkKellyInput

```typescript
// Estimation-error-shrunk portfolio Kelly

/** Input for {@link shrunkKelly}. */
```

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk#VaROptions

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

```typescript
export interface VaROptions {
    /** Confidence level in (0, 1). Default 0.95. */
    confidence?: number;
    /**
     * Estimation method. Default `'historical'`.
     *   - `'historical'` — the empirical (hyndman-fan-7) tail quantile of the sample;
     *   - `'parametric'` — the Gaussian quantile of the fitted (μ, σ), optionally Cornish-Fisher;
     *   - `'monteCarlo'` — draws from the **fitted NORMAL** and takes its empirical tail. It captures
     *     no non-normality whatsoever (same two moments as `'parametric'`, plus sampling noise), so
     *     prefer `'parametric'` unless you specifically want sampling diagnostics; use
     *     `'historical'` or the EVT tools when the shape of the tail matters.
     */
    method?: VaRMethod;
    /** Holding-period horizonPeriods in periods; scales by √-time. Default 1. */
    horizonPeriods?: number;
    /**
     * Parametric only: Cornish-Fisher adjustment for skew/excess-kurtosis. Default false. Applied
     * only where the expansion is a monotone quantile map; outside that domain the plain Gaussian
     * quantile is reported with a `risk.cornish_fisher_out_of_domain` warning and
     * `cornishFisher: false`. Over a multi-period `horizonPeriods` the moments are rescaled to the
     * horizon under iid aggregation (`skew/√h`, `excessKurtosis/h`), disclosed as
     * `assumptions.momentScaling: 'iid'`. On a non-parametric method it is ignored with an info
     * warning, never silently.
     */
    cornishFisher?: boolean;
    /** Monte-Carlo only: number of simulated paths. Default 10000. */
    samples?: number;
    /** Monte-Carlo only: PRNG seed for reproducibility. Default 1. */
    seed?: number;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- confidence?: number; default: not declared — Confidence level in (0, 1). Default 0.95.
- cornishFisher?: boolean; default: not declared — Parametric only: Cornish-Fisher adjustment for skew/excess-kurtosis. Default false. Applied
only where the expansion is a monotone quantile map; outside that domain the plain Gaussian
quantile is reported with a `risk.cornish_fisher_out_of_domain` warning and
`cornishFisher: false`. Over a multi-period `horizonPeriods` the moments are rescaled to the
horizon under iid aggregation (`skew/√h`, `excessKurtosis/h`), disclosed as
`assumptions.momentScaling: 'iid'`. On a non-parametric method it is ignored with an info
warning, never silently.
- horizonPeriods?: number; default: not declared — Holding-period horizonPeriods in periods; scales by √-time. Default 1.
- method?: VaRMethod; default: not declared — Estimation method. Default `'historical'`.
  - `'historical'` — the empirical (hyndman-fan-7) tail quantile of the sample;
  - `'parametric'` — the Gaussian quantile of the fitted (μ, σ), optionally Cornish-Fisher;
  - `'monteCarlo'` — draws from the **fitted NORMAL** and takes its empirical tail. It captures
    no non-normality whatsoever (same two moments as `'parametric'`, plus sampling noise), so
    prefer `'parametric'` unless you specifically want sampling diagnostics; use
    `'historical'` or the EVT tools when the shape of the tail matters.
- samples?: number; default: not declared — Monte-Carlo only: number of simulated paths. Default 10000.
- seed?: number; default: not declared — Monte-Carlo only: PRNG seed for reproducibility. Default 1.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk#blackLitterman

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Black-Litterman (1992): blend a market-equilibrium prior on expected returns with subjective views
to get a posterior `μ_BL` and covariance, then mean-variance-optimize. The prior is either supplied
(`priorMean`) or reverse-engineered from market weights (`π = δ·Σ·w_mkt`); each view `j` carries an
uncertainty `Ω_jj` (default the He–Litterman `τ·pᵀΣp`). Posterior:
  `M = [(τΣ)⁻¹ + PᵀΩ⁻¹P]⁻¹`,  `μ_BL = M·[(τΣ)⁻¹π + PᵀΩ⁻¹Q]`,  `Σ_post = Σ + M`.

Returns the standard `Computed` envelope (dx §2.4): the defaulted `tau: 0.05` / `riskAversion: 2.5`
are echoed in `assumptions` (never silently applied), and the posterior solve's convergence lives
in `diagnostics.converged` with an `optimize.not_converged` warning when it fails.

```typescript
export declare function blackLitterman(options: BlackLittermanOptions): BlackLittermanResult;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (options): BlackLittermanOptions; default: not declared
- (options).constraints?: OptimizeConstraints; default: not declared — Constraints applied to the posterior mean-variance weights.
- (options).covariance: Matrix; default: not declared — Asset return covariance Σ (n×n).
- (options).marketWeights?: ArrayLike<number>; default: not declared — Market-cap weights to reverse-engineer the prior `π = δ·Σ·w_mkt`.
- (options).priorMean?: ArrayLike<number>; default: not declared — Prior (equilibrium) expected returns π. Provide this, or `marketWeights` to imply it.
- (options).riskAversion?: number; default: not declared — Risk-aversion δ for the implied prior and the posterior mean-variance weights. Default 2.5.
- (options).tau?: number; default: not declared — Scalar τ scaling the prior uncertainty of the mean (default 0.05).
- (options).views: BlackLittermanView[]; default: not declared — Investor views (at least one).
- return.assumptions: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Assumptions<{ tau: number; riskAversion: number; views: number; }>; default: not declared — Every applied convention, echoed back.
- return.diagnostics: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Diagnostics; default: not declared — How the value was computed, plus any warnings.
- return.provenance?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Provenance; default: not declared — Optional data lineage when the inputs came from a provider.
- return.value: { posteriorCovariance: number[][]; posteriorMean: number[]; priorMean: number[]; weights: number[]; }; default: not declared — The computed value. Never `NaN` or `±Infinity`: a value the model cannot produce is `null`
beside a diagnostic that says why (Law 7 — a warning never licenses a non-finite number).
- return.value.posteriorCovariance: number[][]; default: not declared — Posterior return covariance `Σ + M`, where `M` is the posterior covariance of the mean.
- return.value.posteriorMean: number[]; default: not declared — Posterior (views-blended) expected returns.
- return.value.priorMean: number[]; default: not declared — The supplied or market-implied equilibrium prior π.
- return.value.weights: number[]; default: not declared — Mean-variance-optimal weights under the posterior.
