### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk#conditionalValueAtRiskOptimize

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Minimize portfolio CVaR over a scenario set (Rockafellar–Uryasev, projected subgradient).
`value` carries the weights plus the optimized `conditionalValueAtRisk` and the `valueAtRisk` threshold; `assumptions`
additionally echo the tail confidence `alpha`.

```typescript
export declare function conditionalValueAtRiskOptimize(scenarios: number[][], options?: CVaROptimizeOptions): CVaROptimizeResult;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (options)?: CVaROptimizeOptions; default: not declared
- (options).alpha?: number; default: not declared — Tail confidence α: optimize the mean of the worst `(1 − α)` fraction of losses. Default 0.95.
- (options).bounds?: [number, number][]; default: not declared — Per-asset `[lo, hi]` bounds.
- (options).budget?: number; default: not declared — Sum-to budget (`Σw`). Default 1 (fully invested).
- (options).groups?: GroupConstraint[]; default: not declared — Sector/group exposure caps (`min ≤ Σ_group w ≤ max`).
- (options).longOnly?: boolean; default: not declared — Forbid short positions (`w ≥ 0`). Ignored where `bounds` is given.
- (options).maximumIterations?: number; default: not declared — Projected-subgradient iteration cap. Default 4000.
- (options).minReturn?: number; default: not declared — Optional minimum mean return `μᵀw ≥ minReturn` (μ = per-asset scenario means).
- (options).step?: number; default: not declared — Initial subgradient step size (decays as `step/√t`). Defaults to `1/‖g₀‖` — the step that moves
the FIRST iterate a distance of about 1 in weight space, which is the scale weights live on.
A fixed default (this used to be `1`) is unit-dependent: on decimal daily returns ‖g‖ ≈ 0.01,
so every step moved ~1e-2·(1/√t) and the run plateaued a long way from the optimum while
reporting `converged: true`. Pass an explicit `step` only to override that scaling.
- (options).tolerance?: number; default: not declared — Relative-improvement tolerance for convergence: the run is `converged` only once the best CVaR
improves by less than this over the final 25 iterations. Default `1e-6`.
- (options).transactionCosts?: { perUnitTurnover: number | number[]; previousWeights: number[]; }; default: not declared — Linear transaction cost charged on the trade away from a base portfolio. Subtracted from the
objective as `Σ perUnitTurnover_i·|w_i − previousWeights_i|` (a scalar applies to every asset). Needs `previousWeights`.
- (options).transactionCosts.perUnitTurnover: number | number[]; default: not declared
- (options).transactionCosts.previousWeights: number[]; default: not declared
- (options).turnover?: TurnoverConstraint; default: not declared — Turnover budget against a base portfolio (`Σ|w − previousWeights| ≤ max`).
- (scenarios): number[][]; default: not declared
- return.assumptions: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Assumptions<{ objective: string; budget: number; confidence: number; }>; default: not declared — Every applied convention, echoed back.
- return.diagnostics: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Diagnostics; default: not declared — How the value was computed, plus any warnings.
- return.provenance?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Provenance; default: not declared — Optional data lineage when the inputs came from a provider.
- return.value: { conditionalValueAtRisk: number; objective: number; valueAtRisk: number; weights: number[]; }; default: not declared — The computed value. Never `NaN` or `±Infinity`: a value the model cannot produce is `null`
beside a diagnostic that says why (Law 7 — a warning never licenses a non-finite number).
- return.value.conditionalValueAtRisk: number; default: not declared — The optimized CVaR — mean loss over the worst `(1 − α)` tail (a positive magnitude).
- return.value.objective: number; default: not declared
- return.value.valueAtRisk: number; default: not declared — The VaR threshold (loss quantile at α) at the solution.
- return.value.weights: number[]; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk#costAwareKelly

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Cost-aware Kelly for a continuous edge. Costs — a per-period holding cost plus an amortized round-trip
cost, `c = holdingCost + roundTripCost/horizonPeriods` — reduce the drift (`μ → μ − c`, variance unchanged),
so the growth-optimal size shrinks to `netKelly = max(0, (μ−c)/σ²)` and below the breakeven cost `μ`
the edge is not worth betting. Reports gross vs net Kelly, the growth drag, the penalty for naively
betting gross while paying costs, and refuses a losing bet. See `docs/specs/cost-aware-kelly.md`.

```typescript
export declare function costAwareKelly(input: CostAwareKellyInput): CostAwareKelly;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (input): CostAwareKellyInput; default: not declared
- (input).edge: { gaussian: { mean: number; variance: number; }; } | { returns: ArrayLike<number>; }; default: not declared — The per-period edge: a Gaussian mean/variance, or a return sample (μ, σ² computed from it).
- (input).edge.gaussian: { mean: number; variance: number; }; default: not declared
- (input).edge.gaussian.mean: number; default: not declared
- (input).edge.gaussian.variance: number; default: not declared
- (input).edge.returns: ArrayLike<number>; default: not declared
- (input).fraction?: number; default: not declared — Fractional-Kelly multiplier applied to `netKelly`. Default 0.5. Must be > 0.
- (input).holdingCost?: number; default: not declared — Per-period holding cost per unit of position (financing / borrow / carry). Default 0.
- (input).horizonPeriods?: number; default: not declared — Expected holding periods, to amortize `roundTripCost`. Required when `roundTripCost > 0`.
- (input).roundTripCost?: number; default: not declared — One-time round-trip cost per unit of position (entry + exit). Default 0. Requires `horizonPeriods`.
- return.assumptions: { conventionsVersion: string; edgeType: 'gaussian' | 'returns'; fraction: number; }; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.conventionsVersion: string; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.edgeType: 'returns' | 'gaussian'; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.fraction: number; default: not declared
- return.breakevenCost: number; default: not declared — `μ` — the cost at which the edge vanishes.
- return.costPerPeriod: number; default: not declared — Per-period cost drag `c = holdingCost + roundTripCost/horizonPeriods`.
- return.diagnostics: Diagnostics; default: not declared
- return.grossGrowth: number | null; default: not declared — `μ²/(2σ²)` — expected log-growth at gross Kelly with no costs; `null` with `grossKelly`.
- return.grossKelly: number | null; default: not declared — `μ/σ²` — the growth-optimal fraction ignoring costs; `null` when the edge has zero variance (C hygiene).
- return.growthDrag: number | null; default: not declared — `grossGrowth − netGrowth` — the log-growth the costs cost you; `null` with `grossKelly`.
- return.ignoringCostsGrowth: number | null; default: not declared — Log-growth of naively betting gross Kelly while paying costs (`≤ netGrowth`); `null` with `grossKelly`.
- return.isProfitable: boolean; default: not declared — Whether the net edge is positive (`c < μ`).
- return.mean: number; default: not declared — The edge mean `μ` used.
- return.netGrowth: number | null; default: not declared — `(μ−c)²/(2σ²)` — expected log-growth at net Kelly (the achievable optimum with costs); `null` with `grossKelly`.
- return.netKelly: number | null; default: not declared — `max(0, (μ−c)/σ²)` — the cost-aware growth-optimal fraction; `null` with `grossKelly`.
- return.rationale: string; default: not declared — Prose an agent relays.
- return.recommendedFraction: number | null; default: not declared — `fraction · netKelly` — the recommended size after fractional-Kelly; `null` with `grossKelly`.
- return.variance: number; default: not declared — The edge variance `σ²` used.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk#covariance

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Estimate a portfolio covariance (and mean returns) from raw return history — the first step of
every optimizer journey. Delegates estimation to `estimateCovariance` (`method: 'auto'`
defaults to the sample covariance and shrinks only when it is singular/ill-conditioned, always
disclosing what it did), and reports the full conditioning diagnostics so a caller knows the
matrix is safe to invert BEFORE optimizing with it.

```typescript
export declare function covariance(input: CovarianceInput, options?: CovarianceOptions): CovarianceResult;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (input).returns: number[][]; default: not declared — Observations-major returns: `returns[t][k]` is asset `k`'s simple return in period `t` —
one row per period, one column per asset (the natural CSV/dataframe orientation, and the
TRANSPOSE of `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/math`'s variables-major `estimateCovariance` input). Every row must
have the same number of assets.
- (options)?: EstimateCovarianceOptions; default: not declared
- (options).conditionThreshold?: number; default: not declared — Condition-number threshold above which `'auto'` shrinks rather than using the sample. Default 1e4.
- (options).halfLife?: number; default: not declared — EWMA half-life in periods (method `'ewma'`); `λ = 2^{−1/halfLife}` when `lambda` is omitted.
- (options).lambda?: number; default: not declared — EWMA decay `0 < λ < 1` (method `'ewma'`). Default 0.94 (RiskMetrics).
- (options).ledoitWolfTarget?: 'identity' | 'constant-correlation' | 'single-index'; default: not declared — Ledoit–Wolf shrinkage target when the method resolves to `'ledoit-wolf'` (explicitly or via `'auto'`).
`'identity'` (default), `'constant-correlation'` (fits correlated returns better), or `'single-index'`
(the market-model target, best-specified for stock returns).
- (options).market?: ArrayLike<number>; default: not declared — Observed market return series for the `'single-index'` target (length `T`). Omitted → the
equal-weight cross-sectional proxy is used and disclosed via `assumptions.marketProxy`.
- (options).method?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/math').CovarianceMethod; default: not declared — Estimator; default `'auto'`.
- (options).population?: boolean; default: not declared — Population (`1/T`) vs sample (`1/(T−1)`) normalization. Default `true` (matches Ledoit–Wolf).
- (options).ridge?: number; default: not declared — Ridge diagonal load as a fraction of the average variance (method `'ridge'`). Default 0.1; > 0.
- return.assumptions: { conventionsVersion: string; method: 'sample' | 'ledoit-wolf' | 'ridge' | 'ewma'; observations: number; orientation: 'observations-major'; }; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.conventionsVersion: string; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.method: 'sample' | 'ledoit-wolf' | 'ridge' | 'ewma'; default: not declared — The estimator actually used (`'auto'` resolves before reporting).
- return.assumptions.observations: number; default: not declared

- return.diagnostics: Diagnostics & { conditionNumber: number | null; effectiveRank: number; isPositiveDefinite: boolean; lambda?: number; maxEigenvalue: number; minEigenvalue: number; shrinkage?: number; }; default: not declared
- return.diagnostics.autoReason?: string; default: not declared — When a meta-engine (e.g. `engines.auto()`) selected a delegate, this is a one-sentence,
human-readable explanation of WHY that delegate was chosen (`engine` then names the delegate).
Absent when no auto-selection took place.
- return.diagnostics.conditionNumber: number | null; default: not declared — `null` when the matrix is singular (κ = ∞ has no JSON representation; see warnings).
- return.diagnostics.converged?: boolean; default: not declared — Whether an iterative procedure converged. `false` means the value is not trustworthy.
- return.diagnostics.decomposition?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Named intermediate quantities the value decomposes into — a par spread's protection leg and
risky annuity, a forward variance's near/far legs. The H-series explain paths disclose their

- return.diagnostics.effectiveRank: number; default: not declared
- return.diagnostics.engine?: string; default: not declared — Pricing/solver engine name, e.g. `black-scholes-merton`.
- return.diagnostics.finiteDifferenceBumps?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Finite-difference engines: the ACTUAL bump sizes used for FD Greeks (spec P2.3) — adaptive
near the vol/time boundaries, so the caller can see exactly what was differenced.
Keys: `spotStep`, `volatilityStep`, `timeStepYears`, `rateStep`, and — extended Greeks only —
`dividendYieldStep`. Each is the actual step differenced, in the unit of the coordinate it

- return.diagnostics.isPositiveDefinite: boolean; default: not declared
- return.diagnostics.iterations?: number; default: not declared — Iteration count for iterative methods.
- return.diagnostics.lambda?: number; default: not declared
- return.diagnostics.maxEigenvalue: number; default: not declared
- return.diagnostics.method?: string; default: not declared — Numerical method, e.g. `closed-form`, `brent`, `finite-difference`.
- return.diagnostics.minEigenvalue: number; default: not declared
- return.diagnostics.selection?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing').SelectionReport; default: not declared — The structured engine-selection report (Gate C, `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing`): who was selected,

Deflated Sharpe Ratio (Bailey & López de Prado 2014): the PSR evaluated against the *expected
maximum* Sharpe that `N` independent trials would produce by chance, so selecting the best of a
parameter sweep is penalised. Pass the trial Sharpes (variance computed for you) or `trialCount` plus
their variance directly.

```typescript
export declare function deflatedSharpeRatio(statistics: SharpeStatistics, trials: { trialSharpes: ArrayLike<number>; } | { trialCount: number; varianceSharpe: number; }): DeflatedSharpeResult;
```

- (statistics).observations: number; default: not declared — Number of observations.
- (statistics).sharpe: number | null; default: not declared — Per-observation Sharpe ratio `mean(excess)/std` (NOT annualized). `null` (C hygiene) when the
returns have zero variance: there is no dispersion to scale by, and the report says so.
- (statistics).skewness: number; default: not declared — Skewness `γ₃` of the returns.
- (trials): { trialSharpes: ArrayLike<number>; } | { trialCount: number; varianceSharpe: number; }; default: not declared
- (trials).trialCount: number; default: not declared
- (trials).trialSharpes: ArrayLike<number>; default: not declared
- (trials).varianceSharpe: number; default: not declared
- return.assumptions: { [k: string]: unknown; conventionsVersion: string; }; default: not declared — Applied conventions, echoed (Law 2 report grammar).
- return.assumptions.conventionsVersion: string; default: not declared
- return.deflatedSharpe: number | null; default: not declared — `null` when the statistics carry no Sharpe (a zero-variance series).
- return.diagnostics: { warnings: QuantWarning[]; }; default: not declared — Structured warnings; always present (possibly empty).
- return.diagnostics.warnings: QuantWarning[]; default: not declared
- return.expectedMaxSharpe: number; default: not declared — Expected maximum Sharpe across `trialCount` under the null — the deflation benchmark `SR₀`.
- return.probabilisticSharpe: number | null; default: not declared — The un-deflated PSR (benchmark 0), for comparison.
- return.trialCount: number; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk#efficientFrontier

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Trace the constrained mean-variance efficient frontier by composing `minVariance`,
`meanVariance`, and (with a risk-free rate) `maxSharpe` under ONE constraint set.

```ts
efficientFrontier({
  mean,
  covariance,
  grid: { kind: 'points', count: 20 },
  constraints: { longOnly: true },
  riskFreeRatePerPeriod: 0.04 / 252,
});
```

`value.points` keeps every grid point in order; a target outside the achievable range is a
`feasible: false` point whose `reason` names the range, never a throw. `diagnostics.monotone`
reports whether volatility rises with expected return across the solved points (the shape a
correct frontier has) and names the first violation in a warning when it does not.

```typescript
export declare function efficientFrontier(input: EfficientFrontierInput): EfficientFrontierResult;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (input): EfficientFrontierInput; default: not declared
- (input).constraints?: EfficientFrontierConstraints; default: not declared — The optimizer's feasible-region grammar (`longOnly`, `bounds`, `budget`, `groups`, …).
- (input).covariance: Matrix; default: not declared — Asset return covariance Σ (n×n).
- (input).grid: EfficientFrontierGrid; default: not declared
- (input).mean: ArrayLike<number>; default: not declared — Per-asset expected returns as a dense stored-data ArrayLike (same period as covariance).
- (input).riskFreeRatePerPeriod?: number; default: not declared — Risk-free rate in the SAME per-period units as `mean` (a daily problem takes 0.04/252, not
0.04) — the `maxSharpe` spelling. When present every point reports a Sharpe ratio and the
tangency portfolio is solved and reported under `value.tangency`.
- return.assumptions: { budget: number; constraintSummary: string; conventionsVersion: string; grid: { kind: EfficientFrontierGridKind; count: number; }; objective: 'mean-variance'; riskFreeRatePerPeriod?: number; }; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.budget: number; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.constraintSummary: string; default: not declared — Prose summary of the constraint set every point was solved under.
- return.assumptions.conventionsVersion: string; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.grid: { count: number; kind: EfficientFrontierGridKind; }; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.grid.count: number; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.grid.kind: 'risk-aversion' | 'target-return' | 'points'; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.objective: 'mean-variance'; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.riskFreeRatePerPeriod?: number; default: not declared
- return.diagnostics: Diagnostics & { converged: boolean; failedCount: number; iterations: number; maximumReturnBounded: boolean | null; monotone: boolean; solvedCount: number; }; default: not declared
- return.diagnostics.autoReason?: string; default: not declared — When a meta-engine (e.g. `engines.auto()`) selected a delegate, this is a one-sentence,
human-readable explanation of WHY that delegate was chosen (`engine` then names the delegate).
Absent when no auto-selection took place.
- return.diagnostics.converged?: boolean; default: not declared — Whether an iterative procedure converged. `false` means the value is not trustworthy.
Every solved point converged (false when any point failed or stopped early).
- return.diagnostics.decomposition?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Named intermediate quantities the value decomposes into — a par spread's protection leg and
risky annuity, a forward variance's near/far legs. The H-series explain paths disclose their
arithmetic here so a caller can audit the ratio, not just receive it (3B.3).
- return.diagnostics.engine?: string; default: not declared — Pricing/solver engine name, e.g. `black-scholes-merton`.
- return.diagnostics.failedCount: number; default: not declared
- return.diagnostics.finiteDifferenceBumps?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Finite-difference engines: the ACTUAL bump sizes used for FD Greeks (spec P2.3) — adaptive
near the vol/time boundaries, so the caller can see exactly what was differenced.
Keys: `spotStep`, `volatilityStep`, `timeStepYears`, `rateStep`, and — extended Greeks only —
`dividendYieldStep`. Each is the actual step differenced, in the unit of the coordinate it
bumps. (This doc named the retired `hS`/`hSig`/`hT`/`hR`/`hQ` keys for one release after the
emit sites had moved to the semantic names, so a caller following it read `undefined`.)
- return.diagnostics.iterations?: number; default: not declared — Iteration count for iterative methods.
Total solver iterations across the sweep.
- return.diagnostics.maximumReturnBounded: boolean | null; default: not declared — `true` when finite, `false` when unbounded, `null` when the proof is undetermined.
- return.diagnostics.method?: string; default: not declared — Numerical method, e.g. `closed-form`, `brent`, `finite-difference`.
- return.diagnostics.monotone: boolean; default: not declared — Volatility is non-decreasing with expected return across the solved points.
- return.diagnostics.selection?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing').SelectionReport; default: not declared — The structured engine-selection report (Gate C, `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing`): who was selected,
why, and — for automatic selection — every candidate considered with its verdict. This is the
machine-readable superset of `engine` + `autoReason` (which remain for compatibility);
`selected.name` always agrees with `engine` when both are present.
- return.diagnostics.solvedCount: number; default: not declared
- return.diagnostics.timingMs?: number; default: not declared — Wall-clock timing in milliseconds, when measured.
- return.diagnostics.warmup?: number; default: not declared — Series facades: number of leading output slots that are warmup sentinels (null/NaN) while the
computation seeds. Equals the input length when the indicator never emitted.
- return.diagnostics.warnings: QuantWarning[]; default: not declared — Structured warnings; always present (possibly empty).
- return.value: EfficientFrontierValue; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk#estimateExpectedReturns

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Estimate per-asset expected returns under an EXPLICIT method — the `mean` for `maxSharpe`,
`meanVariance`, `kelly`, and `efficientFrontier`.

```ts
estimateExpectedReturns({ method: 'historical-mean', returns, periodsPerYear: 252 });
estimateExpectedReturns({ method: 'exponentially-weighted', returns, halfLifePeriods: 60 });
estimateExpectedReturns({
  method: 'capital-asset-pricing',
  betas: [0.8, 1.2],
  annualRiskFreeRate: 0.04,
  annualMarketRiskPremium: 0.05,
});
estimateExpectedReturns({ method: 'supplied', expectedReturns: [0.08, 0.1], annualized: true });
```

`value.annualized` always states the unit of the result; the sample methods report per-period
means unless `periodsPerYear` is given, the capital-asset-pricing method is annual by
construction, and the supplied method carries the caller's own flag.

```typescript
export declare function estimateExpectedReturns(input: EstimateExpectedReturnsInput): ExpectedReturnsResult;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (input): EstimateExpectedReturnsInput; default: not declared
- (input).annualMarketRiskPremium: number; default: not declared — Annual market risk premium (decimal) — the premium itself, not the market return.
- (input).annualRiskFreeRate: number; default: not declared — Annual risk-free rate (decimal).
- (input).annualized: boolean; default: not declared — Whether the supplied values are annual (`true`) or per-period (`false`). Required.
- (input).asOf?: string | number; default: not declared — Point-in-time cut: every row whose timestamp is AFTER this instant is excluded from the
estimate and the excluded count is disclosed in `diagnostics.excludedAfterAsOf`. Without
`observationTimestamps` nothing can be screened — the result then carries a warning.
- (input).assetIds?: string[]; default: not declared — Optional asset labels aligned to the columns; echoed on the result.
Optional asset labels aligned to `betas`; echoed on the result.
Optional asset labels aligned to `expectedReturns`; echoed on the result.
- (input).betas: number[]; default: not declared — Per-asset market betas (one per asset).
- (input).expectedReturns: number[]; default: not declared — Caller-supplied expected returns, one per asset.
- (input).halfLifePeriods: number; default: not declared — Half-life of the observation weights in PERIODS: observation `t` of `T` carries weight
`0.5^((T − 1 − t) / halfLifePeriods)` before normalization, so the most recent row is the
heaviest. Required — there is no universal decay rate.
- (input).method: ('capital-asset-pricing') | ('exponentially-weighted') | ('historical-mean') | ('supplied'); default: not declared
- (input).observationTimestamps?: (string | number)[]; default: not declared — Optional observation instants aligned 1:1 with the rows of `returns` (epoch milliseconds or
an ISO date / zoned datetime), non-decreasing. Required for `asOf` to screen anything.
- (input).periodsPerYear?: number; default: not declared — Annualize by this factor (e.g. `252` for daily, `12` for monthly data): the reported means
become `periodMean × periodsPerYear`. OMITTED means per-period means with `annualized: false`
— annualization is never silent.
- (input).returns: number[][]; default: not declared — Observations-major returns — the same orientation as `CovarianceInput`: `returns[t][k]` is
asset `k`'s simple return in period `t` (one row per period, one column per asset).
- return.assumptions: { annualMarketRiskPremium?: number; annualRiskFreeRate?: number; asOf?: EpochMs; conventionsVersion: string; estimationConvention: string; halfLifePeriods?: number; method: ExpectedReturnsMethod; periodsPerYear?: number; }; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.annualMarketRiskPremium?: number; default: not declared — Echoed for `'capital-asset-pricing'`.
- return.assumptions.annualRiskFreeRate?: number; default: not declared — Echoed for `'capital-asset-pricing'`.
- return.assumptions.asOf?: number; default: not declared — The resolved point-in-time cut (epoch milliseconds), when `asOf` was given.
- return.assumptions.conventionsVersion: string; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.estimationConvention: string; default: not declared — Prose statement of exactly how the numbers were produced.
- return.assumptions.halfLifePeriods?: number; default: not declared — Echoed for `'exponentially-weighted'`.
- return.assumptions.method: 'supplied' | 'capital-asset-pricing' | 'historical-mean' | 'exponentially-weighted'; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.periodsPerYear?: number; default: not declared — Echoed when annualization was requested (sample methods only).
- return.diagnostics: Diagnostics & { effectiveSampleSize?: number; excludedAfterAsOf?: number; sampleSize: number; }; default: not declared
- return.diagnostics.autoReason?: string; default: not declared — When a meta-engine (e.g. `engines.auto()`) selected a delegate, this is a one-sentence,
human-readable explanation of WHY that delegate was chosen (`engine` then names the delegate).
Absent when no auto-selection took place.
- return.diagnostics.converged?: boolean; default: not declared — Whether an iterative procedure converged. `false` means the value is not trustworthy.
- return.diagnostics.decomposition?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Named intermediate quantities the value decomposes into — a par spread's protection leg and
risky annuity, a forward variance's near/far legs. The H-series explain paths disclose their

- return.diagnostics.effectiveSampleSize?: number; default: not declared — `(Σw)² / Σw²` of the observation weights (`'exponentially-weighted'` only).
- return.diagnostics.engine?: string; default: not declared — Pricing/solver engine name, e.g. `black-scholes-merton`.
- return.diagnostics.excludedAfterAsOf?: number; default: not declared — Rows excluded because their timestamp is after `asOf` (when both were supplied).
- return.diagnostics.finiteDifferenceBumps?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Finite-difference engines: the ACTUAL bump sizes used for FD Greeks (spec P2.3) — adaptive

emit sites had moved to the semantic names, so a caller following it read `undefined`.)
- return.diagnostics.iterations?: number; default: not declared — Iteration count for iterative methods.
- return.diagnostics.method?: string; default: not declared — Numerical method, e.g. `closed-form`, `brent`, `finite-difference`.
- return.diagnostics.sampleSize: number; default: not declared — Return observations consumed (after point-in-time screening); 0 for methods without a sample.
- return.diagnostics.selection?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing').SelectionReport; default: not declared — The structured engine-selection report (Gate C, `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing`): who was selected,
why, and — for automatic selection — every candidate considered with its verdict. This is the
machine-readable superset of `engine` + `autoReason` (which remain for compatibility);
`selected.name` always agrees with `engine` when both are present.
- return.diagnostics.timingMs?: number; default: not declared — Wall-clock timing in milliseconds, when measured.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk#extremeValueTailRisk

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Extreme-tail VaR and Expected Shortfall via the MonteCarloNeil–Frey peaks-over-threshold method, shown beside
the empirical and normal numbers with a fat-tail ratio. When the confidence sits outside the fitted
tail (`1 − p ≥ Nu/n`) EVT cannot extrapolate, so the empirical quantile is reported with a warning
instead of a fabricated EVT number. See `docs/specs/evt-tail-risk.md`.

```typescript
export declare function extremeValueTailRisk(returns: ArrayLike<number>, options?: { confidence?: number; } & GeneralizedParetoFitOptions): ExtremeValueTailRisk;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (options)?: { confidence?: number; } & GeneralizedParetoFitOptions; default: not declared
- (options).confidence?: number; default: not declared
- (options).method?: 'pwm' | 'mle'; default: not declared — Estimator; default `'pwm'` (closed-form, robust).
- (options).minExceedances?: number; default: not declared — Exceedance count below which the fit is warned as unreliable; default 10.
- (options).tailFraction?: number; default: not declared — Worst fraction of losses used as exceedances; default 0.10. Ignored when `threshold` is set.
- (options).threshold?: number; default: not declared — Explicit loss threshold `u` (overrides `tailFraction`).
- (returns): ArrayLike<number>; default: not declared
- return.assumptions: { confidence: number; conventionsVersion: string; }; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.confidence: number; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.conventionsVersion: string; default: not declared
- return.conditionalValueAtRisk: number; default: not declared — EVT Expected Shortfall (`≥ var`; `Infinity` when `ξ ≥ 1`).
- return.confidence: number; default: not declared
- return.diagnostics: Diagnostics; default: not declared
- return.empirical: { conditionalValueAtRisk: number; valueAtRisk: number; }; default: not declared — The empirical (historical) VaR/ES at the same confidence, for comparison.
- return.empirical.conditionalValueAtRisk: number; default: not declared
- return.empirical.valueAtRisk: number; default: not declared
- return.fit: GeneralizedParetoFit; default: not declared — The underlying GPD fit.
- return.normal: { conditionalValueAtRisk: number; valueAtRisk: number; }; default: not declared — The normal (Gaussian) VaR/ES at the same confidence, for comparison.
- return.normal.conditionalValueAtRisk: number; default: not declared
- return.normal.valueAtRisk: number; default: not declared
- return.tailFatnessRatio: number; default: not declared — `evt.var / normal.var` — how much fatter the tail is than the Gaussian says.
- return.valueAtRisk: number; default: not declared — EVT VaR — a positive loss magnitude.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk#kellyBet

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Size a single bet by the Kelly criterion — compute the growth-optimal fraction from the edge, then
scale it down sanely (half-Kelly by default, a drawdown budget, a hard cap) with the growth, the
drawdown risk, and the fat-tail correction all disclosed. See `docs/specs/kelly-sizing.md`.

```typescript
export declare function kellyBet(input: KellyBetInput): KellySizing;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (input): KellyBetInput; default: not declared
- (input).drawdownLimit?: { maxProbability: number; toFraction: number; }; default: not declared — Cap the applied Kelly multiple so `P(ever falling to toFraction of starting bankroll) ≤ maxProbability`.
- (input).drawdownLimit.maxProbability: number; default: not declared
- (input).drawdownLimit.toFraction: number; default: not declared
- (input).edge: { binary: BinaryEdge; } | { outcomes: EdgeOutcome[]; } | { gaussian: { mean: number; variance: number; }; } | { returns: ArrayLike<number>; }; default: not declared
- (input).edge.binary: BinaryEdge; default: not declared
- (input).edge.gaussian: { mean: number; variance: number; }; default: not declared
- (input).edge.gaussian.mean: number; default: not declared
- (input).edge.gaussian.variance: number; default: not declared
- (input).edge.outcomes: EdgeOutcome[]; default: not declared
- (input).edge.returns: ArrayLike<number>; default: not declared
- (input).fraction?: number; default: not declared — Fraction of full Kelly to apply (0.5 = half-Kelly). Default 0.5. Must be > 0.
- (input).horizonPeriods?: number; default: not declared — Optional horizonPeriods (periods) for the growth projection. Must be > 0 when given.
- (input).maxFraction?: number; default: not declared — Hard cap on the recommended fraction of bankroll (e.g. 1 = no leverage). Must be > 0.
- return.appliedFraction: number | null; default: not declared — `κ = recommendedFraction / fullKelly` — the applied Kelly multiple (0 when there's no edge);
`null` when `fullKelly` is null (undefined against a non-existent optimum).
- return.assumptions: { conventionsVersion: string; drawdownModel: 'continuous-gbm'; edgeType: 'binary' | 'outcomes' | 'gaussian' | 'returns'; fraction: number; }; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.conventionsVersion: string; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.drawdownModel: 'continuous-gbm'; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.edgeType: 'returns' | 'gaussian' | 'binary' | 'outcomes'; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.fraction: number; default: not declared
- return.bindingConstraint: 'fraction' | 'drawdown-limit' | 'max-fraction' | 'no-edge' | 'no-downside'; default: not declared — Which cap set the recommended fraction (`no-downside` = unbounded edge with no cap supplied).
- return.diagnostics: Diagnostics; default: not declared
- return.drawdownRisk: { probability: number; toFraction: number; }; default: not declared — `P(wealth ever falls to toFraction of the starting bankroll)` at the recommended fraction (continuous model).
- return.drawdownRisk.probability: number; default: not declared
- return.drawdownRisk.toFraction: number; default: not declared
- return.fullKelly: number | null; default: not declared — `f*` — the growth-optimal fraction of bankroll. `null` when the edge has **no downside**, so
log-growth increases without bound and there is no finite unconstrained optimum (finite-success
law — never `Infinity`; a `risk.kelly_unbounded` diagnostic explains it).
- return.gaussianKelly?: number; default: not declared — Returns path only: the Gaussian `μ/σ²` estimate, for comparison with the exact empirical `f*`.
- return.growthRate: number | null; default: not declared — Expected per-period log-growth at the recommended fraction; `null` when there is none.
- return.growthRateFull: number | null; default: not declared — Expected per-period log-growth at full Kelly (the maximum); `null` for a no-downside edge.
- return.horizonGrowth?: { growthMultiple: number; horizonPeriods: number; logGrowth: number; }; default: not declared — Present when `horizonPeriods` is given: the median wealth projection over the horizonPeriods.
- return.horizonGrowth.growthMultiple: number; default: not declared
- return.horizonGrowth.horizonPeriods: number; default: not declared
- return.horizonGrowth.logGrowth: number; default: not declared
- return.periodsToDouble: number | null; default: not declared — `ln 2 / growthRate` — periods to double at the recommended fraction (`Infinity` when growth ≤ 0,
`null` when there is no finite recommendation).
- return.rationale: string; default: not declared — Prose an agent relays.
- return.recommendedFraction: number | null; default: not declared — The recommended fraction after the fractional/drawdown/max caps (≥ 0). `null` only for a
no-downside edge with **no** explicit cap — a finite recommendation then requires a `maxFraction`.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk#linkAttribution

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Link single-period Brinson attributions across time with **Cariño's** logarithmic coefficients, so the
cumulative allocation / selection / interaction sum **exactly** to the compounded (geometric) active
return — the property the naive arithmetic sum lacks. Each period's effects are scaled by `βₜ = kₜ/k`;
per-segment effects are linked with the same `βₜ`. See `docs/specs/attribution-linking.md`.

```typescript
export declare function linkAttribution(periods: AttributionPeriod[], options?: LinkAttributionOptions): LinkedAttribution;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (periods): AttributionPeriod[]; default: not declared
- return.activeReturn: number; default: not declared — `portfolioReturn − benchmarkReturn` (the geometric active return).
- return.allocation: number; default: not declared — Linked cumulative effects — `allocation + selection + interaction = activeReturn`, exact.
- return.assumptions: { conventionsVersion: string; method: LinkMethod; periods: number; }; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.conventionsVersion: string; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.method: 'carino'; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.periods: number; default: not declared
- return.benchmarkReturn: number; default: not declared — Compounded benchmark return `∏(1+Bₜ) − 1`.
- return.diagnostics: Diagnostics; default: not declared
- return.interaction: number; default: not declared
- return.linkingCoefficients: LinkingCoefficient[]; default: not declared — The per-period linking coefficient `βₜ` (with the period `label` when supplied).
- return.method: 'carino'; default: not declared
- return.portfolioReturn: number; default: not declared — Compounded portfolio return `∏(1+Pₜ) − 1`.
- return.segments?: SegmentEffect[]; default: not declared — Linked per-segment effects — present only when every period supplied segments.
- return.selection: number; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk#meanExcessPlot

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

The **mean-excess plot** — the standard tool for choosing the EVT peaks-over-threshold cutoff the rest of
the pack takes as an input. The mean-excess `e(u) = E[X − u | X > u]` is linear in `u` (slope `ξ/(1−ξ)`)
above the true tail threshold and non-linear below it, so the threshold is read off as where the curve
straightens. Returns the curve, a heuristic `suggestedThreshold`, the `tailIndexEstimate` from that
region's slope, and the `suggestedTailFraction` to hand to {@link fitGeneralizedParetoTail}. See
`docs/specs/mean-excess-plot.md`.

```typescript
export declare function meanExcessPlot(returns: ArrayLike<number>, options?: MeanExcessPlotOptions): MeanExcessPlot;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (options)?: MeanExcessPlotOptions; default: not declared
- (options).gridSize?: number; default: not declared — Auto-grid point count. Default 25.
- (options).linearTolerance?: number; default: not declared — Normalized deviation below which the mean-excess counts as linear. Default 0.1.
- (options).minExceedances?: number; default: not declared — Minimum exceedances the top threshold retains (and the fit-reliability floor). Default 10.
- (options).startQuantile?: number; default: not declared — Auto-grid lower bound as a loss quantile in (0, 1). Default 0.5 (the median loss).
- (options).thresholds?: number[]; default: not declared — Explicit candidate thresholds (loss units); else an auto grid.
- (returns): ArrayLike<number>; default: not declared
- return.assumptions: { conventionsVersion: string; losses: number; observations: number; }; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.conventionsVersion: string; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.losses: number; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.observations: number; default: not declared
- return.diagnostics: Diagnostics; default: not declared
- return.points: MeanExcessPoint[]; default: not declared
- return.suggestedTailFraction: number; default: not declared — `Nu(suggestedThreshold)/n` — hand to `fitGeneralizedParetoTail({ tailFraction })`.
- return.suggestedThreshold: number; default: not declared — Heuristic tail-onset threshold — the lowest `u` above which `e(·)` is ~linear.
- return.tailIndexEstimate: number; default: not declared — `ξ` from the slope over `[suggestedThreshold, uₘₐₓ]`: `ξ = slope/(1+slope)`.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk#optionsMargin

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Initial margin / buying-power for a single-underlying, single-expiry multi-leg option position
(spec §15.3, product review §6). The expiration payoff is piecewise-linear, so the requirement is:

 - **long only** (all legs bought): the net debit paid (fully-paid, no additional margin);
 - **covered defined risk** (every short leg is offset — verticals, condors, butterflies): the
   max loss;
 - **uncovered short puts** (more short put contracts than long ones): the Reg-T naked-put
   requirement on the uncovered contracts + the max loss of the rest. A short put's loss is
   *bounded* (the underlying stops at 0), but bounded is not the same as covered: charging the
   whole `(strike − premium)` exercise value margins a margin account as if it were
   cash-secured, ~4× the Reg-T requirement one function away (`nakedPutMargin`). Opt into the
   cash-secured basis for a cash/IRA account with `putMarginBasis: 'cash-secured'`;
 - **undefined risk** (a net-short call leaves the upside unbounded): the Reg-T naked requirement
   summed over the short legs — a conservative strategy-based approximation (a portfolio-margin
   engine would net offsets more finely).

Coverage is counted contract-for-contract per option type, pairing the highest strikes first, so
a 1×1 spread is covered and the extra short in a 2×1 ratio is not. `maxLoss` is unaffected by the
margin basis — it stays the position's true worst case at expiration.

Pure and clock-free; premiums, strikes, and the underlier are explicit inputs.

```typescript
export declare function optionsMargin(legs: readonly OptionMarginLeg[], options: OptionsMarginOptions): OptionsMarginResult;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (legs): readonly OptionMarginLeg[]; default: not declared
- (options): OptionsMarginOptions; default: not declared
- (options).equityRate?: number; default: not declared — Reg-T naked "equity" rate — the % of underlying (default 0.20).
- (options).floorRate?: number; default: not declared — Reg-T naked floor rate — the % of underlying (calls) / strike (puts) minimum (default 0.10).
- (options).multiplier?: number; default: not declared — Contract multiplier (default 100).
- (options).putMarginBasis?: PutMarginBasis; default: not declared — Basis for UNCOVERED short puts. Default `'reg-t-naked'` — a margin account's actual
requirement. Use `'cash-secured'` for a cash/IRA account, where the whole exercise value must
be posted. Echoed in `assumptions.putMarginBasis`.
- (options).spot: number; default: not declared — Current price of the underlying (> 0).
- return.assumptions: { [k: string]: unknown; conventionsVersion: string; }; default: not declared — Applied conventions, echoed (Law 2 report grammar).
- return.assumptions.conventionsVersion: string; default: not declared
- return.buyingPowerReduction: number; default: not declared — Buying-power reduction — what the account must set aside. Equals `initialMargin` for margin
accounts; for a long-only (fully-paid) position it is the net debit paid.
- return.definedRisk: boolean; default: not declared — True when the position's loss is capped (spreads / condors / butterflies / long options).
- return.diagnostics: { warnings: QuantWarning[]; }; default: not declared — Structured warnings; always present (possibly empty).
- return.diagnostics.warnings: QuantWarning[]; default: not declared
- return.initialMargin: number; default: not declared — Initial margin / buying-power requirement, in account currency.
- return.maxLoss: number | null; default: not declared — Worst-case expiration loss magnitude per contract; `null` when the loss is unbounded (e.g. a
naked call — no finite worst case exists; `Infinity` is not JSON-safe, Law 7). `definedRisk:
false` is the primary unbounded discriminant, and a `risk.unbounded_loss` warning explains the
null.
- return.method: 'reg-t-naked' | 'defined-risk-max-loss' | 'reg-t-naked-put' | 'long-premium'; default: not declared — How the requirement was derived. `'reg-t-naked-put'` is the bounded-but-uncovered case: the
loss IS capped (a put's underlying stops at 0), but the position is short naked puts, so the
requirement is the Reg-T naked-put charge on the uncovered contracts plus the capped max loss
of whatever remains — not the cash-secured exercise value.
- return.netDebit: number; default: not declared — Net debit paid (> 0) or credit received (< 0), per contract.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk#probabilityOfBacktestOverfitting

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

**Probability of backtest overfitting** (Bailey & López de Prado's CSCV). Given a `T × N` matrix of
per-period returns — `T` time observations (rows) × `N` strategy configurations you selected among
(columns) — split the rows into `S` blocks, and over **every** `C(S, S/2)` symmetric partition into an
in-sample and an out-of-sample half: pick the IS-best configuration, then measure its OOS rank. PBO is
the fraction of splits where the IS winner lands **below the OOS median** — the probability that
picking the best backtest buys you a below-average live result. `≈ 0.5` means the selection is worthless
out of sample; `≈ 0` means a genuinely persistent edge. Depends only on `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core`/`math`.

```typescript
export declare function probabilityOfBacktestOverfitting(returns: number[][], options?: BacktestOverfittingProbabilityOptions): BacktestOverfittingProbabilityResult;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (options)?: BacktestOverfittingProbabilityOptions; default: not declared
- (options).splits?: number; default: not declared — Number of disjoint contiguous row-blocks `S` (even, `4 ≤ S ≤ 16`). Default `16` (Bailey & López de
Prado). The `C(S, S/2)` train/test splits grow fast in `S`; the observation count is trimmed to a
multiple of `S` (the oldest rows dropped).
- (returns): number[][]; default: not declared
- return.assumptions: { [k: string]: unknown; conventionsVersion: string; }; default: not declared — Applied conventions, echoed (Law 2 report grammar).
- return.assumptions.conventionsVersion: string; default: not declared
- return.backtestOverfittingProbability: number; default: not declared — Probability of backtest overfitting: the fraction of the `C(S, S/2)` symmetric train/test splits on
which the in-sample-best configuration ranks **below the out-of-sample median** (logit `λ < 0`). Near
`0.5` for noise (selection is worthless out of sample), near `0` for a genuinely persistent edge.
- return.combinations: number; default: not declared — Number of symmetric train/test splits evaluated: `C(S, S/2)`.
- return.diagnostics: { warnings: QuantWarning[]; }; default: not declared — Structured warnings; always present (possibly empty).
- return.diagnostics.warnings: QuantWarning[]; default: not declared
- return.medianLogit: number; default: not declared — Median logit `λ = ln(r̄/(1−r̄))` across the splits (`r̄` = OOS relative rank of the IS-best); `< 0` ⇒ overfit-leaning.
- return.observations: number; default: not declared — Observations (rows) used after trimming to a multiple of `S`.
- return.splits: number; default: not declared — Blocks `S` actually used.
- return.trials: number; default: not declared — Number of strategy configurations (columns) `N`.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk#purgedKFold

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Purged & embargoed K-fold cross-validation (López de Prado, *Advances in Financial ML* ch. 7).
Each fold's test set is a contiguous block; training drops any observation within `purgeGap` of the
test block (label-overlap purge) and within the trailing `embargo·n` window after it.

Throws a typed `input.out_of_range` naming the largest viable `purgeGap` when the requested purge
(with the embargo) would leave a fold with an empty training set — an unusable split is an error,
not an empty array to be discovered downstream.

```typescript
export declare function purgedKFold(observationCount: number, options: PurgedKFoldOptions): Split[];
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (observationCount): number; default: not declared
- (options): PurgedKFoldOptions; default: not declared
- (options).embargo?: number; default: not declared — Fraction of `n` to embargo after each test fold (default 0).
- (options).folds: number; default: not declared — Number of folds (≥ 2).
- (options).purgeGap?: number; default: not declared — Observations to purge on each side of a test fold (label-overlap buffer; default 0).

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk#shrunkKelly

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Estimation-error-shrunk portfolio Kelly. The plug-in weights `Σ̂⁻¹μ̂` overbet because `μ̂`/`Σ̂` are
estimated from a finite sample; this scales them by the growth-optimal factor
`c* = max(0, 1 − (n/T)/θ̂²)` (`θ̂² = μ̂ᵀΣ̂⁻¹μ̂`), returns a zero book when the estimated edge is
indistinguishable from sampling noise (`n/T ≥ θ̂²`), and discloses the biased-vs-corrected Sharpe and
the naive book's (often negative) expected out-of-sample growth. See `docs/specs/shrunk-kelly.md`.

```typescript
export declare function shrunkKelly(input: ShrunkKellyInput): ShrunkKelly;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (input): ShrunkKellyInput; default: not declared
- (input).covariance: number[][]; default: not declared — Estimated covariance Σ̂ (n×n, symmetric positive-definite).
- (input).fraction?: number; default: not declared — Extra fractional-Kelly multiplier applied on top of the estimation shrinkage (e.g. 0.5). Default 1.
- (input).mean: number[]; default: not declared — Estimated per-period expected (excess) returns μ̂, one per asset.
- (input).sampleSize: number; default: not declared — Number of observations T the estimates came from. Must be > 0.
- return.appliedScaling: number; default: not declared — The applied scaling `fraction · c*`.
- return.assumptions: { assets: number; conventionsVersion: string; fraction: number; sampleSize: number; }; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.assets: number; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.conventionsVersion: string; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.fraction: number; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.sampleSize: number; default: not declared
- return.correctedSharpeSquared: number; default: not declared — Bias-corrected out-of-sample squared Sharpe `θ̂² − n/T` (may be ≤ 0).
- return.diagnostics: Diagnostics; default: not declared
- return.expectedGrowth: number; default: not declared — Expected out-of-sample log-growth at the applied scaling.
- return.inSampleSharpeSquared: number; default: not declared — In-sample squared Sharpe `θ̂² = μ̂ᵀΣ̂⁻¹μ̂` (biased high).
- return.naiveExpectedGrowth: number; default: not declared — Expected out-of-sample log-growth of the naive (unshrunk) book — often negative.
- return.naiveWeights: number[]; default: not declared — Naive plug-in Kelly weights `Σ̂⁻¹μ̂` (before any shrinkage).
- return.shrinkage: number; default: not declared — Estimation-error shrinkage factor `c* ∈ [0, 1]`.
- return.weights: number[]; default: not declared — Shrunk Kelly weights `fraction · c* · Σ̂⁻¹μ̂`.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk#spectralRisk

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

A coherent spectral risk measure (Acerbi): a weighted average of the loss quantiles with a
non-decreasing weight on worse outcomes. Pass `{ riskAversion }` for the exponential spectrum
`φ(p) = k·e^(−k(1−p))/(1−e^(−k))` (default `k = 10`), or `{ alpha }` for the Expected-Shortfall
spectrum `φ(p) = 𝟙[p ≥ α]/(1−α)` — ES being the flat-tail special case. See the spec.

```typescript
export declare function spectralRisk(returns: ArrayLike<number>, options?: { riskAversion?: number; } | { alpha: number; }): SpectralRisk;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (options)?: { riskAversion?: number; } | { alpha: number; }; default: not declared
- (options).alpha: number; default: not declared
- (options).riskAversion?: number; default: not declared
- (returns): ArrayLike<number>; default: not declared
- return.alpha?: number; default: not declared — Level `α` for the Expected-Shortfall spectrum.
- return.assumptions: { conventionsVersion: string; }; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.conventionsVersion: string; default: not declared
- return.diagnostics: Diagnostics; default: not declared
- return.riskAversion?: number; default: not declared — Risk-aversion `k` for the exponential spectrum.
- return.spectrum: 'exponential' | 'expected-shortfall'; default: not declared
- return.value: number; default: not declared — The spectral risk measure — a positive loss magnitude.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk#taylorPnl

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Greeks-Taylor P&L of a single position's Greeks under a scenario (per unit).

```typescript
export declare function taylorPnl(greeks: PositionGreeks, scenario: Scenario): TaylorPnlResult;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (greeks): PositionGreeks; default: not declared
- (greeks).charm?: number; default: not declared — ∂Δ/∂T per year of time-to-expiry — the options package's `charm` (delta drift as expiry recedes). Optional.
- (greeks).color?: number; default: not declared — Accepted from a whole `ExtendedGreeks`; not used by the second-order expansion.
- (greeks).delta?: number; default: not declared — ∂V/∂S per $1 of spot.
- (greeks).deltaRate?: number; default: not declared — ∂²V/∂S∂r per $ per 1% rate — the spot-rate cross (`∂Δ/∂r`). Optional.
- (greeks).gamma?: number; default: not declared — ∂²V/∂S² per $1².
- (greeks).lambda?: number | null; default: not declared — Accepted from a whole `ExtendedGreeks` (`null` = elasticity undefined); not used by the expansion.
- (greeks).phi?: number; default: not declared — φ = ∂V/∂q per 1% dividend yield — the options package's `phi` (dividend rho). Optional.
- (greeks).rho?: number; default: not declared — ∂V/∂r per 1% rate (0.01), as the options package reports it.
- (greeks).rhoConvexity?: number; default: not declared — ∂²V/∂r² per (1%)² — rho convexity. Optional.
- (greeks).speed?: number; default: not declared — Accepted from a whole `ExtendedGreeks`; not used by the second-order expansion.
- (greeks).spot?: number; default: not declared — Reference spot, required to resolve percent spot shocks into price moves.
- (greeks).theta?: number; default: not declared — ∂V/∂t per CALENDAR DAY (negative for a long option), as the options package reports it.
- (greeks).thetaConvexity?: number; default: not declared — ∂²V/∂t² per calendar day² — theta convexity (theta's own bleed). Optional.
- (greeks).thetaRate?: number; default: not declared — ∂²V/∂t∂r per calendar day per 1% rate — the time-rate cross (`∂Θ/∂r`). Optional.
- (greeks).ultima?: number; default: not declared — Accepted from a whole `ExtendedGreeks`; not used by the second-order expansion.
- (greeks).value: number; default: not declared — Current mark value of the position (per unit).
- (greeks).vanna?: number; default: not declared — ∂²V/∂S∂σ per 1.00 σ per $ — the options package's `vanna`. Optional — omitted ⇒ its term is 0.
- (greeks).vega?: number; default: not declared — ∂V/∂σ per 1 volatility point (0.01), as the options package reports it.
- (greeks).vera?: number; default: not declared — ∂²V/∂σ∂r per 1.00 σ per 1.00 rate — the options package's `vera`. Optional.
- (greeks).veta?: number; default: not declared — ∂vega/∂T per year of time-to-expiry, vega per 1.00 σ — the options package's `veta`. Optional.
- (greeks).vomma?: number; default: not declared — ∂²V/∂σ² per 1.00 σ² — the options package's `vomma`. Optional.
- (greeks).zomma?: number; default: not declared — Accepted from a whole `ExtendedGreeks`; not used by the second-order expansion.
- (scenario): Scenario; default: not declared
- (scenario).name: string; default: not declared
- (scenario).shocks: Shock[]; default: not declared
- return.assumptions: { [k: string]: unknown; conventionsVersion: string; }; default: not declared — Applied conventions, echoed (Law 2 report grammar).
- return.assumptions.conventionsVersion: string; default: not declared
- return.charm: number; default: not declared — Second-order spot–time cross term: `charm·dS·dt` (0 when `charm` is absent).
- return.delta: number; default: not declared
- return.deltaRate: number; default: not declared — Second-order spot–rate cross term: `deltaRate·dS·dr` (0 when `deltaRate` is absent).
- return.diagnostics: { warnings: QuantWarning[]; }; default: not declared — Structured warnings; always present (possibly empty).
- return.diagnostics.warnings: QuantWarning[]; default: not declared
- return.gamma: number; default: not declared
- return.other: number; default: not declared — Residual = repriced − value − (the Greek terms); 0 for a pure Taylor reprice.
- return.phi: number; default: not declared — First-order dividend-carry term: `φ·dq` (0 when `phi` is absent).
- return.rho: number; default: not declared
- return.rhoConvexity: number; default: not declared — Second-order rate-convexity term: `½·rhoConvexity·dr²` (0 when `rhoConvexity` is absent).
- return.theta: number; default: not declared
- return.thetaConvexity: number; default: not declared — Second-order time-convexity term: `½·thetaConvexity·dt²` (0 when `thetaConvexity` is absent).
- return.thetaRate: number; default: not declared — Second-order time–rate cross term: `thetaRate·dt·dr` (0 when `thetaRate` is absent).
- return.total: number; default: not declared
- return.vanna: number; default: not declared — Second-order spot–vol cross term: `vanna·dS·dσ` (0 when `vanna` is absent).
- return.vega: number; default: not declared
- return.vera: number; default: not declared — Second-order vol–rate cross term: `vera·dσ·dr` (0 when `vera` is absent).
- return.veta: number; default: not declared — Second-order vol–time cross term: `veta·dσ·dt` (0 when `veta` is absent).
- return.vomma: number; default: not declared — Second-order vol-convexity term: `½·vomma·dσ²` (0 when `vomma` is absent).

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk#valueAtRiskReport

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Full VaR + CVaR report for a single return/P&L series.

```typescript
export declare function valueAtRiskReport(returns: ArrayLike<number>, options?: VaROptions): VaRResult;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (options)?: VaROptions; default: not declared
- (options).confidence?: number; default: not declared — Confidence level in (0, 1). Default 0.95.
- (options).cornishFisher?: boolean; default: not declared — Parametric only: Cornish-Fisher adjustment for skew/excess-kurtosis. Default false. Applied
only where the expansion is a monotone quantile map; outside that domain the plain Gaussian
quantile is reported with a `risk.cornish_fisher_out_of_domain` warning and
`cornishFisher: false`. Over a multi-period `horizonPeriods` the moments are rescaled to the
horizon under iid aggregation (`skew/√h`, `excessKurtosis/h`), disclosed as
`assumptions.momentScaling: 'iid'`. On a non-parametric method it is ignored with an info
warning, never silently.
- (options).horizonPeriods?: number; default: not declared — Holding-period horizonPeriods in periods; scales by √-time. Default 1.
- (options).method?: VaRMethod; default: not declared — Estimation method. Default `'historical'`.
  - `'historical'` — the empirical (hyndman-fan-7) tail quantile of the sample;
  - `'parametric'` — the Gaussian quantile of the fitted (μ, σ), optionally Cornish-Fisher;
  - `'monteCarlo'` — draws from the **fitted NORMAL** and takes its empirical tail. It captures
    no non-normality whatsoever (same two moments as `'parametric'`, plus sampling noise), so
    prefer `'parametric'` unless you specifically want sampling diagnostics; use
    `'historical'` or the EVT tools when the shape of the tail matters.
- (options).samples?: number; default: not declared — Monte-Carlo only: number of simulated paths. Default 10000.
- (options).seed?: number; default: not declared — Monte-Carlo only: PRNG seed for reproducibility. Default 1.
- (returns): ArrayLike<number>; default: not declared
- return.assumptions: { [k: string]: unknown; conventionsVersion: string; }; default: not declared — Applied conventions, echoed (Law 2 report grammar).
- return.assumptions.conventionsVersion: string; default: not declared
- return.conditionalValueAtRisk: number; default: not declared — Conditional VaR / expected shortfall (mean loss beyond VaR); ≥ `var`.
- return.confidence: number; default: not declared
- return.cornishFisher?: boolean; default: not declared — Whether the Cornish-Fisher adjustment was actually APPLIED to the VaR quantile (parametric
only). `false` when it was requested but its expansion was out of domain — the plain Gaussian
quantile was reported instead and a `risk.cornish_fisher_out_of_domain` warning says so.
- return.diagnostics: { warnings: QuantWarning[]; }; default: not declared — Structured warnings; always present (possibly empty). This is the ONE warnings channel: the
legacy top-level `warnings` twin was removed pre-1.0 (two arrays that had to be kept in sync is
a defect waiting to happen — a caller reading the stale one silently misses a disclosure).
- return.diagnostics.warnings: QuantWarning[]; default: not declared
- return.horizonPeriods: number; default: not declared
- return.method: VaRMethod; default: not declared
- return.samples?: number; default: not declared — Monte-Carlo only: the number of simulated samples actually drawn.
- return.seed?: number; default: not declared — Monte-Carlo only: the PRNG seed actually used (echoed for reproducibility).
- return.valueAtRisk: number; default: not declared — Positive loss magnitude at `confidence`.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk/optimize#EfficientFrontierConstraints

Kind: type; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Frontier constraints are the shared feasible-region grammar. Linear transaction costs are an
objective penalty, not a feasible-region constraint, and therefore belong in a direct
`meanVariance` solve rather than a gross mean-variance frontier.

```typescript
/**
 * Frontier constraints are the shared feasible-region grammar. Linear transaction costs are an
 * objective penalty, not a feasible-region constraint, and therefore belong in a direct
 * `meanVariance` solve rather than a gross mean-variance frontier.
 */
export type EfficientFrontierConstraints = Omit<OptimizeConstraints, 'transactionCosts'>;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- bounds?: [number, number][]; default: not declared — Per-asset `[lo, hi]` bounds.
- budget?: number; default: not declared — Sum-to budget (`Σw`). Default 1 (fully invested).
- groups?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk').GroupConstraint[]; default: not declared — Sector/group exposure caps (`min ≤ Σ_group w ≤ max`).
- longOnly?: boolean; default: not declared — Forbid short positions (`w ≥ 0`). Ignored where `bounds` is given.
- maximumIterations?: number; default: not declared — Projected-gradient iteration cap. Default 5000.
- tolerance?: number; default: not declared — Projected-gradient convergence tolerance on the weight step. Default 1e-11.
- turnover?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk').TurnoverConstraint; default: not declared — Turnover budget against a base portfolio (`Σ|w − previousWeights| ≤ max`).
- turnover.max: number; default: not declared — Maximum one-way + reverse (L1) turnover allowed.
- turnover.previousWeights: number[]; default: not declared — Current weights to measure turnover against.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk/portfolio#PutMarginBasis

Kind: type; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

How an UNCOVERED short put is margined:
  - `'reg-t-naked'` (default) — the Reg-T naked-put requirement, i.e. {@link nakedPutMargin};
  - `'cash-secured'` — the full expiration max loss `(strike − premium)·multiplier`, i.e. the
    cash a cash-secured seller must post. That is ~4× the Reg-T number and is what a
    retail-cash account (or an IRA) actually needs.

```typescript
/**
 * How an UNCOVERED short put is margined:
 *   - `'reg-t-naked'` (default) — the Reg-T naked-put requirement, i.e. {@link nakedPutMargin};
 *   - `'cash-secured'` — the full expiration max loss `(strike − premium)·multiplier`, i.e. the
 *     cash a cash-secured seller must post. That is ~4× the Reg-T number and is what a
 *     retail-cash account (or an IRA) actually needs.
 */
export type PutMarginBasis = 'reg-t-naked' | 'cash-secured';
```

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk/scenario#StressTestInput

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

```typescript
export interface StressTestInput<T> {
    positions: readonly Position<T>[];
    scenarios: readonly Scenario[];
    options?: StressOptions<T>;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- options?: StressOptions<T>; default: not declared
- options.reprice?: (position: Position<T>, scenario: Scenario) => number; default: not declared — Custom revaluation: return the position's **new value per unit** under the scenario. Falls back
to the Greeks-Taylor expansion when omitted.
- options.reprice(position): Position<T>; default: not declared
- options.reprice(position).data?: T; default: not declared
- options.reprice(position).greeks?: PositionGreeks; default: not declared
- options.reprice(position).id?: string; default: not declared
- options.reprice(position).multiplier?: number; default: not declared — Contract multiplier applied to per-unit value and Greeks (100 for a listed US equity option
whose Greeks are per share and whose `quantity` is in contracts). Default 1. Applied by
`aggregateGreeks`, `stressTest` and the book tools; disclosed in their assumptions.
- options.reprice(position).quantity?: number; default: not declared — Number of units held (signed). Default 1.
- options.reprice(position).value?: number; default: not declared — Current mark per unit — the BASE a custom `reprice` differences against (H11). When `reprice`
is supplied, either this or `greeks.value` must be present; the base is never assumed 0.
- options.reprice(scenario): Scenario; default: not declared
- options.reprice(scenario).name: string; default: not declared
- options.reprice(scenario).shocks: Shock[]; default: not declared
- positions: readonly Position<T>[]; default: not declared
- scenarios: readonly Scenario[]; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk/value-at-risk#ValueAtRiskAssumptionExtras

Kind: type; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Conventions a VaR-family explain envelope discloses.

```typescript
/** Conventions a VaR-family explain envelope discloses. */
export type ValueAtRiskAssumptionExtras = {
    confidence: number;
    method: VaRMethod;
    horizonPeriods: number;
    seed?: number;
    samples?: number;
    cornishFisher?: boolean;
    /** Historical only: the order-statistic interpolation rule (`hyndman-fan-7`, the R/NumPy default). */
    quantileEstimator?: string;
    /** Monte-Carlo only: the law actually simulated (`fitted-normal` — first two moments only). */
    distribution?: string;
    /** Cornish-Fisher over a multi-period horizon: how skew/kurtosis were scaled (`iid`). */
    momentScaling?: string;
};
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- confidence: number; default: not declared
- cornishFisher?: boolean; default: not declared
- distribution?: string; default: not declared — Monte-Carlo only: the law actually simulated (`fitted-normal` — first two moments only).
- horizonPeriods: number; default: not declared
- method: VaRMethod; default: not declared
- momentScaling?: string; default: not declared — Cornish-Fisher over a multi-period horizon: how skew/kurtosis were scaled (`iid`).
- quantileEstimator?: string; default: not declared — Historical only: the order-statistic interpolation rule (`hyndman-fan-7`, the R/NumPy default).
- samples?: number; default: not declared
- seed?: number; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/scenarios#FullRevaluationScenarioPortfolioBindingDescriptor

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Serializable full-revaluation durable-portfolio binding descriptor.

```typescript
/** Serializable full-revaluation durable-portfolio binding descriptor. */
export interface FullRevaluationScenarioPortfolioBindingDescriptor extends ScenarioPortfolioBindingDescriptorBase {
    readonly valuationMethod: 'full-revaluation';
    readonly instrumentDescriptor: unknown;
    readonly instrumentDescriptorHash: string;
    readonly pricer: ScenarioPricerDescriptor;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- accountId: string; default: not declared
- bindingDescriptorHash: string; default: not declared
- book?: string; default: not declared
- id: string; default: not declared
- instrumentDescriptor: unknown; default: not declared
- instrumentDescriptorHash: string; default: not declared
- instrumentId: string; default: not declared
- pricer: ScenarioPricerDescriptor; default: not declared
- pricer.capabilities: Readonly<PricerCapabilities>; default: not declared
- pricer.capabilities.batch: boolean; default: not declared — Whether `priceBatch` exists (one observation set, many instruments — the book fast path).
- pricer.capabilities.greeks: 'none' | 'analytic' | 'finite-difference' | 'delegated'; default: not declared — How Greeks are produced when `request.greeks` is set: closed-form (`analytic`), bump-and-
reprice (`finite-difference`), by whatever engine was selected (`delegated`), or not at all
(`none` — the request is not honored and no `greeks` field appears; never fabricated zeros).
- pricer.capabilities.randomness: 'none' | 'seeded'; default: not declared — Where the pricer's randomness lives — behaviorally verified, replacing the earlier
`deterministic: boolean` (pre-1.0 rename, 2026-08-23, second external review):

  - `'none'` — same instrument + observations + request → byte-identical COMPLETE results,
    and a supplied `request.seed` is IGNORED entirely (verified: identical results with and
    without one).
  - `'seeded'` — the pricer consumes randomness, but ONLY through the caller's
    `request.seed`: the seed is REQUIRED (its absence is a typed `input.missing_field`
    refusal naming `request.seed`), it is echoed at `assumptions.seed`, and two same-seed
    calls return byte-identical COMPLETE results. Batches obey the derivation law documented
    on {@link PricerValuationRequest.seed}: item `i` prices under `seed + i`.

There is deliberately NO free-running mode: a pricer whose results the kit cannot reproduce
under a fixed seed makes claims the kit cannot verify, and a claim the kit cannot verify is
marketing. Free-running randomness is non-conformant.
- pricer.name: string; default: not declared
- pricer.version: string; default: not declared
- strategy?: string; default: not declared
- tags: readonly string[]; default: not declared
- valuationMethod: 'full-revaluation'; default: not declared

- apply(input).target.pricer.capabilities: { readonly batch: boolean; readonly greeks: 'analytic' | 'finite-difference' | 'delegated' | 'none'; readonly randomness: 'none' | 'seeded'; }; default: not declared
- apply(input).target.pricer.capabilities.batch: boolean; default: not declared — Whether `priceBatch` exists (one observation set, many instruments — the book fast path).
- apply(input).target.pricer.capabilities.greeks: 'none' | 'analytic' | 'finite-difference' | 'delegated'; default: not declared — How Greeks are produced when `request.greeks` is set: closed-form (`analytic`), bump-and-
reprice (`finite-difference`), by whatever engine was selected (`delegated`), or not at all
(`none` — the request is not honored and no `greeks` field appears; never fabricated zeros).
- apply(input).target.pricer.capabilities.randomness: 'none' | 'seeded'; default: not declared — Where the pricer's randomness lives — behaviorally verified, replacing the earlier
`deterministic: boolean` (pre-1.0 rename, 2026-08-23, second external review):

  - `'none'` — same instrument + observations + request → byte-identical COMPLETE results,
    and a supplied `request.seed` is IGNORED entirely (verified: identical results with and
    without one).
  - `'seeded'` — the pricer consumes randomness, but ONLY through the caller's
    `request.seed`: the seed is REQUIRED (its absence is a typed `input.missing_field`
    refusal naming `request.seed`), it is echoed at `assumptions.seed`, and two same-seed
    calls return byte-identical COMPLETE results. Batches obey the derivation law documented
    on {@link PricerValuationRequest.seed}: item `i` prices under `seed + i`.

There is deliberately NO free-running mode: a pricer whose results the kit cannot reproduce
under a fixed seed makes claims the kit cannot verify, and a claim the kit cannot verify is
marketing. Free-running randomness is non-conformant.

- apply(input).target.strategy?: string; default: not declared

- target.pricer.capabilities: { readonly batch: boolean; readonly greeks: 'analytic' | 'finite-difference' | 'delegated' | 'none'; readonly randomness: 'none' | 'seeded'; }; default: not declared
- target.pricer.capabilities.batch: boolean; default: not declared — Whether `priceBatch` exists (one observation set, many instruments — the book fast path).
- target.pricer.capabilities.greeks: 'none' | 'analytic' | 'finite-difference' | 'delegated'; default: not declared — How Greeks are produced when `request.greeks` is set: closed-form (`analytic`), bump-and-
reprice (`finite-difference`), by whatever engine was selected (`delegated`), or not at all
(`none` — the request is not honored and no `greeks` field appears; never fabricated zeros).
- target.pricer.capabilities.randomness: 'none' | 'seeded'; default: not declared — Where the pricer's randomness lives — behaviorally verified, replacing the earlier
`deterministic: boolean` (pre-1.0 rename, 2026-08-23, second external review):

  - `'none'` — same instrument + observations + request → byte-identical COMPLETE results,
    and a supplied `request.seed` is IGNORED entirely (verified: identical results with and
    without one).
  - `'seeded'` — the pricer consumes randomness, but ONLY through the caller's
    `request.seed`: the seed is REQUIRED (its absence is a typed `input.missing_field`
    refusal naming `request.seed`), it is echoed at `assumptions.seed`, and two same-seed
    calls return byte-identical COMPLETE results. Batches obey the derivation law documented
    on {@link PricerValuationRequest.seed}: item `i` prices under `seed + i`.

There is deliberately NO free-running mode: a pricer whose results the kit cannot reproduce
under a fixed seed makes claims the kit cannot verify, and a claim the kit cannot verify is
marketing. Free-running randomness is non-conformant.

- resolve(input).target.pricer.capabilities.greeks: 'none' | 'analytic' | 'finite-difference' | 'delegated'; default: not declared — How Greeks are produced when `request.greeks` is set: closed-form (`analytic`), bump-and-
reprice (`finite-difference`), by whatever engine was selected (`delegated`), or not at all
(`none` — the request is not honored and no `greeks` field appears; never fabricated zeros).
- resolve(input).target.pricer.capabilities.randomness: 'none' | 'seeded'; default: not declared — Where the pricer's randomness lives — behaviorally verified, replacing the earlier
`deterministic: boolean` (pre-1.0 rename, 2026-08-23, second external review):

  - `'none'` — same instrument + observations + request → byte-identical COMPLETE results,
    and a supplied `request.seed` is IGNORED entirely (verified: identical results with and
    without one).
  - `'seeded'` — the pricer consumes randomness, but ONLY through the caller's
    `request.seed`: the seed is REQUIRED (its absence is a typed `input.missing_field`
    refusal naming `request.seed`), it is echoed at `assumptions.seed`, and two same-seed
    calls return byte-identical COMPLETE results. Batches obey the derivation law documented
    on {@link PricerValuationRequest.seed}: item `i` prices under `seed + i`.

There is deliberately NO free-running mode: a pricer whose results the kit cannot reproduce
under a fixed seed makes claims the kit cannot verify, and a claim the kit cannot verify is
marketing. Free-running randomness is non-conformant.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/scenarios#ScenarioPortfolioBindingDescriptor
