Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- accountId: string; default: not declared
- bindingDescriptorHash: string; default: not declared
- book?: string; default: not declared
- id: string; default: not declared
- instrumentDescriptor: unknown; default: not declared
- instrumentDescriptorHash: string; default: not declared
- instrumentId: string; default: not declared
- pricer: ScenarioPricerDescriptor; default: not declared
- pricer.capabilities: Readonly<PricerCapabilities>; default: not declared
- pricer.capabilities.batch: boolean; default: not declared — Whether `priceBatch` exists (one observation set, many instruments — the book fast path).
- pricer.capabilities.greeks: 'none' | 'analytic' | 'finite-difference' | 'delegated'; default: not declared — How Greeks are produced when `request.greeks` is set: closed-form (`analytic`), bump-and-
reprice (`finite-difference`), by whatever engine was selected (`delegated`), or not at all
(`none` — the request is not honored and no `greeks` field appears; never fabricated zeros).
- pricer.capabilities.randomness: 'none' | 'seeded'; default: not declared — Where the pricer's randomness lives — behaviorally verified, replacing the earlier
`deterministic: boolean` (pre-1.0 rename, 2026-08-23, second external review):

  - `'none'` — same instrument + observations + request → byte-identical COMPLETE results,
    and a supplied `request.seed` is IGNORED entirely (verified: identical results with and
    without one).
  - `'seeded'` — the pricer consumes randomness, but ONLY through the caller's
    `request.seed`: the seed is REQUIRED (its absence is a typed `input.missing_field`
    refusal naming `request.seed`), it is echoed at `assumptions.seed`, and two same-seed
    calls return byte-identical COMPLETE results. Batches obey the derivation law documented
    on {@link PricerValuationRequest.seed}: item `i` prices under `seed + i`.

There is deliberately NO free-running mode: a pricer whose results the kit cannot reproduce
under a fixed seed makes claims the kit cannot verify, and a claim the kit cannot verify is
marketing. Free-running randomness is non-conformant.

- pricer.version: string; default: not declared
- strategy?: string; default: not declared
- tags: readonly string[]; default: not declared
- taylor: { readonly baseValuePerUnit: number; readonly factors: TaylorFactors; readonly sensitivities: Readonly<TaylorSensitivities>; }; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/scenarios#ScenarioPricingResult

Detached Gate-C pricing result retained without discarding domain-specific fields.

```typescript
/** Detached Gate-C pricing result retained without discarding domain-specific fields. */
export type ScenarioPricingResult = Readonly<Record<string, unknown>> & {
    readonly value: number;
    readonly assumptions: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>;

    };

```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- assumptions: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>; default: not declared
- diagnostics: Readonly<Diagnostics> & { readonly warnings: readonly QuantWarning[]; }; default: not declared
- diagnostics.autoReason?: string; default: not declared — When a meta-engine (e.g. `engines.auto()`) selected a delegate, this is a one-sentence,
human-readable explanation of WHY that delegate was chosen (`engine` then names the delegate).
Absent when no auto-selection took place.
- diagnostics.converged?: boolean; default: not declared — Whether an iterative procedure converged. `false` means the value is not trustworthy.
- diagnostics.decomposition?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Named intermediate quantities the value decomposes into — a par spread's protection leg and
risky annuity, a forward variance's near/far legs. The H-series explain paths disclose their
arithmetic here so a caller can audit the ratio, not just receive it (3B.3).
- diagnostics.engine?: string; default: not declared — Pricing/solver engine name, e.g. `black-scholes-merton`.
- diagnostics.finiteDifferenceBumps?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Finite-difference engines: the ACTUAL bump sizes used for FD Greeks (spec P2.3) — adaptive
near the vol/time boundaries, so the caller can see exactly what was differenced.
Keys: `spotStep`, `volatilityStep`, `timeStepYears`, `rateStep`, and — extended Greeks only —
`dividendYieldStep`. Each is the actual step differenced, in the unit of the coordinate it
bumps. (This doc named the retired `hS`/`hSig`/`hT`/`hR`/`hQ` keys for one release after the
emit sites had moved to the semantic names, so a caller following it read `undefined`.)
- diagnostics.iterations?: number; default: not declared — Iteration count for iterative methods.
- diagnostics.method?: string; default: not declared — Numerical method, e.g. `closed-form`, `brent`, `finite-difference`.
- diagnostics.selection?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing').SelectionReport; default: not declared — The structured engine-selection report (Gate C, `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing`): who was selected,
why, and — for automatic selection — every candidate considered with its verdict. This is the
machine-readable superset of `engine` + `autoReason` (which remain for compatibility);
`selected.name` always agrees with `engine` when both are present.
- diagnostics.selection.candidates?: readonly import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing').SelectionCandidate[]; default: not declared — Candidates an automatic selection considered; absent for explicit mode.
- diagnostics.selection.mode: 'explicit' | 'automatic'; default: not declared
- diagnostics.selection.reason: string; default: not declared — Why the selected engine answers this request.
- diagnostics.selection.selected: { name: string; version?: string; }; default: not declared
- diagnostics.selection.selected.name: string; default: not declared
- diagnostics.selection.selected.version?: string; default: not declared
- diagnostics.timingMs?: number; default: not declared — Wall-clock timing in milliseconds, when measured.
- diagnostics.warmup?: number; default: not declared — Series facades: number of leading output slots that are warmup sentinels (null/NaN) while the
computation seeds. Equals the input length when the indicator never emitted.
- diagnostics.warnings: (QuantWarning[]) | (readonly QuantWarning[]); default: not declared — Structured warnings; always present (possibly empty).
- value: number; default: not declared

- pricer.capabilities.batch: boolean; default: not declared — Whether `priceBatch` exists (one observation set, many instruments — the book fast path).
- pricer.capabilities.greeks: 'none' | 'analytic' | 'finite-difference' | 'delegated'; default: not declared — How Greeks are produced when `request.greeks` is set: closed-form (`analytic`), bump-and-
reprice (`finite-difference`), by whatever engine was selected (`delegated`), or not at all
(`none` — the request is not honored and no `greeks` field appears; never fabricated zeros).
- pricer.capabilities.randomness: 'none' | 'seeded'; default: not declared — Where the pricer's randomness lives — behaviorally verified, replacing the earlier
`deterministic: boolean` (pre-1.0 rename, 2026-08-23, second external review):

  - `'none'` — same instrument + observations + request → byte-identical COMPLETE results,
    and a supplied `request.seed` is IGNORED entirely (verified: identical results with and
    without one).
  - `'seeded'` — the pricer consumes randomness, but ONLY through the caller's
    `request.seed`: the seed is REQUIRED (its absence is a typed `input.missing_field`
    refusal naming `request.seed`), it is echoed at `assumptions.seed`, and two same-seed
    calls return byte-identical COMPLETE results. Batches obey the derivation law documented
    on {@link PricerValuationRequest.seed}: item `i` prices under `seed + i`.

There is deliberately NO free-running mode: a pricer whose results the kit cannot reproduce
under a fixed seed makes claims the kit cannot verify, and a claim the kit cannot verify is
marketing. Free-running randomness is non-conformant.
- pricer.name: string; default: not declared
- pricer.version: string; default: not declared
- quantity: number; default: not declared
- strategy?: string; default: not declared
- tags: readonly string[]; default: not declared
- targetDescriptorHash: string; default: not declared
- taylor: { readonly baseValuePerUnit: number; readonly factors: TaylorFactors; readonly sensitivities: Readonly<TaylorSensitivities>; }; default: not declared
- taylor.baseValuePerUnit: number; default: not declared

Greeks for a Taylor target in TotalFinance's ONE unit system — the units `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/options` reports
(theta per calendar day, vega per volatility point, rho and phi per 1%, second-order terms in the
options package's conventions). See `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk`'s `PositionGreeks`; the Taylor engine converts
internally.

```typescript
/** Raw per-unit derivatives in the exact units consumed by `taylorPnl`. */
/**
 * Greeks for a Taylor target in TotalFinance's ONE unit system — the units `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/options` reports
 * (theta per calendar day, vega per volatility point, rho and phi per 1%, second-order terms in the
 * options package's conventions). See `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/risk`'s `PositionGreeks`; the Taylor engine converts
 * internally.
 */
export interface TaylorSensitivities {
    delta?: number;
    gamma?: number;
    vega?: number;
    theta?: number;
    rho?: number;
    vanna?: number;
    vomma?: number;
    charm?: number;
    veta?: number;
    vera?: number;
    deltaRate?: number;
    thetaRate?: number;
    rhoConvexity?: number;
    thetaConvexity?: number;
    /** φ = ∂V/∂q per 1% dividend yield (the options package's `phi`). */
    phi?: number;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- charm?: number; default: not declared
- delta?: number; default: not declared
- deltaRate?: number; default: not declared
- gamma?: number; default: not declared
- phi?: number; default: not declared — φ = ∂V/∂q per 1% dividend yield (the options package's `phi`).
- rho?: number; default: not declared
- rhoConvexity?: number; default: not declared
- theta?: number; default: not declared
- thetaConvexity?: number; default: not declared
- thetaRate?: number; default: not declared
- vanna?: number; default: not declared
- vega?: number; default: not declared
- vera?: number; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy#BuildStrategyInput

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Build a named strategy chosen at runtime: `buildStrategy({ name: 'ironCondor', input })` is exactly
`ironCondor(input)` with the name as data — for agents, UIs, and config-driven callers.
Unknown names throw a typed `input.invalid_enum` error carrying the full catalog (with a
did-you-mean hint when only the casing is off); `listStrategies()` documents every input shape.

```typescript
/**
 * Build a named strategy chosen at runtime: `buildStrategy({ name: 'ironCondor', input })` is exactly
 * `ironCondor(input)` with the name as data — for agents, UIs, and config-driven callers.
 * Unknown names throw a typed `input.invalid_enum` error carrying the full catalog (with a
 * did-you-mean hint when only the casing is off); `listStrategies()` documents every input shape.
 */
export interface BuildStrategyInput {
    /** The exact strategy name returned by {@link listStrategies}. */
    name: string;
    /** Builder-specific strategy fields; inspect the matching descriptor's `exampleInput`. */
    input: Record<string, unknown>;
    /** Optional position construction and model-premium configuration. */
    config?: PositionConfig;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- config?: PositionConfig; default: not declared — Optional position construction and model-premium configuration.
- config.expiry?: string; default: not declared — Position-level default expiry (`YYYY-MM-DD` → 16:00 ET, or a datetime) applied to every leg
that has no `expiry` of its own. Named builders route their input's `expiry` here. Precedence
per leg: `leg.expiry` > `expiry` > `market.expiry` (R4).
- config.market?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumMarket; default: not declared — Market for model-priced entry premiums (required when `premiums: 'model'` and any leg omits its
premium) — AND the position's remembered market (R5): `probability()`, `monteCarloProbability()`,
`value()`, `scenarioTable()`, and `chartData()` use it as their default market, with per-call
fields merged over it. Results echo `marketSource: 'construction' | 'call' | 'merged'`.
- config.market.asOf: string | number; default: not declared — Entry time (epoch ms or ISO). Each leg's entry `t = yearFraction(asOf, leg.expiry ?? market.expiry)`.
- config.market.dividendYield?: number; default: not declared
- config.market.expiry?: string; default: not declared — Default expiry for legs without their own `expiry` (single-expiry structures).
- config.market.riskFreeRate: number; default: not declared
- config.market.spot: number; default: not declared
- config.market.volatility: number; default: not declared — Entry implied volatility (annualized decimal) for unpriced legs that carry no `impliedVolatility`
of their own — a leg's own volatility always wins, exactly as it does when `value()` marks it.
- config.multiplier?: number; default: not declared — Contract multiplier for option legs (default 100).
- config.premiums?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumSource; default: not declared — Entry-premium source: `'user'` (from the leg inputs, default) or `'model'` (priced from `market`).
- input: Record<string, unknown>; default: not declared — Builder-specific strategy fields; inspect the matching descriptor's `exampleInput`.
- name: string; default: not declared — The exact strategy name returned by {@link listStrategies}.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy#CalendarInput

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

A calendar (horizontal) spread: same strike, short near leg + long far leg. Multi-expiry by
construction, so there is deliberately NO single `expiry` field — the per-side
`nearExpiry`/`farExpiry` are the only spelling (a bare `expiry` throws a teaching error).

```typescript
/**
 * A calendar (horizontal) spread: same strike, short near leg + long far leg. Multi-expiry by
 * construction, so there is deliberately NO single `expiry` field — the per-side
 * `nearExpiry`/`farExpiry` are the only spelling (a bare `expiry` throws a teaching error).
 */
export interface CalendarInput extends Omit<UnitInput, 'expiry'> {
    strike: number;
    /** Near expiry of the short leg (`YYYY-MM-DD` → 16:00 ET, or a datetime). */
    nearExpiry: string;
    /** Premium received on the short near leg. */
    shortPremium?: number;
    /** Far expiry of the long leg. */
    farExpiry: string;
    /** Premium paid on the long far leg. */
    longPremium?: number;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- farExpiry: string; default: not declared — Far expiry of the long leg.
- longPremium?: number; default: not declared — Premium paid on the long far leg.
- nearExpiry: string; default: not declared — Near expiry of the short leg (`YYYY-MM-DD` → 16:00 ET, or a datetime).
- quantity?: number; default: not declared — Number of structures (default 1). Every leg scales by this.
- shortPremium?: number; default: not declared — Premium received on the short near leg.
- strike: number; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy#ExplainPositionOptions

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Options for {@link explainPosition}.

```typescript
/** Options for {@link explainPosition}. */
export interface ExplainPositionOptions {
    /** Market for probability + greeks (spot/vol/rate/asOf); merges over the position's own market. */
    market?: Partial<MarkToMarketInput>;
    /** Underlying name for the prose (e.g. `'AAPL'`); default `'the underlying'`. */
    underlyingLabel?: string;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- market?: Partial<MarkToMarketInput>; default: not declared — Market for probability + greeks (spot/vol/rate/asOf); merges over the position's own market.
- market.asOf?: string | number; default: not declared — Snapshot time. Epoch ms, or an ISO date/datetime string parsed at the boundary.
- market.dividendYield?: number; default: not declared
- market.expiry?: string; default: not declared
- market.legVolatilities?: readonly (number | undefined)[]; default: not declared — Per-leg volatility OVERRIDES for this call (Preview P1), aligned to `position.legs`: leg `i`
prices at `legVolatilities[i]` when it is a number, else at its own `impliedVolatility`, else at
the position-level `volatility` (`volatilityShock` still adds on top). This is how a mark from
CURRENT contract quotes reaches a position whose legs were built with entry volatilities — the
position stays immutable, the call states the market. `assumptions.volatilitySource` reports
`'perCall'` when any override applied.
- market.riskFreeRate?: number; default: not declared
- market.spot?: number; default: not declared — Underlying spot price (WS3.2: renamed from `underlyingPrice` for workspace consistency).
- market.volatility?: number; default: not declared — Position-level implied volatility. OPTIONAL: a position whose every option leg carries its own
`iv` prices entirely per-leg and needs no position vol. It is required (and validated positive)
only when at least one un-expired option leg has no per-leg `iv`; omitting it then throws.
- market.volatilityShock?: number; default: not declared — Additive volatility shock (decimal) applied to EVERY effective leg volatility — the per-leg
`impliedVolatility` when a leg carries one, and the position-level `volatility` otherwise. This
is what makes a volatility scenario reach per-leg-IV legs; without it, shocking only
`volatility` is a silent no-op for legs that fix their own implied volatility.
- underlyingLabel?: string; default: not declared — Underlying name for the prose (e.g. `'AAPL'`); default `'the underlying'`.

```typescript
// ───────────────────────── iron butterfly / condor variants ─────────────────────────
/** Iron butterfly: short ATM call + short ATM put + long OTM wings (a short straddle + long strangle). */
export interface IronButterflyInput extends UnitInput {
```

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy#Leg

Kind: type; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

A single position leg: a stock row or an option row, discriminated by `kind`.

```typescript
/** A single position leg: a stock row or an option row, discriminated by `kind`. */
export type Leg = StockLeg | OptionLeg;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- expiry?: (string) | (undefined); default: not declared — Optional per-leg expiry (`YYYY-MM-DD` → 16:00 ET, or a full datetime). When omitted the leg uses
the position-level expiry supplied to `value()`. Set it for multi-expiry structures (calendars,
diagonals, double diagonals) so each leg is priced at its own time-to-expiry.
- impliedVolatility?: (number) | (undefined); default: not declared — Optional per-leg implied volatility (decimal, e.g. `0.28`). When set, `value()`/`chartData()`/
`scenarioTable()` price this leg at its own IV instead of the position-level `vol` — so a real
chain (four distinct IVs on an iron condor) marks correctly. When omitted, the leg falls back to
the position-level `vol`. The result's `assumptions.volatilitySource` reports which was used.
- kind: ('call' | 'put') | ('stock'); default: not declared
- premium?: (number) | (undefined); default: not declared — Entry premium per share.
- price?: (number) | (undefined); default: not declared — Entry price per share.
Never on an option row (a stock row's entry price).
- quantity: number; default: not declared — Signed shares: positive = long, negative = short.
Signed contracts: positive = long, negative = short.
- strike?: (number) | (undefined); default: not declared — Never on a stock row (typed so a union read narrows to `undefined`, not to a fake 0).

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy#LegInput

Kind: type; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

A leg before entry-price resolution: an option's `premium` (or a stock's `price`) is optional
and filled by the model — the Black–Scholes–Merton premium, the market spot — when omitted
under `{ premiums: 'model', market }`.

```typescript
/**
 * A leg before entry-price resolution: an option's `premium` (or a stock's `price`) is optional

export type LegInput = (Omit<StockLeg, 'price'> & {

    premium?: number;
});
```

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy#MarkToMarketInput

```typescript
    /** Underlying spot price (WS3.2: renamed from `underlyingPrice` for workspace consistency). */
    spot: number;
    /** Snapshot time. Epoch ms, or an ISO date/datetime string parsed at the boundary. */

     * `impliedVolatility` when a leg carries one, and the position-level `volatility` otherwise. This
     * is what makes a volatility scenario reach per-leg-IV legs; without it, shocking only
     * `volatility` is a silent no-op for legs that fix their own implied volatility.

    volatilityShock?: number;
    /**
     * Per-leg volatility OVERRIDES for this call (Preview P1), aligned to `position.legs`: leg `i`
     * prices at `legVolatilities[i]` when it is a number, else at its own `impliedVolatility`, else at
     * the position-level `volatility` (`volatilityShock` still adds on top). This is how a mark from
     * CURRENT contract quotes reaches a position whose legs were built with entry volatilities — the
     * position stays immutable, the call states the market. `assumptions.volatilitySource` reports
     * `'perCall'` when any override applied.
     */
    legVolatilities?: readonly (number | undefined)[];
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- asOf: string | number; default: not declared — Snapshot time. Epoch ms, or an ISO date/datetime string parsed at the boundary.
- dividendYield?: number; default: not declared
- expiry: string; default: not declared
- legVolatilities?: readonly (number | undefined)[]; default: not declared — Per-leg volatility OVERRIDES for this call (Preview P1), aligned to `position.legs`: leg `i`
prices at `legVolatilities[i]` when it is a number, else at its own `impliedVolatility`, else at
the position-level `volatility` (`volatilityShock` still adds on top). This is how a mark from
CURRENT contract quotes reaches a position whose legs were built with entry volatilities — the
position stays immutable, the call states the market. `assumptions.volatilitySource` reports
`'perCall'` when any override applied.
- riskFreeRate: number; default: not declared
- spot: number; default: not declared — Underlying spot price (WS3.2: renamed from `underlyingPrice` for workspace consistency).
- volatility?: number; default: not declared — Position-level implied volatility. OPTIONAL: a position whose every option leg carries its own
`iv` prices entirely per-leg and needs no position vol. It is required (and validated positive)
only when at least one un-expired option leg has no per-leg `iv`; omitting it then throws.
- volatilityShock?: number; default: not declared — Additive volatility shock (decimal) applied to EVERY effective leg volatility — the per-leg
`impliedVolatility` when a leg carries one, and the position-level `volatility` otherwise. This
is what makes a volatility scenario reach per-leg-IV legs; without it, shocking only
`volatility` is a silent no-op for legs that fix their own implied volatility.

```typescript
/** Options for {@link optimizeStrategy}. */
export interface OptimizeStrategyOptions {

     * Valuation instant — epoch milliseconds or a zoned ISO datetime, the ONE valuation-instant
```

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy#OptimizedStrategy

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

A scanned candidate re-scored under the trader's thesis.

```typescript
/** A scanned candidate re-scored under the trader's thesis. */
export interface OptimizedStrategy extends ScanCandidate {
    expiry: string;
    /** Year fraction to this expiry. */
    timeToExpiryYears: number;
    /** Expected P&L under the thesis (per contract, 100×). */
    thesisExpectedValue: number;
    /** Probability of profit under the thesis. */
    thesisProbabilityOfProfit: number;
    /** `thesisEv / |maxLoss|` (0 when risk is unbounded) — the defined-risk read; never falls back to margin. */
    thesisExpectedValuePerRisk: number;
    /** The candidate's Reg-T buying-power requirement (the honest capital denominator). */
    capital: OptimizedStrategyCapital;
    /** `thesisEv / capital.requirement`; `null` (never `Infinity`) when the requirement is zero. */
    thesisExpectedValuePerCapital: number | null;
    /** Kelly sizing verdict — present only when `sizing` was requested (2B never populates it). */
    kelly?: OptimizedStrategyKelly;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- capital: OptimizedStrategyCapital; default: not declared — The candidate's Reg-T buying-power requirement (the honest capital denominator).

- capital.assumptions.conventionsVersion: string; default: not declared

- capital.method: 'reg-t-naked' | 'defined-risk-max-loss' | 'reg-t-naked-put' | 'long-premium'; default: not declared — How the requirement was derived.
- capital.requirement: number; default: not declared — Buying-power reduction the account must set aside (per contract, 100×).

- kelly.sizing.diagnostics.autoReason?: string; default: not declared — When a meta-engine (e.g. `engines.auto()`) selected a delegate, this is a one-sentence,

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy#OptimizerThesis

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

The trader's view of the terminal price — a lognormal centered at a target (or drift).

```typescript
/** The trader's view of the terminal price — a lognormal centered at a target (or drift). */
export interface OptimizerThesis {
    /** Median terminal price (the central view). If omitted, the median is `spot·e^{drift·t}`. */
    targetPrice?: number;
    /** Annualized volatility capturing the trader's UNCERTAINTY (σ_log at expiry = `volatility·√t`). Required, > 0. */
    volatility: number;
    /** Annualized drift used when `targetPrice` is omitted (default 0 — a flat view). */
    drift?: number;
    /** Escape hatch: an arbitrary terminal density `p(price, t)` (replaces the lognormal shape). */
    pdf?: (price: number, timeToExpiryYears: number) => number;
    /**
     * Required with `pdf`: the price range `{ from, to }` covering the density's support. The custom
     * density is integrated over exactly this range (not the `volatility` window), so its mass is never
     * silently truncated. Ignored for the lognormal thesis.
     */
    pdfRange?: {
        from: number;
        to: number;
    };
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- drift?: number; default: not declared — Annualized drift used when `targetPrice` is omitted (default 0 — a flat view).
- pdf?: (price: number, timeToExpiryYears: number) => number; default: not declared — Escape hatch: an arbitrary terminal density `p(price, t)` (replaces the lognormal shape).
- pdf(price): number; default: not declared
- pdf(timeToExpiryYears): number; default: not declared
- pdfRange?: { from: number; to: number; }; default: not declared — Required with `pdf`: the price range `{ from, to }` covering the density's support. The custom
density is integrated over exactly this range (not the `volatility` window), so its mass is never
silently truncated. Ignored for the lognormal thesis.
- pdfRange.from: number; default: not declared
- pdfRange.to: number; default: not declared
- targetPrice?: number; default: not declared — Median terminal price (the central view). If omitted, the median is `spot·e^{drift·t}`.
- volatility: number; default: not declared — Annualized volatility capturing the trader's UNCERTAINTY (σ_log at expiry = `volatility·√t`). Required, > 0.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy#OptionLeg

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

An option leg. `quantity` is signed contracts — positive = long, negative = short — scaled by the
position multiplier; `premium` is the entry premium per share.

```typescript
/**
 * An option leg. `quantity` is signed contracts — positive = long, negative = short — scaled by the
 * position multiplier; `premium` is the entry premium per share.
 */
export interface OptionLeg {
    kind: 'call' | 'put';
    /** Never on an option row (a stock row's entry price). */
    price?: undefined;
    strike: number;
    /** Entry premium per share. */
    premium: number;
    /** Signed contracts: positive = long, negative = short. */
    quantity: number;
    /**
     * Optional per-leg expiry (`YYYY-MM-DD` → 16:00 ET, or a full datetime). When omitted the leg uses
     * the position-level expiry supplied to `value()`. Set it for multi-expiry structures (calendars,
     * diagonals, double diagonals) so each leg is priced at its own time-to-expiry.
     */
    expiry?: string;
    /**
     * Optional per-leg implied volatility (decimal, e.g. `0.28`). When set, `value()`/`chartData()`/
     * `scenarioTable()` price this leg at its own IV instead of the position-level `vol` — so a real
     * chain (four distinct IVs on an iron condor) marks correctly. When omitted, the leg falls back to
     * the position-level `vol`. The result's `assumptions.volatilitySource` reports which was used.
     */
    impliedVolatility?: number;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- expiry?: string; default: not declared — Optional per-leg expiry (`YYYY-MM-DD` → 16:00 ET, or a full datetime). When omitted the leg uses

diagonals, double diagonals) so each leg is priced at its own time-to-expiry.
- impliedVolatility?: number; default: not declared — Optional per-leg implied volatility (decimal, e.g. `0.28`). When set, `value()`/`chartData()`/
`scenarioTable()` price this leg at its own IV instead of the position-level `vol` — so a real
chain (four distinct IVs on an iron condor) marks correctly. When omitted, the leg falls back to
the position-level `vol`. The result's `assumptions.volatilitySource` reports which was used.
- kind: 'call' | 'put'; default: not declared
- premium: number; default: not declared — Entry premium per share.
- price?: undefined; default: not declared — Never on an option row (a stock row's entry price).
- quantity: number; default: not declared — Signed contracts: positive = long, negative = short.
- strike: number; default: not declared

```typescript
export interface PayoffMetrics {

    /** Net credit received (the negation of `netDebit`). */
    netCredit: number;
    /** Maximum profit at expiration, or `null` when the profit is unbounded (`bounded.profit`). */
    maxProfit: number | null;
    /** Maximum loss at expiration as a negative number, or `null` when unbounded (`bounded.loss`). */
    maxLoss: number | null;
    /**
     * Whether each tail is bounded. An unbounded side is `null` above, never `Infinity` (B3): a
     * naked short call has `bounded.loss === false`, a long call `bounded.profit === false`.
     */
    bounded: {
        profit: boolean;
        loss: boolean;
    };
    /** Underlying prices at which expiration P&L is zero. */
    breakevens: number[];
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- bounded: { loss: boolean; profit: boolean; }; default: not declared — Whether each tail is bounded. An unbounded side is `null` above, never `Infinity` (B3): a
naked short call has `bounded.loss === false`, a long call `bounded.profit === false`.
- bounded.loss: boolean; default: not declared
- bounded.profit: boolean; default: not declared
- breakevens: number[]; default: not declared — Underlying prices at which expiration P&L is zero.
- maxLoss: number | null; default: not declared — Maximum loss at expiration as a negative number, or `null` when unbounded (`bounded.loss`).
- maxProfit: number | null; default: not declared — Maximum profit at expiration, or `null` when the profit is unbounded (`bounded.profit`).
- netCredit: number; default: not declared — Net credit received (the negation of `netDebit`).
- netDebit: number; default: not declared — Net cash to enter: positive = debit paid, negative = credit received.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy#Position

Kind: class; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

```typescript
export declare class Position {
  constructor(legs: readonly LegInput[], config?: PositionConfig);
  assumptions(): PositionAssumptions;
  chartData(options?: { prices?: number[] | PriceRange; include?: ChartInclude; market?: Partial<Omit<MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; }): Array<{ underlyingPrice: number; expirationPnl?: number; currentPnl?: number; delta?: number; theta?: number; }>;

  probability(overrides?: Partial<ProbabilityInput>): ProbabilityMetrics;

}
```

per leg: `leg.expiry` > `expiry` > `market.expiry` (R4).
- (config).market?: PremiumMarket; default: not declared — Market for model-priced entry premiums (required when `premiums: 'model'` and any leg omits its
premium) — AND the position's remembered market (R5): `probability()`, `monteCarloProbability()`,

fields merged over it. Results echo `marketSource: 'construction' | 'call' | 'merged'`.
- (config).multiplier?: number; default: not declared — Contract multiplier for option legs (default 100).
- (config).premiums?: PremiumSource; default: not declared — Entry-premium source: `'user'` (from the leg inputs, default) or `'model'` (priced from `market`).
- (legs): readonly LegInput[]; default: not declared

the caller (`'user'`) or model-priced from a market (`'model'`), plus the contract multiplier.

- assumptions().return.multiplier: number; default: not declared — Contract multiplier applied to option legs.
- assumptions().return.premiumSource: PremiumSource; default: not declared — `'user'` when every entry premium was supplied; `'model'` when any was priced from `market`.
- assumptions().return.premiumVolatilitySource?: PremiumVolatilitySource; default: not declared — When premiums were modeled, which volatility priced them: each leg's own `impliedVolatility`
(`'leg'`), the position-level `market.volatility` (`'position'`), or both across legs
(`'mixed'`) — the same source `value()` marks with, so a chain-fed position opens flat.
- chartData: (options?: { prices?: number[] | PriceRange; include?: ChartInclude; market?: Partial<Omit<MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; }) => Array<{ underlyingPrice: number; expirationPnl?: number; currentPnl?: number; delta?: number; theta?: number; }>; default: not declared — Chart-ready output (spec §12.5). - chartData(options).prices.steps: number; default: not declared
- chartData(options).prices.to: number; default: not declared
- constructedAs?: string; default: not declared — PROVENANCE, not identity (dx §4.5): the named builder that constructed this position, absent
for raw `strategy(legs)`. Because positions are immutable this can never go stale — but a
rebuilt-after-tweak position has no name. For "what is this NOW?" use `classifyStrategy`.
- legs: readonly Readonly<Leg>[]; default: not declared — The resolved legs — a frozen snapshot (deep-copied at construction, `Object.freeze`d per leg

market object later never silently retargets the position. `probability()`, `value()`,

- market.dividendYield?: number; default: not declared

- market.riskFreeRate: number; default: not declared
- market.spot: number; default: not declared
- market.volatility: number; default: not declared — Entry implied volatility (annualized decimal) for unpriced legs that carry no `impliedVolatility`
of their own — a leg's own volatility always wins, exactly as it does when `value()` marks it.
- metrics: () => PayoffMetrics; default: not declared — Net debit/credit, max profit/loss, and breakevens. The expiration payoff is piecewise-linear, so
these are computed ANALYTICALLY from the kink set (every option strike plus every stock entry
price) and the tail slopes — never by sampling a coarse grid, which missed breakevens beyond the
last strike (e.g. a lone long stock, or a deep-ITM option) and ignored stock entry prices.
- metrics().return.bounded: { loss: boolean; profit: boolean; }; default: not declared — Whether each tail is bounded. An unbounded side is `null` above, never `Infinity` (B3): a
naked short call has `bounded.loss === false`, a long call `bounded.profit === false`.
- metrics().return.bounded.loss: boolean; default: not declared
- metrics().return.bounded.profit: boolean; default: not declared
- metrics().return.breakevens: number[]; default: not declared — Underlying prices at which expiration P&L is zero.
- metrics().return.maxLoss: number | null; default: not declared — Maximum loss at expiration as a negative number, or `null` when unbounded (`bounded.loss`).
- metrics().return.maxProfit: number | null; default: not declared — Maximum profit at expiration, or `null` when the profit is unbounded (`bounded.profit`).
- metrics().return.netCredit: number; default: not declared — Net credit received (the negation of `netDebit`).
- metrics().return.netDebit: number; default: not declared — Net cash to enter: positive = debit paid, negative = credit received.
- monteCarloProbability: (overrides: Partial<ProbabilityMonteCarloInput> & { seed: number; }) => ProbabilityMonteCarloMetrics; default: not declared — Monte-Carlo probability metrics (spec §12.6): the simulated analogue of {@link probability}, for
cross-validation and path-dependent reads. Terminal lognormal paths give the probability of profit
and expected P&L (with a standard error); the probability of touching each breakeven is estimated
with the Brownian-bridge continuous-monitoring correction. Seeded and deterministic.
- monteCarloProbability().return.assumptions: Assumptions<{ marketSource: MarketSource; probabilityModel: ProbabilityModel; }>; default: not declared — Applied conventions, plus where the market fields came from — construction market, call site,
or a merge (R5) — as `assumptions.marketSource` (R2: never hoisted to the top level).
- monteCarloProbability().return.expectedValue: number; default: not declared — Monte-Carlo expected expiration P&L.
- monteCarloProbability().return.expectedValueStandardError: number; default: not declared — Standard error of the expected-value estimate.
- monteCarloProbability().return.paths: number; default: not declared — Number of paths simulated.
- monteCarloProbability().return.pnlQuantiles?: { quantile: number; pnl: number; }[]; default: not declared — Requested expiration-P&L quantiles (the profit cone), present only when `pnlQuantiles` was set.
- monteCarloProbability().return.probabilityOfProfit: number; default: not declared — Monte-Carlo probability of a positive expiration P&L.
- monteCarloProbability().return.probabilityOfTouch: TouchProbability[]; default: not declared — Probability of touching each breakeven before expiry, estimated from simulated paths with the
Brownian-bridge continuous-monitoring correction (discrete sampling alone would under-count).
- monteCarloProbability().return.seed: number; default: not declared — The PRNG seed, echoed for reproducibility (stochastic-provenance rule, cf. `MonteCarloStatistics.seed`).
- monteCarloProbability(overrides): Partial<ProbabilityMonteCarloInput> & { seed: number; }; default: not declared
- monteCarloProbability(overrides).asOf?: string | number; default: not declared — Snapshot time. Epoch ms, or an ISO date/datetime string parsed at the boundary.
- monteCarloProbability(overrides).dividendYield?: number; default: not declared
- monteCarloProbability(overrides).expectedReturn?: number; default: not declared — Annualized expected return, the drift of the `realWorld` measure.

**REQUIRED when `measure: 'realWorld'`, and rejected otherwise.** It used to default to
`riskFreeRate`, so `measure: 'realWorld'` with no expected return silently returned the
risk-neutral probabilities while `assumptions.probabilityModel.measure` still reported
`'realWorld'` — a result whose own echoed assumptions contradicted the number it carried.
Choosing the real-world measure IS choosing a drift, so the drift must be stated.
- monteCarloProbability(overrides).expiry?: string; default: not declared
- monteCarloProbability(overrides).localVolatility?: (level: number, timeToExpiryYears: number) => number; default: not declared — Optional Dupire local-volatility function `σ_loc(level, t)` (e.g. from
`@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility`'s `surfaceLocalVolatility` or `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/options`'s `dupireLocalVolatility`). When provided, the
simulation steps under local vol instead of a single lognormal σ, so probability-of-profit,
expected P&L, and probability-of-touch all reflect the volatility smile/skew — the smile-aware

- monteCarloProbability(overrides).measure?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMeasure; default: not declared — Terminal measure: `riskNeutral` (drift `r − q`, default) or `realWorld` (drift `expectedReturn − q`).
- monteCarloProbability(overrides).paths?: number; default: not declared — Number of simulated paths (default 50_000).
- monteCarloProbability(overrides).pnlQuantiles?: number[]; default: not declared — Optional P&L quantiles to report (each in `(0, 1)`), forming an expiration profit "cone" from the
simulated terminal distribution. E.g. `[0.05, 0.5, 0.95]` → 5th/50th/95th-percentile P&L.
- monteCarloProbability(overrides).riskFreeRate?: number; default: not declared

- return.market.asOf: string | number; default: not declared — Entry time (epoch ms or ISO). Each leg's entry `t = yearFraction(asOf, leg.expiry ?? market.expiry)`.
- return.market.dividendYield?: number; default: not declared
- return.market.expiry?: string; default: not declared — Default expiry for legs without their own `expiry` (single-expiry structures).
- return.market.riskFreeRate: number; default: not declared
- return.market.spot: number; default: not declared
- return.market.volatility: number; default: not declared — Entry implied volatility (annualized decimal) for unpriced legs that carry no `impliedVolatility`
of their own — a leg's own volatility always wins, exactly as it does when `value()` marks it.
- return.metrics: () => PayoffMetrics; default: not declared — Net debit/credit, max profit/loss, and breakevens. The expiration payoff is piecewise-linear, so
these are computed ANALYTICALLY from the kink set (every option strike plus every stock entry
price) and the tail slopes — never by sampling a coarse grid, which missed breakevens beyond the
last strike (e.g. a lone long stock, or a deep-ITM option) and ignored stock entry prices.
- return.monteCarloProbability: (overrides: Partial<ProbabilityMonteCarloInput> & { seed: number; }) => ProbabilityMonteCarloMetrics; default: not declared — Monte-Carlo probability metrics (spec §12.6): the simulated analogue of {@link probability}, for
cross-validation and path-dependent reads. Terminal lognormal paths give the probability of profit
and expected P&L (with a standard error); the probability of touching each breakeven is estimated
with the Brownian-bridge continuous-monitoring correction. Seeded and deterministic.
- return.multiplier: number; default: not declared
- return.netDebit: () => number; default: not declared — Net cash to enter (positive = debit, negative = credit).
- return.payoff: (options?: { prices?: number[] | PriceRange; }) => PayoffResult; default: not declared — Expiration payoff metrics plus a chart-ready grid of points (spec §12.2). `prices` is an explicit
grid array or a `{ from, to, steps }` range; omit it to frame the strike-derived default window
(the same one a payoff diagram draws).
- return.pnlAtExpiry: (underlyingPrice: number) => number; default: not declared — Expiration P&L at an underlying price.
- return.premiumSource: PremiumSource; default: not declared — How the entry premiums were sourced: `'user'` (supplied) or `'model'` (priced from `market`).
- return.premiumVolatilitySource?: PremiumVolatilitySource; default: not declared — When modeled, which volatility priced the entries (`'leg'`, `'position'` or `'mixed'`).
- return.probability: (overrides?: Partial<ProbabilityInput>) => ProbabilityMetrics; default: not declared — Probability & scenario metrics (spec §12.6): probability of profit, expected value, reward/risk,
and the probability of touching each breakeven — under an explicit, echoed lognormal model.
- return.scenarioTable: (options?: { market?: Partial<Omit<MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; prices?: number[] | PriceRange; volatilityShocks?: number[]; daysForward?: number[]; }) => ScenarioTableResult; default: not declared — Scenario table (spec §12.6): mark-to-market P&L and Greeks across a grid of underlying prices,
additive vol shocks, and days forward — the standard "what-if" matrix for an options ticket.
- return.value: (overrides?: Partial<MarkToMarketInput>) => MarkToMarketResult; default: not declared — Mark-to-market value, P&L, per-leg and aggregate Greeks via BSM (spec §12.3).
- return.whatIfCube: (options?: WhatIfCubeOptions) => WhatIfCubeResult; default: not declared — A what-if **cube**: the position marked over the full spot × vol-shock × days-forward grid, plus
the **optimal-exit surface** — for each (spot, vol) outcome, the day along the time axis that
optimizes P&L (`max-pnl` by default, or `min-pnl`). `scenarioTable` extended a dimension: it returns
a navigable cube (axes + row-major cells) with the reductions a trader wants, not a flat row list.

Every cell is a `value()` mark (time-aware, per-leg-IV, shock-through-to-leg-IV), so calendars and
per-leg volatilities behave identically. The optimal-exit surface is a CONDITIONAL what-if ("if the
underlying is here with this vol shock, which day marks best?"), not a path-dependent stopping rule.
See `docs/specs/what-if-cube.md`.
- scenarioTable: (options?: { market?: Partial<Omit<MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; prices?: number[] | PriceRange; volatilityShocks?: number[]; daysForward?: number[]; }) => ScenarioTableResult; default: not declared — Scenario table (spec §12.6): mark-to-market P&L and Greeks across a grid of underlying prices,
additive vol shocks, and days forward — the standard "what-if" matrix for an options ticket.
- scenarioTable().return.assumptions: Assumptions<{ marketSource: MarketSource; }>; default: not declared — Every applied convention, echoed back.
- scenarioTable().return.diagnostics: Diagnostics; default: not declared — How the value was computed, plus any warnings.
- scenarioTable().return.provenance?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Provenance; default: not declared — Optional data lineage when the inputs came from a provider.
- scenarioTable().return.value: ScenarioRow[]; default: not declared — The computed value. Never `NaN` or `±Infinity`: a value the model cannot produce is `null`
beside a diagnostic that says why (Law 7 — a warning never licenses a non-finite number).
- scenarioTable(options)?: { daysForward?: number[]; market?: Partial<Omit<MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; prices?: number[] | PriceRange; volatilityShocks?: number[]; }; default: not declared
- scenarioTable(options).daysForward?: number[]; default: not declared — Calendar days to advance `asOf`, e.g. `[0, 1, 7]`. Default `[0]`.
- scenarioTable(options).market?: Partial<Omit<MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; default: not declared — Market overrides; defaults from the construction market (R5).
- scenarioTable(options).market.asOf?: string | number; default: not declared — Snapshot time. Epoch ms, or an ISO date/datetime string parsed at the boundary.
- scenarioTable(options).market.dividendYield?: number; default: not declared
- scenarioTable(options).market.expiry?: string; default: not declared
- scenarioTable(options).market.legVolatilities?: readonly (number | undefined)[]; default: not declared — Per-leg volatility OVERRIDES for this call (Preview P1), aligned to `position.legs`: leg `i`
prices at `legVolatilities[i]` when it is a number, else at its own `impliedVolatility`, else at
the position-level `volatility` (`volatilityShock` still adds on top). This is how a mark from
CURRENT contract quotes reaches a position whose legs were built with entry volatilities — the
position stays immutable, the call states the market. `assumptions.volatilitySource` reports
`'perCall'` when any override applied.
- scenarioTable(options).market.riskFreeRate?: number; default: not declared
- scenarioTable(options).market.volatility?: number; default: not declared — Position-level implied volatility. OPTIONAL: a position whose every option leg carries its own
`iv` prices entirely per-leg and needs no position vol. It is required (and validated positive)
only when at least one un-expired option leg has no per-leg `iv`; omitting it then throws.
- scenarioTable(options).market.volatilityShock?: number; default: not declared — Additive volatility shock (decimal) applied to EVERY effective leg volatility — the per-leg
`impliedVolatility` when a leg carries one, and the position-level `volatility` otherwise. This
is what makes a volatility scenario reach per-leg-IV legs; without it, shocking only
`volatility` is a silent no-op for legs that fix their own implied volatility.
- scenarioTable(options).prices?: number[] | PriceRange; default: not declared — Spot axis: an explicit grid array or a `{ from, to, steps }` range. Omit for the default window.
- scenarioTable(options).prices.from: number; default: not declared
- scenarioTable(options).prices.steps: number; default: not declared
- scenarioTable(options).prices.to: number; default: not declared
- scenarioTable(options).volatilityShocks?: number[]; default: not declared — Additive vol shocks (decimal), e.g. `[-0.05, 0, 0.05]`. Default `[0]`.
- value: (overrides?: Partial<MarkToMarketInput>) => MarkToMarketResult; default: not declared — Mark-to-market value, P&L, per-leg and aggregate Greeks via BSM (spec §12.3).
- value().return.assumptions: Assumptions<{ volatilitySource: VolatilitySource; marketSource: MarketSource; }>; default: not declared — Every applied convention, echoed back.
- value().return.diagnostics: Diagnostics; default: not declared — How the value was computed, plus any warnings.
- value().return.greeks: ExtendedGreeks; default: not declared — Book-aggregate extended greeks: additive fields summed over legs; `lambda` (Δ·S/V) recomputed at
the book level (null when the book value underflows to 0).

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy#PositionAssumptions

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Position-construction assumptions (design law #3): how entry premiums were sourced.

```typescript
/** Position-construction assumptions (design law #3): how entry premiums were sourced. */
export interface PositionAssumptions {
    /** `'user'` when every entry premium was supplied; `'model'` when any was priced from `market`. */
    premiumSource: PremiumSource;
    /**
     * When premiums were modeled, which volatility priced them: each leg's own `impliedVolatility`
     * (`'leg'`), the position-level `market.volatility` (`'position'`), or both across legs
     * (`'mixed'`) — the same source `value()` marks with, so a chain-fed position opens flat.
     */
    premiumVolatilitySource?: PremiumVolatilitySource;
    /** Contract multiplier applied to option legs. */
    multiplier: number;
    /** The named builder that constructed this position (provenance — see `classifyStrategy`). */
    constructedAs?: string;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- constructedAs?: string; default: not declared — The named builder that constructed this position (provenance — see `classifyStrategy`).
- multiplier: number; default: not declared — Contract multiplier applied to option legs.
- premiumSource: PremiumSource; default: not declared — `'user'` when every entry premium was supplied; `'model'` when any was priced from `market`.
- premiumVolatilitySource?: PremiumVolatilitySource; default: not declared — When premiums were modeled, which volatility priced them: each leg's own `impliedVolatility`
(`'leg'`), the position-level `market.volatility` (`'position'`), or both across legs
(`'mixed'`) — the same source `value()` marks with, so a chain-fed position opens flat.

```typescript
    /** The classification, or `'custom'`. */
    name: string;

    aliases: string[];

        /** Maximum loss (negative), or `null` when unbounded. */
        maxLoss: number | null;
        breakevens: number[];
        /** `|maxProfit / maxLoss|`, or `null` when undefined (an unbounded side or a zero max loss). */
        rewardToRisk: number | null;
    };

    timeBias?: TimeBias;
    probability?: {
        probabilityOfProfit: number;
        expectedValue: number;
    };
    greeks?: {
        delta: number;
        gamma: number;
        theta: number;
        vega: number;
        rho: number;
    };
    risks: string[];

    summary: string;

        conventionsVersion: string;
        /** How the name was derived — always the structural classifier (identity is never remembered). */
        classifier: 'structural-base-signature';
        /** Whether a usable market priced the greek/probability posture (false = payoff-only read). */
        marketDependent: boolean;
    };
    /** Structured warnings; always present (possibly empty) — a missing market explains itself here. */

}
```

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy#ProbabilityMonteCarloInput

```typescript
export interface ProbabilityMonteCarloInput extends Omit<ProbabilityInput, 'volatility'> {
    /**
     * Annualized volatility of the constant-vol lognormal. Required unless {@link localVolatility} is supplied
     * (a local-volatility path ignores it except as the model echo's representative vol).
     */
    volatility?: number;
    /**
     * Optional Dupire local-volatility function `σ_loc(level, t)` (e.g. from
     * `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility`'s `surfaceLocalVolatility` or `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/options`'s `dupireLocalVolatility`). When provided, the
     * simulation steps under local vol instead of a single lognormal σ, so probability-of-profit,
     * expected P&L, and probability-of-touch all reflect the volatility smile/skew — the smile-aware
     * multi-leg read. The function is evaluated at the price and time reached at each step.
     */
    localVolatility?: (level: number, timeToExpiryYears: number) => number;
    /** Seed for the deterministic PRNG (required — the simulation never reads the system clock). */
    seed: number;
    /** Number of simulated paths (default 50_000). */
    paths?: number;
    /** Monitoring steps per path for the probability-of-touch estimate (default 50). */
    steps?: number;
    /**
     * Optional P&L quantiles to report (each in `(0, 1)`), forming an expiration profit "cone" from the
     * simulated terminal distribution. E.g. `[0.05, 0.5, 0.95]` → 5th/50th/95th-percentile P&L.
     */
    pnlQuantiles?: number[];
}
```

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy#SCAN_OBJECTIVES

Kind: value; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Every ranking objective a scan accepts, as DATA — the single source the type, the runtime guard and
the error message are all derived from.

RV11 — these were three copies: a hand-written union here, a hand-written array in `optimizer.ts`,
and a third hand-written list inside the error string. The string copy drifted and kept teaching
`pop|ev` after both were renamed, because plain prose is invisible to a rename of the quoted
literals. One tuple, and `.join(', ')` for the message, is what makes that impossible rather than
merely fixed.

`'return'` became `'returnOnRisk'` in the same pass: it ranked by `returnOnRisk` and the candidate
output already called that number `returnOnRisk`, so one quantity carried two public names.

```typescript
export declare const SCAN_OBJECTIVES: readonly ['probabilityOfProfit', 'expectedValue', 'returnOnRisk', 'expectedValuePerRisk'];
```

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy#ScanCandidate

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

```typescript
export interface ScanCandidate {
    structure: ScanStructure;
    /** The structure's strikes, ascending. */
    strikes: number[];
    /** Net debit (> 0 paid) or credit (< 0 received), PER CONTRACT (multiplier-scaled, 100×) — the
     * same units as `maxProfit`/`maxLoss`/`expectedValue` and `Position.netDebit()`. */
    netDebit: number;
    /** Max profit / max loss / expected value are per contract (100× multiplier, as in `Position`). */
    maxProfit: number | null;
    maxLoss: number | null;
    /** Whether each tail of the expiration payoff is bounded (a `null` bound above is unbounded). */
    bounded: {
        profit: boolean;
        loss: boolean;
    };
    breakevens: number[];
    probabilityOfProfit: number;
    expectedValue: number;
    /**
     * `|maxProfit / maxLoss|` — the same definition as `Position.probability().riskReward` — or
     * `null` when undefined (an unbounded side or a zero max loss). Never `Infinity` (B3).
     */
    returnOnRisk: number | null;
    /** `expectedValue / |maxLoss|` — a risk-normalized EV; 0 when risk is unbounded. */
    expectedValuePerRisk: number;
    /** Liquidity in `[0, 1]` from the legs' relative bid/ask spreads (1 = tight), null if unpriced. */
    liquidity: number | null;
    /** The value of the ranking objective for this candidate; `null` when the objective is undefined for it. */
    score: number | null;
    /**
     * The resolved legs (premiums included, whatever their source), so every candidate is
     * MATERIALIZABLE (WS7.3): `strategy(candidate.legs)` reconstructs the exact position for charting or
     * mark-to-market, and `strategy(candidate.legs).metrics()` reproduces the reported payoff metrics.
     */
    legs: Leg[];
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- bounded: { profit: boolean; loss: boolean; }; default: not declared — Whether each tail of the expiration payoff is bounded (a `null` bound above is unbounded).
- bounded.loss: boolean; default: not declared
- bounded.profit: boolean; default: not declared
- breakevens: number[]; default: not declared
- expectedValue: number; default: not declared
- expectedValuePerRisk: number; default: not declared — `expectedValue / |maxLoss|` — a risk-normalized EV; 0 when risk is unbounded.
- legs: Leg[]; default: not declared — The resolved legs (premiums included, whatever their source), so every candidate is
MATERIALIZABLE (WS7.3): `strategy(candidate.legs)` reconstructs the exact position for charting or
mark-to-market, and `strategy(candidate.legs).metrics()` reproduces the reported payoff metrics.
- liquidity: number | null; default: not declared — Liquidity in `[0, 1]` from the legs' relative bid/ask spreads (1 = tight), null if unpriced.
- maxLoss: number | null; default: not declared
- maxProfit: number | null; default: not declared — Max profit / max loss / expected value are per contract (100× multiplier, as in `Position`).
- netDebit: number; default: not declared — Net debit (> 0 paid) or credit (< 0 received), PER CONTRACT (multiplier-scaled, 100×) — the
same units as `maxProfit`/`maxLoss`/`expectedValue` and `Position.netDebit()`.
- probabilityOfProfit: number; default: not declared
- returnOnRisk: number | null; default: not declared — `|maxProfit / maxLoss|` — the same definition as `Position.probability().riskReward` — or
`null` when undefined (an unbounded side or a zero max loss). Never `Infinity` (B3).
- score: number | null; default: not declared — The value of the ranking objective for this candidate; `null` when the objective is undefined for it.
- strikes: number[]; default: not declared — The structure's strikes, ascending.
- structure: ScanStructure; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy#ScanObjective

```typescript
/** Ranking objective; `expectedValuePerRisk` (expected value ÷ max loss) is the default. */
export type ScanObjective = (typeof SCAN_OBJECTIVES)[number];
```

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy#ScanOptions

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

```typescript
export interface ScanOptions {
    /** Underlying spot price (WS3.2: renamed from `underlyingPrice` for workspace consistency). */
    spot: number;
    /**
     * Valuation instant. Epoch ms or a zoned ISO datetime, resolved at the boundary by core's
     * `resolveValuationAsOf` — the ONE valuation-instant grammar shared by `Position.probability()`,
     * the what-if cube and every other pricing boundary. A bare date is refused: a 0DTE's value
     * depends on the time of day.
     */
    asOf: EpochMs | string;
    /** Option expiry (`YYYY-MM-DD` → 16:00 ET, or a full datetime). */
    expiry: string;
    riskFreeRate: number;
    dividendYield?: number;
    /** The option chain — one row per strike, ascending or not (sorted internally). */
    chain: ScanQuoteRow[];
    /** Constant annualized volatility used for probabilityOfProfit / expectedValue scoring and to price any missing premiums. */
    volatility?: number;
    /**
     * Per-strike implied-volatility smile. Used to price any missing per-strike premiums (takes
     * precedence over `volatility`). **Scoring uses a SINGLE volatility:** `probabilityOfProfit` and
     * `expectedValue` are computed closed-form at the at-spot volatility `smile(spot)` (or
     * `volatility`), not the full smile — for smile-consistent probabilities, price a specific structure
     * with `Position.monteCarloProbability({ localVolatility })`.
     */
    smile?: (strike: number) => number;
    /** Which structures to enumerate (default: all). */
    structures?: ScanStructure[];
    /** Cap on the width (strike distance) of any single wing/spread, in price units. */
    maxWidth?: number;
    /** Keep only candidates with probability-of-profit ≥ this. */
    minProbabilityOfProfit?: number;
    /** Keep only candidates whose max loss ≤ this (in the position's P&L units — per contract, 100×). */
    maxRisk?: number;
    /** Ranking objective (default `expectedValuePerRisk`). */
    rankBy?: ScanObjective;
    /** Return only the top-N ranked candidates (default 25). */
    top?: number;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- asOf: string | number; default: not declared — Valuation instant. Epoch ms or a zoned ISO datetime, resolved at the boundary by core's
`resolveValuationAsOf` — the ONE valuation-instant grammar shared by `Position.probability()`,
the what-if cube and every other pricing boundary. A bare date is refused: a 0DTE's value
depends on the time of day.
- chain: ScanQuoteRow[]; default: not declared — The option chain — one row per strike, ascending or not (sorted internally).
- dividendYield?: number; default: not declared
- expiry: string; default: not declared — Option expiry (`YYYY-MM-DD` → 16:00 ET, or a full datetime).
- maxRisk?: number; default: not declared — Keep only candidates whose max loss ≤ this (in the position's P&L units — per contract, 100×).
- maxWidth?: number; default: not declared — Cap on the width (strike distance) of any single wing/spread, in price units.
- minProbabilityOfProfit?: number; default: not declared — Keep only candidates with probability-of-profit ≥ this.
- rankBy?: 'probabilityOfProfit' | 'expectedValue' | 'returnOnRisk' | 'expectedValuePerRisk'; default: not declared — Ranking objective (default `expectedValuePerRisk`).
- riskFreeRate: number; default: not declared
- smile?: (strike: number) => number; default: not declared — Per-strike implied-volatility smile. Used to price any missing per-strike premiums (takes
precedence over `volatility`). **Scoring uses a SINGLE volatility:** `probabilityOfProfit` and
`expectedValue` are computed closed-form at the at-spot volatility `smile(spot)` (or

- smile(strike): number; default: not declared
- spot: number; default: not declared — Underlying spot price (WS3.2: renamed from `underlyingPrice` for workspace consistency).
- structures?: ScanStructure[]; default: not declared — Which structures to enumerate (default: all).
- top?: number; default: not declared — Return only the top-N ranked candidates (default 25).
- volatility?: number; default: not declared — Constant annualized volatility used for probabilityOfProfit / expectedValue scoring and to price any missing premiums.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy#ScenarioTableResult

Kind: type; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Result of `scenarioTable()` — the R2 one-envelope form: `value` is the grid rows, `assumptions`
echoes the conventions plus `marketSource` (construction/call/merged, R5), and warnings ride
`diagnostics.warnings` (WS3.7). A shocked volatility that lands at or below the 1e-6 floor is
clamped rather than priced at a non-positive vol; when that happens the affected cells are
flagged in the diagnostics instead of silently returning floor-vol numbers.

```typescript
/**
 * Result of `scenarioTable()` — the R2 one-envelope form: `value` is the grid rows, `assumptions`
 * echoes the conventions plus `marketSource` (construction/call/merged, R5), and warnings ride
 * `diagnostics.warnings` (WS3.7). A shocked volatility that lands at or below the 1e-6 floor is
 * clamped rather than priced at a non-positive vol; when that happens the affected cells are
 * flagged in the diagnostics instead of silently returning floor-vol numbers.
 */
export type ScenarioTableResult = Computed<ScenarioRow[], {
    marketSource: MarketSource;
}>;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- assumptions: Assumptions<{ marketSource: MarketSource; }>; default: not declared — Every applied convention, echoed back.
- assumptions.asOf?: number; default: not declared
- assumptions.calendar?: string; default: not declared
- assumptions.calendarVersion?: string; default: not declared
- assumptions.compounding?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').InterestCompounding; default: not declared
- assumptions.compounding.periodsPerYear: number; default: not declared
- assumptions.compounding.type: 'periodic'; default: not declared
- assumptions.conventionsVersion: string; default: not declared
- assumptions.dayCount?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').DayCount; default: not declared
- assumptions.dividendModel?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').DividendModel; default: not declared
- assumptions.engine?: string; default: not declared
- assumptions.expiryConvention?: 'us-equity-close' | 'explicit-instant'; default: not declared — How the contract's expiry label was resolved to an instant: `'us-equity-close'` when a
date-only `YYYY-MM-DD` expiry resolved to the US equity/options close — 16:00 America/New_York,
or 13:00 on an early-close day;
`'explicit-instant'` when the caller supplied a zoned datetime. Named so the convention is
never silent (alignment spec P1.6); instrument builders own the full story in Phase 3.
- assumptions.marketSource: MarketSource; default: not declared
- assumptions.model?: string; default: not declared
- assumptions.seed?: number; default: not declared — The randomness seed this result was computed under — REQUIRED echo for a
`randomness: 'seeded'` Pricer (Gate C, 2026-08-23): a stochastic result that does not name
its seed cannot be replayed from the result alone. Deterministic paths never set it.
- assumptions.timeToExpiryConvention?: never; default: not declared
- assumptions.timeToExpiryYears?: number; default: not declared
- assumptions.units?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').GreekUnits; default: not declared
- assumptions.units.rho: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').RhoUnit; default: not declared
- assumptions.units.theta: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').ThetaUnit; default: not declared
- assumptions.units.vega: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').VegaUnit; default: not declared
- diagnostics: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Diagnostics; default: not declared — How the value was computed, plus any warnings.
- diagnostics.autoReason?: string; default: not declared — When a meta-engine (e.g. `engines.auto()`) selected a delegate, this is a one-sentence,
human-readable explanation of WHY that delegate was chosen (`engine` then names the delegate).
Absent when no auto-selection took place.
- diagnostics.converged?: boolean; default: not declared — Whether an iterative procedure converged. `false` means the value is not trustworthy.
- diagnostics.decomposition?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Named intermediate quantities the value decomposes into — a par spread's protection leg and
risky annuity, a forward variance's near/far legs. The H-series explain paths disclose their
arithmetic here so a caller can audit the ratio, not just receive it (3B.3).
- diagnostics.engine?: string; default: not declared — Pricing/solver engine name, e.g. `black-scholes-merton`.
- diagnostics.finiteDifferenceBumps?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Finite-difference engines: the ACTUAL bump sizes used for FD Greeks (spec P2.3) — adaptive
near the vol/time boundaries, so the caller can see exactly what was differenced.
Keys: `spotStep`, `volatilityStep`, `timeStepYears`, `rateStep`, and — extended Greeks only —
`dividendYieldStep`. Each is the actual step differenced, in the unit of the coordinate it
bumps. (This doc named the retired `hS`/`hSig`/`hT`/`hR`/`hQ` keys for one release after the
emit sites had moved to the semantic names, so a caller following it read `undefined`.)
- diagnostics.iterations?: number; default: not declared — Iteration count for iterative methods.
- diagnostics.method?: string; default: not declared — Numerical method, e.g. `closed-form`, `brent`, `finite-difference`.
- diagnostics.selection?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing').SelectionReport; default: not declared — The structured engine-selection report (Gate C, `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing`): who was selected,
why, and — for automatic selection — every candidate considered with its verdict. This is the
machine-readable superset of `engine` + `autoReason` (which remain for compatibility);
`selected.name` always agrees with `engine` when both are present.
- diagnostics.selection.candidates?: readonly import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing').SelectionCandidate[]; default: not declared — Candidates an automatic selection considered; absent for explicit mode.
- diagnostics.selection.mode: 'explicit' | 'automatic'; default: not declared
- diagnostics.selection.reason: string; default: not declared — Why the selected engine answers this request.
- diagnostics.selection.selected: { name: string; version?: string; }; default: not declared
- diagnostics.selection.selected.name: string; default: not declared
- diagnostics.selection.selected.version?: string; default: not declared
- diagnostics.timingMs?: number; default: not declared — Wall-clock timing in milliseconds, when measured.
- diagnostics.warmup?: number; default: not declared — Series facades: number of leading output slots that are warmup sentinels (null/NaN) while the
computation seeds. Equals the input length when the indicator never emitted.
- diagnostics.warnings: QuantWarning[]; default: not declared — Structured warnings; always present (possibly empty).
- provenance?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Provenance; default: not declared — Optional data lineage when the inputs came from a provider.
- provenance.asOf?: number; default: not declared
- provenance.dataset?: string; default: not declared
- provenance.provider?: string; default: not declared
- provenance.receivedAt?: number; default: not declared
- provenance.requestId?: string; default: not declared
- provenance.sourceVersion?: string; default: not declared
- provenance.warnings?: QuantWarning[]; default: not declared
- value: ScenarioRow[]; default: not declared — The computed value. Never `NaN` or `±Infinity`: a value the model cannot produce is `null`
beside a diagnostic that says why (Law 7 — a warning never licenses a non-finite number).

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy#WhatIfCubeOptions

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Options for {@link Position.whatIfCube }.

```typescript
/** Options for {@link Position.whatIfCube}. */
export interface WhatIfCubeOptions {
    /** Market overrides; defaults from the construction market (R5). */
    market?: Partial<Omit<MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>;
    /** Spot axis: an explicit grid array or a `{ from, to, steps }` range. Omit for the default window. */
    prices?: number[] | PriceRange;
    /** Additive vol shocks (decimal), e.g. `[-0.05, 0, 0.05]`. Default `[0]`. */
    volatilityShocks?: number[];
    /** Calendar days to advance `asOf`, e.g. `[0, 7, 30]`. Default `[0]`. */
    daysForward?: number[];
    /** Which extremum the optimal-exit surface picks per (spot, vol); default `'max-pnl'`. */
    objective?: 'max-pnl' | 'min-pnl';
    /**
     * Opt-in probability weighting (Wave 6 §3). When set, the result gains a `probability` block with the
     * per-day spot mass, disclosed tails, and per-(vol, day) expected P&L. Requires strictly increasing
     * unique prices and non-negative days.
     */
    probability?: WhatIfProbabilityOptions;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- daysForward?: number[]; default: not declared — Calendar days to advance `asOf`, e.g. `[0, 7, 30]`. Default `[0]`.
- market?: Partial<Omit<MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; default: not declared — Market overrides; defaults from the construction market (R5).
- market.asOf?: string | number; default: not declared — Snapshot time. Epoch ms, or an ISO date/datetime string parsed at the boundary.
- market.dividendYield?: number; default: not declared
- market.expiry?: string; default: not declared
- market.legVolatilities?: readonly (number | undefined)[]; default: not declared — Per-leg volatility OVERRIDES for this call (Preview P1), aligned to `position.legs`: leg `i`
prices at `legVolatilities[i]` when it is a number, else at its own `impliedVolatility`, else at
the position-level `volatility` (`volatilityShock` still adds on top). This is how a mark from
CURRENT contract quotes reaches a position whose legs were built with entry volatilities — the
position stays immutable, the call states the market. `assumptions.volatilitySource` reports
`'perCall'` when any override applied.
- market.riskFreeRate?: number; default: not declared
- market.volatility?: number; default: not declared — Position-level implied volatility. OPTIONAL: a position whose every option leg carries its own
`iv` prices entirely per-leg and needs no position vol. It is required (and validated positive)
only when at least one un-expired option leg has no per-leg `iv`; omitting it then throws.
- market.volatilityShock?: number; default: not declared — Additive volatility shock (decimal) applied to EVERY effective leg volatility — the per-leg
`impliedVolatility` when a leg carries one, and the position-level `volatility` otherwise. This
is what makes a volatility scenario reach per-leg-IV legs; without it, shocking only
`volatility` is a silent no-op for legs that fix their own implied volatility.
- objective?: 'max-pnl' | 'min-pnl'; default: not declared — Which extremum the optimal-exit surface picks per (spot, vol); default `'max-pnl'`.
- prices?: number[] | PriceRange; default: not declared — Spot axis: an explicit grid array or a `{ from, to, steps }` range. Omit for the default window.
- prices.from: number; default: not declared
- prices.steps: number; default: not declared
- prices.to: number; default: not declared
- probability?: WhatIfProbabilityOptions; default: not declared — Opt-in probability weighting (Wave 6 §3). When set, the result gains a `probability` block with the
per-day spot mass, disclosed tails, and per-(vol, day) expected P&L. Requires strictly increasing
unique prices and non-negative days.
- probability.gridPolicy?: 'report-and-renormalize' | 'include-in-edge-bins'; default: not declared — How finite price-grid tails are handled; default `'report-and-renormalize'`.
- probability.model: WhatIfProbabilityModel; default: not declared
- probability.model.annualizedVolatility: number; default: not declared
- probability.model.density: (price: number, yearsForward: number) => number; default: not declared
- probability.model.density(price): number; default: not declared
- probability.model.density(yearsForward): number; default: not declared
- probability.model.drift: number; default: not declared — Annualized arithmetic GBM drift used directly for the underlying process.
- probability.model.expectedReturn: number; default: not declared — Annualized total expected return before dividend yield.
- probability.model.kind: ('custom') | ('gbm'); default: not declared
- probability.model.measure?: ('explicit') | ('realWorld') | ('riskNeutral'); default: not declared
- probability.model.support: { from: number; to: number; }; default: not declared
- probability.model.support.from: number; default: not declared
- probability.model.support.to: number; default: not declared
- volatilityShocks?: number[]; default: not declared — Additive vol shocks (decimal), e.g. `[-0.05, 0, 0.05]`. Default `[0]`.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy#WhatIfCubeProbability

- return.chartData: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; include?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ChartInclude; market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; }) => Array<{ underlyingPrice: number; expirationPnl?: number; currentPnl?: number; delta?: number; theta?: number; }>; default: not declared — Chart-ready output (spec §12.5).
