### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy#explainPosition

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

```typescript
export declare function explainPosition(position: Position, options?: ExplainPositionOptions): PositionExplanation;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (options)?: ExplainPositionOptions; default: not declared
- (options).market?: Partial<MarkToMarketInput>; default: not declared — Market for probability + greeks (spot/vol/rate/asOf); merges over the position's own market.
- (options).market.asOf?: string | number; default: not declared — Snapshot time. Epoch ms, or an ISO date/datetime string parsed at the boundary.
- (options).market.dividendYield?: number; default: not declared
- (options).market.expiry?: string; default: not declared
- (options).market.legVolatilities?: readonly (number | undefined)[]; default: not declared — Per-leg volatility OVERRIDES for this call (Preview P1), aligned to `position.legs`: leg `i`
prices at `legVolatilities[i]` when it is a number, else at its own `impliedVolatility`, else at
the position-level `volatility` (`volatilityShock` still adds on top). This is how a mark from
CURRENT contract quotes reaches a position whose legs were built with entry volatilities — the
position stays immutable, the call states the market. `assumptions.volatilitySource` reports
`'perCall'` when any override applied.
- (options).market.riskFreeRate?: number; default: not declared
- (options).market.spot?: number; default: not declared — Underlying spot price (WS3.2: renamed from `underlyingPrice` for workspace consistency).
- (options).market.volatility?: number; default: not declared — Position-level implied volatility. OPTIONAL: a position whose every option leg carries its own
`iv` prices entirely per-leg and needs no position vol. It is required (and validated positive)
only when at least one un-expired option leg has no per-leg `iv`; omitting it then throws.
- (options).market.volatilityShock?: number; default: not declared — Additive volatility shock (decimal) applied to EVERY effective leg volatility — the per-leg
`impliedVolatility` when a leg carries one, and the position-level `volatility` otherwise. This
is what makes a volatility scenario reach per-leg-IV legs; without it, shocking only
`volatility` is a silent no-op for legs that fix their own implied volatility.
- (options).underlyingLabel?: string; default: not declared — Underlying name for the prose (e.g. `'AAPL'`); default `'the underlying'`.
- (position): Position; default: not declared
- (position).assumptions: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PositionAssumptions; default: not declared — Position-construction assumptions (design law #3): whether the entry premiums were supplied by
the caller (`'user'`) or model-priced from a market (`'model'`), plus the contract multiplier.
- (position).chartData: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; include?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ChartInclude; market?: Partial<Omit<MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; }) => Array<{ underlyingPrice: number; expirationPnl?: number; currentPnl?: number; delta?: number; theta?: number; }>; default: not declared — Chart-ready output (spec §12.5). Current P&L / live Greeks need a market: per-call fields
merge over the construction market (R5), so a model-premium position charts with no `market`.
- (position).constructedAs?: string; default: not declared — PROVENANCE, not identity (dx §4.5): the named builder that constructed this position, absent
for raw `strategy(legs)`. Because positions are immutable this can never go stale — but a
rebuilt-after-tweak position has no name. For "what is this NOW?" use `classifyStrategy`.
- (position).legs: readonly Readonly<Leg>[]; default: not declared — The resolved legs — a frozen snapshot (deep-copied at construction, `Object.freeze`d per leg
and as an array). A Position is immutable by design: to tweak a strategy, edit your own leg
list and rebuild with `strategy(editedLegs, config)` — every downstream calculation is generic
over the legs, so the rebuilt position needs no named builder. Mutating this array throws
instead of silently diverging from `assumptions()`/cached results.
- (position).market?: Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumMarket>; default: not declared — The market this position was built with, if any — a frozen copy (R5), so mutating the caller's
market object later never silently retargets the position. `probability()`, `value()`,
`scenarioTable()`, and `chartData()` default to it; per-call fields merge over it.
- (position).market.asOf: string | number; default: not declared — Entry time (epoch ms or ISO). Each leg's entry `t = yearFraction(asOf, leg.expiry ?? market.expiry)`.
- (position).market.dividendYield?: number; default: not declared
- (position).market.expiry?: string; default: not declared — Default expiry for legs without their own `expiry` (single-expiry structures).
- (position).market.riskFreeRate: number; default: not declared
- (position).market.spot: number; default: not declared
- (position).market.volatility: number; default: not declared — Entry implied volatility (annualized decimal) for unpriced legs that carry no `impliedVolatility`
of their own — a leg's own volatility always wins, exactly as it does when `value()` marks it.
- (position).metrics: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffMetrics; default: not declared — Net debit/credit, max profit/loss, and breakevens. The expiration payoff is piecewise-linear, so
these are computed ANALYTICALLY from the kink set (every option strike plus every stock entry
price) and the tail slopes — never by sampling a coarse grid, which missed breakevens beyond the
last strike (e.g. a lone long stock, or a deep-ITM option) and ignored stock entry prices.
- (position).monteCarloProbability: (overrides: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloInput> & { seed: number; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloMetrics; default: not declared — Monte-Carlo probability metrics (spec §12.6): the simulated analogue of {@link probability}, for
cross-validation and path-dependent reads. Terminal lognormal paths give the probability of profit
and expected P&L (with a standard error); the probability of touching each breakeven is estimated
with the Brownian-bridge continuous-monitoring correction. Seeded and deterministic.
- (position).multiplier: number; default: not declared
- (position).netDebit: () => number; default: not declared — Net cash to enter (positive = debit, negative = credit).
- (position).payoff: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffResult; default: not declared — Expiration payoff metrics plus a chart-ready grid of points (spec §12.2). `prices` is an explicit
grid array or a `{ from, to, steps }` range; omit it to frame the strike-derived default window
(the same one a payoff diagram draws).
- (position).pnlAtExpiry: (underlyingPrice: number) => number; default: not declared — Expiration P&L at an underlying price.
- (position).premiumSource: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumSource; default: not declared — How the entry premiums were sourced: `'user'` (supplied) or `'model'` (priced from `market`).
- (position).premiumVolatilitySource?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumVolatilitySource; default: not declared — When modeled, which volatility priced the entries (`'leg'`, `'position'` or `'mixed'`).
- (position).probability: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMetrics; default: not declared — Probability & scenario metrics (spec §12.6): probability of profit, expected value, reward/risk,
and the probability of touching each breakeven — under an explicit, echoed lognormal model.
- (position).scenarioTable: (options?: { market?: Partial<Omit<MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; volatilityShocks?: number[]; daysForward?: number[]; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ScenarioTableResult; default: not declared — Scenario table (spec §12.6): mark-to-market P&L and Greeks across a grid of underlying prices,
additive vol shocks, and days forward — the standard "what-if" matrix for an options ticket.
- (position).value: (overrides?: Partial<MarkToMarketInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketResult; default: not declared — Mark-to-market value, P&L, per-leg and aggregate Greeks via BSM (spec §12.3).
- (position).whatIfCube: (options?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeOptions) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeResult; default: not declared — A what-if **cube**: the position marked over the full spot × vol-shock × days-forward grid, plus
the **optimal-exit surface** — for each (spot, vol) outcome, the day along the time axis that
optimizes P&L (`max-pnl` by default, or `min-pnl`). `scenarioTable` extended a dimension: it returns
a navigable cube (axes + row-major cells) with the reductions a trader wants, not a flat row list.

Every cell is a `value()` mark (time-aware, per-leg-IV, shock-through-to-leg-IV), so calendars and
per-leg volatilities behave identically. The optimal-exit surface is a CONDITIONAL what-if ("if the
underlying is here with this vol shock, which day marks best?"), not a path-dependent stopping rule.
See `docs/specs/what-if-cube.md`.
- return.aliases: string[]; default: not declared — Other payoff-identical names.
- return.assumptions: { classifier: 'structural-base-signature'; conventionsVersion: string; marketDependent: boolean; }; default: not declared — Applied conventions, echoed (Law 2 report grammar).
- return.assumptions.classifier: 'structural-base-signature'; default: not declared — How the name was derived — always the structural classifier (identity is never remembered).
- return.assumptions.conventionsVersion: string; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.marketDependent: boolean; default: not declared — Whether a usable market priced the greek/probability posture (false = payoff-only read).
- return.definedRisk: boolean; default: not declared
- return.diagnostics: { warnings: QuantWarning[]; }; default: not declared — Structured warnings; always present (possibly empty) — a missing market explains itself here.
- return.diagnostics.warnings: QuantWarning[]; default: not declared
- return.directionalBias: DirectionalBias; default: not declared
- return.economics: { breakevens: number[]; maxLoss: number | null; maxProfit: number | null; net: number; rewardToRisk: number | null; }; default: not declared
- return.economics.breakevens: number[]; default: not declared
- return.economics.maxLoss: number | null; default: not declared — Maximum loss (negative), or `null` when unbounded.
- return.economics.maxProfit: number | null; default: not declared — Maximum profit, or `null` when unbounded.
- return.economics.net: number; default: not declared — Net cash: `+` = debit paid, `−` = credit received (per contract).
- return.economics.rewardToRisk: number | null; default: not declared — `|maxProfit / maxLoss|`, or `null` when undefined (an unbounded side or a zero max loss).
- return.greeks?: { delta: number; gamma: number; rho: number; theta: number; vega: number; }; default: not declared
- return.greeks.delta: number; default: not declared
- return.greeks.gamma: number; default: not declared
- return.greeks.rho: number; default: not declared
- return.greeks.theta: number; default: not declared
- return.greeks.vega: number; default: not declared
- return.moveBias: MoveBias; default: not declared
- return.name: string; default: not declared — The classification, or `'custom'`.
- return.probability?: { expectedValue: number; probabilityOfProfit: number; }; default: not declared
- return.probability.expectedValue: number; default: not declared
- return.probability.probabilityOfProfit: number; default: not declared
- return.risks: string[]; default: not declared
- return.structure: string; default: not declared — Readable leg list, sorted by strike.
- return.summary: string; default: not declared — The prose narrative composing all of the above.
- return.timeBias?: TimeBias; default: not declared
- return.volatilityBias?: VolatilityBias; default: not declared — Present when a market is available.

- return.scenarioTable: (options?: { market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; volatilityShocks?: number[]; daysForward?: number[]; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ScenarioTableResult; default: not declared — Scenario table (spec §12.6): mark-to-market P&L and Greeks across a grid of underlying prices,
additive vol shocks, and days forward — the standard "what-if" matrix for an options ticket.
- return.value: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketResult; default: not declared — Mark-to-market value, P&L, per-leg and aggregate Greeks via BSM (spec §12.3).
- return.whatIfCube: (options?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeOptions) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeResult; default: not declared — A what-if **cube**: the position marked over the full spot × vol-shock × days-forward grid, plus
the **optimal-exit surface** — for each (spot, vol) outcome, the day along the time axis that
optimizes P&L (`max-pnl` by default, or `min-pnl`). `scenarioTable` extended a dimension: it returns
a navigable cube (axes + row-major cells) with the reductions a trader wants, not a flat row list.

Every cell is a `value()` mark (time-aware, per-leg-IV, shock-through-to-leg-IV), so calendars and
per-leg volatilities behave identically. The optimal-exit surface is a CONDITIONAL what-if ("if the
underlying is here with this vol shock, which day marks best?"), not a path-dependent stopping rule.
See `docs/specs/what-if-cube.md`.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy#inverseIronButterfly

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

```typescript
export declare const inverseIronButterfly: (input: s.IronButterflyInput, config?: PositionConfig) => Position;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (config)?: PositionConfig | undefined; default: not declared
- (config).expiry?: string; default: not declared — Position-level default expiry (`YYYY-MM-DD` → 16:00 ET, or a datetime) applied to every leg
that has no `expiry` of its own. Named builders route their input's `expiry` here. Precedence
per leg: `leg.expiry` > `expiry` > `market.expiry` (R4).
- (config).market?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumMarket; default: not declared — Market for model-priced entry premiums (required when `premiums: 'model'` and any leg omits its
premium) — AND the position's remembered market (R5): `probability()`, `monteCarloProbability()`,
`value()`, `scenarioTable()`, and `chartData()` use it as their default market, with per-call
fields merged over it. Results echo `marketSource: 'construction' | 'call' | 'merged'`.
- (config).multiplier?: number; default: not declared — Contract multiplier for option legs (default 100).
- (config).premiums?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumSource; default: not declared — Entry-premium source: `'user'` (from the leg inputs, default) or `'model'` (priced from `market`).
- (input): s.IronButterflyInput; default: not declared
- (input).body: number | { callPremium?: number; putPremium?: number; strike: number; }; default: not declared — ATM body (shared-strike rule): the strike sold twice, with per-type premiums. A bare strike
number is shorthand for `{ strike }` (R3).
- (input).body.callPremium?: number; default: not declared
- (input).body.putPremium?: number; default: not declared
- (input).body.strike: number; default: not declared
- (input).callWing: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').Role; default: not declared — Long call wing above the body.
- (input).expiry?: string; default: not declared — Expiry applied to every leg of this structure (`YYYY-MM-DD` → 16:00 ET, or a datetime).
- (input).putWing: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').Role; default: not declared — Long put wing below the body.
- (input).quantity?: number; default: not declared — Number of structures (default 1). Every leg scales by this.
- return.assumptions: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PositionAssumptions; default: not declared — Position-construction assumptions (design law #3): whether the entry premiums were supplied by
the caller (`'user'`) or model-priced from a market (`'model'`), plus the contract multiplier.
- return.chartData: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; include?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ChartInclude; market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; }) => Array<{ underlyingPrice: number; expirationPnl?: number; currentPnl?: number; delta?: number; theta?: number; }>; default: not declared — Chart-ready output (spec §12.5). Current P&L / live Greeks need a market: per-call fields
merge over the construction market (R5), so a model-premium position charts with no `market`.
- return.constructedAs?: string; default: not declared — PROVENANCE, not identity (dx §4.5): the named builder that constructed this position, absent
for raw `strategy(legs)`. Because positions are immutable this can never go stale — but a
rebuilt-after-tweak position has no name. For "what is this NOW?" use `classifyStrategy`.
- return.legs: readonly Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').Leg>[]; default: not declared — The resolved legs — a frozen snapshot (deep-copied at construction, `Object.freeze`d per leg
and as an array). A Position is immutable by design: to tweak a strategy, edit your own leg
list and rebuild with `strategy(editedLegs, config)` — every downstream calculation is generic
over the legs, so the rebuilt position needs no named builder. Mutating this array throws
instead of silently diverging from `assumptions()`/cached results.
- return.market?: Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumMarket>; default: not declared — The market this position was built with, if any — a frozen copy (R5), so mutating the caller's
market object later never silently retargets the position. `probability()`, `value()`,
`scenarioTable()`, and `chartData()` default to it; per-call fields merge over it.
- return.market.asOf: string | number; default: not declared — Entry time (epoch ms or ISO). Each leg's entry `t = yearFraction(asOf, leg.expiry ?? market.expiry)`.
- return.market.dividendYield?: number; default: not declared
- return.market.expiry?: string; default: not declared — Default expiry for legs without their own `expiry` (single-expiry structures).
- return.market.riskFreeRate: number; default: not declared
- return.market.spot: number; default: not declared
- return.market.volatility: number; default: not declared — Entry implied volatility (annualized decimal) for unpriced legs that carry no `impliedVolatility`
of their own — a leg's own volatility always wins, exactly as it does when `value()` marks it.
- return.metrics: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffMetrics; default: not declared — Net debit/credit, max profit/loss, and breakevens. The expiration payoff is piecewise-linear, so
these are computed ANALYTICALLY from the kink set (every option strike plus every stock entry
price) and the tail slopes — never by sampling a coarse grid, which missed breakevens beyond the
last strike (e.g. a lone long stock, or a deep-ITM option) and ignored stock entry prices.
- return.monteCarloProbability: (overrides: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloInput> & { seed: number; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloMetrics; default: not declared — Monte-Carlo probability metrics (spec §12.6): the simulated analogue of {@link probability}, for
cross-validation and path-dependent reads. Terminal lognormal paths give the probability of profit
and expected P&L (with a standard error); the probability of touching each breakeven is estimated
with the Brownian-bridge continuous-monitoring correction. Seeded and deterministic.
- return.multiplier: number; default: not declared
- return.netDebit: () => number; default: not declared — Net cash to enter (positive = debit, negative = credit).
- return.payoff: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffResult; default: not declared — Expiration payoff metrics plus a chart-ready grid of points (spec §12.2). `prices` is an explicit
grid array or a `{ from, to, steps }` range; omit it to frame the strike-derived default window
(the same one a payoff diagram draws).
- return.pnlAtExpiry: (underlyingPrice: number) => number; default: not declared — Expiration P&L at an underlying price.
- return.premiumSource: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumSource; default: not declared — How the entry premiums were sourced: `'user'` (supplied) or `'model'` (priced from `market`).
- return.premiumVolatilitySource?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumVolatilitySource; default: not declared — When modeled, which volatility priced the entries (`'leg'`, `'position'` or `'mixed'`).
- return.probability: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMetrics; default: not declared — Probability & scenario metrics (spec §12.6): probability of profit, expected value, reward/risk,
and the probability of touching each breakeven — under an explicit, echoed lognormal model.
- return.scenarioTable: (options?: { market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; volatilityShocks?: number[]; daysForward?: number[]; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ScenarioTableResult; default: not declared — Scenario table (spec §12.6): mark-to-market P&L and Greeks across a grid of underlying prices,

- return.whatIfCube: (options?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeOptions) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeResult; default: not declared — A what-if **cube**: the position marked over the full spot × vol-shock × days-forward grid, plus

- return.premiumSource: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumSource; default: not declared — How the entry premiums were sourced: `'user'` (supplied) or `'model'` (priced from `market`).
- return.premiumVolatilitySource?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumVolatilitySource; default: not declared — When modeled, which volatility priced the entries (`'leg'`, `'position'` or `'mixed'`).
- return.probability: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMetrics; default: not declared — Probability & scenario metrics (spec §12.6): probability of profit, expected value, reward/risk,
and the probability of touching each breakeven — under an explicit, echoed lognormal model.
- return.scenarioTable: (options?: { market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; volatilityShocks?: number[]; daysForward?: number[]; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ScenarioTableResult; default: not declared — Scenario table (spec §12.6): mark-to-market P&L and Greeks across a grid of underlying prices,
additive vol shocks, and days forward — the standard "what-if" matrix for an options ticket.
- return.value: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketResult; default: not declared — Mark-to-market value, P&L, per-leg and aggregate Greeks via BSM (spec §12.3).
- return.whatIfCube: (options?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeOptions) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeResult; default: not declared — A what-if **cube**: the position marked over the full spot × vol-shock × days-forward grid, plus
the **optimal-exit surface** — for each (spot, vol) outcome, the day along the time axis that
optimizes P&L (`max-pnl` by default, or `min-pnl`). `scenarioTable` extended a dimension: it returns
a navigable cube (axes + row-major cells) with the reductions a trader wants, not a flat row list.

Every cell is a `value()` mark (time-aware, per-leg-IV, shock-through-to-leg-IV), so calendars and
per-leg volatilities behave identically. The optimal-exit surface is a CONDITIONAL what-if ("if the
underlying is here with this vol shock, which day marks best?"), not a path-dependent stopping rule.
See `docs/specs/what-if-cube.md`.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy#ironButterfly

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

```typescript
export declare const ironButterfly: (input: s.IronButterflyInput, config?: PositionConfig) => Position;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (config)?: PositionConfig | undefined; default: not declared
- (config).expiry?: string; default: not declared — Position-level default expiry (`YYYY-MM-DD` → 16:00 ET, or a datetime) applied to every leg
that has no `expiry` of its own. Named builders route their input's `expiry` here. Precedence
per leg: `leg.expiry` > `expiry` > `market.expiry` (R4).
- (config).market?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumMarket; default: not declared — Market for model-priced entry premiums (required when `premiums: 'model'` and any leg omits its
premium) — AND the position's remembered market (R5): `probability()`, `monteCarloProbability()`,
`value()`, `scenarioTable()`, and `chartData()` use it as their default market, with per-call
fields merged over it. Results echo `marketSource: 'construction' | 'call' | 'merged'`.
- (config).multiplier?: number; default: not declared — Contract multiplier for option legs (default 100).
- (config).premiums?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumSource; default: not declared — Entry-premium source: `'user'` (from the leg inputs, default) or `'model'` (priced from `market`).
- (input): s.IronButterflyInput; default: not declared
- (input).body: number | { callPremium?: number; putPremium?: number; strike: number; }; default: not declared — ATM body (shared-strike rule): the strike sold twice, with per-type premiums. A bare strike
number is shorthand for `{ strike }` (R3).
- (input).body.callPremium?: number; default: not declared
- (input).body.putPremium?: number; default: not declared
- (input).body.strike: number; default: not declared
- (input).callWing: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').Role; default: not declared — Long call wing above the body.
- (input).expiry?: string; default: not declared — Expiry applied to every leg of this structure (`YYYY-MM-DD` → 16:00 ET, or a datetime).
- (input).putWing: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').Role; default: not declared — Long put wing below the body.
- (input).quantity?: number; default: not declared — Number of structures (default 1). Every leg scales by this.
- return.assumptions: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PositionAssumptions; default: not declared — Position-construction assumptions (design law #3): whether the entry premiums were supplied by
the caller (`'user'`) or model-priced from a market (`'model'`), plus the contract multiplier.
- return.chartData: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; include?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ChartInclude; market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; }) => Array<{ underlyingPrice: number; expirationPnl?: number; currentPnl?: number; delta?: number; theta?: number; }>; default: not declared — Chart-ready output (spec §12.5). Current P&L / live Greeks need a market: per-call fields
merge over the construction market (R5), so a model-premium position charts with no `market`.
- return.constructedAs?: string; default: not declared — PROVENANCE, not identity (dx §4.5): the named builder that constructed this position, absent
for raw `strategy(legs)`. Because positions are immutable this can never go stale — but a
rebuilt-after-tweak position has no name. For "what is this NOW?" use `classifyStrategy`.
- return.legs: readonly Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').Leg>[]; default: not declared — The resolved legs — a frozen snapshot (deep-copied at construction, `Object.freeze`d per leg
and as an array). A Position is immutable by design: to tweak a strategy, edit your own leg
list and rebuild with `strategy(editedLegs, config)` — every downstream calculation is generic
over the legs, so the rebuilt position needs no named builder. Mutating this array throws
instead of silently diverging from `assumptions()`/cached results.
- return.market?: Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumMarket>; default: not declared — The market this position was built with, if any — a frozen copy (R5), so mutating the caller's
market object later never silently retargets the position. `probability()`, `value()`,
`scenarioTable()`, and `chartData()` default to it; per-call fields merge over it.
- return.market.asOf: string | number; default: not declared — Entry time (epoch ms or ISO). Each leg's entry `t = yearFraction(asOf, leg.expiry ?? market.expiry)`.
- return.market.dividendYield?: number; default: not declared
- return.market.expiry?: string; default: not declared — Default expiry for legs without their own `expiry` (single-expiry structures).
- return.market.riskFreeRate: number; default: not declared
- return.market.spot: number; default: not declared
- return.market.volatility: number; default: not declared — Entry implied volatility (annualized decimal) for unpriced legs that carry no `impliedVolatility`
of their own — a leg's own volatility always wins, exactly as it does when `value()` marks it.
- return.metrics: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffMetrics; default: not declared — Net debit/credit, max profit/loss, and breakevens. The expiration payoff is piecewise-linear, so
these are computed ANALYTICALLY from the kink set (every option strike plus every stock entry
price) and the tail slopes — never by sampling a coarse grid, which missed breakevens beyond the
last strike (e.g. a lone long stock, or a deep-ITM option) and ignored stock entry prices.
- return.monteCarloProbability: (overrides: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloInput> & { seed: number; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloMetrics; default: not declared — Monte-Carlo probability metrics (spec §12.6): the simulated analogue of {@link probability}, for
cross-validation and path-dependent reads. Terminal lognormal paths give the probability of profit
and expected P&L (with a standard error); the probability of touching each breakeven is estimated
with the Brownian-bridge continuous-monitoring correction. Seeded and deterministic.
- return.multiplier: number; default: not declared
- return.netDebit: () => number; default: not declared — Net cash to enter (positive = debit, negative = credit).
- return.payoff: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffResult; default: not declared — Expiration payoff metrics plus a chart-ready grid of points (spec §12.2). `prices` is an explicit
grid array or a `{ from, to, steps }` range; omit it to frame the strike-derived default window
(the same one a payoff diagram draws).
- return.pnlAtExpiry: (underlyingPrice: number) => number; default: not declared — Expiration P&L at an underlying price.
- return.premiumSource: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumSource; default: not declared — How the entry premiums were sourced: `'user'` (supplied) or `'model'` (priced from `market`).
- return.premiumVolatilitySource?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumVolatilitySource; default: not declared — When modeled, which volatility priced the entries (`'leg'`, `'position'` or `'mixed'`).
- return.probability: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMetrics; default: not declared — Probability & scenario metrics (spec §12.6): probability of profit, expected value, reward/risk,
and the probability of touching each breakeven — under an explicit, echoed lognormal model.
- return.scenarioTable: (options?: { market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; volatilityShocks?: number[]; daysForward?: number[]; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ScenarioTableResult; default: not declared — Scenario table (spec §12.6): mark-to-market P&L and Greeks across a grid of underlying prices,

- return.whatIfCube: (options?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeOptions) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeResult; default: not declared — A what-if **cube**: the position marked over the full spot × vol-shock × days-forward grid, plus

- return.payoff: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffResult; default: not declared — Expiration payoff metrics plus a chart-ready grid of points (spec §12.2). `prices` is an explicit
grid array or a `{ from, to, steps }` range; omit it to frame the strike-derived default window
(the same one a payoff diagram draws).
- return.pnlAtExpiry: (underlyingPrice: number) => number; default: not declared — Expiration P&L at an underlying price.
- return.premiumSource: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumSource; default: not declared — How the entry premiums were sourced: `'user'` (supplied) or `'model'` (priced from `market`).
- return.premiumVolatilitySource?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumVolatilitySource; default: not declared — When modeled, which volatility priced the entries (`'leg'`, `'position'` or `'mixed'`).
- return.probability: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMetrics; default: not declared — Probability & scenario metrics (spec §12.6): probability of profit, expected value, reward/risk,
and the probability of touching each breakeven — under an explicit, echoed lognormal model.
- return.scenarioTable: (options?: { market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; volatilityShocks?: number[]; daysForward?: number[]; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ScenarioTableResult; default: not declared — Scenario table (spec §12.6): mark-to-market P&L and Greeks across a grid of underlying prices,
additive vol shocks, and days forward — the standard "what-if" matrix for an options ticket.
- return.value: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketResult; default: not declared — Mark-to-market value, P&L, per-leg and aggregate Greeks via BSM (spec §12.3).
- return.whatIfCube: (options?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeOptions) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeResult; default: not declared — A what-if **cube**: the position marked over the full spot × vol-shock × days-forward grid, plus
the **optimal-exit surface** — for each (spot, vol) outcome, the day along the time axis that
optimizes P&L (`max-pnl` by default, or `min-pnl`). `scenarioTable` extended a dimension: it returns
a navigable cube (axes + row-major cells) with the reductions a trader wants, not a flat row list.

Every cell is a `value()` mark (time-aware, per-leg-IV, shock-through-to-leg-IV), so calendars and
per-leg volatilities behave identically. The optimal-exit surface is a CONDITIONAL what-if ("if the
underlying is here with this vol shock, which day marks best?"), not a path-dependent stopping rule.
See `docs/specs/what-if-cube.md`.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy#legs

Kind: value; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Plain leg records for custom strategies. No direction or size is inferred.

```typescript
export declare const legs: { readonly call: (input: OptionLegInput) => OptionLegRow; readonly put: (input: OptionLegInput) => OptionLegRow; readonly stock: (input: StockLegInput) => StockLeg; };
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- call: (input: OptionLegInput) => OptionLegRow; default: not declared — Build a call leg. Signed quantity is in contracts; premium is per share.
- call().return.expiry?: string; default: not declared — Optional per-leg expiry (`YYYY-MM-DD` → 16:00 ET, or a full datetime). When omitted the leg uses
the position-level expiry supplied to `value()`. Set it for multi-expiry structures (calendars,
diagonals, double diagonals) so each leg is priced at its own time-to-expiry.
- call().return.impliedVolatility?: number; default: not declared — Optional per-leg implied volatility (decimal, e.g. `0.28`). When set, `value()`/`chartData()`/
`scenarioTable()` price this leg at its own IV instead of the position-level `vol` — so a real
chain (four distinct IVs on an iron condor) marks correctly. When omitted, the leg falls back to
the position-level `vol`. The result's `assumptions.volatilitySource` reports which was used.
- call().return.kind: 'call' | 'put'; default: not declared
- call().return.premium?: number; default: not declared
- call().return.price?: undefined; default: not declared — Never on an option row (a stock row's entry price).
- call().return.quantity: number; default: not declared — Signed contracts: positive = long, negative = short.
- call().return.strike: number; default: not declared
- call(input): OptionLegInput; default: not declared
- call(input).expiry?: string; default: not declared — Per-leg expiry: a YYYY-MM-DD label (16:00 ET) or zoned ISO datetime.
- call(input).impliedVolatility?: number; default: not declared — Positive per-leg implied volatility, as an annualized decimal (0.20 = 20%).
- call(input).premium?: number | undefined; default: not declared — Entry premium per share. Omit it (or pass `undefined`) and supply `{ premiums: 'model', market }`
on the position config to have it priced from the market. Accepts `undefined` explicitly so
builders can forward an optional slot premium without a conditional spread.
- call(input).quantity: number; default: not declared — Signed contracts: positive = long, negative = short. Required, finite and nonzero.
- call(input).strike: number; default: not declared — Positive strike price per share.
- put: (input: OptionLegInput) => OptionLegRow; default: not declared — Build a put leg. Signed quantity is in contracts; premium is per share.
- put().return.expiry?: string; default: not declared — Optional per-leg expiry (`YYYY-MM-DD` → 16:00 ET, or a full datetime). When omitted the leg uses
the position-level expiry supplied to `value()`. Set it for multi-expiry structures (calendars,
diagonals, double diagonals) so each leg is priced at its own time-to-expiry.
- put().return.impliedVolatility?: number; default: not declared — Optional per-leg implied volatility (decimal, e.g. `0.28`). When set, `value()`/`chartData()`/
`scenarioTable()` price this leg at its own IV instead of the position-level `vol` — so a real
chain (four distinct IVs on an iron condor) marks correctly. When omitted, the leg falls back to
the position-level `vol`. The result's `assumptions.volatilitySource` reports which was used.
- put().return.kind: 'call' | 'put'; default: not declared
- put().return.premium?: number; default: not declared
- put().return.price?: undefined; default: not declared — Never on an option row (a stock row's entry price).
- put().return.quantity: number; default: not declared — Signed contracts: positive = long, negative = short.
- put().return.strike: number; default: not declared
- put(input): OptionLegInput; default: not declared
- put(input).expiry?: string; default: not declared — Per-leg expiry: a YYYY-MM-DD label (16:00 ET) or zoned ISO datetime.
- put(input).impliedVolatility?: number; default: not declared — Positive per-leg implied volatility, as an annualized decimal (0.20 = 20%).
- put(input).premium?: number | undefined; default: not declared — Entry premium per share. Omit it (or pass `undefined`) and supply `{ premiums: 'model', market }`
on the position config to have it priced from the market. Accepts `undefined` explicitly so
builders can forward an optional slot premium without a conditional spread.
- put(input).quantity: number; default: not declared — Signed contracts: positive = long, negative = short. Required, finite and nonzero.
- put(input).strike: number; default: not declared — Positive strike price per share.
- stock: (input: StockLegInput) => StockLeg; default: not declared — Build a stock leg. Signed quantity is in shares; price is the entry price per share.
- stock().return.expiry?: undefined; default: not declared
- stock().return.impliedVolatility?: undefined; default: not declared
- stock().return.kind: 'stock'; default: not declared
- stock().return.premium?: undefined; default: not declared
- stock().return.price: number; default: not declared — Entry price per share.
- stock().return.quantity: number; default: not declared — Signed shares: positive = long, negative = short.
- stock().return.strike?: undefined; default: not declared — Never on a stock row (typed so a union read narrows to `undefined`, not to a fake 0).
- stock(input): StockLegInput; default: not declared
- stock(input).price: number; default: not declared — Entry price per share.
- stock(input).quantity: number; default: not declared — Signed shares: positive = long, negative = short. Not scaled by the option multiplier.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy#longCall

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

```typescript
export declare const longCall: (input: s.SingleLegInput, config?: PositionConfig) => Position;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (config)?: PositionConfig | undefined; default: not declared
- (config).expiry?: string; default: not declared — Position-level default expiry (`YYYY-MM-DD` → 16:00 ET, or a datetime) applied to every leg
that has no `expiry` of its own. Named builders route their input's `expiry` here. Precedence
per leg: `leg.expiry` > `expiry` > `market.expiry` (R4).
- (config).market?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumMarket; default: not declared — Market for model-priced entry premiums (required when `premiums: 'model'` and any leg omits its
premium) — AND the position's remembered market (R5): `probability()`, `monteCarloProbability()`,
`value()`, `scenarioTable()`, and `chartData()` use it as their default market, with per-call
fields merged over it. Results echo `marketSource: 'construction' | 'call' | 'merged'`.
- (config).multiplier?: number; default: not declared — Contract multiplier for option legs (default 100).
- (config).premiums?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumSource; default: not declared — Entry-premium source: `'user'` (from the leg inputs, default) or `'model'` (priced from `market`).
- (input): s.SingleLegInput; default: not declared
- (input).expiry?: string; default: not declared — Expiry applied to every leg of this structure (`YYYY-MM-DD` → 16:00 ET, or a datetime).
- (input).premium?: number; default: not declared
- (input).quantity?: number; default: not declared — Number of structures (default 1). Every leg scales by this.
- (input).strike: number; default: not declared
- return.assumptions: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PositionAssumptions; default: not declared — Position-construction assumptions (design law #3): whether the entry premiums were supplied by
the caller (`'user'`) or model-priced from a market (`'model'`), plus the contract multiplier.
- return.chartData: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; include?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ChartInclude; market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; }) => Array<{ underlyingPrice: number; expirationPnl?: number; currentPnl?: number; delta?: number; theta?: number; }>; default: not declared — Chart-ready output (spec §12.5). Current P&L / live Greeks need a market: per-call fields
merge over the construction market (R5), so a model-premium position charts with no `market`.
- return.constructedAs?: string; default: not declared — PROVENANCE, not identity (dx §4.5): the named builder that constructed this position, absent
for raw `strategy(legs)`. Because positions are immutable this can never go stale — but a
rebuilt-after-tweak position has no name. For "what is this NOW?" use `classifyStrategy`.
- return.legs: readonly Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').Leg>[]; default: not declared — The resolved legs — a frozen snapshot (deep-copied at construction, `Object.freeze`d per leg
and as an array). A Position is immutable by design: to tweak a strategy, edit your own leg
list and rebuild with `strategy(editedLegs, config)` — every downstream calculation is generic
over the legs, so the rebuilt position needs no named builder. Mutating this array throws
instead of silently diverging from `assumptions()`/cached results.
- return.market?: Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumMarket>; default: not declared — The market this position was built with, if any — a frozen copy (R5), so mutating the caller's
market object later never silently retargets the position. `probability()`, `value()`,
`scenarioTable()`, and `chartData()` default to it; per-call fields merge over it.
- return.market.asOf: string | number; default: not declared — Entry time (epoch ms or ISO). Each leg's entry `t = yearFraction(asOf, leg.expiry ?? market.expiry)`.
- return.market.dividendYield?: number; default: not declared
- return.market.expiry?: string; default: not declared — Default expiry for legs without their own `expiry` (single-expiry structures).
- return.market.riskFreeRate: number; default: not declared
- return.market.spot: number; default: not declared
- return.market.volatility: number; default: not declared — Entry implied volatility (annualized decimal) for unpriced legs that carry no `impliedVolatility`
of their own — a leg's own volatility always wins, exactly as it does when `value()` marks it.
- return.metrics: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffMetrics; default: not declared — Net debit/credit, max profit/loss, and breakevens. The expiration payoff is piecewise-linear, so
these are computed ANALYTICALLY from the kink set (every option strike plus every stock entry
price) and the tail slopes — never by sampling a coarse grid, which missed breakevens beyond the
last strike (e.g. a lone long stock, or a deep-ITM option) and ignored stock entry prices.
- return.monteCarloProbability: (overrides: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloInput> & { seed: number; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloMetrics; default: not declared — Monte-Carlo probability metrics (spec §12.6): the simulated analogue of {@link probability}, for
cross-validation and path-dependent reads. Terminal lognormal paths give the probability of profit
and expected P&L (with a standard error); the probability of touching each breakeven is estimated
with the Brownian-bridge continuous-monitoring correction. Seeded and deterministic.
- return.multiplier: number; default: not declared
- return.netDebit: () => number; default: not declared — Net cash to enter (positive = debit, negative = credit).
- return.payoff: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffResult; default: not declared — Expiration payoff metrics plus a chart-ready grid of points (spec §12.2). `prices` is an explicit

- return.pnlAtExpiry: (underlyingPrice: number) => number; default: not declared — Expiration P&L at an underlying price.
- return.premiumSource: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumSource; default: not declared — How the entry premiums were sourced: `'user'` (supplied) or `'model'` (priced from `market`).
- return.premiumVolatilitySource?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumVolatilitySource; default: not declared — When modeled, which volatility priced the entries (`'leg'`, `'position'` or `'mixed'`).
- return.probability: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMetrics; default: not declared — Probability & scenario metrics (spec §12.6): probability of profit, expected value, reward/risk,
and the probability of touching each breakeven — under an explicit, echoed lognormal model.
- return.scenarioTable: (options?: { market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; volatilityShocks?: number[]; daysForward?: number[]; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ScenarioTableResult; default: not declared — Scenario table (spec §12.6): mark-to-market P&L and Greeks across a grid of underlying prices,

- return.value: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketResult; default: not declared — Mark-to-market value, P&L, per-leg and aggregate Greeks via BSM (spec §12.3).
- return.whatIfCube: (options?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeOptions) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeResult; default: not declared — A what-if **cube**: the position marked over the full spot × vol-shock × days-forward grid, plus


Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (config)?: PositionConfig | undefined; default: not declared
- (config).expiry?: string; default: not declared — Position-level default expiry (`YYYY-MM-DD` → 16:00 ET, or a datetime) applied to every leg
that has no `expiry` of its own. Named builders route their input's `expiry` here. Precedence
per leg: `leg.expiry` > `expiry` > `market.expiry` (R4).
- (config).market?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumMarket; default: not declared — Market for model-priced entry premiums (required when `premiums: 'model'` and any leg omits its
premium) — AND the position's remembered market (R5): `probability()`, `monteCarloProbability()`,
`value()`, `scenarioTable()`, and `chartData()` use it as their default market, with per-call
fields merged over it. Results echo `marketSource: 'construction' | 'call' | 'merged'`.
- (config).multiplier?: number; default: not declared — Contract multiplier for option legs (default 100).
- (config).premiums?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumSource; default: not declared — Entry-premium source: `'user'` (from the leg inputs, default) or `'model'` (priced from `market`).
- (input): s.CondorInput; default: not declared
- (input).expiry?: string; default: not declared — Expiry applied to every leg of this structure (`YYYY-MM-DD` → 16:00 ET, or a datetime).
- (input).k1: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').Role; default: not declared
- (input).k2: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').Role; default: not declared
- (input).k3: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').Role; default: not declared
- (input).k4: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').Role; default: not declared
- (input).quantity?: number; default: not declared — Number of structures (default 1). Every leg scales by this.
- return.assumptions: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PositionAssumptions; default: not declared — Position-construction assumptions (design law #3): whether the entry premiums were supplied by
the caller (`'user'`) or model-priced from a market (`'model'`), plus the contract multiplier.
- return.chartData: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; include?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ChartInclude; market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; }) => Array<{ underlyingPrice: number; expirationPnl?: number; currentPnl?: number; delta?: number; theta?: number; }>; default: not declared — Chart-ready output (spec §12.5). Current P&L / live Greeks need a market: per-call fields
merge over the construction market (R5), so a model-premium position charts with no `market`.
- return.constructedAs?: string; default: not declared — PROVENANCE, not identity (dx §4.5): the named builder that constructed this position, absent
for raw `strategy(legs)`. Because positions are immutable this can never go stale — but a
rebuilt-after-tweak position has no name. For "what is this NOW?" use `classifyStrategy`.
- return.legs: readonly Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').Leg>[]; default: not declared — The resolved legs — a frozen snapshot (deep-copied at construction, `Object.freeze`d per leg
and as an array). A Position is immutable by design: to tweak a strategy, edit your own leg
list and rebuild with `strategy(editedLegs, config)` — every downstream calculation is generic
over the legs, so the rebuilt position needs no named builder. Mutating this array throws
instead of silently diverging from `assumptions()`/cached results.
- return.market?: Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumMarket>; default: not declared — The market this position was built with, if any — a frozen copy (R5), so mutating the caller's
market object later never silently retargets the position. `probability()`, `value()`,
`scenarioTable()`, and `chartData()` default to it; per-call fields merge over it.
- return.market.asOf: string | number; default: not declared — Entry time (epoch ms or ISO). Each leg's entry `t = yearFraction(asOf, leg.expiry ?? market.expiry)`.
- return.market.dividendYield?: number; default: not declared
- return.market.expiry?: string; default: not declared — Default expiry for legs without their own `expiry` (single-expiry structures).
- return.market.riskFreeRate: number; default: not declared
- return.market.spot: number; default: not declared
- return.market.volatility: number; default: not declared — Entry implied volatility (annualized decimal) for unpriced legs that carry no `impliedVolatility`
of their own — a leg's own volatility always wins, exactly as it does when `value()` marks it.
- return.metrics: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffMetrics; default: not declared — Net debit/credit, max profit/loss, and breakevens. The expiration payoff is piecewise-linear, so
these are computed ANALYTICALLY from the kink set (every option strike plus every stock entry
price) and the tail slopes — never by sampling a coarse grid, which missed breakevens beyond the
last strike (e.g. a lone long stock, or a deep-ITM option) and ignored stock entry prices.
- return.monteCarloProbability: (overrides: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloInput> & { seed: number; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloMetrics; default: not declared — Monte-Carlo probability metrics (spec §12.6): the simulated analogue of {@link probability}, for
cross-validation and path-dependent reads. Terminal lognormal paths give the probability of profit
and expected P&L (with a standard error); the probability of touching each breakeven is estimated
with the Brownian-bridge continuous-monitoring correction. Seeded and deterministic.
- return.multiplier: number; default: not declared
- return.netDebit: () => number; default: not declared — Net cash to enter (positive = debit, negative = credit).
- return.payoff: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffResult; default: not declared — Expiration payoff metrics plus a chart-ready grid of points (spec §12.2). `prices` is an explicit
grid array or a `{ from, to, steps }` range; omit it to frame the strike-derived default window
(the same one a payoff diagram draws).
- return.pnlAtExpiry: (underlyingPrice: number) => number; default: not declared — Expiration P&L at an underlying price.
- return.premiumSource: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumSource; default: not declared — How the entry premiums were sourced: `'user'` (supplied) or `'model'` (priced from `market`).
- return.premiumVolatilitySource?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumVolatilitySource; default: not declared — When modeled, which volatility priced the entries (`'leg'`, `'position'` or `'mixed'`).
- return.probability: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMetrics; default: not declared — Probability & scenario metrics (spec §12.6): probability of profit, expected value, reward/risk,
and the probability of touching each breakeven — under an explicit, echoed lognormal model.
- return.scenarioTable: (options?: { market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; volatilityShocks?: number[]; daysForward?: number[]; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ScenarioTableResult; default: not declared — Scenario table (spec §12.6): mark-to-market P&L and Greeks across a grid of underlying prices,
additive vol shocks, and days forward — the standard "what-if" matrix for an options ticket.
- return.value: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketResult; default: not declared — Mark-to-market value, P&L, per-leg and aggregate Greeks via BSM (spec §12.3).
- return.whatIfCube: (options?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeOptions) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeResult; default: not declared — A what-if **cube**: the position marked over the full spot × vol-shock × days-forward grid, plus
the **optimal-exit surface** — for each (spot, vol) outcome, the day along the time axis that
optimizes P&L (`max-pnl` by default, or `min-pnl`). `scenarioTable` extended a dimension: it returns
a navigable cube (axes + row-major cells) with the reductions a trader wants, not a flat row list.

Every cell is a `value()` mark (time-aware, per-leg-IV, shock-through-to-leg-IV), so calendars and
per-leg volatilities behave identically. The optimal-exit surface is a CONDITIONAL what-if ("if the
underlying is here with this vol shock, which day marks best?"), not a path-dependent stopping rule.
See `docs/specs/what-if-cube.md`.

that has no `expiry` of its own. Named builders route their input's `expiry` here. Precedence
per leg: `leg.expiry` > `expiry` > `market.expiry` (R4).
- (config).market?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumMarket; default: not declared — Market for model-priced entry premiums (required when `premiums: 'model'` and any leg omits its
premium) — AND the position's remembered market (R5): `probability()`, `monteCarloProbability()`,
`value()`, `scenarioTable()`, and `chartData()` use it as their default market, with per-call
fields merged over it. Results echo `marketSource: 'construction' | 'call' | 'merged'`.
- (config).multiplier?: number; default: not declared — Contract multiplier for option legs (default 100).
- (config).premiums?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumSource; default: not declared — Entry-premium source: `'user'` (from the leg inputs, default) or `'model'` (priced from `market`).
- (input): s.LadderInput; default: not declared
- (input).expiry?: string; default: not declared — Expiry applied to every leg of this structure (`YYYY-MM-DD` → 16:00 ET, or a datetime).
- (input).lower: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').Role; default: not declared
- (input).middle: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').Role; default: not declared
- (input).quantity?: number; default: not declared — Number of structures (default 1). Every leg scales by this.
- (input).upper: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').Role; default: not declared
- return.assumptions: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PositionAssumptions; default: not declared — Position-construction assumptions (design law #3): whether the entry premiums were supplied by
the caller (`'user'`) or model-priced from a market (`'model'`), plus the contract multiplier.
- return.chartData: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; include?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ChartInclude; market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; }) => Array<{ underlyingPrice: number; expirationPnl?: number; currentPnl?: number; delta?: number; theta?: number; }>; default: not declared — Chart-ready output (spec §12.5). Current P&L / live Greeks need a market: per-call fields
merge over the construction market (R5), so a model-premium position charts with no `market`.
- return.constructedAs?: string; default: not declared — PROVENANCE, not identity (dx §4.5): the named builder that constructed this position, absent
for raw `strategy(legs)`. Because positions are immutable this can never go stale — but a
rebuilt-after-tweak position has no name. For "what is this NOW?" use `classifyStrategy`.
- return.legs: readonly Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').Leg>[]; default: not declared — The resolved legs — a frozen snapshot (deep-copied at construction, `Object.freeze`d per leg
and as an array). A Position is immutable by design: to tweak a strategy, edit your own leg
list and rebuild with `strategy(editedLegs, config)` — every downstream calculation is generic
over the legs, so the rebuilt position needs no named builder. Mutating this array throws
instead of silently diverging from `assumptions()`/cached results.
- return.market?: Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumMarket>; default: not declared — The market this position was built with, if any — a frozen copy (R5), so mutating the caller's
market object later never silently retargets the position. `probability()`, `value()`,
`scenarioTable()`, and `chartData()` default to it; per-call fields merge over it.
- return.market.asOf: string | number; default: not declared — Entry time (epoch ms or ISO). Each leg's entry `t = yearFraction(asOf, leg.expiry ?? market.expiry)`.
- return.market.dividendYield?: number; default: not declared
- return.market.expiry?: string; default: not declared — Default expiry for legs without their own `expiry` (single-expiry structures).
- return.market.riskFreeRate: number; default: not declared
- return.market.spot: number; default: not declared
- return.market.volatility: number; default: not declared — Entry implied volatility (annualized decimal) for unpriced legs that carry no `impliedVolatility`
of their own — a leg's own volatility always wins, exactly as it does when `value()` marks it.
- return.metrics: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffMetrics; default: not declared — Net debit/credit, max profit/loss, and breakevens. The expiration payoff is piecewise-linear, so
these are computed ANALYTICALLY from the kink set (every option strike plus every stock entry
price) and the tail slopes — never by sampling a coarse grid, which missed breakevens beyond the
last strike (e.g. a lone long stock, or a deep-ITM option) and ignored stock entry prices.
- return.monteCarloProbability: (overrides: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloInput> & { seed: number; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloMetrics; default: not declared — Monte-Carlo probability metrics (spec §12.6): the simulated analogue of {@link probability}, for
cross-validation and path-dependent reads. Terminal lognormal paths give the probability of profit
and expected P&L (with a standard error); the probability of touching each breakeven is estimated
with the Brownian-bridge continuous-monitoring correction. Seeded and deterministic.
- return.multiplier: number; default: not declared
- return.netDebit: () => number; default: not declared — Net cash to enter (positive = debit, negative = credit).
- return.payoff: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffResult; default: not declared — Expiration payoff metrics plus a chart-ready grid of points (spec §12.2). `prices` is an explicit
grid array or a `{ from, to, steps }` range; omit it to frame the strike-derived default window
(the same one a payoff diagram draws).
- return.pnlAtExpiry: (underlyingPrice: number) => number; default: not declared — Expiration P&L at an underlying price.
- return.premiumSource: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumSource; default: not declared — How the entry premiums were sourced: `'user'` (supplied) or `'model'` (priced from `market`).
- return.premiumVolatilitySource?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumVolatilitySource; default: not declared — When modeled, which volatility priced the entries (`'leg'`, `'position'` or `'mixed'`).
- return.probability: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMetrics; default: not declared — Probability & scenario metrics (spec §12.6): probability of profit, expected value, reward/risk,
and the probability of touching each breakeven — under an explicit, echoed lognormal model.
- return.scenarioTable: (options?: { market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; volatilityShocks?: number[]; daysForward?: number[]; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ScenarioTableResult; default: not declared — Scenario table (spec §12.6): mark-to-market P&L and Greeks across a grid of underlying prices,
additive vol shocks, and days forward — the standard "what-if" matrix for an options ticket.
- return.value: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketResult; default: not declared — Mark-to-market value, P&L, per-leg and aggregate Greeks via BSM (spec §12.3).
- return.whatIfCube: (options?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeOptions) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeResult; default: not declared — A what-if **cube**: the position marked over the full spot × vol-shock × days-forward grid, plus
the **optimal-exit surface** — for each (spot, vol) outcome, the day along the time axis that
optimizes P&L (`max-pnl` by default, or `min-pnl`). `scenarioTable` extended a dimension: it returns
a navigable cube (axes + row-major cells) with the reductions a trader wants, not a flat row list.

Every cell is a `value()` mark (time-aware, per-leg-IV, shock-through-to-leg-IV), so calendars and
per-leg volatilities behave identically. The optimal-exit surface is a CONDITIONAL what-if ("if the
underlying is here with this vol shock, which day marks best?"), not a path-dependent stopping rule.
See `docs/specs/what-if-cube.md`.
