### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy#optimizeStrategy

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Search structures × strikes × expiries for the best trade under a thesis. Reuses `scanStrategies` per
expiry, re-scores each candidate under the thesis density, and ranks across all expiries. See the spec.

```typescript
export declare function optimizeStrategy(options: OptimizeStrategyOptions): OptimizeStrategyResult;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (options): OptimizeStrategyOptions; default: not declared
- (options).asOf: string | number; default: not declared — Valuation instant — epoch milliseconds or a zoned ISO datetime, the ONE valuation-instant
grammar shared with `scanStrategies`, `Position.probability()` and the what-if cube. A bare
date is refused everywhere a position is priced: the time of day is the answer for a 0DTE.
- (options).dividendYield?: number; default: not declared
- (options).expiries: OptimizerExpiry[]; default: not declared — The multi-expiry search space (≥ 1 expiry).
- (options).gridPoints?: number; default: not declared — Integration resolution for the thesis metrics (default 801).
- (options).maxRisk?: number; default: not declared — Keep only candidates whose max loss ≤ this (per contract, 100×).
- (options).maxWidth?: number; default: not declared
- (options).minProbabilityOfProfit?: number; default: not declared — Keep only candidates whose MARKET-implied PoP ≥ this.
- (options).minThesisProbabilityOfProfit?: number; default: not declared — Keep only candidates whose THESIS PoP ≥ this.
- (options).objective?: OptimizerObjective; default: not declared — Ranking objective (default `'thesisExpectedValuePerRisk'`).
- (options).riskFreeRate: number; default: not declared
- (options).sizing?: OptimizerSizingOptions; default: not declared — Opt-in Kelly sizing. When set, each candidate gains a `kelly` verdict; omit for no Kelly work.
- (options).smile?: (strike: number) => number; default: not declared — Default pricing smile (takes precedence over `volatility` for pricing).
- (options).spot: number; default: not declared
- (options).structures?: ScanStructure[]; default: not declared — Which structures to enumerate (default: all the scanner's).
- (options).thesis: OptimizerThesis; default: not declared
- (options).top?: number; default: not declared — Top-N across all expiries (default 25).
- (options).volatility?: number; default: not declared — Default pricing volatility for missing premiums + the scanner's market-implied metrics.
- return.assumptions: { conventionsVersion: string; expiries: number; gridPoints: number; objective: OptimizerObjective; }; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.conventionsVersion: string; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.expiries: number; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.gridPoints: number; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.objective: OptimizerObjective; default: not declared
- return.candidates: OptimizedStrategy[]; default: not declared — Top-N candidates across all expiries, ranked by `objective` (descending).
- return.diagnostics: Diagnostics; default: not declared
- return.thesis: { drift?: number; median: 'target' | 'drift'; targetPrice?: number; volatility: number; }; default: not declared
- return.thesis.drift?: number; default: not declared
- return.thesis.median: 'drift' | 'target'; default: not declared
- return.thesis.targetPrice?: number; default: not declared
- return.thesis.volatility: number; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy#payoffSvg

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Render a {@link Position}'s payoff diagram as a self-contained `<svg>` string. See the spec.

```typescript
export declare function payoffSvg(position: Position, options?: PayoffSvgOptions): string;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (options)?: PayoffSvgOptions; default: not declared
- (options).height?: number; default: not declared — Height in px (default 360).
- (options).includeCurrentPnl?: boolean; default: not declared — Also draw the CURRENT (pre-expiry) P&L curve (dashed); needs a market (or the position's own).
- (options).market?: Partial<Omit<MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; default: not declared
- (options).market.asOf?: string | number; default: not declared — Snapshot time. Epoch ms, or an ISO date/datetime string parsed at the boundary.
- (options).market.dividendYield?: number; default: not declared
- (options).market.expiry?: string; default: not declared
- (options).market.legVolatilities?: readonly (number | undefined)[]; default: not declared — Per-leg volatility OVERRIDES for this call (Preview P1), aligned to `position.legs`: leg `i`
prices at `legVolatilities[i]` when it is a number, else at its own `impliedVolatility`, else at
the position-level `volatility` (`volatilityShock` still adds on top). This is how a mark from
CURRENT contract quotes reaches a position whose legs were built with entry volatilities — the
position stays immutable, the call states the market. `assumptions.volatilitySource` reports
`'perCall'` when any override applied.
- (options).market.riskFreeRate?: number; default: not declared
- (options).market.volatility?: number; default: not declared — Position-level implied volatility. OPTIONAL: a position whose every option leg carries its own
`iv` prices entirely per-leg and needs no position vol. It is required (and validated positive)
only when at least one un-expired option leg has no per-leg `iv`; omitting it then throws.
- (options).market.volatilityShock?: number; default: not declared — Additive volatility shock (decimal) applied to EVERY effective leg volatility — the per-leg
`impliedVolatility` when a leg carries one, and the position-level `volatility` otherwise. This
is what makes a volatility scenario reach per-leg-IV legs; without it, shocking only
`volatility` is a silent no-op for legs that fix their own implied volatility.
- (options).prices?: PriceRange; default: not declared — X-axis price range. Omit for an auto-range around the strikes + breakevens.
- (options).spot?: number; default: not declared — Draw a marker at the current spot.
- (options).theme?: 'light' | 'dark'; default: not declared — Color theme (default 'light').
- (options).title?: string; default: not declared — Chart title (XML-escaped).
- (options).width?: number; default: not declared — Width in px (default 640).
- (position): Position; default: not declared
- (position).assumptions: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PositionAssumptions; default: not declared — Position-construction assumptions (design law #3): whether the entry premiums were supplied by
the caller (`'user'`) or model-priced from a market (`'model'`), plus the contract multiplier.
- (position).chartData: (options?: { prices?: number[] | PriceRange; include?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ChartInclude; market?: Partial<Omit<MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; }) => Array<{ underlyingPrice: number; expirationPnl?: number; currentPnl?: number; delta?: number; theta?: number; }>; default: not declared — Chart-ready output (spec §12.5). Current P&L / live Greeks need a market: per-call fields
merge over the construction market (R5), so a model-premium position charts with no `market`.
- (position).constructedAs?: string; default: not declared — PROVENANCE, not identity (dx §4.5): the named builder that constructed this position, absent
for raw `strategy(legs)`. Because positions are immutable this can never go stale — but a
rebuilt-after-tweak position has no name. For "what is this NOW?" use `classifyStrategy`.
- (position).legs: readonly Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').Leg>[]; default: not declared — The resolved legs — a frozen snapshot (deep-copied at construction, `Object.freeze`d per leg
and as an array). A Position is immutable by design: to tweak a strategy, edit your own leg
list and rebuild with `strategy(editedLegs, config)` — every downstream calculation is generic
over the legs, so the rebuilt position needs no named builder. Mutating this array throws
instead of silently diverging from `assumptions()`/cached results.
- (position).market?: Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumMarket>; default: not declared — The market this position was built with, if any — a frozen copy (R5), so mutating the caller's
market object later never silently retargets the position. `probability()`, `value()`,
`scenarioTable()`, and `chartData()` default to it; per-call fields merge over it.
- (position).market.asOf: string | number; default: not declared — Entry time (epoch ms or ISO). Each leg's entry `t = yearFraction(asOf, leg.expiry ?? market.expiry)`.
- (position).market.dividendYield?: number; default: not declared
- (position).market.expiry?: string; default: not declared — Default expiry for legs without their own `expiry` (single-expiry structures).
- (position).market.riskFreeRate: number; default: not declared
- (position).market.spot: number; default: not declared
- (position).market.volatility: number; default: not declared — Entry implied volatility (annualized decimal) for unpriced legs that carry no `impliedVolatility`
of their own — a leg's own volatility always wins, exactly as it does when `value()` marks it.
- (position).metrics: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffMetrics; default: not declared — Net debit/credit, max profit/loss, and breakevens. The expiration payoff is piecewise-linear, so
these are computed ANALYTICALLY from the kink set (every option strike plus every stock entry
price) and the tail slopes — never by sampling a coarse grid, which missed breakevens beyond the
last strike (e.g. a lone long stock, or a deep-ITM option) and ignored stock entry prices.
- (position).monteCarloProbability: (overrides: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloInput> & { seed: number; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloMetrics; default: not declared — Monte-Carlo probability metrics (spec §12.6): the simulated analogue of {@link probability}, for
cross-validation and path-dependent reads. Terminal lognormal paths give the probability of profit
and expected P&L (with a standard error); the probability of touching each breakeven is estimated
with the Brownian-bridge continuous-monitoring correction. Seeded and deterministic.
- (position).multiplier: number; default: not declared
- (position).netDebit: () => number; default: not declared — Net cash to enter (positive = debit, negative = credit).
- (position).payoff: (options?: { prices?: number[] | PriceRange; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffResult; default: not declared — Expiration payoff metrics plus a chart-ready grid of points (spec §12.2). `prices` is an explicit
grid array or a `{ from, to, steps }` range; omit it to frame the strike-derived default window
(the same one a payoff diagram draws).
- (position).pnlAtExpiry: (underlyingPrice: number) => number; default: not declared — Expiration P&L at an underlying price.
- (position).premiumSource: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumSource; default: not declared — How the entry premiums were sourced: `'user'` (supplied) or `'model'` (priced from `market`).
- (position).premiumVolatilitySource?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumVolatilitySource; default: not declared — When modeled, which volatility priced the entries (`'leg'`, `'position'` or `'mixed'`).
- (position).probability: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMetrics; default: not declared — Probability & scenario metrics (spec §12.6): probability of profit, expected value, reward/risk,
and the probability of touching each breakeven — under an explicit, echoed lognormal model.
- (position).scenarioTable: (options?: { market?: Partial<Omit<MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; prices?: number[] | PriceRange; volatilityShocks?: number[]; daysForward?: number[]; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ScenarioTableResult; default: not declared — Scenario table (spec §12.6): mark-to-market P&L and Greeks across a grid of underlying prices,
additive vol shocks, and days forward — the standard "what-if" matrix for an options ticket.
- (position).value: (overrides?: Partial<MarkToMarketInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketResult; default: not declared — Mark-to-market value, P&L, per-leg and aggregate Greeks via BSM (spec §12.3).
- (position).whatIfCube: (options?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeOptions) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeResult; default: not declared — A what-if **cube**: the position marked over the full spot × vol-shock × days-forward grid, plus
the **optimal-exit surface** — for each (spot, vol) outcome, the day along the time axis that
optimizes P&L (`max-pnl` by default, or `min-pnl`). `scenarioTable` extended a dimension: it returns
a navigable cube (axes + row-major cells) with the reductions a trader wants, not a flat row list.

Every cell is a `value()` mark (time-aware, per-leg-IV, shock-through-to-leg-IV), so calendars and
per-leg volatilities behave identically. The optimal-exit surface is a CONDITIONAL what-if ("if the
underlying is here with this vol shock, which day marks best?"), not a path-dependent stopping rule.
See `docs/specs/what-if-cube.md`.

- return.payoff: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffResult; default: not declared — Expiration payoff metrics plus a chart-ready grid of points (spec §12.2). `prices` is an explicit
grid array or a `{ from, to, steps }` range; omit it to frame the strike-derived default window
(the same one a payoff diagram draws).
- return.pnlAtExpiry: (underlyingPrice: number) => number; default: not declared — Expiration P&L at an underlying price.
- return.premiumSource: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumSource; default: not declared — How the entry premiums were sourced: `'user'` (supplied) or `'model'` (priced from `market`).
- return.premiumVolatilitySource?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumVolatilitySource; default: not declared — When modeled, which volatility priced the entries (`'leg'`, `'position'` or `'mixed'`).
- return.probability: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMetrics; default: not declared — Probability & scenario metrics (spec §12.6): probability of profit, expected value, reward/risk,
and the probability of touching each breakeven — under an explicit, echoed lognormal model.
- return.scenarioTable: (options?: { market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; volatilityShocks?: number[]; daysForward?: number[]; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ScenarioTableResult; default: not declared — Scenario table (spec §12.6): mark-to-market P&L and Greeks across a grid of underlying prices,
additive vol shocks, and days forward — the standard "what-if" matrix for an options ticket.
- return.value: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketResult; default: not declared — Mark-to-market value, P&L, per-leg and aggregate Greeks via BSM (spec §12.3).
- return.whatIfCube: (options?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeOptions) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeResult; default: not declared — A what-if **cube**: the position marked over the full spot × vol-shock × days-forward grid, plus
the **optimal-exit surface** — for each (spot, vol) outcome, the day along the time axis that
optimizes P&L (`max-pnl` by default, or `min-pnl`). `scenarioTable` extended a dimension: it returns
a navigable cube (axes + row-major cells) with the reductions a trader wants, not a flat row list.

Every cell is a `value()` mark (time-aware, per-leg-IV, shock-through-to-leg-IV), so calendars and
per-leg volatilities behave identically. The optimal-exit surface is a CONDITIONAL what-if ("if the
underlying is here with this vol shock, which day marks best?"), not a path-dependent stopping rule.
See `docs/specs/what-if-cube.md`.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy#putRatioBackspread

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

```typescript
export declare const putRatioBackspread: (input: s.RatioInput, config?: PositionConfig) => Position;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (config)?: PositionConfig | undefined; default: not declared
- (config).expiry?: string; default: not declared — Position-level default expiry (`YYYY-MM-DD` → 16:00 ET, or a datetime) applied to every leg
that has no `expiry` of its own. Named builders route their input's `expiry` here. Precedence
per leg: `leg.expiry` > `expiry` > `market.expiry` (R4).
- (config).market?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumMarket; default: not declared — Market for model-priced entry premiums (required when `premiums: 'model'` and any leg omits its
premium) — AND the position's remembered market (R5): `probability()`, `monteCarloProbability()`,
`value()`, `scenarioTable()`, and `chartData()` use it as their default market, with per-call
fields merged over it. Results echo `marketSource: 'construction' | 'call' | 'merged'`.
- (config).multiplier?: number; default: not declared — Contract multiplier for option legs (default 100).
- (config).premiums?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumSource; default: not declared — Entry-premium source: `'user'` (from the leg inputs, default) or `'model'` (priced from `market`).
- (input): s.RatioInput; default: not declared
- (input).expiry?: string; default: not declared — Expiry applied to every leg of this structure (`YYYY-MM-DD` → 16:00 ET, or a datetime).
- (input).long: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').Role; default: not declared
- (input).quantity?: number; default: not declared — Number of structures (default 1). Every leg scales by this.
- (input).ratio?: number; default: not declared — Number of short legs per long (default 2).
- (input).short: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').Role; default: not declared
- return.assumptions: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PositionAssumptions; default: not declared — Position-construction assumptions (design law #3): whether the entry premiums were supplied by
the caller (`'user'`) or model-priced from a market (`'model'`), plus the contract multiplier.
- return.chartData: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; include?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ChartInclude; market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; }) => Array<{ underlyingPrice: number; expirationPnl?: number; currentPnl?: number; delta?: number; theta?: number; }>; default: not declared — Chart-ready output (spec §12.5). Current P&L / live Greeks need a market: per-call fields
merge over the construction market (R5), so a model-premium position charts with no `market`.
- return.constructedAs?: string; default: not declared — PROVENANCE, not identity (dx §4.5): the named builder that constructed this position, absent
for raw `strategy(legs)`. Because positions are immutable this can never go stale — but a
rebuilt-after-tweak position has no name. For "what is this NOW?" use `classifyStrategy`.
- return.legs: readonly Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').Leg>[]; default: not declared — The resolved legs — a frozen snapshot (deep-copied at construction, `Object.freeze`d per leg
and as an array). A Position is immutable by design: to tweak a strategy, edit your own leg
list and rebuild with `strategy(editedLegs, config)` — every downstream calculation is generic
over the legs, so the rebuilt position needs no named builder. Mutating this array throws
instead of silently diverging from `assumptions()`/cached results.
- return.market?: Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumMarket>; default: not declared — The market this position was built with, if any — a frozen copy (R5), so mutating the caller's

- return.market.dividendYield?: number; default: not declared
- return.market.expiry?: string; default: not declared — Default expiry for legs without their own `expiry` (single-expiry structures).
- return.market.riskFreeRate: number; default: not declared
- return.market.spot: number; default: not declared
- return.market.volatility: number; default: not declared — Entry implied volatility (annualized decimal) for unpriced legs that carry no `impliedVolatility`
of their own — a leg's own volatility always wins, exactly as it does when `value()` marks it.
- return.metrics: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffMetrics; default: not declared — Net debit/credit, max profit/loss, and breakevens. The expiration payoff is piecewise-linear, so
these are computed ANALYTICALLY from the kink set (every option strike plus every stock entry
price) and the tail slopes — never by sampling a coarse grid, which missed breakevens beyond the
last strike (e.g. a lone long stock, or a deep-ITM option) and ignored stock entry prices.
- return.monteCarloProbability: (overrides: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloInput> & { seed: number; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloMetrics; default: not declared — Monte-Carlo probability metrics (spec §12.6): the simulated analogue of {@link probability}, for

- return.payoff: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffResult; default: not declared — Expiration payoff metrics plus a chart-ready grid of points (spec §12.2). `prices` is an explicit
grid array or a `{ from, to, steps }` range; omit it to frame the strike-derived default window
(the same one a payoff diagram draws).
- return.pnlAtExpiry: (underlyingPrice: number) => number; default: not declared — Expiration P&L at an underlying price.
- return.premiumSource: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumSource; default: not declared — How the entry premiums were sourced: `'user'` (supplied) or `'model'` (priced from `market`).
- return.premiumVolatilitySource?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumVolatilitySource; default: not declared — When modeled, which volatility priced the entries (`'leg'`, `'position'` or `'mixed'`).
- return.probability: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMetrics; default: not declared — Probability & scenario metrics (spec §12.6): probability of profit, expected value, reward/risk,
and the probability of touching each breakeven — under an explicit, echoed lognormal model.
- return.scenarioTable: (options?: { market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; volatilityShocks?: number[]; daysForward?: number[]; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ScenarioTableResult; default: not declared — Scenario table (spec §12.6): mark-to-market P&L and Greeks across a grid of underlying prices,
additive vol shocks, and days forward — the standard "what-if" matrix for an options ticket.
- return.value: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketResult; default: not declared — Mark-to-market value, P&L, per-leg and aggregate Greeks via BSM (spec §12.3).
- return.whatIfCube: (options?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeOptions) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeResult; default: not declared — A what-if **cube**: the position marked over the full spot × vol-shock × days-forward grid, plus
the **optimal-exit surface** — for each (spot, vol) outcome, the day along the time axis that
optimizes P&L (`max-pnl` by default, or `min-pnl`). `scenarioTable` extended a dimension: it returns
a navigable cube (axes + row-major cells) with the reductions a trader wants, not a flat row list.

Every cell is a `value()` mark (time-aware, per-leg-IV, shock-through-to-leg-IV), so calendars and
per-leg volatilities behave identically. The optimal-exit surface is a CONDITIONAL what-if ("if the
underlying is here with this vol shock, which day marks best?"), not a path-dependent stopping rule.
See `docs/specs/what-if-cube.md`.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy#scanStrategies

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Enumerate, score, and rank option structures over a strike grid. `candidates` carries the top-N
by the chosen objective, each with the full payoff/probability metrics.

```typescript
export declare function scanStrategies(options: ScanOptions): ScanResult;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (options): ScanOptions; default: not declared
- (options).asOf: string | number; default: not declared — Valuation instant. Epoch ms or a zoned ISO datetime, resolved at the boundary by core's
`resolveValuationAsOf` — the ONE valuation-instant grammar shared by `Position.probability()`,
the what-if cube and every other pricing boundary. A bare date is refused: a 0DTE's value
depends on the time of day.
- (options).chain: ScanQuoteRow[]; default: not declared — The option chain — one row per strike, ascending or not (sorted internally).
- (options).dividendYield?: number; default: not declared
- (options).expiry: string; default: not declared — Option expiry (`YYYY-MM-DD` → 16:00 ET, or a full datetime).
- (options).maxRisk?: number; default: not declared — Keep only candidates whose max loss ≤ this (in the position's P&L units — per contract, 100×).
- (options).maxWidth?: number; default: not declared — Cap on the width (strike distance) of any single wing/spread, in price units.
- (options).minProbabilityOfProfit?: number; default: not declared — Keep only candidates with probability-of-profit ≥ this.
- (options).rankBy?: 'probabilityOfProfit' | 'expectedValue' | 'returnOnRisk' | 'expectedValuePerRisk'; default: not declared — Ranking objective (default `expectedValuePerRisk`).
- (options).riskFreeRate: number; default: not declared
- (options).smile?: (strike: number) => number; default: not declared — Per-strike implied-volatility smile. Used to price any missing per-strike premiums (takes
precedence over `volatility`). **Scoring uses a SINGLE volatility:** `probabilityOfProfit` and
`expectedValue` are computed closed-form at the at-spot volatility `smile(spot)` (or
`volatility`), not the full smile — for smile-consistent probabilities, price a specific structure
with `Position.monteCarloProbability({ localVolatility })`.
- (options).spot: number; default: not declared — Underlying spot price (WS3.2: renamed from `underlyingPrice` for workspace consistency).
- (options).structures?: ScanStructure[]; default: not declared — Which structures to enumerate (default: all).
- (options).top?: number; default: not declared — Return only the top-N ranked candidates (default 25).
- (options).volatility?: number; default: not declared — Constant annualized volatility used for probabilityOfProfit / expectedValue scoring and to price any missing premiums.
- return.assumptions: { conventionsVersion: string; dayCount: 'ACT/365F'; rankBy: ScanObjective; scoringVolatility: number; structures: ScanStructure[]; timeToExpiryYears: number; }; default: not declared — Applied conventions, echoed (Law 2 report grammar).
- return.assumptions.conventionsVersion: string; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.dayCount: 'ACT/365F'; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.rankBy: 'probabilityOfProfit' | 'expectedValue' | 'returnOnRisk' | 'expectedValuePerRisk'; default: not declared — The ranking objective that produced the order (and each candidate's `score`).
- return.assumptions.scoringVolatility: number; default: not declared — The single at-spot volatility that `probabilityOfProfit`/`expectedValue` are scored at (see the `smile` doc).
- return.assumptions.structures: ScanStructure[]; default: not declared — The structures that were enumerated.
- return.assumptions.timeToExpiryYears: number; default: not declared — Year fraction to the scanned expiry.
- return.candidates: ScanCandidate[]; default: not declared — The top-N candidates by the ranking objective, descending, each fully metric'd.
- return.diagnostics: Diagnostics; default: not declared — Structured warnings; always present (possibly empty).

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy#shortCall

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

```typescript
export declare const shortCall: (input: s.SingleLegInput, config?: PositionConfig) => Position;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (config)?: PositionConfig | undefined; default: not declared
- (config).expiry?: string; default: not declared — Position-level default expiry (`YYYY-MM-DD` → 16:00 ET, or a datetime) applied to every leg
that has no `expiry` of its own. Named builders route their input's `expiry` here. Precedence
per leg: `leg.expiry` > `expiry` > `market.expiry` (R4).
- (config).market?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumMarket; default: not declared — Market for model-priced entry premiums (required when `premiums: 'model'` and any leg omits its
premium) — AND the position's remembered market (R5): `probability()`, `monteCarloProbability()`,
`value()`, `scenarioTable()`, and `chartData()` use it as their default market, with per-call
fields merged over it. Results echo `marketSource: 'construction' | 'call' | 'merged'`.
- (config).multiplier?: number; default: not declared — Contract multiplier for option legs (default 100).
- (config).premiums?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumSource; default: not declared — Entry-premium source: `'user'` (from the leg inputs, default) or `'model'` (priced from `market`).
- (input): s.SingleLegInput; default: not declared
- (input).expiry?: string; default: not declared — Expiry applied to every leg of this structure (`YYYY-MM-DD` → 16:00 ET, or a datetime).
- (input).premium?: number; default: not declared
- (input).quantity?: number; default: not declared — Number of structures (default 1). Every leg scales by this.
- (input).strike: number; default: not declared
- return.assumptions: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PositionAssumptions; default: not declared — Position-construction assumptions (design law #3): whether the entry premiums were supplied by
the caller (`'user'`) or model-priced from a market (`'model'`), plus the contract multiplier.
- return.chartData: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; include?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ChartInclude; market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; }) => Array<{ underlyingPrice: number; expirationPnl?: number; currentPnl?: number; delta?: number; theta?: number; }>; default: not declared — Chart-ready output (spec §12.5). Current P&L / live Greeks need a market: per-call fields
merge over the construction market (R5), so a model-premium position charts with no `market`.
- return.constructedAs?: string; default: not declared — PROVENANCE, not identity (dx §4.5): the named builder that constructed this position, absent
for raw `strategy(legs)`. Because positions are immutable this can never go stale — but a
rebuilt-after-tweak position has no name. For "what is this NOW?" use `classifyStrategy`.
- return.legs: readonly Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').Leg>[]; default: not declared — The resolved legs — a frozen snapshot (deep-copied at construction, `Object.freeze`d per leg
and as an array). A Position is immutable by design: to tweak a strategy, edit your own leg
list and rebuild with `strategy(editedLegs, config)` — every downstream calculation is generic
over the legs, so the rebuilt position needs no named builder. Mutating this array throws
instead of silently diverging from `assumptions()`/cached results.
- return.market?: Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumMarket>; default: not declared — The market this position was built with, if any — a frozen copy (R5), so mutating the caller's
market object later never silently retargets the position. `probability()`, `value()`,
`scenarioTable()`, and `chartData()` default to it; per-call fields merge over it.
- return.market.asOf: string | number; default: not declared — Entry time (epoch ms or ISO). Each leg's entry `t = yearFraction(asOf, leg.expiry ?? market.expiry)`.
- return.market.dividendYield?: number; default: not declared
- return.market.expiry?: string; default: not declared — Default expiry for legs without their own `expiry` (single-expiry structures).
- return.market.riskFreeRate: number; default: not declared
- return.market.spot: number; default: not declared
- return.market.volatility: number; default: not declared — Entry implied volatility (annualized decimal) for unpriced legs that carry no `impliedVolatility`
of their own — a leg's own volatility always wins, exactly as it does when `value()` marks it.
- return.metrics: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffMetrics; default: not declared — Net debit/credit, max profit/loss, and breakevens. The expiration payoff is piecewise-linear, so
these are computed ANALYTICALLY from the kink set (every option strike plus every stock entry
price) and the tail slopes — never by sampling a coarse grid, which missed breakevens beyond the
last strike (e.g. a lone long stock, or a deep-ITM option) and ignored stock entry prices.
- return.monteCarloProbability: (overrides: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloInput> & { seed: number; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloMetrics; default: not declared — Monte-Carlo probability metrics (spec §12.6): the simulated analogue of {@link probability}, for
cross-validation and path-dependent reads. Terminal lognormal paths give the probability of profit
and expected P&L (with a standard error); the probability of touching each breakeven is estimated
with the Brownian-bridge continuous-monitoring correction. Seeded and deterministic.
- return.multiplier: number; default: not declared
- return.netDebit: () => number; default: not declared — Net cash to enter (positive = debit, negative = credit).
- return.payoff: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffResult; default: not declared — Expiration payoff metrics plus a chart-ready grid of points (spec §12.2). `prices` is an explicit
grid array or a `{ from, to, steps }` range; omit it to frame the strike-derived default window
(the same one a payoff diagram draws).
- return.pnlAtExpiry: (underlyingPrice: number) => number; default: not declared — Expiration P&L at an underlying price.
- return.premiumSource: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumSource; default: not declared — How the entry premiums were sourced: `'user'` (supplied) or `'model'` (priced from `market`).
- return.premiumVolatilitySource?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumVolatilitySource; default: not declared — When modeled, which volatility priced the entries (`'leg'`, `'position'` or `'mixed'`).
- return.probability: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMetrics; default: not declared — Probability & scenario metrics (spec §12.6): probability of profit, expected value, reward/risk,
and the probability of touching each breakeven — under an explicit, echoed lognormal model.

- return.value: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketResult; default: not declared — Mark-to-market value, P&L, per-leg and aggregate Greeks via BSM (spec §12.3).
- return.whatIfCube: (options?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeOptions) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeResult; default: not declared — A what-if **cube**: the position marked over the full spot × vol-shock × days-forward grid, plus

the caller (`'user'`) or model-priced from a market (`'model'`), plus the contract multiplier.
- return.chartData: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; include?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ChartInclude; market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; }) => Array<{ underlyingPrice: number; expirationPnl?: number; currentPnl?: number; delta?: number; theta?: number; }>; default: not declared — Chart-ready output (spec §12.5). Current P&L / live Greeks need a market: per-call fields
merge over the construction market (R5), so a model-premium position charts with no `market`.
- return.constructedAs?: string; default: not declared — PROVENANCE, not identity (dx §4.5): the named builder that constructed this position, absent
for raw `strategy(legs)`. Because positions are immutable this can never go stale — but a
rebuilt-after-tweak position has no name. For "what is this NOW?" use `classifyStrategy`.
- return.legs: readonly Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').Leg>[]; default: not declared — The resolved legs — a frozen snapshot (deep-copied at construction, `Object.freeze`d per leg
and as an array). A Position is immutable by design: to tweak a strategy, edit your own leg
list and rebuild with `strategy(editedLegs, config)` — every downstream calculation is generic
over the legs, so the rebuilt position needs no named builder. Mutating this array throws
instead of silently diverging from `assumptions()`/cached results.
- return.market?: Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumMarket>; default: not declared — The market this position was built with, if any — a frozen copy (R5), so mutating the caller's
market object later never silently retargets the position. `probability()`, `value()`,
`scenarioTable()`, and `chartData()` default to it; per-call fields merge over it.
- return.market.asOf: string | number; default: not declared — Entry time (epoch ms or ISO). Each leg's entry `t = yearFraction(asOf, leg.expiry ?? market.expiry)`.
- return.market.dividendYield?: number; default: not declared
- return.market.expiry?: string; default: not declared — Default expiry for legs without their own `expiry` (single-expiry structures).
- return.market.riskFreeRate: number; default: not declared
- return.market.spot: number; default: not declared
- return.market.volatility: number; default: not declared — Entry implied volatility (annualized decimal) for unpriced legs that carry no `impliedVolatility`
of their own — a leg's own volatility always wins, exactly as it does when `value()` marks it.
- return.metrics: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffMetrics; default: not declared — Net debit/credit, max profit/loss, and breakevens. The expiration payoff is piecewise-linear, so
these are computed ANALYTICALLY from the kink set (every option strike plus every stock entry
price) and the tail slopes — never by sampling a coarse grid, which missed breakevens beyond the
last strike (e.g. a lone long stock, or a deep-ITM option) and ignored stock entry prices.
- return.monteCarloProbability: (overrides: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloInput> & { seed: number; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloMetrics; default: not declared — Monte-Carlo probability metrics (spec §12.6): the simulated analogue of {@link probability}, for
cross-validation and path-dependent reads. Terminal lognormal paths give the probability of profit
and expected P&L (with a standard error); the probability of touching each breakeven is estimated
with the Brownian-bridge continuous-monitoring correction. Seeded and deterministic.
- return.multiplier: number; default: not declared
- return.netDebit: () => number; default: not declared — Net cash to enter (positive = debit, negative = credit).
- return.payoff: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffResult; default: not declared — Expiration payoff metrics plus a chart-ready grid of points (spec §12.2). `prices` is an explicit
grid array or a `{ from, to, steps }` range; omit it to frame the strike-derived default window
(the same one a payoff diagram draws).
- return.pnlAtExpiry: (underlyingPrice: number) => number; default: not declared — Expiration P&L at an underlying price.
- return.premiumSource: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumSource; default: not declared — How the entry premiums were sourced: `'user'` (supplied) or `'model'` (priced from `market`).
- return.premiumVolatilitySource?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumVolatilitySource; default: not declared — When modeled, which volatility priced the entries (`'leg'`, `'position'` or `'mixed'`).
- return.probability: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMetrics; default: not declared — Probability & scenario metrics (spec §12.6): probability of profit, expected value, reward/risk,
and the probability of touching each breakeven — under an explicit, echoed lognormal model.
- return.scenarioTable: (options?: { market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; volatilityShocks?: number[]; daysForward?: number[]; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ScenarioTableResult; default: not declared — Scenario table (spec §12.6): mark-to-market P&L and Greeks across a grid of underlying prices,
additive vol shocks, and days forward — the standard "what-if" matrix for an options ticket.
- return.value: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketResult; default: not declared — Mark-to-market value, P&L, per-leg and aggregate Greeks via BSM (spec §12.3).
- return.whatIfCube: (options?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeOptions) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeResult; default: not declared — A what-if **cube**: the position marked over the full spot × vol-shock × days-forward grid, plus
the **optimal-exit surface** — for each (spot, vol) outcome, the day along the time axis that
optimizes P&L (`max-pnl` by default, or `min-pnl`). `scenarioTable` extended a dimension: it returns
a navigable cube (axes + row-major cells) with the reductions a trader wants, not a flat row list.

Every cell is a `value()` mark (time-aware, per-leg-IV, shock-through-to-leg-IV), so calendars and
per-leg volatilities behave identically. The optimal-exit surface is a CONDITIONAL what-if ("if the
underlying is here with this vol shock, which day marks best?"), not a path-dependent stopping rule.
See `docs/specs/what-if-cube.md`.

- return.chartData: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; include?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ChartInclude; market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; }) => Array<{ underlyingPrice: number; expirationPnl?: number; currentPnl?: number; delta?: number; theta?: number; }>; default: not declared — Chart-ready output (spec §12.5). Current P&L / live Greeks need a market: per-call fields
merge over the construction market (R5), so a model-premium position charts with no `market`.
- return.constructedAs?: string; default: not declared — PROVENANCE, not identity (dx §4.5): the named builder that constructed this position, absent
for raw `strategy(legs)`. Because positions are immutable this can never go stale — but a
rebuilt-after-tweak position has no name. For "what is this NOW?" use `classifyStrategy`.
- return.legs: readonly Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').Leg>[]; default: not declared — The resolved legs — a frozen snapshot (deep-copied at construction, `Object.freeze`d per leg
and as an array). A Position is immutable by design: to tweak a strategy, edit your own leg
list and rebuild with `strategy(editedLegs, config)` — every downstream calculation is generic
over the legs, so the rebuilt position needs no named builder. Mutating this array throws
instead of silently diverging from `assumptions()`/cached results.
- return.market?: Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumMarket>; default: not declared — The market this position was built with, if any — a frozen copy (R5), so mutating the caller's
market object later never silently retargets the position. `probability()`, `value()`,
`scenarioTable()`, and `chartData()` default to it; per-call fields merge over it.
- return.market.asOf: string | number; default: not declared — Entry time (epoch ms or ISO). Each leg's entry `t = yearFraction(asOf, leg.expiry ?? market.expiry)`.
- return.market.dividendYield?: number; default: not declared
- return.market.expiry?: string; default: not declared — Default expiry for legs without their own `expiry` (single-expiry structures).
- return.market.riskFreeRate: number; default: not declared
- return.market.spot: number; default: not declared
- return.market.volatility: number; default: not declared — Entry implied volatility (annualized decimal) for unpriced legs that carry no `impliedVolatility`
of their own — a leg's own volatility always wins, exactly as it does when `value()` marks it.
- return.metrics: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffMetrics; default: not declared — Net debit/credit, max profit/loss, and breakevens. The expiration payoff is piecewise-linear, so
these are computed ANALYTICALLY from the kink set (every option strike plus every stock entry
price) and the tail slopes — never by sampling a coarse grid, which missed breakevens beyond the
last strike (e.g. a lone long stock, or a deep-ITM option) and ignored stock entry prices.
- return.monteCarloProbability: (overrides: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloInput> & { seed: number; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloMetrics; default: not declared — Monte-Carlo probability metrics (spec §12.6): the simulated analogue of {@link probability}, for
cross-validation and path-dependent reads. Terminal lognormal paths give the probability of profit
and expected P&L (with a standard error); the probability of touching each breakeven is estimated
with the Brownian-bridge continuous-monitoring correction. Seeded and deterministic.
- return.multiplier: number; default: not declared
- return.netDebit: () => number; default: not declared — Net cash to enter (positive = debit, negative = credit).
- return.payoff: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffResult; default: not declared — Expiration payoff metrics plus a chart-ready grid of points (spec §12.2). `prices` is an explicit
grid array or a `{ from, to, steps }` range; omit it to frame the strike-derived default window
(the same one a payoff diagram draws).
- return.pnlAtExpiry: (underlyingPrice: number) => number; default: not declared — Expiration P&L at an underlying price.
- return.premiumSource: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumSource; default: not declared — How the entry premiums were sourced: `'user'` (supplied) or `'model'` (priced from `market`).
- return.premiumVolatilitySource?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumVolatilitySource; default: not declared — When modeled, which volatility priced the entries (`'leg'`, `'position'` or `'mixed'`).
- return.probability: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMetrics; default: not declared — Probability & scenario metrics (spec §12.6): probability of profit, expected value, reward/risk,
and the probability of touching each breakeven — under an explicit, echoed lognormal model.
- return.scenarioTable: (options?: { market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; volatilityShocks?: number[]; daysForward?: number[]; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ScenarioTableResult; default: not declared — Scenario table (spec §12.6): mark-to-market P&L and Greeks across a grid of underlying prices,
additive vol shocks, and days forward — the standard "what-if" matrix for an options ticket.
- return.value: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketResult; default: not declared — Mark-to-market value, P&L, per-leg and aggregate Greeks via BSM (spec §12.3).
- return.whatIfCube: (options?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeOptions) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeResult; default: not declared — A what-if **cube**: the position marked over the full spot × vol-shock × days-forward grid, plus
the **optimal-exit surface** — for each (spot, vol) outcome, the day along the time axis that
optimizes P&L (`max-pnl` by default, or `min-pnl`). `scenarioTable` extended a dimension: it returns
a navigable cube (axes + row-major cells) with the reductions a trader wants, not a flat row list.

Every cell is a `value()` mark (time-aware, per-leg-IV, shock-through-to-leg-IV), so calendars and
per-leg volatilities behave identically. The optimal-exit surface is a CONDITIONAL what-if ("if the
underlying is here with this vol shock, which day marks best?"), not a path-dependent stopping rule.
See `docs/specs/what-if-cube.md`.

the caller (`'user'`) or model-priced from a market (`'model'`), plus the contract multiplier.
- return.chartData: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; include?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ChartInclude; market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; }) => Array<{ underlyingPrice: number; expirationPnl?: number; currentPnl?: number; delta?: number; theta?: number; }>; default: not declared — Chart-ready output (spec §12.5). Current P&L / live Greeks need a market: per-call fields
merge over the construction market (R5), so a model-premium position charts with no `market`.
- return.constructedAs?: string; default: not declared — PROVENANCE, not identity (dx §4.5): the named builder that constructed this position, absent
for raw `strategy(legs)`. Because positions are immutable this can never go stale — but a
rebuilt-after-tweak position has no name. For "what is this NOW?" use `classifyStrategy`.
- return.legs: readonly Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').Leg>[]; default: not declared — The resolved legs — a frozen snapshot (deep-copied at construction, `Object.freeze`d per leg
and as an array). A Position is immutable by design: to tweak a strategy, edit your own leg
list and rebuild with `strategy(editedLegs, config)` — every downstream calculation is generic
over the legs, so the rebuilt position needs no named builder. Mutating this array throws
instead of silently diverging from `assumptions()`/cached results.
- return.market?: Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumMarket>; default: not declared — The market this position was built with, if any — a frozen copy (R5), so mutating the caller's
market object later never silently retargets the position. `probability()`, `value()`,
`scenarioTable()`, and `chartData()` default to it; per-call fields merge over it.
- return.market.asOf: string | number; default: not declared — Entry time (epoch ms or ISO). Each leg's entry `t = yearFraction(asOf, leg.expiry ?? market.expiry)`.
- return.market.dividendYield?: number; default: not declared
- return.market.expiry?: string; default: not declared — Default expiry for legs without their own `expiry` (single-expiry structures).
- return.market.riskFreeRate: number; default: not declared
- return.market.spot: number; default: not declared
- return.market.volatility: number; default: not declared — Entry implied volatility (annualized decimal) for unpriced legs that carry no `impliedVolatility`
of their own — a leg's own volatility always wins, exactly as it does when `value()` marks it.
- return.metrics: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffMetrics; default: not declared — Net debit/credit, max profit/loss, and breakevens. The expiration payoff is piecewise-linear, so
these are computed ANALYTICALLY from the kink set (every option strike plus every stock entry
price) and the tail slopes — never by sampling a coarse grid, which missed breakevens beyond the
last strike (e.g. a lone long stock, or a deep-ITM option) and ignored stock entry prices.
- return.monteCarloProbability: (overrides: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloInput> & { seed: number; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloMetrics; default: not declared — Monte-Carlo probability metrics (spec §12.6): the simulated analogue of {@link probability}, for
cross-validation and path-dependent reads. Terminal lognormal paths give the probability of profit
and expected P&L (with a standard error); the probability of touching each breakeven is estimated
with the Brownian-bridge continuous-monitoring correction. Seeded and deterministic.
- return.multiplier: number; default: not declared
- return.netDebit: () => number; default: not declared — Net cash to enter (positive = debit, negative = credit).
- return.payoff: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffResult; default: not declared — Expiration payoff metrics plus a chart-ready grid of points (spec §12.2). `prices` is an explicit
grid array or a `{ from, to, steps }` range; omit it to frame the strike-derived default window
(the same one a payoff diagram draws).
- return.pnlAtExpiry: (underlyingPrice: number) => number; default: not declared — Expiration P&L at an underlying price.
- return.premiumSource: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumSource; default: not declared — How the entry premiums were sourced: `'user'` (supplied) or `'model'` (priced from `market`).
- return.premiumVolatilitySource?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumVolatilitySource; default: not declared — When modeled, which volatility priced the entries (`'leg'`, `'position'` or `'mixed'`).
- return.probability: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMetrics; default: not declared — Probability & scenario metrics (spec §12.6): probability of profit, expected value, reward/risk,
and the probability of touching each breakeven — under an explicit, echoed lognormal model.
- return.scenarioTable: (options?: { market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; volatilityShocks?: number[]; daysForward?: number[]; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ScenarioTableResult; default: not declared — Scenario table (spec §12.6): mark-to-market P&L and Greeks across a grid of underlying prices,
additive vol shocks, and days forward — the standard "what-if" matrix for an options ticket.
- return.value: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketResult; default: not declared — Mark-to-market value, P&L, per-leg and aggregate Greeks via BSM (spec §12.3).
- return.whatIfCube: (options?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeOptions) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeResult; default: not declared — A what-if **cube**: the position marked over the full spot × vol-shock × days-forward grid, plus
the **optimal-exit surface** — for each (spot, vol) outcome, the day along the time axis that
optimizes P&L (`max-pnl` by default, or `min-pnl`). `scenarioTable` extended a dimension: it returns
a navigable cube (axes + row-major cells) with the reductions a trader wants, not a flat row list.

Every cell is a `value()` mark (time-aware, per-leg-IV, shock-through-to-leg-IV), so calendars and
per-leg volatilities behave identically. The optimal-exit surface is a CONDITIONAL what-if ("if the
underlying is here with this vol shock, which day marks best?"), not a path-dependent stopping rule.
See `docs/specs/what-if-cube.md`.

- return.assumptions: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PositionAssumptions; default: not declared — Position-construction assumptions (design law #3): whether the entry premiums were supplied by
the caller (`'user'`) or model-priced from a market (`'model'`), plus the contract multiplier.
- return.chartData: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; include?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ChartInclude; market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; }) => Array<{ underlyingPrice: number; expirationPnl?: number; currentPnl?: number; delta?: number; theta?: number; }>; default: not declared — Chart-ready output (spec §12.5). Current P&L / live Greeks need a market: per-call fields
merge over the construction market (R5), so a model-premium position charts with no `market`.
- return.constructedAs?: string; default: not declared — PROVENANCE, not identity (dx §4.5): the named builder that constructed this position, absent
for raw `strategy(legs)`. Because positions are immutable this can never go stale — but a
rebuilt-after-tweak position has no name. For "what is this NOW?" use `classifyStrategy`.
- return.legs: readonly Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').Leg>[]; default: not declared — The resolved legs — a frozen snapshot (deep-copied at construction, `Object.freeze`d per leg
and as an array). A Position is immutable by design: to tweak a strategy, edit your own leg
list and rebuild with `strategy(editedLegs, config)` — every downstream calculation is generic
over the legs, so the rebuilt position needs no named builder. Mutating this array throws
instead of silently diverging from `assumptions()`/cached results.
- return.market?: Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumMarket>; default: not declared — The market this position was built with, if any — a frozen copy (R5), so mutating the caller's
market object later never silently retargets the position. `probability()`, `value()`,
`scenarioTable()`, and `chartData()` default to it; per-call fields merge over it.
- return.market.asOf: string | number; default: not declared — Entry time (epoch ms or ISO). Each leg's entry `t = yearFraction(asOf, leg.expiry ?? market.expiry)`.
- return.market.dividendYield?: number; default: not declared
- return.market.expiry?: string; default: not declared — Default expiry for legs without their own `expiry` (single-expiry structures).
- return.market.riskFreeRate: number; default: not declared
- return.market.spot: number; default: not declared
- return.market.volatility: number; default: not declared — Entry implied volatility (annualized decimal) for unpriced legs that carry no `impliedVolatility`
of their own — a leg's own volatility always wins, exactly as it does when `value()` marks it.
- return.metrics: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffMetrics; default: not declared — Net debit/credit, max profit/loss, and breakevens. The expiration payoff is piecewise-linear, so
these are computed ANALYTICALLY from the kink set (every option strike plus every stock entry
price) and the tail slopes — never by sampling a coarse grid, which missed breakevens beyond the
last strike (e.g. a lone long stock, or a deep-ITM option) and ignored stock entry prices.
- return.monteCarloProbability: (overrides: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloInput> & { seed: number; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloMetrics; default: not declared — Monte-Carlo probability metrics (spec §12.6): the simulated analogue of {@link probability}, for
cross-validation and path-dependent reads. Terminal lognormal paths give the probability of profit
and expected P&L (with a standard error); the probability of touching each breakeven is estimated
with the Brownian-bridge continuous-monitoring correction. Seeded and deterministic.
- return.multiplier: number; default: not declared
- return.netDebit: () => number; default: not declared — Net cash to enter (positive = debit, negative = credit).
- return.payoff: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffResult; default: not declared — Expiration payoff metrics plus a chart-ready grid of points (spec §12.2). `prices` is an explicit
grid array or a `{ from, to, steps }` range; omit it to frame the strike-derived default window
(the same one a payoff diagram draws).
- return.pnlAtExpiry: (underlyingPrice: number) => number; default: not declared — Expiration P&L at an underlying price.
- return.premiumSource: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumSource; default: not declared — How the entry premiums were sourced: `'user'` (supplied) or `'model'` (priced from `market`).
- return.premiumVolatilitySource?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumVolatilitySource; default: not declared — When modeled, which volatility priced the entries (`'leg'`, `'position'` or `'mixed'`).
- return.probability: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMetrics; default: not declared — Probability & scenario metrics (spec §12.6): probability of profit, expected value, reward/risk,
and the probability of touching each breakeven — under an explicit, echoed lognormal model.
- return.scenarioTable: (options?: { market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; volatilityShocks?: number[]; daysForward?: number[]; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ScenarioTableResult; default: not declared — Scenario table (spec §12.6): mark-to-market P&L and Greeks across a grid of underlying prices,
additive vol shocks, and days forward — the standard "what-if" matrix for an options ticket.
- return.value: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketResult; default: not declared — Mark-to-market value, P&L, per-leg and aggregate Greeks via BSM (spec §12.3).
- return.whatIfCube: (options?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeOptions) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeResult; default: not declared — A what-if **cube**: the position marked over the full spot × vol-shock × days-forward grid, plus
the **optimal-exit surface** — for each (spot, vol) outcome, the day along the time axis that
optimizes P&L (`max-pnl` by default, or `min-pnl`). `scenarioTable` extended a dimension: it returns
a navigable cube (axes + row-major cells) with the reductions a trader wants, not a flat row list.

Every cell is a `value()` mark (time-aware, per-leg-IV, shock-through-to-leg-IV), so calendars and
per-leg volatilities behave identically. The optimal-exit surface is a CONDITIONAL what-if ("if the
underlying is here with this vol shock, which day marks best?"), not a path-dependent stopping rule.
See `docs/specs/what-if-cube.md`.

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (config)?: PositionConfig | undefined; default: not declared
- (config).expiry?: string; default: not declared — Position-level default expiry (`YYYY-MM-DD` → 16:00 ET, or a datetime) applied to every leg
that has no `expiry` of its own. Named builders route their input's `expiry` here. Precedence
per leg: `leg.expiry` > `expiry` > `market.expiry` (R4).
- (config).market?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumMarket; default: not declared — Market for model-priced entry premiums (required when `premiums: 'model'` and any leg omits its
premium) — AND the position's remembered market (R5): `probability()`, `monteCarloProbability()`,
`value()`, `scenarioTable()`, and `chartData()` use it as their default market, with per-call
fields merged over it. Results echo `marketSource: 'construction' | 'call' | 'merged'`.
- (config).multiplier?: number; default: not declared — Contract multiplier for option legs (default 100).
- (config).premiums?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumSource; default: not declared — Entry-premium source: `'user'` (from the leg inputs, default) or `'model'` (priced from `market`).
- (positionLegs): readonly LegInput[]; default: not declared
- bearCallLadder: (input: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').LadderInput, config?: PositionConfig) => Position; default: not declared
- bearCallLadder().return.assumptions: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PositionAssumptions; default: not declared — Position-construction assumptions (design law #3): whether the entry premiums were supplied by
the caller (`'user'`) or model-priced from a market (`'model'`), plus the contract multiplier.
- bearCallLadder().return.chartData: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; include?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ChartInclude; market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; }) => Array<{ underlyingPrice: number; expirationPnl?: number; currentPnl?: number; delta?: number; theta?: number; }>; default: not declared — Chart-ready output (spec §12.5). Current P&L / live Greeks need a market: per-call fields
merge over the construction market (R5), so a model-premium position charts with no `market`.
- bearCallLadder().return.constructedAs?: string; default: not declared — PROVENANCE, not identity (dx §4.5): the named builder that constructed this position, absent
for raw `strategy(legs)`. Because positions are immutable this can never go stale — but a
rebuilt-after-tweak position has no name. For "what is this NOW?" use `classifyStrategy`.
- bearCallLadder().return.legs: readonly Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').Leg>[]; default: not declared — The resolved legs — a frozen snapshot (deep-copied at construction, `Object.freeze`d per leg
and as an array). A Position is immutable by design: to tweak a strategy, edit your own leg
list and rebuild with `strategy(editedLegs, config)` — every downstream calculation is generic
over the legs, so the rebuilt position needs no named builder. Mutating this array throws
instead of silently diverging from `assumptions()`/cached results.
- bearCallLadder().return.market?: Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumMarket>; default: not declared — The market this position was built with, if any — a frozen copy (R5), so mutating the caller's
market object later never silently retargets the position. `probability()`, `value()`,
`scenarioTable()`, and `chartData()` default to it; per-call fields merge over it.
- bearCallLadder().return.market.asOf: string | number; default: not declared — Entry time (epoch ms or ISO). Each leg's entry `t = yearFraction(asOf, leg.expiry ?? market.expiry)`.
- bearCallLadder().return.market.dividendYield?: number; default: not declared
- bearCallLadder().return.market.expiry?: string; default: not declared — Default expiry for legs without their own `expiry` (single-expiry structures).
- bearCallLadder().return.market.riskFreeRate: number; default: not declared
- bearCallLadder().return.market.spot: number; default: not declared
- bearCallLadder().return.market.volatility: number; default: not declared — Entry implied volatility (annualized decimal) for unpriced legs that carry no `impliedVolatility`
of their own — a leg's own volatility always wins, exactly as it does when `value()` marks it.
- bearCallLadder().return.metrics: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffMetrics; default: not declared — Net debit/credit, max profit/loss, and breakevens. The expiration payoff is piecewise-linear, so
these are computed ANALYTICALLY from the kink set (every option strike plus every stock entry
price) and the tail slopes — never by sampling a coarse grid, which missed breakevens beyond the
last strike (e.g. a lone long stock, or a deep-ITM option) and ignored stock entry prices.
- bearCallLadder().return.monteCarloProbability: (overrides: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloInput> & { seed: number; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloMetrics; default: not declared — Monte-Carlo probability metrics (spec §12.6): the simulated analogue of {@link probability}, for
cross-validation and path-dependent reads. Terminal lognormal paths give the probability of profit
and expected P&L (with a standard error); the probability of touching each breakeven is estimated
with the Brownian-bridge continuous-monitoring correction. Seeded and deterministic.
- bearCallLadder().return.multiplier: number; default: not declared
- bearCallLadder().return.netDebit: () => number; default: not declared — Net cash to enter (positive = debit, negative = credit).

grid array or a `{ from, to, steps }` range; omit it to frame the strike-derived default window
(the same one a payoff diagram draws).

- bearCallLadder().return.probability: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMetrics; default: not declared — Probability & scenario metrics (spec §12.6): probability of profit, expected value, reward/risk,
and the probability of touching each breakeven — under an explicit, echoed lognormal model.
- bearCallLadder().return.scenarioTable: (options?: { market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; volatilityShocks?: number[]; daysForward?: number[]; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ScenarioTableResult; default: not declared — Scenario table (spec §12.6): mark-to-market P&L and Greeks across a grid of underlying prices,

- bearCallLadder().return.value: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketResult; default: not declared — Mark-to-market value, P&L, per-leg and aggregate Greeks via BSM (spec §12.3).
- bearCallLadder().return.whatIfCube: (options?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeOptions) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeResult; default: not declared — A what-if **cube**: the position marked over the full spot × vol-shock × days-forward grid, plus
the **optimal-exit surface** — for each (spot, vol) outcome, the day along the time axis that
optimizes P&L (`max-pnl` by default, or `min-pnl`). `scenarioTable` extended a dimension: it returns
a navigable cube (axes + row-major cells) with the reductions a trader wants, not a flat row list.

Every cell is a `value()` mark (time-aware, per-leg-IV, shock-through-to-leg-IV), so calendars and
per-leg volatilities behave identically. The optimal-exit surface is a CONDITIONAL what-if ("if the
underlying is here with this vol shock, which day marks best?"), not a path-dependent stopping rule.
See `docs/specs/what-if-cube.md`.
