- putRatioBackspread().return.chartData: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; include?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ChartInclude; market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; }) => Array<{ underlyingPrice: number; expirationPnl?: number; currentPnl?: number; delta?: number; theta?: number; }>; default: not declared — Chart-ready output (spec §12.5). Current P&L / live Greeks need a market: per-call fields
merge over the construction market (R5), so a model-premium position charts with no `market`.
- putRatioBackspread().return.constructedAs?: string; default: not declared — PROVENANCE, not identity (dx §4.5): the named builder that constructed this position, absent
for raw `strategy(legs)`. Because positions are immutable this can never go stale — but a
rebuilt-after-tweak position has no name. For "what is this NOW?" use `classifyStrategy`.
- putRatioBackspread().return.legs: readonly Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').Leg>[]; default: not declared — The resolved legs — a frozen snapshot (deep-copied at construction, `Object.freeze`d per leg
and as an array). A Position is immutable by design: to tweak a strategy, edit your own leg
list and rebuild with `strategy(editedLegs, config)` — every downstream calculation is generic
over the legs, so the rebuilt position needs no named builder. Mutating this array throws
instead of silently diverging from `assumptions()`/cached results.
- putRatioBackspread().return.market?: Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumMarket>; default: not declared — The market this position was built with, if any — a frozen copy (R5), so mutating the caller's
market object later never silently retargets the position. `probability()`, `value()`,
`scenarioTable()`, and `chartData()` default to it; per-call fields merge over it.

- putRatioBackspread().return.market.dividendYield?: number; default: not declared
- putRatioBackspread().return.market.expiry?: string; default: not declared — Default expiry for legs without their own `expiry` (single-expiry structures).
- putRatioBackspread().return.market.riskFreeRate: number; default: not declared
- putRatioBackspread().return.market.spot: number; default: not declared
- putRatioBackspread().return.market.volatility: number; default: not declared — Entry implied volatility (annualized decimal) for unpriced legs that carry no `impliedVolatility`
of their own — a leg's own volatility always wins, exactly as it does when `value()` marks it.
- putRatioBackspread().return.metrics: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffMetrics; default: not declared — Net debit/credit, max profit/loss, and breakevens. The expiration payoff is piecewise-linear, so
these are computed ANALYTICALLY from the kink set (every option strike plus every stock entry
price) and the tail slopes — never by sampling a coarse grid, which missed breakevens beyond the
last strike (e.g. a lone long stock, or a deep-ITM option) and ignored stock entry prices.
- putRatioBackspread().return.monteCarloProbability: (overrides: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloInput> & { seed: number; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloMetrics; default: not declared — Monte-Carlo probability metrics (spec §12.6): the simulated analogue of {@link probability}, for
cross-validation and path-dependent reads. Terminal lognormal paths give the probability of profit
and expected P&L (with a standard error); the probability of touching each breakeven is estimated
with the Brownian-bridge continuous-monitoring correction. Seeded and deterministic.
- putRatioBackspread().return.multiplier: number; default: not declared
- putRatioBackspread().return.netDebit: () => number; default: not declared — Net cash to enter (positive = debit, negative = credit).
- putRatioBackspread().return.payoff: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffResult; default: not declared — Expiration payoff metrics plus a chart-ready grid of points (spec §12.2). `prices` is an explicit
grid array or a `{ from, to, steps }` range; omit it to frame the strike-derived default window
(the same one a payoff diagram draws).

- return.payoff: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffResult; default: not declared — Expiration payoff metrics plus a chart-ready grid of points (spec §12.2). `prices` is an explicit
grid array or a `{ from, to, steps }` range; omit it to frame the strike-derived default window
(the same one a payoff diagram draws).
- return.pnlAtExpiry: (underlyingPrice: number) => number; default: not declared — Expiration P&L at an underlying price.
- return.premiumSource: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumSource; default: not declared — How the entry premiums were sourced: `'user'` (supplied) or `'model'` (priced from `market`).
- return.premiumVolatilitySource?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumVolatilitySource; default: not declared — When modeled, which volatility priced the entries (`'leg'`, `'position'` or `'mixed'`).
- return.probability: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMetrics; default: not declared — Probability & scenario metrics (spec §12.6): probability of profit, expected value, reward/risk,
and the probability of touching each breakeven — under an explicit, echoed lognormal model.
- return.scenarioTable: (options?: { market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; volatilityShocks?: number[]; daysForward?: number[]; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ScenarioTableResult; default: not declared — Scenario table (spec §12.6): mark-to-market P&L and Greeks across a grid of underlying prices,
additive vol shocks, and days forward — the standard "what-if" matrix for an options ticket.
- return.value: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketResult; default: not declared — Mark-to-market value, P&L, per-leg and aggregate Greeks via BSM (spec §12.3).
- return.whatIfCube: (options?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeOptions) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeResult; default: not declared — A what-if **cube**: the position marked over the full spot × vol-shock × days-forward grid, plus
the **optimal-exit surface** — for each (spot, vol) outcome, the day along the time axis that
optimizes P&L (`max-pnl` by default, or `min-pnl`). `scenarioTable` extended a dimension: it returns
a navigable cube (axes + row-major cells) with the reductions a trader wants, not a flat row list.

Every cell is a `value()` mark (time-aware, per-leg-IV, shock-through-to-leg-IV), so calendars and
per-leg volatilities behave identically. The optimal-exit surface is a CONDITIONAL what-if ("if the
underlying is here with this vol shock, which day marks best?"), not a path-dependent stopping rule.
See `docs/specs/what-if-cube.md`.

- reverseJadeLizard().return.assumptions: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PositionAssumptions; default: not declared — Position-construction assumptions (design law #3): whether the entry premiums were supplied by
the caller (`'user'`) or model-priced from a market (`'model'`), plus the contract multiplier.
- reverseJadeLizard().return.chartData: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; include?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ChartInclude; market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; }) => Array<{ underlyingPrice: number; expirationPnl?: number; currentPnl?: number; delta?: number; theta?: number; }>; default: not declared — Chart-ready output (spec §12.5). Current P&L / live Greeks need a market: per-call fields
merge over the construction market (R5), so a model-premium position charts with no `market`.
- reverseJadeLizard().return.constructedAs?: string; default: not declared — PROVENANCE, not identity (dx §4.5): the named builder that constructed this position, absent
for raw `strategy(legs)`. Because positions are immutable this can never go stale — but a
rebuilt-after-tweak position has no name. For "what is this NOW?" use `classifyStrategy`.
- reverseJadeLizard().return.legs: readonly Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').Leg>[]; default: not declared — The resolved legs — a frozen snapshot (deep-copied at construction, `Object.freeze`d per leg
and as an array). A Position is immutable by design: to tweak a strategy, edit your own leg
list and rebuild with `strategy(editedLegs, config)` — every downstream calculation is generic
over the legs, so the rebuilt position needs no named builder. Mutating this array throws
instead of silently diverging from `assumptions()`/cached results.
- reverseJadeLizard().return.market?: Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumMarket>; default: not declared — The market this position was built with, if any — a frozen copy (R5), so mutating the caller's
market object later never silently retargets the position. `probability()`, `value()`,
`scenarioTable()`, and `chartData()` default to it; per-call fields merge over it.

of their own — a leg's own volatility always wins, exactly as it does when `value()` marks it.
- reverseJadeLizard().return.metrics: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffMetrics; default: not declared — Net debit/credit, max profit/loss, and breakevens. The expiration payoff is piecewise-linear, so
these are computed ANALYTICALLY from the kink set (every option strike plus every stock entry
price) and the tail slopes — never by sampling a coarse grid, which missed breakevens beyond the
last strike (e.g. a lone long stock, or a deep-ITM option) and ignored stock entry prices.
- reverseJadeLizard().return.monteCarloProbability: (overrides: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloInput> & { seed: number; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloMetrics; default: not declared — Monte-Carlo probability metrics (spec §12.6): the simulated analogue of {@link probability}, for
cross-validation and path-dependent reads. Terminal lognormal paths give the probability of profit
and expected P&L (with a standard error); the probability of touching each breakeven is estimated
with the Brownian-bridge continuous-monitoring correction. Seeded and deterministic.

- shortCallButterfly().return.probability: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMetrics; default: not declared — Probability & scenario metrics (spec §12.6): probability of profit, expected value, reward/risk,
and the probability of touching each breakeven — under an explicit, echoed lognormal model.
- shortCallButterfly().return.scenarioTable: (options?: { market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; volatilityShocks?: number[]; daysForward?: number[]; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ScenarioTableResult; default: not declared — Scenario table (spec §12.6): mark-to-market P&L and Greeks across a grid of underlying prices,
additive vol shocks, and days forward — the standard "what-if" matrix for an options ticket.
- shortCallButterfly().return.value: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketResult; default: not declared — Mark-to-market value, P&L, per-leg and aggregate Greeks via BSM (spec §12.3).
- shortCallButterfly().return.whatIfCube: (options?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeOptions) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeResult; default: not declared — A what-if **cube**: the position marked over the full spot × vol-shock × days-forward grid, plus
the **optimal-exit surface** — for each (spot, vol) outcome, the day along the time axis that
optimizes P&L (`max-pnl` by default, or `min-pnl`). `scenarioTable` extended a dimension: it returns
a navigable cube (axes + row-major cells) with the reductions a trader wants, not a flat row list.

Every cell is a `value()` mark (time-aware, per-leg-IV, shock-through-to-leg-IV), so calendars and
per-leg volatilities behave identically. The optimal-exit surface is a CONDITIONAL what-if ("if the
underlying is here with this vol shock, which day marks best?"), not a path-dependent stopping rule.
See `docs/specs/what-if-cube.md`.

that has no `expiry` of its own. Named builders route their input's `expiry` here. Precedence
per leg: `leg.expiry` > `expiry` > `market.expiry` (R4).

premium) — AND the position's remembered market (R5): `probability()`, `monteCarloProbability()`,
`value()`, `scenarioTable()`, and `chartData()` use it as their default market, with per-call
fields merged over it. Results echo `marketSource: 'construction' | 'call' | 'merged'`.

- shortCallCondor().return.legs: readonly Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').Leg>[]; default: not declared — The resolved legs — a frozen snapshot (deep-copied at construction, `Object.freeze`d per leg
and as an array). A Position is immutable by design: to tweak a strategy, edit your own leg

instead of silently diverging from `assumptions()`/cached results.

- shortCallCondor().return.metrics: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffMetrics; default: not declared — Net debit/credit, max profit/loss, and breakevens. The expiration payoff is piecewise-linear, so
these are computed ANALYTICALLY from the kink set (every option strike plus every stock entry
price) and the tail slopes — never by sampling a coarse grid, which missed breakevens beyond the
last strike (e.g. a lone long stock, or a deep-ITM option) and ignored stock entry prices.
- shortCallCondor().return.monteCarloProbability: (overrides: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloInput> & { seed: number; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloMetrics; default: not declared — Monte-Carlo probability metrics (spec §12.6): the simulated analogue of {@link probability}, for
cross-validation and path-dependent reads. Terminal lognormal paths give the probability of profit
and expected P&L (with a standard error); the probability of touching each breakeven is estimated
with the Brownian-bridge continuous-monitoring correction. Seeded and deterministic.

and expected P&L (with a standard error); the probability of touching each breakeven is estimated
with the Brownian-bridge continuous-monitoring correction. Seeded and deterministic.

- shortGuts().return.netDebit: () => number; default: not declared — Net cash to enter (positive = debit, negative = credit).
- shortGuts().return.payoff: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffResult; default: not declared — Expiration payoff metrics plus a chart-ready grid of points (spec §12.2). `prices` is an explicit
grid array or a `{ from, to, steps }` range; omit it to frame the strike-derived default window
(the same one a payoff diagram draws).

- shortGuts().return.premiumVolatilitySource?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumVolatilitySource; default: not declared — When modeled, which volatility priced the entries (`'leg'`, `'position'` or `'mixed'`).
- shortGuts().return.probability: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMetrics; default: not declared — Probability & scenario metrics (spec §12.6): probability of profit, expected value, reward/risk,
and the probability of touching each breakeven — under an explicit, echoed lognormal model.
- shortGuts().return.scenarioTable: (options?: { market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; volatilityShocks?: number[]; daysForward?: number[]; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ScenarioTableResult; default: not declared — Scenario table (spec §12.6): mark-to-market P&L and Greeks across a grid of underlying prices,
additive vol shocks, and days forward — the standard "what-if" matrix for an options ticket.
- shortGuts().return.value: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketResult; default: not declared — Mark-to-market value, P&L, per-leg and aggregate Greeks via BSM (spec §12.3).
- shortGuts().return.whatIfCube: (options?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeOptions) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeResult; default: not declared — A what-if **cube**: the position marked over the full spot × vol-shock × days-forward grid, plus
the **optimal-exit surface** — for each (spot, vol) outcome, the day along the time axis that
optimizes P&L (`max-pnl` by default, or `min-pnl`). `scenarioTable` extended a dimension: it returns
a navigable cube (axes + row-major cells) with the reductions a trader wants, not a flat row list.

Every cell is a `value()` mark (time-aware, per-leg-IV, shock-through-to-leg-IV), so calendars and
per-leg volatilities behave identically. The optimal-exit surface is a CONDITIONAL what-if ("if the
underlying is here with this vol shock, which day marks best?"), not a path-dependent stopping rule.
See `docs/specs/what-if-cube.md`.

that has no `expiry` of its own. Named builders route their input's `expiry` here. Precedence
per leg: `leg.expiry` > `expiry` > `market.expiry` (R4).

premium) — AND the position's remembered market (R5): `probability()`, `monteCarloProbability()`,
`value()`, `scenarioTable()`, and `chartData()` use it as their default market, with per-call
fields merged over it. Results echo `marketSource: 'construction' | 'call' | 'merged'`.

these are computed ANALYTICALLY from the kink set (every option strike plus every stock entry
price) and the tail slopes — never by sampling a coarse grid, which missed breakevens beyond the
last strike (e.g. a lone long stock, or a deep-ITM option) and ignored stock entry prices.

- shortPutCondor().return.metrics: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffMetrics; default: not declared — Net debit/credit, max profit/loss, and breakevens. The expiration payoff is piecewise-linear, so
these are computed ANALYTICALLY from the kink set (every option strike plus every stock entry
price) and the tail slopes — never by sampling a coarse grid, which missed breakevens beyond the
last strike (e.g. a lone long stock, or a deep-ITM option) and ignored stock entry prices.
- shortPutCondor().return.monteCarloProbability: (overrides: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloInput> & { seed: number; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloMetrics; default: not declared — Monte-Carlo probability metrics (spec §12.6): the simulated analogue of {@link probability}, for
cross-validation and path-dependent reads. Terminal lognormal paths give the probability of profit
and expected P&L (with a standard error); the probability of touching each breakeven is estimated
with the Brownian-bridge continuous-monitoring correction. Seeded and deterministic.
- shortPutCondor().return.multiplier: number; default: not declared
- shortPutCondor().return.netDebit: () => number; default: not declared — Net cash to enter (positive = debit, negative = credit).
- shortPutCondor().return.payoff: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffResult; default: not declared — Expiration payoff metrics plus a chart-ready grid of points (spec §12.2). `prices` is an explicit
grid array or a `{ from, to, steps }` range; omit it to frame the strike-derived default window
(the same one a payoff diagram draws).
- shortPutCondor().return.pnlAtExpiry: (underlyingPrice: number) => number; default: not declared — Expiration P&L at an underlying price.
- shortPutCondor().return.premiumSource: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumSource; default: not declared — How the entry premiums were sourced: `'user'` (supplied) or `'model'` (priced from `market`).
- shortPutCondor().return.premiumVolatilitySource?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumVolatilitySource; default: not declared — When modeled, which volatility priced the entries (`'leg'`, `'position'` or `'mixed'`).
- shortPutCondor().return.probability: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMetrics; default: not declared — Probability & scenario metrics (spec §12.6): probability of profit, expected value, reward/risk,
and the probability of touching each breakeven — under an explicit, echoed lognormal model.
- shortPutCondor().return.scenarioTable: (options?: { market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; volatilityShocks?: number[]; daysForward?: number[]; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ScenarioTableResult; default: not declared — Scenario table (spec §12.6): mark-to-market P&L and Greeks across a grid of underlying prices,
additive vol shocks, and days forward — the standard "what-if" matrix for an options ticket.
- shortPutCondor().return.value: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketResult; default: not declared — Mark-to-market value, P&L, per-leg and aggregate Greeks via BSM (spec §12.3).
- shortPutCondor().return.whatIfCube: (options?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeOptions) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeResult; default: not declared — A what-if **cube**: the position marked over the full spot × vol-shock × days-forward grid, plus
the **optimal-exit surface** — for each (spot, vol) outcome, the day along the time axis that
optimizes P&L (`max-pnl` by default, or `min-pnl`). `scenarioTable` extended a dimension: it returns
a navigable cube (axes + row-major cells) with the reductions a trader wants, not a flat row list.

Every cell is a `value()` mark (time-aware, per-leg-IV, shock-through-to-leg-IV), so calendars and
per-leg volatilities behave identically. The optimal-exit surface is a CONDITIONAL what-if ("if the
underlying is here with this vol shock, which day marks best?"), not a path-dependent stopping rule.
See `docs/specs/what-if-cube.md`.

that has no `expiry` of its own. Named builders route their input's `expiry` here. Precedence
per leg: `leg.expiry` > `expiry` > `market.expiry` (R4).
- shortPutCondor(config).market?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumMarket; default: not declared — Market for model-priced entry premiums (required when `premiums: 'model'` and any leg omits its
premium) — AND the position's remembered market (R5): `probability()`, `monteCarloProbability()`,
`value()`, `scenarioTable()`, and `chartData()` use it as their default market, with per-call
fields merged over it. Results echo `marketSource: 'construction' | 'call' | 'merged'`.

market object later never silently retargets the position. `probability()`, `value()`,
`scenarioTable()`, and `chartData()` default to it; per-call fields merge over it.

- shortSyntheticFuture().return.market.dividendYield?: number; default: not declared
- shortSyntheticFuture().return.market.expiry?: string; default: not declared — Default expiry for legs without their own `expiry` (single-expiry structures).
- shortSyntheticFuture().return.market.riskFreeRate: number; default: not declared
- shortSyntheticFuture().return.market.spot: number; default: not declared

of their own — a leg's own volatility always wins, exactly as it does when `value()` marks it.
- shortSyntheticFuture().return.metrics: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffMetrics; default: not declared — Net debit/credit, max profit/loss, and breakevens. The expiration payoff is piecewise-linear, so
these are computed ANALYTICALLY from the kink set (every option strike plus every stock entry
price) and the tail slopes — never by sampling a coarse grid, which missed breakevens beyond the
last strike (e.g. a lone long stock, or a deep-ITM option) and ignored stock entry prices.
- shortSyntheticFuture().return.monteCarloProbability: (overrides: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloInput> & { seed: number; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloMetrics; default: not declared — Monte-Carlo probability metrics (spec §12.6): the simulated analogue of {@link probability}, for
cross-validation and path-dependent reads. Terminal lognormal paths give the probability of profit
and expected P&L (with a standard error); the probability of touching each breakeven is estimated
with the Brownian-bridge continuous-monitoring correction. Seeded and deterministic.
- shortSyntheticFuture().return.multiplier: number; default: not declared
- shortSyntheticFuture().return.netDebit: () => number; default: not declared — Net cash to enter (positive = debit, negative = credit).
- shortSyntheticFuture().return.payoff: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffResult; default: not declared — Expiration payoff metrics plus a chart-ready grid of points (spec §12.2). `prices` is an explicit
grid array or a `{ from, to, steps }` range; omit it to frame the strike-derived default window
(the same one a payoff diagram draws).

- shortSyntheticFuture().return.premiumVolatilitySource?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumVolatilitySource; default: not declared — When modeled, which volatility priced the entries (`'leg'`, `'position'` or `'mixed'`).
- shortSyntheticFuture().return.probability: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMetrics; default: not declared — Probability & scenario metrics (spec §12.6): probability of profit, expected value, reward/risk,
and the probability of touching each breakeven — under an explicit, echoed lognormal model.
- shortSyntheticFuture().return.scenarioTable: (options?: { market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; volatilityShocks?: number[]; daysForward?: number[]; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ScenarioTableResult; default: not declared — Scenario table (spec §12.6): mark-to-market P&L and Greeks across a grid of underlying prices,
additive vol shocks, and days forward — the standard "what-if" matrix for an options ticket.
- shortSyntheticFuture().return.value: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketResult; default: not declared — Mark-to-market value, P&L, per-leg and aggregate Greeks via BSM (spec §12.3).
- shortSyntheticFuture().return.whatIfCube: (options?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeOptions) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeResult; default: not declared — A what-if **cube**: the position marked over the full spot × vol-shock × days-forward grid, plus
the **optimal-exit surface** — for each (spot, vol) outcome, the day along the time axis that
optimizes P&L (`max-pnl` by default, or `min-pnl`). `scenarioTable` extended a dimension: it returns
a navigable cube (axes + row-major cells) with the reductions a trader wants, not a flat row list.

Every cell is a `value()` mark (time-aware, per-leg-IV, shock-through-to-leg-IV), so calendars and
per-leg volatilities behave identically. The optimal-exit surface is a CONDITIONAL what-if ("if the
underlying is here with this vol shock, which day marks best?"), not a path-dependent stopping rule.
See `docs/specs/what-if-cube.md`.

over the legs, so the rebuilt position needs no named builder. Mutating this array throws
instead of silently diverging from `assumptions()`/cached results.
- strap().return.market?: Readonly<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumMarket>; default: not declared — The market this position was built with, if any — a frozen copy (R5), so mutating the caller's
market object later never silently retargets the position. `probability()`, `value()`,
`scenarioTable()`, and `chartData()` default to it; per-call fields merge over it.
- strap().return.market.asOf: string | number; default: not declared — Entry time (epoch ms or ISO). Each leg's entry `t = yearFraction(asOf, leg.expiry ?? market.expiry)`.
- strap().return.market.dividendYield?: number; default: not declared
- strap().return.market.expiry?: string; default: not declared — Default expiry for legs without their own `expiry` (single-expiry structures).
- strap().return.market.riskFreeRate: number; default: not declared
- strap().return.market.spot: number; default: not declared
- strap().return.market.volatility: number; default: not declared — Entry implied volatility (annualized decimal) for unpriced legs that carry no `impliedVolatility`
of their own — a leg's own volatility always wins, exactly as it does when `value()` marks it.
- strap().return.metrics: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffMetrics; default: not declared — Net debit/credit, max profit/loss, and breakevens. The expiration payoff is piecewise-linear, so
these are computed ANALYTICALLY from the kink set (every option strike plus every stock entry
price) and the tail slopes — never by sampling a coarse grid, which missed breakevens beyond the
last strike (e.g. a lone long stock, or a deep-ITM option) and ignored stock entry prices.
- strap().return.monteCarloProbability: (overrides: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloInput> & { seed: number; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMonteCarloMetrics; default: not declared — Monte-Carlo probability metrics (spec §12.6): the simulated analogue of {@link probability}, for
cross-validation and path-dependent reads. Terminal lognormal paths give the probability of profit
and expected P&L (with a standard error); the probability of touching each breakeven is estimated
with the Brownian-bridge continuous-monitoring correction. Seeded and deterministic.
- strap().return.multiplier: number; default: not declared
- strap().return.netDebit: () => number; default: not declared — Net cash to enter (positive = debit, negative = credit).
- strap().return.payoff: (options?: { prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PayoffResult; default: not declared — Expiration payoff metrics plus a chart-ready grid of points (spec §12.2). `prices` is an explicit
grid array or a `{ from, to, steps }` range; omit it to frame the strike-derived default window
(the same one a payoff diagram draws).
- strap().return.pnlAtExpiry: (underlyingPrice: number) => number; default: not declared — Expiration P&L at an underlying price.
- strap().return.premiumSource: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumSource; default: not declared — How the entry premiums were sourced: `'user'` (supplied) or `'model'` (priced from `market`).
- strap().return.premiumVolatilitySource?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumVolatilitySource; default: not declared — When modeled, which volatility priced the entries (`'leg'`, `'position'` or `'mixed'`).
- strap().return.probability: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ProbabilityMetrics; default: not declared — Probability & scenario metrics (spec §12.6): probability of profit, expected value, reward/risk,
and the probability of touching each breakeven — under an explicit, echoed lognormal model.
- strap().return.scenarioTable: (options?: { market?: Partial<Omit<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; prices?: number[] | import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PriceRange; volatilityShocks?: number[]; daysForward?: number[]; }) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').ScenarioTableResult; default: not declared — Scenario table (spec §12.6): mark-to-market P&L and Greeks across a grid of underlying prices,
additive vol shocks, and days forward — the standard "what-if" matrix for an options ticket.
- strap().return.value: (overrides?: Partial<import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketInput>) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').MarkToMarketResult; default: not declared — Mark-to-market value, P&L, per-leg and aggregate Greeks via BSM (spec §12.3).
- strap().return.whatIfCube: (options?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeOptions) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').WhatIfCubeResult; default: not declared — A what-if **cube**: the position marked over the full spot × vol-shock × days-forward grid, plus
the **optimal-exit surface** — for each (spot, vol) outcome, the day along the time axis that
optimizes P&L (`max-pnl` by default, or `min-pnl`). `scenarioTable` extended a dimension: it returns
a navigable cube (axes + row-major cells) with the reductions a trader wants, not a flat row list.

Every cell is a `value()` mark (time-aware, per-leg-IV, shock-through-to-leg-IV), so calendars and
per-leg volatilities behave identically. The optimal-exit surface is a CONDITIONAL what-if ("if the
underlying is here with this vol shock, which day marks best?"), not a path-dependent stopping rule.
See `docs/specs/what-if-cube.md`.
- strap(config)?: PositionConfig | undefined; default: not declared
- strap(config).expiry?: string; default: not declared — Position-level default expiry (`YYYY-MM-DD` → 16:00 ET, or a datetime) applied to every leg
that has no `expiry` of its own. Named builders route their input's `expiry` here. Precedence
per leg: `leg.expiry` > `expiry` > `market.expiry` (R4).
- strap(config).market?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').PremiumMarket; default: not declared — Market for model-priced entry premiums (required when `premiums: 'model'` and any leg omits its
premium) — AND the position's remembered market (R5): `probability()`, `monteCarloProbability()`,
`value()`, `scenarioTable()`, and `chartData()` use it as their default market, with per-call
fields merged over it. Results echo `marketSource: 'construction' | 'call' | 'merged'`.
- strap(config).multiplier?: number; default: not declared — Contract multiplier for option legs (default 100).

- strap(input): import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy').SyntheticInput; default: not declared

- strap(input).putPremium?: number; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy#strategyFromChain

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Build a {@link Position} from an option chain. Returns the position, its resolved legs (premiums and
per-leg IVs attached), and the fills (contract / premium / delta per leg). Missing quotes throw
`strategy.strike_unavailable`; delta-targeted selection without deltas throws `strategy.delta_required`.

```typescript
export declare function strategyFromChain(rows: OptionQuote[], options: FromChainOptions): FromChainResult;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (options): FromChainOptions; default: not declared
- (rows): OptionQuote[]; default: not declared
- return.assumptions: { conventionsVersion: string; expiry: string; multiplier: number; priceSource: PriceSource; quantity: number; }; default: not declared — C (hygiene): the conventions the selection applied — above all which quoted price became each premium.
- return.assumptions.conventionsVersion: string; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.expiry: string; default: not declared — The selection expiry (the NEAR expiry for a calendar).
- return.assumptions.multiplier: number; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.priceSource: PriceSource; default: not declared — The price source every premium was read from (`'mid'` by default; never a silent fallback).
- return.assumptions.quantity: number; default: not declared
- return.fills: ChainFill[]; default: not declared
- return.legs: Leg[]; default: not declared
- return.position: Position; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy#strategyOf

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Build a position from legs.

```typescript
export declare function strategyOf(legs: readonly LegInput[], config?: PositionConfig): Position;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (config)?: PositionConfig | undefined; default: not declared
- (config).expiry?: string; default: not declared — Position-level default expiry (`YYYY-MM-DD` → 16:00 ET, or a datetime) applied to every leg
that has no `expiry` of its own. Named builders route their input's `expiry` here. Precedence
per leg: `leg.expiry` > `expiry` > `market.expiry` (R4).
- (config).market?: PremiumMarket; default: not declared — Market for model-priced entry premiums (required when `premiums: 'model'` and any leg omits its
premium) — AND the position's remembered market (R5): `probability()`, `monteCarloProbability()`,
`value()`, `scenarioTable()`, and `chartData()` use it as their default market, with per-call
fields merged over it. Results echo `marketSource: 'construction' | 'call' | 'merged'`.
- (config).multiplier?: number; default: not declared — Contract multiplier for option legs (default 100).
- (config).premiums?: PremiumSource; default: not declared — Entry-premium source: `'user'` (from the leg inputs, default) or `'model'` (priced from `market`).
- (legs): readonly LegInput[]; default: not declared
- return.assumptions: () => PositionAssumptions; default: not declared — Position-construction assumptions (design law #3): whether the entry premiums were supplied by
the caller (`'user'`) or model-priced from a market (`'model'`), plus the contract multiplier.
- return.chartData: (options?: { prices?: number[] | PriceRange; include?: ChartInclude; market?: Partial<Omit<MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; }) => Array<{ underlyingPrice: number; expirationPnl?: number; currentPnl?: number; delta?: number; theta?: number; }>; default: not declared — Chart-ready output (spec §12.5). Current P&L / live Greeks need a market: per-call fields
merge over the construction market (R5), so a model-premium position charts with no `market`.
- return.constructedAs?: string; default: not declared — PROVENANCE, not identity (dx §4.5): the named builder that constructed this position, absent
for raw `strategy(legs)`. Because positions are immutable this can never go stale — but a
rebuilt-after-tweak position has no name. For "what is this NOW?" use `classifyStrategy`.
- return.legs: readonly Readonly<Leg>[]; default: not declared — The resolved legs — a frozen snapshot (deep-copied at construction, `Object.freeze`d per leg
and as an array). A Position is immutable by design: to tweak a strategy, edit your own leg
list and rebuild with `strategy(editedLegs, config)` — every downstream calculation is generic
over the legs, so the rebuilt position needs no named builder. Mutating this array throws
instead of silently diverging from `assumptions()`/cached results.
- return.market?: Readonly<PremiumMarket>; default: not declared — The market this position was built with, if any — a frozen copy (R5), so mutating the caller's
market object later never silently retargets the position. `probability()`, `value()`,
`scenarioTable()`, and `chartData()` default to it; per-call fields merge over it.
- return.market.asOf: string | number; default: not declared — Entry time (epoch ms or ISO). Each leg's entry `t = yearFraction(asOf, leg.expiry ?? market.expiry)`.
- return.market.dividendYield?: number; default: not declared
- return.market.expiry?: string; default: not declared — Default expiry for legs without their own `expiry` (single-expiry structures).
- return.market.riskFreeRate: number; default: not declared
- return.market.spot: number; default: not declared
- return.market.volatility: number; default: not declared — Entry implied volatility (annualized decimal) for unpriced legs that carry no `impliedVolatility`
of their own — a leg's own volatility always wins, exactly as it does when `value()` marks it.
- return.metrics: () => PayoffMetrics; default: not declared — Net debit/credit, max profit/loss, and breakevens. The expiration payoff is piecewise-linear, so
these are computed ANALYTICALLY from the kink set (every option strike plus every stock entry
price) and the tail slopes — never by sampling a coarse grid, which missed breakevens beyond the
last strike (e.g. a lone long stock, or a deep-ITM option) and ignored stock entry prices.
- return.monteCarloProbability: (overrides: Partial<ProbabilityMonteCarloInput> & { seed: number; }) => ProbabilityMonteCarloMetrics; default: not declared — Monte-Carlo probability metrics (spec §12.6): the simulated analogue of {@link probability}, for
cross-validation and path-dependent reads. Terminal lognormal paths give the probability of profit
and expected P&L (with a standard error); the probability of touching each breakeven is estimated
with the Brownian-bridge continuous-monitoring correction. Seeded and deterministic.
- return.multiplier: number; default: not declared
- return.netDebit: () => number; default: not declared — Net cash to enter (positive = debit, negative = credit).
- return.payoff: (options?: { prices?: number[] | PriceRange; }) => PayoffResult; default: not declared — Expiration payoff metrics plus a chart-ready grid of points (spec §12.2). `prices` is an explicit
grid array or a `{ from, to, steps }` range; omit it to frame the strike-derived default window
(the same one a payoff diagram draws).
- return.pnlAtExpiry: (underlyingPrice: number) => number; default: not declared — Expiration P&L at an underlying price.
- return.premiumSource: PremiumSource; default: not declared — How the entry premiums were sourced: `'user'` (supplied) or `'model'` (priced from `market`).
- return.premiumVolatilitySource?: PremiumVolatilitySource; default: not declared — When modeled, which volatility priced the entries (`'leg'`, `'position'` or `'mixed'`).
- return.probability: (overrides?: Partial<ProbabilityInput>) => ProbabilityMetrics; default: not declared — Probability & scenario metrics (spec §12.6): probability of profit, expected value, reward/risk,
and the probability of touching each breakeven — under an explicit, echoed lognormal model.
- return.scenarioTable: (options?: { market?: Partial<Omit<MarkToMarketInput, 'spot'>>; prices?: number[] | PriceRange; volatilityShocks?: number[]; daysForward?: number[]; }) => ScenarioTableResult; default: not declared — Scenario table (spec §12.6): mark-to-market P&L and Greeks across a grid of underlying prices,
additive vol shocks, and days forward — the standard "what-if" matrix for an options ticket.
- return.value: (overrides?: Partial<MarkToMarketInput>) => MarkToMarketResult; default: not declared — Mark-to-market value, P&L, per-leg and aggregate Greeks via BSM (spec §12.3).
- return.whatIfCube: (options?: WhatIfCubeOptions) => WhatIfCubeResult; default: not declared — A what-if **cube**: the position marked over the full spot × vol-shock × days-forward grid, plus
the **optimal-exit surface** — for each (spot, vol) outcome, the day along the time axis that
optimizes P&L (`max-pnl` by default, or `min-pnl`). `scenarioTable` extended a dimension: it returns
a navigable cube (axes + row-major cells) with the reductions a trader wants, not a flat row list.

Every cell is a `value()` mark (time-aware, per-leg-IV, shock-through-to-leg-IV), so calendars and
per-leg volatilities behave identically. The optimal-exit surface is a CONDITIONAL what-if ("if the
underlying is here with this vol shock, which day marks best?"), not a path-dependent stopping rule.
See `docs/specs/what-if-cube.md`.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy#strategySignature

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Normalize legs to a structural BASE signature string (order-, scale-, and spacing-independent).
Two leg lists share a base signature iff they have the same (kind, sign, strike-rank,
quantity-ratio, expiry-rank) multiset — strike DISTANCES are deliberately not encoded (spacing
distinguishes only butterflies from broken wings, handled as a tie-breaker in
{@link classifyStrategy}, never here).

```typescript
export declare function strategySignature(legs: readonly ClassifiableLeg[]): string;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (legs): readonly ClassifiableLeg[]; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/strategy/scanner#ScanResult

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

The scan report (Law 2 report grammar): the ranked candidates plus the applied conventions
(`assumptions`) and a warnings channel (`diagnostics`).

```typescript
/**
 * The scan report (Law 2 report grammar): the ranked candidates plus the applied conventions
 * (`assumptions`) and a warnings channel (`diagnostics`).
 */
export interface ScanResult {
    /** The top-N candidates by the ranking objective, descending, each fully metric'd. */
    candidates: ScanCandidate[];
    /** Applied conventions, echoed (Law 2 report grammar). */
    assumptions: {
        conventionsVersion: string;
        dayCount: 'ACT/365F';
        /** The ranking objective that produced the order (and each candidate's `score`). */
        rankBy: ScanObjective;
        /** The structures that were enumerated. */
        structures: ScanStructure[];
        /** Year fraction to the scanned expiry. */
        timeToExpiryYears: number;
        /** The single at-spot volatility that `probabilityOfProfit`/`expectedValue` are scored at (see the `smile` doc). */
        scoringVolatility: number;
    };
    /** Structured warnings; always present (possibly empty). */
    diagnostics: Diagnostics;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- assumptions: { conventionsVersion: string; dayCount: 'ACT/365F'; rankBy: ScanObjective; scoringVolatility: number; structures: ScanStructure[]; timeToExpiryYears: number; }; default: not declared — Applied conventions, echoed (Law 2 report grammar).
- assumptions.conventionsVersion: string; default: not declared
- assumptions.dayCount: 'ACT/365F'; default: not declared
- assumptions.rankBy: 'probabilityOfProfit' | 'expectedValue' | 'returnOnRisk' | 'expectedValuePerRisk'; default: not declared — The ranking objective that produced the order (and each candidate's `score`).
- assumptions.scoringVolatility: number; default: not declared — The single at-spot volatility that `probabilityOfProfit`/`expectedValue` are scored at (see the `smile` doc).
- assumptions.structures: ScanStructure[]; default: not declared — The structures that were enumerated.
- assumptions.timeToExpiryYears: number; default: not declared — Year fraction to the scanned expiry.
- candidates: ScanCandidate[]; default: not declared — The top-N candidates by the ranking objective, descending, each fully metric'd.
- diagnostics: Diagnostics; default: not declared — Structured warnings; always present (possibly empty).
- diagnostics.autoReason?: string; default: not declared — When a meta-engine (e.g. `engines.auto()`) selected a delegate, this is a one-sentence,
human-readable explanation of WHY that delegate was chosen (`engine` then names the delegate).
Absent when no auto-selection took place.
- diagnostics.converged?: boolean; default: not declared — Whether an iterative procedure converged. `false` means the value is not trustworthy.
- diagnostics.decomposition?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Named intermediate quantities the value decomposes into — a par spread's protection leg and
risky annuity, a forward variance's near/far legs. The H-series explain paths disclose their
arithmetic here so a caller can audit the ratio, not just receive it (3B.3).
- diagnostics.engine?: string; default: not declared — Pricing/solver engine name, e.g. `black-scholes-merton`.
- diagnostics.finiteDifferenceBumps?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Finite-difference engines: the ACTUAL bump sizes used for FD Greeks (spec P2.3) — adaptive
near the vol/time boundaries, so the caller can see exactly what was differenced.
Keys: `spotStep`, `volatilityStep`, `timeStepYears`, `rateStep`, and — extended Greeks only —
`dividendYieldStep`. Each is the actual step differenced, in the unit of the coordinate it
bumps. (This doc named the retired `hS`/`hSig`/`hT`/`hR`/`hQ` keys for one release after the
emit sites had moved to the semantic names, so a caller following it read `undefined`.)
- diagnostics.iterations?: number; default: not declared — Iteration count for iterative methods.
- diagnostics.method?: string; default: not declared — Numerical method, e.g. `closed-form`, `brent`, `finite-difference`.
- diagnostics.selection?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing').SelectionReport; default: not declared — The structured engine-selection report (Gate C, `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing`): who was selected,
why, and — for automatic selection — every candidate considered with its verdict. This is the
machine-readable superset of `engine` + `autoReason` (which remain for compatibility);
`selected.name` always agrees with `engine` when both are present.
- diagnostics.selection.candidates?: readonly import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing').SelectionCandidate[]; default: not declared — Candidates an automatic selection considered; absent for explicit mode.
- diagnostics.selection.mode: 'explicit' | 'automatic'; default: not declared
- diagnostics.selection.reason: string; default: not declared — Why the selected engine answers this request.
- diagnostics.selection.selected: { name: string; version?: string; }; default: not declared
- diagnostics.selection.selected.name: string; default: not declared
- diagnostics.selection.selected.version?: string; default: not declared
- diagnostics.timingMs?: number; default: not declared — Wall-clock timing in milliseconds, when measured.
- diagnostics.warmup?: number; default: not declared — Series facades: number of leading output slots that are warmup sentinels (null/NaN) while the
computation seeds. Equals the input length when the indicator never emitted.
- diagnostics.warnings: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').QuantWarning[]; default: not declared — Structured warnings; always present (possibly empty).

```typescript
/**

} : 'gex' extends P ? {
    gamma?: number;
} : unknown) & ('dex' extends G ? {
    delta: number;
} : 'dex' extends P ? {
    delta?: number;
} : unknown);
```


Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- delta: number; default: not declared — Signed option delta at the print (calls > 0, puts < 0).
- premium: number; default: not declared — Trade premium in dollars (`price · size · multiplier`).
- side: 'buy' | 'sell'; default: not declared — Estimated aggressor side (e.g. from {@link FlowAnalysis}).
- type: OptionType; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/structure#ExposureAggregate

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/structure#ExposureMarket

Kind: type; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Market snapshot for `exposure()` — the workspace-canonical {@link MarketInputs}, except `spot` is
optional here because it falls back to each quote's `underlyingPrice` when omitted (WS3.2), and
`asOf` also accepts the ONE canonical "when" grammar (core `resolveAsOf`): epoch ms, `YYYY-MM-DD`
(UTC midnight), or a ZONED ISO datetime — a bare zone-less datetime throws the teaching error.

```typescript
/**
 * Market snapshot for `exposure()` — the workspace-canonical {@link MarketInputs}, except `spot` is
 * optional here because it falls back to each quote's `underlyingPrice` when omitted (WS3.2), and
 * `asOf` also accepts the ONE canonical "when" grammar (core `resolveAsOf`): epoch ms, `YYYY-MM-DD`
 * (UTC midnight), or a ZONED ISO datetime — a bare zone-less datetime throws the teaching error.
 */
export type ExposureMarket = Omit<MarketInputs, 'spot' | 'asOf'> & {
    /** Spot price. Falls back to each quote's `underlyingPrice` when omitted. */
    spot?: number;
    /** Snapshot time: epoch ms, `'YYYY-MM-DD'`, or a zoned ISO datetime (core `resolveAsOf` grammar). */
    asOf: EpochMs | string;
};
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- asOf: string | number; default: not declared — Snapshot time: epoch ms, `'YYYY-MM-DD'`, or a zoned ISO datetime (core `resolveAsOf` grammar).
- dividendYield?: number; default: not declared — Continuous dividend yield; defaults to 0 when omitted.
- riskFreeRate: number; default: not declared
- spot?: number; default: not declared — Spot price. Falls back to each quote's `underlyingPrice` when omitted.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/structure#ExposureProfile

Kind: class; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

A computed exposure profile with levels, by-strike/by-expiry views, and scenario maps. R2
envelope: the sign convention and every resolved knob live in `assumptions`; model limitations
ride `diagnostics.warnings` as `model.limitation` entries — nothing is hoisted top-level.

SELECTIVE (selective Greeks and exposure spec, decision 11). A profile built with
`exposure({ …, metrics })` — or a shortcut such as {@link gammaExposure} — computed ONLY the
selected metrics and the Black–Scholes outputs they need. Its rows and `aggregate` carry exactly
those metrics; an uncomputed metric is ABSENT, never zero. `G` is the set the type guarantees (a
literal selection) and `P` the set that may be present (a dynamic selection); both default to every
metric — the full profile `exposure()` has always returned.

```typescript
export declare class ExposureProfile<G extends ExposureMetric = ExposureMetric, P extends ExposureMetric = G> {
  constructor(request: ExposureInput<undefined>);
  readonly aggregate: ExposureAggregate<G, P>;
  readonly assumptions: Assumptions<{ timeDecayDirection: 'perCalendarDayElapsed'; scanVolatilityPolicy: 'stickyStrike'; convention: { name: string; calls: number; puts: number; }; gammaUnit: GammaUnit; priceSource: PriceSource; minTimeToExpiry: number; defaultMultiplier: number; metrics?: readonly ExposureMetric[]; }>;
  atSpot(spot: number): AtSpotExposure<G, P>;
  byExpiry<M extends ExposureMetric = G>(metrics?: readonly M[]): ExpiryRow<M>[];
  byStrike<M extends ExposureMetric = G>(metrics?: readonly M[]): StrikeRow<M>[];
  readonly contracts: readonly Readonly<ContractExposureRow<G, P>>[];
  readonly diagnostics: Diagnostics;
  levels(options?: { pinRiskBand?: number; }): Levels;
  netDrift(): NetDrift;
  scenarioMap<M extends ExposureMetric = DefaultScenarioMetric>(options?: ScenarioMapOptions<M>): ScenarioMap<M>;
  readonly spot: number;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (request): ExposureInput<undefined>; default: not declared
- (request).config: ExposureConfig; default: not declared
- (request).market: ExposureMarket; default: not declared
- (request).metrics?: undefined; default: not declared — The exposures to compute, e.g. `['gex']` or `['gex', 'dex', 'vanna']`. Omit it for the full
profile (every metric, exactly as before). A selection — explicit, nonempty, each name once —
computes only those metrics and the Black–Scholes outputs they need, and is echoed in
`assumptions.metrics`; uncomputed metrics are absent from the result, never zero.
- (request).quotes: OptionQuote[]; default: not declared
- aggregate: ExposureAggregate<G, P>; default: not declared
- assumptions: Assumptions<{ timeDecayDirection: 'perCalendarDayElapsed'; scanVolatilityPolicy: 'stickyStrike'; convention: { name: string; calls: number; puts: number; }; gammaUnit: GammaUnit; priceSource: PriceSource; minTimeToExpiry: number; defaultMultiplier: number; metrics?: readonly ExposureMetric[]; }>; default: not declared
- assumptions.asOf?: number; default: not declared

- assumptions.calendarVersion?: string; default: not declared
- assumptions.compounding?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').InterestCompounding; default: not declared
- assumptions.compounding.periodsPerYear: number; default: not declared
- assumptions.compounding.type: 'periodic'; default: not declared
- assumptions.convention: { name: string; calls: number; puts: number; }; default: not declared — The resolved sign convention (echoed; its caveat rides `diagnostics.warnings`).
- assumptions.convention.calls: number; default: not declared

- assumptions.engine?: string; default: not declared

or 13:00 on an early-close day;
`'explicit-instant'` when the caller supplied a zoned datetime. Named so the convention is
never silent (alignment spec P1.6); instrument builders own the full story in Phase 3.
- assumptions.gammaUnit: GammaUnit; default: not declared — GEX unit: `per1PercentMove` (spec formula) or `perPoint`.
- assumptions.metrics?: readonly ExposureMetric[]; default: not declared — The metrics this profile computed, as requested. Present only when `metrics` was passed; a
profile without it is the full profile (every metric).
- assumptions.minTimeToExpiry: number; default: not declared — Contracts with time-to-expiry (years) at/below this were skipped.
- assumptions.model?: string; default: not declared
- assumptions.priceSource: PriceSource; default: not declared — Quote price used for the IV fallback when a quote has no usable `impliedVolatility`.
- assumptions.scanVolatilityPolicy: 'stickyStrike'; default: not declared — Spot-shift scans (zeroGamma, scenarioMap) hold each contract's IV fixed (sticky-strike).
- assumptions.seed?: number; default: not declared — The randomness seed this result was computed under — REQUIRED echo for a

echoed in `assumptions.scanVolatilityPolicy`) — only spot moves and gamma/delta are re-evaluated. This is
the intraday dashboard path (one cheap greek pass per tick); a full {@link exposure} re-run — which
re-derives IV, the extended greeks, and levels — is the per-refresh path. At the profile's original
spot this reproduces `aggregate.gex`/`aggregate.dex` exactly (same operations, same order).

A selective profile re-evaluates only what it selected: a {@link gammaExposure} profile returns
`{ gex }` and computes gamma alone. A profile that selected neither `gex` nor `dex` refuses.

- byStrike: <M extends ExposureMetric = G>(metrics?: readonly M[]) => StrikeRow<M>[]; default: not declared — Chart-ready by-strike profile (one row per strike, totals summed), narrowed to `metrics` —

`dividendYieldStep`. Each is the actual step differenced, in the unit of the coordinate it

- levels().return.callWall: number | null; default: not declared — Strike with the largest summed |call GEX| across ALL expiries (resistance). Magnitude, not signed:

- netDrift: () => NetDrift; default: not declared — Net dealer-hedging drift estimate (spec §11.5): the gamma regime (pinning vs trending), the

vol moves. An ESTIMATE from the positioning model — not a price forecast. An empty or
identically-zero book has no gamma structure: `zeroGamma`/`distanceToZeroGamma`/`gammaRegime`/

- netDrift().return.bias: 'trend' | 'pin' | null; default: not declared — `pin` (gamma pulls spot toward zero-gamma) / `trend` (pushes away) / null.

(`−∂DEX/∂T` per day), so it reads the same direction as the passage of time.
- netDrift().return.distanceToZeroGamma: number | null; default: not declared — Signed distance from spot to zero-gamma as a fraction of spot (positive ⇒ flip is above spot).

because the value is 100x smaller than a per-unit-volatility reading of the same greek.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/structure#ExposureTotals

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

```typescript
export interface ExposureTotals {
    /** Dollar gamma exposure (`Γ·OI·mult·spot²·0.01` per-1%-move, signed by convention). */
    gex: number;
    /** Dollar delta exposure (`Δ·OI·mult·spot`). */
    dex: number;
    /** Vega exposure (`vega/1%·OI·mult`). */
    vega: number;
    /** Vanna exposure: dollar-delta change per +1% vol. */
    vanna: number;
    /**
     * Charm exposure: signed dollar-delta change as ONE calendar day ELAPSES (positive ⇒ dealer delta
     * increases day-over-day). Reported as `−∂DEX/∂T` per day, so its sign matches the passage of time.
     */
    charm: number;
    /** Theta exposure: dollar option-price decay per calendar day. */
    theta: number;
    /** Vomma (volga) exposure: change in vega exposure per +1% vol. */
    vomma: number;
    /**
     * Speed exposure: the CHANGE IN `gex` for a **+1% spot move**, in the same unit as `gex`
     * (`gammaUnit`). It is the full derivative of the GEX definition, not the bare third-order greek:
     * per-1%-move, `Δgex = (speed·S + 2·Γ)·OI·mult·sign·S²·1e-4`; per-point, `(speed·S + Γ)·OI·mult·sign·S·0.01`.
     * So `aggregate.speed ≈ atSpot(spot·1.01).gex − atSpot(spot).gex` (a first-order estimate of it).
     */
    speed: number;
    /**
     * Color exposure: signed change in GEX as ONE calendar day ELAPSES (`−∂GEX/∂T` per day), in the
     * same unit as `gex` (`gammaUnit`), so a positive value means dealer gamma exposure grows as time
     * passes. Per 1% move it is `−color·OI·mult·sign·S²·0.01/365`; per point, `−color·OI·mult·sign·S/365`.
     */
    color: number;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- charm: number; default: not declared — Charm exposure: signed dollar-delta change as ONE calendar day ELAPSES (positive ⇒ dealer delta
increases day-over-day). Reported as `−∂DEX/∂T` per day, so its sign matches the passage of time.
- color: number; default: not declared — Color exposure: signed change in GEX as ONE calendar day ELAPSES (`−∂GEX/∂T` per day), in the
same unit as `gex` (`gammaUnit`), so a positive value means dealer gamma exposure grows as time
passes. Per 1% move it is `−color·OI·mult·sign·S²·0.01/365`; per point, `−color·OI·mult·sign·S/365`.
- dex: number; default: not declared — Dollar delta exposure (`Δ·OI·mult·spot`).
- gex: number; default: not declared — Dollar gamma exposure (`Γ·OI·mult·spot²·0.01` per-1%-move, signed by convention).
- speed: number; default: not declared — Speed exposure: the CHANGE IN `gex` for a **+1% spot move**, in the same unit as `gex`
(`gammaUnit`). It is the full derivative of the GEX definition, not the bare third-order greek:
per-1%-move, `Δgex = (speed·S + 2·Γ)·OI·mult·sign·S²·1e-4`; per-point, `(speed·S + Γ)·OI·mult·sign·S·0.01`.
So `aggregate.speed ≈ atSpot(spot·1.01).gex − atSpot(spot).gex` (a first-order estimate of it).
- theta: number; default: not declared — Theta exposure: dollar option-price decay per calendar day.
- vanna: number; default: not declared — Vanna exposure: dollar-delta change per +1% vol.
- vega: number; default: not declared — Vega exposure (`vega/1%·OI·mult`).
- vomma: number; default: not declared — Vomma (volga) exposure: change in vega exposure per +1% vol.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/structure#FlowClassificationSource

Kind: type; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

`provided-or-quotes` is the backwards-compatible rule: supplied buy/sell wins, but unknown or
absent classification falls through to quotes. `provided-first` preserves supplied unknowns
and uses quotes only when classification is absent. `provided-only` never infers from quotes;
`quotes-only` ignores supplied classifications (but still validates their enum).

```typescript
/**
 * `provided-or-quotes` is the backwards-compatible rule: supplied buy/sell wins, but unknown or
 * absent classification falls through to quotes. `provided-first` preserves supplied unknowns
 * and uses quotes only when classification is absent. `provided-only` never infers from quotes;
 * `quotes-only` ignores supplied classifications (but still validates their enum).
 */
export type FlowClassificationSource = 'provided-or-quotes' | 'provided-first' | 'provided-only' | 'quotes-only';
```

```typescript
 * selections or a union-valued element.
 */
export type GuaranteedSuppliedExposureMetrics<S extends readonly SuppliedExposureMetric[] | undefined> = [
    S
] extends [
    undefined
] ? SuppliedExposureMetric : [
    S
] extends [
    readonly SuppliedExposureMetric[]
] ? GuaranteedSelection<NonNullable<S>> : never;
```

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/structure#Levels

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

```typescript
export interface Levels {
    /**
     * Spot level where net GEX flips sign, chosen as the interpolated gamma-flip NEAREST spot when the
     * profile has more than one flip in [0.8·spot, 1.2·spot]. Null when no flip exists in range.
     */
    zeroGamma: number | null;
    /** All interpolated gamma-flip levels in [0.8·spot, 1.2·spot], sorted ascending (may be empty). */
    gammaFlips: number[];
    /** Direction at the current spot: `positive` (mean-reverting) or `negative` (trending), or null. */
    gammaRegime: 'positive' | 'negative' | null;
    /**
     * Strike with the largest summed |call GEX| across ALL expiries (resistance). Magnitude, not signed:
     * the wall is where the most call gamma sits, which is the same strike whichever way the convention
     * signs it.
     */
    callWall: number | null;
    /** Strike with the largest summed |put GEX| across ALL expiries, under the convention (support). */
    putWall: number | null;
    maxGammaStrike: number | null;
    minGammaStrike: number | null;
    /**
     * Strike minimizing total in-the-money option value to holders (max writer profit), computed for the
     * NEAREST expiry only — max pain is expiry-specific and cannot be aggregated across expirations.
     */
    maxPain: number | null;
    largestCallOpenInterest: number | null;
    largestPutOpenInterest: number | null;
    vannaWall: number | null;
    charmWall: number | null;
    /** Nearest high-gamma strike to spot, with `atRisk` true when spot is within `pinRiskBand`. */
    pinRisk: {
        strike: number;
        atRisk: boolean;
    } | null;
    /**
     * Largest net-|GEX| strike (calls + puts summed per strike) among 0DTE contracts — expiring on the
     * snapshot's own **America/New_York** trading date (not its UTC date: after 20:00 ET the UTC date is
     * already tomorrow, which flagged the NEXT session's expiry as 0DTE).
     */
    zeroDaysToExpiryWall: number | null;
    /** Largest net-|GEX| strike (calls + puts summed per strike) in the nearest Friday (weekly) expiry. */
    weeklyOpexWall: number | null;
    /** Largest net-|GEX| strike (calls + puts summed per strike) in the nearest monthly OPEX (3rd-Friday). */
    monthlyOpexWall: number | null;
}
```

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/structure#NetDrift

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Net dealer-hedging drift estimate (spec §11.5).

```typescript
/** Net dealer-hedging drift estimate (spec §11.5). */
export interface NetDrift {
    /** `positive` (mean-reverting/pinning) or `negative` (trending), or null. */
    gammaRegime: 'positive' | 'negative' | null;
    /** The zero-gamma level (gamma flip) — the attractor in positive gamma, repeller in negative. */
    zeroGamma: number | null;
    /** Signed distance from spot to zero-gamma as a fraction of spot (positive ⇒ flip is above spot). */
    distanceToZeroGamma: number | null;
    /** `pin` (gamma pulls spot toward zero-gamma) / `trend` (pushes away) / null. */
    bias: 'pin' | 'trend' | null;
    /**
     * Aggregate charm exposure: signed dealer delta to re-hedge as ONE calendar day ELAPSES (drift into
     * expiry). Positive ⇒ dealers accumulate long delta day-over-day. Uses the elapsed-time sign
     * (`−∂DEX/∂T` per day), so it reads the same direction as the passage of time.
     */
    charmFlowPerDay: number;
    /**
     * Aggregate vanna exposure: signed dealer delta to re-hedge per +1 VOL POINT (a +0.01 move in
     * implied volatility), matching the per-1%-move convention `gex` uses. The unit is in the name
     * because the value is 100x smaller than a per-unit-volatility reading of the same greek.
     */
    vannaFlowPerVolatilityPoint: number;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- bias: 'trend' | 'pin' | null; default: not declared — `pin` (gamma pulls spot toward zero-gamma) / `trend` (pushes away) / null.
- charmFlowPerDay: number; default: not declared — Aggregate charm exposure: signed dealer delta to re-hedge as ONE calendar day ELAPSES (drift into
expiry). Positive ⇒ dealers accumulate long delta day-over-day. Uses the elapsed-time sign
(`−∂DEX/∂T` per day), so it reads the same direction as the passage of time.
- distanceToZeroGamma: number | null; default: not declared — Signed distance from spot to zero-gamma as a fraction of spot (positive ⇒ flip is above spot).
- gammaRegime: 'positive' | 'negative' | null; default: not declared — `positive` (mean-reverting/pinning) or `negative` (trending), or null.
- vannaFlowPerVolatilityPoint: number; default: not declared — Aggregate vanna exposure: signed dealer delta to re-hedge per +1 VOL POINT (a +0.01 move in
implied volatility), matching the per-1%-move convention `gex` uses. The unit is in the name
because the value is 100x smaller than a per-unit-volatility reading of the same greek.
- zeroGamma: number | null; default: not declared — The zero-gamma level (gamma flip) — the attractor in positive gamma, repeller in negative.

never silent (alignment spec P1.6); instrument builders own the full story in Phase 3.
- assumptions.heuristicRule: 'empty-low-coverage-volume-opposed-expansion-mixed'; default: not declared
- assumptions.interval: '[open,min(close,asOf))'; default: not declared
- assumptions.minimumClassificationCoverage: number; default: not declared
- assumptions.model?: string; default: not declared
- assumptions.multiplier: number; default: not declared
- assumptions.orderPolicy: 'stable-timestamp-sort'; default: not declared
- assumptions.premiumRule: 'provided-else-price-times-size-times-multiplier'; default: not declared
- assumptions.priceOverlaySymbol: string | null; default: not declared
- assumptions.priceRule: 'in-session-latest-before-bucket-end-no-backfill'; default: not declared
- assumptions.priceTieBreak: 'underlying-trade-then-quote-then-option-trade-last-input'; default: not declared
- assumptions.seed?: number; default: not declared — The randomness seed this result was computed under — REQUIRED echo for a
`randomness: 'seeded'` Pricer (Gate C, 2026-08-23): a stochastic result that does not name
its seed cannot be replayed from the result alone. Deterministic paths never set it.
- assumptions.sessionDate: string; default: not declared

- diagnostics.autoReason?: string; default: not declared — When a meta-engine (e.g. `engines.auto()`) selected a delegate, this is a one-sentence,
human-readable explanation of WHY that delegate was chosen (`engine` then names the delegate).
Absent when no auto-selection took place.
- diagnostics.converged?: boolean; default: not declared — Whether an iterative procedure converged. `false` means the value is not trustworthy.
- diagnostics.decomposition?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Named intermediate quantities the value decomposes into — a par spread's protection leg and
risky annuity, a forward variance's near/far legs. The H-series explain paths disclose their
arithmetic here so a caller can audit the ratio, not just receive it (3B.3).
- diagnostics.engine?: string; default: not declared — Pricing/solver engine name, e.g. `black-scholes-merton`.
- diagnostics.finiteDifferenceBumps?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Finite-difference engines: the ACTUAL bump sizes used for FD Greeks (spec P2.3) — adaptive

Keys: `spotStep`, `volatilityStep`, `timeStepYears`, `rateStep`, and — extended Greeks only —
`dividendYieldStep`. Each is the actual step differenced, in the unit of the coordinate it
bumps. (This doc named the retired `hS`/`hSig`/`hT`/`hR`/`hQ` keys for one release after the

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/structure#StrikeRow

A by-strike row narrowed to the requested metrics: only the selected `M` keys are present (WS2.4),

includes `'gex'` the row additionally carries the {@link GexSplit} call/put columns (WS4.5); when it
does not, the conditional intersects with `unknown` (a no-op) so non-gex rows stay lean.

```typescript
/**
 * A by-strike row narrowed to the requested metrics: only the selected `M` keys are present (WS2.4),
```

The `byStrike` and `byExpiry` breakdowns of a report, by the request's `breakdowns` flag: present

is a runtime `boolean` the type cannot know.

```typescript
/**
 * The `byStrike` and `byExpiry` breakdowns of a report, by the request's `breakdowns` flag: present
 * when it is omitted or `true` (the released report), absent for `false`, and optional when the flag
 * is a runtime `boolean` the type cannot know.
 */
export type SuppliedExposureBreakdownsFor<G extends SuppliedExposureMetric = SuppliedExposureMetric, P extends SuppliedExposureMetric = G, B extends boolean | undefined = undefined> = [
    B
] extends [
    false
] ? unknown : [
    B
] extends [
    true | undefined
] ? {
    byStrike: Array<SuppliedExposureTotalsFor<G, P> & {
        strike: number;
    }>;
    /** Groups economically identical expiry instants, even when labels use different time zones. */
    byExpiry: Array<SuppliedExposureTotalsFor<G, P> & {
        expiry: string;
        expiresAt: number;
    }>;
} : {
    byStrike?: Array<SuppliedExposureTotalsFor<G, P> & {
        strike: number;
    }>;
    byExpiry?: Array<SuppliedExposureTotalsFor<G, P> & {
        expiry: string;
        expiresAt: number;
    }>;
};
```

```typescript
 * provenance REQUIRED. Delta and gamma are NOT multiplied by open interest or contract multiplier.
 */
export interface SuppliedExposureGreeks extends OptionQuoteGreeks {
    /** Signed price delta per underlying unit; never converted to an absolute put delta. */
    delta: number;
    /** Signed change in delta per ONE spot-price point, not per 1% and not dollar gamma. */
    gamma: number;
    provenance: {
        /** Actual provider/model identifier, e.g. 'vendor-feed-v2' or 'bsm-2026-09'. */
        source: string;
        /** Actual Greek observation instant in epoch milliseconds, not report generation time. */
        timestampMs: number;
        model?: string;
    };
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- delta: number; default: not declared — Signed price delta per underlying unit; never converted to an absolute put delta.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/structure#SuppliedExposureReport

Kind: type; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Plain JSON-safe analysis report, directly compatible with saved-analysis report grammar.

`G`/`P` follow the `metrics` selection (guaranteed/possible metrics); both default to GEX and DEX,
today's report. A GEX+DEX report requires BOTH supplied Greeks on every row that supplies Greeks,
so the two metrics are always computed over the same included rows. `B` is the `breakdowns` flag
({@link SuppliedExposureBreakdownsFor}); by default the report carries both breakdowns.

```typescript
/**
 * Plain JSON-safe analysis report, directly compatible with saved-analysis report grammar.
 *
 * `G`/`P` follow the `metrics` selection (guaranteed/possible metrics); both default to GEX and DEX,
 * today's report. A GEX+DEX report requires BOTH supplied Greeks on every row that supplies Greeks,
 * so the two metrics are always computed over the same included rows. `B` is the `breakdowns` flag
 * ({@link SuppliedExposureBreakdownsFor}); by default the report carries both breakdowns.
 */
export type SuppliedExposureReport<G extends SuppliedExposureMetric = SuppliedExposureMetric, P extends SuppliedExposureMetric = G, B extends boolean | undefined = undefined> = {
    contributions: SuppliedExposureContributionFor<G, P>[];
    aggregate: SuppliedExposureTotalsFor<G, P>;
} & SuppliedExposureBreakdownsFor<G, P, B> & {
    coverage: {
        scope: 'suppliedQuotesOnly';
        status: 'emptyInput' | 'noEligibleQuotes' | 'partialInput' | 'allInputQuotesIncluded';
        totalQuotes: number;
        includedQuotes: number;
        excludedQuotes: number;
        /** Included / supplied rows; null for an empty chain. Not coverage of an unknown full universe. */
        fraction: number | null;
        /** Rows beyond the first matching underlying/type/style/strike/expiry instant, across sources/times. */
        duplicateContractQuotes: number;
        /** Included rows beyond the first included matching identity; these can double-count OI. */
        duplicateIncludedContractQuotes: number;
        /** Counts overlap when a row has several reasons. */
        exclusionCounts: Record<SuppliedExposureExclusion, number>;
    };
    assumptions: SuppliedExposureAssumptionsFor<G, P>;
    diagnostics: Diagnostics;
};
```

- diagnostics.selection.mode: 'explicit' | 'automatic'; default: not declared

- diagnostics.timingMs?: number; default: not declared — Wall-clock timing in milliseconds, when measured.
- diagnostics.warmup?: number; default: not declared — Series facades: number of leading output slots that are warmup sentinels (null/NaN) while the
computation seeds. Equals the input length when the indicator never emitted.
- diagnostics.warnings: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').QuantWarning[]; default: not declared — Structured warnings; always present (possibly empty).
