from prose. Absent — not an empty object — for indicators whose behaviour holds no such choice,
so its presence always means something.
- indicator: string; default: not declared — The indicator's registry/snapshot kind, e.g. `'rsi'`.
- parameters: Record<string, unknown>; default: not declared — The parameters the computation ran with: declared defaults merged with the caller's parameters.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis#TechnicalAnalysisExplain

Kind: type; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

The TA explain envelope: core `Computed` whose diagnostics ALWAYS carry the warmup count.

```typescript
/** The TA explain envelope: core `Computed` whose diagnostics ALWAYS carry the warmup count. */
export type TechnicalAnalysisExplain<Out> = Omit<Computed<Out[], TechnicalAnalysisAssumptionExtras>, 'diagnostics'> & {
    diagnostics: Computed<Out[], TechnicalAnalysisAssumptionExtras>['diagnostics'] & {
        warmup: number;
    };
};
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- assumptions: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Assumptions<TechnicalAnalysisAssumptionExtras>; default: not declared — Every applied convention, echoed back.
- assumptions.asOf?: number; default: not declared
- assumptions.calendar?: string; default: not declared
- assumptions.calendarVersion?: string; default: not declared
- assumptions.compounding?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').InterestCompounding; default: not declared
- assumptions.compounding.periodsPerYear: number; default: not declared
- assumptions.compounding.type: 'periodic'; default: not declared
- assumptions.conventions?: Readonly<Record<string, string | number | boolean>>; default: not declared — The indicator's declared conventions, when it has any that a caller could otherwise only learn
from prose. Absent — not an empty object — for indicators whose behaviour holds no such choice,
so its presence always means something.
- assumptions.conventionsVersion: string; default: not declared
- assumptions.dayCount?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').DayCount; default: not declared
- assumptions.dividendModel?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').DividendModel; default: not declared
- assumptions.engine?: string; default: not declared
- assumptions.expiryConvention?: 'us-equity-close' | 'explicit-instant'; default: not declared — How the contract's expiry label was resolved to an instant: `'us-equity-close'` when a
date-only `YYYY-MM-DD` expiry resolved to the US equity/options close — 16:00 America/New_York,
or 13:00 on an early-close day;
`'explicit-instant'` when the caller supplied a zoned datetime. Named so the convention is
never silent (alignment spec P1.6); instrument builders own the full story in Phase 3.
- assumptions.indicator: string; default: not declared — The indicator's registry/snapshot kind, e.g. `'rsi'`.
- assumptions.model?: string; default: not declared
- assumptions.parameters: Record<string, unknown>; default: not declared — The parameters the computation ran with: declared defaults merged with the caller's parameters.
- assumptions.seed?: number; default: not declared — The randomness seed this result was computed under — REQUIRED echo for a
`randomness: 'seeded'` Pricer (Gate C, 2026-08-23): a stochastic result that does not name
its seed cannot be replayed from the result alone. Deterministic paths never set it.
- assumptions.timeToExpiryConvention?: never; default: not declared
- assumptions.timeToExpiryYears?: number; default: not declared
- assumptions.units?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').GreekUnits; default: not declared
- assumptions.units.rho: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').RhoUnit; default: not declared
- assumptions.units.theta: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').ThetaUnit; default: not declared
- assumptions.units.vega: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').VegaUnit; default: not declared
- diagnostics: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Diagnostics & { warmup: number; }; default: not declared
- diagnostics.autoReason?: string; default: not declared — When a meta-engine (e.g. `engines.auto()`) selected a delegate, this is a one-sentence,
human-readable explanation of WHY that delegate was chosen (`engine` then names the delegate).
Absent when no auto-selection took place.
- diagnostics.converged?: boolean; default: not declared — Whether an iterative procedure converged. `false` means the value is not trustworthy.
- diagnostics.decomposition?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Named intermediate quantities the value decomposes into — a par spread's protection leg and
risky annuity, a forward variance's near/far legs. The H-series explain paths disclose their
arithmetic here so a caller can audit the ratio, not just receive it (3B.3).
- diagnostics.engine?: string; default: not declared — Pricing/solver engine name, e.g. `black-scholes-merton`.
- diagnostics.finiteDifferenceBumps?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Finite-difference engines: the ACTUAL bump sizes used for FD Greeks (spec P2.3) — adaptive
near the vol/time boundaries, so the caller can see exactly what was differenced.
Keys: `spotStep`, `volatilityStep`, `timeStepYears`, `rateStep`, and — extended Greeks only —
`dividendYieldStep`. Each is the actual step differenced, in the unit of the coordinate it
bumps. (This doc named the retired `hS`/`hSig`/`hT`/`hR`/`hQ` keys for one release after the
emit sites had moved to the semantic names, so a caller following it read `undefined`.)
- diagnostics.iterations?: number; default: not declared — Iteration count for iterative methods.
- diagnostics.method?: string; default: not declared — Numerical method, e.g. `closed-form`, `brent`, `finite-difference`.
- diagnostics.selection?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing').SelectionReport; default: not declared — The structured engine-selection report (Gate C, `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing`): who was selected,
why, and — for automatic selection — every candidate considered with its verdict. This is the
machine-readable superset of `engine` + `autoReason` (which remain for compatibility);
`selected.name` always agrees with `engine` when both are present.
- diagnostics.selection.candidates?: readonly import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing').SelectionCandidate[]; default: not declared — Candidates an automatic selection considered; absent for explicit mode.
- diagnostics.selection.mode: 'explicit' | 'automatic'; default: not declared
- diagnostics.selection.reason: string; default: not declared — Why the selected engine answers this request.
- diagnostics.selection.selected: { name: string; version?: string; }; default: not declared
- diagnostics.selection.selected.name: string; default: not declared
- diagnostics.selection.selected.version?: string; default: not declared
- diagnostics.timingMs?: number; default: not declared — Wall-clock timing in milliseconds, when measured.
- diagnostics.warmup?: number; default: not declared — Series facades: number of leading output slots that are warmup sentinels (null/NaN) while the
computation seeds. Equals the input length when the indicator never emitted.
- diagnostics.warnings: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').QuantWarning[]; default: not declared — Structured warnings; always present (possibly empty).
- provenance?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Provenance; default: not declared — Optional data lineage when the inputs came from a provider.
- provenance.asOf?: number; default: not declared
- provenance.dataset?: string; default: not declared
- provenance.provider?: string; default: not declared
- provenance.receivedAt?: number; default: not declared
- provenance.requestId?: string; default: not declared
- provenance.sourceVersion?: string; default: not declared
- provenance.warnings?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').QuantWarning[]; default: not declared
- value: Out[]; default: not declared — The computed value. Never `NaN` or `±Infinity`: a value the model cannot produce is `null`
beside a diagnostic that says why (Law 7 — a warning never licenses a non-finite number).

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis#TechnicalAnalysisSnapshot

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Serialized streaming-state snapshot (3B.N7).

The ENVELOPE is explicit and public: `kind` says which indicator wrote it, `schemaVersion` says
which shape it is in. `state` is deliberately OPAQUE — a consumer may persist it and hand it back
to `fromJSON`, but may not branch on indicator-private keys, which is why those keys are allowed
to stay compact where size matters.

This replaced a flat shape that put an abbreviated `v` and arbitrary stream state at the SAME
level, so nothing distinguished the contract from the payload.

```typescript
/**
 * Serialized streaming-state snapshot (3B.N7).
 *
 * The ENVELOPE is explicit and public: `kind` says which indicator wrote it, `schemaVersion` says
 * which shape it is in. `state` is deliberately OPAQUE — a consumer may persist it and hand it back
 * to `fromJSON`, but may not branch on indicator-private keys, which is why those keys are allowed
 * to stay compact where size matters.
 *
 * This replaced a flat shape that put an abbreviated `v` and arbitrary stream state at the SAME
 * level, so nothing distinguished the contract from the payload.
 */
export interface TechnicalAnalysisSnapshot {
    kind: string;
    /** Schema version, stamped at the serialization boundary by {@link snapshotOf}. */
    schemaVersion: number;
    /** Indicator-private stream state. Round-trip it; never read into it. */
    state: Record<string, unknown>;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- kind: string; default: not declared
- schemaVersion: number; default: not declared — Schema version, stamped at the serialization boundary by {@link snapshotOf}.
- state: Record<string, unknown>; default: not declared — Indicator-private stream state. Round-trip it; never read into it.

bumps. (This doc named the retired `hS`/`hSig`/`hT`/`hR`/`hQ` keys for one release after the
emit sites had moved to the semantic names, so a caller following it read `undefined`.)

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis#alignToBars

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Project a higher-timeframe series onto a lower-timeframe bar index, strictly causally (spec §13,
WS6.2). `higherSeries[j]` is a value computed on `higherBars[j]`, whose bucket `[ts, ts + iv)` is
usable only once it has CLOSED, i.e. at LTF times `≥ higherBars[j].timestampMs + intervalMs`. The LTF value at bar `i`
is a step-hold of the last HTF bar that has closed by `lowerBars[i].timestampMs`; it is `NaN` before the
first HTF bucket closes. No LTF output ever depends on an unclosed HTF bar — the `request.security`
lookahead is impossible by construction.

`higherBars` must be ascending by `timestampMs`. The interval is `options.intervalMs` if given, else inferred as the
smallest positive gap between consecutive HTF bars (with a single HTF bar and no `intervalMs`, the
bar never becomes usable and every output is `NaN`).

```typescript
export declare function alignToBars(input: AlignToBarsInput): number[];
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (input): AlignToBarsInput; default: not declared
- (input).higherBars: ArrayLike<TimeBar>; default: not declared
- (input).higherSeries: ArrayLike<number>; default: not declared
- (input).lowerBars: ArrayLike<TimeBar>; default: not declared
- (input).options?: AlignOptions; default: not declared

emit sites had moved to the semantic names, so a caller following it read `undefined`.)
- explain().return.diagnostics.iterations?: number; default: not declared — Iteration count for iterative methods.
- explain().return.diagnostics.method?: string; default: not declared — Numerical method, e.g. `closed-form`, `brent`, `finite-difference`.
- explain().return.diagnostics.selection?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing').SelectionReport; default: not declared — The structured engine-selection report (Gate C, `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing`): who was selected,
why, and — for automatic selection — every candidate considered with its verdict. This is the
machine-readable superset of `engine` + `autoReason` (which remain for compatibility);
`selected.name` always agrees with `engine` when both are present.
- explain().return.diagnostics.timingMs?: number; default: not declared — Wall-clock timing in milliseconds, when measured.
- explain().return.diagnostics.warmup?: number; default: not declared — Series facades: number of leading output slots that are warmup sentinels (null/NaN) while the
computation seeds. Equals the input length when the indicator never emitted.
- explain().return.diagnostics.warnings: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').QuantWarning[]; default: not declared — Structured warnings; always present (possibly empty).
- explain().return.provenance?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Provenance; default: not declared — Optional data lineage when the inputs came from a provider.
- explain().return.value: number[]; default: not declared — The computed value. Never `NaN` or `±Infinity`: a value the model cannot produce is `null`
beside a diagnostic that says why (Law 7 — a warning never licenses a non-finite number).
- explain(input): ArrayLike<BarInput>; default: not declared
- explain(parameters)?: AwesomeParameters | undefined; default: not declared
- explain(parameters).fast?: number; default: not declared
- explain(parameters).slow?: number; default: not declared

- fromJSON().return.next: (input: BarInput) => number | null; default: not declared
- fromJSON().return.peek: (input: BarInput) => number | null; default: not declared — The value that WOULD result from `next(input)` applied to the committed state, WITHOUT committing
it. Call it repeatedly with the forming bar's evolving value; call `next(input)` once at bar close
to commit. Between commits the committed state is untouched, so a live chart never repaints its
closed bars. The default cost is O(snapshot) per call (clone-and-apply); indicators may override
with an O(1) form later.
- fromJSON().return.toJSON: () => TechnicalAnalysisSnapshot; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis#candleAverage

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

TA-Lib's `TA_CANDLEAVERAGE` at every bar: `factor · (avg of `range` over the preceding `averagePeriod`
bars) / denom`, where `denom = 2` for the Shadows range type (it sums two shadows) else `1`. With
`averagePeriod = 0` the current bar's own range is used. Bars before the trailing window is full get
`NaN` (the pattern is in its lookback there).

```typescript
export declare function candleAverage(bars: ArrayLike<BarInput>, setting: CandleSetting): number[];
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (bars): ArrayLike<BarInput>; default: not declared
- (setting): CandleSetting; default: not declared
- (setting).averagePeriod: number; default: not declared — Trailing-average period; 0 means "use the current bar's range" (no averaging).
- (setting).factor: number; default: not declared
- (setting).range: CandleRangeType; default: not declared

arithmetic here so a caller can audit the ratio, not just receive it (3B.3).

- explain().return.diagnostics.finiteDifferenceBumps?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Finite-difference engines: the ACTUAL bump sizes used for FD Greeks (spec P2.3) — adaptive
near the vol/time boundaries, so the caller can see exactly what was differenced.

`dividendYieldStep`. Each is the actual step differenced, in the unit of the coordinate it
bumps. (This doc named the retired `hS`/`hSig`/`hT`/`hR`/`hQ` keys for one release after the

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis#checkSnapshotVersion

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Validate a snapshot's schema version before restoring. A newer version is rejected — this build
can't know what changed, so restoring would silently corrupt state, which design law #4 forbids.
An OLDER version is rejected too: the v1 flat shape has no `state`, so "accepting" it would
restore an indicator with every field undefined.

```typescript
export declare function checkSnapshotVersion(snapshot: TechnicalAnalysisSnapshot): void;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (snapshot): TechnicalAnalysisSnapshot; default: not declared
- (snapshot).kind: string; default: not declared
- (snapshot).schemaVersion: number; default: not declared — Schema version, stamped at the serialization boundary by {@link snapshotOf}.
- (snapshot).state: Record<string, unknown>; default: not declared — Indicator-private stream state. Round-trip it; never read into it.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis#condition

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Build a custom condition. `refs` are the column aliases / `alias.field` / raw OHLCV fields the
predicate reads via `context.get(...)` — they are validated up front like the built-in conditions, so
a typo fails loud. Pass `[]` for a condition that reads nothing (or reads only constants).

```typescript
export declare function condition(refs: readonly string[], predicate: (context: SignalContext, barIndex: number) => boolean): Condition;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (predicate): (context: SignalContext, barIndex: number) => boolean; default: not declared
- (refs): readonly string[]; default: not declared
- return.refs: readonly string[]; default: not declared — String operands (column aliases, dotted sub-fields, raw fields) this condition reads.

required, its warmup, and its cross-library aliases. Throws on an unknown name. See the spec.

```typescript
export declare function describeIndicator(name: string, probeLength?: number): IndicatorDescription;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (name): string; default: not declared
- (probeLength)?: number; default: not declared
- return.aliases?: Omit<IndicatorAliasRow, 'totalfinance'>; default: not declared — Cross-library aliases (TA-Lib / pandas-ta / TradingView), when known.
- return.aliases.pandas?: string | string[]; default: not declared — pandas-ta name(s), snake_case.
- return.aliases.talib?: string | string[]; default: not declared — TA-Lib function name(s), uppercase.
- return.aliases.tradingview?: string; default: not declared — TradingView display name.
- return.category: IndicatorCategory; default: not declared
- return.conventions?: Readonly<Record<string, string | number | boolean>>; default: not declared — The choices this indicator made that its parameters do not reveal (Wilder vs EMA smoothing, what
a flat window resolves to, how the first value is seeded) — present only where such a choice
exists. This is the field that answers "why does your RSI disagree with my other library?"
without leaving the tool schema.
- return.defaults: Record<string, unknown>; default: not declared — Declared default per optional parameter; a derived default is a resolver function.
- return.inputs: IndicatorInputs; default: not declared — Input kind expected by the indicator.
- return.name: string; default: not declared — Canonical registered name.
- return.output: IndicatorOutputMetadata; default: not declared — The output metadata — recursive value schema + optional visualization (Wave 6 §4).
- return.parameters: string[]; default: not declared — All parameter names (including defaulted ones the caller may omit).
- return.required: string[]; default: not declared — Parameters with no default — the caller must supply these.
- return.warmup: number | null; default: not declared — Leading bars before the first real value, or `null` if it never emitted within the probe.

- explain().return.diagnostics: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Diagnostics & { warmup: number; }; default: not declared
- explain().return.diagnostics.autoReason?: string; default: not declared — When a meta-engine (e.g. `engines.auto()`) selected a delegate, this is a one-sentence,
human-readable explanation of WHY that delegate was chosen (`engine` then names the delegate).
Absent when no auto-selection took place.
- explain().return.diagnostics.converged?: boolean; default: not declared — Whether an iterative procedure converged. `false` means the value is not trustworthy.
- explain().return.diagnostics.decomposition?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Named intermediate quantities the value decomposes into — a par spread's protection leg and
risky annuity, a forward variance's near/far legs. The H-series explain paths disclose their
arithmetic here so a caller can audit the ratio, not just receive it (3B.3).
- explain().return.diagnostics.engine?: string; default: not declared — Pricing/solver engine name, e.g. `black-scholes-merton`.
- explain().return.diagnostics.finiteDifferenceBumps?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Finite-difference engines: the ACTUAL bump sizes used for FD Greeks (spec P2.3) — adaptive
near the vol/time boundaries, so the caller can see exactly what was differenced.
Keys: `spotStep`, `volatilityStep`, `timeStepYears`, `rateStep`, and — extended Greeks only —
`dividendYieldStep`. Each is the actual step differenced, in the unit of the coordinate it
bumps. (This doc named the retired `hS`/`hSig`/`hT`/`hR`/`hQ` keys for one release after the
emit sites had moved to the semantic names, so a caller following it read `undefined`.)
- explain().return.diagnostics.iterations?: number; default: not declared — Iteration count for iterative methods.
- explain().return.diagnostics.method?: string; default: not declared — Numerical method, e.g. `closed-form`, `brent`, `finite-difference`.
- explain().return.diagnostics.selection?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing').SelectionReport; default: not declared — The structured engine-selection report (Gate C, `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing`): who was selected,
why, and — for automatic selection — every candidate considered with its verdict. This is the
machine-readable superset of `engine` + `autoReason` (which remain for compatibility);
`selected.name` always agrees with `engine` when both are present.
- explain().return.diagnostics.timingMs?: number; default: not declared — Wall-clock timing in milliseconds, when measured.

- explain().return.value: DmiPoint[]; default: not declared — The computed value. Never `NaN` or `±Infinity`: a value the model cannot produce is `null`
beside a diagnostic that says why (Law 7 — a warning never licenses a non-finite number).

Even Better Sinewave (pandas-ta `ebsw`), bounded roughly to [-1, 1].

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis#features

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

```typescript
export declare function features(candles: BarInput[]): FeaturePipeline;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (candles): BarInput[]; default: not declared
- return.applyBars: <P, Out>(indicator: Indicator<P, BarInput, Out>, parameters: P, options: AliasOpt & { as: string; }) => FeaturePipeline; default: not declared — Apply any bar indicator (BarInput → Out) to the candles.
- return.applySeries: <P, Out>(field: Field, indicator: Indicator<P, number, Out>, parameters: P, options: AliasOpt & { as: string; }) => FeaturePipeline; default: not declared — Apply any series indicator (number → Out) to a price field. The generic escape hatch that lets
the pipeline reach every indicator in the catalog, not just the named convenience methods.
- return.atr: (parameters?: WilderPeriodParameters, options?: AliasOpt) => FeaturePipeline; default: not declared — `parameters` is optional: ATR's Wilder period defaults to 14, exactly as `atr(bars)` does.
- return.bbands: (field: Field, parameters?: BollingerParameters, options?: AliasOpt) => FeaturePipeline; default: not declared — `parameters` is optional: Bollinger's period defaults to 20, exactly as `bbands(series)` does.
- return.column: (alias: string, values: FeatureColumn) => FeaturePipeline; default: not declared — Inject a precomputed column under an alias.
- return.ema: (field: Field, parameters: PeriodParameters, options?: AliasOpt) => FeaturePipeline; default: not declared
- return.field: (field: Field) => number[]; default: not declared — The raw `field` column (`close`, `high`, …) as a number array.
- return.macd: (field: Field, parameters?: MacdParameters, options?: AliasOpt) => FeaturePipeline; default: not declared
- return.obv: (options?: AliasOpt) => FeaturePipeline; default: not declared
- return.returns: (field: Field, options?: AliasOpt) => FeaturePipeline; default: not declared
- return.rollingVolatility: (field: Field, parameters: RollingVolatilityParameters, options?: AliasOpt) => FeaturePipeline; default: not declared
- return.rsi: (field: Field, parameters?: RsiParameters, options?: AliasOpt) => FeaturePipeline; default: not declared — `parameters` is optional: RSI's period defaults to 14, exactly as `rsi(series)` does.
- return.sma: (field: Field, parameters: PeriodParameters, options?: AliasOpt) => FeaturePipeline; default: not declared — The convenience methods all follow one order, and the order is the point: validate the alias,
then CALL THE INDICATOR, then build the auto-name from the parameters it just accepted.

The first version built the name first — `` `sma_${field}_${parameters.period}` `` — so a caller
who omitted `parameters` got `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'period')`
from the pipeline instead of `sma`'s own teaching `InputError`. Worse for `rsi` and `atr`, whose
direct forms default to 14: the fluent wrapper was STRICTER than the thing it wraps. Calling the
indicator first delegates every parameter question to the validator that owns it.
- return.toColumns: () => Record<string, FeatureColumn>; default: not declared — Columnar output keyed by alias.
- return.toRows: () => Record<string, unknown>[]; default: not declared — Row-oriented output: one object per bar with each alias as a key.
- return.vwap: (options?: AliasOpt) => FeaturePipeline; default: not declared
- return.wma: (field: Field, parameters: PeriodParameters, options?: AliasOpt) => FeaturePipeline; default: not declared

- explain().return.diagnostics.decomposition?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Named intermediate quantities the value decomposes into — a par spread's protection leg and
risky annuity, a forward variance's near/far legs. The H-series explain paths disclose their
arithmetic here so a caller can audit the ratio, not just receive it (3B.3).
- explain().return.diagnostics.engine?: string; default: not declared — Pricing/solver engine name, e.g. `black-scholes-merton`.
- explain().return.diagnostics.finiteDifferenceBumps?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Finite-difference engines: the ACTUAL bump sizes used for FD Greeks (spec P2.3) — adaptive
near the vol/time boundaries, so the caller can see exactly what was differenced.

`dividendYieldStep`. Each is the actual step differenced, in the unit of the coordinate it
bumps. (This doc named the retired `hS`/`hSig`/`hT`/`hR`/`hQ` keys for one release after the
emit sites had moved to the semantic names, so a caller following it read `undefined`.)

why, and — for automatic selection — every candidate considered with its verdict. This is the
machine-readable superset of `engine` + `autoReason` (which remain for compatibility);
`selected.name` always agrees with `engine` when both are present.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis#gapFill

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Opening gaps with fill tracking: the same events {@link gaps} detects, plus whether and when each
one closed. A gap fills when a later bar trades back to the prior close.

A gap requires the open to leave the prior bar's RANGE — above its high or below its low — which
is the definition {@link gaps} uses and the only one that means anything on a real tape. This
function previously fired on any open that merely differed from the prior close: on a 500-bar
random walk with no true gaps, `gaps()` returned 0 events and this returned 499, one per bar. The
two are now the same event universe, so `sizeFraction` and `minSizeFraction` mean the same thing
in both and a caller can pair them.

`minSizeFraction` filters small gaps as a FRACTION of the prior close (`0.005` = 0.5%), the same
unit `sizeFraction` reports. Default 0 — every detected gap.

```typescript
export declare function gapFill(bars: ArrayLike<BarInput>, options?: { minSizeFraction?: number; }): GapFillReport;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (bars): ArrayLike<BarInput>; default: not declared
- (options)?: { minSizeFraction?: number; }; default: not declared
- (options).minSizeFraction?: number; default: not declared
- return.assumptions: { conventionsVersion: string; minSizeFraction: number; }; default: not declared — Applied conventions, echoed (Law 2 report grammar).
- return.assumptions.conventionsVersion: string; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.minSizeFraction: number; default: not declared
- return.diagnostics: { warnings: QuantWarning[]; }; default: not declared — Structured warnings; always present (possibly empty).
- return.diagnostics.warnings: QuantWarning[]; default: not declared
- return.events: GapFillEvent[]; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis#gaps

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Opening gaps: this bar's open leaves the prior bar's RANGE (above its high or below its low).
`sizeFraction` is measured from the prior CLOSE — the level a fill has to trade back to — and
`minSizeFraction` filters in that same unit (`0.005` = 0.5%). {@link gapFill} detects exactly these
events and adds fill tracking.

```typescript
export declare function gaps(bars: ArrayLike<BarInput>, options?: { minSizeFraction?: number; }): GapsReport;
```

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis#getIndicator

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

The registered entry for `name`, or `undefined`.

The result is DEEPLY FROZEN. It is a view of the registry, not a copy to edit: mutating it used to
reach the facade's own validation allowlist.


rare default computed from another parameter. Bound at built-in construction/custom registration so
`.explain().assumptions.parameters` echoes every default that engages.

with an O(1) form later.
- fromJSON().return.toJSON: () => TechnicalAnalysisSnapshot; default: not declared
- fromJSON().return.value: number | null; default: not declared
- fromJSON(snapshot): TechnicalAnalysisSnapshot; default: not declared
- fromJSON(snapshot).kind: string; default: not declared
- fromJSON(snapshot).schemaVersion: number; default: not declared — Schema version, stamped at the serialization boundary by {@link snapshotOf}.
- fromJSON(snapshot).state: Record<string, unknown>; default: not declared — Indicator-private stream state. Round-trip it; never read into it.
- stream: (parameters?: TrendTestParameters | undefined) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis').LiveStream<number, number>; default: not declared
- stream().return.next: (input: number) => number | null; default: not declared
- stream().return.peek: (input: number) => number | null; default: not declared — The value that WOULD result from `next(input)` applied to the committed state, WITHOUT committing
it. Call it repeatedly with the forming bar's evolving value; call `next(input)` once at bar close
to commit. Between commits the committed state is untouched, so a live chart never repaints its
closed bars. The default cost is O(snapshot) per call (clone-and-apply); indicators may override
with an O(1) form later.
- stream().return.toJSON: () => TechnicalAnalysisSnapshot; default: not declared
- stream().return.value: number | null; default: not declared
- stream(parameters)?: TrendTestParameters | undefined; default: not declared
- stream(parameters).period?: number; default: not declared — Lookback (compare against the value `period` bars ago). Default 1.
- stream(parameters).strict?: boolean; default: not declared — Require every step in the window to move the same way (default false → just endpoints).

- fromJSON().return.peek: (input: number) => number | null; default: not declared — The value that WOULD result from `next(input)` applied to the committed state, WITHOUT committing

arithmetic here so a caller can audit the ratio, not just receive it (3B.3).
- explain().return.diagnostics.engine?: string; default: not declared — Pricing/solver engine name, e.g. `black-scholes-merton`.
- explain().return.diagnostics.finiteDifferenceBumps?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Finite-difference engines: the ACTUAL bump sizes used for FD Greeks (spec P2.3) — adaptive
near the vol/time boundaries, so the caller can see exactly what was differenced.
Keys: `spotStep`, `volatilityStep`, `timeStepYears`, `rateStep`, and — extended Greeks only —
`dividendYieldStep`. Each is the actual step differenced, in the unit of the coordinate it
bumps. (This doc named the retired `hS`/`hSig`/`hT`/`hR`/`hQ` keys for one release after the
emit sites had moved to the semantic names, so a caller following it read `undefined`.)
- explain().return.diagnostics.iterations?: number; default: not declared — Iteration count for iterative methods.
- explain().return.diagnostics.method?: string; default: not declared — Numerical method, e.g. `closed-form`, `brent`, `finite-difference`.
- explain().return.diagnostics.selection?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing').SelectionReport; default: not declared — The structured engine-selection report (Gate C, `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing`): who was selected,
why, and — for automatic selection — every candidate considered with its verdict. This is the
machine-readable superset of `engine` + `autoReason` (which remain for compatibility);
`selected.name` always agrees with `engine` when both are present.
- explain().return.diagnostics.timingMs?: number; default: not declared — Wall-clock timing in milliseconds, when measured.
- explain().return.diagnostics.warmup?: number; default: not declared — Series facades: number of leading output slots that are warmup sentinels (null/NaN) while the
computation seeds. Equals the input length when the indicator never emitted.
- explain().return.diagnostics.warnings: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').QuantWarning[]; default: not declared — Structured warnings; always present (possibly empty).
- explain().return.provenance?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Provenance; default: not declared — Optional data lineage when the inputs came from a provider.
- explain().return.value: number[]; default: not declared — The computed value. Never `NaN` or `±Infinity`: a value the model cannot produce is `null`
beside a diagnostic that says why (Law 7 — a warning never licenses a non-finite number).
- explain(input): ArrayLike<number>; default: not declared
- explain(parameters)?: { period?: number; } | undefined; default: not declared
- explain(parameters).period?: number; default: not declared

- fromJSON().return.next: (input: number) => number | null; default: not declared
- fromJSON().return.peek: (input: number) => number | null; default: not declared — The value that WOULD result from `next(input)` applied to the committed state, WITHOUT committing
it. Call it repeatedly with the forming bar's evolving value; call `next(input)` once at bar close
to commit. Between commits the committed state is untouched, so a live chart never repaints its
closed bars. The default cost is O(snapshot) per call (clone-and-apply); indicators may override
with an O(1) form later.

closed bars. The default cost is O(snapshot) per call (clone-and-apply); indicators may override
with an O(1) form later.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis#marketStructure

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Label the swing sequence (HH/HL/LH/LL) and flag breaks of structure. A higher-high while already
bullish is a continuation (BOS); a higher-high that reverses a bearish run is a change of character
(CHoCH), and symmetrically for lower-lows.

The first swing high and the first swing low carry `label: null` — a label is a comparison with the
previous swing of that kind, and there is none yet.

```typescript
export declare function marketStructure(bars: ArrayLike<BarInput>, options?: { strength?: number; }): MarketStructure;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (bars): ArrayLike<BarInput>; default: not declared
- (options)?: { strength?: number; }; default: not declared
- (options).strength?: number; default: not declared
- return.assumptions: { conventionsVersion: string; strength: number; }; default: not declared — Applied conventions, echoed (Law 2 report grammar).
- return.assumptions.conventionsVersion: string; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.strength: number; default: not declared
- return.diagnostics: { warnings: QuantWarning[]; }; default: not declared — Structured warnings; always present (possibly empty).
- return.diagnostics.warnings: QuantWarning[]; default: not declared
- return.events: StructureEvent[]; default: not declared
- return.swings: LabeledSwing[]; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis#orbRetest

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Opening-range retest aligned to the input: after a close breaks the range, `+1` on the first bar
that pulls back to touch the range high (a retest of an up-breakout), `−1` for a retest of the
range low. A new breakout in a direction re-arms that side; NaN during the opening range.

```typescript
export declare function orbRetest(bars: ArrayLike<BarInput>, options: OpeningRangeParameters): number[];
```

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis#previousSessionLevels

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

For each bar, the high/low/close of the PRIOR session (the fully-completed session before the bar's
own). `sessionIds[i]` groups bars (bars carry no timestamp, so the caller supplies the grouping —
pass day ids for "previous day high/low", week ids for "previous week high/low"). Bars in the first
session get NaN levels.

```typescript
export declare function previousSessionLevels(bars: ArrayLike<BarInput>, sessionIds: ArrayLike<number>): (PriorSessionLevel | null)[];
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (bars): ArrayLike<BarInput>; default: not declared
- (sessionIds): ArrayLike<number>; default: not declared

Price Distance — 2·(H−L) + |open − close[drift]| − |close − open|.


arithmetic here so a caller can audit the ratio, not just receive it (3B.3).

- explain().return.diagnostics.finiteDifferenceBumps?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Finite-difference engines: the ACTUAL bump sizes used for FD Greeks (spec P2.3) — adaptive
near the vol/time boundaries, so the caller can see exactly what was differenced.
Keys: `spotStep`, `volatilityStep`, `timeStepYears`, `rateStep`, and — extended Greeks only —
`dividendYieldStep`. Each is the actual step differenced, in the unit of the coordinate it
bumps. (This doc named the retired `hS`/`hSig`/`hT`/`hR`/`hQ` keys for one release after the
emit sites had moved to the semantic names, so a caller following it read `undefined`.)
- explain().return.diagnostics.iterations?: number; default: not declared — Iteration count for iterative methods.
- explain().return.diagnostics.method?: string; default: not declared — Numerical method, e.g. `closed-form`, `brent`, `finite-difference`.

why, and — for automatic selection — every candidate considered with its verdict. This is the
machine-readable superset of `engine` + `autoReason` (which remain for compatibility);
`selected.name` always agrees with `engine` when both are present.
- explain().return.diagnostics.timingMs?: number; default: not declared — Wall-clock timing in milliseconds, when measured.

beside a diagnostic that says why (Law 7 — a warning never licenses a non-finite number).

- fromJSON().return.peek: (input: BarInput) => number | null; default: not declared — The value that WOULD result from `next(input)` applied to the committed state, WITHOUT committing
it. Call it repeatedly with the forming bar's evolving value; call `next(input)` once at bar close
to commit. Between commits the committed state is untouched, so a live chart never repaints its
closed bars. The default cost is O(snapshot) per call (clone-and-apply); indicators may override

human-readable explanation of WHY that delegate was chosen (`engine` then names the delegate).
Absent when no auto-selection took place.
- explain().return.diagnostics.converged?: boolean; default: not declared — Whether an iterative procedure converged. `false` means the value is not trustworthy.
- explain().return.diagnostics.decomposition?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Named intermediate quantities the value decomposes into — a par spread's protection leg and
risky annuity, a forward variance's near/far legs. The H-series explain paths disclose their
arithmetic here so a caller can audit the ratio, not just receive it (3B.3).
- explain().return.diagnostics.engine?: string; default: not declared — Pricing/solver engine name, e.g. `black-scholes-merton`.
- explain().return.diagnostics.finiteDifferenceBumps?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Finite-difference engines: the ACTUAL bump sizes used for FD Greeks (spec P2.3) — adaptive
near the vol/time boundaries, so the caller can see exactly what was differenced.
Keys: `spotStep`, `volatilityStep`, `timeStepYears`, `rateStep`, and — extended Greeks only —
`dividendYieldStep`. Each is the actual step differenced, in the unit of the coordinate it
bumps. (This doc named the retired `hS`/`hSig`/`hT`/`hR`/`hQ` keys for one release after the
emit sites had moved to the semantic names, so a caller following it read `undefined`.)
- explain().return.diagnostics.iterations?: number; default: not declared — Iteration count for iterative methods.
- explain().return.diagnostics.method?: string; default: not declared — Numerical method, e.g. `closed-form`, `brent`, `finite-difference`.

why, and — for automatic selection — every candidate considered with its verdict. This is the
machine-readable superset of `engine` + `autoReason` (which remain for compatibility);
`selected.name` always agrees with `engine` when both are present.

risky annuity, a forward variance's near/far legs. The H-series explain paths disclose their
arithmetic here so a caller can audit the ratio, not just receive it (3B.3).

`dividendYieldStep`. Each is the actual step differenced, in the unit of the coordinate it
bumps. (This doc named the retired `hS`/`hSig`/`hT`/`hR`/`hQ` keys for one release after the

- explain().return.diagnostics.engine?: string; default: not declared — Pricing/solver engine name, e.g. `black-scholes-merton`.
- explain().return.diagnostics.finiteDifferenceBumps?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Finite-difference engines: the ACTUAL bump sizes used for FD Greeks (spec P2.3) — adaptive
near the vol/time boundaries, so the caller can see exactly what was differenced.
Keys: `spotStep`, `volatilityStep`, `timeStepYears`, `rateStep`, and — extended Greeks only —
`dividendYieldStep`. Each is the actual step differenced, in the unit of the coordinate it
bumps. (This doc named the retired `hS`/`hSig`/`hT`/`hR`/`hQ` keys for one release after the
emit sites had moved to the semantic names, so a caller following it read `undefined`.)
- explain().return.diagnostics.iterations?: number; default: not declared — Iteration count for iterative methods.

why, and — for automatic selection — every candidate considered with its verdict. This is the
machine-readable superset of `engine` + `autoReason` (which remain for compatibility);
`selected.name` always agrees with `engine` when both are present.
- explain().return.diagnostics.timingMs?: number; default: not declared — Wall-clock timing in milliseconds, when measured.

beside a diagnostic that says why (Law 7 — a warning never licenses a non-finite number).
- explain(input): ArrayLike<Pair>; default: not declared
- explain(parameters)?: { period?: number; } | undefined; default: not declared
- explain(parameters).period?: number; default: not declared
- fromJSON: (snapshot: TechnicalAnalysisSnapshot) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis').LiveStream<Pair, number>; default: not declared
- fromJSON().return.next: (input: Pair) => number | null; default: not declared
- fromJSON().return.peek: (input: Pair) => number | null; default: not declared — The value that WOULD result from `next(input)` applied to the committed state, WITHOUT committing

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis#readSnapshot

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Validate a snapshot envelope and open its state for checked reading.

`expected` is the kind the CALLING restorer produces. Passing it is what turns a restorer from
"rebuilds itself out of whatever numbers are in front of it" into one that knows whose snapshot it
is holding — and it costs the call site four characters.

A LIST is accepted for the handful of restorers that serve a FAMILY: one `MomentStream` class backs
both `standardDeviation` and `variance`, and reads which one it is off the snapshot. Those are the
restorers that genuinely may not pin a single kind — and a list still pins the family, which is the
whole guarantee. A restorer that pins nothing is the defect this parameter exists to remove, so
there is no form of this call that omits it.

Order matters, and each step is the precondition of the next: an envelope that is not an object has
no version; a version this build cannot read makes every field meaningless; a snapshot from another
indicator has the wrong fields entirely, so reporting a missing field would send the reader looking
in the wrong place.

```typescript
export declare function readSnapshot<Kind extends string>(snapshot: TechnicalAnalysisSnapshot, expected: Kind | readonly Kind[]): SnapshotState<Kind>;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (expected): Kind | readonly Kind[]; default: not declared
- (snapshot): TechnicalAnalysisSnapshot; default: not declared
- (snapshot).kind: string; default: not declared
- (snapshot).schemaVersion: number; default: not declared — Schema version, stamped at the serialization boundary by {@link snapshotOf}.
- (snapshot).state: Record<string, unknown>; default: not declared — Indicator-private stream state. Round-trip it; never read into it.
- return.boolean: (field: string) => boolean; default: not declared — A boolean flag.
- return.cached: <T>(field: string) => T | null; default: not declared — The LAST EMITTED OUTPUT, cached so a restored stream's `.value` is not blank until the next bar.

Deliberately the loosest accessor, and the only one that tolerates non-finite: `NaN` is a real
output. `acos` outside [-1, 1] is NaN; a `fairValueGaps` point reads `{ top: NaN, bottom: NaN }`
until a gap forms. Rejecting those would refuse to restore a correct stream.

What it still refuses is a value of a kind no indicator ever outputs — a string, a boolean, a
function — which is what a foreign or hand-edited snapshot looks like.

A missing key reads as `null` rather than throwing: the cache is an optimisation, and a snapshot
that predates an indicator caching its value must restore to "no value yet", not fail.
- return.child: (field: string) => TechnicalAnalysisSnapshot; default: not declared — A nested snapshot envelope — a composed indicator's child (`macd` carries three EMAs).

Only the SHAPE is checked here. The child's own `fromJSON` calls `readSnapshot` with the kind it
expects, so a child from the wrong indicator is convicted there, with that indicator's name on
the message rather than the parent's.
- return.children: (field: string) => TechnicalAnalysisSnapshot[]; default: not declared — A fresh array of nested snapshot envelopes.
- return.has: (field: string) => boolean; default: not declared — Does the state carry this key at all? For a field a newer build may legitimately omit.
- return.integer: (field: string) => number; default: not declared — A whole number ≥ 0 — a count, an index, a bar offset. A fractional count restores a stream whose
window boundaries never line up again, which shows up as an off-by-a-fraction output rather than
as an error.
- return.kind: Kind; default: not declared — The indicator kind this state belongs to — the prefix on every message, and, for a FAMILY
restorer, the narrowed member the guard just proved. `readSnapshot(s, MOMENT_KINDS)` hands back
a state whose `kind` is `'standardDeviation' | 'variance'`, so the restorer feeds it straight
into its constructor instead of re-asserting `snapshot.kind as string` — which is the cast the
guard exists to make unnecessary.
- return.literal: <T extends string | number>(field: string, allowed: readonly T[]) => T; default: not declared — A value drawn from a closed set — a mode, a method, a moving-average family, a trade direction.

Numbers as well as strings: `TradeDirection` is `-1 | 0 | 1`, and reading it as a plain number
would accept `7` as a trade direction.
- return.literals: <T extends string | number>(field: string, allowed: readonly T[]) => T[]; default: not declared — A fresh array of values drawn from a closed set.
- return.lookback: (field: string) => number; default: not declared — A lookback: an integer ≥ 1.

This is the asymmetry the reader exists to close. `ta.rsi.stream({ period: -3 })` throws from
`requirePeriod`; `RsiStream.fromJSON` read the same number straight out of state and built a
stream with a negative window, which produces `undefined` buffer reads and silent NaN.
- return.number: (field: string) => number; default: not declared — A number: sums, running averages, thresholds, multipliers.

Non-finite is permitted HERE and refused at the door. `readSnapshot` has already walked the whole
state: an encoded non-finite has been decoded (the indicator computed it — a zero price series
makes every log-return NaN), and a raw one has been rejected as damage. By the time an accessor
runs, `NaN` can only mean the first.
- return.numberOrNull: (field: string) => number | null; default: not declared — A number or `null` — a running value that has not been established yet.
- return.numberRows: (field: string) => number[][]; default: not declared — A fresh array of fresh number arrays — a matrix of windows.
- return.numbers: (field: string) => number[]; default: not declared — A FRESH array of finite numbers.

Fresh matters: the previous `state['buf'] as number[]` aliased the caller's snapshot, so two
streams restored from one snapshot object shared a buffer and corrupted each other. Restorers
used to spell that defence themselves (`[...(state['buf'] as number[])]`) and could forget to.
- return.numbersOrNull: (field: string) => number[] | null; default: not declared — A fresh array of finite numbers, or `null`.
- return.optionalNumber: (field: string) => number | undefined; default: not declared — A number the state may omit entirely (an optional parameter a stream carries).
- return.optionalNumbers: (field: string) => number[] | undefined; default: not declared — A fresh array of finite numbers the state may omit.
- return.raw: Record<string, unknown>; default: not declared — The raw state object. For a restorer that must hand a whole sub-object to a helper.
- return.record: <T>(field: string) => T; default: not declared — A structured record the indicator persists whole — a bar, a candle, an accumulator.

Members are not walked: their shape is the indicator's own business and varies per record type.
The check is that it IS a record, which is what separates a usable snapshot from `"acc"` or `7`.
- return.recordOrNull: <T>(field: string) => T | null; default: not declared — A structured record, or `null` when the indicator has not established one.
- return.records: <T>(field: string) => T[]; default: not declared — A fresh array of structured records — persisted bars, candles, levels.
- return.text: (field: string) => string; default: not declared — A string.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis#resample

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Resample ascending timestamped bars to a higher timeframe on epoch-aligned buckets. OHLC =
first-open / max-high / min-low / last-close; volume is summed; VWAP is volume-weighted over the
bucket's typical prices. Only COMPLETED buckets are emitted by default — the final (forming) bucket
is emitted only with `{ includePartial: true }` and flagged `partial: true`. Bars must be ascending
by `timestampMs` (throws otherwise).

```typescript
export declare function resample(bars: ArrayLike<TimeBar>, interval: ResampleInterval, options?: ResampleOptions): ResampledBar[];
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (bars): ArrayLike<TimeBar>; default: not declared
- (interval): ResampleInterval; default: not declared
- (options)?: ResampleOptions; default: not declared
- (options).includePartial?: boolean; default: not declared — Emit the final, still-forming bucket (flagged `partial: true`). Default `false`.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis#rescale

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- explain().return.diagnostics: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Diagnostics & { warmup: number; }; default: not declared

- explain().return.diagnostics.converged?: boolean; default: not declared — Whether an iterative procedure converged. `false` means the value is not trustworthy.

risky annuity, a forward variance's near/far legs. The H-series explain paths disclose their
arithmetic here so a caller can audit the ratio, not just receive it (3B.3).
- explain().return.diagnostics.engine?: string; default: not declared — Pricing/solver engine name, e.g. `black-scholes-merton`.
- explain().return.diagnostics.finiteDifferenceBumps?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Finite-difference engines: the ACTUAL bump sizes used for FD Greeks (spec P2.3) — adaptive

`dividendYieldStep`. Each is the actual step differenced, in the unit of the coordinate it
bumps. (This doc named the retired `hS`/`hSig`/`hT`/`hR`/`hQ` keys for one release after the
emit sites had moved to the semantic names, so a caller following it read `undefined`.)
- explain().return.diagnostics.iterations?: number; default: not declared — Iteration count for iterative methods.
- explain().return.diagnostics.method?: string; default: not declared — Numerical method, e.g. `closed-form`, `brent`, `finite-difference`.
- explain().return.diagnostics.selection?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing').SelectionReport; default: not declared — The structured engine-selection report (Gate C, `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing`): who was selected,
why, and — for automatic selection — every candidate considered with its verdict. This is the
machine-readable superset of `engine` + `autoReason` (which remain for compatibility);
`selected.name` always agrees with `engine` when both are present.
- explain().return.diagnostics.timingMs?: number; default: not declared — Wall-clock timing in milliseconds, when measured.
- explain().return.diagnostics.warmup?: number; default: not declared — Series facades: number of leading output slots that are warmup sentinels (null/NaN) while the
computation seeds. Equals the input length when the indicator never emitted.
- explain().return.diagnostics.warnings: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').QuantWarning[]; default: not declared — Structured warnings; always present (possibly empty).
- explain().return.provenance?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Provenance; default: not declared — Optional data lineage when the inputs came from a provider.
- explain().return.value: number[]; default: not declared — The computed value. Never `NaN` or `±Infinity`: a value the model cannot produce is `null`
beside a diagnostic that says why (Law 7 — a warning never licenses a non-finite number).
- explain(input): ArrayLike<number>; default: not declared

- fromJSON().return.peek: (input: number) => number | null; default: not declared — The value that WOULD result from `next(input)` applied to the committed state, WITHOUT committing
it. Call it repeatedly with the forming bar's evolving value; call `next(input)` once at bar close
to commit. Between commits the committed state is untouched, so a live chart never repaints its
closed bars. The default cost is O(snapshot) per call (clone-and-apply); indicators may override
with an O(1) form later.
- fromJSON().return.toJSON: () => TechnicalAnalysisSnapshot; default: not declared
- fromJSON().return.value: number | null; default: not declared
- fromJSON(snapshot): TechnicalAnalysisSnapshot; default: not declared
- fromJSON(snapshot).kind: string; default: not declared

- fromJSON(snapshot).state: Record<string, unknown>; default: not declared — Indicator-private stream state. Round-trip it; never read into it.
- stream: (parameters?: RescaleParameters | undefined) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis').LiveStream<number, number>; default: not declared
- stream().return.next: (input: number) => number | null; default: not declared

`.explain().assumptions.parameters` echoes every default that engages.

- return.indicator.fromJSON: (snapshot: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis').TechnicalAnalysisSnapshot) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis').LiveStream<any, any>; default: not declared

- return.name: string; default: not declared
- return.output: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis').IndicatorOutputMetadata; default: not declared — The indicator's output metadata (recursive value schema + optional visualization) — Wave 6 §4.

- explain().return.diagnostics: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Diagnostics & { warmup: number; }; default: not declared
- explain().return.diagnostics.autoReason?: string; default: not declared — When a meta-engine (e.g. `engines.auto()`) selected a delegate, this is a one-sentence,
human-readable explanation of WHY that delegate was chosen (`engine` then names the delegate).
Absent when no auto-selection took place.
- explain().return.diagnostics.converged?: boolean; default: not declared — Whether an iterative procedure converged. `false` means the value is not trustworthy.
- explain().return.diagnostics.decomposition?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Named intermediate quantities the value decomposes into — a par spread's protection leg and
risky annuity, a forward variance's near/far legs. The H-series explain paths disclose their
arithmetic here so a caller can audit the ratio, not just receive it (3B.3).
- explain().return.diagnostics.engine?: string; default: not declared — Pricing/solver engine name, e.g. `black-scholes-merton`.
- explain().return.diagnostics.finiteDifferenceBumps?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Finite-difference engines: the ACTUAL bump sizes used for FD Greeks (spec P2.3) — adaptive
near the vol/time boundaries, so the caller can see exactly what was differenced.
Keys: `spotStep`, `volatilityStep`, `timeStepYears`, `rateStep`, and — extended Greeks only —
`dividendYieldStep`. Each is the actual step differenced, in the unit of the coordinate it
bumps. (This doc named the retired `hS`/`hSig`/`hT`/`hR`/`hQ` keys for one release after the
emit sites had moved to the semantic names, so a caller following it read `undefined`.)
- explain().return.diagnostics.iterations?: number; default: not declared — Iteration count for iterative methods.
- explain().return.diagnostics.method?: string; default: not declared — Numerical method, e.g. `closed-form`, `brent`, `finite-difference`.
- explain().return.diagnostics.selection?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing').SelectionReport; default: not declared — The structured engine-selection report (Gate C, `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing`): who was selected,
why, and — for automatic selection — every candidate considered with its verdict. This is the
machine-readable superset of `engine` + `autoReason` (which remain for compatibility);
`selected.name` always agrees with `engine` when both are present.
- explain().return.diagnostics.timingMs?: number; default: not declared — Wall-clock timing in milliseconds, when measured.
- explain().return.diagnostics.warmup?: number; default: not declared — Series facades: number of leading output slots that are warmup sentinels (null/NaN) while the
computation seeds. Equals the input length when the indicator never emitted.

beside a diagnostic that says why (Law 7 — a warning never licenses a non-finite number).

- fromJSON().return.peek: (input: number) => number | null; default: not declared — The value that WOULD result from `next(input)` applied to the committed state, WITHOUT committing

`dividendYieldStep`. Each is the actual step differenced, in the unit of the coordinate it
bumps. (This doc named the retired `hS`/`hSig`/`hT`/`hR`/`hQ` keys for one release after the

why, and — for automatic selection — every candidate considered with its verdict. This is the
machine-readable superset of `engine` + `autoReason` (which remain for compatibility);

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis#rsi

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Wilder's RSI (period 14 default, disclosed via `.explain()`).

Flat-series convention: when the average loss over the window is zero (a flat or monotonically
rising series), TotalFinance returns **100** (the RS → ∞ limit; TradingView's convention). TA-Lib
emits 0 there and pandas-ta NaN — see `docs/compatibility/talib-differences.md`.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis#searchIndicators

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Filter the registry by a name/alias search and category, then paginate — the token-lean alternative to
pulling all ~335 indicators. `query` matches the canonical name or any TA-Lib/pandas/TradingView alias.
`match: 'auto'` (default) uses exact/substring hits when any exist and falls back to a deterministic
Damerau–Levenshtein fuzzy match only when they do not; queried rows carry inspectable `match` evidence.
See `docs/specs/wave6-quant-moats.md` §4.

```typescript
export declare function searchIndicators(options?: SearchIndicatorsOptions): SearchIndicatorsResult;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (options)?: SearchIndicatorsOptions; default: not declared
- (options).category?: IndicatorCategory; default: not declared
- (options).limit?: number; default: not declared — Non-negative safe-integer page size; omit for all matches.
- (options).match?: SearchMatchMode; default: not declared — Match mode (default `'auto'`). Only meaningful with a `query`.
- (options).minScore?: number; default: not declared — Minimum fuzzy similarity in `[0, 1]` (default `0.7`). Only used for fuzzy matching, needs a `query`.
- (options).offset?: number; default: not declared — Non-negative safe-integer page offset; default 0.
- (options).query?: string; default: not declared — Case-insensitive substring/fuzzy match of the canonical name OR any alias.
- return.indicators: IndicatorRow[]; default: not declared
- return.limit: number | null; default: not declared — The applied page size (`null` = unbounded).
- return.offset: number; default: not declared
- return.total: number; default: not declared — Matches before pagination.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis#snapshotOf

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Stamp indicator state into the public envelope. Every `toJSON` goes through here.

This is also where the state becomes JSON-SAFE: after `snapshotOf`, no number in the tree is
non-finite, so `JSON.stringify` is lossless and any raw `NaN` a reader later encounters can only
have come from damage — which is what lets {@link SnapshotState} refuse it.

`kind` is guarded because the natural wrong call is `snapshotOf(stream)` — reaching for the
serializer as if it took the thing to serialize. That produced an envelope whose `kind` was a live
stream object and whose `state` was `undefined`: it survives `JSON.stringify` (as `{}`) and only
fails much later, at a `fromJSON` that cannot say why.

```typescript
export declare function snapshotOf(kind: string, state: Record<string, unknown>): TechnicalAnalysisSnapshot;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (kind): string; default: not declared
- (state): Record<string, unknown>; default: not declared
- return.kind: string; default: not declared
- return.schemaVersion: number; default: not declared — Schema version, stamped at the serialization boundary by {@link snapshotOf}.
- return.state: Record<string, unknown>; default: not declared — Indicator-private stream state. Round-trip it; never read into it.

with an O(1) form later.

- (parameters)?: StochasticParameters | undefined; default: not declared
- (parameters).dPeriod?: number; default: not declared — %D smoothing. Defaults to 3 (universal).
- (parameters).kPeriod?: number; default: not declared — %K lookback. Defaults to 14 (Lane; universal); echoed via `.explain()`.
- (parameters).smoothK?: number; default: not declared — SMA smoothing applied to the raw %K before %D — the standard SLOW stochastic (TA-Lib STOCH's
`slowk_period`, typically 3). Defaults to 1: no smoothing, i.e. the FAST stochastic.
- explain: (input: ArrayLike<BarInput>, parameters?: StochasticParameters | undefined) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis').TechnicalAnalysisExplain<StochasticPoint>; default: not declared

- explain().return.diagnostics: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Diagnostics & { warmup: number; }; default: not declared
- explain().return.diagnostics.autoReason?: string; default: not declared — When a meta-engine (e.g. `engines.auto()`) selected a delegate, this is a one-sentence,
human-readable explanation of WHY that delegate was chosen (`engine` then names the delegate).
Absent when no auto-selection took place.
- explain().return.diagnostics.converged?: boolean; default: not declared — Whether an iterative procedure converged. `false` means the value is not trustworthy.
- explain().return.diagnostics.decomposition?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Named intermediate quantities the value decomposes into — a par spread's protection leg and
risky annuity, a forward variance's near/far legs. The H-series explain paths disclose their
arithmetic here so a caller can audit the ratio, not just receive it (3B.3).
- explain().return.diagnostics.engine?: string; default: not declared — Pricing/solver engine name, e.g. `black-scholes-merton`.
- explain().return.diagnostics.finiteDifferenceBumps?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Finite-difference engines: the ACTUAL bump sizes used for FD Greeks (spec P2.3) — adaptive
near the vol/time boundaries, so the caller can see exactly what was differenced.
Keys: `spotStep`, `volatilityStep`, `timeStepYears`, `rateStep`, and — extended Greeks only —
`dividendYieldStep`. Each is the actual step differenced, in the unit of the coordinate it
bumps. (This doc named the retired `hS`/`hSig`/`hT`/`hR`/`hQ` keys for one release after the
emit sites had moved to the semantic names, so a caller following it read `undefined`.)
- explain().return.diagnostics.iterations?: number; default: not declared — Iteration count for iterative methods.
- explain().return.diagnostics.method?: string; default: not declared — Numerical method, e.g. `closed-form`, `brent`, `finite-difference`.

why, and — for automatic selection — every candidate considered with its verdict. This is the
machine-readable superset of `engine` + `autoReason` (which remain for compatibility);
`selected.name` always agrees with `engine` when both are present.
- explain().return.diagnostics.timingMs?: number; default: not declared — Wall-clock timing in milliseconds, when measured.
- explain().return.diagnostics.warmup?: number; default: not declared — Series facades: number of leading output slots that are warmup sentinels (null/NaN) while the

- explain().return.provenance?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Provenance; default: not declared — Optional data lineage when the inputs came from a provider.
- explain().return.value: StochasticPoint[]; default: not declared — The computed value. Never `NaN` or `±Infinity`: a value the model cannot produce is `null`
beside a diagnostic that says why (Law 7 — a warning never licenses a non-finite number).

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis#streamAsync

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Feed a stream from an **async iterable** source (spec §13.2 streaming adapters), yielding each
non-`null` (post-warmup) output as it is produced. Lets indicators consume live feeds — websockets,
async DB cursors, generators — without buffering the whole series. Pure: it reads only what the
source yields and never touches the clock.

```typescript
export declare function streamAsync<In, Out>(stream: IndicatorStream<In, Out>, source: AsyncIterable<In>): AsyncGenerator<Out>;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (source): AsyncIterable<In>; default: not declared
- (stream): IndicatorStream<In, Out>; default: not declared
- (stream).next: (input: In) => Out | null; default: not declared
- (stream).toJSON: () => TechnicalAnalysisSnapshot; default: not declared
- (stream).value: Out | null; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis#swings

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Swing highs/lows: a swing high is a bar whose high strictly exceeds the highs of the `strength`
bars on each side (and symmetrically for lows). The first and last `strength` bars can never be
swings. `strength` defaults to 2 (the Bill Williams fractal window).

```typescript
export declare function swings(bars: ArrayLike<BarInput>, options?: { strength?: number; }): Swings;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (bars): ArrayLike<BarInput>; default: not declared
- (options)?: { strength?: number; }; default: not declared
- (options).strength?: number; default: not declared
- return.assumptions: { conventionsVersion: string; strength: number; }; default: not declared — Applied conventions, echoed (Law 2 report grammar).
- return.assumptions.conventionsVersion: string; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.strength: number; default: not declared
- return.diagnostics: { warnings: QuantWarning[]; }; default: not declared — Structured warnings; always present (possibly empty).
- return.diagnostics.warnings: QuantWarning[]; default: not declared
- return.highs: SwingPoint[]; default: not declared
- return.lows: SwingPoint[]; default: not declared

risky annuity, a forward variance's near/far legs. The H-series explain paths disclose their
arithmetic here so a caller can audit the ratio, not just receive it (3B.3).

- explain().return.diagnostics.finiteDifferenceBumps?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Finite-difference engines: the ACTUAL bump sizes used for FD Greeks (spec P2.3) — adaptive
near the vol/time boundaries, so the caller can see exactly what was differenced.
Keys: `spotStep`, `volatilityStep`, `timeStepYears`, `rateStep`, and — extended Greeks only —
`dividendYieldStep`. Each is the actual step differenced, in the unit of the coordinate it
bumps. (This doc named the retired `hS`/`hSig`/`hT`/`hR`/`hQ` keys for one release after the
emit sites had moved to the semantic names, so a caller following it read `undefined`.)

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis#tickVolumeProfile

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Volume-by-price built from the **actual trade prints** (each trade's full size lands in the bucket
of its exact price — no bar-range smearing), with the POC, value area, and a per-price buy/sell
delta (footprint). This is the trade-level counterpart to the bar-based `volumeProfile`.

```typescript
export declare function tickVolumeProfile(trades: readonly Trade[], parameters?: TickVolumeProfileParameters): TickVolumeProfile;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (parameters)?: TickVolumeProfileParameters; default: not declared
- (parameters).bins?: number; default: not declared — Number of equal-width buckets between the min and max trade price. Default 50.
- (parameters).method?: AggressorMethod; default: not declared — Aggressor method for the buy/sell split. Default `'quote'` if quotes given, else `'tick'`.
- (parameters).quotes?: readonly Quote[]; default: not declared
- (parameters).tickSize?: number; default: not declared — Bucket width in price units (e.g. one tick). Mutually exclusive with `bins` (tickSize wins).
- (parameters).valueAreaFraction?: number; default: not declared — Fraction of total volume defining the value area. Default 0.7.
- (trades): readonly Trade[]; default: not declared
- return.assumptions: { bins: number | null; conventionsVersion: string; method: AggressorMethod; tickSize: number | null; valueAreaFraction: number; }; default: not declared — Applied conventions, echoed — the binning mode that WON is non-null (`tickSize` beats `bins`).
- return.assumptions.bins: number | null; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.conventionsVersion: string; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.method: AggressorMethod; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis#tosStdevAll

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Thinkorswim Standard Deviation All: OLS line plus source-standard-deviation bands.

Omitting `period` uses **all history seen so far** (a causal, stream-friendly expanding window) —
a deliberate TotalFinance choice. This is NOT the single full-series regression overlay that ThinkorSwim
/ pandas-ta's `tos_stdevall` draws (a constant line over the whole chart); pass an explicit `period`
for a fixed rolling window. See docs/compatibility/talib-differences.md.

```typescript
export declare const tosStdevAll: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis').Indicator<TosStdevAllParameters, number, TosStdevAllPoint>;
```

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/technical-analysis#trix

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

TRIX — the 1-bar rate of change of a triple-smoothed EMA, in percent.

Warmup is TA-Lib's TRIX lookback, `3·(period − 1) + 1`: the triple EMA itself first exists at
`3·(period − 1)`, and the rate of change needs the bar after that.

- explain().return.diagnostics.converged?: boolean; default: not declared — Whether an iterative procedure converged. `false` means the value is not trustworthy.
- explain().return.diagnostics.decomposition?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Named intermediate quantities the value decomposes into — a par spread's protection leg and
risky annuity, a forward variance's near/far legs. The H-series explain paths disclose their
arithmetic here so a caller can audit the ratio, not just receive it (3B.3).
- explain().return.diagnostics.engine?: string; default: not declared — Pricing/solver engine name, e.g. `black-scholes-merton`.
- explain().return.diagnostics.finiteDifferenceBumps?: Record<string, number>; default: not declared — Finite-difference engines: the ACTUAL bump sizes used for FD Greeks (spec P2.3) — adaptive
near the vol/time boundaries, so the caller can see exactly what was differenced.
Keys: `spotStep`, `volatilityStep`, `timeStepYears`, `rateStep`, and — extended Greeks only —
`dividendYieldStep`. Each is the actual step differenced, in the unit of the coordinate it
bumps. (This doc named the retired `hS`/`hSig`/`hT`/`hR`/`hQ` keys for one release after the
emit sites had moved to the semantic names, so a caller following it read `undefined`.)
- explain().return.diagnostics.iterations?: number; default: not declared — Iteration count for iterative methods.
- explain().return.diagnostics.method?: string; default: not declared — Numerical method, e.g. `closed-form`, `brent`, `finite-difference`.
- explain().return.diagnostics.selection?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing').SelectionReport; default: not declared — The structured engine-selection report (Gate C, `@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core/pricing`): who was selected,
why, and — for automatic selection — every candidate considered with its verdict. This is the
machine-readable superset of `engine` + `autoReason` (which remain for compatibility);
`selected.name` always agrees with `engine` when both are present.
- explain().return.diagnostics.timingMs?: number; default: not declared — Wall-clock timing in milliseconds, when measured.

closed bars. The default cost is O(snapshot) per call (clone-and-apply); indicators may override
with an O(1) form later.
- stream().return.toJSON: () => TechnicalAnalysisSnapshot; default: not declared
- stream().return.value: number | null; default: not declared
- stream(parameters)?: { period?: number; } | undefined; default: not declared
- stream(parameters).period?: number; default: not declared
