### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility#ForwardSkewFacade

Kind: type; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

```typescript
export type ForwardSkewFacade = ((surface: VolatilitySurface, from: string | number, to: string | number, options?: {
    step?: number;
}) => number) & {
    explain: (surface: VolatilitySurface, from: string | number, to: string | number, options?: {
        step?: number;
    }) => Omit<Computed<number>, 'assumptions'> & {
        assumptions: ForwardSkewAssumptions;
    };
};
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (from): string | number; default: not declared
- (options)?: { step?: number; } | undefined; default: not declared
- (options).step?: number; default: not declared
- (surface): VolatilitySurface; default: not declared
- (surface).arbitrage: (options?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').ArbitrageCheckOptions) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').ArbitrageReport; default: not declared — Run the static no-arbitrage diagnostics (calendar + butterfly) over this surface.
- (surface).assumptions: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Assumptions<{ shock?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SurfaceShock; }>; default: not declared
- (surface).diagnostics: Diagnostics; default: not declared
- (surface).essvi?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').ESSVIParameters; default: not declared — The global eSSVI parameters when `model: 'essvi'`, else `undefined`.
- (surface).expiries: () => string[]; default: not declared — Sorted list of the surface's expiry labels.
- (surface).heston?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/options').HestonParameters; default: not declared — The global Heston parameters when `model: 'heston'`, else `undefined`.
- (surface).impliedVolatility: (strike: number, expiry: string | number) => number; default: not declared — Implied vol at `(strike, expiry)`. Throws if the surface is empty (never fabricates).
- (surface).impliedVolatilityByDelta: (callDelta: number, expiry: string | number) => number; default: not declared — Implied vol on the call-delta axis: interpolate the strike whose call-delta equals `callDelta`
(∈ (0, 1)) from the slice's stored delta ladder, then read the smile there. A 0.25 delta selects
the 25-delta call strike.
- (surface).impliedVolatilityByMoneyness: (moneyness: number, expiry: string | number, options?: { forward?: boolean; }) => number; default: not declared — Implied vol on the moneyness axis. `moneyness` is `K/S` (spot-moneyness) by default, or `K/F`
(forward-moneyness) when `forward` is set — so `impliedVolatilityByMoneyness(1, e)` is the at-the-money(-forward) vol.

For a NUMERIC `expiry` (a maturity in years) the forward is computed AT THAT MATURITY,
`F(t) = spot·e^{(r−q)·t}` — not borrowed from the nearest fitted slice, which anchored a
mid-expiry query to a neighbour's forward and shifted the ATM-forward point off by the carry
between them.
- (surface).lookup: (strike: number, expiry: string | number) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SurfaceLookup; default: not declared — Implied vol at `(strike, expiry)` with diagnostics. Strike uses the per-slice smile; expiry
interpolates total variance linearly between the two bracketing slices. `extrapolated` is true
when the query lies outside the fitted strike range or expiry range.
- (surface).model: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SurfaceModel; default: not declared
- (surface).points: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SurfacePoint[]; default: not declared
- (surface).shock: (shifts: { parallel?: number; skewTilt?: number; }, { sticky }?: { sticky?: 'strike' | 'moneyness'; }) => VolatilitySurface; default: not declared — Return a NEW surface with a shifted vol structure, produced WITHOUT re-fitting: each stored IV
sample gains a `parallel` offset plus a `skewTilt · k` skew rotation (`k = ln(K/forward)`,
log-moneyness), the per-slice deltas are recomputed from the shifted IVs, and only the
interpolators are rebuilt. The shock is echoed in the new surface's `assumptions.shock`.

`sticky`: `'strike'` (default) pins the tilt to each stored strike's own log-moneyness vs the slice
forward; `'moneyness'` lets the same additive shift travel with moneyness. Because the shift is
applied to the stored strike-indexed IV samples, both modes coincide at the stored strikes in this
eager v1 — the distinction only matters once a surface is re-anchored to a new spot/forward, which
this method does not do; the requested mode is recorded in `assumptions.shock.sticky` so a caller
that later re-anchors knows how the tilt was meant to travel.

Parametric models (`svi`/`sabr`/`heston`) have no closed-form shock, so the current smile is SAMPLED
at each slice's stored strikes, those samples are shifted, and the result DEGRADES to
`'interpolated'` with a `volatility.shock_degraded_to_interpolated` `warn` — the parametric fit is not
re-fit. Non-parametric models (`raw`/`interpolated`/`smoothed`) are preserved.
- (surface).slice: (expiry: string | number) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SurfaceSlice | undefined; default: not declared — The smile at an expiry (exact label or nearest by `t`), or `undefined` if none.
- (surface).slices: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SurfaceSlice[]; default: not declared
- (surface).ssvi?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SSVIParameters; default: not declared — The global SSVI parameters when `model: 'ssvi'`, else `undefined`.
- (surface).toJSON: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').VolatilitySurfaceSnapshot; default: not declared — Serialize the surface to a plain, JSON-safe {@link VolatilitySurfaceSnapshot} (no closures). Restore it
with {@link VolatilitySurface.fromJSON}; the pair round-trips `iv()` identically on all six models.
- (surface).toRows: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SurfaceRow[]; default: not declared — The smile-chart / heatmap feed: one {@link SurfaceRow} per (slice, stored strike), with
`logMoneyness = ln(strike/forward)` and the stored `delta`/`iv`. Per the workspace missing-value
policy (WS2.12), any non-finite chart-facing numeric is emitted as `null` (never `NaN`, never
omitted).
- (to): string | number; default: not declared
- explain: (surface: VolatilitySurface, from: string | number, to: string | number, options?: { step?: number; }) => Omit<Computed<number>, 'assumptions'> & { assumptions: ForwardSkewAssumptions; }; default: not declared
- explain().return.assumptions: ForwardSkewAssumptions; default: not declared
- explain().return.diagnostics: Diagnostics; default: not declared — How the value was computed, plus any warnings.
- explain().return.provenance?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Provenance; default: not declared — Optional data lineage when the inputs came from a provider.
- explain().return.value: number; default: not declared — The computed value. Never `NaN` or `±Infinity`: a value the model cannot produce is `null`
beside a diagnostic that says why (Law 7 — a warning never licenses a non-finite number).
- explain(from): string | number; default: not declared
- explain(options)?: { step?: number; } | undefined; default: not declared
- explain(options).step?: number; default: not declared
- explain(surface): VolatilitySurface; default: not declared
- explain(surface).arbitrage: (options?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').ArbitrageCheckOptions) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').ArbitrageReport; default: not declared — Run the static no-arbitrage diagnostics (calendar + butterfly) over this surface.
- explain(surface).assumptions: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Assumptions<{ shock?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SurfaceShock; }>; default: not declared
- explain(surface).diagnostics: Diagnostics; default: not declared
- explain(surface).essvi?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').ESSVIParameters; default: not declared — The global eSSVI parameters when `model: 'essvi'`, else `undefined`.
- explain(surface).expiries: () => string[]; default: not declared — Sorted list of the surface's expiry labels.
- explain(surface).heston?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/options').HestonParameters; default: not declared — The global Heston parameters when `model: 'heston'`, else `undefined`.
- explain(surface).impliedVolatility: (strike: number, expiry: string | number) => number; default: not declared — Implied vol at `(strike, expiry)`. Throws if the surface is empty (never fabricates).

this method does not do; the requested mode is recorded in `assumptions.shock.sticky` so a caller
that later re-anchors knows how the tilt was meant to travel.

Parametric models (`svi`/`sabr`/`heston`) have no closed-form shock, so the current smile is SAMPLED
at each slice's stored strikes, those samples are shifted, and the result DEGRADES to
`'interpolated'` with a `volatility.shock_degraded_to_interpolated` `warn` — the parametric fit is not
re-fit. Non-parametric models (`raw`/`interpolated`/`smoothed`) are preserved.
- (surface).slice: (expiry: string | number) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SurfaceSlice | undefined; default: not declared — The smile at an expiry (exact label or nearest by `t`), or `undefined` if none.
- (surface).slices: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SurfaceSlice[]; default: not declared
- (surface).ssvi?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SSVIParameters; default: not declared — The global SSVI parameters when `model: 'ssvi'`, else `undefined`.
- (surface).toJSON: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').VolatilitySurfaceSnapshot; default: not declared — Serialize the surface to a plain, JSON-safe {@link VolatilitySurfaceSnapshot} (no closures). Restore it
with {@link VolatilitySurface.fromJSON}; the pair round-trips `iv()` identically on all six models.
- (surface).toRows: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SurfaceRow[]; default: not declared — The smile-chart / heatmap feed: one {@link SurfaceRow} per (slice, stored strike), with
`logMoneyness = ln(strike/forward)` and the stored `delta`/`iv`. Per the workspace missing-value
policy (WS2.12), any non-finite chart-facing numeric is emitted as `null` (never `NaN`, never
omitted).
- (to): string | number; default: not declared
- explain: (surface: VolatilitySurface, from: string | number, to: string | number) => Omit<Computed<number>, 'assumptions'> & { assumptions: ForwardVolatilityAssumptions; }; default: not declared
- explain().return.assumptions: ForwardVolatilityAssumptions; default: not declared
- explain().return.diagnostics: Diagnostics; default: not declared — How the value was computed, plus any warnings.
- explain().return.provenance?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Provenance; default: not declared — Optional data lineage when the inputs came from a provider.
- explain().return.value: number; default: not declared — The computed value. Never `NaN` or `±Infinity`: a value the model cannot produce is `null`
beside a diagnostic that says why (Law 7 — a warning never licenses a non-finite number).
- explain(from): string | number; default: not declared
- explain(surface): VolatilitySurface; default: not declared
- explain(surface).arbitrage: (options?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').ArbitrageCheckOptions) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').ArbitrageReport; default: not declared — Run the static no-arbitrage diagnostics (calendar + butterfly) over this surface.
- explain(surface).assumptions: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Assumptions<{ shock?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SurfaceShock; }>; default: not declared
- explain(surface).diagnostics: Diagnostics; default: not declared
- explain(surface).essvi?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').ESSVIParameters; default: not declared — The global eSSVI parameters when `model: 'essvi'`, else `undefined`.
- explain(surface).expiries: () => string[]; default: not declared — Sorted list of the surface's expiry labels.
- explain(surface).heston?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/options').HestonParameters; default: not declared — The global Heston parameters when `model: 'heston'`, else `undefined`.
- explain(surface).impliedVolatility: (strike: number, expiry: string | number) => number; default: not declared — Implied vol at `(strike, expiry)`. Throws if the surface is empty (never fabricates).
- explain(surface).impliedVolatilityByDelta: (callDelta: number, expiry: string | number) => number; default: not declared — Implied vol on the call-delta axis: interpolate the strike whose call-delta equals `callDelta`
(∈ (0, 1)) from the slice's stored delta ladder, then read the smile there. A 0.25 delta selects
the 25-delta call strike.
- explain(surface).impliedVolatilityByMoneyness: (moneyness: number, expiry: string | number, options?: { forward?: boolean; }) => number; default: not declared — Implied vol on the moneyness axis. `moneyness` is `K/S` (spot-moneyness) by default, or `K/F`
(forward-moneyness) when `forward` is set — so `impliedVolatilityByMoneyness(1, e)` is the at-the-money(-forward) vol.

For a NUMERIC `expiry` (a maturity in years) the forward is computed AT THAT MATURITY,
`F(t) = spot·e^{(r−q)·t}` — not borrowed from the nearest fitted slice, which anchored a
mid-expiry query to a neighbour's forward and shifted the ATM-forward point off by the carry
between them.
- explain(surface).lookup: (strike: number, expiry: string | number) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SurfaceLookup; default: not declared — Implied vol at `(strike, expiry)` with diagnostics. Strike uses the per-slice smile; expiry
interpolates total variance linearly between the two bracketing slices. `extrapolated` is true
when the query lies outside the fitted strike range or expiry range.
- explain(surface).model: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SurfaceModel; default: not declared
- explain(surface).points: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SurfacePoint[]; default: not declared
- explain(surface).shock: (shifts: { parallel?: number; skewTilt?: number; }, { sticky }?: { sticky?: 'strike' | 'moneyness'; }) => VolatilitySurface; default: not declared — Return a NEW surface with a shifted vol structure, produced WITHOUT re-fitting: each stored IV
sample gains a `parallel` offset plus a `skewTilt · k` skew rotation (`k = ln(K/forward)`,
log-moneyness), the per-slice deltas are recomputed from the shifted IVs, and only the
interpolators are rebuilt. The shock is echoed in the new surface's `assumptions.shock`.

`sticky`: `'strike'` (default) pins the tilt to each stored strike's own log-moneyness vs the slice
forward; `'moneyness'` lets the same additive shift travel with moneyness. Because the shift is
applied to the stored strike-indexed IV samples, both modes coincide at the stored strikes in this
eager v1 — the distinction only matters once a surface is re-anchored to a new spot/forward, which
this method does not do; the requested mode is recorded in `assumptions.shock.sticky` so a caller
that later re-anchors knows how the tilt was meant to travel.

Parametric models (`svi`/`sabr`/`heston`) have no closed-form shock, so the current smile is SAMPLED
at each slice's stored strikes, those samples are shifted, and the result DEGRADES to
`'interpolated'` with a `volatility.shock_degraded_to_interpolated` `warn` — the parametric fit is not
re-fit. Non-parametric models (`raw`/`interpolated`/`smoothed`) are preserved.
- explain(surface).slice: (expiry: string | number) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SurfaceSlice | undefined; default: not declared — The smile at an expiry (exact label or nearest by `t`), or `undefined` if none.
- explain(surface).slices: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SurfaceSlice[]; default: not declared
- explain(surface).ssvi?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SSVIParameters; default: not declared — The global SSVI parameters when `model: 'ssvi'`, else `undefined`.
- explain(surface).toJSON: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').VolatilitySurfaceSnapshot; default: not declared — Serialize the surface to a plain, JSON-safe {@link VolatilitySurfaceSnapshot} (no closures). Restore it
with {@link VolatilitySurface.fromJSON}; the pair round-trips `iv()` identically on all six models.
- explain(surface).toRows: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SurfaceRow[]; default: not declared — The smile-chart / heatmap feed: one {@link SurfaceRow} per (slice, stored strike), with
`logMoneyness = ln(strike/forward)` and the stored `delta`/`iv`. Per the workspace missing-value
policy (WS2.12), any non-finite chart-facing numeric is emitted as `null` (never `NaN`, never
omitted).
- explain(to): string | number; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility#GarchFit

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

A fitted GARCH(1,1) model. `converged`/`iterations` mirror the optimizer result honestly.

```typescript
// ───────────────────────────────────── GARCH(1,1) ─────────────────────────────────────
/** A fitted GARCH(1,1) model. `converged`/`iterations` mirror the optimizer result honestly. */
export interface GarchFit {
    /** Constant term of the variance recursion (`> 0`). */
    omega: number;
    /** ARCH coefficient on the lagged squared return (`≥ 0`). */
    alpha: number;
    /** GARCH coefficient on the lagged conditional variance (`≥ 0`). */
    beta: number;
    /** `α + β` — the variance half-life driver; `< 1` for a stationary fit. */
    persistence: number;
    /** Unconditional variance `ω / (1 − α − β)` the forecast mean-reverts to. */
    longRunVariance: number;
    /** Maximized Gaussian log-likelihood; `null` when the likelihood is degenerate (disclosed). */
    logLikelihood: number | null;
    /** Whether the optimizer converged (never fabricated). */
    converged: boolean;
    /** Optimizer iterations performed. */
    iterations: number;
    /** Applied conventions, echoed (Law 2 report grammar). */
    assumptions: {
        conventionsVersion: string;
        mean: 'zero' | 'sample';
        observations: number;
        /** Whether the primary start was caller-supplied (`initialParameters`) or the classic (0.05, 0.90). */
        initialParameters: 'supplied' | 'default';
    };
    /** Structured warnings; a degenerate / non-converged fit explains itself here. */
    diagnostics: {
        warnings: QuantWarning[];
    };
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- alpha: number; default: not declared — ARCH coefficient on the lagged squared return (`≥ 0`).
- assumptions: { conventionsVersion: string; initialParameters: 'supplied' | 'default'; mean: 'zero' | 'sample'; observations: number; }; default: not declared — Applied conventions, echoed (Law 2 report grammar).
- assumptions.conventionsVersion: string; default: not declared
- assumptions.initialParameters: 'supplied' | 'default'; default: not declared — Whether the primary start was caller-supplied (`initialParameters`) or the classic (0.05, 0.90).
- assumptions.mean: 'zero' | 'sample'; default: not declared
- assumptions.observations: number; default: not declared
- beta: number; default: not declared — GARCH coefficient on the lagged conditional variance (`≥ 0`).
- converged: boolean; default: not declared — Whether the optimizer converged (never fabricated).
- diagnostics: { warnings: QuantWarning[]; }; default: not declared — Structured warnings; a degenerate / non-converged fit explains itself here.
- diagnostics.warnings: QuantWarning[]; default: not declared
- iterations: number; default: not declared — Optimizer iterations performed.
- logLikelihood: number | null; default: not declared — Maximized Gaussian log-likelihood; `null` when the likelihood is degenerate (disclosed).
- longRunVariance: number; default: not declared — Unconditional variance `ω / (1 − α − β)` the forecast mean-reverts to.
- omega: number; default: not declared — Constant term of the variance recursion (`> 0`).
- persistence: number; default: not declared — `α + β` — the variance half-life driver; `< 1` for a stationary fit.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility#MinimumVarianceDeltaOptions

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Inputs for {@link minimumVarianceDelta}. Provide exactly one of `volatilitySpotBeta` or `skewSlope`.

```typescript
/** Inputs for {@link minimumVarianceDelta}. Provide exactly one of `volatilitySpotBeta` or `skewSlope`. */
export interface MinimumVarianceDeltaOptions {
    type: OptionType;
    spot: number;
    strike: number;
    /** Time to expiry in years. */
    timeToExpiryYears: number;
    riskFreeRate: number;
    /** The option's implied vol (decimal). */
    volatility: number;
    /** Continuous dividend yield (decimal, default 0). */
    dividendYield?: number;
    /**
     * ∂σ/∂S directly (decimal vol **per $1 of spot**) — the empirical / minimum-variance β (preferred).
     * Take it from `estimateVolatilitySpotBeta(...).value.volatilitySpotBeta`, which is already in
     * these units. `stickyRegime`'s `volatilitySpotBetaPerLogSpot` is ∂σ/∂lnS — `S ×` larger — so
     * divide it by spot before passing it here, or the smile adjustment is scaled by the spot price.
     */
    volatilitySpotBeta?: number;
    /** ∂σ/∂ln(K) (`SkewMetrics.skewSlope`) — mapped to β via `regime`. */
    skewSlope?: number;
    /** How `skewSlope` maps to β. Default `'sticky-moneyness'`. */
    regime?: 'sticky-strike' | 'sticky-moneyness';
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- dividendYield?: number; default: not declared — Continuous dividend yield (decimal, default 0).
- regime?: 'sticky-strike' | 'sticky-moneyness'; default: not declared — How `skewSlope` maps to β. Default `'sticky-moneyness'`.
- riskFreeRate: number; default: not declared
- skewSlope?: number; default: not declared — ∂σ/∂ln(K) (`SkewMetrics.skewSlope`) — mapped to β via `regime`.
- spot: number; default: not declared
- strike: number; default: not declared
- timeToExpiryYears: number; default: not declared — Time to expiry in years.
- type: OptionType; default: not declared
- volatility: number; default: not declared — The option's implied vol (decimal).
- volatilitySpotBeta?: number; default: not declared — ∂σ/∂S directly (decimal vol **per $1 of spot**) — the empirical / minimum-variance β (preferred).
Take it from `estimateVolatilitySpotBeta(...).value.volatilitySpotBeta`, which is already in
these units. `stickyRegime`'s `volatilitySpotBetaPerLogSpot` is ∂σ/∂lnS — `S ×` larger — so
divide it by spot before passing it here, or the smile adjustment is scaled by the spot price.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility#RiskNeutralDistribution

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

```typescript
export interface RiskNeutralDistribution {
    /** Risk-neutral PDF at strike `K`: `e^{rT}·∂²C/∂K²` (clamped ≥ 0 — see {@link diagnostics}). */
    density(strike: number): number;
    /** Risk-neutral CDF `P(S_T ≤ K) = 1 + e^{rT}·∂C/∂K`, clamped to [0, 1]. */
    cdf(strike: number): number;
    probabilityBelow(strike: number): number;
    probabilityAbove(strike: number): number;
    probabilityBetween(lowerStrike: number, upperStrike: number): number;
    /**
     * LIVE disclosure channel for the two places this object silently repairs itself — it accumulates
     * as the closures are called, so read it AFTER querying (it starts empty):
     *
     *  • `model.limitation` "negative density clamped" — `∂²C/∂K²` came out negative, which means the
     *    smile is butterfly-arbitrageable there. The clamp keeps `density()` a density; the warning
     *    stops a caller integrating a repaired curve and calling it the market's distribution.
     *  • `model.limitation` "one-sided difference" — a query within `step` of zero, where the centred
     *    difference would price a NEGATIVE strike (which returned `NaN`).
     */
    diagnostics: Diagnostics;
}
```

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility#RiskReversalButterfly

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

The risk-reversal / butterfly decomposition of a smile.

```typescript
/** The risk-reversal / butterfly decomposition of a smile. */
export interface RiskReversalButterfly {
    /** ATM vol (at `K = forward`). */
    atmVolatility: number;
    /** The δ-delta call strike. */
    callStrike: number;
    /** The vol at the call strike. */
    callVolatility: number;
    /** The δ-delta put strike. */
    putStrike: number;
    /** The vol at the put strike. */
    putVolatility: number;
    /** `callVolatility − putVolatility` — the skew (< 0 ⇒ puts bid). */
    riskReversal: number;
    /** `(callVolatility + putVolatility)/2 − atmVolatility` — the curvature (> 0 ⇒ smile). */
    butterfly: number;
    delta: number;
    assumptions: {
        conventionsVersion: string;
        deltaConvention: 'forward';
        delta: number;
    };
    diagnostics: Diagnostics;
}
```

```typescript
/** Options for {@link calibrateSsvi}. */
export interface SSVICalibrationOptions {
    /** Curvature family; default `'power-law'`. */
    phi?: 'power-law' | 'heston';
    /**
     * Least-squares weighting of the total-variance residuals: `'uniform'` (default) or `'vega'` — weight each
     * point by its Black vega `∝ φ(d₁)·√t`, so liquid ATM/near-the-money strikes dominate the fit and thin,
     * low-vega wings are downweighted.
     */
    weight?: 'uniform' | 'vega';
    /** Outer-search iteration budget (default 1,000, maximum 10,000). */
    maximumIterations?: number;
    /** Outer-search tolerance (default 1e-12). */
    tolerance?: number;
    /**
     * Warm start for the `(ρ, φ)` search (Stage 4.5): `phi.kind` must equal the calibration's `phi`
     * family. The θ knots are fixed from the data and are not a start.
     */
    initialParameters?: {
        rho: number;
        phi: SSVIPhi;
    };
}
```

- tolerance?: number; default: not declared — Outer-search tolerance (default 1e-12).

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility#SSVISliceInput

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

One maturity slice of the market surface.

```typescript
/** One maturity slice of the market surface. */
export interface SSVISliceInput {
    /** Maturity in years. */
    timeToExpiryYears: number;
    /** Log-moneyness `ln(K/F)` per observation. */
    k: number[];
    /** Total variance `σ²·t` aligned to `k`. Provide this or `iv`. */
    w?: number[];
    /** Implied volatilities aligned to `k` (converted to `w = iv²·t`). Provide this or `w`. */
    impliedVolatility?: number[];
}
```

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility#SVICalibrationOptions

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

```typescript
export interface SVICalibrationOptions {
    /** Outer-search iteration budget (default 400, maximum 10,000). */
    maximumIterations?: number;
    /** Outer-search tolerance (default 1e-12). */
    tolerance?: number;
    /**
     * The slice's maturity in years. Supplied ⇒ the fit-vs-data deviation check (see
     * {@link calibrateSvi}) is expressed in true implied-VOL points, `σ = √(w/t)`. Omitted ⇒ `t = 1`,
     * i.e. the check runs on `√w = σ√t` — still a vol scale, but shrunk by `√t` on a short slice.
     */
    timeToExpiryYears?: number;
    /**
     * Warm start for the outer `(m, σ)` search (Stage 4.5). Tried FIRST, ahead of the four built-in
     * starts — ties keep the first, so a warm start never loses to a cold fit. `a`, `b`, and `ρ` are
     * solved by the inner normal equations at every `(m, σ)` and are therefore not accepted as
     * starts (a member the search cannot honor is refused, never ignored).
     */
    initialParameters?: SVIWarmStart;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- initialParameters?: SVIWarmStart; default: not declared — Warm start for the outer `(m, σ)` search (Stage 4.5). Tried FIRST, ahead of the four built-in
starts — ties keep the first, so a warm start never loses to a cold fit. `a`, `b`, and `ρ` are
solved by the inner normal equations at every `(m, σ)` and are therefore not accepted as
starts (a member the search cannot honor is refused, never ignored).
- initialParameters.m: number; default: not declared
- initialParameters.sigma: number; default: not declared — `> 0`.
- maximumIterations?: number; default: not declared — Outer-search iteration budget (default 400, maximum 10,000).
- timeToExpiryYears?: number; default: not declared — The slice's maturity in years. Supplied ⇒ the fit-vs-data deviation check (see
{@link calibrateSvi}) is expressed in true implied-VOL points, `σ = √(w/t)`. Omitted ⇒ `t = 1`,
i.e. the check runs on `√w = σ√t` — still a vol scale, but shrunk by `√t` on a short slice.
- tolerance?: number; default: not declared — Outer-search tolerance (default 1e-12).

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility#SVISmileInput

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Total-variance smile input for {@link calibrateSvi}: log-moneyness `k` and total variance `w` points.

```typescript
/**
 * Calibrate a raw-SVI slice to observed `(k, w)` total-variance points. Needs at least 5 distinct
 * strikes to identify the five parameters. The calibration is penalized for butterfly violations and
 * refined toward an arbitrage-free fit; the result carries its RMSE plus the verified
 * `butterflyFree` / `minButterflyG` diagnostics (it is *not* assumed arbitrage-free).
 *
 * **The fit is an arbitrage-free PROJECTION of the data, so it is also checked AGAINST the data.**
 * The butterfly penalty deliberately walks the fit away from an arbitrageable smile, and
 * `butterflyFree`/`minButterflyG` measure the FITTED slice's own density — they say nothing about how
 * far that slice ended up from the quotes. A smile that embeds butterfly arbitrage can therefore be
 * projected onto a clean SVI a hundred vol points away, which is a perfectly arbitrage-free answer to
 * a different question. So the result reports the fit-vs-data distance in implied-VOL points
 * (`σ = √(w/t)`, with `t` from `options.timeToExpiryYears`, default 1): when the RMSE exceeds
 * `max(0.005, 2% of mean IV)` or any single point is off by more than 5 vol points, `converged` is
 * `false` and a `volatility.calibration_fit_deviation` warning carries `{ rmse, maxDeviation }`.
 */
/** Total-variance smile input for {@link calibrateSvi}: log-moneyness `k` and total variance `w` points. */
export interface SVISmileInput {
    /** Log-moneyness `ln(K/F)` per observation. */
    k: number[];
    /** Total implied variance `σ²·t` aligned to `k`. */
    w: number[];
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- k: number[]; default: not declared — Log-moneyness `ln(K/F)` per observation.
- w: number[]; default: not declared — Total implied variance `σ²·t` aligned to `k`.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility#SabrBartlettGreeks

```typescript
/** The Bartlett (minimum-variance) SABR greeks, alongside the naive SABR greeks they adjust. */
```

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility#StickyRegime

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

The measured regime.

```typescript
/** The measured regime. */
export interface StickyRegime {
    /**
     * `∂σ_K/∂lnS` — the empirical vol-spot beta from the regression, **per LOG spot** (vol points per
     * 100% spot move). NOT the same quantity as `VolatilitySpotBeta.volatilitySpotBeta` /
     * `minimumVarianceDelta({ volatilitySpotBeta })`, which are `∂σ/∂S` — per DOLLAR. The two differ by
     * a factor of `S`: feeding this straight into the hedge would scale the smile adjustment by the
     * spot price. Divide by the reference spot first (`estimateVolatilitySpotBeta` does exactly that
     * when its `basis` is `'log'`).
     */
    volatilitySpotBetaPerLogSpot: number;
    tStatistic: number;
    /** How much of the fixed-strike vol's change spot returns explain. */
    rSquared: number;
    /** Position on the axis: 0 = sticky-strike, 1 = sticky-moneyness (`= −β/skewSlope`); `null` if no reference. */
    stickiness: number | null;
    regime: 'sticky-strike' | 'sticky-moneyness' | 'intermediate' | 'indeterminate';
    observations: number;
    assumptions: {
        conventionsVersion: string;
        skewSlope: number | null;
    };
    diagnostics: Diagnostics;
}
```

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility#SurfaceConfig

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Non-market surface configuration: price source, model, and per-model calibration knobs (WS3.2).

```typescript
/** Non-market surface configuration: price source, model, and per-model calibration knobs (WS3.2). */
export interface SurfaceConfig {
    /** Which quote price to invert when a quote has no `impliedVolatility` (default `mid`). */
    priceSource?: PriceSource;
    /**
     * `interpolated` (PCHIP, default), `raw` (linear), `smoothed` (Gaussian kernel), `svi`/`sabr`
     * (parametric per expiry), `ssvi` (one global arbitrage-free surface SVI), `essvi` (SSVI with a
     * per-maturity skew), or `heston` (one global stochastic-vol model fit to the whole surface).
     */
    model?: SurfaceModel;
    /** Below this many usable strikes, an expiry slice is flagged sparse (default 3). */
    minQuotesPerExpiry?: number;
    /** SABR backbone exponent β ∈ [0, 1] for `model: 'sabr'` (default 0.5). */
    sabrBeta?: number;
    /** SABR Hagan expansion for `model: 'sabr'` (default `'lognormal'`). */
    sabrVolatilityType?: SabrVolatilityType;
    /** Gaussian-kernel bandwidth (in log-moneyness) for `model: 'smoothed'` (default auto). */
    smoothingBandwidth?: number;
    /** Warm start (partial pin) for the global `model: 'heston'` calibration — threads into `calibrateHestonSurface`'s `initialParameters`. */
    hestonInitialParameters?: Partial<HestonParameters>;
    /** COS cosine-term count for the `model: 'heston'` calibration & evaluation (default 128). */
    cosineExpansionTerms?: number;
    /** Curvature family for the global `model: 'ssvi'` calibration (default `'power-law'`). */
    ssviPhi?: 'power-law' | 'heston';
    /** Least-squares weighting for `model: 'ssvi'`: `'uniform'` (default) or `'vega'` (ATM-dominant). */
    ssviWeight?: 'uniform' | 'vega';
    /** Curvature family for the global `model: 'essvi'` calibration (default `'power-law'`). */
    essviPhi?: 'power-law' | 'heston';
    /** Least-squares weighting for `model: 'essvi'`: `'uniform'` (default) or `'vega'` (ATM-dominant). */
    essviWeight?: 'uniform' | 'vega';
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- cosineExpansionTerms?: number; default: not declared — COS cosine-term count for the `model: 'heston'` calibration & evaluation (default 128).
- essviPhi?: 'power-law' | 'heston'; default: not declared — Curvature family for the global `model: 'essvi'` calibration (default `'power-law'`).
- essviWeight?: 'vega' | 'uniform'; default: not declared — Least-squares weighting for `model: 'essvi'`: `'uniform'` (default) or `'vega'` (ATM-dominant).
- hestonInitialParameters?: Partial<HestonParameters>; default: not declared — Warm start (partial pin) for the global `model: 'heston'` calibration — threads into `calibrateHestonSurface`'s `initialParameters`.
- hestonInitialParameters.kappa?: number; default: not declared — Mean-reversion speed κ.
- hestonInitialParameters.rho?: number; default: not declared — Spot/variance correlation ρ ∈ [−1, 1].
- hestonInitialParameters.sigma?: number; default: not declared — Volatility of variance ξ ("vol of vol").
- hestonInitialParameters.theta?: number; default: not declared — Long-run variance θ.
- hestonInitialParameters.v0?: number; default: not declared — Initial instantaneous variance v₀ (= σ₀²).
- minQuotesPerExpiry?: number; default: not declared — Below this many usable strikes, an expiry slice is flagged sparse (default 3).
- model?: SurfaceModel; default: not declared — `interpolated` (PCHIP, default), `raw` (linear), `smoothed` (Gaussian kernel), `svi`/`sabr`
(parametric per expiry), `ssvi` (one global arbitrage-free surface SVI), `essvi` (SSVI with a
per-maturity skew), or `heston` (one global stochastic-vol model fit to the whole surface).
- priceSource?: PriceSource; default: not declared — Which quote price to invert when a quote has no `impliedVolatility` (default `mid`).
- sabrBeta?: number; default: not declared — SABR backbone exponent β ∈ [0, 1] for `model: 'sabr'` (default 0.5).
- sabrVolatilityType?: SabrVolatilityType; default: not declared — SABR Hagan expansion for `model: 'sabr'` (default `'lognormal'`).
- smoothingBandwidth?: number; default: not declared — Gaussian-kernel bandwidth (in log-moneyness) for `model: 'smoothed'` (default auto).
- ssviPhi?: 'power-law' | 'heston'; default: not declared — Curvature family for the global `model: 'ssvi'` calibration (default `'power-law'`).
- ssviWeight?: 'vega' | 'uniform'; default: not declared — Least-squares weighting for `model: 'ssvi'`: `'uniform'` (default) or `'vega'` (ATM-dominant).

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility#SurfaceMode

```typescript
/** One principal mode of surface motion. */
export interface SurfaceMode {
    /** The eigenvector across the grid (sign-canonicalized so the loadings sum ≥ 0). */
    loadings: number[];

}
```

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility#SurfaceModel

Kind: type; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

`raw`/`interpolated`/`smoothed` are non-parametric (linear, PCHIP, and a Gaussian-kernel smoother);
`svi`/`sabr` fit a parametric smile per expiry; `heston` calibrates one global stochastic-vol model
to the whole surface. Parametric models fall back to an interpolated smile for expiries with too few
strikes. (Dupire local-volatility *surface fitting* is sequenced later — spec §10.1.)

```typescript
/**
 * `raw`/`interpolated`/`smoothed` are non-parametric (linear, PCHIP, and a Gaussian-kernel smoother);
 * `svi`/`sabr` fit a parametric smile per expiry; `heston` calibrates one global stochastic-vol model
 * to the whole surface. Parametric models fall back to an interpolated smile for expiries with too few
 * strikes. (Dupire local-volatility *surface fitting* is sequenced later — spec §10.1.)
 */
export type SurfaceModel = 'raw' | 'interpolated' | 'smoothed' | 'svi' | 'sabr' | 'ssvi' | 'essvi' | 'heston';
```

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility#SurfaceScenario

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

One shocked-surface scenario (a `sigma`-standard-deviation move along one mode).

```typescript
/** One shocked-surface scenario (a `sigma`-standard-deviation move along one mode). */
export interface SurfaceScenario {
    /** 0-indexed mode. */
    mode: number;
    shape: SurfaceMode['shape'];
    sigma: number;
    /**
     * `sigma·√λ·loadings` — the (unclamped) surface change vector, in the PCA's own units: VOL POINTS

    /**
     * The shocked surface, floored: `max(floor, base + shockVector)` for an `absolute` PCA,
     * `max(floor, base · (1 + shockVector))` for a `relative` one.
     */
    shockedSurface: number[];
}
```

- shape: 'level' | 'slope' | 'curvature' | 'higher-order'; default: not declared
- shockVector: number[]; default: not declared — `sigma·√λ·loadings` — the (unclamped) surface change vector, in the PCA's own units: VOL POINTS
for an `absolute` PCA, FRACTIONS of the base vol for a `relative` one.
- shockedSurface: number[]; default: not declared — The shocked surface, floored: `max(floor, base + shockVector)` for an `absolute` PCA,
`max(floor, base · (1 + shockVector))` for a `relative` one.
- sigma: number; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility#SurfaceSlice

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

One per-expiry smile, strikes ascending.

```typescript
/** One per-expiry smile, strikes ascending. */
export interface SurfaceSlice {
    expiry: string;
    /** Time to expiry in years (ACT/365F). */
    timeToExpiryYears: number;
    /** Forward `S·e^{(r−q)t}`. */
    forward: number;

    /** Fitted SABR parameters when `model: 'sabr'` (absent if the slice fell back to interpolation). */
    sabr?: SabrParameters;
    /** The globally-calibrated SSVI parameters when `model: 'ssvi'` (shared across all slices). */
    ssvi?: SSVIParameters;
    /** The globally-calibrated eSSVI parameters when `model: 'essvi'` (shared across all slices). */
    essvi?: ESSVIParameters;
    /** The globally-calibrated Heston parameters when `model: 'heston'` (shared across all slices). */
    heston?: HestonParameters;
}
```

- deltas: number[]; default: not declared — Call-delta `e^{−qt}·N(d1)` at each strike (the smile's delta axis, for skew lookups).
- essvi?: ESSVIParameters; default: not declared — The globally-calibrated eSSVI parameters when `model: 'essvi'` (shared across all slices).
- essvi.phi: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SSVIPhi; default: not declared — Curvature function (global), same family as SSVI.
- essvi.phi.eta: number; default: not declared
- essvi.phi.gamma: number; default: not declared
- essvi.phi.kind: ('heston') | ('power-law'); default: not declared
- essvi.phi.lambda: number; default: not declared
- essvi.thetaTerm: { timeToExpiryYears: number; theta: number; rho: number; }[]; default: not declared — Per-knot `(t, θ, ρ)`: θ strictly increasing (calendar backbone), ρ ∈ (−1, 1) per maturity.
- expiry: string; default: not declared
- forward: number; default: not declared — Forward `S·e^{(r−q)t}`.
- heston?: HestonParameters; default: not declared — The globally-calibrated Heston parameters when `model: 'heston'` (shared across all slices).
- heston.kappa: number; default: not declared — Mean-reversion speed κ.
- heston.rho: number; default: not declared — Spot/variance correlation ρ ∈ [−1, 1].
- heston.sigma: number; default: not declared — Volatility of variance ξ ("vol of vol").
- heston.theta: number; default: not declared — Long-run variance θ.
- heston.v0: number; default: not declared — Initial instantaneous variance v₀ (= σ₀²).
- impliedVolatilities: number[]; default: not declared
- sabr?: SabrParameters; default: not declared — Fitted SABR parameters when `model: 'sabr'` (absent if the slice fell back to interpolation).
- sabr.alpha: number; default: not declared — Initial volatility level α (> 0).
- sabr.beta: number; default: not declared — Backbone exponent β ∈ [0, 1].
- sabr.nu: number; default: not declared — Volatility of volatility ν (≥ 0).
- sabr.rho: number; default: not declared — Correlation ρ ∈ (−1, 1).
- ssvi?: SSVIParameters; default: not declared — The globally-calibrated SSVI parameters when `model: 'ssvi'` (shared across all slices).
- ssvi.phi: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SSVIPhi; default: not declared — Curvature function.
- ssvi.phi.eta: number; default: not declared
- ssvi.phi.gamma: number; default: not declared
- ssvi.phi.kind: ('heston') | ('power-law'); default: not declared
- ssvi.phi.lambda: number; default: not declared
- ssvi.rho: number; default: not declared — Global skew `ρ ∈ (−1, 1)`.
- ssvi.thetaTerm: { timeToExpiryYears: number; theta: number; }[]; default: not declared — ATM total-variance knots `(t, θ)`, strictly increasing in both (calendar-arbitrage-free).
- strikes: number[]; default: not declared
- svi?: SVIParameters; default: not declared — Fitted raw-SVI parameters when `model: 'svi'` (absent if the slice fell back to interpolation).
- svi.a: number; default: not declared — Vertical level (minimum total variance is `a + b·σ·√(1−ρ²)`).
- svi.b: number; default: not declared — Wing slope / curvature, `≥ 0`.
- svi.m: number; default: not declared — Horizontal shift (log-moneyness of the smile's centre).
- svi.rho: number; default: not declared — Skew / rotation, `∈ [−1, 1]`.
- svi.sigma: number; default: not declared — Smoothness, `> 0`.
- timeToExpiryYears: number; default: not declared — Time to expiry in years (ACT/365F).

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility#SwaptionCube

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

The calibrated swaption cube (data-only, serializable).

```typescript
/** The calibrated swaption cube (data-only, serializable). */
export interface SwaptionCube {
    /** Calibrated nodes, sorted by `(expiry, tenor)`. */
    nodes: CalibratedSwaptionNode[];
    /** Unique expiries, ascending. */
    expiries: number[];
    /** Unique tenors, ascending. */
    tenors: number[];
    volatilityType: SabrVolatilityType;
    /**
     * The rate displacement applied inside SABR (`0` for plain SABR). Nodes' `forward` fields stay the
     * real (unshifted) rates; the shift lives only in the SABR calibration/evaluation. {@link swaptionCubeVolatility}
     * reads this off the cube. OPTIONAL because legacy (pre-shift) serialized cubes carry no field —
     * evaluation reads an absent shift as `0`; the declaration used to say required while the
     * runtime documented that default, and the 3B.1b spec convicted the mismatch (the TA lesson:
     * when the runtime is right, the DECLARATION is what lies).
     */
    shift?: number;
    assumptions: {
        conventionsVersion: string;
        volatilityType: SabrVolatilityType;
        backbone: 'sabr';
        shift: number;
    };
    diagnostics: Diagnostics;
}
```

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility#SwaptionCubeInput

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Input for {@link swaptionCube}.

```typescript
/** Input for {@link swaptionCube}. */
export interface SwaptionCubeInput {
    nodes: SwaptionCubeNode[];
    /** Default backbone β for every node's calibration (0.5, the rates convention). */
    beta?: number;
    /** Volatility quote convention: `'lognormal'` (Black, default) or `'normal'` (Bachelier). */
    volatilityType?: SabrVolatilityType;
    /**
     * Rate displacement `s ≥ 0` for **shifted (displaced) SABR** — SABR is lognormal and needs
     * `forward, strike > 0`, so a negative-rate cube must be calibrated on `forward + s` / `strike + s`.
     * Default `0` (plain SABR). With `s > 0` the `'lognormal'` volatilities are *shifted*-lognormal — price with
     * Black on the shifted rates, `annuity · Black(forward + s, strike + s, vol, expiry)`; `'normal'`
     * (Bachelier) volatilities are unchanged (a common shift cancels in `forward − strike`). See
     * `docs/specs/swaption-cube-shift.md`.
     */
    shift?: number;
    /** `calibrateSabrSmile` iteration cap (pass-through). */
    maximumIterations?: number;
    /** `calibrateSabrSmile` tolerance (pass-through). */
    tolerance?: number;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- beta?: number; default: not declared — Default backbone β for every node's calibration (0.5, the rates convention).
- maximumIterations?: number; default: not declared — `calibrateSabrSmile` iteration cap (pass-through).
- nodes: SwaptionCubeNode[]; default: not declared
- shift?: number; default: not declared — Rate displacement `s ≥ 0` for **shifted (displaced) SABR** — SABR is lognormal and needs
`forward, strike > 0`, so a negative-rate cube must be calibrated on `forward + s` / `strike + s`.
Default `0` (plain SABR). With `s > 0` the `'lognormal'` volatilities are *shifted*-lognormal — price with
Black on the shifted rates, `annuity · Black(forward + s, strike + s, vol, expiry)`; `'normal'`
(Bachelier) volatilities are unchanged (a common shift cancels in `forward − strike`). See
`docs/specs/swaption-cube-shift.md`.
- tolerance?: number; default: not declared — `calibrateSabrSmile` tolerance (pass-through).
- volatilityType?: SabrVolatilityType; default: not declared — Volatility quote convention: `'lognormal'` (Black, default) or `'normal'` (Bachelier).

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility#VannaVolga5Density

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

The 5-pillar-implied risk-neutral terminal distribution and its moments.

```typescript
/** The 5-pillar-implied risk-neutral terminal distribution and its moments. */
export interface VannaVolga5Density {
    /** Risk-neutral (T-forward-measure) PDF at strike `K`, `∂²C/∂K²` (clamped ≥ 0). */
    density(strike: number): number;
    /** Risk-neutral CDF `P(S_T ≤ K) = 1 + ∂C/∂K` (clamped to [0, 1]). */
    cdf(strike: number): number;
    probabilityBelow(strike: number): number;
    probabilityAbove(strike: number): number;
    probabilityBetween(lowerStrike: number, upperStrike: number): number;
    /** Strike at CDF = `p` (inverse CDF via bisection); `p ∈ (0, 1)`. */
    quantile(probability: number): number;
    /** The sampled grid the moments and quantiles are integrated on. */
    grid: {
        strikes: number[];
        density: number[];
        cdf: number[];
    };
    moments: {
        /** `∫f dK` — total captured probability mass, ≈ 1. */
        totalMass: number;
        /** `∫K·f dK` — the risk-neutral mean, ≈ forward by the martingale property. */
        mean: number;
        variance: number;
        stdev: number;
        skewness: number;
        excessKurtosis: number;
    };
    /** The five market pillars the underlying smile reprices exactly, low → high strike. */
    pillars: VannaVolga5Pillar[];
    innerDelta: number;
    outerDelta: number;
    assumptions: {
        conventionsVersion: string;
        method: 'breeden-litzenberger';
        smile: 'vanna-volga-5';
        measure: 'risk-neutral-forward';
    };
    diagnostics: Diagnostics;
}
```

```typescript
    probabilityAbove(strike: number): number;
    probabilityBetween(lowerStrike: number, upperStrike: number): number;
    /** Strike at CDF = `p` (inverse CDF via bisection); `p ∈ (0, 1)`. */
    quantile(probability: number): number;
    /** The sampled grid the moments and quantiles are integrated on. */
    grid: {
        strikes: number[];
        density: number[];
        cdf: number[];
    };
    moments: {
        /** `∫f dK` — total captured probability mass, ≈ 1. */
        totalMass: number;
        /** `∫K·f dK` — the risk-neutral mean, ≈ forward by the martingale property. */
        mean: number;
        variance: number;
        stdev: number;
        skewness: number;
        excessKurtosis: number;
    };
    pillars: {
        putStrike: number;
        putVolatility: number;
        atmStrike: number;
        atmVolatility: number;
        callStrike: number;
        callVolatility: number;
    };
    order: 1 | 2;
    assumptions: {
        conventionsVersion: string;
        method: 'breeden-litzenberger';
        smile: 'castagna-mercurio';
        measure: 'risk-neutral-forward';
        order: 1 | 2;
    };
    diagnostics: Diagnostics;
}
```

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility#VolatilitySpotBeta

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

The empirical vol–spot β and its regression diagnostics.

```typescript
/** The empirical vol–spot β and its regression diagnostics. */
export interface VolatilitySpotBeta {
    /**
     * `β = ∂σ/∂S` in decimal vol **per $1 of spot** — feed straight to
     * `minimumVarianceDelta({ volatilitySpotBeta })`, which expects the same per-dollar units.
     *
     * Units matter here: `stickyRegime` reports `volatilitySpotBetaPerLogSpot` = `∂σ/∂lnS` (per 100%
     * spot move), which is `S ×` this number. On a `'log'` basis the conversion is done for you
     * (`slope / referenceSpot`); {@link slope} is the raw regression coefficient in its own basis.
     */
    volatilitySpotBeta: number;
    /** The regression slope: `∂σ/∂ln S` (`'log'`) or `∂σ/∂S` (`'level'`). */
    slope: number;
    /** Standard error of the slope. */
    slopeStandardError: number;
    /** t-statistic of the slope. */
    slopeTStatistic: number;
    /** Correlation of the IV change with the spot-change regressor (leverage ⇒ negative). */
    correlation: number;
    /** Coefficient of determination `R²`. */
    rSquared: number;
    /** Change observations used (after dropping bad pairs). */
    observationCount: number;
    /** Dropped (non-finite / non-positive) change observations. */
    dropped: number;
    /** Reference spot used for the `∂σ/∂S` conversion. */
    referenceSpot: number;
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- correlation: number; default: not declared — Correlation of the IV change with the spot-change regressor (leverage ⇒ negative).
- dropped: number; default: not declared — Dropped (non-finite / non-positive) change observations.
- observationCount: number; default: not declared — Change observations used (after dropping bad pairs).
- rSquared: number; default: not declared — Coefficient of determination `R²`.
- referenceSpot: number; default: not declared — Reference spot used for the `∂σ/∂S` conversion.
- slope: number; default: not declared — The regression slope: `∂σ/∂ln S` (`'log'`) or `∂σ/∂S` (`'level'`).
- slopeStandardError: number; default: not declared — Standard error of the slope.
- slopeTStatistic: number; default: not declared — t-statistic of the slope.
- volatilitySpotBeta: number; default: not declared — `β = ∂σ/∂S` in decimal vol **per $1 of spot** — feed straight to
`minimumVarianceDelta({ volatilitySpotBeta })`, which expects the same per-dollar units.

Units matter here: `stickyRegime` reports `volatilitySpotBetaPerLogSpot` = `∂σ/∂lnS` (per 100%
spot move), which is `S ×` this number. On a `'log'` basis the conversion is done for you
(`slope / referenceSpot`); {@link slope} is the raw regression coefficient in its own basis.

{@link buildSmile} from the stored slice parameters — never re-fitted — so the restored surface answers
`iv()` identically to the one that produced the snapshot.
- fromJSON().return.arbitrage: (options?: ArbitrageCheckOptions) => ArbitrageReport; default: not declared — Run the static no-arbitrage diagnostics (calendar + butterfly) over this surface.
- fromJSON().return.assumptions: Assumptions<{ shock?: SurfaceShock; }>; default: not declared

- fromJSON().return.expiries: () => string[]; default: not declared — Sorted list of the surface's expiry labels.
- fromJSON().return.heston?: HestonParameters; default: not declared — The global Heston parameters when `model: 'heston'`, else `undefined`.
- fromJSON().return.impliedVolatility: (strike: number, expiry: string | number) => number; default: not declared — Implied vol at `(strike, expiry)`. Throws if the surface is empty (never fabricates).
- fromJSON().return.impliedVolatilityByDelta: (callDelta: number, expiry: string | number) => number; default: not declared — Implied vol on the call-delta axis: interpolate the strike whose call-delta equals `callDelta`
(∈ (0, 1)) from the slice's stored delta ladder, then read the smile there. A 0.25 delta selects
the 25-delta call strike.
- fromJSON().return.impliedVolatilityByMoneyness: (moneyness: number, expiry: string | number, options?: { forward?: boolean; }) => number; default: not declared — Implied vol on the moneyness axis. `moneyness` is `K/S` (spot-moneyness) by default, or `K/F`
(forward-moneyness) when `forward` is set — so `impliedVolatilityByMoneyness(1, e)` is the at-the-money(-forward) vol.

For a NUMERIC `expiry` (a maturity in years) the forward is computed AT THAT MATURITY,
`F(t) = spot·e^{(r−q)·t}` — not borrowed from the nearest fitted slice, which anchored a
mid-expiry query to a neighbour's forward and shifted the ATM-forward point off by the carry
between them.
- fromJSON().return.lookup: (strike: number, expiry: string | number) => SurfaceLookup; default: not declared — Implied vol at `(strike, expiry)` with diagnostics. Strike uses the per-slice smile; expiry
interpolates total variance linearly between the two bracketing slices. `extrapolated` is true
when the query lies outside the fitted strike range or expiry range.
- fromJSON().return.model: SurfaceModel; default: not declared
- fromJSON().return.points: SurfacePoint[]; default: not declared
- fromJSON().return.shock: (shifts: { parallel?: number; skewTilt?: number; }, { sticky }?: { sticky?: 'strike' | 'moneyness'; }) => VolatilitySurface; default: not declared — Return a NEW surface with a shifted vol structure, produced WITHOUT re-fitting: each stored IV
sample gains a `parallel` offset plus a `skewTilt · k` skew rotation (`k = ln(K/forward)`,
log-moneyness), the per-slice deltas are recomputed from the shifted IVs, and only the
interpolators are rebuilt. The shock is echoed in the new surface's `assumptions.shock`.

`sticky`: `'strike'` (default) pins the tilt to each stored strike's own log-moneyness vs the slice
forward; `'moneyness'` lets the same additive shift travel with moneyness. Because the shift is
applied to the stored strike-indexed IV samples, both modes coincide at the stored strikes in this
eager v1 — the distinction only matters once a surface is re-anchored to a new spot/forward, which
this method does not do; the requested mode is recorded in `assumptions.shock.sticky` so a caller
that later re-anchors knows how the tilt was meant to travel.

Parametric models (`svi`/`sabr`/`heston`) have no closed-form shock, so the current smile is SAMPLED
at each slice's stored strikes, those samples are shifted, and the result DEGRADES to
`'interpolated'` with a `volatility.shock_degraded_to_interpolated` `warn` — the parametric fit is not
re-fit. Non-parametric models (`raw`/`interpolated`/`smoothed`) are preserved.
- fromJSON().return.slice: (expiry: string | number) => SurfaceSlice | undefined; default: not declared — The smile at an expiry (exact label or nearest by `t`), or `undefined` if none.
- fromJSON().return.slices: SurfaceSlice[]; default: not declared
- fromJSON().return.ssvi?: SSVIParameters; default: not declared — The global SSVI parameters when `model: 'ssvi'`, else `undefined`.
- fromJSON().return.toJSON: () => VolatilitySurfaceSnapshot; default: not declared — Serialize the surface to a plain, JSON-safe {@link VolatilitySurfaceSnapshot} (no closures). Restore it
with {@link VolatilitySurface.fromJSON}; the pair round-trips `iv()` identically on all six models.
- fromJSON().return.toRows: () => SurfaceRow[]; default: not declared — The smile-chart / heatmap feed: one {@link SurfaceRow} per (slice, stored strike), with
`logMoneyness = ln(strike/forward)` and the stored `delta`/`iv`. Per the workspace missing-value
policy (WS2.12), any non-finite chart-facing numeric is emitted as `null` (never `NaN`, never
omitted).
- fromJSON(snapshot): VolatilitySurfaceSnapshot; default: not declared
- fromJSON(snapshot).assumptions: Assumptions<{ shock?: SurfaceShock; }>; default: not declared
- fromJSON(snapshot).config: { cosineExpansionTerms: number; dividendYield: number; riskFreeRate: number; sabrBeta: number; sabrVolatilityType: SabrVolatilityType; smoothingBandwidth?: number; }; default: not declared — Config knobs needed to rebuild the per-slice interpolators without re-solving from quotes.
- fromJSON(snapshot).config.cosineExpansionTerms: number; default: not declared
- fromJSON(snapshot).config.dividendYield: number; default: not declared
- fromJSON(snapshot).config.riskFreeRate: number; default: not declared
- fromJSON(snapshot).config.sabrBeta: number; default: not declared

- return.shock: (shifts: { parallel?: number; skewTilt?: number; }, { sticky }?: { sticky?: 'strike' | 'moneyness'; }) => VolatilitySurface; default: not declared — Return a NEW surface with a shifted vol structure, produced WITHOUT re-fitting: each stored IV
sample gains a `parallel` offset plus a `skewTilt · k` skew rotation (`k = ln(K/forward)`,
log-moneyness), the per-slice deltas are recomputed from the shifted IVs, and only the
interpolators are rebuilt. The shock is echoed in the new surface's `assumptions.shock`.

`sticky`: `'strike'` (default) pins the tilt to each stored strike's own log-moneyness vs the slice
forward; `'moneyness'` lets the same additive shift travel with moneyness. Because the shift is
applied to the stored strike-indexed IV samples, both modes coincide at the stored strikes in this
eager v1 — the distinction only matters once a surface is re-anchored to a new spot/forward, which
this method does not do; the requested mode is recorded in `assumptions.shock.sticky` so a caller
that later re-anchors knows how the tilt was meant to travel.

Parametric models (`svi`/`sabr`/`heston`) have no closed-form shock, so the current smile is SAMPLED
at each slice's stored strikes, those samples are shifted, and the result DEGRADES to
`'interpolated'` with a `volatility.shock_degraded_to_interpolated` `warn` — the parametric fit is not
re-fit. Non-parametric models (`raw`/`interpolated`/`smoothed`) are preserved.

with {@link VolatilitySurface.fromJSON}; the pair round-trips `iv()` identically on all six models.

`logMoneyness = ln(strike/forward)` and the stored `delta`/`iv`. Per the workspace missing-value
policy (WS2.12), any non-finite chart-facing numeric is emitted as `null` (never `NaN`, never
omitted).

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility#VolatilitySurfaceSnapshot

Kind: interface; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

A serialized surface (spec WS4.4). Carries the model, per-slice smile state (including any fitted
`svi`/`sabr`/`heston` parameters), points, assumptions/diagnostics, the global Heston parameters, `spotRef`,
and the config knobs needed to REBUILD interpolators. Closures are never serialized —
{@link VolatilitySurface.fromJSON} rebuilds them from this state so the restored surface answers `iv()`
identically.

```typescript
/**
 * A serialized surface (spec WS4.4). Carries the model, per-slice smile state (including any fitted
 * `svi`/`sabr`/`heston` parameters), points, assumptions/diagnostics, the global Heston parameters, `spotRef`,
 * and the config knobs needed to REBUILD interpolators. Closures are never serialized —
 * {@link VolatilitySurface.fromJSON} rebuilds them from this state so the restored surface answers `iv()`
 * identically.
 */
export interface VolatilitySurfaceSnapshot {
    schemaVersion: string;
    model: SurfaceModel;
    slices: SurfaceSlice[];
    points: SurfacePoint[];
    assumptions: Assumptions<{
        shock?: SurfaceShock;
    }>;
    diagnostics: Diagnostics;
    /** The global SSVI parameters when `model: 'ssvi'`. */
    ssvi?: SSVIParameters;
    /** The global eSSVI parameters when `model: 'essvi'`. */
    essvi?: ESSVIParameters;
    /** The global Heston parameters when `model: 'heston'`. */
    heston?: HestonParameters;
    referenceSpot: number;
    /** Config knobs needed to rebuild the per-slice interpolators without re-solving from quotes. */
    config: {
        riskFreeRate: number;
        dividendYield: number;
        sabrBeta: number;
        sabrVolatilityType: SabrVolatilityType;
        smoothingBandwidth?: number;
        cosineExpansionTerms: number;
    };
}
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- assumptions: Assumptions<{ shock?: SurfaceShock; }>; default: not declared

date-only `YYYY-MM-DD` expiry resolved to the US equity/options close — 16:00 America/New_York,
or 13:00 on an early-close day;
`'explicit-instant'` when the caller supplied a zoned datetime. Named so the convention is

- assumptions.shock.sticky: 'strike' | 'moneyness'; default: not declared — Which quantity the tilt is pinned to: `'strike'` (default) or `'moneyness'`.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility#arbitrageReport

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Run all static no-arbitrage checks over a set of slices (Law 2 report grammar).

```typescript
export declare function arbitrageReport(slices: ArbitrageSlice[], options?: ArbitrageCheckOptions): ArbitrageReport;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (options)?: ArbitrageCheckOptions; default: not declared
- (options).butterflyPoints?: number; default: not declared — Log-moneyness samples per slice for the butterfly check (default 40, must be ≥ 3).
- (options).calendarPoints?: number; default: not declared — Log-moneyness samples for each calendar pair (default 21, must be ≥ 2).
- (options).step?: number; default: not declared — Central-difference step in log-moneyness for the density derivatives (default 0.01, must be > 0).
- (options).tolerance?: number; default: not declared — Tolerance below which a breach is reported (default 1e-4, must be finite ≥ 0).
- (slices): ArbitrageSlice[]; default: not declared
- return.arbitrageFree: boolean; default: not declared — True when no calendar or butterfly violation was found.
- return.assumptions: { butterflyPoints: number; calendarPoints: number; conventionsVersion: string; step: number; tolerance: number; }; default: not declared — Applied conventions/knobs, echoed (Law 2 report grammar).
- return.assumptions.butterflyPoints: number; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.calendarPoints: number; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.conventionsVersion: string; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.step: number; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.tolerance: number; default: not declared
- return.checks: { butterfly: boolean; calendar: boolean; }; default: not declared — Per-check pass/fail summary.
- return.checks.butterfly: boolean; default: not declared

- return.diagnostics: Diagnostics; default: not declared — Structured warnings (carried-through surface warnings live here); always present.

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility#atmTermStructure

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

The ATM implied-vol term structure: ATM IV and total variance per expiry, with a monotonicity flag.

```typescript
export declare function atmTermStructure(surface: VolatilitySurface): AtmTermStructure;
```

Members/parameters (default = JSDoc only; not declared means no documented default):

- (surface): VolatilitySurface; default: not declared
- (surface).arbitrage: (options?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').ArbitrageCheckOptions) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').ArbitrageReport; default: not declared — Run the static no-arbitrage diagnostics (calendar + butterfly) over this surface.
- (surface).assumptions: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/core').Assumptions<{ shock?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SurfaceShock; }>; default: not declared
- (surface).diagnostics: Diagnostics; default: not declared
- (surface).essvi?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').ESSVIParameters; default: not declared — The global eSSVI parameters when `model: 'essvi'`, else `undefined`.
- (surface).expiries: () => string[]; default: not declared — Sorted list of the surface's expiry labels.
- (surface).heston?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/options').HestonParameters; default: not declared — The global Heston parameters when `model: 'heston'`, else `undefined`.
- (surface).impliedVolatility: (strike: number, expiry: string | number) => number; default: not declared — Implied vol at `(strike, expiry)`. Throws if the surface is empty (never fabricates).
- (surface).impliedVolatilityByDelta: (callDelta: number, expiry: string | number) => number; default: not declared — Implied vol on the call-delta axis: interpolate the strike whose call-delta equals `callDelta`
(∈ (0, 1)) from the slice's stored delta ladder, then read the smile there. A 0.25 delta selects
the 25-delta call strike.
- (surface).impliedVolatilityByMoneyness: (moneyness: number, expiry: string | number, options?: { forward?: boolean; }) => number; default: not declared — Implied vol on the moneyness axis. `moneyness` is `K/S` (spot-moneyness) by default, or `K/F`
(forward-moneyness) when `forward` is set — so `impliedVolatilityByMoneyness(1, e)` is the at-the-money(-forward) vol.

For a NUMERIC `expiry` (a maturity in years) the forward is computed AT THAT MATURITY,
`F(t) = spot·e^{(r−q)·t}` — not borrowed from the nearest fitted slice, which anchored a
mid-expiry query to a neighbour's forward and shifted the ATM-forward point off by the carry
between them.
- (surface).lookup: (strike: number, expiry: string | number) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SurfaceLookup; default: not declared — Implied vol at `(strike, expiry)` with diagnostics. Strike uses the per-slice smile; expiry
interpolates total variance linearly between the two bracketing slices. `extrapolated` is true
when the query lies outside the fitted strike range or expiry range.
- (surface).model: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SurfaceModel; default: not declared
- (surface).points: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SurfacePoint[]; default: not declared
- (surface).shock: (shifts: { parallel?: number; skewTilt?: number; }, { sticky }?: { sticky?: 'strike' | 'moneyness'; }) => VolatilitySurface; default: not declared — Return a NEW surface with a shifted vol structure, produced WITHOUT re-fitting: each stored IV
sample gains a `parallel` offset plus a `skewTilt · k` skew rotation (`k = ln(K/forward)`,
log-moneyness), the per-slice deltas are recomputed from the shifted IVs, and only the
interpolators are rebuilt. The shock is echoed in the new surface's `assumptions.shock`.

`sticky`: `'strike'` (default) pins the tilt to each stored strike's own log-moneyness vs the slice
forward; `'moneyness'` lets the same additive shift travel with moneyness. Because the shift is
applied to the stored strike-indexed IV samples, both modes coincide at the stored strikes in this
eager v1 — the distinction only matters once a surface is re-anchored to a new spot/forward, which
this method does not do; the requested mode is recorded in `assumptions.shock.sticky` so a caller
that later re-anchors knows how the tilt was meant to travel.

Parametric models (`svi`/`sabr`/`heston`) have no closed-form shock, so the current smile is SAMPLED
at each slice's stored strikes, those samples are shifted, and the result DEGRADES to
`'interpolated'` with a `volatility.shock_degraded_to_interpolated` `warn` — the parametric fit is not
re-fit. Non-parametric models (`raw`/`interpolated`/`smoothed`) are preserved.
- (surface).slice: (expiry: string | number) => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SurfaceSlice | undefined; default: not declared — The smile at an expiry (exact label or nearest by `t`), or `undefined` if none.
- (surface).slices: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SurfaceSlice[]; default: not declared
- (surface).ssvi?: import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SSVIParameters; default: not declared — The global SSVI parameters when `model: 'ssvi'`, else `undefined`.
- (surface).toJSON: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').VolatilitySurfaceSnapshot; default: not declared — Serialize the surface to a plain, JSON-safe {@link VolatilitySurfaceSnapshot} (no closures). Restore it
with {@link VolatilitySurface.fromJSON}; the pair round-trips `iv()` identically on all six models.
- (surface).toRows: () => import('@insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility').SurfaceRow[]; default: not declared — The smile-chart / heatmap feed: one {@link SurfaceRow} per (slice, stored strike), with
`logMoneyness = ln(strike/forward)` and the stored `delta`/`iv`. Per the workspace missing-value
policy (WS2.12), any non-finite chart-facing numeric is emitted as `null` (never `NaN`, never
omitted).
- return.assumptions: { conventionsVersion: string; coordinate: 'atm-total-variance'; }; default: not declared — Applied conventions, echoed (Law 2 report grammar).
- return.assumptions.conventionsVersion: string; default: not declared
- return.assumptions.coordinate: 'atm-total-variance'; default: not declared
- return.calendarMonotone: boolean; default: not declared — Whether ATM total variance is non-decreasing across maturities (calendar-arbitrage-free ATM).
- return.diagnostics: Diagnostics; default: not declared — Structured warnings; a non-monotone ATM structure discloses itself here.
- return.points: AtmTermPoint[]; default: not declared

### @insiderfinance/totalfinance/volatility#calendarSkew

Kind: function; stability: stable-by-law (pre-1.0; not a 1.0 stability guarantee).

Calendar skew: how the ATM skew slope changes from the near to the far expiry (`slope_far −
slope_near`). Negative when the near-dated smile is steeper (the usual term-structure-of-skew shape).

Facade (H22): the plain call returns the scalar; `.explain()` discloses the sorted near/far
expiries and the canonical `0.05` log-moneyness central-difference step in `assumptions`, and both
ATM skew slopes in `diagnostics.decomposition`. Hand-attached (not `seriesFacade`) so the plain
call's first-touch teaching errors stay byte-identical.

```typescript
export declare const calendarSkew: CalendarSkewFacade;
```
